title: chore: remove user-facing MeshManager references and stale solar-forecast gallery script (#6048)
body:
## Summary

MeshManager is winding down and `Yeraze/meshmanager` is archived. MeshMonitor now provides multi-source monitoring and analysis natively, so this PR removes the remaining **user-facing** dependencies on MeshManager.

Closes #6048.

## solar-forecast.py decision: REMOVE the gallery entry

**Decision:** removed the gallery entry (did not port).

**Reasoning:**
- The `solar-forecast.py` script does **not** live in the MeshMonitor repo — it is hosted only in the archived `Yeraze/meshmanager` repo (`githubPath: Yeraze/meshmanager/...`). There is no local file to delete.
- It requires a **running MeshManager instance** (`MESHMANAGER_URL`) and calls MeshManager's `/api/analysis/solar-forecast`, so it is broken for any new user who installs it.
- MeshMonitor already covers solar forecasting natively: the built-in **Solar Monitoring Analysis** report (`docs/features/analysis-reports.md`) plus the `GET /api/analysis/solar-forecast?lookback_days=N&sources=…` endpoint.
- A direct port is **not quick and clearly correct**: MeshMonitor's endpoint is session-authenticated and per-source/permission scoped, and the output must be reformatted for an auto-responder. title: fix(security): nonce-based CSP, drop unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval from script-src (MISC-09) [DO NOT MERGE]
body:
## MISC-09 (#6085): remove `unsafe-inline` / `unsafe-eval` from `script-src`

Defense-in-depth XSS hardening. Moves trusted inline scripts to a per-request
nonce and tightens the production `script-src` so it never ships
`'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'`.

> ⚠️ **DO NOT MERGE yet — hold for human review.** This carries white-page
> risk by nature (a CSP that is too tight blanks the app). It has been
> browser-validated (below), but please sign off before merging.

### The real hole this closes

`script-src` was only strict when `isProduction && cookieSecure` were **both**
true. But `COOKIE_SECURE` defaults to **false** (the HTTP-friendly Quick-Start
default, and the normal case behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy), so the
typical production deployment fell into the loose branch and shipped
`'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'` to every visitor. Additionally,
`'unsafe-inline'` was added to `script-src` whenever any analytics provider was
enabled, even in the "secure" branch.

### What changed

- **`script-src` is now strict for all production runs** (keyed on `NODE_ENV`
  only, decoupled from `COOKIE_SECURE`): `'self' 'nonce-<per-request>'`. No
  `'unsafe-inline'`, no `'unsafe-eval'`.
- **Per-request nonce**: a fresh 128-bit base64 nonce is generated per response
  in `dynamicCspMiddleware` and exposed on `res.locals.cspNonce`.
- **Inline scripts that were nonce-tagged**: the app's own scripts in the built
  `index.html` / `embed.html` are *all* external `src=` files (the main bundle,
  `registerSW.js`, `cors-detection.js`) already covered by `'self'` — there are
  **no inline scripts** in the shipped HTML shell. The **only** inline scripts
  ever served are the **analytics snippets** (GA4 inline config, PostHog
  bootstrap, Matomo, and the admin "custom" snippet). `generateAnalyticsScript`
  now stamps every emitted `<script>` tag with the nonce, via a
  `__CSP_NONCE__` placeholder baked into the cached HTML and substituted with
  the real per-request nonce at serve time in `staticServing`.
- **Embed page**: `createEmbedCspMiddleware` now uses the nonce instead of
  `'unsafe-inline'` (with an `'unsafe-inline'` fallback only if no nonce is set).
- **Dev mode unchanged**: development (`NODE_ENV !== production`) keeps
  `'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'` because the Vite toolchain injects
  un-nonced inline scripts and relies on `eval` for HMR — a nonce cannot reach
  those.

### What still requires a loosened directive, and why

| Directive | Value kept | Where | Why |
|-----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| `script-src` | `'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'` | **development only** | Vite HMR injects un-nonced inline scripts and uses `eval`. Never emitted in production. |
| `style-src` | `'unsafe-inline'` | all modes | Leaflet, MapLibre and React inline style props set per-element `style="…"` attributes at runtime. CSP nonces apply to `<style>`/`<script>` elements, **not** style attributes, so a nonce cannot cover them; removing it blanks t

title: fix(security): prevent remote argv injection via OTA node names in script runners (#6090)
body:
## Verdict

**Legitimate.** The expand-then-split argv flaw fixed for the `/scripts/test` route in #6089 (MISC-06 / #6076) was also present in the **live** `meshtasticManager` script runners. Confirmed against current `main`.

## The vulnerability

The three script runners — auto-responder, geofence, and timer triggers — expanded their script-args template into a single string and **then** split it into argv:

```
expandedArgs = await replace*Tokens(trigger.scriptArgs, …)   // expand first
scriptArgsList = this.parseScriptArgs(expandedArgs)          // split second
```

Template tokens such as `{LONG_NAME}` / `{SHORT_NAME}` are populated from **over-the-air mesh traffic** (a node's self-reported name). A node whose name carried spaces or quotes therefore split into **extra argv elements** when a configured script trigger fired — a remote argv-injection vector reachable without any local access.

## What changed

- Added a shared `expandScriptArgsTokens(template, expandElement)` helper that **tokenizes the admin-authored template into argv first** (reusing the existing, tested `parseScriptArgs`, whose quote/space boundaries are chosen by the trusted admin), **then expands template tokens inside each resulting element**. Per-element expansion confines each OTA-sourced value to the single argument it appears in, so a hostile node name can never inject new arguments.
- Routed all three runners (auto-responder, geofence, timer) through the helper.
- No env change needed: all three already spawned via `buildScriptChildEnv()` (secret-stripping + `PYTHONSAFEPATH`, INJ-01/MISC-01) from the #6089 work.
- Added `meshtasticManager.scriptArgsInjection.test.ts`: asserts a node name with spaces/quotes/`;`/`$()` stays a single argv element, that the structure of a multi-token template is preserved, that the old expand-then-split ordering would have split it, and a real-spawn check that the child receives exactly one positional argument.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` — clean
- New + related runner suites (`scriptArgsInjection`, `autoAckTokens`, `geofence`, `autoResponderSyntax`, `scriptRoutes.security`) — 44/44 pass
- `npm run lint:ci` (in-repo) — clean

Closes #6090

title: fix(security): gate per-source forwarding toggle on automation enable (#6096)
body:
## Verdict

Confirmed against current `main`: `POST /api/automations/:id/enable` lacked the per-source forwarding-toggle gate that PR #6095 added to `POST /:id/run-now`. The audit also found a second ungated activation path — `PUT /api/automations/:id` ran the gate only when a new `config` was supplied, so `PUT {enabled:true}` with no config armed the stored graph ungated. Both are fixed.

Enabling a privileged-authored forwarding-toggle automation (schedule-triggered `action.setSourceForwardingEnabled`) arms the scheduler, so it would later fire on its own against sources the enabling user cannot act on — a way around the save-time / run-now per-source check.

## What changed

`src/server/routes/automationRoutes.ts`:
- **`POST /:id/enable`** — fetch the stored automation and apply `checkForwardingTogglePermission(req, res, auto.config)` before `setEnabled(true)`. Mirrors run-now: admins pass; automations with no forwarding-toggle action are unaffected; an absent row skips the gate and `setEnabled` is a harmless no-op (preserves the existing no-404 behaviour).
- **`PUT /:id`** — when the patch flips `enabled` on and no new `config` is supplied, gate against the stored config. (A supplied config was already gated; disabling is never gated.)

**Audit of the remaining handlers:** `/:id/disable` turns forwarding off (safe); `/:id/reset-homes` requires an already-enabled automation, so it is covered transitively once `/enable` is gated; `/`, `/import`, `/:id/duplicate`, `PUT` (with config) and `/:id/run-now` were already gated. No other activation path is missing the gate.

## Tests

New `src/server/routes/automationRoutes.enableGate.test.ts` (uses `createRouteTestApp()`), mirroring `automationRoutes.runNow.test.ts`:
- enable of a forwarding-toggle automation without the per-source grant → `403 FORWARDING_SOURCE_FORBIDDEN` (and the row stays disabled)
- enable with per-source `automation:write` → allowed, row enabled
- admin → allowed
- non-forwarding automation → unaffected
- `PUT {enabled:true}` without config: without grant → 403, with grant → allowed; `PUT {enabled:false}` never gated

Confirmed the enable-403 test fails before the fix and passes after.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` on the new suite + runNow/duplicate/setAutomationEnabled/setSourceForwardingEnabled — 41 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run lint:ci` (worktree-filtered) — clean

Closes #6096

body:
## Cluster C7 — SSRF + settings authorization

Remediates the C7 cluster from the automated Shannon pentest. Each finding was verified against current code before fixing; all six were legit.

| ID | Issue | Verdict | Action | Note |
|----|-------|---------|--------|------|
| SSRF-01 | #6060 | LEGIT | Fixed | Hex-group IPv4-mapped IPv6 bypassed `classifyIPv6` |
| SSRF-02 | #6061 | LEGIT | Fixed | Provider URL unguarded + internal body reflected |
| SSRF-03 | #6078 | LEGIT | Fixed | Stored Apprise URL reached internal services |
| SSRF-04 | #6079 | LEGIT | Fixed | Probe denylist missed loopback/RFC1918/IPv6/hex-group |
| SSRF-05 | #6080 | LEGIT | Fixed | MeshCore TCP connect took an unvalidated host |
| AUTHZ-06 | #6070 | LEGIT | Fixed | Global-only settings writable by a single-source grantee |

### SSRF-01 (#6060) — HIGH
`classifyIPv6` only matched the dotted-decimal IPv4-mapped form (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`), but the WHATWG URL parser normalizes every mapped form to the hex-group representation (`::ffff:7f00:1`) before the guard runs — so the regex was dead code and loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / cloud-metadata addresses slipped past all classification. Now both textual forms are normalized to the embedded IPv4 and classified as v4, including before the always-blocked check so the hex-group metadata form is caught. This single fix hardens every guard consumer (link preview, tile test, map style, elevation, …).

### SSRF-02 (#6061) — HIGH
The LibreTranslate/DeepL/OpenAI providers fetched an operator-configurable endpoint with no SSRF guard and reflected the upstream response body verbatim in the thrown error (→ API error message), exfiltrating internal service content. Now the endpoint is validated with `assertSafeUrl` and the thrown error is status-only (body logged server-side at debug). Admin-gated (`requireAdmin` on `/translate/test`), but guarded as defense-in-depth. Google's endpoint is fixed (`googleapis.com`) and left unchanged.

### SSRF-03 (#6078) — MEDIUM
Every outbound Apprise API call (health/config/notify) now runs through `safeFetch`, so a stored `appriseApiServerUrl` / per-source `apprise_url` can no longer aim notifications at cloud metadata. `settings:write`-gated.

### SSRF-04 (#6079) — MEDIUM
The `test-apprise` probe's hand-rolled denylist only blocked `169.254/16` dotted and two metadata hostnames. The probe URL now runs through the guard; a blocked target returns 400 instead of a timing/status oracle. `settings:write`-gated.

### SSRF-05 (#6080) — MEDIUM
The MeshCore TCP connect endpoint opened a socket to an arbitrary host. `tcpHost` is now validated with `assertSafeHost`.

### AUTHZ-06 (#6070) — MEDIUM
`GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS` were only filtered on a per-source save, so a non-admin with `settings:write` on one source could overwrite install-wide, security-relevant keys (`externalUrl`, `pkiDmDecryptionGloballyEnabled`, `position_estimation_*`, …) via an unscoped POST. title: fix(security): harden auth/session/DB surfaces (C9)
body:
## Summary

Remediates cluster **C9 (auth / session / DB hardening)** from the Shannon automated pentest. Each finding was verified against current code before fixing; all seven were legit. Fixes are minimal and localized, each with a regression test (fails before / passes after).

## Per-finding verdict & fix

| ID | Issue | Verdict | Action | Fix |
|----|-------|---------|--------|-----|
| MISC-04 | #6074 | LEGIT | Fixed | Admin reset now terminates the target user's sessions. |
| MISC-07 | #6077 | LEGIT | Fixed | Self password change invalidates the user's other sessions, keeps current. |
| AUTH-03 | #6082 | LEGIT | Fixed | `check-default-password` gated to authenticated admins; others get non-revealing `false`. |
| AUTH-02 | #6081 | LEGIT | Fixed | Unknown-user login runs a dummy bcrypt compare → constant-time. |
| MISC-05 | #6075 | LEGIT | Fixed | MFA backup-code consume is an atomic compare-and-swap. |
| MISC-10 | #6086 | LEGIT | Fixed | `news/user/status` rejects a non-string `lastSeenNewsId`. |
| MISC-08 | #6084 | LEGIT | Fixed | `/api/health` returns only `{status:"ok"}` to anonymous callers. |

### Details

- **MISC-04 / MISC-07 — session invalidation.** Added `AuthRepository.deleteSessionsByUserId(userId, exceptSid?)` (scans the shared session store, matches the serialized `userId`, portable across SQLite/PG/MySQL) exposed as `DatabaseService.deleteSessionsByUserIdAsync`. `resetUserPassword` invalidates all of the target user's sessions; the self change-password route invalidates the user's other sessions and preserves the current one by `sid`.
- **AUTH-03 — default-password disclosure.** The endpoint now runs `optionalAuth()` and returns the real status only to an authenticated admin. The only consumer (`useSecurityCheck`, authenticated) is unaffected; anonymous/non-admin callers get `false`.
- **AUTH-02 — login timing oracle.** `authenticateAsync` now runs `bcrypt.compare` against a fixed cost-10 dummy hash when the username is unknown or has no password, so the missing-user path takes the same time as a wrong-password path.
- **MISC-05 — MFA backup-code TOCTOU.** Replaced the read-verify-write with `AuthRepository.consumeBackupCode(userId, expectedCodes, remainingCodes)`, a CAS `UPDATE … WHERE mfaBackupCodes = :expected` that returns whether it won. title: fix(security): C8 authorization — automation run-now per-source gate (#6071)
body:
## C8 — Authorization (IDOR + automation)

Remediates cluster C8 from the Shannon automated pentest. Each finding was verified against current `main` before acting.

### AUTHZ-07 (#6071) — Automation run-now bypassed per-source authorization — **FIXED**

`POST /api/automations/:id/run-now` dispatches an automation's **live** actions but only checked the global `automations:write` grant. The per-source gate that the save paths (create/update/import/duplicate) apply via `checkForwardingTogglePermission` — requiring `automation` write on every source a `setSourceForwardingEnabled` action targets — was not re-applied at execute time. A user holding only the global grant could therefore fire a forwarding-toggle automation that someone else authored against a source they cannot otherwise act on.

**Fix:** re-apply the same stored-config gate in the run-now handler before dispatch, mirroring the `duplicate` handler. When the automation row is absent the gate is skipped and the engine reports `not_found` as before. Automations without a forwarding-toggle action are unaffected; admins pass.

Regression tests added to `automationRoutes.runNow.test.ts` (verified failing before, passing after).

### AUTHZ-04 (#6068) — DM IDOR — **NOT A VULNERABILITY (closed as not planned)**

MeshMonitor has no user-to-node ownership model; its confidentiality boundary is source-scoped RBAC. The DM endpoint already enforces that boundary via `requireSourcePermission('messages','read')` + `getSourceTarget(req)` — another source's DMs are never returned, and an explicit `?sourceId=` the caller lacks `messages:read` on is rejected. `messages:read` on a source is read access to all of that source's observed traffic (channel and DM alike) by design. Details posted on the issue.

- `npx vitest run` on touched route tests — 22 passed

title: fix(security): confine backup file paths and tighten backup authz (C3)
body:
## Shannon pentest cluster C3 — backup file-path + authorization

Each finding was verified against current `main`. All five are legitimate and fixed.

| ID | Issue | Severity | Verdict | Fix |
|----|-------|----------|---------|-----|
| INJ-02 | #6054 | HIGH | LEGIT | Confine DB-sourced backup path before delete |
| INJ-03 | #6055 | HIGH | LEGIT | Confine DB-sourced backup path before read |
| AUTHZ-02 | #6053 | HIGH | LEGIT | System backup create → `requireAdmin()` |
| AUTHZ-03 | #6067 | MEDIUM | LEGIT | System backup list/delete → `requireAdmin()` |
| AUTHZ-09 | #6073 | MEDIUM | LEGIT | Device backup list/download/delete → source-scoped gate |

### INJ-02 / INJ-03 — path containment

`backupFileService.getBackup()` / `deleteBackup()` validated the URL `filename`
with a regex, then read the actual on-disk path from the `backup_history.filePath`
**column** and used it unchecked. A tampered row could point `filePath` anywhere,
turning download into an arbitrary file read and delete into an arbitrary file
wipe. The system-backup `purgeOldBackups()` had the same shape on
`system_backup_history.backupPath`, where a `../../` value would recursively
delete an arbitrary tree.

New helper `src/server/utils/pathContainment.ts#resolveWithinDir(root, target)`
resolves a path and throws unless it is `root` or a descendant (rejecting `..`
traversal, absolute escapes, and sibling-prefix bypass). It now guards every
DB-sourced path before any `fs` read/delete:
`backupFileService.getBackup`/`deleteBackup`/`purgeOldBackups` (against the
device-backup dir) and `systemBackupService.getBackupPath`/`purgeOldBackups`
(against the system-backup dir). Legitimate backups, whose stored paths are
inside the backup dir, are unaffected.

### AUTHZ-02 / AUTHZ-03 — system backups are admin-only

`configuration` is a per-source resource. `requirePermission('configuration', …)`
with no `sourceIdFrom` passes on a grant for **any** single source, so a non-admin
with `configuration:write` on one source could create, list, and delete full
cross-source database archives (which contain every source's channel PSKs, MQTT
credentials, password hashes, and API token hashes). A system backup is global
by nature — there is no source to scope to — so create/list/delete now use
`requireAdmin()`, matching the download endpoint, which was already admin-only.

### AUTHZ-09 — device backups are source-scoped

The device-backup list/download/delete endpoints had the same ANY-source union
hole. They now use `requireDeviceSourcePermission('configuration', …, 'query')`,

title: fix(security): gate channel PSK exposure + channel-db ownership (C4)
body:
## Summary

Remediates Shannon pentest cluster **C4 — channel PSK exposure / channel ACL authz**. Each finding was verified against current code before fixing; all four were LEGIT (reproducible in the current tree).

| ID | Issue | Severity | Verdict | Fix |
|----|-------|----------|---------|-----|
| MISC-02 | #6058 | HIGH | LEGIT | `POST /api/channels/encode-url` gate raised `configuration:read` → `configuration:write` |
| MISC-03 | #6059 | HIGH | LEGIT | `GET /api/channels/:id/export` gate raised `channel_N:read` → `channel_N:write` |
| MISC-11 | #6087 | LOW | LEGIT | Channel-database listing: masked callers now get a constant `(hidden)` sentinel instead of the first 8 base64 chars of the PSK |
| AUTHZ-08 | #6072 | MEDIUM | LEGIT | Per-row ownership check added to channel-database update / delete / ACL get+set+delete handlers |

## Details

**MISC-02 / MISC-03 — full AES PSK handed to read-only users.** Both `encode-url` (PSK embedded in the returned Meshtastic URL) and `/:id/export` (raw base64 PSK in the JSON body) are key-exfiltration surfaces: the PSK decrypts all traffic on a channel and lets the holder inject authenticated packets. The channel listing already masks PSKs for read-only callers, so these endpoints were a side door around that policy. Exporting key material is a privileged action, so the gate is now **write**. Authorized callers (write holders / admins) are unaffected; the feature keeps working.

**MISC-11 — partial PSK preview to anonymous users.** The listing returned `pskPreview` = first 8 base64 chars (~6 raw key bytes) to anyone with `channel_database:read`, including the default anonymous grant. That both confirmed a PSK was set and let a caller fingerprint channels sharing a key by matching previews. Non-write callers now receive a constant `(hidden)` sentinel — PSK presence is still conveyed (`pskLength`, `(hidden)` vs `(none)`), but no key bytes and no cross-channel oracle. The only legitimate consumer of `pskPreview` is the admin-only Channel Database UI, which gets the full key via the write/admin path and is unchanged.

**AUTHZ-08 — flat global write grant with no ownership boundary.** `channel_database:write` let any holder overwrite another user's PSK and grant/revoke another user's ACLs on entries they did not create (including admin-owned entries). `channel_database` stays **global-by-design** (per CLAUDE.md — no `sourceId` column); the fix is an authorization check, not source scoping. A per-row `canManageEntry` gate now requires `createdBy === caller` (or admin) on update, delete, and the ACL get/set/delete handlers. Entries with no recorded creator are admin-only (fail-safe). Create/list/read are unchanged.

## Tests (fail before, pass after)

- `deviceSourcePermission.scope.test.ts`: encode-url case flipped to `action: 'write'`, which auto-generates the "403s with only configuration:read" case (MISC-02) and keeps the gate/table consistent.
- `channelRoutes.exportAuthz.test.ts` (new): read-only → 403, writ

title: fix(security): analytics stored-XSS encoding + admin-gate (C5)
body:
## Summary

Remediates cluster **C5 — analytics-settings stored XSS + weak CSP** from the Shannon pentest. Each finding was verified against current code before changing anything.

The analytics `<script>` generator (`src/server/utils/analyticsScriptGenerator.ts`) injects provider snippets into every page's `<head>`. It interpolated admin-supplied values into inline scripts / HTML attributes with no context-correct encoding, so values meant to be *data* (API keys, domains) could carry *code*.

## Per-finding verdict

| ID | Issue | Verdict | Action |
|----|-------|---------|--------|
| XSS-01 | #6062 | **Legit** — PostHog `apiKey` broke out of the inline script via an embedded `</script>` | **Fixed**: `apiKey` strictly allowlisted (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`); `apiHost` encoded for the JS-string context |
| XSS-02 | #6063 | **Legit** — Plausible `domain` broke out of the `data-domain=""` attribute | **Fixed**: domain HTML-attribute-encoded |
| XSS-03 | #6064 | **Legit (nuanced)** — the `custom` provider is *intended* arbitrary-script injection; it was already admin-only in practice (see below), but the authorization was implicit | **Fixed/hardened**: analytics writes made explicitly admin-only |
| MISC-09 | #6085 | **Legit (low)** — CSP relaxes to `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval` in dev and re-adds `unsafe-inline` for inline analytics in prod | **Deferred** (not closed): a safe fix needs a per-response nonce-based CSP; tracked on the issue. This PR removes the injection vectors at the source so the XSS findings no longer rely on the CSP |

## Details

**XSS-01 / XSS-02 (and two latent siblings).** Added shared `escapeHtmlAttribute` and `escapeJsString` helpers and applied context-correct encoding at every interpolation site. `escapeJsString` also escapes `<`/`>` so an embedded `</script>` can't close the inline script (the HTML-parser-confusion vector). The same two bugs existed unreported in the **Umami** (attribute) and **Matomo** (JS-string) snippets — both hardened with the same helpers. GA4 and Cloudflare were already safe via strict regex allowlists and are unchanged.

**XSS-03.** The `custom` provider deliberately lets an operator inject an arbitrary analytics `<script>`. In practice this already required an admin: `analyticsConfig` (which holds the script/key/domain payloads) is a `SECRET_SETTINGS_KEYS` entry, so a non-admin `settings:write` save already drops it, and the Settings UI gates the section on `isAdmin`. However, the server only required `settings:write`, and the non-secret `analyticsProvider` key could still be set by a non-admin. To make the trust boundary explicit and consistent with the UI, `analyticsProvider` + `analyticsConfig` are added to `ADMIN_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`. An admin injecting script into their own deployment is the intended feature and is not a privilege boundary crossing.

## Tests (regression: fail before, pass after)

- `src/server/utils/analyticsScriptGenerator.test.ts` — 7 breakout/allowlist assertions fail on the old

title: fix(security): close script-engine RCE holes (C1)
body:
## Summary

Remediates the **C1 — Script-engine RCE** cluster from the Shannon pentest. Every finding was re-verified against current `main` before changing anything. All five are **LEGIT**; fixes below keep the scripting feature working and just close the holes.

| ID | Issue | Verdict | Outcome | Note |
|----|-------|---------|---------|------|
| INJ-01 | #6052 | LEGIT | Fixed | Privilege gap (upload=write, exec=read) + full `process.env` handed to the child. Execute now needs the same privilege as upload (admin); secrets stripped from every script child env. |
| AUTHZ-01 | #6051 | LEGIT | Fixed | `settings` is a per-source resource; the routes omitted `sourceIdFrom`, so the union branch in `checkPermissionAsync` passed on **any** single-source grant. Scripts are global with no sourceId, so the correct gate is `requireAdmin()`. |
| INJ-04 | #6056 | LEGIT | Fixed | `npm install` ran without `--ignore-scripts`; a malicious/compromised `package.json` postinstall hook executed. Added the flag; installer env sanitised. |
| MISC-01 | #6057 | LEGIT | Fixed | Python runs as `python3 /data/scripts/foo.py`, so CPython prepends the scripts dir to `sys.path[0]` and an uploaded `requests.py`/`os.py` shadows the real module. Set `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` (incl. for `python -m pip`); `PYTHONPATH` deps mechanism preserved. |
| MISC-06 | #6076 | LEGIT | Fixed | Mock-node tokens were expanded into the args string **before** it was tokenized, so a `SHORT_NAME` with whitespace/flags split into extra argv. Now the template is tokenized first and tokens expand within each element. |

## Changes

- **Permission gate.** `POST /scripts/test`, `POST /scripts/import`, `POST /scripts/dependencies/install`, `PUT /scripts/:f/source`, `POST /scripts/:f/update`, `POST /scripts/:f/rollback`, `DELETE /scripts/:f` now use `requireAdmin()`. Read-only endpoints (inventory, deps status, update checks, export) are unchanged on `settings:read`.
- **Secret stripping.** New shared `buildScriptChildEnv()` / `sanitizeScriptEnv()` in `scriptRunner.ts`, used by the test route, the generic `runScript` runner, and the three `meshtasticManager` inline runners. Drops `SESSION_SECRET`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `DATABASE_*`, `OIDC_*`, `VAPID_*`, and any name matching `*SECRET* / *PASSWORD* / *TOKEN* / *PRIVATE_KEY* / *CREDENTIAL* / *API_KEY*`.
- **Python shadowing.** `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` for Python children and the pip installer.
- **npm.** `--ignore-scripts` on the dependency install; installer env sanitised too.
- **Argv confinement.** Tokenize-first arg expansion in `/scripts/test`.
- **Tests.** `scriptRunner.security.test.ts` (env/secret unit coverage), an `--ignore-scripts` assertion in `scriptDependencyService.test.ts`, and `scriptRoutes.security.test.ts` (route harness: admin gate + end-to-end secret-stripping and single-argv confinement).

## Behaviour change (noted for review)

Script **management and execution** is now admin-only on the backend. The Scripts settings section was already admin-gated in

title: fix(security): validate API token before skipping CSRF (#6050)
body:
## Verdict: LEGIT (confirmed against current code)

Finding AUTH-01 / cluster C2 — CSRF bypass via any `Authorization: Bearer` header.

`src/server/middleware/csrf.ts` skipped CSRF validation whenever a request
carried any `Authorization: Bearer` header, checking only the `Bearer ` prefix
and never the token value:

```
if (authHeader && authHeader.startsWith('Bearer ')) { return next(); }
```

This is exploitable today. `requireAuth`/`optionalAuth` resolve `req.session.userId`
(the session cookie) **before** falling back to a Bearer token, so a request
authenticated by a session cookie — which IS CSRF-able — could add
`Authorization: Bearer <anything>` to skip CSRF on every state-mutating route
(POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH), e.g. creating an admin user or writing settings.

## Fix

The Bearer exemption now fires **only when the token is validated**:
`databaseService.validateApiTokenAsync(token)` must resolve to an active user.

- A bogus Bearer value falls through to normal CSRF enforcement, so a
  session-cookie request can no longer bypass CSRF.
- Token-validation errors **fail closed** (CSRF enforced).
- A genuine API-token request (valid `mm_v1_…`, no cookie) still skips CSRF —
  a token is not an ambient browser credential and cannot be forged cross-site,
  which is the original, legitimate reason for the exemption.

`csrfProtection` is now async (only the Bearer branch awaits; all other paths
stay synchronous).

## Tests

- `src/server/middleware/csrf.test.ts` — unit coverage of the branch: valid
  token skips, bogus token enforces, inactive-user token enforces, validation
  error fails closed.
- `src/server/middleware/csrf.bearer.integration.test.ts` — end-to-end via
  `createRouteTestApp()` (real session + real DB + real minted API token):
  session cookie + bogus Bearer + no CSRF token is **rejected (403
  CSRF_TOKEN_REQUIRED)**; the same session with a valid CSRF token still works;
  a genuine API-token request still works.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` on both touched test files — 14 passed
- `npm run lint:ci` (in-repo) — clean

Closes #6050

title: fix(automation): persist cooldown and rate-limit state across restarts
body:
## Problem

The Automation Engine kept its spam guards only in memory: the last-fire times behind `cooldownSeconds` / `cooldownScope`, and the fire times behind `rateLimit { maxActions, windowSeconds }`. Restarting the process wiped them, so every rule was armed again. Disabling and then re-enabling a rule did the same thing, because `load()` dropped state for rules that were not loaded. This is the bug from Mesh impact checklist §3.

## Fix

- A new table, `automation_fire_state` (migration 219 on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL, built with the idempotent helpers). It is global with no `sourceId`, the same as `automations`. Rows:
  - `kind='cooldown'`: one row per (automation, cooldown key). The key is what `cooldownKeyFor()` returns: `''`, a node, or `source:node`. `firedAt` holds the last fire in ms.
  - `kind='rate'`: one row per automation. `events` holds a JSON array of the fire times still inside the window. It never holds more than `maxActions` entries.
  - A unique index on (automationId, kind, scopeKey). The table is listed in `BACKUP_TABLES` and in the CLI `TABLE_ORDER`.
- `AutomationFireStateRepository` uses Drizzle only and has no raw SQL.
- Engine changes:
  - Each fire queues a write. Writes run in order on one promise chain, and a fire never waits for one. If a write fails, the engine logs it and the in-memory guard still holds.
  - `load()` runs on startup and after every save, enable, disable and delete. Before the new index goes live, it waits for queued writes to finish, then restores the stored rows for live rules. For a cooldown it keeps the later of the memory and disk times, so restoring can only hold a rule back, never fire it. It also deletes rows that belong to deleted rules, rows older than the rule's current window, and rows of a kind the rule no longer uses.
  - A stored time later than now (the clock stepped back) is treated as now, so it holds for one window instead of until the clock catches up.
  - When the key set overflows and gets trimmed, the matching stored rows are deleted with one ranged delete.
  - `runNow` on a disabled rule reads that rule's rows first, so a manual fire still respects the cooldown after a restart.
- The `DELETE /api/automations/:id` route deletes the rule's rows. `load()` also clears leftover rows, for example from the auto-ack converter's delete or from a write that was still queued when the rule was deleted.
- Behaviour:
  - A restart is never a fire. Loading state only reads and fires nothing.
  - Disabling and re-enabling a rule keeps its last fire.
  - Saving a rule (same id) keeps its last fire.
  - Deleting a rule removes its rows.
  - Changing `cooldownScope` changes the key format, so the rule starts fresh under the new scope. That is what happened before this change too. The old keys expire and get pruned.

No limits, defaults or UI change. This only persists state that already existed.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. This change adds no packets and no timers. Th

title: fix(automations): make telemetry triggers fire, with a per-node hourly floor and loop guard
body:
## Summary

`trigger.telemetry` ("Telemetry is received") has never fired. The engine handles `telemetry:batch` by calling `onTelemetry`, but only `dataEventEmitter.emitTelemetry` schedules that event, and nothing has ever called it. #1186 added the method with no caller; the Automation Engine (#3653) built on it. The Automation Tester builds telemetry contexts directly, so a test showed "matched" while live readings never arrived.

This PR wires the emitter and adds the safety rails the user chose:

- **Emit from ingest.** Meshtastic TCP (`saveTelemetryMetrics`, every TELEMETRY_APP reading) and Meshtastic MQTT (`TELEMETRY_APP` ingest) emit each stored reading. Only live readings count: firmware 2.8 NodeDB replays (hourly and on every reconnect) and stale frames are stored but not emitted, so automations never fire on old values.
- **(a) Floor.** The engine raises any `trigger.telemetry` cooldown below 3600 s to 3600 s, per node (`effectiveTelemetryCooldown` in `src/types/automation.ts`). `sourceNode` becomes `node`, so one node heard on two sources fires once. A user-set whole-automation window is kept, since it is stricter. The cooldown field's help reads "Telemetry triggers are limited to once per node per hour."
- **(b) Loop guard.** Every telemetry request we send (`sendTelemetryRequest` incl. hijack retries, `requestLocalStats`, remote LocalStats) is remembered by packet id in `src/server/services/ownTelemetryRequests.ts` (process-wide, 10 min TTL, 1024 cap). A reading whose `decoded.requestId` matches one is flagged `answersOwnRequest` and never fires a telemetry trigger, on the TCP source or on an MQTT source that hears the same reply. This breaks the `telemetry → action.requestData(telemetry)` loop, which the #3914 guard can't catch because the reply comes from a remote node.
- **(c) Notice.** A one-time, dismissible notice on the Automations page lists saved automations that use the telemetry trigger, marks disabled ones, and explains that they did not fire before, fire now, and are capped at once per node per hour. Dismissal is stored per browser (localStorage).
- **(d) LocalStats exemption.** LocalStats readings (`noiseFloor`, uptime, packet counters) skip the #3914 self-origin guard, but only for telemetry triggers. Only our own node produces them, so the Device Health "High noise floor" alert could never fire otherwise. Our own device/environment telemetry and our own text stay blocked. The loop guard still applies to LocalStats.

### Sites not wired, and why

| Site | Why skipped |
|---|---|
| `transportTrafficService.ts` | Our own derived transport counters (`systemPacketsRx*`), not a node's telemetry reading. |
| MeshCore poller / remote-telemetry scheduler | Every reading answers a request we sent (poll or `req_telemetry_sync`), the same class as the loop guard. Rows use `mc_*` names and a synthesized nodeNum the Meshtastic-shaped trigger can't resolve. |
| `meshcoreMqttManager` observer noise floor | MeshCore, `mc_status_noise_

title: perf(poll): send only what changed since the client's last poll
body:
## Problem

`/api/poll` sends every node of a source on every tick, though most nodes have not changed since the last one. Measured on origin/main (7fbb308eb, after #6023-#6032), the node list is about 95% of each reply:

| Source | Nodes | Full reply (raw / on the wire) | Server time |
|---|---|---|---|
| MT (TCP) | 933 | 922 KB / 114 KB | 144-154 ms |
| MT 2 (TCP) | 1039 | 1012 KB / 124 KB | 148-154 ms |
| MQTT 3 | 3292 | 2822 KB / 309 KB | 279-286 ms |
| Florida MQTT | 5760 | 4735 KB / 480 KB | 278 ms |
| MQTT 6 | 6462 | 5464 KB / 553 KB | 409-427 ms |

A source page polls every 30 s with the socket up and every 5 s without it. In the browser, the MT nodes page fetched 16.5 MB of poll replies (2.0 MB on the wire) in 90 idle seconds without the socket, and 2.8 MB (340 KB on the wire) with it. The client parses all of it, and TanStack's structural sharing then deep-compares all of it against the cached copy.

## Fix

The client opts in by sending a `cursor`: an empty one on its first poll, then the `pollCursor` from the reply it last merged. The server then sends only what changed since that reply:

- the nodes whose content changed, with their current content;
- `removedNodes`: nodeNums gone since the cursor (deleted, purged, or hidden by a permission change);
- `nodeOrder`: every nodeNum in reply order, only when the order changed;
- `unchangedSections`: sections the client already holds, which are left out of the reply (messages, channels, traceroutes, telemetryNodes, ...).

**Server** (`src/server/services/pollDeltaTracker.ts`). The route still builds the full, permission-filtered reply exactly as before. It does not read any `updatedAt` column or keep a change journal fed from the node write paths. The tracker keeps, per (user, source), a hash and a "changed in version" number for each node, for the order, and for each section, plus a timestamped tombstone for each removed node. It folds each build into that history and answers the cursor from it. This approach has three consequences:
- No write path can be missed: whatever changes the built reply (position, telemetry, user info, favourite/ignore, keys, overrides, estimates, sign-flip correction, deletes) changes a hash.
- Permissions work the same way: a delta only ever carries content from the current filtered build. A node that a revoked grant hides leaves the build and goes out as a removal. A node that a new grant shows arrives as an addition. No permissions hash is needed.
- The client gets the full reply when the cursor is missing, from another epoch (server restart or evicted state), older than a pruned tombstone (15 min TTL), or when the build has two rows with the same nodeNum.

Callers that send no `cursor` get the old reply byte for byte, with no new keys. This covers ImportConfigModal, embeds, scripts and the system tests. Memory use: at most 100 states, each about 100 bytes per node; a state idle for 10 min is dropped. Each reply is now serialized from per-node and per-section

title: perf(messages): memoize message rows and virtualize long MeshCore lists
body:
## Problem

Measured on current main (7fbb308eb, Phase 1 and 2 merged) with Puppeteer: commits, and the components each commit really rendered.

- **Channel view.** Each live update rebuilds every message from fresh JSON (new objects, new `Date`s), and App passes new `getNodeName`/`getNodeShortName` functions on every render. The rows were inline JSX in one `.map`, so every update redrew every row. Sitting 20 s on a 39-row channel: **8,670–9,391 component renders** on desktop and **8,670** on a phone at 4x CPU. Each row rendered **12 times** (`sender-name` 468 renders for 39 rows) with no new messages.
- Each row also ran `list.filter(isTapbackOf)` and `list.find(isReplyTo)` over the whole conversation: O(n²) per render.
- The DM view (MessagesTab) and the unified messages page had the same inline-row pattern.
- `useChannels()` and `useUnreadCountsFromPoll()` returned a new `[]` / `{}` on every render while the poll had no data.
- **MeshCore lists** rendered every row. MC-Sandbox (757 nodes, 300 after the age filter) put **7,700 DOM elements** on the Nodes page and 2,376 on Node Details. On a phone at 4x CPU, scrolling the Nodes list had 2 long tasks and a worst frame gap of 98 ms.

## Fix

- **Memoized message rows**: `DmMessageRow`, `ChannelMessageRow` (`src/components/messages/`) and `UnifiedMessageRow` (inside `UnifiedMessagesPage`). The markup moved over unchanged. Scrolling and loading older messages live in the container and are untouched.
  - Props compare **by value** (`messageRowPropsEqual`: primitives, `Date` by time, arrays and plain objects a few levels deep). A re-fetched but unchanged message counts as equal.

title: perf(socket): push MQTT node updates over the socket, coalesced per source
body:
## Problem

MQTT ingest (`mqtt_bridge` and `mqtt_broker`, both through `mqttIngestion.ts`) writes node rows (lastHeard, position) on every NodeInfo, position, text and telemetry packet, but it raised no socket event for them. Only `message:new` went out. An MQTT source view therefore saw node changes only on the 30 s backup poll.

Measured on the dev container running clean `origin/main` (one Socket.IO client per source, `join-source`, 300 s):

| Source (type) | node rows changed in 5 min | node events on socket | socket events/min | bytes/min |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yeraze MQTT Broker (`mqtt_broker`) | 56 | 0 | 0.6 | 184 |
| Official MQTT (`mqtt_bridge`) | 54 | 0 | 0.6 | 184 |
| Sandbox (`meshtastic_tcp`) | 6 | 2 `node:updated` | 1.0 | 177 |
| MC-Sandbox (`meshcore`) | n/a | `meshcore:*` | 1.4 | 474 |

### What emits what (investigation)

| Path | Socket events raised | Node freshness on socket |
|---|---|---|
| Meshtastic TCP (`meshtasticManager`) | `node:updated` (position, NodeInfo, key state), `message:new`, `connection:status`, `traceroute:complete`, `routing:update`, `client-notification`; admin-only `node:discovered/mobility/rebooted/powerChanged` | yes, per packet |
| MQTT bridge + broker (`mqttIngestion`) | `message:new` only | **none (fixed here)** |
| MeshCore companion (`meshcoreManager`) | `meshcore:*` incl. `meshcore:contact:updated` (already batched 1 s) | yes |
| MeshCore over MQTT (`meshcoreMqttManager`) | `meshcore:message` only | none (not in scope) |
| Reticulum | `reticulum:message`, delivery state | n/a |

Client: `useWebSocket` merges `node:updated` into the per-source poll cache, appends `message:new`, and invalidates poll (debounced) on `routing:update` / `telemetry:batch`. `useMeshCore` / `useReticulum` handle their own events. Source views `join-source`; unified views `join-all-sources`. Subscription and per-event gating already work as intended.

## Fix

- New UI-only event `node:batch`: `dataEventEmitter.emitNodeBatchUpdate(nodeNum, fields, sourceId)` queues changed fields per node and sends **one merged event per source every 2 s** (`NODE_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS`). Repeated updates to one node merge, latest value wins; `undefined` fields are dropped; `flushPending()` flushes it on shutdown.
- MQTT ingest queues `lastHeard` on NodeInfo / text / telemetry and `lastHeard` + `latitude/longitude/altitude` on position (same fields the TCP position path sends). Ignored, geo-ignored and distance-dropped senders return before this, so they queue nothing.
- Gate (`socketEventGates.ts`): per node, same rule as `node:updated` (`channel_N:viewOnMap` on the node's last-heard channel, no row = withheld, private override removed without `nodes_private:read`), checked on the event's own source. The facts load once per event, only when a non-admin is subscribed.

title: perf(dashboard): do the dashboard age cut in SQL
body:
## Problem

With `?ageWindow=settings` (#6032), the dashboard bundles send only the nodes the map can draw: 3,746 of 18,464 rows on the dev data set. But the server still reads, masks and maps all 18k rows, then drops 80% of them in memory. On current main (7fbb308eb) that costs **339 ms server p50** per call, and `/api/health` stalls for **311 ms (p95)** while dashboard calls run back to back.

## Fix

Push the age cut into the node read (Meshtastic sources; MeshCore nodes come from the manager, not this table, and still go through the in-memory pass unchanged).

- **Two steps, keyed by nodeNum.** One query finds the nodeNums with at least one row in the selected sources that is heard inside the window (plus the 1 h grace), a favourite, an aged-out aircraft, or a local node. Each source's read then takes every row of those nodes (`nodeNum IN (...)`). A node kept because any of its rows passes keeps all its rows, as #6032 requires. `nodeNum` is the unified key (`mt:<nodeNum>`) of every Meshtastic DB row.
- **Superset, then the same exact pass.** The SQL step picks a superset of what `applyDashboardAgeWindow` keeps: it ignores channel visibility, floors the cutoff, and takes the time before the in-memory pass does. `applyDashboardAgeWindow` still runs on the result unchanged, so the output is exactly #6032's.
- **One scan, not one per source.** The live nodeNums are found once per request and bound as a list into each per-source read. Above 5,000 live nodes (`DASHBOARD_LIVE_NODE_LIST_MAX`, well under every backend's bind limit) each read uses the same query as a subquery instead.
- **`nodeCount` stays the uncut total.** A `GROUP BY channel` count goes through the same `filterNodesByChannelPermission` (one stand-in row per channel; the filter reads only `channel`), plus the synthesized local node when there is one.
- **Order.** `getAllNodes` now breaks `updatedAt` ties on `nodeNum`, so the filtered read (a different query plan) returns rows in the same order as the full one. Before this, the order among rows with an identical `updatedAt` was undefined.
- **No flag, no change.** Without `ageWindow=settings` nothing new runs. Map Analysis still loads the full bundle.
- **Index check.** On the dev DB (17.7k rows, 6 sources) SQLite uses `idx_nodes_source_id` for the live-nodeNum scan, the `(nodeNum, sourceId)` primary key for the per-source read, and `idx_nodes_source_id` for the count. A `(sourceId, lastHeard)` index does not help: the OR with favourite / aircraft / local still needs every row of the source. No migration.

## Before / after

Dev container, `build --no-cache`, same data set, deployed and measured back to back in one lock hold: a clean `origin/main` worktree (7fbb308eb, #6032 merged), then this branch. `GET /api/unified/dashboard?sources=<all 8>&ageWindow=settings`, admin. Scripts are in `perf/p3-dashsql/`; the main numbers are in `perf/p3-baseline/dashsql-main-*.json`.

title: perf(dashboard): leave out nodes the dashboard map hides by age
body:
## Problem

After #6028, `GET /api/unified/dashboard` still sends every node row ever heard. On the dev data set (8 sources, current main dce67a5ee) it returns 18,457 rows, 19.9 MB raw (1.79 MB gzip), and the server takes ~520 ms per call. The dashboard map then drops most of them: it shows only nodes heard inside the node-age setting (36 h here), plus favourites. Only 3,784 rows belong to a node the map can draw; the other 14,674 rows (80%) are parsed, merged and thrown away by the client every 15 s.

## Fix

`?ageWindow=settings` on both dashboard bundles (`/api/unified/dashboard`, `/api/sources/:id/dashboard`) drops node rows the map would hide by age. No new setting.

- **Window:** the existing `maxNodeAgeHours` (and the MeshCore `maxInfraNodeAgeHours` for repeaters / room servers). The map uses the widest value across every source in view (`useMaxNodeAgeHoursAcross`), so the server takes the widest across **every** configured source (per-source row, else global row, else default, like `GET /api/settings?sourceId`), never less than the default (what the client uses while its settings queries load), and 0 on any source turns the cut off. A 1 h grace covers the gap between the server's clock and the client's render. The setting is a per-source server setting, so no query param carries it.
- **Slider:** the Map Features age slider can only narrow the window (`MapAgeFilterControl`, `effectiveMapMaxAgeHours`), never widen it, so the setting is the upper bound and the slider keeps working unchanged.
- **Kept regardless of age:** favourites, aged-out aircraft (they bypass the map's gate), and every source's local node (the polar grid centres on it even when stale).
- **Cross-source:** the decision is made per node, keyed exactly like the client merge (`unifiedNodeKey`). If any row of a node passes, every row of that node is kept across all sources. The merged node takes its `lastHeard` as the max, `isFavorite` as an OR, and its position from whichever row has one, so dropping an old row of a live node could move or hide its marker.
- **Opt-in:** only `DashboardPage` sends the flag (`DASHBOARD_DATA_OPTIONS`). Without it the bundles are byte-for-byte what they were. **Map Analysis does not send it**: its markers have no age gate (they fade by a time slider) and its traceroute / neighbour layers resolve endpoints of any age from these nodes. Keeping it on the full bundle is the simplest way to keep every Map Analysis view identical; the flag is part of the query key, so the two pages never share a cache entry by mistake.
- **Node totals:** the sidebar showed `nodes.length` for the selected single source. The bundle now carries `nodeCount` (rows before the cut) and the page uses it, so that total does not shrink. Other totals come from `/status` and `/api/unified/status` and are unchanged.

title: fix: recognize proxy-signed-in users on the first auth status request
body:
A browser that has signed in through Cloudflare Access or oauth2-proxy can request `/api/auth/status` before any other API endpoint. The status route reads the session without first running authentication middleware, so a fresh session is reported as `authenticated: false` despite the proxy supplying an identity. The UI consequently shows the login screen instead of recognizing the signed-in user and their administrator role.

Run the existing `optionalAuth()` middleware on the status route so it checks the proxy identity and binds the user to the session before status is read. This reuses the existing group checks, provisioning, role refresh and session-fixation protection. Login, logout and OIDC callback middleware are unchanged.

Twelve regression cases use the real SQLite route harness and authentication/session middleware, with harness-wide authentication disabled to reproduce the route's behavior. They cover first-request proxy sign-in, session rotation, role changes, denied groups, disabled provisioning, local/OIDC fallback, anonymous access and logout isolation. The Cloudflare fixture exercises claim extraction under the existing trusted-proxy model; it does not test cryptographic JWT validation.

### Validation

- Rebased onto `f9880bb12`; all 84 tests across the four authentication suites pass, including all 12 new regression cases.
- Against the original unchanged upstream base, the new regression suite produced 6 failures and 6 passes; all 12 pass with the fix.
- Production typecheck, `lint:ci`, frontend build, server build and diff whitespace checks pass on the rebased branch.
- An earlier full-suite run on the original base reported 32,433 passing, 50 failing and 1,765 pending tests. The 49 decoder failures reproduced on unchanged upstream and disappeared on both checkouts after building the missing `zstd-napi` dependency. The polling failure also reproduced on unchanged upstream and was intermittent. Both implicated suites subsequently passed all 93 tests on both checkouts.
- The full suite was not rerun after rebasing. Docker system tests and physical-device acceptance have not been performed.

title: perf(render): keep compose draft and map view out of app-wide contexts
body:
## Problem

Measured on current main (f9880bb12, Phase 1 merged) with Puppeteer, counting React commits and the components each commit really rendered (bailed-out subtrees skipped):

- **Typing 20 characters in a DM** re-rendered about **2,900 components per keystroke** on desktop (58,500 in total, 551 ms of script). The draft (`newMessage`) lived in `MessagingContext`, and App reads that context, so each keystroke re-rendered App and most of the tree. On a phone at 4x CPU slowdown: 494 ms of script and 368 ms TBT for 20 characters.
- **Panning the map** wrote `mapCenter` into `MapContext` on every `moveend`. App and about 10 other components read that context, so each pan re-rendered all of them.
- `useTelemetryNodes` built four new `Set`s on every render, and `useDeviceNodes` built a new one on every render with data. Every memo keyed on them recomputed each time.
- The node list sort computed each node's key twice per comparison. With hop sorting in traceroute mode, each key scans and JSON-parses every traceroute: O(n log n × traceroutes).

## Fix

- **Compose draft → `src/contexts/composeDraftStore.ts`**, a small external store (`useSyncExternalStore`), one per `MessagingProvider`. The new **`MessageComposeInput`** (text box, byte counter, mentions, emoji and send buttons) is the **only** component that subscribes to it. MessagesTab and ChannelsTab no longer take `newMessage`/`setNewMessage` props. They read the draft once, without subscribing, for the bell and translate actions. App's send handlers read it at send time. `MessagingContext` keeps a stable `setNewMessage`. All #4183 draft-scoping behaviour stays the same: clear on conversation switch, `openDmWithDraft` prefill, and `openDmForCompose` plus the compose-focus callback ref.
- **Map centre/zoom → `src/contexts/mapViewStore.ts`**, one store per `MapProvider`, still saved to localStorage under the same `mapCenter`/`mapZoom` keys. `MapPositionHandler` and `ZoomHandler` write to it without subscribing. Nothing subscribes to the centre: NodesTab reads it only to seed a newly mounted map, and `BaseMap`/`Map3DView` treat centre as mount-only. Zoom readers subscribe to the threshold they draw against: NodesTab to `zoom >= 13` (labels) and `zoom >= neighborInfoMinZoom`, App via `useSourceView` to `zoom < TRACEROUTE_LOW_ZOOM` (8). As a side effect, the `useTraceroutePaths` memo now rebuilds only when that threshold flips, not on every zoom step.
- `useTelemetryNodes` / `useDeviceNodes` return the same `Set` until the list contents change. The empty-poll fallback is kept.
- New helper `sortNodesByField` (`src/utils/nodeSort.ts`) computes each key once (decorate, sort, undecorate) and uses one shared `Intl.Collator`. A test checks that it matches the old comparator exactly, tie order included.

body:

| Messages (`/source/:id/messages`) | 1483 KB | 89 |
| Dashboard (`/`) | 785 KB | 53 |

Static closure from the build (raw / gzip): the source app (`App` chunk plus static imports) was 5002 / 1357 KB. `App-*.js` alone was 1331 KB raw, and `BaseMap-*.js` (mostly maplibre-gl) was 1217 KB raw.

## Fix

- **Tabs are lazy chunks.** `src/appTabs.ts` holds each tab as a `lazyWithPreload(() => import(...))`. `App` renders the tab `<Routes>` inside one `<Suspense>` with a small pane placeholder (`RouteLoading variant="pane"`), so the header and sidebar stay in place. Routes, URLs, `VALID_TABS` and what each tab renders are unchanged.
- **No waterfall on landing.** `SourceApp` (main.tsx) calls `preloadAppTabForPath(splat)`, so the landing tab's chunk downloads alongside `App`'s own chunk instead of after it.
- **Prefetch on intent.** `SourceNav` items take an optional `onIntent`, called on pointerenter and focus. The sidebar uses it to preload that tab's chunk.
- **MapLibre on demand.** `BaseMap` lazy-loads `VectorTileLayer` only when a vector tileset draws, and `Map3DView` lazy-loads `Base3DMap` only in 3D. The WebGL fallback path is unchanged: the probe and `vectorSupport` still decide before the lazy layer is asked for.
- **recharts on demand.** The DM pane's graphs in `MessagesTab` are lazy. The traceroute segment SNR chart moved out of `useTraceroutePaths` into `components/SegmentSnrChart.tsx` and loads with the first popup that draws it. `DISTRIBUTION_COLORS`/`ChartDataEntry` moved to a chart-free `packetStatsChartData.ts`; `PacketStatsChart` still re-exports both.
- **Config search on demand.** `ConfigSearchHost` keeps only the shortcut and the open state. The palette (`ConfigSearchPanel`: section catalogue plus modal) loads on the first open.
- **Stale chunks after a deploy.** The existing `vite:preloadError` reload-once handler moves from main.tsx to `utils/chunkReload.ts`, unchanged except for one fix: it now reads `sessionStorage` lazily, so blocked storage can't throw at startup. Each tab is still wrapped in its own `ErrorBoundary`.

### CSS cascade (the eager-CSS plugin)

All page CSS has to stay in the entry sheet in its pre-split order (#5558). The `meshmonitor-eager-css` walk now also follows `lazyWithPreload(() => import('x'))` calls, at their source position. A plain `lazy()` inside a page is still not followed. Each split-out component's lazy declaration sits where its static import was, so the walk order is the same.

title: perf(dashboard): leave unread node fields out of the dashboard bundles
body:
## Problem

`GET /api/unified/dashboard` (polled every 15 s by the dashboard and every Map Analysis layer) sent every node column for every node. Measured on current main (f9880bb12) against the dev data set (8 sources, ~18k node rows):

| Section | Bytes |
|---|---|
| nodes | 35,080 KB (17,962 rows, 93 keys each) |
| traceroutes | 94 KB |
| neighborInfo | 8 KB |
| channels | 5 KB |

Nodes are 99.7% of the body. Per-field bytes are spread evenly: most of a node is key names and `null`s across 93 columns. 37 of those columns are read only by the Nodes, Messages and Security tabs, which load nodes from their own endpoints. No dashboard consumer reads them.

Server cost per call: ~770 ms, and the event loop stalls ~600 ms each time (every `/api/health` probe that overlapped a dashboard call took >500 ms).

## Fix

- `src/utils/dashboardNodeFields.ts`: the list of 37 omitted fields (key and packet-rate checks, position detail and raw override columns, admin and housekeeping columns, `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, `macaddr`, ...). A comment explains why each group is unused and says to remove a field from the list before a dashboard view reads it.
- `buildSourceNodes(source, user, { slim: true })`, used by both dashboard bundles (`/api/unified/dashboard` and `/api/sources/:id/dashboard`):
  - reads the nodes table without the omitted columns (`getAllNodes(sourceId, { omitColumns })`, a Drizzle column subset, all three backends). Columns the filter/mask steps still need (`positionChannel`, the override columns, `positionOverrideIsPrivate`, `aircraftFixed*`) are still read.
  - runs channel filtering, position masking, the override step, sign-flip correction and the asset overlay unchanged, then drops the omitted fields from each node.
- `GET /api/sources/:id/nodes` is unchanged and still returns every field.

How the "no consumer reads it" list was built: for each column I listed every client file that references it, then checked whether that file handles nodes from `useDashboardUnifiedData` / `useDashboardSourceData` (DashboardPage, DashboardMap, its popups and `nodeCardModel`, the Map Analysis layers and inspector, `useOwnNodePositions`, `mergeUnifiedSourceData`). Fields with any reference on that path stay (for example `notes`, `firstHeard`, `nodeStatus`, `lastMessageHops`, `positionLocationSource`, all aircraft fields the merge or popup reads).

**Age filter:** not applied (see Not in scope). The dashboard map hides nodes older than the window, but other consumers of the same hook don't use the same rule (favorite bypass, infra age, map age slider, traceroute and neighbor endpoints in Map Analysis), so a server cutoff would change what some views show.

**Cache:** not added. Profiling the build on a copy of the dev DB: `getAllNodes` for all sources costs ~200 ms (raw SQL 67 ms, Drizzle row mapping ~100 ms, `normalizeBigInts` ~40 ms), `JSON.stringify` 61 ms. One browser polls every 15 s, so a few-second TTL cache would almost never hit, and on a busy mesh

title: perf(telemetry): cache date formatters, memoize chart data, drop dots/animation on large series
body:
## Problem

The MT Info tab (telemetry charts) was the slowest page change in the perf pass (main @ 2474890b2):

| MT Info | settle | TBT | longest task | script |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| desktop | 4.35 s | 1,545 ms | 527 ms | 3,270 ms |
| mobile, 4x CPU | 10.5 s | 7,293 ms | 2,834 ms | 8,324 ms |

A trace of the page change put **901–1,222 ms** of self time in `formatTime` (`toLocaleTimeString` with options builds a new `Intl.DateTimeFormat` per call, once per data point, on every render) and ~460 ms in recharts' line animation (`getTotalLength`). Every chart also drew one SVG marker per point (115k dot renders).

## Fix

- **`src/utils/datetime.ts`**: `getCachedDateTimeFormat(locale, options)` keeps one `Intl.DateTimeFormat` per (locale, options); `formatTime` uses it. Output is identical (same `en-US` locale, same 12/24 h options, runtime time zone); an invalid date still returns `"Invalid Date"` rather than throwing. Every `formatTime` caller (`formatDateTime`, `formatMessageTime`, `formatChartAxisTimestamp`, …) gets the speed-up for free.
- **`TelemetryGraphs`** (Info tab, MT and MeshCore node details): `prepareChartData` / `groupByType` are now pure module functions; the widget builds its points (incl. paxcounter merge + display scale) in a `useMemo` keyed on its inputs, and the parent memoizes the per-type grouping so each widget keeps the same series arrays across renders. Stable empty defaults replace `= []` / `= new Map()` so they don't break the memo.
- **`TelemetryChart`** (dashboard widgets): same memoization, moved above the early returns.
- **Markers**: `telemetryMarkerRadius` now returns line-only above `MAX_MARKER_POINTS = 100`, measured or not (#5196's width scaling still applies below that). `activeDot` is unchanged, so hover/tooltip still highlights the point. The dashboard `TelemetryChart` (fixed `r: 3`) and the MeshCore Info view (fixed `r: 2`) now drop markers above the same threshold.
- **Animation off** (`isAnimationActive={false}`) on the telemetry series in `TelemetryGraphs`, `TelemetryChart` and `PacketRateGraphs` (also on the Info tab). `CombinedTelemetryChart` and the MeshCore view already had it off.

Visual change: series with more than 100 points render as a plain line (no dots), and lines appear at once instead of drawing in.

## Before / after

Puppeteer `runtime/nav.cjs` (trimmed to Nodes → Info → Settings), dev container, same DB. "Before" = the perf-pass baseline on main 2474890b2; "after" = this branch, two runs each.

| MT Info | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| desktop settle | 4,353 ms | 3,491–3,551 ms |
| desktop TBT | 1,545 ms | 466–482 ms |
| desktop longest task | 527 ms | 251–254 ms |
| desktop script time | 3,270 ms | 1,232–1,275 ms |
| desktop DOM nodes | 5,159 | 3,847 |
| mobile 4x settle | 10,523 ms | 5,227–6,226 ms |
| mobile 4x TBT | 7,293 ms | 2,919–2,931 ms |
| mobile 4x longest task | 2,834 ms | 1,336–1,515 ms |

title: perf(dashboard): fetch once after auth, memoize merge and markers
body:
## Problem

Measured on the dev container (main 2474890b2, Unified dashboard, ~975 node markers, 34 MB `/api/unified/dashboard` payload):

- **Every signed-in load fetched `/api/unified/dashboard` twice.** The dashboard and status query keys include `isAuthenticated`. The queries fired with `false` before auth resolved, then again with `true`. Auth resolved late because `AuthProvider.refreshAuth` waited on a serial `/api/users/:id/channel-database-permissions` call before it set the auth status.
- **`mergeUnifiedSourceData` ran on every DashboardPage render** (108-246 ms each). It sat outside any memo, so each of the ~10 staggered 15 s queries re-ran it.
- **Every render re-rendered every marker.** The fresh `nodes` array broke every memo in `DashboardMap`. Marker descriptors, `position` tuples and `<Popup>` children were rebuilt, so all ~975 `<Marker>`s rendered on every commit (21k marker renders in 35 s idle in the perf pass).

## Fix

1. **Auth gate** (`useDashboardData.ts`): the auth-keyed queries (`useSourceStatuses`, `useUnifiedStatus`, `useDashboardSourceData`, `useDashboardUnifiedData`) set `enabled` only after auth resolves (`loading === false`). The keys still include `isAuthenticated`, so login and logout still refetch.
2. **AuthContext** sets the auth status as soon as `/api/auth/status` answers. Channel-database permissions load after it, without blocking. No frontend code reads `channelDbPermissions` / `hasChannelDbPermission` outside the context. Until the permissions arrive, `hasChannelDbPermission` denies non-admins, the same answer it gave when that fetch failed. A sequence guard stops a slow reply from an older refresh from overwriting a newer status.
3. **Memoized merge**: `useDashboardUnifiedData` keys on a string of the source fields the merge reads, not on the caller's fresh `sources` array, and wraps the merge in `useMemo` on the query data. A per-node merge cache reuses a node's merged object when its input records are the same objects. TanStack's structural sharing keeps an unchanged record's reference across polls, so unchanged nodes keep their identity. The nodes array keeps its reference too when nothing changed. The return object is memoized.
   - I kept `structuralSharing` on. Turning it off would save its ~110 ms per refetch, but every node would come back as a new object, which would defeat the per-node cache and the marker memo below. That would cost more than it saves.
4. **Stable markers**:
   - `DashboardMap` memoizes the descriptor list and reuses each descriptor, `<Popup>` element included, while the node object, position, opacity and pin settings are unchanged.
   - Age opacity rounds to 0.01, a change you cannot see, so a 15 s poll doesn't give every marker a new opacity.
   - `DashboardPage.handleNodeSourceSelect` is now a `useCallback`.
   - The shared `NodeMarkersLayer` renders each marker through a `memo` wrapper and caches the below-zoom-gate click wrapper per key, so an unchanged marker skips. Other

title: perf(http): compress responses and cache hashed assets
body:
## Problem

No response was compressed: the server had no compression middleware. Hashed `/assets/*` files and `locales/*.json` went out with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0`, so every load revalidated them.

Measured on main (2474890b2) against the dev container (8 sources):
- A cold, signed-in load moved **75.4 MB**. Most of it is the unified dashboard JSON, **36.3 MB** per call, fetched twice.
- A cold anonymous load moved 32.7 MB.
- `BaseMap-*.js` 1.25 MB, `main-*.css` 663 KB, `locales/en.json` 585 KB, all uncompressed.

## Fix

- `src/server/middleware/httpCompression.ts`: the `compression` middleware (MIT, pure JS, so fine on armv7 and desktop), mounted right after `helmet` in `server.ts`.
  - Threshold 1 KB. gzip level 6 (zlib default). Browsers that offer brotli get brotli at the library's quality 4. Higher levels cost far more CPU on 30 MB+ payloads for a few percent less output.
  - Skipped: `Content-Disposition: attachment` downloads (the packet/MeshCore/message exports write rows with `res.write()` and wait on `drain`; `compression` moves `res.on('drain')` onto its zlib stream but not `res.off('drain')`, so a long export would pile up listeners), `text/event-stream`, types `compressible` doesn't list (images, gzip/zip backups, octet-stream), and requests with `x-no-compression`.
  - socket.io is untouched: it attaches to the HTTP server and answers its own path before Express runs.
- `src/server/staticServing.ts`:
  - `/assets/*` (content-hashed) → `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
  - HTML shell (index, SPA deep links, embed page), `sw.js`, `registerSW.js`, `manifest.webmanifest`, `locales/*.json` → `no-cache` (ETag revalidation). Locales are not hashed, so they are not made immutable.
  - Other files (favicon, logos) keep the express default.
  - Works for both the `BASE_URL` and root branches; paths are matched relative to the build dir.
- Service worker: Workbox precaches with its own revision keys and only runtime-caches navigations, `/api` (NetworkOnly) and map tiles, so nothing changes there. `sw.js` is `no-cache`, so the update flow still sees new builds.
- Desktop (Tauri) runs the same `dist/server/server.js` under bundled Node, with `npm ci --omit=dev`; `compression` is a runtime dependency, so it ships.
- Docs: `docs/configuration/reverse-proxy.md` gets a "Compression and Caching" section: proxy compression is optional now (harmless if left on), and don't override these `Cache-Control` headers.

## Before / after

**Before** (main 2474890b2, live dev container, from the perf pass):

| | Wire size |
|---|---|
| Cold signed-in load, total | 75.4 MB |
| Cold anonymous load, total | 32.7 MB |
| `/api/unified/dashboard` (8 sources), per call | 36.3 MB |
| `assets/*` and `locales/en.json` Cache-Control | `public, max-age=0` |

**After (offline, same settings as the middleware)**: the saved 36.31 MB dashboard payload from that pass, compressed in Node:

| | Wire size | CPU per call (median of 3) |
|---|---|---|
| gzip level

title: perf(server): stop loading every node for unread, unified-message and trail polls
body:
## Problem

Three polled routes loaded every node on a source (~17k rows through Drizzle and `normalizeBigInts`) to answer a small question. Measured on the dev container at `2474890b2`, p50 of 5 warm runs:

| Route | p50 | Poll |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/messages/unread-counts?sourceId=…` | 100 ms (max 1197) | every 10 s per source page |
| `/api/messages/first-unread?sourceId=…` | 91 ms | same |
| `/api/unified/messages?channel=Primary&limit=100` | 246 ms (empty result) | every 10 s |
| `/api/unified/messages?limit=100` | 354 ms (100 rows) | every 10 s |
| `/api/aircraft/trails?hours=168` | 379 ms (7 trails) | dashboard |

The unread SQL itself takes 0.7 ms. The rest was `visibleDmSenders()` calling `getAllNodesAsync(sourceId)` just to build a set of node ids. Unified messages called `nodes.getAllNodes(source.id)` per source only to name senders. Aircraft trails let `buildPositionFilter` load every node on each source, though it only ever checks the handful of flagged aircraft.

## Fix

- **Unread / first-unread:** a new `NodesRepository.getNodeChannelsByNodeIds(nodeIds, sourceScope)` returns `{nodeId, channel}` for just the DM senders in the unread rows. `visibleDmSenders` applies the same rule as before: for an admin, any sender with a node row on the source (or on any source for the admin's every-source read); for anyone else, rows that pass `canViewNode(sourceId, channel)`. The admin still needs the lookup, because the old code also dropped DM senders with no node row, so skipping it would change output.
- **Unified messages:** sender names are resolved after the page is fetched, through the existing `getNodeNamesByNums(nums, [source.id])`, for that page's senders only. A failed lookup still logs a warning and returns the messages without names, as before. Only sender names were ever read from the map; recipients were never looked up.
- **Aircraft trails:** `buildPositionFilter` gets `nodesBySource` built from `getNodesByNums` for the flagged pairs only. The filter runs only on rows that already passed the `wanted` check, so it never looks up any other node.
- `getNodeNamesByNums` and the new method de-duplicate ids and send them in batches of 500 ids, so a large page stays under each backend's bound-parameter limit.

## Before/after

Before: the numbers above (perf baseline on `2474890b2`).

After: **not measured yet.** The deploy-and-measure run was stopped by Claude Code because the host ran low on memory while the run waited for the shared deploy lock. It never started a build. title: perf(poll): check a down source with /api/connection, not the full poll
body:
## Problem

While a source is not connected, App's connection check ran every 5 s and read the **full** `/api/poll` (nodes, messages, channels, traceroutes) just to learn the four link flags. Every always-enabled `usePoll()` observer (`useNodes`, `useChannels`, ...) also kept re-reading the same poll on its own timer and on window focus.

The Florida MQTT bridge reports `connected:false`, so its page pulled the whole poll every 5 s for as long as it stayed open (measured on main 2474890b2):

| Florida MQTT Nodes/Map, idle | requests/min to `/api/poll` | bytes/min |
|---|---|---|
| anonymous, no WebSocket (`idle-attr`) | 12 | **40.1 MB** |
| signed in, WebSocket up (`idle-idle60`) | 12 | **56.8 MB** |

### Why the bridge says `connected:false`

It is not a status-reporting bug. `MqttBridgeManager.getConnectionStatus()` returns `this.client?.isConnected()`, and the Florida bridge's upstream link is really down: `/api/sources/:id/status` shows `authStopped: true`, `upstreamConnected: false`, and the error "Broker rejected the login 5 times in a row, so this bridge stopped reconnecting." For an MQTT bridge/broker, "connected" means the broker link, and that is what it reports. The cost came from the client treating "down" as "read everything every 5 s".

## Fix

- **Status check uses `/api/connection`** (about 100 bytes; same manager lookup and address rule as the poll's `connection` section) instead of the full poll. The result is merged into the cached poll's `connection` field, so `useConnectionInfo()` and the firmware page's "gateway online" check stay current. The fetch time is kept, so the next real read is not skipped as "fresh".
- **One full poll when the source comes back** (in the "connected" transition) and on the **Retry** button. `refreshPollCache` shares a fetch with a mount-time read from the last 3 s, so this does not add a second poll at page load.
- **Backoff + hidden tab** (`useConnectionCheckLoop`): 5 s, 10 s, 20 s, then every 30 s while the result stays the same. A change resets it to 5 s. Nothing runs while `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`. When the tab becomes visible, one check runs at once and the delay resets.
- **No double polling**: `usePoll()` observers inside a `DataProvider` no longer poll on a timer or on focus while App's `connectionStatus !== 'connected'`. They still read once on mount, so cached data still shows. When connected they poll as before (30 s with socket, 5 s without). Outside a `DataProvider` nothing changes. To keep a `.tsx` file from exporting non-components, the context object moved to `src/contexts/dataContextState.ts`.

## Before / after

Measured with `runtime/idle.cjs` (60 s idle). Run on the dev container rebuilt from this branch (`--no-cache`; `/app/dist/assets/App-*.js` holds the new code). The after run was anonymous with no WebSocket, so it matches the `idle-attr` baseline conditions:

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Florida MQTT (disconnected) | 12x `/api/poll`/min, **40.1 M

title: feat(sources): configurable default Meshtastic source (#5245)
body:
Closes #5245

Adds one global, admin-only setting that picks the Meshtastic TCP source used wherever a request names no source. Empty means **Automatic**, which keeps the exact behaviour every install has today.

**Mesh impact:** none. The setting changes which configured radio a source-less send uses, not whether or how often anything is sent.

## Changes

- **Setting** `defaultMeshtasticSourceId` in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`, `ADMIN_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS` (same gate as `ductingOverlayEnabled`) and `SECRET_SETTINGS_KEYS` (non-admins never see which source it names, like `forwardingRules`).
- **Registry** (`sourceManagerRegistry.ts`): new `setPreferredMeshtasticSource()`. `getPrimaryMeshtasticSourceId()` now returns the chosen source while a `meshtastic_tcp` manager is registered under it, else the automatic first-started designation. It is computed on each read, so disable / delete / stop / re-enable need no event wiring. Callers that captured a manager keep it (atomicity rule).
- **Boot** (`bootstrapSources.ts`): reads the setting before any manager starts, so the choice wins whatever its start order.
- **Save** (`settingsRoutes.ts`): blank or the id of an existing `meshtastic_tcp` source (a disabled one is allowed: it takes over once enabled); anything else is `400 INVALID_DEFAULT_MESHTASTIC_SOURCE`. Checked only when the value changes, so a stored id whose source has since gone cannot block later Settings saves (#3806 shape). Applied to the registry live. Settings reset re-applies the stored value.
- **Status route** `GET /api/settings/default-meshtastic-source` (admin only): `{ configuredSourceId, effectiveSourceId, effectiveSourceName, mode: automatic|configured|fallback }`.
- **Source delete** clears the setting when it names the deleted source.
- **v1 `default` alias** and the legacy `first-permitted` resolver (`sourceResolver.ts`) try the chosen source first, when it is enabled and TCP; the caller still needs the permission on it, else the old walk (oldest enabled the caller can use) continues unchanged. Shared helper: `src/server/utils/defaultMeshtasticSource.ts`.
- **v1 `GET /sources`** `isPrimary` now marks the source an admin's `default` resolves to.
- **UI**: new admin-only Global Settings section `DefaultMeshtasticSourceSection` (own save bar, like `ReticulumRetentionSection`): "Automatic (first started)" plus each Meshtastic TCP source (disabled ones marked), an "Unknown source" option when the stored id no longer exists, and a status line naming what is in use now. Searchable via `configSections.ts`; en.json strings.

## Resolution order

For a request that names no source:

1. The chosen default, if a `meshtastic_tcp` manager is registered under it (enabled, auto-connected, started).
2. Otherwise Automatic: the first Meshtastic TCP source started at boot (sidebar order: `displayOrder`, then `createdAt`; the boot loop starts sources one at a time, so this is deterministic).
3. If that automatic primary was r
