title: feat(nodes): track node renames and show them in Node Details (#5862)
body:
Closes #5862.

A node's long and short names were overwritten on every NodeInfo, so a rename left no trace. Each source now logs renames, and Node Details shows a **Name History** section for Meshtastic and MeshCore nodes.

![Name History in Node Details](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/c9dba24361e44ea43023292f1135d95c4aaf1f70/name-history.png?raw=true)

## Decisions (agreed before building)
| | Choice |
|---|---|
| Retention | Newest **50** renames per node per source, trimmed on write |
| Several sources | Stored per source; Node Details **merges** every source the viewer may see the node on, collapsing one rename seen on several sources within 10 minutes ("Seen on N sources") |
| Placeholders | **Skipped**: a first real name replacing `Node !id`, `Unknown`, `Meshtastic abcd`, a last-4-hex short name or `UNK` is not a rename; neither is a real name falling back to one |

## How it works
- **Table:** migration 209 adds `node_name_history`, a per-source table. `protocol` says how to read `nodeKey`: a decimal nodeNum for Meshtastic, a public key for MeshCore. MeshCore has one name, stored in the long-name columns.
- **Write path:** the two node upserts (`NodesRepository`, `MeshCoreRepository`) already read the stored row, so they compare the old names with the values about to be stored. That one place covers TCP, MQTT, contact sync and adverts. A repeat NodeInfo, or a blank incoming name (which keeps the stored name), logs nothing. The history write is best-effort, so a failure never fails the node write.
- **Read path:** `GET /api/nodes/:nodeId/name-history`. Meshtastic uses the node list's own visibility rule (`viewOnMap` on the node's channel, per source); MeshCore uses `nodes:read`, the MeshCore node list's gate. A source the caller can't read is never included.
- **Cleanup:** history is removed with the node on node delete, node purge and source delete, and is included in system backups. Nodes removed by the inactive-node cleanup leave their history behind, at most 50 rows per node, so it's still there if the node comes back.
- **UI:** a self-fetching `NodeNameHistory` component, styled with a CSS module and theme tokens. It renders nothing until a node has been renamed, so most panels look the same, and it collapses past 5 entries. The arrow uses `UiIcon`.

## Mesh impact
None. It's passive: names are read from packets MeshMonitor already receives. It sends nothing, fires no notifications and arms no timer.

## Tests
- `nodeNameHistory.test.ts`: the rename and placeholder rules; the repo round trip, the 50-row cap, and deletes on **SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL** (migration run twice); and the upsert hooks for both protocols, including delete cleanup.
- `nodeNameHistoryMerge.test.ts`: cross-source collapse, and a repeat change outside the 10-minute window.
- `nodeNameHistoryRoutes.test.ts` (route harness): the cross-source merge; a source the caller can't see is hidden; a caller with no grants gets nothing; MeshCore `nodes:read` sc

title: fix(push): renew a rotated push subscription on its sources (#5863)
body:
Fixes #5863.

## Problem
When the browser fired `pushsubscriptionchange`, the service worker POSTed the new subscription to `/api/push/subscribe`, and the server rejected it every time, for two reasons:
- **No `sourceId`:** the route returns 400.
- **No CSRF token:** every API POST needs one, so the request failed with 403 even before the `sourceId` check. The issue doesn't mention this one.

The SW never checked `response.ok`, so it logged nothing useful. Push stopped until the user re-subscribed by hand.

## Fix
- **`POST /api/push/renew`** takes `{ oldEndpoint, subscription }`. The server looks up every row for the old endpoint, writes each row's user and source onto the new endpoint, then deletes the old rows. It writes each new row before deleting the old one, so a failure part way through never leaves the browser with no row.
- **Ownership:** a user-owned row moves only when that same user asks, so knowing someone's old endpoint can't redirect their notifications. Anonymous rows move on the endpoint alone, the same proof `/unsubscribe-all` uses. The response reports `renewed` and `skipped` counts.
- **SW (`src/utils/pushRenewal.ts`):**
  - Fetches a CSRF token, then posts the old endpoint and the new keys.
  - Uses `event.newSubscription` when the browser supplies one.
  - Throws on an HTTP error.
  - With no old endpoint there's nothing to look up, so it logs a warning. The user then re-subscribes from the Notifications tab, which already shows them as not subscribed.
  - The logic moved out of `sw.ts` so tests can drive it; Workbox doesn't load under Vitest.
- `DbPushSubscription` gains the `sourceId` field the mapper already set.

## Caveat on the reported symptom
The Discord report says push dies after **every container auto-update**. A new SW build alone doesn't normally fire `pushsubscriptionchange` (endpoint rotation and expiry do, and Firefox fires it more often than Chrome), so this fix may not explain that symptom on its own. If it persists after this ships, the next places to look are the server's 4xx cleanup in `sendToSubscription` (it deletes a subscription on any 4xx from the push service) and the browser's own console during an update.

## Mesh impact
None. This is browser-to-server only; it sends no packets and arms no timer.

## Tests
- `src/utils/pushRenewal.test.ts` (4): request shape and CSRF header, `newSubscription` reuse, HTTP-error throw, no-old-endpoint path.
- `notificationRoutes.pushPerSource.test.ts` gains three `/renew` tests on the route harness: all sources move, another user's rows don't move, and bad input is rejected.
- Full suite: 31,733 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped locally; no schema change). `tsc` clean on both configs; `lint:ci` clean.

body: Phase 2b of #5248, following #5860 (server decrypt). It makes AEAD editable on a node's own channels. ## What changed - **Device channel editor:** a new **"AEAD channel (AES-CCM, Experimental)"** checkbox, with the maintainer-approved warning under it: > **AEAD cuts this channel off from nodes that don't use it.** Nodes on older firmware, or with AEAD off, can no longer read or send on this channel, even with the same name and key. Turn it on for every node on the channel at the same time. - **Turning it on** opens a confirm dialog with the same text. **Turning it off** is always allowed, with no dialog, so a channel set by another app can be switched back. - **Gates, in the UI and on the server:** - firmware ≥ 2.8.1, through a new `supportedModules.aeadChannels` from `MeshtasticManager.supportsAeadChannels()`; - a non-empty key. `PUT /api/channels/:id` returns `400 AEAD_UNSUPPORTED` or `400 AEAD_NEEDS_KEY` and sends nothing to the radio. No timers, no retries, no notifications. - **The risk is reach, not traffic.** AEAD silently cuts off nodes without it. title: feat(channels): decrypt AEAD (AES-CCM) channels server-side (#5248 Phase 2a)
body: Phase 2a of #5248 (plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/AEAD_CHANNELS_PLAN.md`). Server-side decryption of AEAD channels from firmware 2.8.1, plus the Channel Database checkbox. The device-channel checkbox, with the warning and confirm dialog, is Phase 2b. Firmware `v2.8.1.8e6a88d` contains meshtastic/firmware#9749. I re-checked the wire format against that tag and it matches the plan. ## What changed - **Migration 208:** adds `channel_database.useAead` (boolean, not null, default false) on all three backends. `channel_database` is global, so there's no `sourceId`; it's already in `BACKUP_TABLES`. - **Hash:** an AEAD row's channel hash is `xorHash(name) ^ xorHash(psk) ^ 0xAE`. That covers name validation and hash-aware attribution: an AEAD row and a plain row with the same name and key resolve to the right row. - **Decrypt:** RFC 3610 AES-CCM with a 12-byte tag, a 13-byte nonce (the CTR nonce cut to 13 bytes), and AAD `LE32(from) ‖ LE32(to)`. - A tag failure is a clean miss. - An AEAD row is never tried with CTR, matching firmware. - **`packet.to` is now passed by every decrypt caller,** because the AAD binds it: TCP ingest, MQTT ingest, `ok_to_mqtt`, broker portnum peek, and retroactive decryption. An AEAD row is skipped when the destination is unknown. - **Hint:** when no key opens a packet and its hash equals a known plain row's hash `^ 0xAE`, the server logs at **debug** level only, as agreed. - **Channel Database UI:** - an **"AEAD channel (AES-CCM, Experimental)"** checkbox, Meshtastic rows only; - the existing AEAD badge on those rows; - the flag survives JSON export/import and channel-URL import. - **Changing the flag** re-runs retroactive decryption for that row. ## Not changed - **No stored-hash backfill:** enabled rows compute their hash from name and key, and only passive rows with no key store one. - **No compose limit change:** a 200-byte message plus `Data` framing, the 16-byte header and the 12-byte tag stays under 255. ## Mesh impact None. No packets are sent, and there are no timers or new notifications. It's decrypt-only, and decrypted packets go through the existing ingest and permission paths. ## Tests - `channelDecryptionService.aead.test.ts`, 13 tests: - Node's CCM against the RFC 3610 vector the firmware tests also use; - packets built with the firmware's own nonce and AAD layout; - AES-256; - a wrong destination, a tampered tag, a missing destination, and a CTR packet on an AEAD row all miss; - a plain row can't open an AEAD packet; - attribution and name validation with `^ 0xAE`; - `peekPortnum` and `tryDecryptWithChannel`; - the debug hint. - `channelDatabase.useAead.test.ts` uses the route harness on real SQLite: create, toggle, retroactive re-run, and MeshCore rows ignoring the flag. - Migration 208 has a SQLite

title: fix(mqtt): show a forwarder's own uplinked packets on its source (#5858)
body:
Fixes #5858.

## Cause

`handleDownlink` in `mqttBridgeManager.ts` returned early when a downlink matched the bridge's own uplink echo (same topic + packet id within 60 s). That return sat **before** ingestion. So when a forwarder bridge uplinked the user's own message from the built-in broker, the copy its upstream sent back was thrown away, and the message never landed on the forwarder source. Other nodes' traffic was never uplinked by us, so it showed up normally, which matches the report.

`relayOtherBridges` and `bridgeOriginOf` play no part: they only gate the uplink direction.

## Fix

The echo is now ingested on the forwarder's source. It still skips the `local-packet` emit (mqttLink devices) and the republish to the local broker, so the anti-loop behavior is unchanged.

## Mesh impact

- **Airtime:** none; no new sends. The echo still never reaches a radio or the local broker.
- **Spam:** the ingested row is a normal reception on the forwarder source. Copies of the same packet heard through *other* gateways (different topic) were already ingested, so no new kind of event reaches automations or notifications. Message rows dedupe per source by `${sourceId}_${from}_${packetId}`.
- **Timers:** none.

## Tests

- New `mqttBridgeManager.ownUplinkEcho.test.ts`: the echo is ingested but not republished or relayed; foreign traffic still does all three. It fails without the fix.
- Full Vitest suite: 31,701 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped; no schema change).
- tsc and `lint:ci` clean.

Not done: the per-source echo-drop counter the issue suggests. The echo is no longer dropped, so the main reason for it is gone.

title: feat(autoack): separate IP (MQTT/UDP) row in the Auto-Ack matrix (#5796)
body:
Closes #5796

## Summary

Auto-Acknowledge gets a third row, **IP (MQTT / UDP)**, for both Channel and Direct messages. A message is IP when `viaMqtt === true`, or its transport mechanism is `MQTT` (5) or `MULTICAST_UDP` (6). `API` (7) is not IP. The IP check runs first, so an IP message never lands in the 0-hop or multi-hop row, whatever its hop count.

- **Decision helpers** (`src/server/utils/autoAckDecision.ts`): new `autoAckIsIp(viaMqtt, transportMechanism)`. `autoAckIsZeroHop()` takes the transport too, so it is false for UDP as well as MQTT. `autoAckCellKey(isDM, isZeroHop, isIp)` returns `autoAck{Channel,Direct}Ip` when `isIp` is set.
- **How IP reaches auto-ack:** `checkAutoAcknowledge` reads `message.viaMqtt` and `message.transportMechanism`. `processTextMessageProtobuf` already stores both on the `TextMessage` it passes in (`transportMechanism` comes from `resolveRadioPacketTransport(meshPacket)`), so nothing new had to be passed through and nothing is guessed again. MQTT bridge and broker sources never call `checkAutoAcknowledge`. Their message rows carry `viaMqtt: true` / transport `MQTT`, so in automations they read `viaIp = 1`.
- **0-hop reply template:** it is now chosen by the ZeroHop cell, not by `hopsTraveled === 0`. An MQTT/UDP message at 0 hops gets the standard template. The 0-hop template often has `{SNR}`/`{RSSI}`, which mean nothing over IP, and those odd numbers are what the issue reports. This also matches what the converter already did.
- **Settings:** six new per-source keys `autoAck{Channel,Direct}Ip{Reply,Tapback,ReplyDm}Enabled`, added to both `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` (allowlist for saves) and `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS` (source-scoped storage).
- **No migration.** An unset key already reads as off (`settingsToMatrix` / `=== 'true'`), so the new row starts off on every install, existing ones included. No values are copied from MultiHop, as decided.
- **Automation Engine:** a new trigger field `viaIp` (always 1 or 0, never NaN) uses the same `autoAckIsIp()`. `zeroHop` is now 0 for UDP too. The converter writes `viaIp == 1` for IP cells, and `zeroHop == 0 AND viaIp == 0` for MultiHop cells. The rule set stays a flat AND chain, so converted automations still decompile into the builder. `viaIp` is listed in the field picker and the substitutions help.
- **UI** (`AutoAcknowledgeSection.tsx`): the matrix now has two columns (Channel | Direct) and one row per path (0 hops, multi-hop, IP). The IP row is last, with a note under it: MQTT/UDP messages used to be answered by the other rows and now need the IP row turned on. Saving uses the existing `matrixToSettings()` spread, so no other save code changed.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/automation.md` (new "IP Row" section) and `docs/features/automation-engine.md` (`viaIp`, updated `zeroHop`, removed the template note that no longer applies).
- MeshCore auto-ack has its own logic and does not use this matrix, so it is unchanged.

+# Passkeys
+
+A passkey lets you sign in with your device's fingerprint, face or PIN instead of a password. Your device keeps the private key. MeshMonitor stores only the public half.
+
+Passkeys work for **local accounts only**. Accounts that sign in through [SSO (OpenID Connect)](/configuration/sso) or proxy authentication cannot add passkeys.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- **HTTPS, or `http://localhost`.** Browsers turn passkeys off on plain HTTP. On such a page MeshMonitor hides the passkey controls and shows a short note. See [HTTP vs HTTPS](/configuration/http-vs-https).
+- **A fixed hostname.** A passkey works only on the hostname where you added it. If you add one at `https://mesh.example.com`, your browser will not offer it at `https://192.168.1.50:8080`, at a `.local` name, or at a port-forward URL. Pick one address, and add your passkeys there.
+- **A browser or device that supports passkeys.** Current Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox do, with a platform authenticator, a password manager or a security key.
+
+Each passkey in your list shows the hostname it works on.
+
+## Add, rename and remove a passkey
+
+1. Sign in with your password.
+2. Open the user menu (your username in the header) and choose **Passkeys**.
+3. Select **Add a passkey**, name it (for example, "Work laptop"), and select **Continue**.
+4. Approve the prompt from your browser or device.
+
+In the same dialog you can **Rename** or **Delete** any passkey. The list shows when each one was added and last used. Add more than one passkey (for example, a laptop and a phone) so losing one device does not lock you out.
+
+## Sign in with a passkey
+
+On the login page, choose **Sign in with a passkey** and approve the prompt. You do not type a username.
+
+Your browser can also offer your passkey in the username field. Click the field and pick the passkey from the autofill list.
+
+A passkey sign-in **skips the two-factor (TOTP) code**. The passkey already proves two things: you hold the device, and you passed its fingerprint, face or PIN check. Password sign-in still asks for the code.
+
+## Reverse proxy and subpath installs
+
+MeshMonitor reads the hostname and scheme from each request unless you set the variables below.
+
+- Set `TRUST_PROXY` so MeshMonitor sees the real scheme (`https`). See [Reverse Proxy](/configuration/reverse-proxy).
+- Make the proxy pass the original `Host` header.
+- A `BASE_URL` subpath (for example `/meshmonitor`) needs no passkey setting. A passkey binds to the hostname only, not the path.
+
+If you cannot meet those two conditions, set `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` and `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS`.
+
+## Settings
+
+Both variables are optional. At startup, MeshMonitor logs a warning if either is unset.
+
+| Variable | Default | Description |
+|----------|---------|-------------|
+| `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` | request hostname | The hostname passkeys bind to. Use a bare hostname with no scheme, port or path. MeshMonitor lowercases it. |
+| `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS` | `<scheme>://<host>` of the request | Comma-separated list of full origins allowed to use passkeys. Each needs a scheme, and a port if it is not the default. MeshMonitor trims spaces and trailing slashes. |
+
+Set them when:
+
+- You sit behind a reverse proxy that does not forward the right `Host` or scheme.
+- You reach MeshMonitor under more than one hostname. The RP ID is one hostname. Pick a parent domain that covers them all, and list each origin.
+
+```yaml
+environment:
+  - WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=mesh.example.com
+  - WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=https://mesh.example.com
+```
+
+Two names under one parent domain:
+
+```yaml
+environment:
+  - WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=example.com
+  - WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=https://mesh.example.com,https://mesh-admin.example.com
+```
+
+::: warning
+Changing the RP ID later makes existing passkeys stop working, because they bind to the old hostname. Add new passkeys after the change.
+:::
+
+## Passkey-only accounts
+
+You can turn off password sign-in for your account. Then only your passkeys, or a recovery code, sign you in.
+
+**Turn it off:**
+
+1. Add at least one passkey (two is safer).
+2. Open the user menu, choose **Passkeys**, and select **Turn off password sign-in**.
+3. Select **Continue with a passkey** and approve the browser prompt. This proves the passkey works and that you are at the keyboard.
+4. MeshMonitor shows **10 one-time recovery codes**. Copy or download them, store them away from this device, and tick **I saved these codes**. MeshMonitor shows them once and cannot show them again.
+
+If you are the only admin, MeshMonitor warns you first and asks you to type `DISABLE` to confirm. If you lose your passkeys and your codes, nobody can sign in to manage MeshMonitor.
+
+**While it is off:**
+
+- Password sign-in fails with the same "Invalid username or password" error as a wrong password.
+- You cannot change your password.
+- You cannot delete your last passkey. Turn password sign-in back on first.
+
+**Turn it back on:** open **Passkeys** and select **Turn password sign-in back on**. This discards your recovery codes.
+
+## Lost your passkey
+
+### Use a recovery code
+
+1. On the login form, select **Lost your passkey? Use a recovery code**.
+2. Enter your username and one recovery code.
+3. MeshMonitor signs you in, turns password sign-in back on, and asks you to **Choose a new password**.
+
+Each code works once. When you use one, MeshMonitor discards the rest. Add a new passkey afterwards, and turn password sign-in off again if you want a new set of codes. Accounts with a locked password (set by an admin) skip the new-password step.
+
+### Ask an admin
+
+An admin can set a new password for you in the **Users** tab. That turns password sign-in back on, and you can sign in with the new password.
+
+## Admin tasks
+
+In **Users**, each row shows the user's passkey count. Select **Passkeys** to see a user's passkeys and **Revoke** one. Use this when a device is lost or stolen.
+
+Revoking has one limit. You cannot revoke the last passkey of a user whose password sign-in is off, because that would lock them out. Set a new password for the user first, which turns password sign-in back on, then revoke.
+
+Passkey events (add, rename, delete, admin revoke, password sign-in on or off, recovery code use, failed passkey sign-ins) go to the audit log.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+**The browser offers no passkey, or the button is missing.**
+Check that the page uses HTTPS or `http://localhost`. Then check the address bar: a passkey works only on the hostname where you added it. Open **Passkeys** to see that hostname.
+
+**"The passkey request expired."**
+A passkey request lasts 5 minutes. Try again.
+
+**"Passkey sign-in failed."**
+The passkey is unknown, the account is inactive or not local, or local login is off (`DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH`). Sign in with your password, or a recovery code.
+
+**"This passkey is already added."**
+Your device already holds a passkey for this account. Pick a different authenticator.
+
+**Passkeys fail behind a proxy.**
+Set `TRUST_PROXY`, forward the `Host` header, or set `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` and `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS` to match the address in your browser.
+
+**I changed hostnames and my passkeys vanished.**
+They still exist but bind to the old hostname. Use the old address, or add new passkeys on the new one.

title: feat(auth): passkey-only accounts, recovery codes, admin revoke (#5841 3/4)
body:
Refs #5841

PR 3 of 4 from `docs/internal/dev-notes/PASSKEY_5841_SPEC.md` (§6, §8, §13 item 3): passkey-only accounts, recovery codes, the last-admin confirm, and admin view/revoke.

## Routes (`/api/auth/passkey`, all session-only via `requireSessionUser`)

| Route | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `POST /step-up/options` | Authentication options with `allowCredentials` = the caller's own passkeys. Single-use session challenge, purpose `step-up`, bound to the user, 5-minute TTL. 409 `NO_PASSKEYS` with none. |
| `GET /password-login` | `{ disabled, recoveryCodesLeft }` for the profile dialog (small addition, not in the spec table). |
| `POST /password-login` | `{ disabled: true, assertion, confirm? }`: needs a passkey and a step-up assertion from one of the caller's own passkeys, verified through the same helper as login (counter rule, counter stored). Returns 10 codes from `mfaService.generateBackupCodes()` once; bcrypt hashes go in `passkeyRecoveryCodes`. Audited, `notifyAccessChange`. `{ disabled: false }` clears the flag and the codes. |
| `POST /recover` | `authLimiter`, no auth. `{ username, code }` → `mfaService.verifyBackupCode`, then a compare-and-swap write turns password login back on and clears the codes (only one of two racing requests wins). Signs in on a regenerated session with the login session fields. One generic 401 for every failure. |
| `GET /admin/users/:userId`, `DELETE /admin/users/:userId/:id` | `requireAdmin` + session only. Revoke audits `passkey_revoked_by_admin`. Revoking a passkey-only user's last passkey: **409 `LAST_PASSKEY`**, telling the admin to set a new password first. |

**Last admin (D3):** when the caller is the only active admin and `confirm !== 'DISABLE'`, the reply is `{ requireConfirm: true }`, nothing changes, and **the step-up challenge stays in the session**. The client resends the same assertion with `confirm: 'DISABLE'`, so the user sees one passkey prompt. Tested.

## Where the flag gates password sign-in

- `DatabaseService.authenticateAsync`: returns null when `passwordLoginDisabled`, after the bcrypt compare (same timing as a wrong password) and before `lastLoginAt` is written.
- `authenticateLocal` (the only caller): same check, as a second guard. `POST /api/auth/login` therefore sends the exact bad-password 401, and an MFA account never reaches the MFA step.
- `POST /api/auth/verify-mfa`: a pending MFA step that started before the switch flipped gets the existing `Invalid MFA state` 401.
- `POST /api/auth/change-password` (403 `PASSWORD_LOGIN_DISABLED`) and `changePassword()` / `setPasswordAfterRecovery()` in `localAuth.ts`.
- `setUserPassword` / `resetUserPassword` (admin Users tab) turn password login back on and drop the codes.

## Forced password change after recovery

The spec says to reuse the default-password prompt. That prompt is dead code: `useSecurityCheck` is not used by any component, and it only checks the `admin` account for `changeme`. So recovery sets `req.session.p

title: feat(auth): sign in with a passkey (#5841 2/4)
body:
Refs #5841 — PR 2 of 4 (spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/PASSKEY_5841_SPEC.md`, §13 item 2). Builds on the storage from #5849.

## What this adds

**Library.** `@simplewebauthn/server` 14.0.3 and `@simplewebauthn/browser` 14.0.0, pinned exactly (same major; both released 2+ weeks ago). The browser package loads through a dynamic `import()` in `src/services/passkeyClient.ts`, so it lands in its own ~13 KB chunk, not `main`.

**RP config (§5, D7).** Optional `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` and `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS` in `src/server/config/environment.ts`. When unset, the RP ID is `req.hostname` and the origin is `req.protocol://host`, and the server logs a one-time warning at startup. The RP ID used is stored in `rp_id` at registration and shown in the UI.

**Routes** (`src/server/routes/passkeyRoutes.ts`, mounted at `/api/auth/passkey`, all `ok()` / `fail()`):

| Route | Notes |
|---|---|
| `POST /register/options` | requireAuth, local users only (D4), `excludeCredentials` = existing passkeys, `residentKey`/`userVerification: 'preferred'` |
| `POST /register/verify` | verifies, stores the row with its `rp_id`, audit `passkey_registered`, `notifyAccessChange` |
| `POST /login/options` | `authLimiter`, discoverable (empty `allowCredentials`) |
| `POST /login/verify` | `authLimiter`; rejects unknown credential, inactive or non-local user, `DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH`, a user handle naming another user, and a non-zero counter that did not go up; `regenerateSession()` + the same session fields as password login with `authProvider: 'local'`; **no TOTP step (D5)**; audit `login_success` / `login_failed` with `method: 'passkey'` |
| `GET /` | caller's passkeys, no key material |
| `PATCH /:id` | rename, owner-scoped, audited |
| `DELETE /:id` | owner-scoped, audited, `notifyAccessChange`; **refused (409 `LAST_PASSKEY`) for the last passkey while `passwordLoginDisabled` is true** — the flag can only be set from PR 3, but the guard and its test are here |

Challenges live in `req.session.webauthnChallenge` with a 5-minute expiry and are deleted on first use, pass or fail. A challenge made for login cannot be used to register, and the reverse.

`regenerateSession()` moved from `authRoutes.ts` to `src/server/auth/regenerateSession.ts` so both route files share it (no behaviour change).

**UI (§9).**
- "Sign in with a passkey" button on `LoginPage` and `LoginModal`, shown only when `window.isSecureContext && window.PublicKeyCredential` and local auth is on. On success it refreshes auth and reloads, like password login (`AuthContext.loginWithPasskey`).
- Conditional UI: the username field gets `autocomplete="username webauthn"` and the page waits for an autofill pick where the browser supports it.
- User menu → **Passkeys** dialog (beside Two-Factor Auth): list with nickname, hostname, created and last used; Add (asks for a nickname), Rename, Delete with confirm. Without a secure context it says in one line that passkeys need HTTPS or localhost.
- `UiIcon`, CSS modules with `var(--color-*)`

title: feat(auth): passkey storage (#5841 1/4)
body:
Refs #5841

PR 1 of 4 for passkey login (spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/PASSKEY_5841_SPEC.md`, §13 item 1). This PR adds storage only. Routes, UI and `@simplewebauthn` come in PR 2.

## What changes

- **Migration 207** (SQLite / PostgreSQL / MySQL, idempotent):
  - New `user_passkeys` table with the §4 columns (`rp_id` included). FK to `users` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, unique credential id, index on the user column.
  - `users.password_login_disabled` (boolean, default false) and `users.passkey_recovery_codes` (text, nullable).
  - On MySQL the credential id is `VARCHAR(1400) CHARACTER SET ascii COLLATE ascii_bin`. base64url is case-sensitive, so the default `utf8mb4_unicode_ci` would treat two different ids as equal. A WebAuthn id can be 1023 bytes (1364 base64url chars), and utf8mb4 at that length would also break the 3072-byte index limit.
  - Naming follows `users` / `api_tokens`: snake_case on SQLite, camelCase on PG/MySQL.
- **Drizzle schema**: `userPasskeys{Sqlite,Postgres,Mysql}` in `src/db/schema/auth.ts`, the users columns on all three, and `userPasskeys` in `activeSchema`.
- **`PasskeysRepository`** (`src/db/repositories/passkeys.ts`): `create`, `getByCredentialId`, `listByUser`, `listSummariesByUser` (no public key, credential id or counter), `rename` / `delete` scoped to the owning user, `deleteAllForUser`, `updateCounterAndLastUsed`, `countByUser`. Nicknames are capped at 64 characters. `AuthRepository` gains `getPasskeyLoginState`, `setPasswordLoginDisabled` and `setPasskeyRecoveryCodes`. Everything is on `DatabaseService` with `Async` names.
- **Secret stripping**: new `stripUserSecrets()` (`src/server/utils/userSecrets.ts`) holds one list of secret user fields, now with `passkeyRecoveryCodes` added. All five `authRoutes` / `userRoutes` sites that send a user now use it. Side fix: `POST /api/users` and `PUT /api/users/:id` used to strip only `passwordHash`, so they sent the MFA secret and backup codes back to the admin. They no longer do.
- **Backup**: `user_passkeys` is in `BACKUP_TABLES` (after `users`, in the secrets group) and in `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES`. It is also in the `migrate-db` `TABLE_ORDER`. The table in `docs/features/system-backup.md` is updated to match.
- **Test fixtures**: hand-written PG/MySQL `users` DDL in `auth.test.ts` and `132_*.pgmysql.test.ts` gains the two columns. Five route tests that build SQLite from the baseline plus 022 now also run 207.

## Tests

- `207_create_user_passkeys.test.ts` (SQLite, 5): columns and defaults, every spec column, the index, idempotency, unique credential id, cascade.
- `207_create_user_passkeys.pgmysql.test.ts` (PG 4, MySQL 5, each on its own isolated DB): the same checks, plus case-distinct ids and a maximum-length id on MySQL.
- `passkeys.multiBackend.test.ts` (10 × SQLite / PG / MySQL = 30): round-trip, duplicate rejected, per-user list and count, summary without key material, owner-scoped rename and delete (a user cannot delete another user's passkey), deleteAll, a bigin

title: feat(meshcore): override a contact's location (#5842)
body:
Fixes #5842

## Summary

MeshCore contacts get the location override Meshtastic nodes already have, per the maintainer decisions on the issue:

- **MeshMonitor only.** The override lives in new `meshcore_nodes` columns that match the Meshtastic `nodes` ones. Nothing goes to the radio, so Companion and Repeater sources behave the same, and the routes work while the source is disconnected.
- **Same permission.** Editing takes `nodes:write` on the source, the permission the Meshtastic `/api/nodes/:nodeId/position-override` route checks. The new write routes also sit behind `requireAuth()`, like every MeshCore write route (`meshcoreRoutes.scope.test.ts` enforces this), so the anonymous account cannot edit an override.

## What changed

**Storage**
- Migration **206** adds `positionOverrideEnabled`, `latitudeOverride`, `longitudeOverride`, `altitudeOverride`, `positionOverrideIsPrivate` to `meshcore_nodes` on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. It uses the idempotent helpers with full column DDL.
- `MeshCoreRepository`: `getNodePositionOverride`, `getPositionOverridesBySource`, `setNodePositionOverride`, `clearNodePositionOverride`, all scoped by source with `withSourceScope`.
- Advert ingest keeps writing `latitude`/`longitude`. `upsertNode` drops the override keys from its input, so no ingest path can write or clear an override, and the override is never copied into the advert columns.

**Routes**: `GET / POST / DELETE /api/sources/:id/meshcore/nodes/:publicKey/position-override`. They use the `ok`/`fail` envelope and validate the same fields the Meshtastic route checks. A key the source has never seen returns 404. A contact that exists only in memory gets its identity row first.

**Precedence.** One rule, in `src/server/utils/meshcorePositionOverride.ts`: an enabled override wins over the advert position. The row gets `positionIsOverride: true`, so the #5363 sign-flip correction skips it. The rule applies on:
- `GET .../meshcore/nodes`, `GET .../meshcore/contacts`, `POST .../meshcore/contacts/refresh`, `GET .../meshcore/snapshot` (MeshCore map, node list, node details)
- `GET .../meshcore/ingest/nodes`
- `buildSourceNodes` (Dashboard / unified / Map Analysis maps)
- the MeshCore block of `GET /api/nodes`
- the `meshcore:contact:updated` socket event, so an advert cannot move a pinned contact back on screen
- cross-source "heard here" link endpoints, Coverage receiver positions, the Observer receiver-position snapshot, and the CoT feed

An override position is never hidden by the "hide nodes without a current position advert" map filter.

**Privacy** follows the Meshtastic rule:
- A private override is applied only for callers with `nodes_private:read` on the source. Everyone else sees the advert position, with no override fields.
- `buildMeshCorePositionFilter` drops a private-override node for those callers, as `buildPositionFilter` does.

title: docs: passkey login spec for review (#5841)
body:
Spec only, for maintainer review before any code. Refs #5841.

It records the interview decisions (D1–D4), the data model, routes, security rules, passkey-only accounts with recovery codes, the UI, tests, and a four-PR delivery split. **Three open questions are in §12.**

diff:
--- docs/internal/dev-notes/PASSKEY_5841_SPEC.md (+139/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+# Passkey login — spec (#5841)
+
+Status: **approved** (open questions answered 2026-10-15, §12).
+
+## 1. Decisions already made (interview, 2026-10-15)
+
+| # | Decision |
+|---|----------|
+| D1 | Phase 1 = sign in with a passkey, admin can view/revoke passkeys, **passkey-only accounts**. |
+| D2 | Passkey-only recovery = **one-time recovery codes**, shown when password login is turned off. |
+| D3 | The last admin **may** turn off their own password, after a warning and typed confirmation. |
+| D4 | **Local-auth users only.** OIDC and proxy-auth users cannot register passkeys. |
+| D5 | Passkey login **skips TOTP** (Q1). |
+| D6 | Turning off password login needs a **fresh passkey prompt** in that dialog (Q2). |
+| D7 | `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` / `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS` are **optional**; derive from the request when unset (Q3). |
+| D8 | Ship as **four PRs**, merged in order as each goes green; deploy to dev after the last. |
+
+## 2. What exists today
+
+- `POST /api/auth/login` (`src/server/routes/authRoutes.ts`) → `authenticateLocal()` → `regenerateSession()` → sets `req.session.{userId, username, authProvider:'local', isAdmin}`.
+- TOTP MFA: `users.mfa_enabled / mfa_secret / mfa_backup_codes`. A password login with MFA on parks `req.session.pendingMfaUserId` and finishes in `POST /api/auth/verify-mfa`.
+- `src/server/services/mfa.ts` already generates, bcrypt-hashes and consumes one-time backup codes. **The recovery codes in D2 reuse this service** rather than adding a second implementation.
+- `users.password_locked` stops a user changing their own password (admin-set). `DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH` turns off local login entirely.
+- Express `trust proxy` is off unless `TRUST_PROXY` is set; session cookie `secure` follows `COOKIE_SECURE`.
+
+## 3. Library
+
+`@simplewebauthn/server` (server) and `@simplewebauthn/browser` (client), MIT, the de facto standard. Pin exact versions; the browser package is lazy-loaded on the login page and profile page so it stays out of the main chunk (`check:bundle-size`).
+
+## 4. Data model
+
+New table **`user_passkeys`** (all three backends, one migration):
+
+| Column | Type | Notes |
+|--------|------|-------|
+| `id` | PK | |
+| `user_id` | FK → users, `ON DELETE CASCADE` | |
+| `credential_id` | text, **unique** | base64url |
+| `public_key` | text | base64url of the COSE key (text, not BLOB, so one type works on all three backends) |
+| `counter` | bigint | signature counter; see §7 |
+| `transports` | text | JSON array |
+| `device_type` | text | `singleDevice` / `multiDevice` |
+| `backed_up` | boolean | |
+| `rp_id` | text | hostname the passkey was registered on (§5) |
+| `nickname` | text | user-chosen, max 64 chars |
+| `created_at`, `last_used_at` | bigint (ms) | |
+
+New columns on **`users`**:
+
+| Column | Type | Notes |
+|--------|------|-------|
+| `password_login_disabled` | boolean, default false | D1 passkey-only switch |
+| `passkey_recovery_codes` | text, nullable | JSON array of bcrypt hashes (same format as `mfa_backup_codes`) |
+
+Backup: `user_passkeys` goes in `BACKUP_TABLES` **and** `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES` (public keys are not secret, but credential IDs plus user IDs are account data; treat like other auth tables). `systemBackupService.tables.test.ts` enforces the classification.
+
+## 5. Relying party (RP) identity
+
+WebAuthn binds a credential to an **RP ID** (a hostname) and checks the **origin**. Self-hosters reach MeshMonitor many ways (LAN IP, `.local`, reverse-proxied domain), so this is the main deployment trap.
+
+- New optional env vars: `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` (e.g. `mesh.example.com`) and `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS` (comma list, e.g. `https://mesh.example.com`).
+- If unset, derive both from the request (`req.hostname`, `req.protocol`), which is correct only when `TRUST_PROXY` is right behind a proxy. Log a one-time warning at startup when unset.
+- A passkey registered on one hostname will **not** work on another. The profile UI shows the hostname each passkey is bound to (store the RP ID used at registration in a `rp_id` column, so this is exact).
+- WebAuthn needs a **secure context** (HTTPS, or `http://localhost`). On plain-HTTP LAN installs the browser API is absent: the client hides every passkey control when `!window.isSecureContext || !window.PublicKeyCredential`, and the profile page explains why in one line.
+
+## 6. Routes (`src/server/routes/passkeyRoutes.ts`, mounted at `/api/auth/passkey`)
+
+All use `ok()` / `fail()`. Challenges live in the session (`req.session.webauthnChallenge`, with a 5-minute expiry stamp) and are deleted on first use, success or failure.
+
+| Route | Auth | Purpose |
+|-------|------|---------|
+| `POST /register/options` | requireAuth, local users only (D4) | `generateRegistrationOptions`; `excludeCredentials` = user's existing passkeys; `residentKey: 'preferred'`, `userVerification: 'preferred'`. |
+| `POST /register/verify` | requireAuth | `verifyRegistrationResponse`; insert row; audit `passkey_registered`. |
+| `POST /login/options` | none, `authLimiter` | `generateAuthenticationOptions` with **empty `allowCredentials`** (discoverable, username-less). No username input → no account enumeration. |
+| `POST /login/verify` | none, `authLimiter` | Look up by `credential_id`; reject inactive users, non-local users, or when `DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH`; `verifyAuthenticationResponse`; update counter + `last_used_at`; `regenerateSession()`; set the same session fields as password login with `authProvider: 'local'`; audit `login_success` with `method: 'passkey'`. |
+| `GET /` | requireAuth | List the caller's passkeys (no key material). |
+| `PATCH /:id` | requireAuth, owner | Rename. |
+| `DELETE /:id` | requireAuth, owner | Delete. **Refused** if it is the last passkey while `password_login_disabled` is true (would lock the user out). |
+| `POST /step-up/options` | requireAuth, owner | Authentication options limited to the caller's own credentials (`allowCredentials`), for the D6 step-up. |
+| `POST /password-login` | requireAuth, owner | Body `{ disabled: boolean, assertion?, confirm?: string }`. See §8. |
+| `POST /recover` | none, `authLimiter` | Body `{ username, code }`. See §8. |
+| `GET /admin/users/:userId` · `DELETE /admin/users/:userId/:id` | admin | D1 admin view/revoke; audit `passkey_revoked_by_admin`. |
+
+Every route that ends a session or changes credentials calls `notifyAccessChange` the way logout does, so open WebSockets re-check.
+
+## 7. Security rules
+
+- **TOTP and passkeys (D5):** a passkey login **does not** ask for the TOTP code. A passkey with user verification is already two factors (device + biometric/PIN). Password login keeps asking for TOTP as today.
+- **Counter:** reject an authentication whose counter is non-zero and not greater than the stored one (cloned authenticator). Synced passkeys report 0 forever; 0 is accepted.
+- **Rate limiting:** `/login/*` and `/recover` share `authLimiter` with password login.
+- **Audit:** register, rename, delete, admin revoke, password-login on/off, recovery-code use, and failed passkey verifications (`login_failed`, `method: 'passkey'`).
+- **No new authProvider value.** A passkey is a second credential on a local user, so every existing `authProvider === 'local'` check keeps working.
+
+## 8. Passkey-only accounts (D1–D3)
+
+**Turning password login off** (`POST /password-login { disabled: true }`):
+
+1. Requires at least one registered passkey **and** a fresh passkey assertion made in that dialog (D6). The client calls `POST /step-up/options`, the browser prompts for a passkey, and the assertion goes in the request body as `assertion`. The server verifies that it belongs to the caller and uses a single-use challenge. This stops someone at an unlocked browser that is signed in with a password, and proves the passkey works before the password goes.
+2. Generates 10 recovery codes with `mfaService.generateBackupCodes()`, stores bcrypt hashes in `passkey_recovery_codes`, returns the plain codes **once**. The UI makes the user tick "I saved these" before closing.
+3. **Last admin (D3):** if the caller is the only active admin, the response first returns `requireConfirm: true`; the client shows a warning and the user types `DISABLE` to resend with `confirm: 'DISABLE'`. Allowed, not blocked.
+
+**While disabled:** `POST /api/auth/login` returns the same `401 Invalid username or password` as a bad password, so the switch is not revealed to an attacker. `POST /change-password` is refused.
+
+**Turning it back on** (`{ disabled: false }`): clears the flag and the recovery codes.
+
+**Recovery** (`POST /recover { username, code }`): verifies one code with `mfaService.verifyBackupCode`, consumes it, signs the user in, and **turns password login back on** with a forced password change on next page (reuses the existing default-password prompt). A generic error for every failure. Admins can also recover a user by setting a new password in the Users tab, which turns password login back on.
+
+## 9. UI
+
+- **Login page:** a "Sign in with a passkey" button above the password form when supported (§5). The browser's own passkey picker does the rest. Conditional UI (`autocomplete="username webauthn"`) on the username field.
+- **Profile → Security** (beside `MFAManagement`): passkey list (nickname, created, last used, hostname), Add, Rename, Delete; the "Turn off password login" switch with the recovery-code dialog.
+- **Users tab (admin):** passkey count per user; a "Passkeys" dialog with Revoke.
+- `UiIcon`, CSS modules, `var(--color-*)`, strings in `public/locales/en.json`.
+
+## 10. Tests
+
+- Route tests on `createRouteTestApp` for every route: permission, local-only, `DISABLE_LOCAL_AUTH`, challenge single-use and expiry, counter regression, last-passkey delete refusal, last-admin confirm flow, recovery-code consume-once, login 401 parity while password login is off.
+- WebAuthn verification is mocked at the `@simplewebauthn/server` boundary (a real authenticator is not available in CI); one test drives the library with a recorded fixture to catch upgrade breakage.
+- Migration tests on all three backends; backup-table classification test.
+- Client: hidden controls without a secure context; recovery-code dialog cannot close unacknowledged.
+
+## 11. Mesh impact
+
+None. No packets, notifications or timers.
+
+## 12. Answered questions
+
+- **Q1.** Skip TOTP on passkey login → **yes** (D5).
+- **Q2.** Guard on turning off password login → **a fresh passkey prompt in the dialog**, not a recent-login window (D6).
+- **Q3.** RP ID config → **optional env, derive from the request when unset** (D7).
+
+## 13. Delivery
+
+One PR is too big to review well. Split (D8), merged in order as each goes green:
+
+1. Schema + migration + repository + backup classification.
+2. Register / login / list / rename / delete routes + login-page button + profile list.
+3. Passkey-only switch, recovery codes, last-admin confirm, admin revoke.
+4. Docs: `docs/` user guide page (HTTPS requirement, hostname binding, recovery).

title: fix(map): tapping a node in Traceroute mode draws its newest answered run (#5821)
body:
Fixes #5821

## Root cause

`useTraceroutePaths` picked the **newest** traceroute row for the selected node, whatever that row held (`src/hooks/useTraceroutePaths.tsx`: the `selectedNodeTraceroute`, `tracerouteNodeNums` and `tracerouteBounds` memos all used `traceroutesDigest.find(tr => tr.toNodeId === id || tr.fromNodeId === id)`).

Auto-traceroute writes a pending row (`route` NULL) for each request it sends (`recordTracerouteRequest`). On a busy source, the newest row for a node is often one of those: still in flight, or never answered. When the hook picked it:

- `decomposeTraceroute` returned no segments, so no per-node route was drawn;
- `tracerouteNodeNums` was null, so the **Dismiss Traceroute** button did not show;
- `tracerouteBounds` was null, so no zoom-to-fit ran.

Meanwhile NodesTab's popup gate (`hasValidTraceroute`, `NodesTab.tsx:2087`) uses `.some(...)` and found an older row with a full route, so it **hid the popup**. The tap did nothing visible. That matches all three symptoms in the report.

The unified map was unaffected because `DashboardMap` draws every row instead of picking one. Selection itself (`onOmsClick`, touch path) and the per-source poll row shape (`toNodeId`/`fromNodeId` present, requester-first) checked out fine.

## Fix

New `findSelectedNodeTraceroute(rows, nodeId)` in `src/utils/tracerouteSegments.ts`: the newest row for the node where either leg has data (`hasRouteData(route) || hasReturnPath(routeBack, snrBack)`), the same test `decomposeTraceroute` uses. All three memos use it, so the overlay, marker filter, Dismiss button and bounds all describe the same row.

## Tests

- New regression cases in `src/hooks/useTraceroutePaths.test.tsx`: a pending row newer than a complete run still draws the run (and yields node nums and bounds); only-pending yields nothing. The first case fails on the old code.
- Full Vitest suite (`--maxWorkers=2`): 2119 files passed, 1 skipped; 32,994 tests passed, 0 failed, no Errors line.
- `npm run typecheck` and the server tsconfig: clean. `lint:ci`: no in-repo FAIL lines.

## Mesh impact

None. No packet, timer or schedule changes; client-side row selection only.

title: feat(messages): remember Show MQTT/Bridge Messages per source (#5824)
body:
Fixes #5824

## Problem
"Show MQTT/Bridge Messages" was one browser-global localStorage key (`showMqttMessages`). Flipping it on one source flipped it everywhere, and a fresh or private browser reset it to hidden.

Note: the issue says "Show MQTT Nodes" is already per source. It isn't: it's per user on the server (`user_map_preferences` has no `sourceId`). This PR makes the message toggle truly per user **and** per source, as decided with the maintainer.

## Change
- **Migration 205** adds `user_map_preferences.show_mqtt_messages_by_source` (TEXT, JSON `{ sourceId: boolean }`) on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. Idempotent via the shared helpers.
- **`POST /api/user/map-preferences`** accepts `{ showMqttMessages, sourceId }` and updates only that source's entry (read-modify-write). It returns 400 for a non-boolean value or a missing `sourceId`, and 404 for an unknown source, so the map cannot grow without bound. **GET** returns `showMqttMessagesBySource`.
- **`UIContext`**:
  - Reads a per-source local cache (`showMqttMessages:<sourceId>`), falling back to the old global key so nobody loses their setting on upgrade.
  - Applies the server value when it loads.
  - Saves each toggle both locally and to the server. Anonymous users keep the local cache.
  - A toggle made before the server read returns is not overwritten.

## Mesh impact
None. This is a display preference only; it sends no packets, notifications or timers.

## Tests
- Migration 205: adds the column, idempotent, existing rows read NULL.
- Schema maps the column on all three backends; `parseBooleanMap` handles malformed input.
- Route (real harness): per-source isolation, survives other preference saves, empty map by default, 400/404 cases.
- `UIContext` (jsdom, mocked API): per-source cache, legacy fallback, server wins, local kept when server has no entry, save payload, a slow server read doesn't undo a toggle.
- Full Vitest suite: 33,007 passed, 0 failed (PostgreSQL and MySQL suites skipped locally; CI covers them). `tsc` (client and server) clean; `lint:ci` OK.

No UI change beyond persistence, so no screenshot.

title: feat(ui): edit the Observer in MeshCore Configuration; quick configure joins the save (#5831)
body:
## Summary

The last item of #5797. Three changes the maintainer approved:

1. **The Analyzer Observer is edited in MeshCore Configuration.** Enable, region (IATA) and the broker list (add from presets or custom, edit URL / label / auth mode / token audience, remove with a confirm, max 8) now live in **MeshCore → Configuration → Analyzer Observer**, as a SaveBar draft (`useObserverConfigDraft`). The section is split into **Status / Brokers / Credentials** groups.
2. **Quick configure joins the save.** On Device Configuration → MQTT, picking an MQTT source fills the form and *stages* this source's `mqttLink`. Nothing is written until Save; Dismiss undoes both.
3. **One preset look.** A shared `PresetPicker` (chips) draws the Meshtastic broker presets (all three MQTT forms) and the Observer presets. The two preset tables stay separate.

## Decisions

- **Observer save path.** The draft saves through the route the Dashboard modal used: one `PUT /api/sources/:id` with the source's config (as the viewer sees it) and a rebuilt `observer` block. `mergeSourceConfigOnSave` still puts back secrets and masked URL parts, and the server calls `reconfigureObserver` once. The baseline moves only on an accepted save or when the stored block changes (re-seeded during render, the `useSectionBaseline` pattern). Nothing is written on mount.
- **Credentials stay out of the draft.** The signing key and each broker's username/password keep their own routes and buttons (per broker since #5834).
- **Permission.** Editing the broker list needs `configuration:write` **and** `sources:write` (the PUT checks the latter), like `canQuickConfig` (#5820). With only `configuration:write`, the list is read-only and says why.
- **Dashboard modal.** The Observer editor is replaced by a note and a **Configuration** button (it opens `/source/:id/#configuration`; MeshCorePage now opens that view on that hash). A save carries the stored observer block through unchanged (minus the list-only `brokerCount`), so editing a source never drops it. For a repeater an enabled block is turned off instead of failing the save.
- **No Observer at source creation.** I did not keep a minimal enable toggle in the "Add source" form. The Observer can't publish until it has brokers and a signing key or login, and those can only be set once the source exists, so the note says to save first and then configure it.
- **Quick configure order.** Save writes the device MQTT config first (only if those fields changed, so a pick that matches the current fields costs no extra `set_module_config`), then the link. If the device save fails, the link is not written. If the link write fails, the error is shown under the selector, the stage stays, and the next Save retries only the link. After a successful save the selector resets, so the same option can be picked again.
- **Moved module.** `DashboardPage.observerConfig.ts` → `src/components/MeshCore/observerConfig.ts` (plus its test). `DashboardPage.observerBrokers.module

title: feat(ui): danger zone last, in-app confirms, write gating on Device Configuration (#5830)
body:
## Summary

Part of the #5797 cleanup. Implements the decisions in #5830.

- **Danger zone last.** Meshtastic Device Configuration: Reboot and Purge Node Database move from the red box at the top to a **Danger zone** section at the end of the page, after Firmware Updates. Reload Config stays at the top as a header action on the Import/Export section; the "this writes to your node" warning stays there as a one-line note.
- **One shared look.** New `DangerZone` (`src/components/shared/config/DangerZone.tsx` + CSS module), built on `ConfigSection` with a new `tone="danger"` header. MeshCore's Device Management (reboot, key backup/restore) now uses it too.
- **In-app confirms, no `window.confirm`.** Meshtastic reboot and MeshCore reboot use `ConfirmDialog`. Purge (type `PURGE`) and MeshCore private-key import (type `IMPORT`) use `TypedConfirmDialog`. The action runs only from the dialog's Confirm. `useMeshCore` still sends `confirm: true` for the server's DANGER_CONFIRM_REQUIRED check, so the dialog is the guard and has no bypass.
- **Write gating.** The Meshtastic page checks `hasPermission('configuration', 'write', { sourceId })` for the current source. Every device/module section gets `canWrite` and passes it to its `ConfigSection` (fieldset disables the body); MQTT passes its existing `canEditMqtt`; PKI DM uses the same per-source check. Import and the danger buttons disable for read-only users. Export and Reload stay usable (they only read).
- **Admin Commands link.** The danger zone says shutdown, DFU and factory reset live on Admin Commands and links there (`buildAdminCommandsPath`). Admins only, since only they can open that page.
- **SectionNav:** `config-danger` ("Danger zone") moves to the end of `configurationNavItems`; `config-import-export` is now first and also matches "reload".
- Kept: MeshCore per-section Save buttons; MeshCore per-node schedule panels in Node Details.

### Judgment calls
- **Channels and Backup sections are not gated on `configuration:write`.** Channel saves are gated per slot (`channel_N` write) on the server, so a page-level gate would lock out channel-only writers. Backup's list has read-only downloads that the fieldset would disable; its writes are already refused server-side.
- Confirm words are fixed English (`PURGE`, `IMPORT`) so they stay stable across languages; the prompt around them is translated.
- Dropped now-unused en keys (`config.warning_title`, `config.warning_description`, `config.reboot_confirm`, `config.purge_confirm`); other locales are left for Weblate.

## Mesh impact

No new device writes. Reboot, purge and key import send exactly what they did before, only after the in-app confirm. Moving sections triggers no loads or saves on mount. No timers, no notifications.

## Tests

- `ConfigurationTab.dangerZone.test.tsx` (new): danger zone renders last and Import/Export first; reboot opens ConfirmDialog and sends only on Confirm; cancel sends nothing; purge needs `PURGE` (wrong case stays locked); r

title: feat(ui): one channel editing model for Meshtastic and MeshCore (#5829)
body:
## Summary

Meshtastic and MeshCore channel config now use the same editing model: each channel is a card that opens in place, like Auto Responder, and has its own **Save to device**.

### Shared pieces (`src/components/shared/config/`)
- **`ConfigItemCard`**: `TriggerCard` turned into a general card. It adds a leading badge, a notice line, optional Edit/Delete, an accent outline and a footer the caller supplies. `TriggerCard` now wraps it and adds the Done footer, so its callers did not change. `TriggerCard.module.css` moved to `ConfigItemCard.module.css`.
- **`ChannelKeyField`**: masked by default, with Show/Hide, Copy (the button reads "Copied" for a moment), Generate (`generateBytes`), `format: 'base64' | 'hex'`, an `allowedBytes` length check with `aria-invalid`, and `readOnly` + `hint` for derived keys. #5837 (`PasswordField`) is not merged yet, so the show/hide toggle lives inside this field.
- `channelKey.ts` (generate / length / base64-hex helpers), `ChannelEncryptionLabel` (built on `pskEncryptionStatus`), and `useDiscardGuard` + `DiscardChangesDialog`.

### Decisions applied
- **Inline cards on both protocols.** One card is open at a time. Opening another card (or Add, Import, Reorder) while the open card has unsaved edits asks **Discard changes / Keep editing**. Cancel drops the draft.
- **Save to device per channel.** It makes one write, sends no SaveBar, and never batches. On an existing channel it stays off until the draft changes.
- **Meshtastic**
  - Lists only configured slots (role != DISABLED); slot numbers stay visible.
  - **Add channel (slot N)** opens a new card on the lowest free slot (0–7). With all 8 in use the button is disabled, with the reason in its title and next to it.
  - Collapsed card shows: slot, name + AEAD badge, encryption chip, Primary/Secondary, Uplink/Downlink, position precision with accuracy, and the Channel Database key-collision warning (#3644).
  - The editor keeps: role select (same rules as before), position precision with accuracy readout, uplink/downlink.
  - Key field is base64. Valid lengths are 0/1/16/32 bytes. The AA== "no encryption" key still shows as empty, and clearing a field that held a key still sends `''` (#5835).
  - Gating: `canWrite = hasPermission('configuration','write',{ sourceId })` through `ConfigSection`. The server still checks `channel_N:write`.
  - Delete confirm uses the shared **ConfirmDialog**. Its text: "disables the channel on the device and permanently deletes its message history in MeshMonitor. The messages cannot be recovered." The confirm button reads "Delete channel and messages". I chose not to use TypedConfirmDialog: many channels have no name (or a 1–2 character name) to type, the device side can be re-added at once, and the dialog already names the purge on the button itself.
  - Kept: drag reorder + **Apply Order** (reboot) and per-slot JSON export/import. Import into an empty slot moved to an **Import to slot N** button next to Add. While a reorder is pend

## Summary

title: fix(config): expect the reboot that most Device Configuration saves cause (#5823)
body:
## Summary

Most Device Configuration saves make a Meshtastic node reboot about 7 s later, but the Configuration tab treated eight of them as reboot-free and the module saves as silent. The UI did not expect the TCP drop and did not re-read config afterwards. Now every save that reboots tells the app to expect it.

`src/utils/configRebootRules.ts` is the one place that says what each save does, so a new section only needs a row there. I checked it against `AdminModule.cpp` at v2.7.9, v2.7.20, v2.7.26, v2.8.0 and v2.8.1.

| Save | Before 2.8 | 2.8.0+ | Signal now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner, Device, Power, Display | reboots if certain fields changed | same | **possible** (no field compare, per maintainer) |
| Position, Network, Security | always | always | always |
| LoRa | reboots on radio changes | **never** (applied live) | always on < 2.8, none on 2.8+ (unknown version reads as < 2.8) |
| MQTT, Serial, ExtNotif, Store&Forward, Range Test, Telemetry, Canned Msg, Audio, Remote HW, NeighborInfo, Ambient Lighting, Detection Sensor, Paxcounter, Traffic Mgmt, TAK | always | always | always |
| Status Message | never (2.7.20+ clears `shouldReboot`) | never | none |
| MeshBeacon | n/a (2.8+ only) | never | none |

The table in #5823 said Status Message reboots on 2.7; it does not. It exists from 2.7.20, and every version that has it clears `shouldReboot`.

## What `onConfigChangeTriggeringReboot` does

It is `handleConfigChangeTriggeringReboot` in `App.tsx`: it sets the connection status to `rebooting` (which pauses the 5 s connection poll) and opens `RebootModal`. It **sends no reboot command and writes no config**. The modal waits 30 s, checks the connection, then polls `POST /api/nodes/refresh` (a local `want_config_id` + module-config read over the TCP link, no RF) until the node's `rebootCount` goes up. When it closes, App bumps `configRefreshTrigger`, and ConfigurationTab re-reads config from the server and reseeds its forms (`configVersion`, #5813). So the form is not stale after the reboot.

The callback now takes `'always' | 'possible'`.

## RebootModal changes

- **Wording.** For a possible reboot the title reads "Device May Restart" and the wait text "The node may restart to apply this change. Please wait...". If the node stays up, it closes with "Configuration saved. The node did not need to restart." A certain reboot keeps the old text.
- **Fewer polls for a possible reboot.** 5 polls instead of 20. A node that restarted reports the new count on the first poll after reconnect, so a node that did not restart no longer holds the screen for ~2 minutes and 20 refresh cycles.
- **Baseline read at open.** The modal now reads `rebootCount` when it opens, before the node restarts, not after the 30 s wait. Before, a reconnect that had already updated the count by then made the baseline equal the new count, so the modal polled all 20 times. This is a read of the server's copy; nothing goes to the node. title: fix(channels): clearable PSK, meshcore_mqtt guard, MeshCore Public slot, missing strings (#5826)
body:
Fixes the four channel bugs from #5826 before the Channels convergence. Each one has a test that fails on `main`.

## 1. Meshtastic PSK can't be cleared

The help text says "Leave empty for no encryption", but the client sent `psk || undefined` and the server kept the old key.

**Contract:** an absent or `null` `psk` keeps the stored key, as before. An explicit `psk: ''` means "no encryption".

- **Device bytes.** A cleared key is written as the 1-byte `0x00` key (`AA==`, the `none` shorthand), not a 0-byte key. In firmware `Channels::getKey`, a **SECONDARY** channel with a 0-byte PSK uses the primary's key, so an empty key would leave it encrypted. `0x00` turns encryption off for every role. `AQ==` (`0x01`) is the default public key, which is different again.
- **Server** (`channelRoutes.ts`, Meshtastic branch only): `''` becomes `NO_ENCRYPTION_PSK` (`AA==`). The route stores it and sends it, which matches what a device sync reports back for that slot. The MeshCore branch is unchanged: `''` still fails its 16-byte check.
- **Client** (`ChannelsConfigSection.tsx`): the client sends `''` only when the user empties a field that held a key. A field that opened empty sends nothing, so a save from a user who never received the key can't wipe it. An `AA==` key shows as an empty field.
- `AA==` now reads as "no key" everywhere:
  - **Server:** `getEncryptionStatus` reports `none`, and `normalizePsk` in `channelCollision.ts` maps it to no key, so it never collides.
  - **Client:** one shared helper in `src/utils/publicChannel.ts` (`pskEncryptionStatus` / `hasPrivatePsk`) now backs `ChannelsTab`, `ChannelsConfigSection`, `NodeFilterPopup`, `AdminCommandsTab` and `RadioConfigurationSection`.
  - **Clamp warning:** `isKnownPublicChannel` counts `AA==` as public, so the 2.8 precision-clamp warning still fires on a cleared channel.
  - Before this, a device-synced "encryption off" channel showed a lock icon.
- `NO_ENCRYPTION_PSK` lives in `src/server/utils/channelPsk.ts`.
- **Other callers of the PUT:** the only other caller is the Meshtastic delete flow, which already sends `psk: ''` with `role: 0`. That disabled slot now gets `0x00` instead of an empty key, which makes no difference on a disabled channel. Import uses its own route and is unchanged.
- **Side fix, in the route:** the PUT route's device push used to pass a stored `null` PSK through to `channelPskToBytes`, which threw, so the push failed with only a log line. The route (`channelRoutes.ts`) now turns a `null` key into "no key" before the push, the same as `''` always was. `channelPskToBytes` itself is unchanged.

## 2. `meshcore_mqtt` sources took the Meshtastic branch

The PUT and DELETE routes checked `sourceType === 'meshcore'`, so an ingest source fell through to the Meshtastic path. On DELETE that path purged the source's messages and channel row. Both routes now return **400 `SOURCE_HAS_NO_DEVICE`** for a `meshcore_mqtt` source. The check runs after the per-channel permission check, so a c

title: fix(meshcore): Observer credentials are set and cleared per broker (#5825)
body:
## Bug

The MeshCore → Configuration → Analyzer Observer section had one "Broker username / password" block. Its requests carried no `brokerKey`:

- **Clear** sent a key-less `DELETE`, which ran `store.clear()` and wiped **every** broker's stored credential. The confirm mentioned one credential.
- **Save** sent a key-less `PUT`, which stored a shared "legacy" credential. Only a broker matching the old `observer.brokerUrl` reads it, and a Dashboard-modal save drops `brokerUrl`, so after one the page still said "Stored for user X" for a credential no broker used.
- The signing-key block followed `brokers[0].authMode` only, so a mixed setup whose first broker used a password hid the key block.

## Fix

- The single block is gone. Each username/password broker's card in the Brokers panel (`MeshCoreObserverBrokerPanel`, new `renderBrokerExtra` slot) shows that broker's status ("Stored for user X" / "Not set") with **Set** and **Clear** (new `MeshCoreObserverBrokerCredentials`). Both send that broker's `brokerKey`.
- **Clear** confirms through the shared `ConfirmDialog` (not `window.confirm`), and the title and message name the broker.
- `useObserverCredentials` now needs a `brokerKey` for `saveCredentials` / `clearCredentials`. The one key-less action left, `clearLegacyCredential`, sends `?legacy=1`. One request at a time across all brokers, since the store does a read-modify-write.
- The signing-key block shows when **any** broker uses token auth.

## Legacy handling

- Store: new `clearLegacy(sourceId)` removes only the legacy entry and keeps every per-broker entry. It deletes the row once nothing is left. If the row can't be decrypted (SESSION_SECRET changed), it deletes the whole row, since nothing in it can be read and this is the only way to forget it when nothing new can be stored. New `getLegacyUsername()`.
- Route: `GET/PUT/DELETE /credentials` responses gain `legacy: { username } | null`, redacted to `{ username: null }` for no-login callers. `DELETE ?legacy=1` removes only the legacy entry. `?legacy=` with any other value, or together with `brokerKey`, returns 400 `INVALID_PARAMETER`.
- **A bare key-less DELETE now does the same as `?legacy=1`.** I grepped for other callers: the Dashboard modal only PUTs with `brokerKey`, and no system test or script calls DELETE. So nothing relied on the wipe-everything behaviour, and the route comment documents the change. A key-less PUT still stores the legacy credential, kept for backward compatibility, but no UI sends one.
- UI: if a legacy credential exists, a one-line note names it and offers **Remove old shared credential**, with a confirm that says per-broker logins are kept. If the row can't be decrypted, the page offers **Remove unreadable credentials**.

Permissions are unchanged: writes still need `configuration:write` on the source, and no response carries a password.

**Mesh impact:** none. The Observer publishes over the internet, not LoRa. Credential changes still call `refreshObserverPubli

title: fix(geofence): record trigger results on the source's own key
body:
**Bug.** `MeshtasticManager.updateGeofenceTriggerResult` read `geofenceTriggers` from the source's own key (`getSettingForSource`) but wrote the result back with the **global** `setSetting`. Each geofence fire copied that source's trigger list into the global key, where it bled into other sources through the settings GET-merge. The timer-trigger result writer had the same bug, already fixed; see `meshtasticManager.timerTriggerScope.perSource.test.ts`.

**Fix.** Write back with `setSourceSetting(this.sourceId, 'geofenceTriggers', …)`.

**Test.** `meshtasticManager.geofenceTriggerScope.perSource.test.ts` checks that the read and the write both use the source's own key, and that the global key is never written.

I spotted this while fixing #5827.

**Mesh impact:** none, but this removes a way for one source's geofence triggers to fire on another source.

title: fix(timers): keep the server's run state on save; one name, Timer Triggers (#5827)
body:
**Bug.** The settings page loads the timer list once and posts the whole list back on save. That save sent the page's stale `lastRun`, `lastResult` and `lastError`, overwriting a newer run the scheduler had recorded since the page loaded.

**Fix.** Both save routes take the run state from the stored trigger with the same id. A trigger the server hasn't seen yet starts with no run state.
- Meshtastic: `POST /api/settings` with `timerTriggers`, per-source and global.
- MeshCore: `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/automation/timers`.
- The shared helper is `src/server/utils/timerRunState.ts`.

**Naming.** The Meshtastic section was titled "Timed Events". It now reads **Timer Triggers**, matching the nav button, the docs anchor and MeshCore. The docs heading keeps "(Timed Events)" as an alias.

**Tests**
- Helper unit tests.
- A harness route test for each save route: stale `lastRun` is ignored, the stored value is kept, and a new trigger starts clean.
- The related Timer Triggers suites pass. tsc (app and server) and `lint:ci` are clean.

**Mesh impact:** none. The scheduler's timing is unchanged, and a save still restarts it as before.

Closes #5827. Refs #5797.

title: fix(meshcore): per-node schedule toggles roll back on a failed save and ignore stale replies
body:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs in the three per-node MeshCore schedule panels (Telemetry Retrieval, Neighbours Retrieval, Time Sync), which mount in `MeshCoreDirectMessagesView` for the selected remote node.

### What reproduced (each with a failing test first)

1. **No rollback on a failed PATCH: reproduced in all three panels.** The checkbox flips before the PATCH returns. If the PATCH failed (error body or thrown fetch), the box stayed flipped, so the UI said "On" while the server still had "Off". A failed interval save left the typed value in the field the same way.
2. **Cross-node race on save: reproduced in all three panels.** The panels are not keyed by node, and `save()` set state with no guard. A save that resolved after the user picked another node painted node A's config onto node B. (With a naive rollback, a late *failure* would also roll node B back, so the test covers that too.)
3. **Cross-node race on the initial GET: did NOT reproduce.** The load effect already has a `cancelled` flag. A regression test now pins that behaviour; no code change.

### Fix

- `save(patch, rollback)` now takes a rollback. On a failed save it restores the previous checkbox value or interval and shows the existing error text (no new wording).
- A `currentEndpoint` ref (set in the existing load effect) names the node on screen. `save()` drops any reply, success or failure, whose endpoint no longer matches. `saving` still clears in `finally`.

I guarded inside each panel instead of adding `key={selected}` in the parent so the fix lives with the code it protects and the panels can be tested alone.

### Mesh impact

These PATCHes change RF poll schedules, so the request count stays the same: one PATCH per checkbox change, the interval still commits on blur only, no new effects, and "Poll Now" / "Sync Now" are untouched. No new packets or timers. The tests assert exactly one PATCH per toggle and none while typing.

## Tests

New `src/components/MeshCore/MeshCoreNodeScheduleConfig.saveRace.test.tsx`, run against all three panels (21 tests):
- a failed PATCH (error body, and a thrown fetch) puts the checkbox back; exactly one PATCH
- a successful PATCH keeps the new state
- a failed interval PATCH puts the field back; typing sends nothing, blur sends one PATCH
- node A's late save success does not paint onto node B
- node A's late save failure does not roll node B back or show A's error
- node A's late GET does not paint onto node B (passed before the fix too)

15 of the 21 failed before the fix. All pass after it.

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npm run lint:ci` (in-repo FAIL lines): none
- Full Vitest suite (`--maxWorkers=2`): 2103 files passed, 32845 tests passed, 0 failed, JSON `success: true`, no Errors line. PG/MySQL containers were not running, so those suites skipped (this change is frontend only).

Refs #5797

title: fix(mqtt): gate the device MQTT form on configuration:write
body:
**Bug:** the device MQTT form (Device Configuration → MQTT) checked `sources:write`, but its save route `POST /api/config/mqtt` checks `configuration:write`.
- A user with only `configuration:write` saw the form locked, though their save would succeed.
- A user with only `sources:write` could edit the form, but the save then failed with a 403.

**Fix:**
- The form is gated on `configuration:write`.
- **Quick configure** also writes this source's `mqttLink` (`PUT /api/sources/:id`), so its select needs **both** permissions.
- Admins are unaffected.

Tests: the existing permission tests are updated, plus new cases for configuration-only, sources-only and both.

Found while auditing the MQTT/Observer pair for #5797.

Mesh impact: none. This is UI gating only, and the server already enforced `configuration:write`.

Part of #5797. Auto Acknowledge and Auto Announce now use the same field groups, in the same order, with the same group headings, on Meshtastic and MeshCore. Protocol-only fields stay inside their group.

title: fix(config): SaveBar baselines follow successful saves and reloads
body:
Refs #5797

## What was wrong

All five suspected bugs reproduced. I wrote `ConfigurationTab.saveBarBaselines.test.tsx` first, against unchanged `main`. It drives the real NodeIdentity, Device and NeighborInfo sections through `ConfigurationTab`, with a stand-in SaveBar and the API mocked. All 7 tests failed before the fix:

| # | Bug | Failing test evidence (pre-fix) |
|---|-----|------|
| 1 | The section stays dirty after a successful save. `hasChanges` was a `useMemo` over a ref it never listed as a dependency. | `a successful save clears the section`: `expected 'true' to be 'false'` |
| 2 | A failed save becomes the baseline. Every page handler catches its own error and resolves, and the section moved the ref after `await onSave()` whatever the outcome. | `a failed save stays dirty, and Dismiss goes back...`: Dismiss left `'Bravo Node'`, expected `'Alpha Node'` |
| 3 | Device re-baselined whenever the page-wide `isSaving` flag went false. Saving any other section, or a failed Device save, made unsaved Device edits the baseline. | `saving another section does not turn unsaved Device edits into the baseline` and `a failed Device save keeps the edit pending`: Dismiss did not revert the LED checkbox |
| 4 | Reload config left stale baselines in every section except Telemetry. | `Reload config re-baselines...`: node-identity was `'true'` (phantom change) right after the reload |
| 5 | NeighborInfo recorded the pre-clamp interval. | Once 1 was fixed, I put back `commit(values)` (pre-clamp) and the test failed: `expected 'true' to be 'false'`. The handler did send 14400. |

How bug 5 happens in the UI: the interval field has `min=14400`, so an out-of-range value blocks Save while the field is visible. The clamp still runs when NeighborInfo is turned off, which hides the field, or when the loaded value is under the floor.

## The fix

- **`src/hooks/useSectionBaseline.ts`** (new): keeps the baseline in **state** and returns `{ baseline, hasChanges, commit }`.
  - It compares scalars by value and arrays/objects by content (admin keys, beacon targets).
  - When `reseedKey` changes, it takes the current values during render, so the first render after a reload is already clean.
  - `keepOnReseed` lists fields the reload does not refresh. Position keeps fixed lat/lon/alt; MQTT keeps `mapShouldReportLocation`.
- **`ConfigurationTab.tsx`**:
  - All 25 `handleSave*` handlers now resolve `true` only when the API call succeeded, and `false` on error or when a validation check holds the save. Toasts and status messages are unchanged.
  - `telemetryConfigVersion` is now `configVersion`. It is bumped once per successful Reload config, in the same batch as the setters. It goes to the sections that reload refreshes: NodeIdentity, Device, LoRa, Position, Power, Display, Telemetry, MQTT, NeighborInfo, Network.
- **Sections**: `onSave` is now typed `() => Promise<boolean>`, and each section calls `commit` only on `true`.
  - Converted to the hook: NodeIdentity, Device
