title: feat(ui): one Auto Responder workflow for Meshtastic and MeshCore (#5808)
body:
## Summary

Both Auto Responder sections now follow one "hybrid" workflow, built from shared pieces in `src/components/shared/automation/`:

- **`TriggerCard`**: collapsed, it shows the enable toggle (MeshCore only, since Meshtastic triggers have no `enabled` field), the title (MeshCore name, or the highlighted Meshtastic pattern), a one-line response summary, chips (type, channels, DM, multiline, verify, cooldown, delay, scope), and Edit and Delete. Expanded, it shows the protocol's editor with a **Done** button. Only one card is open at a time, and a new trigger opens expanded. The editor's number fields report to a card scope nested in the section scope, so Done and the SaveBar stay off while a field holds invalid text (#5649).
- **`ConfirmDialog`**: Delete now asks first on both protocols. It portals to `body` and uses `useDialogA11y` (role=dialog, Escape, focus trap and restore). Deleting only edits the draft; the SaveBar saves it.
- **`PatternTestBox`**: a multi-line sample box. For each line it lists the matching triggers and a preview of the reply. It is protocol-agnostic (`match(trigger, text)`) and purely local.
- **`TriggerListFilter`**: search plus type filter, shown once a section has more than 5 triggers.

Edits go straight to the section draft. The existing SaveBars (`auto-responder`, `meshcore-auto-responder`) still save, using the same endpoints and payloads.

## Workflow: before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Meshtastic add | Large inline Add form (with its own live test) above the list | **Add Trigger** button opens a new expanded card |
| Meshtastic edit | `TriggerItem` inline edit with its own Save/Cancel | Edit expands the card, Done collapses it, SaveBar saves |
| Meshtastic test | Quick-test input plus a separate multi-line test with details/debug toggles and live HTTP/script buttons | One local `PatternTestBox` (mode `first`, flags shadowed matches) |
| MeshCore list | Always-open editable cards; Remove with no confirm | Collapsed cards with an on/off switch; Delete asks first |
| MeshCore add | Small add card (name, pattern, response) | Same **Add trigger** button and expanded card as Meshtastic |
| MeshCore test | none | Local `PatternTestBox` (mode `all`, mirrors server regex matching) |

## Moved fields (Meshtastic): every Add-form and edit-form field is now in `auto-responder/TriggerEditor.tsx`

Pattern(s) with the "N patterns" badge, valid/count/parameter chips, response type (text / HTTP / script / **traceroute** / mailbox; the add form lacked traceroute), text response, HTTP URL, script select, traceroute target plus help, mailbox help, **script args** (edit form only before), cooldown with help and description, channels (incl. **"none" for scripts**, edit form only before), multiline, verify (DM only), and a response preview with example values. title: fix(channels): send sourceId with channel export
body:
Channel **Export** (Device Configuration → Channels, and Admin Commands for the local node) always failed: `GET /api/channels/:id/export` requires `?sourceId` (`requireSourceId('query')`), but `apiService.exportChannel` never sent it.

Verified on the dev container: without `sourceId` → `400 MISSING_SOURCE_ID`; with it → `200`.

Both callers already resolve a concrete source with `useResolvedSourceId()`; they now pass it through. New unit test in `api.test.ts`.

Found while auditing Channels for #5797.

Mesh impact: none (read-only download).

title: ci(docker): give the amd64/arm64 release build room to finish
body:
## Summary

The v4.17.1-rc2 Docker build failed twice with `The action 'Build and push (amd64, arm64)' has timed out after 40 minutes`. This was not a code error.

The emulated arm64 half of `build-main` has been running right at the 40-minute step cap:

| Release | Build and push |
|---|---|
| v4.17.0-rc5 | 33m |
| v4.17.0-rc6 | 36m |
| v4.17.0-rc7 | 35m |
| v4.17.0-rc8 | 39m57s |
| v4.17.0-rc9 | 29m |
| v4.17.0 | 39m18s |
| v4.17.1-rc1 | 37m |
| v4.17.1-rc2 | timed out at 40m, twice |

This raises the step cap to 70 min and the job cap to 75 min, with a comment. It is the same fix `build-armv7` got earlier, and for the same reason: when `build-main` fails, the multi-arch `:VERSION` tag is never published.

A re-run of the rc2 run still uses the workflow file at the rc2 tag, so this only helps releases cut after it merges.

## Mesh impact

None. CI only.

title: fix(packet-monitor): recognise fw 2.8 NodeDB replays by packet id (#5426)
body:
## Summary

Refs #5426 (reported again on 4.17.0). Firmware 2.8's NodeDB replay bursts are back in the Packet Monitor because the #5450 guard measured the wrong thing.

## Cause

#5450 dropped a replay only when its `rx_time` was more than 120 s old, on the belief that a replay keeps the original receive time. Firmware v2.8.1 `PhoneAPI.cpp` shows otherwise. Since meshtastic/firmware#11014 (2.8.0), `makeReplayPositionPacket()` and its telemetry and node-status siblings set:

- `rx_time = header->last_heard`, the node's last-heard time, not when that position was received. **Any node heard in the last two minutes therefore produces a replay that looks live.** On a busy mesh that is the reported burst.
- `has_rx_time` only when `last_heard` is a wall-clock time. A node with no clock sends **no `rx_time`**, which we also treated as live.
- `rx_rssi` deliberately absent.
- `id = makeReplayPacketId(num, rx_time, kind)`: `h = num; h = h*2654435761 + rx_time; h = h*2654435761 + kind` (uint32, 0 → 1).

## Fix

- `isFirmwareReplayPacket(from, id, rx_time)` in `replayGuard.ts` recomputes that id for the replayed kinds: device metrics (2), position / environment metrics (3), node status (36). A real packet id matches by chance about once in 4 billion.
- **Verified on real data:** in the dev container's packet log, the one replay row that leaked through matches exactly. It was the only match among the 400 recent LoRa position and telemetry rows checked, and none of the real receptions (all with RSSI) matched.
- Wired into every place that relied on the age check to exclude replays:
  - the **packet log**
  - the **per-transport packet counters**
  - **live node discovery** (a replay could fire a "new node" event, and with it notifications)
  - the **cross-source link recorder**
- The packet log also treats an RF packet with **no `rx_time` and RSSI explicitly absent** as a replay: the no-clock case, where the id cannot be recomputed. A pre-2.8 bare `0` RSSI does not trigger it.
- The existing age rule stays for 2.8 alphas from before #11014.

## Mesh impact

None. Read-side classification only: nothing is sent, and fewer false "new node" events fire.

## Test plan

- [x] `isFirmwareReplayPacket`: the real captured packet matches; an id, sender or rx_time off by one does not; every replayed kind matches against an independent BigInt implementation; missing inputs do not
- [x] Packet log: a fresh-rx_time replay is caught by its id where the age rule misses it; the no-clock case is caught; RSSI present or a bare 0 is kept
- [x] Node discovery: a fresh-looking replay is not a discovery; a real packet still is
- [x] Full Vitest suite: 2,091 files, 32,719 passed, 0 failed; `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean
- [ ] Not yet confirmed by the reporter on their meshtasticd install

title: fix(docker): BLE bridge healthcheck follows the BLE link, not the TCP port
body:
## Summary

Follows Yeraze/meshtastic-ble-bridge#20 ([comment](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshtastic-ble-bridge/pull/20#issuecomment-6174639774): "Configurator not up to date").

That PR made the bridge touch the file named by `HEALTH_FILE` every 10 s while the BLE link is up, and exit 1 when it cannot reconnect. Its image and `docker-compose.yml` check the file's age. MeshMonitor's Configurator, `docker-compose.ble.yml` and the BLE bridge docs still checked only that port 4403 accepted connections, so a wedged bridge read healthy.

## Changes

- **Docker Configurator** (`DockerComposeConfigurator.vue`) and **`docker-compose.ble.yml`**: set `HEALTH_FILE=/tmp/ble-bridge.health`; the healthcheck checks the file is under 60 s old; `start_period` 60 s. Same check as the bridge's own image.
- **MeshMonitor's dependency on the bridge is now `service_started`** (was `service_healthy`). With the new check, "healthy" means "BLE link up", so `docker compose up` would refuse to start MeshMonitor while the node is out of range. MeshMonitor reconnects to the bridge on its own. This matches how the serial bridge is wired.
- **Docs** (`docs/configuration/ble-bridge.md`): the overlay snippet now carries the health check. A new "Health check and recovery" section explains that the bridge exits to recover and Docker does not restart unhealthy containers, and gives the reason for the dependency.

`command: ${BLE_ADDRESS}` stays: the image's entrypoint is still `python -m cli.main`.

## Mesh impact

None. Docker setup only.

## Test plan

- [x] `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.ble.yml config` parses and renders the new healthcheck and `condition: service_started`
- [ ] Not run against a live BLE node

@@ -192,9 +192,24 @@ services:

     environment:
       - BLE_ADDRESS=${BLE_ADDRESS:-}
+      - HEALTH_FILE=/tmp/ble-bridge.health
     command: ${BLE_ADDRESS:-}
+    healthcheck:
+      test: ["CMD", "python3", "-c", "import os, sys, time; f = '/tmp/ble-bridge.health'; sys.exit(0 if os.path.exists(f) and time.time() - os.path.getmtime(f) < 60 else 1)"]
+      interval: 30s
+      timeout: 10s
+      retries: 3
+      start_period: 60s
 ```
 
+#### Health check and recovery
+
+The bridge touches the file named by `HEALTH_FILE` every 10 seconds while the BLE link is up and data is flowing. The health check reports the container healthy only while that file is fresh, so `docker ps` shows `unhealthy` when the link is down, even though port 4403 still accepts connections.

+When the bridge cannot reconnect after 10 attempts, it exits with code 1 and `restart: unless-stopped` starts it again. Docker does not restart a container just because it is unhealthy; recovery comes from the exit.

+MeshMonitor depends on the bridge with `condition: service_started`, so MeshMonitor still starts when the node is out of range, and reconnects once the bridge is up.

## Summary

Refs #5013. A step-by-step **MQTT Setup Guide** (`docs/features/mqtt-setups.md`, at meshmonitor.org/features/mqtt-setups), plus links to it from every MQTT settings surface in the app.

> **Merge #5799 first.** This branch sits on it because the guide documents its behaviour ("bridges do not relay each other", **Relay traffic from other bridges**). Until #5799 merges, this PR also shows that commit; after, only the docs commit remains.

## The guide

- **The parts and which way traffic flows:** a table for the node MQTT module, broker, bridge and source link: what each takes from where, sends where, and whether it can put packets on the air. It separates "monitor only" from "bridge into the mesh", which the reporter asked for.
- **Setup 1: one node to an upstream server**, with filters: automation traffic (the production problem fixed in #5787), uplink channels, topic filters, bounding box, mode. Explains why to use broker + bridge rather than a bridge alone: a node linked straight to a bridge skips the uplink filters and `ok_to_mqtt`.
- **Setup 2: several nodes:** the broker delivers node A's uplink to node B; when that means a second transmission; firmware dedup; Downlink Enabled on one node per RF area; cap at 0.
- **Setup 3: one node to several servers:** one bridge per server; downlink copies from two servers; bridges do not relay each other; recommended mode per server; do not point two per-gateway bridges at one server (client-ID takeover).
- **How much airtime downlink costs**, plus a pre-flight checklist.

## In the app

- New `MqttDocsLinks` (setup guide + reference) on the bridge settings page, the Add Source form for brokers and bridges, and Device → MQTT Module (next to Quick configure).
- The hop-limit fields link to the airtime section.
- Bridge **Mode** help now says which way each mode moves traffic.
- **Bridge MQTT proxy to** help says how to link a bridge instead (it lists brokers only).

## Reference fixes (`mqtt-broker.md`)

- Linking a bridge is done with **Quick configure**, not Sources → Edit (the docs said otherwise).
- A node linked straight to a bridge skips the bridge's uplink filters and `ok_to_mqtt` check.
- The feature matrix no longer lists geo among the uplink filters (there is none).
- A tip at the top points to the guide; the guide is in the sidebar under Integrations.

## Mesh impact

None. Docs and links only; no sends, events or timers.

title: fix(mqtt): bridges stop relaying each other's upstream; close the echo race (#5013)
body:
## Summary

Refs #5013 (the reporter asked whether MeshMonitor could inject the same MQTT traffic more than once, or loop it). Mapping every MQTT path for a setup guide turned up two real problems, both fixed here. The guide itself follows in a separate PR.

## Problems

1. **Two bridges on one broker relayed each other's upstream.** Bridge A republishes upstream A's traffic into the broker; the broker raises `local-packet`; bridge B treated it as local and uplinked it to upstream B. In per-gateway mode that publish went out under the foreign gateway's client ID. When the two upstreams already share traffic, a packet could pass back and forth without end: a test with the relay forced on counted **1,289** uplinks of one packet in under a second.
2. **A bridge's echo check raced.** Aedes emits `publish` synchronously inside `publish()`, so the bridge's own `handleUplink` ran before the downlink echo was recorded (it was recorded in `.then()`). A bridge could send its own downlinked packet back upstream once. The mqttLink path already records first for this reason; the loop test tolerated "1 original + at most 1 echo".

## Fix

- The broker keeps a 60 s map of (from, id) → the bridge that brought it in (`markBridgeOrigin` / `bridgeOriginOf`, same bound as the skip-raise marks). A bridge does not uplink a packet another bridge brought down. Skips count in `uplinkBridgeRelayDrops`.
- New per-bridge option **Relay traffic from other bridges** (`relayOtherBridges`), **off by default**, for anyone who means to join two upstreams. Validated, redacted like the other bridge booleans, with a "Not relayed so far" count on the bridge settings page.
- A bridge never sends the same (topic, id) upstream twice within a minute, and never hands the same packet to the broker twice. That keeps the opt-in from looping too.
- The downlink echo is recorded before the local republish.
- Reference docs: new "Bridges do not relay each other" section; corrected loop-suppression text and the feature matrix.

## Behaviour change

A setup with several bridges on one broker that relied on upstream-to-upstream relaying stops relaying until **Relay traffic from other bridges** is ticked. Everything that started locally (nodes, client-proxy devices, other MQTT clients) is uplinked as before.

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime:** none added. A packet that both upstreams carry still reaches the radios at most once per bridge, and the firmware drops repeats. Less upstream traffic overall.
2. **Spam:** fewer publishes, and the loop is closed. No events or notifications.
3. **Timers:** none. The marks are in memory for 60 s, the same window the existing echo caches use. A restart drops them, which is safe: the worst case is a single relay during that minute.

## Test plan

- [x] Two bridges on one broker: the other bridge's downlink is not uplinked (drop counted, upstream sees only the original); with the opt-in it is relayed exactly once (no loop); locally originated traffic still goes out

title: feat(meshcore): remember and resume remote-admin sessions (#5785)
body:
## Summary

Closes #5785. MeshMonitor now remembers a MeshCore remote-admin login. Once a session exists, the console can resume it, and scheduled jobs can send commands, without a fresh login exchange on the air.

Decisions follow the reporter's answers on the issue: sessions do not expire, they survive a MeshMonitor restart, and scheduled jobs reuse them.

## Firmware basis (meshcore-dev/MeshCore main @ a366955cb2)

- A repeater drops a CLI DM from a sender that is not in its ACL, with no reply (`Mesh::onRecvPacket` only tries peers from `searchPeersByHash`, which on a repeater scans the client ACL). So a stale session shows up as a plain CLI timeout.
- CLI text runs only for an admin client (`MyMesh::onPeerDataRecv`).
- Admin ACL entries are saved to flash about 5 s after the login and reloaded at boot, so they survive a repeater reboot. Guest logins are not saved. LRU eviction of non-admins happens only when the table is full; there is no idle timeout.

## What changed

**Backend**
- Migration 204 `meshcore_admin_sessions` (per source: target key, our companion's key at login time, login time, isAdmin). Idempotent on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. Purged with the source. Backed up (it holds no secret; see below).
- A session counts only while the connected companion's public key matches the one that logged in, so a different radio on the source gets no session. It is not cleared on disconnect, because the ACL lives on the remote.
- Recorded on every successful **admin** login (`/admin/login`, `/admin/login-with-saved`, `ensureSavedLogin`). Cleared on a refused login, on forgetting the stored password, and by the new **Log out**.
- `ensureSavedLogin()` resumes a live session with no login. When a resumed session then gets no reply (time sync, both neighbour paths), MeshMonitor clears it, does **one** fresh saved-password login, and retries **once**. There are no loops.
- New routes: `GET /admin/session/:publicKey` (remote_admin read, database only) and `DELETE /admin/session/:publicKey` (remote_admin write, sends nothing). Both use `ok()`/`fail()` and are scoped by `sourceIdFrom: 'params.id'`.

**Frontend (remote console)**
- On mount it reads the session (no airtime). With a session it shows **Resume session** (enables the console, sends nothing), **Log in again**, and the login time. Logged in, it shows **Log out**.
- On a resumed session, a CLI timeout adds: "No reply. If the node rebooted or dropped the session, log in again."
- It still never logs in or resumes on its own.

**Docs**: `MESHCORE_REMOTE_ADMIN.md` (a new "Remembered admin sessions" section with citations, plus the corrected "wiped on reboot" claim and cost model) and `docs/features/meshcore.md` ("Resuming a session").

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime: lower.** A resumed console command is 2 packets (command + reply) instead of 4. A scheduled time sync is 2 instead of 4 with a live session. A stale session costs at worst 1 + 4 (the command that times out, then login and retry), on

title: fix(mqtt): raise encrypted uplinks by their real portnum (#5791)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5791. "Raise hop count for backhaul" never matched packets from a phone's MQTT client proxy, because the proxy uplinks them channel-encrypted. The broker's forward hook could not read the portnum, so it treated it as unknown and only clamped.

## What changed

- `ChannelDecryptionService.peekPortnum()`: a synchronous read of an encrypted packet's portnum using the channel keys already cached. It never refreshes the cache, writes to the DB or logs; the ingest path's `tryDecrypt` still does those. It honours the enable switch, name validation, hash-first ordering and `maxDecryptionAttempts`. `tryDecrypt`'s candidate ordering moved into a shared `orderedCandidates()` helper with no change in behaviour.
- `MqttBrokerManager.transformForwardedPayload()` uses it when `decoded` is absent. Both radio egress paths (Aedes `authorizeForward` and the mqttLink path in `meshtasticManager`) go through this one function.
- `hop_limit` sits in the MeshPacket header, outside the ciphertext, so the envelope is re-encoded around the **same encrypted bytes**. Nothing is decrypted on the wire or re-encrypted.
- The broker loads the channel cache at start when a raise is configured, so the first packet is not missed.
- Clamp exemptions now also apply to encrypted packets we can read.
- Docs: `docs/features/mqtt-broker.md` explains that encrypted packets need a matching key in the channel database.

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime**: no new packets. A raise the operator has already turned on now also applies to encrypted packets whose key MeshMonitor holds, for the portnums they opted into. Those packets now flood up to the target (1–3) hops, as the setting already promised. The existing UI warnings ("Raising text is loud") apply unchanged, and the cap of 3 and the clamp still hold.
2. **Spam**: none. No events, notifications or automations, and no retries.
3. **Timers**: none.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests use a real AES-CTR packet encrypted with the default key: encrypted text is raised; the ciphertext survives byte for byte with no `decoded` added; a portnum that was not opted in is left alone; a clamp exemption is honoured; nothing is raised when server-side decryption is off. The existing "no key opens it ⇒ never raised, still clamped" tests still pass.
- [x] Full Vitest suite: 2,086 files, 31,846 tests passed, 0 failed
- [x] `tsc` (server) clean; `lint:ci` clean
- [ ] Not tried against a live phone client proxy

title: feat(auto-ack): nearer nodes answer a channel message first (#5788)
body:
## Summary

Biases the Auto-Acknowledge channel wait by hop count, so the MeshMonitor instance nearest the sender tends to answer and the farther ones more often stay silent.

Closes #5788. Suggested by @huntchak.

## What changed

Before a channel auto-ack, MeshMonitor waits a random time, then stays quiet if enough other nodes already answered. That wait was a flat 5 to 30 seconds for everyone.

Now the **lower bound rises 3 seconds per hop** the triggering message travelled to reach this node. The 30-second upper bound does not move.

| Hops | Window |
|---|---|
| 0 (direct) | 5–30 s |
| 1 | 8–30 s |
| 2 | 11–30 s |
| 3 | 14–30 s |
| 7 | 26–30 s |

- The floor never comes within 2 s of the ceiling, so two instances at the same distance still spread out.
- Unknown, negative or non-numeric hop counts add nothing. More than 7 counts as 7. A packet relayed over MQTT has no usable hop count and gets no extra wait.
- With a Pre-Send Delay over 5 s, the bias is added inside that delay's own 25 s window, as before.
- Direct messages are untouched.

The penalty is a constant (`AUTO_ACK_HOP_PENALTY_MS = 3000`), not a setting: the ordering only works when every instance uses the same number. The maintainer chose 3 s over the issue's 2 s.

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime**: no new packet. It should lower airtime: the nearest instance fires earlier, and distant ones are more likely to count its answer and skip theirs under the existing `autoAckMaxResponses` cap.
2. **Spam**: nothing can send more than before. The wait is still bounded by the same ceiling, the same pending-slot limit and the same cooldown.
3. **Timers**: none added. The existing one-shot wait just gets a different length; nothing persists and a settings save changes nothing.

## Test plan

- [x] Floors for 0–7 hops, ceiling fixed at 30 s, a spread of at least 2 s at every hop count
- [x] A nearer instance never draws a later wait than a farther one for the same roll
- [x] Bad hop values (negative, NaN, Infinity, undefined, fractional, > 7)
- [x] Hop bias on top of a long Pre-Send Delay
- [x] Existing wait tests unchanged (the new argument defaults to 0)
- [x] Full Vitest suite 31,080 passed, 0 failed (PostgreSQL/MySQL suites skipped: no schema change); `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean
- [ ] Not exercised on the rig: it needs two MeshMonitor instances at different hop distances from one sender

title: fix(mqtt): drop automation uplinks on the client-proxy path too (#5414)
body:
## Summary

The MQTT bridge option **Don't uplink MeshMonitor automation traffic** did not cover one uplink path, so Auto-Ack tapbacks (and other automation sends) could still reach the upstream broker.

Refs #5414.

## Cause

There are two ways a packet reaches a bridge for uplink:

1. **From the embedded broker**: a node publishes to MeshMonitor's broker, the broker emits `local-packet`, and the bridge's `handleUplink` runs. This path has the automation check.
2. **Client proxy**: a TCP-connected node with MQTT client proxy on, linked straight to a bridge (`mqttLink`), hands each uplink to MeshMonitor as `FromRadio.mqttClientProxyMessage`. `MeshtasticManager.handleDeviceMqttProxyMessage` forwards it to `MqttBridgeManager.publish()`, which published upstream with **no automation check**.

## Fix

`MqttBridgeManager.publish()` now, when `dropAutomationUplinks` is on, decodes the ServiceEnvelope and drops a packet whose `(from, id)` the automation tracker knows. It counts in `uplinkAutomationDrops`, the same counter the other path uses. A payload that does not decode as a ServiceEnvelope (a JSON topic, a map report) is published as before. With the option off, nothing is decoded.

## Not covered here

On the client-proxy path the bridge's uplink filters and the `ok_to_mqtt` gate are also skipped. That predates this option and is a separate question (the device already applies `ok_to_mqtt` before it proxies), so it is left alone.

## Mesh impact

None on air. This only stops packets from being published upstream; nothing is sent, and no timer is added.

## Test plan

- [x] New cases on `publish()`: an automation send is dropped and counted; a manual send goes out; option off publishes and never decodes; a non-envelope payload goes out; another node's packet with the same id goes out
- [x] Existing `handleUplink` cases unchanged; bridge suites 81 passed
- [x] Full Vitest suite 31,076 passed, 0 failed (PostgreSQL/MySQL suites skipped: no schema change); `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean
- [ ] Not checked against a live upstream broker

title: feat(status): opt-in re-apply of the Status Message after a reboot (#5745)
body:
## Summary

Opt-in mitigation for a Status Message that is lost when the node reboots: MeshMonitor can write it once more when the node comes back empty.

Refs #5745 (kept open: the root cause is in firmware).

## Background

PR #5769 made a Status Message save read the value back from the node. That proves the running config holds it, not that the node wrote it to flash. Some firmware (seen on nRF52 over BLE, 2.8.1) drops the save with no error, so the status is gone after a reboot.

## What changed

- **Setting** `statusMessageReapplyAfterReboot`, per source, **off by default**. A checkbox under the Status Message in the Configuration tab.
- **Remembered value** `statusMessageLastVerified`, per source, written only by a save the node confirmed on read-back (a confirmed clear stores an empty value). It is server-owned and cannot be set through the settings API.
- **On reconnect**, once the node's config has loaded, MeshMonitor reads the node's status fresh. It writes the remembered status only when all of these hold: the setting is on, the remembered status is not empty, the node's status **is empty**, no save is in flight, and this connection has not tried already.
- If the node holds a **different** non-empty status, MeshMonitor leaves it alone and remembers that one instead.
- The write goes through the same verified, single-flight save as a manual save. Success logs at info; a failed or unverified write logs a warning and is not retried on that connection.
- Skipped in passive mode, on firmware without the module, and for MQTT and MeshCore sources.

## Screenshot

![Re-apply after a reboot option](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5745-status-reapply-after-reboot/docs/public/images/features/5745-status-reapply-option.png)

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime**: none. One read, and at most one write plus its read-back, all local admin packets to our own node. The node later includes the restored status in its normal broadcast, as after any manual save.
2. **Spam**: none. No event, notification or automation fires on a re-apply, and no reboot is scheduled. One attempt per connection; no loop and no retry.
3. **Timers**: none. Saving the setting starts nothing and resets no guard. A MeshMonitor restart is a reconnect, so it can make one attempt if the node really is empty; that is intended. The only state that matters, the remembered value, is in the database.

## Known limits

- A status cleared on purpose from another app looks the same as one lost in a reboot, so it would be restored. The help text says so.
- Turning the setting on takes effect at the next reconnect.
- With the setting on, each connect costs one extra local config read.

## Test plan

- [x] Decision function: every branch (off, nothing remembered, node empty, node different, save in flight, already tried, unsupported)
- [x] Manager: off writes nothing; on + empty node + remembered value gives exactly one verified save; a different node value is adopted with

title: feat(meshcore): radio auto-add options and bulk remove of non-favourite contacts (#5777)
body:
## Summary

MeshCore companion radios keep their own contact list. When it fills up, "Add to Radio" fails, and a user attached only over USB had no way to change the policy or free slots from MeshMonitor. This adds the radio's auto-add options and a bulk remove.

Closes #5777.

## What changed

In **Device Configuration → Radio contact list**:

- **Auto-add mode**: every node it hears / only these types (Companions, Repeaters, Room servers, Sensors) / none (manual).
- **Max hops** for auto-add: no limit, direct only, or up to N hops.
- **Replace the oldest non-favourite contact when the list is full.**
- **Remove non-favourite contacts from the radio**, behind a confirm dialog that states how many go and how many stay.

How it works:

- New backend commands send the firmware's `CMD_GET_AUTOADD_CONFIG` (59) and `CMD_SET_AUTOADD_CONFIG` (58) as raw frames; no meshcore.js change. A set is read-modify-write and reads the value back.
- Firmware that does not know these commands answers with an error or nothing. That is reported as "not supported": the new controls are hidden, the old auto-add toggle and Push to radio keep working.
- Bulk remove reads the radio's table fresh and keeps any contact that is a favourite on the radio (`flags & 0x01`) **or** in MeshMonitor. It changes the radio's list only: MeshMonitor keeps its node rows and history (new `removeContact(key, { keepNode: true })`, same per-contact path). One run at a time per source.
- Routes: `GET`/`POST …/meshcore/config/autoadd-config` (`configuration:write` to change) and `POST …/meshcore/contacts/remove-non-favorites` (`nodes:write`).
- The "radio refused: contact list is full" error now points at these controls.

## Screenshot

![Radio contact list options and the bulk-remove confirm dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5777-meshcore-autoadd-config/docs/public/images/features/5777-meshcore-autoadd-contacts.png)

## Mesh impact

None on air. Every command here is a local serial/TCP write to our own radio; nothing is transmitted, no timer is added, and receive-only mode still allows them (as it does the existing auto-add toggle). Bulk remove is user-triggered, confirmed, and single-flight.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend: 58/59 framing, bit packing both ways, untouched bits and hops preserved, error and silence read as unsupported, refused write, two sets do not interleave
- [x] Manager and routes: companion only, per-source permissions and isolation, validation, favourites kept from either side, node rows untouched, concurrent bulk remove refused
- [x] Component: mode logic, hidden when unsupported, dialog counts, permission gating
- [x] Targeted suites 383 passed; `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean
- [x] Rig, MC-Sandbox (local writes only): read the config, flipped overwrite-oldest, read it back, restored it; out-of-range max hops refused with 400. MC-BLESandbox answered "not supported" and the UI hid the controls
- [x] Browser: section and confirm dialog as in the scre

title: fix(meshcore): read room post author key from raw bytes (#5774)
body:
## Summary

Room posts from other users were stored with a corrupted author key, so the author never matched a contact.

Closes #5774.

## Cause

A room post (`SignedPlain`) carries the author's 4 raw public-key bytes at the start of the text payload. `meshcore.js` decodes the whole payload as UTF-8 before MeshMonitor sees it, so every key byte >= 0x80 became U+FFFD, and we then hex-encoded that as `fffd`. The old unit test built its input with `String.fromCharCode`, so it never met a real frame.

## What changed

- **Read the bytes, not the string.** The native backend keeps the raw `ContactMsgRecv` frame from the library's `rx` event (which fires just before the decoded event) and takes the author prefix and body from it. The frame is used once, and only if its sender prefix, text type and timestamp match the decoded event, so one post's bytes cannot attach to another message. The author prefix is always 8 lowercase hex chars.
- **No raw frame, no guess.** If the frame is missing, the author is stored as `unknown`, not as a corrupted string.
- **Rows already corrupted.** They cannot be repaired exactly, so there is no migration. At read time, the bytes that survived (< 0x80, still in position) are matched against known contacts; a name shows only when at least two bytes survived and exactly one contact fits. Otherwise the post shows "Unknown sender".
- **No click-through on a bad key.** An unknown or corrupted author is no longer a link to a DM. That link was the one path we found that could carry a corrupted string into Node Details as a "contact".
- **Removing a leftover.** Deleting a contact whose key is not a real 64-hex key, and that has no stored row, now answers success instead of 409. A real device key still gets the 409.

## Not confirmed

We did not find server code that creates a node or contact row from a room post, so the "ghost contact" in the report is explained only by the click-through path above. If a ghost still appears after this lands, the reporter's steps to it would help.

## Mesh impact

None. Receive-path parsing and display only; nothing is sent and no timer is added.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend tests replay real frames: `rx` with the raw bytes, then the lossy decoded event. Prefixes `6ab2c4d8`, `e19ca7f0`, `c54d319e` from the issue, with an emoji and an accented letter in the body; plus no raw frame, no reuse of a frame, and a frame from another sender
- [x] Manager test: the stored row has the right key and resolves to the contact; component test: the Rooms stream shows the contact name, and "Unknown sender" with no link for a bad key
- [x] Route and manager tests for removing a leftover key
- [x] Targeted suites: 268 + 360 passed; `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean
- [ ] Not checked on a radio: it needs a room server and a second device whose key has high bytes

title: fix(meshcore): telemetry modes all persist; clearer observer IATA label (#5773, #5772)
body:
## Summary

Two small MeshCore configuration fixes.

Closes #5773. Closes #5772.

### #5773 — telemetry modes: only one of three persisted

Saving Basic / Location / Environment fired three writes at once. Each is a read-modify-write of the device's `CMD_SET_OTHER_PARAMS` frame, which carries all three modes plus the advert location policy and the manual-add flag. All three read the same old values; the last frame to land undid the other two. The UI showed "Saved" from its own cache, and a reconnect showed the truth.

- **Server**: the native backend now runs every SetOtherParams writer one at a time (`set_telemetry_mode_*`, `set_advert_loc_policy`, `set_auto_add_contacts`, `set_other_params`). This also protects any other caller, such as the API or a second browser tab.
- **Client**: the configuration view saves the three modes in turn.

### #5772 — "Region (IATA)" label

The observer field names the publisher's airport code in the MQTT topic, not a MeshCore RF region or forwarding scope. Label is now **Observer location (IATA)**; the help text says what it is and is not. No change to validation, topic construction or stored config. I left the `'test'` value accepted everywhere (item 3 in the issue was optional).

## Mesh impact

None. Local serial writes and UI text only; nothing is sent on air and no timer is added.

## Test plan

- [x] New `meshcoreNativeBackend.otherParamsSerialization.test.ts`: three telemetry writes fired together all persist and never overlap; a telemetry write and the location policy stay apart; a failed write does not block the next
- [x] Targeted suites (backend, configuration view, observer config): 507 passed
- [x] `tsc`, `lint:ci` clean
- [x] Rig (MC-Sandbox, local serial writes only): set all three modes in parallel through the API, disconnected and reconnected the source, and all three held; restored the old values the same way

title: feat(meshcore): reactions in Unified Messages, CSV export and automation triggers (#5763)
body:
## Summary

Phase 4, the last phase of the MeshCore reactions epic (#5759): reactions in Unified Messages, CSV export and automation triggers, plus the audit #5763 asked for.

Closes #5763. Closes #5764. Closes #5759.

## What changed

- **Unified Messages**: a MeshCore reaction is a chip on the merged message, not an emoji-only card. A reaction heard on several sources counts once. An unmatched reaction shows as the dim line. Chips are read-only here.
  - The server sends page-independent refs (`meshcoreRowRefs`, `reactionTargetRefs`), built only from rows the viewer may read. The client resolves them across loaded pages. No cross-source target matching.
  - A reaction from an ignored or blocked sender is dropped.
- **CSV export**: MeshCore reactions follow the existing **Include emoji reactions** box (default off, as Meshtastic). Two columns appended: `reaction` and `reply_to_id`. MeshCore `message_id` is now the row id. The first 13 columns keep name and order.
- **Automation trigger**: a MeshCore reaction fires **A message is received** only when the rule ticks the new **Also fire on MeshCore reactions** box. Absent on every existing rule, so nothing changes on upgrade. New trigger fields: `isTapback` (both protocols), and for MeshCore `emoji`, `replyContext`, `reactionTargetId`, `reactionTargetText`, `reactionTargetSender`.

## Screenshot

![Unified Messages with MeshCore reaction chips and an unmatched line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5759-p4-reactions-downstream/docs/public/images/features/5763-unified-meshcore-reactions.png)

## The #5763 audit

#5763 assumed MeshCore reactions would be stored in the Meshtastic `emoji = 1` / `replyId` shape. They are not: a MeshCore reaction has no packet id for `replyId`, its target can be unknown and resolve later, and there are two wire formats, so Phase 2 gave it its own columns on `meshcore_messages`. Most audit rows are therefore "MeshCore never reaches this code", checked in the source:

| Surface | Result |
|---|---|
| Per-message notifications (Apprise, push, desktop) | Never reached: `sendMessagePushNotification` is called from the Meshtastic, MQTT and Reticulum paths only |
| Mention alert | Skips reactions (Phase 2, tested) |
| Auto-Acknowledge | Skips reactions unless `meshcoreReactionsAckOnReceive` is on (Phase 2, tested) |
| Reply threading helpers | Meshtastic table only; MeshCore uses `groupMeshCoreReactions` |
| Translation and its cache | Never reached: reads the Meshtastic table |
| Unified Messages | **Changed here** |
| CSV export | **Changed here** |
| Socket gates | MeshCore events use their own gate (tested) |
| Automation triggers | **Changed here**, opt-in |
| Search (UI and v1) | Leaves reactions out (tested) |
| v1 message API | Never reached |
| MQTT publish, MT↔MC bridge | No MeshCore message is published; the bridge rule does not opt in, so reactions are not relayed (tested) |
| Virtual Node | Relays the raw wire text (tested) |
| Backup / res

## Summary

Phase 3 of the MeshCore reactions epic (#5759): send emoji reactions from MeshMonitor, in MeshCore One format.

Closes #5762. Refs #5759, #5764.

## What changed

- **One send function**, `MeshCoreManager.sendReaction(messageId, emoji)`, used by the new route and by the automation tapback action.
- **Route**: `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/:messageId/reaction` with body `{ emoji }`. Same gates as a normal send: rate limiter, `messages:write` on the source, receive-only check. Typed refusals (`REACTIONS_OUTBOUND_DISABLED`, `DUPLICATE_REACTION`, `TARGET_IS_REACTION`, `TARGET_IS_ROOM_POST`, `TARGET_NO_HASH`, `TARGET_NOT_REACTABLE`, …).
- **UI**: a react button on each reactable message opens the existing emoji picker (the user's tapback set, filtered to emoji MeshCore One accepts). A chip another node left is clickable to add the same emoji. Our own chip has an accent border and shows at once, before the server confirms.
- **Setting**: `meshcoreReactionsOutboundEnabled`, per source, default on, with an airtime warning beside the box. Off hides the button, makes the API answer 409, and makes automations record a skip.
- **Automation**: "Send a tapback" on a MeshCore source reacts to the triggering message, on the source that received it. Every refusal is a recorded skip, not a failed run.

## Screenshots

![Picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5759-p3-outbound-reactions/docs/public/images/features/5762-meshcore-react-picker.png)

![Chips: ours with an accent border, another node's clickable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5759-p3-outbound-reactions/docs/public/images/features/5762-meshcore-react-chips.png)

![Settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5759-p3-outbound-reactions/docs/public/images/features/5762-meshcore-react-settings.png)

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime**: one packet per reaction, about 20 to 75 bytes of text. On a channel it floods: 1 + the number of repeaters that re-send it. A DM follows the known path. No timer, and it does not scale with node count.
2. **Spam**: bounded by the existing `messageLimiter` (shared with chat sends), one send per (message, emoji) from us, and **no retry** of any kind: no echo-miss retry, no DM ack retry, and Resend refuses a reaction row. Our own reaction never reaches the automation trigger path. A message whose text is itself reaction-shaped cannot be reacted to, so two tapback automations cannot answer each other. Receive-only blocks every send.
3. **Timers**: none added. The setting is read at send time; a save re-arms nothing.

Limits and the default were chosen with the maintainer.

## Known limits

- No un-react (MeshCore One has none) and no reactions in rooms.
- A reaction to a row stored before migration 203 uses a rebuilt hash and may not match on other devices.
- If the database insert fails after the radio accepted the packet, a restart could allow one repeat send.

## Licensing

MeshCore

title: feat(meshcore): read inbound emoji reactions as chips (#5761)
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the MeshCore reactions epic (#5759): read emoji reactions sent by MeshCore One and meshcore-open, and show them as reactions.

MeshCore has no reaction packet. These apps send a short text that names the target by a hash, so today a reaction shows as `@[Alice]👍` plus eight odd characters, and can raise a false mention alert or trigger an automation.

Closes #5761. Refs #5759, #5764.

## What changed

- **Migration 203**: seven nullable columns on `meshcore_messages` (`mc1Hash`, `reactionEmoji`, `reactionFormat`, `reactionTargetHash`, `reactionTargetSender`, `reactionTargetId`, `reactionRawText`) and an index on `(sourceId, mc1Hash)`. No backfill. `senderTimestamp` is now kept on every new row.
- **One resolver for three ingest paths** (`meshcoreReactionIngest.ts`): companion, repeater and MQTT. A reaction is stored as a row whose `text` is the emoji, linked to its target. Duplicates (same reactor, emoji, target) are dropped.
- **Late targets**: an unmatched reaction waits (500 per source) and resolves when its target arrives. New event `meshcore:reaction:resolved`, gated like `meshcore:message`.
- **UI**: a chip under the target message with a count and reactor names; one dim line when this source never heard the target. The line turns into a chip on a late match, without a reload.
- **Settings** (MeshCore → Settings → Reactions): `meshcoreReactionsInboundEnabled` (per source, on) and `meshcoreReactionsAckOnReceive` (global, off, with a warning beside the box).
- A reaction row does not count as unread and is left out of search and channel counts. Deleting a message deletes its reactions. A reaction from an ignored sender shows nowhere.

Unified Messages and CSV show an emoji-only line until Phase 4. Sending reactions is Phase 3.

## Screenshots

![Chip and unmatched line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5759-p2-inbound-reactions/docs/public/images/features/5761-meshcore-reaction-chips.png)

![Settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5759-p2-inbound-reactions/docs/public/images/features/5761-meshcore-reaction-settings.png)

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime**: none by default. This phase sends nothing. With `meshcoreReactionsAckOnReceive` on, a reaction that matches an Auto-Acknowledge rule can trigger one reply, under the existing Auto-Ack limits.
2. **Spam**: reduced. A reaction row skips automations, Auto-Responder, Forwarding and mention alerts. Auto-Ack skips it unless the global switch is on. Receive-only still blocks every send.
3. **Timers**: none added. Both settings are read at reaction time, so a save re-arms nothing. The pending-reaction index is rebuilt from the database after a restart.

Limits chosen with the maintainer: index hits take the newest 10; old-row and meshcore-open scans read the newest 200 rows inside 7 days; 500 unmatched reactions wait per source.

## Known limits

- Matching is per source. A reaction heard on one source does not attach to a messa

title: feat(meshcore): reaction codec for MeshCore One and meshcore-open formats (#5760)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the MeshCore reactions epic (#5759): a pure codec for the reaction texts that MeshCore clients send as plain chat messages. Nothing imports it yet; Phase 2 wires it into ingest.

- `src/utils/meshcoreReactions.ts`
  - **MeshCore One (MC1)**: content hash (`SHA256(utf8(text) || u32le(sender second))[0:5]` as 8 lowercase Crockford Base32 chars), channel and DM builders, channel parser for both orders (`@[sender]emoji\nhash` and the pre-1.4.1 `emoji@[sender]\nhash`), DM parser, hash normalisation (`O`→`0`, `I`/`L`→`1`, `U` invalid), and the one-grapheme reaction-emoji rule.
  - **meshcore-open** (read only): v3 `r:{4 hex}:{2 hex}` and both v1 shapes, plus the string hash its targets use.
  - `parseMeshCoreReaction(text, scope)` and a cheap `isReactionText` pre-check for ingest.
  - `MC_REACTION_FORMAT_VERSION`.
- `src/utils/meshcoreOpenEmojiTable.ts`: meshcore-open's 184-entry emoji index table, vendored unchanged with its MIT notice.
- `docs/internal/dev-notes/MESHCORE_REACTIONS_EPIC.md`: the epic plan, the verified wire formats and the decisions taken.

## Licensing

MeshCore One is GPL-3.0 and MeshMonitor is BSD-3-Clause. The MC1 half is written from the format description (its `docs/Reactions.md` and input→output vectors), not from its source. meshcore-open is MIT; only its emoji table is copied, with attribution.

## Plan changes against the issues

The issues assume MeshCore messages live in `messages` with `emoji` / `replyId`. They live in `meshcore_messages`, with string ids and neither column. The epic doc records the revised plan: reactions get their own columns and chips, and Phase 2 must keep the sender's wire timestamp, which we drop today for most rows.

## Mesh impact

None. No packet is sent, no notification fires, no timer is armed.

## Testing

- `src/utils/meshcoreReactions.test.ts`: 249 tests. Hash vectors include MC1's published one (`Hello` / `1704067200` → `b45pc4ek`), meshcore-open's own MC1 vector, and the three Dart VM vectors pinned by meshcore-open's tests.
- Full Vitest suite: 32,175 passed, 0 failed (PostgreSQL and MySQL containers up).
- `npm run typecheck` and the server tsconfig pass.

Closes #5760
Refs #5759

--- docs/internal/dev-notes/MESHCORE_REACTIONS_EPIC.md (+150/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+# MeshCore Reactions Epic (#5759)
+
+Sub-issues: #5760 (A), #5761 (B), #5762 (C), #5763 (D), #5764 (E).
+
+## Goal
+
+Read and send MeshCore emoji reactions so they interoperate with the MeshCore
+One (MC1) iOS app, and read the meshcore-open client's reactions.
+
+## What the issues got wrong
+
+The issues assume MeshCore messages sit in `messages` with `emoji` / `replyId`.
+They do not. The plan below replaces "normalize to `emoji=1` + `replyId`".
+
+- MeshCore messages live in `meshcore_messages`: string ids, no `emoji`, no
+  `replyId`. Reactions get their own columns there and their own chips in
+  `MeshCoreMessageStream`.
+- The hash needs the sender's wire timestamp. We keep it only for our own
+  channel sends. Received rows lose it when the sender's clock is implausible;
+  our own DMs do not store it.
+- One message is one row per source (merged at read time), so a reaction and
+  its target resolve per source.
+- Most `emoji` readers in #5763 never see a MeshCore message. The real leaks: a
+  channel reaction to our message fires a false "mentioned you" alert, and a
+  reaction passes through auto-ack, auto-responder, forwarding and automations
+  as plain text.
+
+## Wire formats
+
+### MC1 (read and send)
+
+Verified against `Avi0n/MeshCoreOne` at `8b141a48` (v1.5.2) and its
+`docs/Reactions.md`. **MC1 is GPL-3.0 and MeshMonitor is BSD-3-Clause: do not
+copy or translate its code. Implement from the format described here.**
+
+- Channel, current: `@[{targetSender}]{emoji}\n{hash}`
+- Channel, legacy (MC1 < 1.4.1), read only: `{emoji}@[{targetSender}]\n{hash}`
+- DM: `{emoji}\n{hash}`
+- `hash` = Crockford Base32 of `SHA256(utf8(text) || u32le(timestamp))[0:5]`:
+  8 chars, **lowercase**, alphabet `0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz`, 40 bits
+  MSB first.
+  - `text` for a channel message is the body **without** the `Sender: ` prefix:
+    everything after the first `:`, spaces and tabs trimmed at both ends.
+  - `timestamp` is the sender's packet timestamp in seconds.
+- Hash read rules: exactly 8 chars; both cases; `O`/`o` → `0`; `I`/`i`/`L`/`l`
+  → `1`; `U`, hyphen and non-ASCII are invalid; normalize to lowercase.
+- Parse, channel: split at the **last** `\n` (no trimming anywhere); the tail
+  must be a valid hash; find the **first** `@[` in the head. If nothing comes
+  before it: sender runs to the **first** `]`, the rest is the emoji. Otherwise
+  (legacy): the text before `@[` is the emoji, the rest must **end** with `]`
+  and the sender is what lies between. The emoji must be a reaction emoji and
+  the sender non-empty.
+- Parse, DM: reject any text containing `@[`; split at the last `\n`; valid
+  hash; the head must be a reaction emoji.
+- Reaction emoji: exactly one extended grapheme cluster, whose first scalar has
+  the Unicode `Emoji` property, and either that scalar is above U+238C or the
+  cluster has more than one scalar. Skin tones, ZWJ sequences, flags, VS16 and
+  keycaps pass; a bare `1`, `#`, `©` fails.
+- Published vector: text `Hello`, timestamp `1704067200` → `b45pc4ek`.
+  Others (same algorithm): `Hello world`/1704067200 → `7a6r3xy1`;
+  `Hello`/1704067201 → `3wh8x8z5`; `World`/1704067200 → `vp1vxnf4`;
+  `Message 0`/0 → `7mt5pe1m`; `café 👍 ok`/1760000000 → `8b5qzwf6`;
+  empty/4294967295 → `npah66y0`.
+- MC1 behaviour worth matching: target lookup is exact, case-sensitive on
+  sender name, newest match wins; a reaction with no target is held and
+  resolved when the target arrives; dedupe on (target, reactor name, emoji); no
+  un-react; several emojis per message allowed; **no reactions in rooms**.
+
+### meshcore-open (read only)
+
+`zjs81/meshcore-open` is MIT. Take the format and the emoji table from **its**
+source, with attribution, not from MC1's copy.
+
+- v3: `r:{4 hex}:{2 hex emoji index}` (9 chars). Hash = Dart `String.hashCode`
+  over the UTF-16 of `"{timestamp}" + senderName (channel only) + first 5
+  UTF-16 units of the text`, masked to 16 bits. Emoji index into a 184-entry
+  table.
+- v1 (before Jan 2026): `r:{millis}_{senderNameHash}_{textHash}:{emoji}`.
+- The Phase 1 architect must confirm both against the meshcore-open source.
+
+## Decisions (user interview, 2026-10-12)
+
+| Topic | Decision |
+|---|---|
+| Unmatched reaction | Store as a reaction with no target; show one dim line ("Alice reacted 👍 to a message not seen here"); becomes a chip if the target arrives later |
+| meshcore-open format | Read it too; never send it |
+| Send limits | Existing HTTP message limiter; one send per (message, emoji) from us; never auto-retry or resend a reaction; automations keep their own limits |
+| Reaction to my message | No alert; stop the false mention alert |
+| `meshcoreReactionsAckOnReceive` | Build it: global, default **off**, warning beside the toggle. Off = Auto-Acknowledge never answers a reaction |
+| Auto-Responder, Forwarding | Always skip reactions |
+| Outbound off for a source | Hide the picker; the API refuses; automations record a skip |
+| Rooms | No reactions |
+| Rig tests | Allowed on `gauntlet` only, between MC-Sandbox and MC-BLESandbox. The user checks against a real MC1 device |
+
+## Mesh impact
+
+- Airtime: one reaction = one channel or DM text packet, flooded like any chat
+  message. No timer, no per-node fan-out.
+- Spam: capped by `messageLimiter`, the per-(message, emoji) dedupe, and no
+  retry. Inbound reactions fire no notification, no auto-responder and no
+  forward. Auto-ack of reactions is off unless the operator turns it on.
+- Timers: none added.
+
+## Phases
+
+- [x] **Phase 1 — codec** (#5760, version constant from #5764). Pure,
+  browser-safe module in `src/utils/`: MC1 hash, build, parse (both channel
+  orders), reaction-emoji test, meshcore-open v3/v1 parse and hash,
+  `MC_REACTION_FORMAT_VERSION`. Unit tests with the vectors above. No wiring.
+  *Exit:* tests green; nothing imports it at runtime.
+- [ ] **Phase 2 — inbound** (#5761, inbound + ack settings from #5764).
+  Migration 203: wire `senderTimestamp` kept on every new row, reaction columns
+  on `meshcore_messages`. Ingest detection and target lookup on every ingest
+  path (companion, repeater, MQTT); late-target resolution; reaction rows kept
+  out of mention alerts, auto-responder, forwarding and (by default) auto-ack;
+  chips and the unmatched-reaction line in the MeshCore channel and DM views;
+  `meshcoreReactionsInboundEnabled` (per source) and
+  `meshcoreReactionsAckOnReceive` (global) with their toggles.
+  *Exit:* an MC1-format channel and DM reaction shows as a chip; no raw
+  reaction text in chat; inbound off stores raw text.
+- [ ] **Phase 3 — outbound** (#5762, outbound setting from #5764). Send route,
+  emoji picker in the MeshCore stream, optimistic local row, dedupe, no retry,
+  `meshcoreReactionsOutboundEnabled` (per source), automation tapback on
+  MeshCore, wire second stored for our own DMs.
+  *Exit:* a reaction sent from MeshMonitor is read back as a reaction by a
+  second source; rig test on `gauntlet`.
+- [ ] **Phase 4 — downstream** (#5763). Unified Messages chips, CSV export,
+  automation trigger `isTapback` and reply target for MeshCore, docs.
+  *Exit:* the audit table in #5763 is answered row by row, with a test or a
+  stated "MeshCore never reaches this".
+
+## Log
+
+- 2026-10-12: plan written; Phase 1 started.
+- 2026-10-12: Phase 1 done. Codec in `src/utils/meshcoreReactions.ts`, table in
+  `src/utils/meshcoreOpenEmojiTable.ts`. Checked against meshcore-open at
+  `3bee159c`; its source corrects the summary above:
+  - The hash is the app's own `stableStringHash` (Jenkins one-at-a-time over
+    UTF-16 units, 30-bit mask, 0 → 1), which upstream tests pin to the Dart VM
+    value. Web builds before `25f197c` (2026-10-11) used another hash and will
+    never match a target.
+  - The table has 184 entries, 178 distinct. Every index is valid.
+  - v1 has two shapes: channel `r:{ms}_{nameHash}_{textHash}:{emoji}` and 1:1
+    `r:{ms}_{8 hex of sender key}:{emoji}`. Ship v1 as parse + best-effort match.
+  - meshcore-open splits a channel body differently from MC1: it strips one
+    space after the colon and does not trim.
+  - **For Phase 2:** our stored channel bodies are `.trim()`ed, wider than MC1's
+    space-and-tab trim. Decide whether to keep the raw wire body for hashing.
+    `@[Alice]👍\nreceived` parses as a reaction (hash `rece1ved`), as in MC1, so
+    expect some unmatched reactions that are really chat.

title: fix(status): read the Status Message back from the node after a save (#5745)
body:
## Summary

A Status Message save sent one `set_module_config` to the local node, then wrote the sent value straight into MeshMonitor's cache (`actualModuleConfig`). `GET /api/config/current` serves that cache, and the firmware reports no error when it drops a write. So the pill and the Configuration tab said "saved" whether or not the node took it.

Now a Status Message save reads the status back from the node before it answers:

| Node's answer | Result | Cache |
|---|---|---|
| Same `nodeStatus` | `200 { success: true, message }` (unchanged shape) | takes the node's answer, not what we sent |
| Another value | `502 STATUSMESSAGE_NOT_APPLIED` | takes the node's value |
| No answer | `504 STATUSMESSAGE_UNVERIFIED` | keeps what it had |

- **Manager:** new `readLocalModuleConfig(configType, timeoutMs)`. It sends the existing `get_module_config_request` (`requestModuleConfig`) and waits for `processAdminMessage` to hand over the section, the same waiter pattern as `refreshLocalSecurityConfig`. A waiter ends on the answer, on its timeout, or on disconnect (`handleDisconnected`); each path clears the timer and the list entry.
- **Service:** `setGenericModuleConfig(type, config, { verify: true })`. The check table (`MODULE_READ_BACK_CHECKS`) holds `statusmessage` only; another no-reboot module can join later. Without `verify`, or for any other module, the save runs as before, so device-backup restore is unchanged.
- **Timing:** one write, then up to two reads of 5 s each (10 s worst case, inside the 30 s socket timeout). Only the read repeats: after no answer, or after a different value (which can be the late reply to a read sent before our write). The write is never re-sent.
- **Concurrency:** verified saves run one at a time per manager, so one save's read-back cannot be answered with another save's state.
- **Compare:** exact string match on `nodeStatus`; an absent field reads as empty, so Clear verifies too. The route already refuses text over 79 bytes, so the firmware stores what we send.
- **UI:** `ApiService.setModuleConfig` now throws `ApiError` (keeps `code`). The pill toast and the Configuration tab's inline error + toast show their own text for the two codes (`quick_status.not_applied`, `quick_status.unverified`). The pill also re-reads the config after such a failure.
- **Docs:** new Status Message section in `docs/features/device.md`.

## What the read-back proves, and what it cannot

- **Proves:** the write reached the node, and the node's running (RAM) config holds the value. This rules out failure point 1 in the issue comment (write lost on the way).
- **Cannot prove:** that the node saved it to flash. A status that passes the check can still be gone after a reboot. That is a node-side save failure (seen on nRF52 with BLE up) and MeshMonitor cannot detect it. The docs say so.

Not in this PR, by decision: re-applying the status after a reboot, delaying reboots, edit-transaction changes, read-back for other modules.

title: feat(messages): show the mesh protocol on message borders (#5744)
body:
## Summary

Message borders now show the mesh protocol.

- **Unified Messages:** the card's 3px left border shows the protocol of the message. Before, it took a colour from the source's slot in the chart palette, so a third Meshtastic source got a new colour. The card `title` names the protocol ("MeshCore message"), so colour is not the only cue. The `MeshCore` pill is gone.
- **Single-source views:** each message gets the same 3px stripe: Meshtastic channel bubbles (`ChannelsTab`), Meshtastic DM bubbles (`MessagesTab`), MeshCore rows (`MeshCoreMessageStream`: channels, DMs, rooms) and Reticulum DM bubbles (`ReticulumDmsView`).

## Decisions (from the maintainer)

1. **Colours** match the node popup's protocol badge: Meshtastic = `var(--color-success)`, MeshCore = `var(--color-caution)`. No new theme tokens.
2. **Other source types:** MQTT sources (`mqtt_broker`, `mqtt_bridge`) carry Meshtastic packets, so they use the Meshtastic colour. Reticulum uses a third colour, `var(--color-accent)`.
3. **Unified Messages:** the border shows the protocol, not `sourceColor(primarySourceId)`. Source tags keep their per-source colours. Removed `.unified-msg-card__proto-badge`, its CSS, its JSX and the `unified.messages.meshcore_badge` key in `en.json`.
4. **Channel and DM views:** a 3px protocol stripe on each message.

## How

- `src/utils/meshProtocol.ts`: `sourceTypeMeshProtocol(type)` returns `'meshtastic' | 'meshcore' | 'reticulum'`; `MESH_PROTOCOL_COLOR_VAR` maps each to its token. It is a new, display-only function. `sourceTypeProtocol()` and `isAnyMeshCoreSourceType()` are unchanged, so no feature gate moves.
- `src/components/messages/ProtocolStripe.module.css`: one shared rule, driven by `data-protocol`. No inline colours, no fallback values in `var()`. No additions to the frozen global sheets (`unified.css` only loses the pill rule).
- A test reads the CSS module and `nodes.css` and fails if the stylesheet, the util or the popup badge drift apart.
- A Unified message with several receptions uses the first reception's source type.
- The Meshtastic tabs read `sourceType` from `useSource()`; `null` (legacy single-source view) reads as Meshtastic.
- The stripe selector has doubled class specificity so it wins over `.message-bubble.spoofed`'s `border` whatever order the sheets load in. The spoofed bubble keeps its red inset ring.

## Mesh impact

No packets, timers or notifications. Display only.

## Tests

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: exit 0
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.server.json`: exit 0
- `npm run lint:ci`: exit 0, no `FAIL` lines (includes the CSS colour check)

title: feat(meshcore): full-size Trace SNR charts per link direction (#5765)
body:
## Summary

Adds full-size Trace SNR charts to the MeshCore contact panel, one per direction of each link (#5765). They sit right below the **Trace SNR history** card, which stays as the glance view.

- **Charts.** New `MeshCoreTraceSnrCharts` (recharts `LineChart` in a `ResponsiveContainer`). Each chart is titled "{{receiver}} heard {{sender}} (dB)" and shows avg, range and sample count. The two directions of a link sit side by side, in `--chart-1` (heard by this contact) and `--chart-3` (this contact heard by the far end).
- **Tooltip.** SNR in dB to 2 decimals, with the absolute time of the sample.
- **Gaps.** The line breaks where two samples are more than 3 hours apart, the same rule the telemetry charts use (`hopSnrChartData`).
- **Range.** A local 24h / 7d / 30d / 90d control, default 7d (the card's window). See "Range control" below.
- **API.** `GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/hop-snr` takes `?points=<n>`: default 120, whole number 1 to 2000, else `400 INVALID_POINTS`. The newest N samples per link are kept. The charts ask for 1000; the card still gets 120. Response shape is unchanged.
- **Row limit.** The repository read was capped at 2000 rows across all links of a contact, which would starve quiet links once the point cap rose. The route now asks for `points * 10` rows (2000 at the default, at most 20000). The default path reads what it read before.
- **Shared naming.** The card's name logic moved to `hopSnrEndName` in `src/utils/meshcoreHopSnr.ts`; the card and the charts both call it.
- **Hidden when empty.** No links, no `traceroute:read`, or no source: the section renders nothing. Once a contact has shown links, an empty range keeps the range control and says "No samples in this range", so the user can get back.

### Range control

The brief asked to reuse the telemetry charts' range if the panel had one. It does not: those charts are a sibling `TelemetryGraphs` in `MeshCoreDirectMessagesView`, which keeps its range in its own state, stops at 7 days (telemetry retention) and is absent for a contact with no telemetry. Trace SNR is kept 90 days. So the new section has its own small control, styled to match.

1. **Airtime:** none. The feature reads rows the source already stored from traces it heard. It sends no packet.
2. **Spam:** none. No message, automation trigger, `dataEventEmitter` event or notification. One extra GET per open contact, and one per range change.

title: feat(meshcore): store TRACE hop SNRs heard by Repeater sources (#5742)
body:
## Summary

A MeshCore **Repeater** source reads the serial CLI, so it never got the Companion `TraceData (0x89)` push that #5722 stores. Its `RAW:` + `RX:` packet log does carry every TRACE it hears. This PR decodes those and feeds the same ingest service, so one code path writes `meshcore_hop_snr` rows for both source types. No schema, route or UI change.

- `src/utils/meshcoreTrace.ts` (new): shared TRACE decoding. Holds `parseTraceDataPush` and its types, moved out of `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts` with no behaviour change, plus `decodeTracePacket` for the raw over-the-air packet and the two event builders.
- `meshcoreTraceIngestService`: `ingest()` and `traceToHopRows()` take an `inFlight` option for a packet caught part-way. A Companion push runs the old path unchanged and stays strict (one SNR per hop).
- `meshcoreManager`: `handleRepeaterRawPacket` decodes TRACE packets and calls the same `storeTraceData` the `trace_data` bridge event uses. A Repeater's rows carry its real key from `get public.key`, not the `'repeater'` placeholder in `localNode`.
- Docs: the Trace SNR History section now says both source types fill the card.

## What a repeater can and cannot attribute

Checked against firmware (`Packet.cpp`, `Mesh.cpp`, `Dispatcher.cpp`, both `MyMesh.cpp`). On the wire a TRACE is `header, [4 transport bytes], path_len, path, payload`. The `path` field holds SNRs (signed quarter-dB), one per hop that has forwarded, and `path_len` is a plain count of them. The payload is `tag, auth code, flags, hop hashes`; `flags & 3` gives the hash width.

A repeater logs the packet as received, at any stage. With `k` SNRs and `N` hops:

| Link | Stored? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| hop `i-1` → hop `i`, for `i < k` | Yes | Hop `i` wrote that SNR itself. Same rows as the Companion path. |
| hop `i-1` → hop `i`, for `i ≥ k` | No | That hop has not heard the packet yet. |
| hop `k-1` → this repeater | Yes, when `k ≥ 1`, an RX line paired, and the repeater's key is known | Hop `k-1` added the last SNR, so it sent this copy and the repeater heard it direct. |
| originator → this repeater (`k = 0`) | No | The packet does not name the originator. |

A finished trace (`k = N`) gives the same event, and the same rows, as a Companion push.

A repeater hears one trace once per stage. The ingest keeps the (tag, auth code) 60 s window and, for in-flight packets, tracks which links it stored, so a later stage adds only new links. When the repeater is itself the next hop, the reading it appends comes back in later stages as a path SNR; that is stored once. After a restart inside the window, a trace already in the table gains no rows.

Limits worth knowing:

- **Needs a packet-logging build.** RAW/RX lines exist only with `-D MESH_PACKET_LOGGING=1`, which stock release builds leave off. On stock repeater firmware this adds nothing.
- **Whole-dB local reading.** The RX line prints `(int)snr`, so the link into the repeater is in whole dB. SNRs inside the packet are quarter-dB.

title: build(deps): bump maplibre-gl from 6.11.2 to 6.13.0
body:
Bumps [maplibre-gl](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js) from 6.11.2 to 6.13.0.
Release notes

Sourced from maplibre-gl's releases.

v6.13.0

✨ Features and improvements

  • Let the globe center reach the poles, where it stopped at 85.05° (#8629) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Speed up symbol layout by skipping line breaking for labels that fit on one line (#8617) (by @​DoFabien)
  • Add experimental CustomLayerInterface.renderToTerrainTile, CustomLayerInterface.terrainTileRevision and renderTerrainHeightMap in the options of prerender, so custom layers can drape what they draw over the terrain and place objects on it on the GPU (#8588) (by @​birkskyum)

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fix a stale cached worker crashing the map after an upgrade: the worker is self-contained again instead of importing maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, and its default URL carries the version as a v query parameter. maplibre-gl-shared.mjs and maplibre-gl-shared-dev.mjs are now empty files, kept so that existing copy steps don't fail; they are deprecated and will be removed in the next major version (#8621) (by @​HarelM)
  • Fix globeDistanceOfLocationsPixels returning NaN when two copies of the same point have a dot product slightly above 1 (#8624)(by @​Dimononon)
  • Keep the camera above the terrain, where a scroll zoom into a mountain could take it under the surface and the zoom's end throw it kilometers up (#8539) (by @​johncarmack1984)

v6.12.0

✨ Features and improvements

  • Add a zoomToUserAccuracy option to GeolocateControlOptions to allow control over map zoom adjustments in line with the Geolocation Position update accuracy, while trackUserLocation is true (#7908,

title: feat(automation): timed events: start, end and time zone on scheduled automations (#5515)
body:
Closes #5515.

## What it does

The Automation Engine could already send on a cron to several Meshtastic and MeshCore channels in one rule. What it lacked for "Timed Events" was a start and an end. This adds them to the existing **On a schedule** trigger instead of building a second scheduler.

- **Start**, **End** and **Time zone** on the schedule trigger. The rule does not fire before the start or at/after the end.
- **At the end the rule turns itself off.** The list shows **Starts …**, **Until …** or **Ended …** beside a timed rule.
- **Minimum interval of 5 minutes** for a scheduled rule, enforced at save.
- **Timed Announcement** template in the gallery: message, sources, channels, repeat, start, end, zone.

Enable, disable, edit, duplicate, delete, Run Now and the run log were already there.

## Decisions (from the maintainer)

| Question | Choice |
|---|---|
| Scope | Extend the schedule trigger. No new page, no new scheduler. |
| Fastest fire | Every 5 minutes. Existing faster rules keep running but cannot be saved again without slowing down. |
| At the end | The rule turns itself off. |
| Cap on send targets | None. |

## How it works

- `src/types/scheduleWindow.ts` (shared, no dependencies) turns `startAt` / `endAt` (wall-clock `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`) plus an IANA `timezone` into instants, and validates them. The cron runs in the same zone.
- Engine: `rescheduleCron` passes the zone to croner, arms a timer for the end, and turns off a rule that is already past its end at load. `onSchedule` skips a tick before the start (no run-log row) and ends the rule on a tick at or after the end.
- Save: `validateAutomationGraph` checks the window. The route checks the cron's shortest gap with croner (`cronMinGapMs`), since the browser does not ship a cron parser. Applies to create, update, import and duplicate. An invalid cron is now refused at save too.
- Builder: two new field kinds, `datetimeLocal` and `timeZone`. Picking a date fills a blank zone with the browser's.

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime.** Sends per hour = targets × fires per hour. The issue's example (6 channels, every 30 minutes, 4 hours) is 48 sends. Before this, a cron could fire every minute, or every few seconds with a 6-field cron: 360+ sends an hour to 6 channels. The 5-minute minimum caps that at 12 fires an hour per rule. There is no cap on targets (maintainer's choice), so the help text beside the cron input says each fire goes to every chosen channel on every chosen source.
2. **Spam.** No new send path. A window can only reduce how often a rule fires. Cooldown and rate limit still apply on each fire.
3. **Timer reset.** The window is part of the saved config, not memory. A restart or a save re-reads the same dates, never counts as a fire, and cannot move the end. A rule past its end is turned off at load, so a restart after the end does not send. Sends missed while the server was down are skipped, not caught up.

title: feat(meshcore): Mentions notification when a message names the source's own node
body:
## What it does

Adds a **Mentions** option to a MeshCore source's **Notifications** tab. When it is on, a channel message or room post that names that source's own node as `@[Name]` sends a notification (Web Push, Apprise, desktop).

MeshCore messages raised no message notification before this, so this is the first one.

## Decisions (from the maintainer)

| Question | Choice |
|---|---|
| Default | **Off.** Opt-in per user and source. An upgrade alerts nobody. |
| Limit | **One alert per sender every 5 minutes**, per source. Other senders still get through. |
| Scope | **Channel messages and room posts.** DMs are not checked. |

## How it works

- `notifyOnMention` on `user_notification_preferences` (migration 202, all three backends, default false).
- `meshcoreMentionNotificationService` subscribes to `meshcore:message` on the event bus. It reads the source's own node name from its manager and matches `@[Name]` on the whole name, ignoring case (`src/utils/meshcoreMentions.ts`). `@[Bob]` does not alert a node called `Bobby`.
- Delivery goes through `broadcastToPreferenceUsers('notifyOnMention', …)`, so it reaches only users who have the option on for that source and hold `messages:read` on it.
- Never alerts on: our own messages (flag, own key, another of our sources' keys, or a channel echo carrying our own name), ignored or blocked senders, DMs, or a source with no node of its own (MeshCore MQTT).

## Mesh impact

1. **Airtime:** none. Nothing is transmitted.
2. **Spam:** the only cost is notifications. A sender can repeat a mention at will, so alerts are capped at one per source and sender every 5 minutes. The slot is taken before delivery, so a failed push is not retried on the next mention. Two mentions that arrive together raise one alert.
3. **Timer reset:** the last-alert times are stored per source in `meshcoreMentionNotifyState`, not in memory. A restart or a settings save does not reopen the window. The key is server-only (not POST-able).

## Limits worth knowing

- A channel packet has no sender key, only the name its device put in the body, so the per-sender limit keys on that name for channel messages.
- Channel selection and keyword filters do not apply to this alert; the Notifications tab hides them for MeshCore anyway.
- The match uses the node's current name. After a rename, mentions of the old name no longer match.

## Tests

- `meshcoreMentions.test.ts` (6): name parsing and whole-name match.
- `meshcoreMentionNotificationService.test.ts` (15): channel and room alerts, DM / no-mention / other-node skipped, ignored sender, four own-message cases, no own name, 5-minute per-sender limit, per-source limit, limit survives a restart, concurrent mentions, failed delivery, long body.
- Migration 202 test, route save test, repository suites on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL (containers were running).
- Full Vitest run: 2035 files pass, no unhandled errors. Both `tsc` projects clean. `lint:ci` clean.
- Live in the dev container: migrati

title: fix(automation): channelName token and filter work on MQTT sources (#5738)
body:
Closes #5738.

## Problem

On an MQTT source, `{{ trigger.channelName }}` came out empty and a channel-name filter never matched.

MQTT ingest stores a message on channel `CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET + <channel database id>` (the reporter's "LongFast #101"). `getChannelName()` looked only in the per-source `channels` table, and an MQTT source has no rows there. The same gap hit any source for a channel decrypted server-side with a Channel Database key.

## Fix

When the source has no `channels` row for that channel number and the number is a virtual one, `getChannelName()` reads the name from the Channel Database entry.

- A stored `channels` row still wins, blank name included. The unnamed primary slot keeps resolving to `''`, which is a valid filter target (#4507). No existing automation changes on a source that has channel rows.
- Meshtastic keys only (`protocol = 'meshtastic'`), and never for a MeshCore source: a MeshCore channel index is a device slot, not a Channel Database id.

## Mesh impact

No new sends, timers or notifications. One behaviour change to note: an automation whose channel filter names a Channel Database channel (for example `LongFast`) now also fires on messages from an MQTT source, where before it could not match. That is the reported bug; the automation's own rate limit and cooldown still apply.

## Tests

- `meshNodeData.channelName.test.ts` (6, real in-memory DB): MQTT source named from the Channel Database, virtual channel on a TCP source, stored row wins including blank primary, null for missing slot and unknown key id, MeshCore key never named for a Meshtastic source, MeshCore source never reads the Channel Database.
- Full Vitest run: 2031 files, 31,255 tests pass, no unhandled errors. Server `tsc` clean. `lint:ci` clean.
