title: feat(ui): number fields can be cleared; blank is outlined and blocks Save (#5649)
body:
Closes #5649

## What was wrong

Number fields were controlled `<input type="number">` elements bound straight to number state:

```tsx
value={cooldown}
onChange={e => setCooldown(parseInt(e.target.value) || 60)}      // or clampInt(v, 0, MAX), Math.max(min, …)
```

Backspace `60` down to nothing and the handler turns the blank into `60` (or `0`, or the minimum) before the next keystroke, and React writes that back into the field. You could not clear the field to type `120`. The reported auto-responder cooldown used `clampInt(e.target.value, 0, COOLDOWN_SECONDS_MAX)`, so blank became `0` and the next digits landed after it. The survey found the same shape at nearly every site:

| How the site handled a change (289 raw inputs, each counted once, first match wins) | Sites |
|---|---|
| `parseInt(v) \|\| default` / `parseFloat(v) \|\| default` (blank snaps to a default; 28 of these also clamp) | 125 |
| bare `parseInt(v)` / `parseFloat(v)` (blank puts `NaN` in state; several forms then saved it) | 44 |
| string state, parsed on save | 30 |
| `Number(v)` (blank becomes `0`) | 29 |
| clamp in `onChange` with no fallback (`Math.max/min`, `clampInt`; 50 sites clamp in all) | 22 |
| `isNaN` / `isFinite` guard, then a default | 21 |
| keystroke dropped unless in range (`if (n >= 1 && n <= 60) set(n)`) | 9 |
| named handler or wrapper component | 9 |

Integer versus decimal, min/max/step, optional blank and the Save gate are listed per site in the table at the end.

No site guarded the mouse wheel, none used `valueAsNumber`, none used a ref.

Blank was not only an annoyance. Sites it reached the backend from: a blank Auto-Announce interval POSTed `autoAnnounceIntervalHours: null`; a blank MeshCore frequency reached `setRadioParams` as `NaN`; a blank waypoint latitude sent a waypoint at 0; GeoJSON line weight PATCHed `NaN`; 15 Device Configuration fields put `NaN` in `ConfigurationTab` state.

## Design

`src/components/common/NumberInput.tsx` (+ CSS module, tests):

- Holds its own text draft. The field can be blank or half-typed; nothing is clamped or rewritten while typing.
- **Emits valid numbers only.** While the text is blank (and required), not a number, a decimal in an `integer` field, or outside `min`/`max`, `onChange` is not called and the parent keeps its last valid number. With `allowEmpty`, blank is legal and emits `null`.
- Invalid: 2px outline in `var(--color-error)`, `aria-invalid`, the reason ("Enter a number", "Must be between 3 and 24", …) through `aria-describedby` and as the tooltip. `showReason` shows the text under the field; modals with room for it use that.
- A blank required field stays blank and red on blur. Valid text settles on the parent's value on blur (`1.` becomes `1`).
- Follows the parent when the value changes from outside and the field is not focused; leaves the text alone while focused.
- Mouse wheel: no site guarded it, so the component does. A focused field drops focus on wheel; the page scrolls and the value does not

title: feat(chat): sender name opens the node popup with status; status emoji badge on the avatar (#5645)
body:
Closes #5645

## What this does

In the channel feed and the DM thread, the sender's **name** now opens the same node popup the avatar already opened. That popup gains the node's **status message** and a relative last-heard line, and it now works from the keyboard. Where a status starts with an emoji, that emoji shows as a small **badge on the sender's avatar**.

![Popup with a real status (rig node Yble on Sandbox)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5645-sender-status-popover/docs/public/images/features/5645-popup-status.png)

![Avatar badges, dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5645-sender-status-popover/docs/public/images/features/5645-avatar-badges-dark.png)

![Popup from a channel sender name, light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5645-sender-status-popover/docs/public/images/features/5645-feed-popup-light.png)

**About the screenshots.** The first is live rig data: `Yeraze BLE Sandbox` on source Sandbox, status `BLESandbox: Test Status Message (2026-08-20)` (letter first, so no badge). No rig node has an emoji-first status, so the other two use a **browser-side fixture**: a `fetch` wrapper in the test browser that adds a status to a few nodes in the `/api/poll` response. No radio, setting or database row was changed.

## Design

The issue was written before reading the code. This PR builds on what is there:

- **One popup, extended.** `NodePopup` already opened from the 32px `.sender-dot` avatar. It keeps its content and actions (More Details / Show on Map / Delete / Purge, traceroute tab) and gains:
  - a status block: full text, `white-space: pre-wrap`, clamped to 3 lines, full text on `title`; absent when the node has no status;
  - last heard as relative time, absolute time on hover; dimmed past 24 h;
  - Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; focus moves into the popup on open; Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside;
  - placement flips below the trigger when the popup does not fit above (`computePopupPlacement`, a pure function). The old code pushed the anchor down to y=320 instead, which covered the trigger.
  - It reads the node from the polled list on each render, so a status change shows while the popup is open.
- **`SenderAvatar`** (`src/components/SenderAvatar/`, CSS module) draws the existing dot unchanged plus one corner slot. `SenderNameButton` is the name as a real `<button>`. Both go through the existing `handleSenderClick`.
- **`getLeadingEmoji(status)`** in `src/utils/statusMessage.ts` returns the first grapheme when it is an emoji, else `null`. `splitGraphemes` is now exported.
- **DM list rows** have no avatar, so the leading emoji joins the row's indicator strip (`StatusEmojiIndicator`), with the same `Status: …` label.

### Decisions

| Question | Choice |
|---|---|
| Surfaces | Channel feed, DM thread (rows + header name), DM list. Not the Nodes list. Not the map. |
| DM list trigger | **None.** The `.node-short` chip still onl

Two new entries under **REST API Clients** in `docs/add-ons/index.md`, in the CardMesh format (#4708). Both are marked early preview and credit maxhayim. Docs only: no code, schema, or migration change.

### Mesh Screensaver (v0.2.0, MIT)

- Both carry the early-preview note.

title: fix(reticulum): phone tab bar filled the screen and hid the page
body:
## The fault

On a phone, a Reticulum source page shows only its tab bar. The bar fills the screen below the status strip: each tab is a full-height column, the active underline sits at the very bottom, the last tab is cut off, and no page content shows.

No issue was filed for this; the maintainer reported it with a screenshot.

## Root cause

`SourceNav` turns into a full-width bottom bar on phones (`.mobileBottomBar`: `width: 100%`, `flex-shrink: 0`). The flex row that holds the nav and the content pane must then stack. If it stays `flex-direction: row`, the bar takes the whole row, stretches to the row's full height, and the content pane beside it gets a width of 0.

MeshCore has that rule: `.meshcore-page-body { flex-direction: column-reverse }` in its mobile block, which #5311 widened to cover landscape phones.

Reticulum (#4698) copied MeshCore's **desktop** row into its own CSS module (`ReticulumPage.module.css` `.pageBody`) and left the mobile rule out. So the earlier fixes, which all landed in `MeshCorePage.css`, never reached it. It has been wrong at every phone size since it shipped.

Measured on current main, 390x844: bar 390x760, content pane 0x0. In landscape (844x390): bar 844x306, content pane 0 wide.

## The fix

One owner for the row, so the source types cannot drift again.

- New `src/components/nav/SourceNavLayout.tsx` + `SourceNavLayout.module.css`: the nav + content row, the content pane's flex sizing, and the `column-reverse` flip under the same media query as SourceNav's bottom bar.
- `ReticulumPage` and `MeshCorePage` both render `<SourceNavLayout nav={...}>`. Their private copies of the row are deleted (`.pageBody`, `.meshcore-page-body`, and the duplicate `flex`/`min-width` on the content panes). Each page still sets how its own pane scrolls.
- Meshtastic is not touched. Its `Sidebar` is `position: fixed` and `App.css` reserves room for the bar with `--app-nav-bar-height`, so it has no in-flow row to share. It already shares `SourceNav` itself.

Most of the line count in the two page files is re-indentation; view with whitespace hidden.

## Screenshots (390x844, source "RNS-Test")

| Before (main) | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/fix/reticulum-mobile-layout/docs/public/images/features/reticulum-mobile-layout-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/fix/reticulum-mobile-layout/docs/public/images/features/reticulum-mobile-layout-after.png) |

## Browser checks

I built this branch's frontend and served it on another port, with API calls proxied to the running dev container (main). The container was not rebuilt, restarted or reconfigured. Element rectangles, main vs this branch:

| Page | Viewport | main: bar / content | branch: bar / content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reticulum | 390x844 | 390x760 / 0x0 | 390x53 at the bottom / 390x708 |
| Reticulum | 844x390 | 844x306 / 0 wide | 844x44 at the bottom / 844x263 |
| Reticulum | 1280x800 | 56x

title: fix(admin): per-section Load for Status Message, Traffic Management and MeshBeacon (client and remote)
body:
## The fault

No GitHub issue: the maintainer asked for a direct fix.

The Admin Commands tab loads a node's config two ways: **Load All Config** and the **Load** button on each section. Each path had its own copy of the code that turns a `/api/admin/load-config` reply into form state, and the copies drifted. Status Message, Traffic Management and MeshBeacon were added to the load-all path only.

So the per-section Load for those three fetched the reply, dropped it, and still showed the green "loaded" tick. The form kept its defaults. A Save from there wrote the defaults over the node's real config.

`security` had the same fault in #5077; TAK (#5641) was added to both paths.

### Section table (before this PR)

| Section | Load button | Single-load case | Load-all case |
|---|---|---|---|
| device | yes | yes | yes |
| lora | yes | yes | yes |
| position | yes | yes | yes |
| mqtt | yes | yes | yes |
| security | yes | yes | yes |
| bluetooth | yes | yes | yes |
| network | yes | yes | yes |
| neighborinfo | yes | yes | yes |
| telemetry | yes | yes | yes |
| **statusmessage** | yes | **no** | yes |
| **trafficmanagement** | yes | **no** | yes |
| **meshbeacon** | yes | **no** | yes |
| tak | yes | yes | yes |
| owner | yes | yes (own endpoint) | yes (own endpoint) |
| channels | yes | yes (own loader) | yes (own loader) |

After this PR every row reads yes / yes, from one table.

## The fix

New `src/components/admin-commands/applyLoadedConfig.ts`:

- `LOAD_CONFIG_TYPES` lists the 13 sections `/api/admin/load-config` serves, in load-all order. `ADMIN_LOAD_SECTIONS` adds `owner` and `channels`.
- `CONFIG_APPLIERS` is a `Record<LoadConfigType, applier>`. A section added to the list with no applier does not compile.
- `applyLoadedConfig(configType, config, setters, { nodeNum })` writes the reply to state and returns `true`. It returns `false`, and writes nothing, for an empty reply or a section with no applier.

`AdminCommandsTab.tsx` drops both hand-written copies (about 300 lines). Load-all loops over `LOAD_CONFIG_TYPES`; the per-section handler calls the same function. A section is marked loaded only when `applyLoadedConfig` returns `true`.

## Decisions

- **Shared applier, not three more `case`s.** The mappings were copied from the load-all path, which already held the full set, so behaviour for the ten sections that worked is the same.
- **Position flags.** The per-section path used to merge decoded flags with `setPositionFlags`; load-all replaced them inside `setPositionConfig`. `decodePositionFlags` returns every flag, so the two give the same state. The shared applier uses the load-all form.
- **Load-all summary toast.** An empty reply already marked the section failed, but was not counted, so the toast could still say "all configs loaded". It now counts as a failure (config sections and owner).
- **Status maps** (initial, node switch, load-all start) come from `ADMIN_LOAD_SECTIONS` in place of three hand-kept lists. The node-switch list

title: feat(security): Protection Level picker for packet_signature_policy (#5612)
body:
Closes #5612

## What this does

Adds a **Protection Level** picker for `SecurityConfig.packet_signature_policy` (field 9, firmware 2.8.0+) to both places security is edited:

- the local **Configuration** tab (`SecurityConfigSection.tsx`)
- the Security block of **Admin Commands** (`AdminCommandsTab.tsx`), for local and remote nodes

Both use one shared component, `PacketSignaturePolicyPicker`. Until now MeshMonitor kept the node's policy across a save (#5637) but could not change it.

## Design

**Client value wins when sent.** The UI sends `packetSignaturePolicy` only when the user changed it. Left out, the server keeps the value it reads from the node, exactly as #5637 does. This is the marked hook in `buildSecurityConfigWrite` (`src/server/utils/securityConfigWrite.ts`), which stays the single builder for local and remote writes. An explicit COMPATIBLE (0) is a choice too: it takes field 9 off the wire, which firmware reads as COMPATIBLE.

**Keys are untouched.** They keep their server-side merge and never reach the client (#4736 / #4632). The read paths return the policy and leave the keys out; tests assert the private key is in no response, operation record or audit row.

**Server checks** (`POST /api/admin/commands`, `setSecurityConfig`), all before anything is read or sent:

| Case | Answer |
|------|--------|
| policy not 0, 1 or 2 | `400 INVALID_SIGNATURE_POLICY` |
| node below 2.8.0, or firmware not known | `400 SIGNATURE_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED` |
| policy omitted | node's own value kept (any firmware) |

Firmware comes from data we already hold, with no mesh traffic: the connected node's metadata for the local node, and the node row (`remoteAdminMetadata`, filled by Retrieve Device Metadata) for a remote one.

**Read paths.** `/load-config` (`security`) returns `packetSignaturePolicy` for local and remote nodes, plus the `firmwareVersion` the server holds for that node. `getCurrentConfig()` (behind `/api/config/current`, which the Configuration tab reads) now states the policy: proto3 leaves a zero enum off the wire and the object spread copies own fields only, so COMPATIBLE used to vanish.

**The picker never guesses.** It is disabled, with the reason beside it, when:

- the node runs firmware below 2.8.0 ("Requires firmware 2.8.0 or later. This node runs X.")
- the firmware version is not known (remote node with no metadata yet)
- the policy could not be read (security config not loaded, or a value this code does not know)

In each case the control reads **Unknown**, never Compatible. In Admin Commands, switching nodes clears the policy and firmware on screen.

**Confirms.**

- Balanced: a plain confirm.
- Strict: a typed confirm (the node's short name; with no short name, its node ID in Admin Commands or its long name in Configuration; never an empty word), plus a warning shown next to the control as soon as Strict is picked, saying what Strict drops and that it can cut the node off from older peers.
- Back to Compatible: no confirm.

title: feat(config): TAK team and role module settings (#5613)
body:
Closes #5613

## What this adds

A **TAK** section with two pickers, Team and Role, in:

- the **Configuration** tab (local node), and
- **Admin Commands → Module Configuration** (local or remote node).

It reads and writes `ModuleConfig.TAKConfig`, and device config backup / restore now carries it.

## Protocol facts (checked against the pinned protobufs, v2.8.0-130, and firmware `develop`)

- `module_config.proto`: `TAKConfig tak = 16 [since_firmware: "2.8.0"]` in the `ModuleConfig` oneof; `message TAKConfig { Team team = 1; MemberRole role = 2; }`.
- `admin.proto`: `ModuleConfigType.TAK_CONFIG = 15`.
- `atak.proto`: `enum Team` has 15 values (0 `Unspecifed_Color` "Default (Cyan)" … 14 `Brown`); `enum MemberRole` has 9 (0 `Unspecifed` "Default (Team Member)" … 8 `K9`). The names keep the proto's spelling.
- `mesh.proto`: `ExcludedModules.TAK_CONFIG = 0x20000`.
- Firmware `AdminModule::handleSetModuleConfig`: the `tak` case leaves `shouldReboot = true`, so **a save reboots the node**.
- Firmware `PositionModule.cpp` reads `moduleConfig.tak.team` / `.role` only while building the TAK position report, which it sends only when the device role is `TAK_TRACKER`.

## Design

**One table, checked against the submodule.** `src/utils/takConfig.ts` holds the Team and MemberRole values, proto names and proto labels, plus `normalizeTakConfig` and `validateTakConfigPayload`. Server and UI share it. `takConfig.test.ts` parses `protobufs/meshtastic/atak.proto` and compares every entry, so a protobuf bump that adds a team or role fails a test.

**Enum names vs numbers.** protobuf.js `toJSON` writes enum *names*, and a decoded local config goes through `res.json()`. So:
- `getCurrentConfig()` and `/api/admin/load-config` always answer `{ team: <number>, role: <number> }` (defaults filled in, since proto3 leaves 0 off the wire).
- The save routes accept a number or a proto name, refuse anything else with `fail(res, 400, 'INVALID_TAK_CONFIG', …)`, and send exactly the two fields as numbers.

**Registry.** `{ id: 'tak', kind: 'module', adminType: 15, field: 'tak' }` in `configTypes.ts`; `'tak'` in `VALID_MODULE_CONFIG_TYPES`; type 15 in `requestAllModuleConfigs` and `LOCAL_MODULE_CONFIG_TYPE_KEYS`. The three "TAK is deliberately skipped" comments are gone and the tests that pinned them are updated.

**Routes.** `POST /api/config/module/tak` (local, `configuration:write`; its two remaining bare `{ error }` replies now use `fail()` with `INVALID_MODULE_TYPE` / `MODULE_CONFIG_FAILED`), `/api/admin/commands` with `setTAKConfig` (via `createSetModuleConfigMessageGeneric('tak', …)`, admin only), and `/api/admin/load-config` with `configType: 'tak'` in both the local and remote switch.

**Gating.**
- Firmware: `supportedModules.takConfig = supportsTakConfig()` (2.8.0). Below that the Config section is dimmed with "needs firmware 2.8.0 or newer". For the Admin tab, a local load on older firmware answers `404 TAK_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED` instead of made-up defaults, and a remote

title: feat(automation): run-scoped step outputs, the empty-send rule, and two variable-store fixes (#5636)
body:
Closes #5636

## What this does

A **Run a script** step can keep its result for the rest of the same run, with no variable. Set **Store result in** to **This run only**, name the result, and later steps read it:

| Token | Renders |
| --- | --- |
| `{{ steps.<name>.output }}` | what the script printed (JSON renders as JSON) |
| `{{ steps.<name>.output.a.b }}` | a path into JSON output |
| `{{ steps.<name>.ok }}` | `true` if the script ran, `false` if it failed |

A `/joke` responder is now: *Run a script* (`joke.py`, This run only, name `joke`) → *Send a message* `{{ steps.joke.output }}`.

## Decisions (as set by the maintainer) and how each is built

1. **Keyed by a user-given name, not the step id.** The issue assumed stable ids; `compile.ts` regenerates ids from position on every save and `decompile` drops them. New param `params.outputName`, `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}`, unique within the automation, checked in `validateAutomationGraph`. `resultVariable` is not overloaded; a step may store to a variable, to the run, both (JSON only), or neither.
2. **Tokens** `steps.<name>.output[.path]` and `steps.<name>.ok`.
3. **v1: Run a script only.** `outputName` on any other block is a validation error.
4. **64 KiB cap** when stored for the run; the step's run-log line says `output "x" was cut to 64 KiB for this run`. The output is never written to run history, the live trace or the audit log (pinned by tests that grep the stored run row and the trace payload for a marker string).
5. **Empty-send rule** — see below.
6. **Two bug fixes** — see below.

## Design

- **Store**: `stepOutputs: Map<name, { ok, output }>` on the per-run `EngineEvalContext`, made in `fireAutomation` and cleared in its `finally`. It is reachable only through that run's context, so concurrent runs cannot share it. Test: two runs of one automation held at a Pause step until both scripts have run; each reply carries its own output.
- **Single pass**: `interpolateAsync` takes its paths from the template only and substitutes once. Output containing `{{ var.x }}` or `{{ steps.y.output }}` is sent as text. Pinned.
- **`varsOnly` fields** (Apprise URLs, waypoint key/source) still accept `var.*` only. Pinned, and the builder says so on the waypoint key.
- **Path walk** uses own properties only (`output.constructor` renders empty).
- **Over-size JSON** cannot be cut and stay JSON, so it is kept as its cut text: the whole-value token renders, a dotted path renders empty.
- **Builder flags, by DAG ancestry** (`stepOutputScopes` in `src/types/automation.ts`, shared by server and builder; rules interleave, so list order is wrong):
  - *always empty* (error): no step stores the name, or the storing step is not an ancestor (another rule, a later step, the step itself, a rule condition reading its own rule).
  - *may be empty* (warning): the storing step is an ancestor but does not always run first — a FINALLY step under ANY / NONE / ALWAYS reading a rule's output.

title: feat(status): quick-access status message pill with presets (#5616)
body:
Closes #5616

## What this adds

A status pill in the app header. It shows the local node's Status Message (cut short with an ellipsis, or "Set status" when empty) and opens a popover with:

- ten stock presets, one tap to set;
- a free-text input with a byte counter;
- Save and Clear;
- a note that other nodes may not see a change for up to 12 hours, and that clearing is not sent.

## Two things that differ from the brief: please check

**1. The limit is 79 bytes, not 80.** `module_config.options` says `*StatusMessageConfig.node_status max_size:80`. nanopb's `max_size` is the C buffer, and the firmware's generated header has `char node_status[80];` (`src/mesh/generated/meshtastic/module_config.pb.h`). That buffer holds the NUL, so 79 bytes of text fit. An 80-byte string fails nanopb's decode and the node drops the whole admin message with no error: the status just never saves. Same off-by-one as #5056. So the UI and server enforce 79. `NODE_STATUS_MAX_BYTES` in `src/utils/statusMessage.ts` is the one place to change it.

**2. The help preset uses 🙋, not 🆘.** The issue comment lists "🆘 Need help (non-urgent)", but the decision was that no preset may read as an emergency or SOS call, and that emoji is the letters "SOS" in a red box. In a truncated pill or node-list row it reads as an SOS. The label is unchanged. Swapping the emoji back is one line in `statusPresets.ts` (plus one test assertion).

## Placement

The mockup's strip (Sources button, node chip, status dots) is `src/components/AppHeader/AppHeader.tsx`, not `.channels-header` in `ChannelsTab.tsx`. The header is on every tab, so the pill is reachable from Channels as asked, and from everywhere else.

It sits in `.header-right`, before the connection badge. `.header-left` is `overflow: hidden` and would clip the popover.

- **Desktop:** pill with text, capped at 14rem; popover 20rem wide under it.
- **Phone, portrait (`max-width: 768px`):** the pill drops to its icon (text stays for screen readers), the same trade the connection badge makes at this breakpoint, since every pixel in `.header-right` comes out of the source name. The popover spans the header with a gutter each side instead of hanging off the pill, which would run off the left of a 390px screen.
- **Phone, landscape (`max-height: 500px`):** wider than 768px, so the block above does not apply (the #5051-#5054 trap). Text kept, capped at 9rem; the popover scrolls inside the short viewport and its presets go three-across.

## Who sees it

`shouldShowQuickStatus()` (`quickStatusGate.ts`), an allowlist:

- signed in, with `configuration:write` on this source;
- a Meshtastic device source (`meshtastic_tcp`, or the legacy single-source view). Hidden on MQTT broker/bridge, MeshCore, Reticulum, and any type added later;
- node connected.

The pill then hides itself unless `/api/config/current` reports `supportedModules.statusmessage` (firmware 2.7.20+, `MeshtasticManager.supportsStatusMessage()`). A user with write but no `configuration

title: feat(admin): shutdown, DFU and factory reset actions, with audit log (#5614, #5615)
body:
Closes #5614
Closes #5615

## What this adds

Four admin actions in the Admin Commands tab, in a "Power and reset" group inside the Danger Zone, next to Reboot:

| Action | `/commands` name | AdminMessage field | Target | Confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shut down | `shutdown` | `int32 shutdown_seconds = 98` | local or remote | local: plain. remote: type the short name |
| Reboot into DFU mode | `enterDfuMode` | `bool enter_dfu_mode_request = 21` | local only | plain |
| Reset config (keeps identity key and BLE bonds) | `factoryResetConfig` | `int32 factory_reset_config = 99` | local only | type the short name |
| Full device reset (new identity) | `factoryResetDevice` | `int32 factory_reset_device = 94` | local only | type the short name |

It also writes an audit log entry for each of these **and for the existing reboot** (both `POST /reboot` and `/commands reboot`), which wrote none before.

## #5614 names the wrong field

The issue asks for `reboot_ota_seconds`. In the pinned protobufs (`protobufs/meshtastic/admin.proto`, v2.8.0-130) that field is `int32 reboot_ota_seconds = 95 [deprecated = true]`, "Only Implemented for ESP32 Devices", deprecated in favour of `reboot_ota_mode` in 2.7.17. It is the ESP32 OTA loader, not DFU.

DFU is `bool enter_dfu_mode_request = 21` ("Enter (UF2) DFU mode"). It has no delay. Firmware `src/modules/AdminModule.cpp`:

- `master`: `#if defined(ARCH_NRF52) || defined(ARCH_RP2040)` → `enterDfuMode()`
- `develop` (2.8 line): adds an `ARCH_STM32` branch
- ESP32: the case logs, shows a banner and does nothing

So there is no `/reboot-ota` route and no `seconds` parameter. A builder test asserts field 21 is on the wire and field 95 is not.

## What the firmware does (checked against `meshtastic/firmware`)

- **Shutdown** — `shutdownAtMsec = (s < 0) ? 0 : millis() + s * 1000`. A negative value cancels. The handler does **not** check `canShutdown`.
- **Factory reset** — both call `NodeDB::factoryReset(eraseBleBonds)`: remove `/prefs`, then `installDefaultNodeDatabase`, `installDefaultDeviceState`, `installDefaultConfig(!eraseBleBonds)`, `installDefaultModuleConfig`, `installDefaultChannels`, then `reboot`. That wipes config, module config, channels and PSKs, admin keys, NodeDB, WiFi settings, and sets the region to `UNSET`. The value in the packet is ignored.
  - `factory_reset_config` → `factoryReset()`: `installDefaultConfig(true)` keeps the private key; BLE bonds stay.
  - `factory_reset_device` → `factoryReset(true)`: the private key goes (new key pair, so a new identity, and on 2.8 a new nodeNum since nodeNum = crc32(pubkey)), BLE bonds are cleared, and ESP32 runs `nvs_flash_erase()`.

## Design

**Server** (`src/server/routes/adminRoutes.ts`, `src/server/protobufService.ts`)

- Four builders: `createEnterDfuModeMessage`, `createShutdownMessage`, `createFactoryResetConfigMessage`, `createFactoryResetDeviceMessage`. They use protobuf field names, so no field numbers appear in the source.
- `LOCAL_ONLY_DEVICE_ACTION

title: fix(security): a local Security save keeps the node's packet signature policy
body:
Refs #5612 (does not close it: that issue adds the UI to set the policy; this PR only stops us from resetting it).

## The fault

Firmware 2.8 added `SecurityConfig.packet_signature_policy` (field 9: COMPATIBLE 0 / BALANCED 1 / STRICT 2). Firmware replaces the whole security struct on a set (`AdminModule::handleSetConfig`: `config.security = c.payload_variant.security`), so a write with no field 9 sets the node to COMPATIBLE.

- `protobufService.createSetSecurityConfigMessage` writes field 9 only when the caller passes `packetSignaturePolicy`.
- The **remote** branch of `setSecurityConfig` passed the value it had just read from the node (#4736).
- The **local** branch merged the keys from the manager cache and never the policy.

So every local Security save (Configuration tab, or Admin Commands aimed at the local node) reset a node that the phone app had set to BALANCED or STRICT back to COMPATIBLE, with no sign to the user.

## The fix

- **One builder for both paths.** New `src/server/utils/securityConfigWrite.ts`: `buildSecurityConfigWrite(clientConfig, current, { allowClientKeys })` merges the node's keys and policy into the write. Local and remote both call it, so they cannot drift again.
- **The local path now reads the device first.** New `MeshtasticManager.refreshLocalSecurityConfig()` sends `get_config_request(SECURITY)` to the local node, waits for the answer (5 s), stores it in the cache, and returns it. The connect-time cache is not good enough: the device does not push later changes, and firmware does not reboot on a security set, so a policy set from another client after we connected is not in the cache.
- **Unknown policy: refuse.** If the local node does not answer, the save returns `409 SECURITY_CONFIG_READBACK_FAILED` through `fail()` and sends nothing. The remote path already failed closed the same way. Guessing "COMPATIBLE" is the silent downgrade this PR removes.
- **A client-supplied policy is dropped** on both paths (before, the local path spread the request body into the write, so a crafted request could set it). There is no UI for it yet, so a value in the body is not a user's choice. The hook for #5612 is one marked line in `buildSecurityConfigWrite`.
- **Keys are unchanged in effect:** still merged server-side, a new private key is local-only and sent with its derived public key (#4632), a remote node's keys never reach the client (#4736). One small hardening: a new private key pasted with a `base64:` prefix is now normalized before it is encoded.

### Firmware older than 2.8

The field does not exist there. The decode of the node's answer (`defaults: true`) reports the absent enum as `0`. The builder treats `0`/absent as "write nothing", so field 9 never goes to a pre-2.8 node. For a 2.8 node at COMPATIBLE the field is also left off, which firmware reads as COMPATIBLE (proto3 default), so nothing is lost. (Before this PR the remote path wrote an explicit `48 00` to pre-2.8 nodes; that was harmless, nanopb skips unknown

title: fix(sources): mask credentials in source config for non-admin editors
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #5619. Two places still returned more of a source's configuration than the caller needs:

1. A signed-in non-admin holding `sources:write` received the stored config with only a short list of named password fields removed, because the edit form saves the whole config back.
2. The Analyzer Observer status routes returned broker URLs as stored.

There is no issue for this; it was found in review of #5619.

## Design

### Source config for non-admin editors

The typed spec in `utils/sourceConfigRedaction.ts` now also says how each field reaches a non-admin editor. A new field or source type still does not compile until it has a rule, and the rule now has to say whether the field is a credential.

| Class | On read | On save |
|---|---|---|
| `plain` | as stored | as sent |
| `secret` | left out; its path is listed in `maskedConfigFields` | missing or `''` keeps the stored value; `null` clears it; anything else replaces it |
| `url` | without `user:password@`, query string, fragment | a part left out is put back from the stored URL; an explicit empty part (`scheme://@host`, trailing `?` / `#`) clears it; a new part replaces it |

Credential-bearing fields:

| Source type | Field | Class | Bound to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meshtastic_tcp` | none | | |
| `meshcore` | `observer.brokerUrl`, `observer.brokers[].url` | url | |
| `meshcore_mqtt` | `brokerUrl` | url | |
| `meshcore_mqtt` | `password` | secret | `brokerUrl` |
| `mqtt_bridge` | `upstream.url` | url | |
| `mqtt_bridge` | `upstream.password` | secret | `upstream.url` |
| `mqtt_broker` | `auth.password` | secret | nothing (a listener's own login) |
| `reticulum` | `bridgeUrl` | url | |
| `reticulum` | `token` | secret | `bridgeUrl` |

Usernames, hosts, ports and every other setting stay visible to an editor. Reticulum `peers[]` and the virtual-node flags hold no credential. Observer signing keys and broker passwords live in their own encrypted stores and are not in `config`.

Rules on save, for a non-admin:

- A stored credential is kept only for the endpoint it was stored for. If the save changes the scheme, host or port of the URL it is bound to, the stored value is dropped unless a new one is sent. The same holds for the hidden parts of a URL.
- List entries (`observer.brokers[]`) are matched to stored entries by scheme, host, port and path, never by position. No match, or more than one, means nothing is carried over.
- A value is only ever read from the same path of the same source. Nothing in a response refers to a stored value, so there is nothing to move to another field or source.
- A URL whose credentials cannot be told from its path (an `@` after a `/`, `?` or `#`; a backslash, whitespace or control character) is withheld whole, and kept only when the field comes back blank.
- A stored field the spec does not classify is not shown, and is preserved.
- A non-admin may not point `observer.brokerUrl` at another endpoint while the single (pre-#5014) Observer broker lo

title: fix(meshcore): Repeater-source nodes open in Node Details and stay on the map (#5632)
body:
Closes #5632

## What was wrong

On a MeshCore Repeater source the Nodes list showed every advert-ingested node with its real name, but the `->` arrow opened Node Details with only the public key filled in, and a node drawn on the map left it after its next advert.

The issue blames the position gate on `GET /api/nodes`. That is not the cause: **no MeshCore view reads `/api/nodes`**. `src/components/NodesTab.tsx` and `NodeDetailsBlock` are the Meshtastic views. The MeshCore page (`MeshCorePage` -> `useMeshCore`) loads `GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/snapshot` and then takes socket pushes.

The real cause is two lists that should agree and did not:

| View | Reads | Source on the server |
|---|---|---|
| Nodes list (`MeshCoreNodesView`) | `nodes` ∪ `contacts` | `getAllNodes()`: stored `meshcore_nodes` rows |
| Node Details (`MeshCoreContactDetailPanel`, via `contactsByKey.get(selected) ?? null`) | `contacts` only | `getContacts()`: the in-memory contact map |
| Nodes map (`MeshCoreMap`) | `contacts` only | same |

A Repeater has no contact table. `seedContactsFromDb` and `refreshContacts` both return early for it, so its in-memory map is always empty and `contacts` came back `[]`. The list showed a hundred named nodes; each opened with `contact = null`, which is the "pubkey prefix and nothing else" shell.

## Why the one node left the map

Stored coordinates were **not** lost. `upsertNode`'s merge guard (#3504) kept them, and a new wire-accurate test confirms the row still holds them with `lastAdvertHadPosition = false`.

The only contacts a Repeater-source client ever held came from live `meshcore:contact:updated` pushes, and the client replaces its record with each push (`contactsRef.current.set(c.publicKey, c)` in `useMeshCore.ts`). A Companion pushes its merged in-memory record (`latitude: data.latitude ?? existing.latitude`). The Repeater pushed the **bare advert** (`latitude: advert.latitude`). So:

1. Advert with a position arrives while the page is open: the push creates the contact, the map draws it, Node Details fills in.
2. The next advert has no position: the push replaces the record with one that has no coordinates, and the marker goes.
3. Any reload re-reads the snapshot, where `contacts` is empty: the node leaves Node Details too.

The infra age filter (#4899), the #5585 hide toggle and the map's own filters were not involved. The neighbours poll had the same fault (it pushed its own fields only).

## Fix

- **`MeshCoreManager.getContactsForView()`**: the contact list for `/snapshot` and `GET /contacts`. A Companion still answers from its in-memory map. A Repeater builds the list from its stored rows (own key and local row left out), so Node Details and the map find every node the list shows. It is keyed on the source's config as well as `deviceType`, so a disconnected Repeater still lists its nodes.
- **`contactFromNodeRow()`**: one row-to-contact mapping, shared with `seedContactsFromDb`.
- **Repeater pushes send the stored row** (

title: fix(traceroute): write the position snapshot on every path; auto-traceroute picker counts either stored form
body:
Two traceroute faults left over from #5611, one commit each. There is no issue for this work; the faults are described below.

## Fault A: the position snapshot was written by one writer out of four

`traceroutes.routePositions` (#1862) holds where each node stood when a run was recorded, so an old run still draws where the nodes were then. `traceroutes.channel` is what `maskTraceroutesByChannel` gates the row on (#3092).

Four code paths write a completed row. Only one wrote these two columns:

| Writer | Backend | Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `insertTraceroute` | PostgreSQL, MySQL | reply with no pending row | both written | both written |
| `updateTracerouteResponse` | PostgreSQL, MySQL | pending row filled by the reply (a run sent from MeshMonitor) | **neither** | both written |
| `upsertTracerouteSync`, insert branch | SQLite | reply with no pending row | **neither** | both written |
| `upsertTracerouteSync`, update branch | SQLite | pending row filled by the reply | **neither** | both written |

So no SQLite row had a snapshot, and no run sent from MeshMonitor had one on any backend. Confirmed on the dev database: the two runs sent from source Sandbox (3639506708 → 2732916556 and → 944633591) have `routePositions` NULL and `channel` NULL.

### The fix

- `replyColumns()` in `src/db/repositories/traceroutes.ts` is now the one definition of the columns a reply fills in. All four writers spread it. `updateTracerouteResponse(id, reply)` takes the reply record in place of eight positional arguments.
- `buildRoutePositionsSnapshot()` in `src/server/utils/tracerouteSnapshot.ts` is now the one snapshot builder. The radio reply path and MQTT ingest each had a copy.

### What the snapshot holds

Both endpoints and every hop of `route` and `routeBack`. For each, the node row on the run's own source is read and its effective position is stored as `{ lat, lng, alt? }` keyed by node number: a public position override when one is set (#2847), else the device GPS. A node with no row or no position is left out, and readers fall back to its live position.

### Privacy

The snapshot is stored once and served to every reader of the row, so it must not hold anything that depends on who is looking.

- **Private position override: one change in content.** The old builders stored the override whether or not it was private. No route that serves traceroute rows checks `nodes_private:read` against the snapshot, so a user who cannot see that pin live could read it from `routePositions`. That leak already existed for PostgreSQL/MySQL reply rows and MQTT rows; writing the snapshot everywhere would have spread it to every SQLite install. The builder now leaves a private-override node out. The reader's live fallback then applies the per-viewer mask. An override is a pin the user set, so the live value is the same point unless the pin moved.
- **`channel` on SQLite is a tightening.** A NULL channel reads as "no restriction" in `maskTraceroutesByChannel`,

title: fix(sources): tighten source config redaction for non-admins
body:
## What

Tightens how a source's `config` is redacted for callers who are not admins.

The old helper removed a short, fixed list of fields and passed the rest of `config` through. That list had not kept up with the source types added since, and any new field was returned until someone added it to the list. There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for a direct fix.

## Design

`src/server/utils/sourceConfigRedaction.ts` holds an **allowlist**. Every field of every source type has one of three classes:

| Class | Who gets it |
|---|---|
| open | anyone who can list sources (feature flags the UI draws from) |
| granted | connection endpoints: a signed-in user with `sources:read`, or an admin |
| withheld | admins only |

A field with no rule is dropped. The spec is typed against the config interfaces, so a new source type, or a new field on a typed config, does not compile until it is classified.

Callers fall into four groups:

- **admin**: unchanged (full config, minus Observer key material).
- **signed in with `sources:write`**: unchanged (config minus passwords). They save the whole config back, so the edit form must round-trip it.
- **signed in with `sources:read`**: the allowlist, endpoints included. URLs lose credentials, query string and fragment.
- **everyone else** (no login, the anonymous account whatever it is granted, or signed in with neither grant): the allowlist without endpoints. The row carries `endpointHidden: true` so the UI can say so.

This is the rule #5602 and #5607 set for the status route and the ingest overview; `mayViewSourceEndpoint` is now the one shared check, and the ingest overview uses it.

Routes changed:

- `GET /api/sources`, `GET /api/sources/:id`, `POST /api/sources/reorder`, and the `POST /api/sources` / `PUT /api/sources/:id` responses all go through one `redactSourceForCaller`.
- `GET /api/sources/:id/status`: free-text errors and Observer broker URLs are blanked (shape kept) for callers who may not see the endpoint. The fixed auth-stop text from #5596/#5610 is kept.
- `GET /api/config`, `GET /api/poll`, `GET /api/connection`, `GET /api/connection/info`: the node address takes the same grant. Being signed in is no longer enough on its own.

UI, when an endpoint is withheld:

- Source card: the Virtual Node badge reads `VN` without a port; the Observer badge counts brokers from a `brokerCount` the server sends in place of the list.
- Info tab and node info modal: the address line reads "Hidden" instead of falling back to another value or printing `:4403`.

## Decisions

- A non-admin `sources:write` holder keeps today's view. Withholding more from them would make their next save drop it. Narrowing this needs a server-side merge on save and is left for a follow-up.
- Backup, restore and settings routes do not use this helper and are unchanged. `preserveSourceCredentials` is unchanged; a blank password on save still keeps the stored one (covered by a test for both editor and admin).
- The legacy MM-SEC

title: fix(backup): back up every table, stream the export, allowlist restore on all backends
body:
## The fault

There is no issue for this; it comes out of the audit in #5602.

A system backup was an opt-in list: `BACKUP_TABLES` named 28 tables, and the schema has 83. Each new table had to be remembered, and 52 were not. A restore of a MeshCore-only install brought back **no nodes, no messages and no automations**. Three more faults sat next to it:

1. **The exporter could not back up a large install at all.** It read each table whole and built one pretty-printed string. On the dev database (`route_segments`: 3.46 M rows) that reaches 1.96 GB of memory and then throws `Invalid string length`. The dev container's `/data/system-backups` is empty for this reason.
2. **PostgreSQL and MySQL restore did not check table names** from `metadata.json` against the allowlist. SQLite did. Neither checked column names; SQLite did.
3. **PostgreSQL restore failed on ten tables** whose `id` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`. Two of them (`auto_favorite_targets`, `auto_favorite_assignments`) were already in the backup, so a PostgreSQL restore with rows in either failed whole.

## What changed

### Every table, or an explicit reason why not

`src/server/services/systemBackupTables.ts` holds two lists:

- `BACKUP_TABLES` — 80 tables, in restore order.
- `BACKUP_EXCLUDED_TABLES` — 3 tables, each with its reason. Unchanged from before:

| Excluded | Reason |
|---|---|
| `sessions` | Live session tokens. A stolen backup would be a stolen login. |
| `push_subscriptions` | Push endpoint secrets (MM-SEC-1 footnote 1). Browsers re-register. |
| `backup_history` | Index of device-config backup files, which are not in a system backup. |

`sqlite_sequence` is SQLite's own bookkeeping and is not a schema table.

All four groups the maintainer asked for are in: configuration and user state, MeshCore and Reticulum data, secrets, and history/logs. **I excluded nothing new.**

### Drift is now a test failure

`systemBackupService.tables.test.ts` (SQLite) and `systemBackupRestore.roundTrip.pgmysql.test.ts` (PostgreSQL, MySQL) read the table set from the **real schema** — the Drizzle definitions for all three dialects, and a database built by replaying every migration on each backend — and fail when:

- a table is in neither list;
- a list names a table that does not exist;
- a foreign-key parent is listed after its child (edges read from `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` / `pg_constraint` / `information_schema`);
- a backed-up table has a secret-looking column (`psk`, `password`, `token`, `credential`, `privateKey`…) and is not in `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES`.

The old test asked for a "security review" before adding a sensitive table. That intent is kept and moved to where it bites: the **exclusion list is pinned** to exactly the three tables above, so taking one out (or adding one) is a visible edit to a test that says why, and a table that holds a secret must be declared with what protects it.

### Restore order and foreign keys

Every foreign key in the schema, on all three backends, poi

    `src/db/migrations.test.ts` does **not** need editing — its assertions are registry-derived and automatically cover the new entry.
    **`settingsKey` is required** (every migration but the 001 baseline has one) — all three backends use it for idempotency tracking. SQLite checks it inline in its loop; PostgreSQL/MySQL go through the ledger in `src/db/migrationLedger.ts` (#4233).

+   you do. If it holds a key, credential or token, list it in `BACKUP_SECRET_TABLES` too.
 3. Make migrations **idempotent** using the shared helpers in `src/server/migrations/helpers.ts`.
    The ledger means a migration normally runs once per database, but a crash between the migration and its ledger write re-runs it, so **idempotency is still mandatory on every backend**. In particular, never write a migration that unconditionally deletes and rebuilds a table — that is what made 030 wipe and rebuild 865k `route_segments` rows on every single boot (#4233). Guard destructive work behind a "has this already been applied?" check, and batch bulk inserts rather than issuing one round-trip per row.

title: test: take wall-clock and module-load cost out of flaky tests
body:
## The fault

There is no issue for this. The full local Vitest suite failed on a busy host while CI stayed green. The same three files kept failing: `meshtasticManager.transportTraffic`, `meshtasticManager.lastHeardReplayGuard` and `meshtasticManager.autoPingAck`, with other `meshtasticManager.*` hook timeouts and one `messages.search` timeout now and then. `EmbedMap.test.tsx` also failed in CI from time to time and passed on rerun.

Tests only. **No production code changed, no migration, no mesh impact.**

## Causes, as reproduced

**1. Module load charged to a hook budget.** 35 `meshtasticManager.*` test files ran `await import('./meshtasticManager.js')` inside `beforeEach`. The first hook paid for the whole module load: about 2.3 s on an idle host. At 4x CPU oversubscription that passes the 10 s `hookTimeout`. The second test's hook then waits on the same import and times out too.

**2. A clock read at collection, compared with a clock read in the test.** `transportTraffic` and `lastHeardReplayGuard` set `nowSec` in the `describe` body, which runs while the file is collected. They then asserted `toBeCloseTo(nowSec, -1)` (within 5 s) against the stamp the manager took from its own `Date.now()`. The slow import sat between the two reads, so the gap was 15 to 29 s under load.

**3. EmbedMap: "spy was called" is not "data arrived".** `EmbedMap` renders its layers when `/config` lands, before the data fetches return, so the first render carries an empty list. The tests did `waitFor(spy called)` then read `mock.calls.at(-1)`. Delaying the mocked data fetch by 30 ms made the old file fail 5 of 14 tests with the exact messages seen in CI: `expected [] to have a length of 1` and `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'key')`.

**4. v1 `messages.search`: bcrypt in a loop.** The `search()` helper minted a new API token (a bcrypt-12 hash, ~210 ms) for every request, and one test made seven requests: about 4 s of its 10 s budget on an idle host.

Production code was checked for a stale module-load timestamp. There is none: `replayGuard.ts` takes `nowMs` from its caller, and the manager passes a fresh `Date.now()`.

## Fixes

- **Import at collection time.** Each of the 35 manager files, and `meshcoreIngestReadRoutes.test.ts`, now does `const managerModule = await import('./meshtasticManager.js')` once at the top of the file, after the mock declarations. Collection has no timeout, so the load cost no longer counts against a hook. The repo already uses top-level `await import` in tests. No timeout was raised anywhere.
- **Pinned clock.** The two wall-clock files fake `Date` only (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })`) at a fixed instant and assert the exact stamp with `toBe`. This is stricter than before: a stamp 3 s off used to pass and now fails.
- **EmbedMap.** A `latestProps(spy, ready)` helper waits for the render that holds the data. The mock now answers the data endpoints 20 ms after `/config`, so every run goes through the empty first rend

title: fix(traceroute): serve every traceroute row requester-first (row-orientation audit)
body:
## The fault

There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for the fix directly. PR #5586 found it in one service and fixed that service. This PR audits every other reader.

A completed traceroute is stored in the `traceroutes` table **two ways round**, depending on which writer made the row:

| How the run started | Stored as |
|---|---|
| Sent through MeshMonitor (UI, auto-traceroute, automation, Virtual Node client). `recordTracerouteRequest` writes a pending row; the reply updates it in place and does not flip `from`/`to`. | `{ from: requester, to: responder }` |
| A reply with no pending row (sent from a phone app, or the pending row timed out), every MQTT-observed row, and our own outgoing reply when another node traceroutes us. | `{ from: responder, to: requester }` |

The `route` / `routeBack` / `snrTowards` / `snrBack` arrays are the same in both: `route` always runs from the requester. So a reader that assumes one endpoint order attaches the route to the wrong end for the other form.

Almost every reader assumed `from` = requester (`[from, ...route, to]`). One (`useTracerouteAnalysis`) and two comments assumed the opposite. Each was right for one form and wrong for the other:

- **Two or more hops:** the first hop is joined to the responder and the last hop to the requester. Those links do not exist.
- **One hop:** the links are right but each carries the other link's SNR.
- **Zero hops:** forward and return are swapped.

## Readers audited

Status is after this PR. "Was wrong for" names the stored form the reader misread before.

| Reader | Assumed | Was wrong for | Wrong outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decomposeTraceroute` (Nodes map via `useTraceroutePaths`, `DashboardMap`, `TracerouteWidget`, Explorer map) | from = requester | reply / MQTT rows | segments drawn responder→first hop and last hop→requester; SNR on the wrong hop | **fixed** (rows now arrive requester-first) |
| `GET /api/embed/:id/traceroutes` | from = requester | reply / MQTT rows | same false segments on public embeds | **fixed** |
| Traceroute Explorer (`/explorer`, `explorerModel`, table, detail, map) | from = requester | reply rows | "from → to" label reversed; one pair split into two (`A>B`, `B>A`); path listed backwards; same packet on a TCP and an MQTT source not de-duplicated | **fixed** |
| Node traceroute panel (`TracerouteBody` popup, `NodePopup`, `TracerouteHistoryModal`, `RouteSegmentTraceroutesModal`, `TracerouteCopyLinks`) | from = requester | reply rows | Forward and Return paths start at the wrong node | **fixed** |
| Traceroute strip + statistical route (`tracerouteStrip`, `tracerouteAggregate`, `/participation`) | from = requester (per row) | reply rows | forward lane built responder-first | **fixed** |
| `useTracerouteAnalysis` (Map Analysis paths, 3D lines, inspector) | from = **responder** | runs sent from MeshMonitor, i.e. most rows on a TCP source | inbound/outbound and SNR attributed to the wrong hop | **fixed** (hook flipped; r

title: fix(mqtt-bridge): stop retrying a rejected broker login, per client
body:
## The fault

There is no issue for this; it is the part of #5602 that was left undone.

An `mqtt_bridge` source whose upstream broker rejects the login (CONNACK 4 or 5) retried for ever at the 60 s backoff cap:

1. **The subscriber client** (`mqttBridgeManager.ts`) showed "Broker rejected authentication" and kept sending a CONNECT every ~60 s for as long as the process lived.
2. **Each per-gateway publisher** (`mqttBridgePublisherPool.ts`) did the same. Worse, `mqtt.js` queues QoS 0 publishes while offline, so every uplink packet for a refused gateway sat in memory, without bound.

#5602 added an opt-in `maxAuthFailures` to the shared `MqttBrokerClient` and used it for MeshCore ingest. This PR opts the bridge in.

## Design

Maintainer decision: **per client, 5 rejections in a row.**

- **Subscriber stops** → the bridge's intake halts. Gateway publishers the broker still accepts keep publishing.
- **One gateway publisher stops** → only that gateway stops. The subscriber and the other gateways carry on. (A CONNACK 5 in the pool can mean the broker refuses one Client ID.)
- A successful connect resets that client's count. Other errors (broker down, network, TLS) never count and keep the normal backoff.
- A **changed** config save, or **Connect**, clears every stop on the source.

### No unbounded queue

- `MqttBrokerClient.publish()` now refuses once the client is stopped, so nothing can reach the `mqtt.js` offline queue.
- On the stop the owner closes the client (`end(true)`), which throws away whatever was queued during the five failing logins.
- The pool keeps the stopped entry as a marker. Without it, the next packet from that gateway would build a new client and hand the broker five more logins.
- `pool.publish()` resolves `'dropped'` for a stopped gateway. It does not throw: the bridge does not count it as sent, does not record an echo, does not set `lastError`. Nothing upstream blocks or retries.
- The subscriber's own uplink (broker-self gateway, `single` mode, and the `mqttLink` client-proxy `publish()`) is dropped the same way. `publish()` returns without a throw when stopped, since the proxy caller logs one warning per throw.
- Drops are counted (`uplinkAuthStoppedDrops`, plus `droppedPublishes` per gateway) and logged **once per stop**, at `warn`.

### Reconnect-storm lessons (#5079) still hold

`STABLE_RESET_MS` (120 s) is untouched and still above the 60 s backoff cap. A stopped client is unregistered from the shared `MqttReconnectCoordinator`, so it holds no slot in the pending set and cannot pin or reset the shared backoff. Tests cover a healthy sibling reconnecting on the shared timer after another gateway stopped.

### Restart

- `POST /api/sources/:id/connect` now accepts `mqtt_bridge`. It calls `reconnectAuthStopped()`, which rebuilds **only** the stopped clients. A connected or still-retrying bridge answers `alreadyRunning` and is not touched, so a repeated click adds no logins.
- A save whose config differs restarts the bridg

title: fix(notifications): a source with no saved preferences uses the built-in defaults, never another source's row
body:
## The fault

There is no issue for this; it was found during #5605.

`getUserNotificationPreferencesAsync(userId, sourceId)` fell back to `getUserPreferences(userId, '')` when the user had no row for that source (the #4020 fallback). With an empty source id the repository dropped the source filter and returned the user's **first row of any source**. So a source the user never configured used the settings saved for another source: enabled channels (by channel number, which is a different channel there), keyword lists, the DM / emoji / MQTT / new-node / traceroute / server-event toggles, the Web Push and Apprise switches, Apprise URLs, node-name prefix and mutes. #5605 isolated the two template columns; everything else still crossed.

Verified on `origin/main` with the new send-count test (below): user 1 has a row on source A only, and source B filters and delivers with A's row.

## Decision applied

No borrowing. Preferences for (user, source) are the row saved for exactly that source, else the built-in defaults.

## What changed

- **Repository** — `getUserPreferences(userId, sourceId?)` is an exact read. `''` or a missing id reads the unsourced `''` row only; it can no longer return a source's row.
- **One definition of the defaults** — `src/utils/notificationDefaults.ts`. Used by the GET route, the filter path, the repository's column fallbacks, the legacy-blob reader and the Notifications tab.
- **Resolver** — `resolveNotificationPreferencesAsync` returns the prefs and where they came from (`row` / `legacyBlob` / `default`). `getUserNotificationPreferencesAsync` now returns null only for an invalid user id.
- **Routes** — GET answers a never-configured source with the defaults and `usingDefaults: true`. POST builds a source's first row from the defaults plus the posted fields. The Apprise test route and the untargeted push/Apprise broadcasts now pass the source id to the node-name-prefix lookup (they read with no source before).
- **Waypoint alerts** — only the row of the waypoint's own source counts (was "any row true", values from the exact row, else `''`, else the user's first row).
- **Web Push for new node / traceroute / server event** — goes only to subscriptions on the event's source. See "Bundled fix" below.
- **UI** — the Notifications tab shows a note when a source has nothing saved; it goes away on save. MeshCore sources get wording that does not mention channels.

### Divergent defaults found, now unified

| Where | What it said |
| --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCES` in `notificationRoutes.ts` (GET) | Web Push on, channels none, `Hi`/`Help`, `Test`/`Copy` |
| Initial state in `NotificationsTab.tsx` | Same, but Web Push **off** |
| Per-column fallbacks in `mapPreferencesRow` | Same booleans, repeated inline |
| Legacy blob reader | Same booleans, repeated inline; keyword lists empty |
| Filter path with no row at all | **Allow every message** (`prefs === null → don't filter`); new-node/traceroute **not** sent; desktop

title: fix(meshcore): Virtual Node sends the packed out_path_len, not a hop count
body:
## The fault

The MeshCore Virtual Node answers `GetContacts` with one `Contact` frame per contact. It wrote the contact's **hop count** into the `out_path_len` byte. On the wire that byte is **packed**:

- top 2 bits: hop-hash width − 1 (1, 2 or 3 bytes per hop; `11` is reserved)
- bottom 6 bits: hop count
- `0xFF`: no route (`OUT_PATH_UNKNOWN`), sends flood

So the hop count is only right for 1-byte hashes. A contact with a 2-hop, 2-byte route went out as `0x02` with `a3 f2 7f 01` behind it; a client (the MeshCore app, Home Assistant) read that as two 1-byte hops `a3`, `f2`. The right byte is `0x42`.

The same wrong value fed the `AddUpdateContact` diff: it compared the client's echoed byte against the stored hop count.

Noted during #5566, which fixed the read side (`decodeOutPathLen()`). There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for a direct fix.

## Layout, checked against source

MeshCore firmware, `meshcore-dev/MeshCore` `main` at `a366955c`:

- `src/Packet.h`: `getPathHashSize() { return (path_len >> 6) + 1; }`, `getPathHashCount() { return path_len & 63; }`, `setPathHashSizeAndCount(sz, n) { path_len = ((sz - 1) << 6) | (n & 63); }`
- `src/Packet.cpp` `isValidPathLen`: refuses hash size 4 ("Reserved for future") and `hash_count * hash_size > MAX_PATH_SIZE`
- `src/helpers/ContactInfo.h`: `#define OUT_PATH_UNKNOWN 0xFF`, `uint8_t out_path_len; uint8_t out_path[MAX_PATH_SIZE];`
- `examples/companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp` `writeContactRespFrame`: `out_frame[i++] = contact.out_path_len; memcpy(&out_frame[i], contact.out_path, MAX_PATH_SIZE);` — the stored byte goes to the app as is. The same function builds `RESP_CODE_CONTACT` and `PUSH_CODE_NEW_ADVERT` (0x8A).
- `updateContactFromFrame`: `contact.out_path_len = frame[i++];` — and comes back as is. `BaseChatMesh::onContactPathRecv` stores `copyPath(...)`, which returns the packed `path_len`.

meshcore.js 1.13.0 (`src/connection/connection.js`): `onContactResponse` / `onNewAdvertPush` read `outPathLen: bufferReader.readInt8()`; `sendCommandAddUpdateContact` writes it with `writeByte`. So a 3-byte route (bit 7 set) reads negative there.

## What MeshMonitor stores

A contact holds `pathLen` (hop **count**, `null` = no route) and `outPath` (comma-separated hop tokens: `a3,7f` / `a3f2,7f01` / `a3f201,7f0102`). The hash width is not stored on its own; it is the token width. `get_contacts`, path discovery and Define Path all write this form.

## The fix

- `encodeOutPathLen(hopCount, hopHashBytes)` in `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts`, beside `decodeOutPathLen()`. Returns the unsigned wire byte. `null` → `0xFF`. Anything firmware's `isValidPathLen` would refuse (width outside 1..3, more than 63 hops, more than 64 path bytes) also → `0xFF`.
- `storedOutPathToWire(outPath, pathLen)` in `meshcoreCompanionCodec.ts` turns the stored form into `{ outPathLen, outPath }`. The tokens decide both fields, so the length byte always frames exactly the bytes behind it:
  - `pathLen` null → `0xFF`, no bytes (firmware

title: fix(meshcore): ingest page header shows region and broker again
body:
## The fault

The MeshCore MQTT ingest page (`MeshCoreIngestView`) shows "—" for **Region** and **Broker**.

The view read both from `overview.status.region` / `overview.status.brokerUrl`. `status` is `MeshCoreMqttManager.getStatus()`, which has never returned either field. The old route test hid this: its fake manager returned them from `getStatus()`, which the real one does not.

There is no issue for this; the maintainer asked for a direct fix.

## The fix

`getStatus()` stays as it is. It feeds `GET /api/sources/:id/status`, which answers callers with no login, and #5602 keeps the broker host and credentials out of it on purpose.

The ingest overview route (`GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/ingest/overview`) now supplies two top-level fields:

| Field | Value | Who gets it |
|---|---|---|
| `region` | the source's region, uppercased as the topic uses it | anyone who passes the route's gate |
| `brokerUrl` | the broker URL with `user:password@` redacted, else `null` | see below |

- `MeshCoreMqttManager.getFeedEndpoint()` returns `{ region, brokerUrl }`. The URL is already run through `redactBrokerUrl()` (`src/server/utils/brokerUrl.ts`, from #5602), so no caller can forget to strip it.
- The view reads `overview.region` / `overview.brokerUrl`. When the overview has loaded and `brokerUrl` is `null` it shows **Hidden** (new key `meshcore.ingest.broker_hidden`) rather than the same dash it shows while loading.

## Decision: who may see the broker host

The overview route is gated on `nodes:read` for the source, behind `optionalAuth()`. The anonymous account often holds `nodes:read` so a public dashboard can list nodes, so the route **is** readable with no login on such installs.

The broker host is source config, not mesh data. So:

- **Region**: shown to every viewer who passes the `nodes:read` gate, anonymous included. It is the topic segment every observer publishes under.
- **Broker host**: shown only to an **admin**, or a **signed-in user with `sources:read`** — the same grant that `GET /api/sources/:id` asks for before it returns a source's config.
- **Anonymous never gets the host**, even if someone grants `sources:read` to the anonymous account. This keeps #5602's rule: no broker host for callers with no login.
- **Nobody gets `user:password@`**, admin included.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. An ingest source has no radio; this is one read route and one page.
2. **Spam:** none. No sends, no events, no notifications.
3. **Safety timers:** none touched.

## Tests

- `meshcoreIngestReadRoutes.permissions.test.ts` (new, `createRouteTestApp` harness, real auth middleware, real `MeshCoreMqttManager` built with `wss://feeduser:hunter2@with-at@broker.example:443/mqtt` and never started):
  - admin: region `MCO` + `wss://***@broker.example:443/mqtt`
  - `status` carries neither field
  - limited user with `nodes:read` only: region, `brokerUrl: null`, host absent from the whole body
  - limited user with `nodes:read` + `sources:read

title: feat(lint): guardrail against hardcoded colours in inline styles and CSS (#5594)
body:
Closes #5594

## Why

A hex / `rgb()` / `hsl()` literal in an inline style or a stylesheet keeps one theme's colour under every theme. That is the root cause of #5592, #5558, #5247, #5135 and #4910, each found in production. Nothing in the toolchain pushed back. Now `lint:ci` does.

## Design

**1. ESLint rule `meshmonitor-ui/no-hardcoded-color`** (`scripts/eslint-rules/no-hardcoded-color.mjs`), on `src/**/*.tsx`, tests excluded. It reports a string or template literal that holds a hex (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits), `rgb()/rgba()` or `hsl()/hsla()` colour when the literal sits:

- under a JSX `style` attribute, or one named `*Style` (`contentStyle`, `labelStyle`), at any depth: nested objects, spreads, ternaries, concatenation, template interpolations; or
- in an object typed `CSSProperties`; or
- anywhere else, as the value of a key only CSS has (`backgroundColor`, `borderLeft`, `boxShadow`, `outline`, ...).

Not flagged, by design: SVG attributes (`fill="#fff"`); a bare `color` key outside a style context (Leaflet path options and `{ key, label, color }` chart series both use it); kebab-case keys (`'background-color'` is a MapLibre paint property); a colour assembled from data (`` `#${hex}` ``, `` `rgb(${c.r}, ${c.g}, ${c.b})` ``); a colour function that reads a token (`rgb(from var(--color-accent) r g b / 50%)`); plain `.ts` files.

A `var(--x, #888)` fallback **is** flagged: the literal is still there.

**2. `scripts/check-css-colors.mjs`**, no new dependency, for every `.css` under `src/` (CSS modules and the legacy global sheets). It counts colour literals in declaration values and skips custom-property definitions (`--x: ...`, so the theme blocks in `App.css` are not violations), selectors (`#add { }`), at-rule preludes, comments, quoted strings and `url(...)`. Own baseline: `css-color-baseline.json`, one count per file. Chained into `lint:ci` before the ESLint ratchet. It reuses the rule's `findColorLiterals()`, so both halves agree on what a colour is.

**3. Ratcheted.** Today's counts are frozen; only a new or higher count fails. No existing violation is fixed here.

| | Literals | Files |
|---|---|---|
| TSX (`no-hardcoded-color`) | 283 | 77 |
| CSS modules | 68 | 22 |
| Global CSS | 187 | 43 |

**4. Exceptions.**
- TSX: `// eslint-disable-next-line meshmonitor-ui/no-hardcoded-color -- #<issue> reason`
- CSS: `/* color-ok: #<issue> reason */` on the line or the line above. A marker with no issue number or no reason is not honoured (tested).
- Files ignore list: tests only. I looked for TSX files that are colour data by nature and found none that need a blanket pass once the rule skips drawing options and palette records, so the list stays empty rather than hiding real inline styles in map and chart components.

## Why not the issue's own proposal

- A second `no-restricted-syntax` block **replaces** the earlier one for the files it matches (flat config), so it would have switched off the raw-`fetch()` ban in components and pages. It would also

title: feat(notifications): user-configurable message notification format + lighter default (#5593)
body:
Closes #5593

## What

A new-message push notification named the source twice (a `[Source]` title prefix and again on the first body line), so a phone's lock screen showed mostly metadata. This PR:

1. Adds **per-user, per-source title/body templates** for message notifications.
2. Ships a **lighter default** that names the source once.
3. Makes **every other notification type** name the source once too.

## Design

- **One formatter**, `src/utils/notificationTemplate.ts`, shared by the server (render), the route (validation) and the UI (live preview). Syntax is the Automation Engine's `{{ token }}`; rendering goes through its `interpolate` / `extractPaths`. There is no second engine.
- **Tokens:** `sourceName`, `channelName`, `senderName`, `senderShortName`, `text`, `serviceLabel`, `isDM`.
- **Storage:** nullable `message_title_template` / `message_body_template` on `user_notification_preferences` (PG/MySQL: `messageTitleTemplate` / `messageBodyTemplate`), migration **196**. NULL = default.
- **Render point:** `messagePushNotifier` (and the Reticulum DM path) now passes the raw values as `payload.message`. Each delivery wrapper (web push, Apprise, desktop) renders the recipient's own template **after** its filter decision, through one helper, `renderMessagePayloadForUserAsync`. The wrappers no longer add a `[sourceName]` title prefix to message notifications.

### New default

| | Title | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Channel | `{{ channelName }} · {{ sourceName }}` | `{{ senderName }}: {{ text }}` |
| DM | `{{ senderName }} · {{ sourceName }}` | `{{ text }}` |

Before: `[M-BAR-EIKSMARKA-WAMB (NF1)] New Meshtastic Message` / `NarrowFast • M-BAR-EIKSMARKA-WAMB (NF1)` / `OSL-CLIENT-ERKO-TECHO: …`
After: `NarrowFast · M-BAR-EIKSMARKA-WAMB (NF1)` / `OSL-CLIENT-ERKO-TECHO: …`

### Other notification types (source once)

| Type | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Traceroute, low battery, inactive node, waypoint | `[Source]` on title **and** body | body only (`[Source] …`); the title leads with the node/waypoint |
| Server start, node reconnected / disconnected | `[Source]` on title **and** body | title suffix (`Node Disconnected · Source`) |
| Security digest | `[Source]` on title **and** first body line | title only |
| New node | body only ("detected by Source") | unchanged |
| Reticulum DM | `[Source] Direct Message from <hash>` | uses the message templates |

## Decisions

- **Unknown tokens are rejected at save**, with the `fail()` envelope (`400 TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`, plus `field` and `unknownTokens`). At render, an unknown token in a row written some other way renders empty and never throws. Both are tested.
- **One template pair for channel and DM.** `{{ channelName }}` is empty for a DM. To keep that from reading badly, a separator left dangling beside an *empty token* is dropped (`{{ channelName }} · {{ sourceName }}` reads `Home` for a DM, not `· Home`). Separators inside real values are untouched (a message that starts with `- ` keeps it). Only

Closes #5592

## What was wrong

`src/components/NotificationsTab.tsx` had no stylesheet. title: feat(automations): role, hops and last-heard tokens on MeshCore node triggers (#5595)
body:
Closes #5595

## What

MeshCore nodes have no node number, so `{{ node.* }}` is empty on `trigger.nodeDiscovered` and `trigger.nodeUpdated`. A MeshCore "new node" alert could say the name and public key and nothing else. This adds the contact facts under `trigger.*`:

| Token | Value |
|-------|-------|
| `{{ trigger.roleName }}` | `Companion` / `Repeater` / `Room Server` / `Sensor`; empty when the type is unknown |
| `{{ trigger.hops }}` | Hop count of the advert frame that fired the trigger (0 = heard direct). Empty when no advert frame fired it |
| `{{ trigger.routeHops }}` | Hop count of the stored route to the node. Empty when no route is stored |
| `{{ trigger.lastHeard }}` | When this source last heard the node, epoch ms, same unit as `trigger.nodeStale` |

## Design

- **Payload.** `NodeDiscoveredData` and `MeshCoreNodeChangedData` extend a new `MeshCoreNodeEventFacts` (`advType`, `hops`, `routeHops`, `lastHeard`). All three emit sites in `meshcoreManager.ts` fill it through one helper, `meshCoreNodeTriggerPayload`. The repeater RAW ingest (#5574) and MQTT ingest do not emit these triggers, so they are untouched.
- **`hops` comes from the raw frame only.** `recordRecentAdvertHash` already decodes the LogRxData advert frame for the packet hash; it now also keeps the hop count, read from the packed `path_len` byte through the existing `decodeOutPathLen` (top 2 bits = hash width, bottom 6 = hop count). The 0xFF sentinel and the reserved 4-byte width read as unknown. Hash and hop count travel together as one `MeshCoreAdvertOrigin`, so a nameless first advert that fires later reports its own hash and its own hops.
- **`hops` is never filled from the cached route.** Path updates, Discover replies and contact re-reads have no advert frame, so `hops` is empty there, the same rule `packetHash` follows. The cached route length goes out under its own name, `routeHops`, and the token help and docs spell out the difference.
- **`lastHeard`** is `contact.lastSeen`, which the manager keeps in epoch ms on our own clock. `lastAdvert` is the sender's clock in seconds and is not used. The context builder also scales a value below 1e11 from seconds to ms, so a wrong unit cannot render a 1970 date.
- **Context.** `buildMeshCoreNodeContext` takes the facts and maps `advType` to `roleName`. `subjectNodeNum` stays null.
- **No `shortName`.** MeshCore has none. The token help and docs say so; `{{ trigger.shortName }}` and `{{ node.shortName }}` render empty and do not throw (tested). The builder flags `trigger.shortName` as unrecognized.
- **Builder.** `SubstitutionsHelp` lists the new tokens (`tokenHints` reads from it). `roleName` / `name` are offered in Text comparison and `hops` / `routeHops` in Number comparison on both node triggers.
- **Test panel.** A new "MeshCore public key" input on the node triggers; when set, the dry run is a MeshCore event built by the same context builder as the live engine, with Name, Role, Advert hops, Stored route hops and Last

title: fix: stop ingest login retries, back up Observer keys, purge key rows on source delete (refs #5596)
body:
Refs #5596

Three existing faults that the look into #5596 turned up. This PR does **not** add token (JWT) auth; that feature is on hold and the issue stays open.

## 1. MeshCore MQTT ingest retried a rejected login for ever

**Fault.** `MeshCoreMqttManager` never listened for `permission-denied`. `MqttBrokerClient` backs off 1 s → 60 s and then keeps going, so a wrong username or password cost the broker one CONNECT about every 60 s for the life of the process.

**Fix.** Rule set by the maintainer: after **5** rejected logins in a row the source stops reconnecting until its config changes or someone reconnects it by hand; a successful connect resets the count.

- `MqttBrokerClient` gains an opt-in `maxAuthFailures`. It counts CONNACK 4/5, resets on `connect`, and at the limit refuses every later retry (own timer and shared-coordinator tick) and emits `auth-stopped` once. Clients that do not pass the option behave as before.
- `MeshCoreMqttManager` opts in at 5, closes the dead socket, and stays registered so its read routes keep serving stored data.
- **Status.** `getStatus()` (served by `GET /api/sources/:id/status`, which the dashboard polls) now carries `authStopped`, `permissionMessage` and `lastError`. The text is fixed: no username, password, broker host or broker error text, because that route answers callers with no login. The sidebar shows "Login rejected", the existing warning badge with the reason, and a Connect button.
- **Clearing the stop.** Two gaps had to close for this to work at all:
  - `PUT /api/sources/:id` had no `meshcore_mqtt` branch. A save changed the stored config and left the running manager on the old one until a process restart, so a corrected password did nothing. A save (or enable) now restarts the source on the new config.
  - `POST /api/sources/:id/connect` refused every `meshcore_mqtt` source with a 400, so an ingest source with auto-connect off could never be started. It now reconnects a stopped or idle source and leaves a connected one alone.
- **Logs.** No log line prints the username or password. A broker URL typed as `scheme://user:pass@host` is now redacted in every `MqttBrokerClient` log line and in the ingest "subscribed" line (this was an existing leak for all MQTT clients).

### Other MQTT client paths

| Path | Rejected login today | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| MeshCore MQTT ingest (`meshcoreMqttManager.ts`) | retried for ever | **fixed** |
| Analyzer Observer publisher (`meshcoreObserverPublisher.ts`) | already hard-stops at `MAX_AUTH_FAILURES = 5` | unchanged |
| `mqtt_bridge` subscriber client (`mqttBridgeManager.ts`) | retries for ever at the 60 s cap; shows "Broker rejected authentication" but never stops | **follow-up** |
| `mqtt_bridge` per-gateway publisher pool (`mqttBridgePublisherPool.ts`) | each gateway client retries for ever | **follow-up** |
| `mqtt_broker` (embedded broker), Meshtastic `mqttLink` proxy | no outbound login | n/a |

The bridge uses the same shared client, so the mechanism
