title: docs(coverage): why a survey looks sparse, plus a hint link in setup guidance (#5591)
body:
Closes #5591

## What

**Docs** (`docs/features/coverage-report.md`)
- New section **Why a survey looks sparse**, after "How to survey" and before "Reading the report":
  - What the survey node holds back
  - What relays and receivers drop (firmware 2.8)
  - What MQTT gateways miss
  - What MeshMonitor cannot see
  - Settings for a survey (table) and a warning against settings that harm the mesh
  - Troubleshooting by symptom
- Fixed the "Position interval 30 seconds or more" advice: 30 s needs a private channel.

**UI** (`CoverageReport.tsx`)
- One hint line in the **Setup guidance** panel: "Fewer dots than you expected? Firmware holds back and drops position packets." plus a link to the new docs section.
- The same 30-second fix in the panel's recommendation text.
- No button or control. The Coverage Report still sends nothing and changes no node.

## Where this differs from the issue

The issue text is partly wrong. The docs follow the firmware source (develop a406eb3 = 2.8.2, master 2.7.27), re-checked for this PR:

| Issue says | Firmware says |
| --- | --- |
| Receiver dedup default is 21600 s (6 h) | `default_traffic_mgmt_position_min_interval_secs (5 * 60 * 60)`: **5 h** (`src/mesh/Default.h`). 6 h is the sender's parked floor. |
| A receiver keeps only the first fix per window | It drops a fix only in the **same grid cell**, on a **well-known channel**, from another node, inside the window (`TrafficManagementModule.cpp`, `Channels::isWellKnownChannel`). A moving node passes. |
| Polite 5% duty-cycle gate throttles position | `PositionModule` calls only `isTxAllowedChannelUtil` (25%, or 40% for TRACKER / TAK_TRACKER). Only the hard region limit applies. |
| Set dedup to 0 on every source | Leave it alone; a private channel avoids dedup. 0 only for a parked test. |
| (not mentioned) | Default-channel floors at boot: position interval at least 1 h, smart minimum at least 5 min (`NodeDB.cpp`). This is why 30 s needs a private channel. |

## Decisions (maintainer)

- Docs section plus one hint line; the issue's pre-flight check and one-click "set to 0" are **not** built.
- The hint links out the same way other in-app doc links do (`https://meshmonitor.org/features/...#anchor`, new tab, `noopener noreferrer`), styled with a CSS-module class and theme tokens.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. No packet is sent; this is docs and one link.
2. **Spam:** none. No message, event, notification or retry is added. The docs warn against Override duty cycle and short intervals on a public channel.
3. **Safety timers:** none added or touched.

## Tests

- `CoverageReport.test.tsx`: new test that the hint renders inside Setup guidance with the right href, `target`, `rel`, and holds no button. File: 41 passed.
- `npm run docs:build`: passes; the built page holds the `why-a-survey-looks-sparse` anchor.
- `tsc` for `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.server.json`: clean. `lint:ci`: no in-repo FAIL lines.
- Full Vitest run (PG and MySQL containers up)

-- **Position interval 30 seconds or more** — more frequent broadcasts add
-  airtime without adding much new coverage data.
+- **Smart position minimum interval of 30 seconds or more, on a private

 (`hop_limit 0`) packet on firmware **2.7.20 or later** — older firmware
@@ -73,6 +77,137 @@ has no advert timer, so the driver sends them by hand.
 | Zero-hop, EU (SF8/BW62.5/CR8) | ~1.1–1.3 s | ~1.9% |
 | Flood, 20 repeaters in reach | ~9 s (US) / ~25 s (EU) | 15–40% |
 
+## Why a survey looks sparse
+
+A thin map does not always mean poor radio reach. Meshtastic firmware holds
+back, drops and filters position packets to save airtime. Those rules suit
+daily use, and a survey runs into most of them. On the map, a packet the
+firmware held back looks the same as a packet the radio never heard.
+
+This section covers Meshtastic. The facts come from the firmware source
+(2.7.27 and 2.8.2); the files are named so you can check them.
+
+### What the survey node holds back
+
+The survey node skips or delays its own position broadcasts in these cases.
+
+- **Busy channel.** The node skips a position when channel use over the last
+  minute is above **25%**. For the **TRACKER** and **TAK_TRACKER** roles the
+  limit is **40%**. The node logs `Ch. util >25%. Skip send` (or `>40%`) each
+  time. (`src/modules/PositionModule.cpp`, `src/airtime.cpp`)
+- **Default channel.** If position goes out on a channel with the default key
+  and a preset name such as `LongFast`, the firmware raises the position
+  interval to at least **1 hour** and the smart position minimum interval to
+  at least **5 minutes**. It does this at every boot, whatever you saved. A
+  30-second interval works only on a private channel. (`src/mesh/NodeDB.cpp`,
+  `src/mesh/Default.h`)
+- **Large mesh.** With more than 40 nodes online, the firmware stretches the
+  interval. TRACKER, TAK_TRACKER, SENSOR and the router roles are exempt.
+  (`src/mesh/Default.h`)
+- **Legal duty cycle.** In a region with a duty-cycle limit, such as EU_868,
+  the node stops sending once it reaches the full limit. The lower "polite"
+  limit does not apply to position packets. (`src/mesh/Router.cpp`)
+
+Firmware **2.8** adds three more:
+
+- **Parked node.** A node that has not moved out of its grid cell, or that
+  uses a fixed position, sends a position at most once every **6 hours**.
+  The LOST_AND_FOUND role is exempt.
+- **Coarse position on public channels.** On a channel anyone can decrypt,
+  the node sends its position at no more than **15 bits** of precision: a
+  grid of roughly 700 m or coarser. A channel with precision 0 sends no
+  position at all. (`src/mesh/PositionPrecision.h`)
+- **Shorter reach.** The firmware may lower `hop_limit` on position
+  broadcasts. It never raises it.
+
+### What relays and receivers drop (firmware 2.8)
+
+Firmware 2.8.0 added the **Traffic Management** module. Firmware 2.7 does not
+have it. It is on by default on every board except STM32WL, and it drops
+repeated positions.
+
+A node drops a position packet only when **all** of these hold:
+
+- another node sent it,
+- it arrived on a well-known channel (default key or no key, and a preset
+  name),
+- it falls in the **same grid cell** as the last position this node passed
+  from that sender, and
+- it arrived inside the dedup window.
+
+The default window is **18,000 seconds (5 hours)**. The protobuf comment says
+6 hours; the firmware uses 5. For a TRACKER or TAK_TRACKER sender the window
+is at most 1 hour, and for LOST_AND_FOUND at most 15 minutes. A value of 0
+turns dedup off. (`src/modules/TrafficManagementModule.cpp`,
+`src/mesh/Default.h`)
+
+The grid cell is as large as the channel's position precision. So:
+
+- **A moving survey node passes.** Each new cell is a new position.
+- **A parked survey node does not.** You get one dot per spot, however long
+  you wait there.
+
+A dropped packet goes no further on that node. The node does not rebroadcast
+it, so receivers further out lose that copy. The node also does not hand it
+to connected apps, so **MeshMonitor never sees it on that source**.
+
+The module's other features (rate limit, unknown-packet drop, NodeInfo direct
+response) are off by default.
+
+### What MQTT gateways miss
+
+- **"OK to MQTT" off.** A gateway on a public broker does not uplink packets
+  from a node that has "OK to MQTT" turned off. A broker on a private IP
+  address skips this check. (`src/mqtt/MQTT.cpp`)
+- **Old gateway firmware.** A gateway drops a zero-hop packet unless it runs
+  firmware 2.7.20 or later.
+- **Dedup does not stop the uplink.** A 2.8 gateway still uplinks a position
+  that its own Traffic Management module dropped. So an MQTT source can show
+  a fix that the same node, as a radio source, does not.
+
+### What MeshMonitor cannot see
+
+MeshMonitor records only the position packets a node hands over. It also
+skips your own node's position, packets that did not arrive over RF, replays
+of old packets, packets with id 0, and packets with a stale receive time.
+
+It has no record of a packet that was never sent or that a node dropped. It
+cannot tell those from a packet lost to poor reach. The
+[Likely gaps](#likely-gaps) lines mark where fixes went missing, not why.
+
+### Settings for a survey
+
+Change these on your own nodes, in the Meshtastic app or on MeshMonitor's
+Configuration tab. The Coverage Report changes nothing for you.
+
+| Setting | For a survey | Why |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Survey channel | A private channel (your own key) that carries position, on the survey node and on each receiver | Avoids the 1-hour and 5-minute floors, the 15-bit limit and receiver dedup |
+| Role | TRACKER on the survey node for the drive | Raises the busy-channel limit to 40% and skips the large-mesh stretch |
+| Smart position minimum interval | 30 s, on a private channel only | The firmware raises it to 5 minutes on a default channel |
+| Position dedup window (Traffic Management, receivers on 2.8) | Leave alone. Set 0 only for a parked test, then put it back | A moving node already passes; 0 lets every repeat through and costs the mesh airtime |
+| Override duty cycle | Do not change | It breaks the legal airtime limit for your region |
+| Traffic Management rate limit | Do not change | Off by default; it does not affect a survey |
+
+::: warning Do not trade the mesh for a denser map
+Turning on **Override duty cycle** can break radio law in your region. A very
+short position interval on a public channel takes airtime from everyone on
+it, and the firmware raises it to 5 minutes anyway. Use a private channel,
+keep `hop_limit 0`, and put the node back to its usual role and settings
+after the drive.
+:::
+
+### Troubleshooting by symptom
+
+| What you see | Likely cause | What to do |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| One dot per parked spot | The node did not leave its grid cell. Smart position sends nothing while it sits still; on 2.8 the 6-hour parked floor and receiver dedup apply too | Expected. Move the node, or use a private channel for a parked test |
+| Dots every 5 minutes or more | The survey node sends position on a default channel, so the firmware raised the interval | Move the survey to a private channel, then reboot the node |
+| Dots snapped to a coarse grid | The channel's position precision is low, or a 2.8 node limited it to 15 bits on a public channel | Use a private channel with full precision |
+| No dots on one 2.8 source, others fine | That node's Traffic Management module dropped the repeats | Use a private channel; for a parked test, set that node's dedup window to 0 and put it back after |
+| MQTT gateways missing | "OK to MQTT" is off on the survey node, the gateway firmware is older than 2.7.20, or MQTT recording is off for that source | Turn on "OK to MQTT" on the survey node; check **Settings → Coverage recording** |
+| Dots stop in a busy area | The node skipped sends above 25% channel use | Check the node log for `Skip send`; use the TRACKER role for the drive |
+

 Open **Analysis & Reports** from the dashboard sidebar, then click the

title: feat(translation): providers own their config fields; one API key per provider (#5518)
body:
Closes #5518

## What this does

Each translation provider now declares its config fields in one place, and each provider has its own API key.

### Design ("B": pure-data descriptors)

`src/types/translationProviders.ts` holds one descriptor per provider. Each field has `settingKey`, `configKey`, `kind` (`url` | `secret` | `text`), `required`, `inputId`, `labelKey`, and optional `hintKey` / `placeholderKey` / `placeholder`. The file is data and pure functions only (it sits in both tsconfigs).

Derived from the descriptors:

| Was a hand list | Now |
|---|---|
| `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`, `SECRET_SETTINGS_KEYS` entries | spread from `TRANSLATION_PROVIDER_SETTING_KEYS` / `..._SECRET_SETTING_KEYS` (literal types survive) |
| URL key list in `settingsRoutes.ts` | `TRANSLATION_PROVIDER_URL_SETTING_KEYS` |
| `ProviderConfig` builds in `translate()` and `testConfig()` | `getStoredProviderConfig(provider)`, which reads that provider's own keys only |
| Per-provider JSX in `TranslationConfigSection` | one loop over the active provider's fields; props are `values` + `onFieldChange(key, value)` |
| Six `initial*` states, load block, baseline, post-save in `SettingsTab` | one `initialTranslationFields` state, looped over the key list |
| Required fields checked only when the provider threw | `missingRequiredTranslationFields` runs before any request (both `translate()` and `testConfig()`) |

Still hand-written, by design: the `SettingsDraft` type and the `handleSave` literal (the persistence test reads that source). A guard test covers both, and `updateField(key, value)` in the section mount fails to compile if a descriptor key is missing from the draft type.

### API key split

| Provider | New secret setting |
|---|---|
| libretranslate | `translationLibreTranslateApiKey` |
| openai | `translationOpenAiApiKey` |
| deepl | `translationDeeplApiKey` |
| google | `translationGoogleApiKey` |

`translationApiKey` is gone from the allowlists and from every reader. Before, switching provider reused the stored key, so a DeepL key went out as a Bearer token to whatever OpenAI-compatible URL was set.

**Migration 195** (`split_translation_api_key`, all three backends, `settingsKey`, idempotent): moves the stored `translationApiKey` to the ACTIVE provider's new key (active = stored `translationProvider`; unset or unknown reads as `libretranslate`). Other providers start blank. It never overwrites a new key that already has a non-blank value. It then deletes the old row, plus any `source:{id}:translationApiKey` copy. With no old row it does nothing. The provider → key map is frozen in the migration.

Backup/restore: backups carry the whole `settings` table and no key names. A restored older backup brings back the old row without the migration's ledger key, so migration 195 runs again on the next start.

### `/api/translate/test`

- Reads only the tested provider's own fields from the body. A field the request omits falls back to that provider's

title: fix(build): eager CSS plugin matches its module id on Windows (#5558)
body:
Closes #5558

## Root cause

The `eagerCss()` plugin in `vite.config.ts` keeps every page's CSS in the entry stylesheet after the route pages became lazy chunks. It built its two constants with `path.resolve`:

```ts
const ENTRY = resolve(__dirname, 'src/main.tsx')
const EAGER_STYLES = resolve(__dirname, 'src/eagerStyles.ts')
...
if (stripQuery(id) !== EAGER_STYLES) return null
```

On Windows `path.resolve` returns `D:\a\...\src\eagerStyles.ts`. Vite's module id is always `D:/a/.../src/eagerStyles.ts`. The two never match, so the plugin returned `null` for its own module, `src/eagerStyles.ts` stayed empty, and each page's CSS stayed in its lazy chunk.

The theme blocks (`:root[data-theme='mocha']` and the rest) live in `src/App.css`. The landing route does not load `App`, so `data-theme` matched no rule and the page was white until a source route pulled the App CSS in.

**CI evidence** (v4.17.0-rc3 `desktop-release`, run 37150473552):

| Job | CSS files | `main-*.css` |
|---|---|---|
| build-macos | 2 | 572 kB |
| build-windows | 76 | 0.67 kB |

PR #5569 fixed a separate, real bug in the theme path. It did not touch this one, which is why the issue was reopened. The theme state logic in `SettingsContext` is correct and unchanged here.

## Changes

- **`vite.config.ts`**: a `toModuleId()` helper turns any path into Vite's forward-slash form. The plugin now passes its constants, the entry it reads, the importer it hands to `this.resolve`, and every walked file through it. `eagerCss`, `toModuleId` and `isEagerStylesId` are exported for tests; the plugin takes optional `entry` / `eagerStyles` / `read` so a test can drive it with `path.win32` paths.
- **No silent failure**: `load` throws when the walk finds no stylesheet; `buildEnd` throws when a build ends without ever loading the placeholder. (Dev server is exempt: it loads modules on demand.)
- **`scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs`**: new check 3. A stylesheet linked from `dist/index.html` must hold the `mocha` and `latte` theme rules (the default dark and light themes). It also prints the CSS file count and the size of each linked sheet.
- **Second Windows bug, same class**: the script's CLI guard was ``import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` ``. On Windows that never matches (`file:///D:/a/...` vs `file://D:\a\...`), so the script would have exited 0 there without checking anything. Now uses `pathToFileURL`.
- **Workflows**: `npm run check:bundle-size` runs right after the frontend build in all three build jobs (Windows, macOS, macOS Intel) of `desktop-ci.yml` and `desktop-release.yml`. I looked at the size budgets first: the desktop jobs run the same `npm run build` as the web build, so the budgets apply as they are. No signing or notarisation step changed. `desktop-ci.yml` now also triggers on `vite.config.ts` and `scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs`; before, a change to the Vite config never ran a Windows build on the PR.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: one note in the bundle-size section.

### Decision: o

title: fix(meshcore): Virtual Node relays SendBinaryReq STATUS/TELEMETRY (#5597)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #5597. The MeshCore Virtual Node only handled GetNeighbours (0x06) inside `SendBinaryReq`; STATUS (0x01) and TELEMETRY (0x03) fell through to `Err(UnsupportedCmd)`, so Home Assistant repeater entities stayed unavailable.

- Add `BinaryRequestTypes.GetStatus` (0x01) and dispatch 0x01/0x03 to a new handler.
- The handler replies `Sent` with a freshly minted tag, fetches via `requestNodeStatus` / `requestRemoteTelemetryRaw`, then pushes a `BinaryResponse` with the same tag. Failures emit nothing, like the sibling handlers.
- `encodeRepeaterStatusData` gains an opt-in 52-byte form (adds `total_rx_air_time_secs`) used only for the binary response. The existing 48-byte StatusResponse push is unchanged.

## Mesh impact
No new radio traffic beyond what the client already requests. The VN only relays one status or telemetry request per client request, with no timers or retries.

## Testing
- New VN tests for 0x01 and 0x03 (tag correlation, 52-byte payload); the "unknown sub-type" test now uses 0x7f.
- `vitest` VN and codec suites pass (216 tests), `tsc` is clean, and `lint:ci` has no in-repo failures.
- Not run: PostgreSQL/MySQL suites (no DB changes) and the full suite.

Thanks to @Netwisdom69 for the detailed analysis.

title: feat(unified): merge one MeshCore message heard by several sources into one row (#5587)
body:
Closes #5587

## What

Unified Messages showed one row per receiving source for a MeshCore message. It now shows one row per message, with every source that heard it under "Heard by" (`receptions[]`, `heard_by_count`). Channel messages and DMs alike. Backend only: the page already renders `receptions[]`.

## What the data allows (and why the issue's key is not used)

The issue proposed `channelIdx : fromPublicKey : text : floor(timestamp/N)`. Three of those four parts differ between sources for the same message:

| Writer | channel key | sender | sender clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| companion, received | `channel-<device slot>` | `fromName`, split by a regex (name ≤ 32 chars, any whitespace after `:`) | `timestamp` = `sender_timestamp*1000` if plausible, else receipt ms |
| repeater (#5551/#5574) | `channel-<1000 + 16 bits of SHA-256(secret)>` + `keyFingerprint` | `fromName`, split by the decoder (first `": "` in 50 chars, no `:[]` in the name) | `timestamp` = sec*1000 if > 0 (never checked), else receipt ms |
| MQTT ingest | `channel-<slot on the source whose key opened it>`; `keyFingerprint` only for virtual-channel keys | as repeater | as repeater |
| our own send | `toPublicKey = channel-<slot>`, `fromPublicKey` = local key | stored local node name, no text prefix | `senderTimestamp` column, channel sends only (#5512) |

- **Packet hash:** no writer stores it. `packetHash` lives on the in-memory message and the event bus only; `meshcore_messages` has no such column. Not usable without a migration, and not needed.
- **Sender timestamp:** the `senderTimestamp` column is set only on our own channel sends. But every *received* row already holds the wire value in `timestamp`, as whole seconds. A `timestamp` with a millisecond part is the receipt clock, written when the sender's clock was rejected. So the wire second is recoverable from stored fields for nearly every row: no migration.

## Design

New pure module `src/server/utils/meshcoreMessageMerge.ts`; `unifiedRoutes.ts` collects permitted rows per source, then clusters once.

**Logical identity**
- Channel: (channel secret fingerprint, sender name, body).
- DM / room post: (sender key first 6 bytes, recipient key first 6 bytes, body). A received DM stores a 6-byte sender prefix, a sent one the full key.

**Channel identity = the secret's fingerprint** (`channelKeyFingerprint`, hex SHA-256(secret)[0..8], the value #5551 already stores). Resolved as: the row's `keyFingerprint`; else the fingerprint of the row's own `(source, slot)` channel key; else, for an MQTT ingest source (which owns no channel rows), the slot's fingerprint when every source using that slot holds the same secret. Unknown secret → the row is never merged across sources.

**Sender and text.** A received row is rebuilt into its wire text (`Name: body`) and split again with one parser, so `Name:body`, bracketed names and 33-49 char names come out the same from both writers. Our own send is not split (its text has no prefix).

Closes #5588

## What changed

MeshCore Trace Path waited a flat 45 s for a reply. It now waits as long as the radio says the trace can take, so a short or dead path fails in about 10 s.

**Policy** (MeshCore One's `flood` profile, `MC1/Utilities/FirmwareSuggestedTimeout.swift`), as named constants in one helper, `src/server/constants/meshcoreFirmwareTimeout.ts`:

```
hint 0 or absent → 30 s
otherwise        → clamp(hint × 1.2 + 8 s, min 5 s, max 60 s)
explicit timeout_ms from a caller → wins
```

`meshcorePathDiscoveryTimeoutMs` (Discover Path, #5508) had the same formula inline. It now calls the shared helper and keeps only its own 20 s floor.

## What the Sent ack carries (checked, not assumed)

- Firmware (`examples/companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp`, `CMD_SEND_TRACE_PATH`): `RESP_CODE_SENT = [code][0][tag u32 LE][est_timeout u32 LE]`, with
  `est_timeout = calcDirectTimeoutMillisFor(airtime, hops) = 500 + (airtime × 6 + 250) × (hops + 1)`.
- Pinned meshcore.js (`onSentResponse`): bytes 2-5 → `expectedAckCrc` (for a trace this is our tag), bytes 6-9 → `estTimeout`.
- Units: milliseconds.
- Scope: it covers every hop in the path we send. With Auto return path on, that list already holds both legs, so the estimate is the round trip. With it off, the estimate covers the one-way list we sent, and the 8 s grace covers the rest.

The backend matches the Sent ack on the tag, so another command's Sent on the shared channel cannot set a trace's wait.

## Design

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts` `trace_path` | Starts with the 30 s no-hint wait, then re-arms from the Sent estimate. The deadline counts from the send, so the total never passes 60 s. A timeout rejects with `MeshCoreTraceTimeoutError`, and `sendCommand` passes `{ timed_out, wait_ms, suggested_timeout_ms }` up. |
| `meshcoreManager.ts` | New `traceContactPathDetailed()` returns `ok` / `timeout` (with `waitMs`) / `failed`. `traceContactPath()` is a thin wrapper that still returns `null` on failure, so automation callers are untouched. |
| Route `POST …/trace-path` | Timeout → `504 MESHCORE_TRACE_TIMEOUT` with `{ reason, waitMs, suggestedTimeoutMs }`. Other failures → `409 MESHCORE_TRACE_FAILED`. Errors now go through `fail()`. Success body is unchanged. |
| UI | The Trace Path button stops its spinner and shows "No reply within N s." next to it. |

**Timeout ladder** (each layer outlasts the one inside it; a unit test pins the order):

| | |
|---|---|
| Longest trace wait | 60 s |
| Radio-op backstop | 65 s (was 60 s, equal to the new max) |
| Bridge command timeout | 70 s |
| HTTP socket timeout for the route | 75 s |

### The 60 s wait and the HTTP layer (#5494)

60 s is past the server's 30 s socket timeout. The route already raised its own socket timeout with an inline `req.setTimeout(75 s)`; it now uses `extendRequestTimeout()` like every other long route and is pinned in `requestTimeout.routes.test.ts`. A new route test runs the app on a real HTTP server with a short s

title: feat(map): traceroute-confirmed reciprocal links on the cross-source layer (#5580)
body:
Closes #5580

## What

The cross-source "heard here" layer (#5561 / #5575) shows one-way edges between our own sources. It cannot show that a **remote** node hears us. Only a traceroute proves that, because the reply has to come back. This overlays that proof on the same layer.

## The rule

A completed traceroute a source's own radio ran has two legs:

```
out:  [us, ...route, destination]       snrTowards[i] measured at out[i+1]
back: [destination, ...routeBack, us]   snrBack[i]    measured at back[i+1]
```

The leg next to our radio is the first hop out and the last hop back. When both name the **same neighbour** (for a zero-hop run, the destination itself), that one RF link carried a packet each way. That is a confirmed reciprocal link. The neighbour heard us at `snrTowards[0]`; we heard it at the last `snrBack` entry.

**Which column is "us": either.** The table stores a completed run two ways. A traceroute sent from MeshMonitor writes a pending row `{from: us, to: destination}` and the reply updates it in place, so our radio stays in `fromNodeNum`. A reply with no pending row (sent from a phone app, or the pending row timed out) is inserted as it arrived, `{from: destination, to: us}`. The route and SNR arrays mean the same in both. The service takes whichever endpoint is the source's local node. The first version assumed only the second form and drew nothing for MeshMonitor's own traceroutes; a live check caught it. Our own outgoing reply to someone else's traceroute also has us in `fromNodeNum`, but has no return leg, so it is rejected as incomplete.

Against the issue's two examples:

- RF direct, `SKYB -> PARC` and `PARC -> SKYB`: confirmed, `SKYB <-> PARC`, with both SNRs.
- MQTT, out via `PTBZ` and back via `SKYC`: not confirmed. Neither link carried both directions.

Not counted: a run some other node made (no leg next to our radio), a run with no recorded return path, a placeholder first hop, and hops further out than our own neighbour.

## Design

**No storage, no migration.** `GET /api/analysis/cross-source-links/traceroute-confirmed?sources=&since=` computes on read from `traceroutes` via the existing `getTraceroutesForSources`. The rule lives in `src/server/services/tracerouteConfirmedLinks.ts` as pure functions.

**Per transport class.** One row per `(source, neighbour, class)`, so the same link confirmed over RF and over MQTT is two lines. Class = the row's `transportMechanism`, except that the unknown-SNR sentinel on either of the two hops makes it MQTT, the rule the map already uses (`hopTransportClass`, #5097).

**Permission.** A source contributes only when the caller can read **both** `nodes` and `traceroute` on it. Runs then go through `maskTraceroutesByChannel`, as the traceroute routes do. Both endpoints go through `buildPositionFilter`, on the link's own source only: a hidden, private or unplaced node yields no line. A one-source user sees that source's links and no trace of any other.

**UI.** A sub-toggle, **Tracero

title: feat(meshcore): map toggle to hide nodes whose latest advert had no position (#5578)
body:
Closes #5578

## What

A MeshCore node that stops sharing its position keeps advertising, without coordinates. Ingest keeps the last stored fix (#3504), which is right, but nothing recorded that the node no longer reports one. The map went on drawing it at a place it had stopped broadcasting.

This adds a per-browser toggle, **Hide nodes without a current position advert**, to the MeshCore map (Map controls) and the Dashboard map (Map Features, offered when the map holds MeshCore nodes). Default off.

## Design

**Storage.** Migration 194 adds `meshcore_nodes.lastAdvertHadPosition`, a nullable boolean, to all three backends and all three schemas. `NULL` = unknown = shown. No backfill: stored coordinates cannot say what the last advert carried.

**Writes.** `false` is a real value to `upsertNode`'s merge (only null/undefined means "not observed"), so it persists while the stored coordinates stay. Every caller derives the flag from one helper, `advertHasPosition()`, which treats absent, 0/0, non-finite and out-of-range as no position.

| Path | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Repeater RAW stream, MeshCore MQTT ingest (`ingestAdvertFrame`) | The advert frame itself. Written on every advert. |
| Companion, advert push | The raw advert frame the radio logs (LogRxData) just before the push. |
| Companion, `NewAdvert` 0x8A with no raw frame | The payload, which the firmware builds from that one advert. |
| Companion, contact sync / key-only 0x80 push | See below. |

**A finding that changed the companion path.** The brief assumed the firmware reports 0/0 for a positionless contact. It does for a contact that *never* advertised a position, but not for one that stopped. `BaseChatMesh::onAdvertRecv` only writes `gps_lat/gps_lon` when the advert has them:

```cpp
if (parser.hasLatLon()) {
  from->gps_lat = parser.getIntLat();
  from->gps_lon = parser.getIntLon();
}
```

So a stored contact keeps its old coordinates after a positionless advert, and the 0x80 push carries the public key alone. A contact record with coordinates therefore proves nothing about the latest advert. The rule:

- contact record with **no** coordinates (0/0) -> `false` (it has never had one);
- contact record **with** coordinates -> flag left unwritten (the stored value stands);
- the raw advert frame, when present, always wins.

Without this, contact sync would have stamped `true` on exactly the nodes the issue is about.

**Reads.** `getAllNodes()` carries `lastAdvertHadPosition` and `positionSource`, so `GET /nodes` returns them; contacts carry the flag; the dashboard node shaping (`sourceDashboardData`, `/api/nodes`) passes both through. `stripPositions` removes both for a viewer without `nodes:viewOnMap`: whether a node shares its position is position data.

**Filter.** One predicate, `isHiddenByPositionlessAdvert(node, enabled)` in `src/utils/meshcoreAdvertPosition.ts`, used by both maps:

- hides only on a recorded `false`;
- never hides a `positionSource === 'telemetry'` node (a live GNS

title: feat(meshcore): split or truncate long Auto-Acknowledge replies (#5564)
body:
Closes #5564

## What

A MeshCore Auto-Acknowledge reply went to the radio with no length check. A template that grew past the text cap after token expansion lost its tail on air, while MeshMonitor stored the full text.

This PR adds a per-source toggle, **Split long messages**, in the MeshCore Auto-Acknowledge section. It is **off by default** and one toggle covers DM and channel replies.

| | Reply fits in one message | Reply is over the cap |
|---|---|---|
| **Off** (default) | Sent as before | Cut server-side to the cap, one send |
| **On** | Sent as before, no marker | Up to 3 sends, `(1/3) ` markers, 10 s apart, last part cut to fit |

Caps (UTF-8 bytes): 150 DM, 130 channel, 120 channel with a named region. These are the caps the HTTP send route already used.

### Behaviour change (deliberate)

With the toggle **off**, an over-long reply is now truncated by MeshMonitor before the send, on a character boundary. Before, the full text went to the radio and into the stored row. The stored row now matches what went on air. The docs call this out.

## Design

- `src/server/utils/splitUtf8Message.ts`: a pure helper. Byte budget, break-point preference (line break, sentence end, punctuation, space, hyphen), hard split that never halves a character (grapheme-aware, so flags and ZWJ emoji stay whole), marker budget reserved up front, max-parts cap, last part truncated. A single part gets no marker.
- `src/server/constants/meshcoreMessageLimits.ts`: the three caps move here so the route (`VALIDATION`) and the manager share one source.
- `checkAutoAcknowledge` (`meshcoreManager.ts`): after the pre-send delay it resolves the cap by destination and scope (override, else channel scope, else source default, as `performScopedSend` does), splits, then sends the parts in order. Before **each** part it re-checks `canTransmit()`. It stops at the first failed send. The 10 s wait is awaited in the handler, outside `runSerialized`, so other sends are not held up.
- Cooldown: stamped once per trigger, before the first send, as before.
- Channel retry (#3979): unchanged; each part opts in as the single reply did.
- Routes: `GET`/`POST /automation/autoack` carry `splitLongMessages`. Only a real boolean `true` turns it on. Both handlers now use `ok()`/`fail()` (same wire shape).
- Settings: `meshcoreAutoAckSplitLongMessages` added to `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` and `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS`. No migration.
- UI: toggle plus a warning next to it: "Long replies go out as up to 3 messages, 10 seconds apart, each marked like "(1/3)". Each one is repeated by every repeater in range." New CSS module for the row and warning.
- The Meshtastic splitter is untouched. Edits to `meshcoreManager.ts` stay in the auto-ack region (plus two imports).

Scope note: a channel reply counts as scoped only when MeshMonitor knows a region name for it, which mirrors the HTTP route. If MeshMonitor has no scope set and the node applies its own default region, the 130-byte cap is used.

## Maintainer

title: feat(meshcore): decrypt GRP_TXT / GRP_DATA in the Packet Decode modal (#5567, #5568)
body:
Closes #5567
Closes #5568

## What

The MeshCore **Packet Monitor → Packet Decode** modal now shows the plaintext of channel packets (`GRP_TXT` 0x05, `GRP_DATA` 0x06) when the server holds the key and the viewer may read that channel. It also fixes the mislabelled block: group packets were shown as "Dest hash / Src hash / Encrypted body", but byte 1 is half the MAC. They now read **Channel hash / Cipher MAC / Ciphertext**.

## Design

Decrypt **on read, server-side**. No plaintext is stored, there is no migration, and no secret reaches the browser.

- **`POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/packets/decode`**, body `{ rawHex }`. `optionalAuth` + `requirePermission('packetmonitor','read')` on that source, `ok()`/`fail()` envelope.
- **`src/server/utils/meshcorePacketPlaintext.ts`** (`decodeGroupPacketForViewer`): decodes the frame, finds keys by channel hash across every source's `channels` rows plus enabled MeshCore `channel_database` rows (`findChannelKeysByHash`), and tries each one whose fingerprint passes `canSeeKeyedMessage` against `resolveMeshcoreKeyAccess`. The gate runs **before** the decrypt, so a key the viewer may not read is never tried.
- **`openGroupFrame`** in `meshcoreFrameIngest.ts`: opens one frame with one key. GRP_TXT goes through `ChannelCrypto`, as ingest does. GRP_DATA verifies the 2-byte HMAC-SHA256 and decrypts AES-128-ECB with `node:crypto`.
- **Decoder** (`meshcorePacketDecode.ts`): 0x06 now gets the same `channelHash | cipherMac | ciphertext` framing as 0x05, under `payload.groupData`.
- **Modal**: calls the endpoint through `ApiService.decodeMeshCoreGroupPacket` when it opens a 0x05/0x06 packet; shows channel name, key origin, sender, sender time and text (or data type, length and a hex + ASCII dump); loading and error states; CSS module; i18n keys in `en.json`.

### Response

```jsonc
// no key, OR a key the viewer may not read, OR anonymous: one shape
{ "success": true, "data": { "decrypted": false, "payloadType": 5, "channelHash": "22" } }

{ "success": true, "data": {
  "decrypted": true, "payloadType": 5, "channelHash": "22",
  "channelName": "ops",
  "keyOrigin": { "kind": "source", "sourceName": "Companion", "currentSource": false },  // or { "kind": "virtual" }
  "text": { "sender": "Alice", "timestampSec": 1700000000, "text": "hello mesh" }        // GRP_DATA: "data": { "dataType", "dataHex" }
} }
```

## Decisions (from the maintainer)

- One PR for both issues; decrypt on read; nothing stored; no secret to the browser.
- No access to the key reads exactly like no key: `Unknown channel (hash 0xNN)`. A route test compares the two response bodies as strings.
- Anonymous viewers never get plaintext, whatever the anonymous user has been granted.
- When several rows hold the key, the name comes from this source's slot, then a virtual channel, then another source, and only from rows the viewer can read.
- Modal only. List rows, the socket feed, the JSONL export and the unified monitor stay ciphertext.

title: fix(packet-monitor): "Hide Own Packets" keeps TX rows; show a hidden count (#5579)
body:
Closes #5579

## Root cause

The server is fine. The per-source Mesh Traffic Monitor hid TX rows in the browser:

- `PacketMonitorPanel` defaults `hideOwnPackets` to `true` (localStorage `packetMonitor.hideOwnPackets`).
- `usePackets` dropped every row with `from_node === ownNodeNum`.
- `logOutgoingPacket` writes TX rows with `from_node = localNodeNum`.

So every TX row matched the filter. The checkbox sits in a collapsed filter drawer, so nothing told the user rows were missing. The Unified Packet Monitor has no such filter, which is why TX showed there.

## Change

- **Filter rule** (`src/hooks/usePackets.ts`): "Hide Own Packets" now hides only our own packets heard back: rows that are not `direction === 'tx'` and whose `from_node` is our node (RF rebroadcast, MQTT, UDP). TX rows always stay. The rule lives in an exported `isOwnPacketEcho()`; it coerces `from_node` with `Number()` for PG/MySQL BIGINT.
- **Hidden count**: `usePackets` returns `hiddenCount` (loaded rows the filter removed). A new `PacketHiddenChip` beside the packet count shows "N hidden" only when N > 0, with a tooltip naming the filter. Clicking it opens the filter drawer.
- **Checkbox hint**: the label keeps its text and gains a tooltip: it hides your own packets heard back; TX rows stay.
- **Docs** (`docs/features/packet-monitor.md`): the page said the monitor shows incoming packets only and that outgoing sends are never logged. Both were out of date. It now describes TX rows, the filter, and the chip.

## Decisions

- No change to the stored default and no settings migration. Existing users are fixed without touching their settings.
- The checkbox label text is unchanged, so the eleven translated locales stay correct; the new tooltip carries the detail. New strings are in `public/locales/en.json` only.
- "X shown / Y total" is unchanged: `shown` is the visible loaded rows, `total` is the server count. The chip counts hidden rows among loaded rows only, and its tooltip says "of the loaded packets".
- Chip styles are in a CSS module with theme tokens; the icon is `UiIcon` (`visibilityOff`).

## Mesh impact checklist

Display only. No packets sent, no notifications, no timers, no server change.

1. Airtime: none.
2. Spam: none.
3. Safety timers: none touched.

## Tests

- `src/hooks/usePackets.test.tsx`: hideOwn on keeps TX rows, hides own RX echoes (with and without a `direction` value), keeps other nodes; `hiddenCount` is right; hideOwn off hides nothing; unknown own node hides nothing; string `from_node` matches.
- `src/components/PacketHiddenChip.test.tsx`: renders nothing at 0 / negative / NaN; shows count and tooltip; click calls the handler.
- `tsc` clean for `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.server.json`; `lint:ci` has no in-repo FAIL lines.
- Full Vitest run with PG and MySQL containers up: 25,861 passed, 109 skipped, 4 failed, all in `src/server/meshtasticManager.lastHeardReplayGuard.test.ts`. That file compares a timestamp taken at collect time with one taken after a slo

title: fix(meshcore): repeater serial health probe and auto-reconnect (#5563)
body:
Closes #5563

## Problem

A directly-attached MeshCore Repeater source could stop answering and still show as connected. Nothing watched the serial link:

- The port had `open` and `error` listeners only. `error` only rejected the open promise; there was no `close` listener. A USB unplug went unseen.
- The reconnect chain fired only from a failed first connect and from the heartbeat, and the heartbeat was native-backend (Companion) only.
- A CLI timeout resolves with `''`, `readRepeaterStat` returns `null`, and both log at debug. Telemetry just stopped.
- `refreshLocalNode()` accepted an empty `get name`, so a wedged device "connected" as `Unknown Repeater` and reset `reconnectAttempts` on every attempt.

## What changed

**Port loss (always on).** `close` and a post-open `error` call `handleSerialPortLost`, which reconnects through the existing `beginReconnect` path with the existing 1-60 s backoff, whatever the heartbeat setting. It ignores a stale port, our own close (`intentionalTeardown`, set by `disconnect()` and `teardownTransportOnly()`), and a loss while a `connect()` is still in flight (that `connect()` now fails on the closed port and retries itself).

**Stall probe (opt-in).** Reuses `heartbeatIntervalSeconds`. Unset or 0 = no probe. When set, the existing `HeartbeatScheduler` runs one serial `clock` through `readRepeaterStat` on the `repeaterCliChain`, with a 5 s timeout. Three misses in a row tear the link down and reconnect.
- A tick is skipped (and counts as healthy) when a `->` reply to any other CLI command landed within the last interval. A busy console is not a stall. The probe's own reply does not count, or it would skip every second tick.
- Any `->` reply counts as alive, so a firmware that answers `Unknown command` is not torn down for it.

**`teardownTransportOnly()`** now closes the serial port, stops the neighbours poll, resets the RAW pairer and rejects in-flight commands. `lastRepeaterNeighborsPollAt` is kept, so a reconnect still waits out the poll interval. A rejected command now also drops its timers and its `serial_data` listener.

**Connect fails on a silent console.** When `get name` returns nothing, `refreshLocalNode()` stops (it skips the five reads behind it, each of which would wait 5 s) and `connect()` throws. Backoff keeps growing. A reply that does not parse (`Unknown command`) still connects as before.

**No advert on a recovered link.** A probe-, close- or error-driven reconnect sets `linkRecoveryReconnect`. The `connect()` that lands skips the on-start auto-announce. The flag survives failed attempts, and `disconnect()` clears it, so a manual disconnect + connect is a real start again. Normal startup is unchanged. Scope: Repeater sources only; Companion heartbeat reconnects behave as before.

**Text.** The heartbeat help on the MeshCore source form, the config comment and `docs/features/meshcore.md` no longer say "Companion only". The help string moved into `public/locales/en.json` (`meshcore.form.heart

title: feat(meshcore): virtual channels in the channel database (#5552)
body:
Closes #5552

Builds on #5574 (#5553 / #5551), now merged.

MeshCore virtual channels: the Channel Database can now hold MeshCore channel secrets. The server uses them to decrypt MeshCore channel messages heard by repeater and MQTT-ingest sources, with no device carrying the key and no ~40-slot companion cap.

## Design (maintainer decisions on #5552)

**Reuse `channel_database` with a `protocol` column** — migration 192
- `protocol TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'meshtastic'` on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. Every existing row is Meshtastic through the default; no backfill.
- A `meshcore` row stores the 16-byte secret (Base64 in `psk`, `pskLength` 16).

**Meshtastic behaviour is unchanged, by construction**
- `getAllAsync()`, `getEnabledAsync()`, `getByNameAsync()`, the passive find-or-create paths and `getPermissionsForUserAsync()` all default to Meshtastic rows. A caller has to pass `'meshcore'` or `'all'` on purpose.
- So packet decrypt (`channelDecryptionService`), MQTT ingest, retroactive decrypt, hash-collision detection, unified channel names and every `CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET + id` surface never see a MeshCore row, and a MeshCore grant never reads as Meshtastic virtual-channel access.
- `GET /api/channel-database` returns Meshtastic rows unless `?protocol=meshcore|all` is passed. Only the Channel Database page and the Users permission editor ask for `all`.

**MeshCore rows skip Meshtastic validation**
- Secret: 32 hex characters or Base64 of exactly 16 bytes. No 1-byte shorthand, no 32-byte keys, no all-zero secret.
- A name starting with `#` may omit the secret: it is derived as SHA-256(name)[0..16], the hashtag-room rule (reuses `deriveHashtagSecretHex`).
- No name-hash validation, no retroactive decrypt (it reads the Meshtastic packet log); the retroactive route answers 400 `NOT_MESHTASTIC`.

**Dedupe by secret**
- One MeshCore row per secret. A second create or an edit onto a stored secret answers 409 `DUPLICATE_SECRET` with `existingId`. The same bytes stored as a Meshtastic key do not count.

**Channel index scheme**
- Messages decrypted with a virtual channel are filed under `keyedChannelIndex(secret)` = 1000 + 16 bits of SHA-256(secret), the scheme #5574 introduced. It is derived from the key, so it cannot collide with device slots (0-~40), with `CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET` (100 + id), or with existing MeshCore message rows, and one key is one channel whether a device or the database holds it.

**Import from device — opt-in, no auto-mirror**
- `POST /api/channel-database/import-meshcore { sourceId }`, behind `channel_database:write`. Copies that MeshCore device source's channels as `meshcore` rows, skipping secrets already stored. Returns names and counts, never a key.
- Nothing mirrors a device. A later add, change or delete on the device leaves the database alone.
- UI: an "Import from MeshCore device" button on the Channel Database page, with a source picker.

**Default-deny**
- New rows (created or imported) get no `channel_database_permissions` row

+## MeshCore Channels
+
+The Channel Database also holds **MeshCore** channel keys. A MeshCore entry is a 16-byte channel secret that MeshMonitor uses to decrypt MeshCore channel messages (GRP_TXT) heard by:
+
+- a **MeshCore MQTT ingest** source, and
+- a directly attached **MeshCore repeater** running a `MESH_PACKET_LOGGING` firmware build.
+
+A companion radio holds about 40 channels. Keys in the Channel Database are held by the server alone, so that limit does not apply. They are never written to a device.
+
+### Adding a MeshCore channel
+
+1. Click **Add Channel** and set **Protocol** to **MeshCore**.
+2. Enter a name.
+3. Enter the **Channel secret**: 32 hex characters or Base64 (16 bytes). For a hashtag channel (a name that starts with `#`, such as `#general`), leave the secret empty. MeshMonitor derives it from the name, as the MeshCore apps do.
+
+Each secret is stored once. Adding a secret that is already stored is refused, whatever name it is given.
+
+### Import from MeshCore device
+
+**Import from MeshCore device** copies the channels of one MeshCore device source into the Channel Database. Pick the source and click **Import**.
+

+- Channels whose key is already stored are skipped.
+
+### Who can read MeshCore channel traffic
+
+New MeshCore entries, added by hand or imported, start with **no user access**. Until an administrator grants it, only administrators can read messages decrypted with that key. Grant access per user under **Users**, in the Channel Database permissions list; MeshCore entries are labelled there.
+
+A message decrypted with a key that also sits on a device source can be read by anyone who can read that channel on that device source.
+
+### What does not apply to MeshCore entries
+
+- **Retroactive processing** re-reads the Meshtastic packet log only. MeshCore entries decrypt new traffic from the moment they are added.

title: feat(map): cross-source "heard here" edges and the cross_source_links table (#5561)
body:
Closes #5561

Builds on #5573 (Phase 0 + #5559 + #5560), now merged. `main` is merged in, so the diff shows only the #5561 changes.

## What this does
Adds a third kind of map edge: **cross-source "heard here" links**. When one of your radios (source A) is heard by another of your sources (B), the map draws a directional edge A -> B. These are measured by MeshMonitor's own receivers, not reported by nodes.

## Design
### Storage: `cross_source_links` (migration 193)
Hourly aggregate, one row per (tx source + node, rx source + node, kind, transport, hour): `txSourceId, txNodeId, rxSourceId, rxNodeId, protocol, kind (origin|relay), transportClass (rf|mqtt_gateway), hourBucket, count, snrMin/Avg/Max, snrCount, rssiAvg, rssiCount, lastHeardAt`.
- Beyond the columns in the decision: `txNodeId`/`rxNodeId` (the route needs the radios to place the endpoints; for a gateway edge the receiver is the gateway, not a source), `protocol`, and `snrCount`/`rssiCount` (a hearing can lack either reading, so a correct running mean needs its own sample count).
- Writes are read-modify-write in the repository, serialised per edge by the recorder. A single-statement upsert would need per-dialect LEAST/COALESCE forms, and MySQL evaluates `ON DUPLICATE KEY` assignments left to right while PG/SQLite do not. Volume is low (only our own radios).
- Migration number: 193 (189 to 192 landed or were claimed while this was in progress).

### Ingest: `crossSourceLinkRecorder.ts`
Three non-blocking hooks, all classified through the shared `crossSourceCorrelation` module:
- **Meshtastic RX path** (`processMeshPacket`, next to `maybeRecordHeardReflood`, outside the `packet_log` gate).
- **MQTT ingest** (`ingestServiceEnvelope` wrapper): a gateway heard one of our radios over RF. Reuses the Coverage gateway rules (`evaluateMqttCoverageReception`): not via-MQTT, not stale, `ok_to_mqtt = no` honoured, a gateway that is one of our own radios skipped. Packets the node table refused (ignored / geo / distance) are skipped.
- **MeshCore** companion `ota_packet` and Observer feed: a signed zero-hop advert (origin) or a flood whose **last** hop hash matches one of our keys (relay).

What becomes an edge:
- `rf` and `mqtt_gateway` only. Broker-delivered MQTT and UDP copies are never stored.
- **`origin` edges need a direct hearing (0 hops)** (confirmed by the maintainer). A multi-hop copy of A's packet proves A sent it, not that B can hear A.
- **`relay` edges only from our own radios' hearings (`rf`)** (maintainer decision). Every source matching the relay byte / last-hop hash gets one, marked inferred. An MQTT gateway or MeshCore Observer hearing never yields a relay edge: on the dev rig a one-byte hash collision drew "likely relayed" from Boca to a gateway near Orlando. The recorder does not store them, `getLinks` never returns them, and the retention sweep deletes any an earlier build stored. Gateway and Observer hearings still yield proven `origin` edges. (4) the `coverage_surveys` table (issue #5277, Coverage Report) — a saved survey is one sender over one time window, heard by receivers on many sources, so it is **global**; it holds no reception data, its receptions are still read through the per-source `/receptions` route, and the survey list is gated on sender visibility. See `docs/internal/dev-notes/COVERAGE_P4_SPEC.md` §2b. (5) the `translation_cache` table (issue #5520) — one row per hashed (text, language) pair, shared so a phrase is translated once; it stores no text and no message reference, and no route reads it. The links from a message to an entry (`message_translations`) ARE per-source, and every read goes through the message-list visibility check. See `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSLATION_CACHE_SPEC.md`. (6) the `cross_source_links` table (issue #5561, map "heard here" edges) — an hourly aggregate of "source A's radio was heard by source B", so each row names **two** sources (`txSourceId`, `rxSourceId`) and has no single `sourceId`. **Two-source read rule:** a row, and anything derived from it, is shown only when the viewer can read BOTH sources (admins see all); never reveal "another source" to someone who can read only one. `CrossSourceLinksRepository.getLinks` takes the permitted source list and requires both ends in it, and the route drops any edge whose endpoint position fails `buildPositionFilter` / `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`. All classification goes through `src/server/services/crossSourceCorrelation.ts` (#5559/#5560 use the same rule read-side). Source deletion and purge remove rows on either end. Adding a new per-source data type should still get a `sourceId` column unless you have a concrete cross-source-by-design reason like decryption.
 - **Permissions are per-source.** `permissions.sourceId` was added in migration 022, refined in 033. `requirePermission(resource, action)` middleware honors source scoping.
 - **Frontend uses `SourceContext`** (`src/contexts/SourceContext.tsx`). `useSource()` returns `{ sourceId, sourceName }`; `sourceId` is `null` outside a `SourceProvider` (legacy/single-source views).
 - **`Unified*Page` components are cross-source consumers** (`UnifiedMessagesPage`, `UnifiedTelemetryPage`, `DashboardPage`).

+### Cross-Source Links
+
+If you run two or more sources, **Show Cross-Source Links** (Map Features,
+off by default) draws an edge whenever one of your radios is heard by
+another of your sources. Unlike traceroute segments and neighbor links, which
+come from what nodes report, these come from what MeshMonitor's own receivers
+heard.
+
+Each edge is **one-way**. The arrow points from the radio that transmitted to
+the radio that heard it. An edge from A to B says nothing about B to A; if both
+directions work you will see two edges.
+
+| Style | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| Solid | Your radio's own packet, heard directly (0 hops) by another source's radio |
+| Long dashes | Heard by an MQTT gateway's (or MeshCore observer's) radio on another source |
+| Dotted | **Likely relay** (inferred): your radio appears to be the last relay of someone else's packet, as heard by another of your own radios |
+
+A likely relay is a best guess. Meshtastic packets carry only the last byte
+of the relaying node's number, and MeshCore paths carry a one to three byte
+hash, so another node can share it. The popup says so. For that reason a
+likely relay is only drawn when one of your **own radios** heard the packet.
+A hearing by an MQTT gateway or a MeshCore observer never produces one: on a
+wide feed, a gateway far away will match the same byte by chance.
+
+Lines get thicker with the number of hearings and fade with age. Click an
+edge for the count, SNR (average, min, max), average RSSI, and when it was
+last heard. The map's age filter sets the window.
+
+Not drawn:
+
+- Copies that arrived only through an MQTT broker or UDP. Those are not RF.
+- A multi-hop copy of your own packet. It proves the packet was sent, not
+  that the two radios can hear each other.
+- Radios on different LoRa presets. They cannot hear each other over RF.
+
+You need read access to **both** sources to see an edge, and both radios'
+positions must be visible to you on the map. Links are kept for the Coverage
+retention period (Settings, Coverage Report) and are not part of backups. They
+start filling from the moment this version runs; there is no backfill.
+
+The same toggle works in the 3D view. The choice is saved in your browser.

title: feat(meshcore): repeater RAW ingest — adverts to Nodes, GRP_TXT to gated channel Messages (#5553, #5551)
body:
Closes #5553
Closes #5551

A repeater on a `MESH_PACKET_LOGGING` build streams every frame it hears as `RAW:` lines. Until now those only reached the Packet Monitor, and only with the packet log on. This PR also turns them into Nodes and channel Messages on the repeater source.

## What changes

**Shared ingest module** — `src/server/services/meshcoreFrameIngest.ts`
- The advert → node upsert and the GRP_TXT key lookup + decrypt moved out of `meshcoreMqttManager` into one module that MQTT and the repeater both call.
- MQTT behaviour is unchanged: same ids (`mqtt_…`), same `channel-<slot>` filing, same `lastHeard` rule. Its existing 91 tests pass untouched.
- `findChannelKeysByHash()` is the one "candidate keys by channel hash" helper the issue asks for.

**#5553 — adverts → Nodes**
- Runs whenever the repeater streams RAW. It is not gated on the packet log.
- Upserts name, type and position into the repeater source's `meshcore_nodes`, with the same "undefined keeps the stored value" rule as MQTT. `lastHeard` is the time we heard it.
- Quiet by design: no new-node notification, no `trigger.nodeDiscovered` / `trigger.nodeUpdated`. Only the contact-updated socket event fires, so an open Nodes list refreshes.
- **Neighbour marker:** new column `meshcore_nodes.repeaterNeighborAt`. Only the 5-minute `neighbors` poll writes it. An advert-only node leaves it NULL, gets no SNR/RSSI and no neighbour-graph row, so it is never taken for a zero-hop neighbour. On a repeater source the Nodes list tags listed neighbours "Neighbour".

**#5551 — GRP_TXT → channel Messages**
- Decrypts with a key from any source's `channels` rows (the repeater holds none). Also not gated on the packet log.
- **Channel index:** `1000 + first 16 bits of SHA-256(secret)`. It comes from the key, not from a slot, so the same key on two sources is one channel, and no device slot or `CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET` (100) value collides with it.
- **Provenance:** new columns `meshcore_messages.keySourceId`, `keyChannelIdx`, `keyFingerprint` (hex SHA-256(secret)[0..8]). The secret is never copied.
- **Read gate** (`src/server/utils/meshcoreKeyAccess.ts`): a row with a fingerprint is visible only to a viewer who can read a channel holding that secret, by the existing rule (`channel_N:read` or `messages:read` on that channel's source). This is ANDed with the normal checks on the repeater source. Admins see all.
  - Applied on: channel page, recent tail, channel counts and unread markers, snapshot, unified feed, search, CSV export, the channel list, and the live socket.
  - Keyed on the secret, not on one (source, slot): holding the key on any source is enough, and if every source drops the key, non-admins lose the rows instead of the grant passing to whatever key lands in that slot next.
- **Channel list:** `/api/channels/all?sourceId=<meshcore source>` adds the keyed channels the viewer may read (name only, `readOnly: true`). The channel view disables the send box on them.

title: feat(cross-source): correlation foundation, packet monitor tags, coverage flags (#5559, #5560)
body:
Closes #5559
Closes #5560

Part 1 of 2 for the cross-source work. #5561 (map edges and the aggregate table) follows in its own PR on top of this foundation.

## What this does
In a multi-source install, one of your radios (A) is heard by another (B). B's RX row then proves something A's own log cannot: A put that packet on the air and B was in range. This PR adds the shared correlation module and its two read-side consumers. **No new storage.**

## Phase 0: `src/server/services/crossSourceCorrelation.ts`
One module; every consumer uses it.

- **Resolver** (`resolveCrossSourceIndex`): readable source ids -> each source's own identity.
  - Meshtastic: the persisted local nodeNum (`resolveLocalNodeNums`), so a disconnected source still correlates.
  - MeshCore: the persisted `isLocalNode` row's public key (new repo method `meshcore.getLocalNodePublicKeysBySource`). It was already persisted (#3884), so no new persistence was needed.
  - Live manager values fill in for a source that connected but has not persisted yet.
- **Pure classifiers** (`classifyMeshtasticReception`, `classifyMeshCoreReception`): origin / likely relay / none, plus transport class `rf | mqtt_gateway | mqtt | udp`.
  - Meshtastic origin: `from_node` is A's nodeNum (proven).
  - Meshtastic likely relay: `relay_node` equals the low byte of A's nodeNum, the packet is not from A, and hops > 0. One byte is ambiguous, so it is always labelled inferred; every matching source is returned as a candidate (no uniqueness requirement, per the maintainer decision).
  - MeshCore origin: an ADVERT with A's public key **whose Ed25519 signature verifies** (`prepareMeshCoreReception`), so a forged advert cannot produce a tag.
  - MeshCore likely relay: a FLOOD packet with a path hash that prefixes A's key.
  - A MeshCore packet-hash match is not used: it only proves two sources heard the same packet, not who sent it.
  - Never tagged: the receiving source itself; two connections to the same physical radio; a gateway/observer row reported by A itself; `API`/`INTERNAL` copies.
- **Permission filter** (`resolveCorrelationSourceIds`, and the index itself): the index only holds sources the viewer can read under the consumer's resource, and the row being classified is from a readable source. So a tag can only name a source the viewer can read on both ends. A viewer with one source never learns another exists.

The investigation note that `maybeRecordHeardReflood` is "prior art" was checked: it is a single-source own-echo recorder, not a cross-source join. Nothing was reused from it here.

## #5559: Unified Packet Monitor
- `GET /api/unified/packets` rows gain `originSourceId`/`originSourceName`, `likelyRelaySourceId`/`likelyRelaySourceName`, `likelyRelayCandidateCount`, `crossSourceTransport`. Gate: `packetmonitor:read` on both sources.
- New filter `?crossSource=any|origin|relay`. It is a post-filter (no storage), so it walks only the complete prefix of the merged stream and hands back a cursor at the la

title: feat(forwarding): source-level master switch, sidebar FWD pill, automation action (#5537)
body:
Closes #5537

## What

Message Forwarding (#5446) had only per-rule on/off flags, so pausing one source meant unticking every rule. This adds a source-level master switch, a sidebar pill to see and flip it, and an Automation Engine action.

"Forwarding" here is Message Forwarding only. It does not touch the MT↔MC bridge, mqttLink, MQTT uplink/downlink or the hop-limit raise.

## Design

**Master switch.** New per-source setting `forwardingEnabled` (`'true'`/`'false'`), read with `getSettingForSource`. Absent reads as ON, so existing installs behave as before. Both call sites (`MeshtasticManager.checkForwarding`, `MeshCoreManager.checkForwarding`) check it before they parse the rules. It lives in the DB, so it survives a restart. The key is in `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS`, `PER_SOURCE_KEYS_NOT_POSTABLE` and the hidden-from-public-GET set, the same as `forwardingRules`: the generic `/api/settings` route cannot write it.

**Route.** `GET /api/sources/:id/forwarding` now returns `{ rules, enabled, limits }`. New `PUT /api/sources/:id/forwarding/enabled` with body `{ enabled: boolean }`, gated on per-source `automation` write, `ok()`/`fail()` envelope.

**Forwarding section.** The shared `ForwardingSection` (used by both the Meshtastic Automation tab and the MeshCore Automations view) gets a header switch. It saves at once, apart from the save bar, and shows a note when forwarding is off. Disabled without `automation` write.

**FWD pill.** Shown on every `DashboardSidebar` source card whose source has forwarding rules: `FWD 2` (on, two rules ticked) or `FWD off`. The state rides on the `GET /api/sources/:id/status` payload the sidebar already polls (`status.forwarding = { enabled, ruleCount, activeRuleCount, canWrite }`), so there is no extra request per source. The block is present only for callers with `automation` read on that source, and only when the source has rules. The pill is clickable only when `canWrite` (per-source `automation` write); otherwise it is a disabled, read-only badge.

**Automation action.** `action.setSourceForwardingEnabled { sourceId, mode: set|toggle, enabled }`, modelled on `action.setAutomationEnabled`. It can turn forwarding on or off.

## Decisions

- **Save-time permission gate.** Automations are global and run as the system, so the gate is at save. Create, update (when `config` changes), import and duplicate all check that the saving user holds `automation` write on every source the graph targets. Admins pass. Failure is `403 FORWARDING_SOURCE_FORBIDDEN` with the denied `sourceIds`.
- **`sourceId` must be a literal.** Validation rejects a `{{ }}` template in `sourceId`; a template would dodge the save-time check. `enabled` may still be a template.
- **Not checked on enable.** `POST /:id/enable` and a `PUT` that only flips `enabled` do not re-run the check: the maintainer decision named save as the gate. A user with global `automations` write can therefore enable an automation an admin saved. Say if you want that path ga

title: fix(lora): correct modem preset tables, add TINY presets, firmware 2.8 region rules, LongModTurbo recipe
body:
Closes #5546
Closes #5547
Closes #5548

## What this fixes

**#5546.** `LONG_TURBO` was labelled CR 4/5. Firmware runs it at 500 kHz / SF11 / CR 4/8. Label only; wire value stays enum 9.

**#5547.** LITE/NARROW showed bandwidth only, and TINY_FAST / TINY_SLOW were missing. While fixing that I found a destructive bug:

- `PRESET_MAP` had no TINY entries, and the Config tab resolved names with `PRESET_MAP[name] || 0`. `/api/config` sends enum names, so a radio on TINY_FAST loaded as LONG_FAST. The LoRa save is a whole-struct replace, so saving any LoRa field pushed LONG_FAST to that radio.

**#5548.** Adds a "Load recipe" menu to the custom-parameters UI, with one recipe: LongModTurbo (500 kHz / SF11 / CR 4/8).

Checked against `meshtastic/firmware` tags `v2.8.0.47db0e3`, `v2.8.1.8e6a88d` and `develop` (`src/mesh/MeshRadio.h`, `src/mesh/RadioInterface.cpp`), and against `v2.7.26.54e0d8d` for what older firmware lacks.

title: feat(dashboard): Live Mesh Activity widget (#5557)
body:
Closes #5557

## What

A new per-source Dashboard widget, **Live Mesh Activity**: every remote node the source heard in a rolling window, like the live mesh activity view in the Meshtastic phone app.

Columns: node (short name + ID), packets, extra receptions, SNR (last + trend arrow), hops (last / min), last heard. Window 1m / 5m / 10m / 30m / 1h (default 10m). Polls every 10 s with a countdown. Sort by packets, SNR, hops or last heard. Row click opens the node.

## Design

- **Repo:** `PacketLogRepository.getNodeActivity({ sourceId, since, localNodeNum, transportClass, visibility })`. One grouped query on `packet_log`, joined back on `MAX(id)` for the latest row's SNR and hops. Excludes `direction = 'tx'` and our own node. Plus `getOldestPacketTimestamp()`.
- **Route:** `GET /api/packets/stats/node-activity?sourceId=&windowMinutes=&transport=`. Reuses `requirePacketPermissions` (`packetmonitor:read` per source) and the non-admin channel/DM visibility rule. Uses the `ok()` / `fail()` envelope. The server picks `since`, so a skewed browser clock cannot shift the window.
- **Migration 190:** index `idx_packet_log_source_timestamp` on `packet_log(sourceId, timestamp)`, all three backends, idempotent. `sourceId` is quoted on PostgreSQL; the rest of `packet_log` is snake_case everywhere.
- **Widget:** `LiveMeshActivityWidget.tsx` + CSS module, new widget type `liveMeshActivity { windowMinutes }`, added to the Add Widget palette. Fetches through `packetApi.getNodeActivity` and TanStack Query (`refetchInterval` 10 s, paused when the tab is hidden).

## Decisions (from the maintainer)

- **RF-only by default**, with an "All transports" toggle to add MQTT and UDP.
- **Extra receptions** = rows − `DISTINCT packet_id`. Exact duplicates are dropped at ingest, so these are real repeat receptions (rebroadcasts).
- **Meshtastic only** for v1. MeshCore dashboards hide custom widgets already.
- **Packet log off:** empty state, "Enable the packet log to see live activity", pointing at Settings → Packet Monitor.
- **Cap cuts the window:** a "Data covers since X" line. X is the oldest row left in `packet_log`. The cap is global, so that row marks where the log starts for every source.

Choices I made that are worth a look:

- **SNR trend** compares the last SNR with the window average; more than 1 dB above or below shows an arrow.
- **Hops** use `hop_start - hop_limit` only when `hop_start > 0` (0 is the firmware's "unknown" value); otherwise `?`.
- The "All transports" toggle is view state and is not saved. The window is saved with the widget (editors only).
- Row cap: 500 nodes per response.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. Read-only; sends no packets.
2. **Spam:** none. No rows written, no events emitted, no notifications.
3. **Safety timers:** none armed.

DB cost: each open widget runs one indexed aggregate plus one `MIN(timestamp)` every 10 s while its tab is visible. The scan is bounded by the packet log cap (default 1000 rows) and served by

title: fix(settings): appearance and UI preferences are global-only (#5558)
body:
Closes #5558

## Problem

The landing page (`/`) and Global Settings stayed light while per-source pages were dark.

The appearance keys (`theme`, `appearanceMode`, `darkTheme`, `lightTheme`) were valid settings keys but not in `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`. So `POST /api/settings?sourceId=X` stored them as `source:X:…`, and `GET /api/settings?sourceId=X` let that copy beat the global value. `SettingsContext` loads server settings shortly after mount and re-applies the theme, so a source page used the source copy and every non-source route used the global value.

This is not the lazy-chunk CSS theory from the issue thread: `data-theme` itself differed between routes.

## Fix

1. **Write path.** The four appearance keys, plus the other global UI preferences with the same exposure, join `GLOBAL_ONLY_SETTINGS_KEYS`. A sourced POST now drops them and reports them in `ignoredKeys`.
2. **Read path.** The sourced GET skips source copies of every global-only key, so a stale row can never override the global value.
3. **Migration 189** (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL; idempotent; `settingsKey`) deletes `source:%:{key}` rows for these keys. Promotion rule, so a user who only ever saved from a source keeps what they see:
   - The four appearance keys are judged as one set. If the global set is unset or still default (`system` / `mocha` / `latte`) and every live source with a copy holds the same four-tuple, that tuple becomes global. Otherwise global wins.
   - Each other key is judged alone: promoted only when global is unset and all source copies agree.
   - Copies from deleted sources are removed but get no vote.

The client needed no change. `SettingsTab.handleSave` already sends everything outside `SETTINGS_TAB_PER_SOURCE_KEYS` on the unscoped POST, including from a source's Settings tab. A new test pins that.

## Audit of other UI preference keys

Made global-only (shown only in global sections, saved only unscoped, read server-side only via `getSetting`): `iconStyle`, `mapPinStyle`, `mapPinColorMode`, `nodeListStyle`, `defaultLandingPage`, `temperatureUnit`, `distanceUnit`, `timeFormat`, `dateFormat`, `preferredSortField`, `preferredSortDirection`, `preferredDashboardSortOption`.

Left alone:
- `mapTileset`, `mapTilesetLight`, `mapTilesetDark` — also overlaid by per-user map preferences; needs its own look.
- `positionHistoryLineStyle`, `neighborInfoMinZoom`, map center/zoom/clustering keys — same latent exposure, map behaviour rather than appearance; left to keep this PR narrow.
- `telemetryVisualizationHours`, `favoriteTelemetryStorageDays` — shown in a per-source section; scope is ambiguous.
- `language` — not in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, never stored server-side.

## Tests

- `settingsRoutes.globalUiPrefs.test.ts` (route harness): sourced POST writes nothing to the source namespace; unscoped POST is what the sourced GET returns; a stale source copy never overrides global; a real per-source key still wins.
- `189_…test.ts`: planner rules plus SQLite `up()` i

title: fix(meshcore): 3-byte Define Path, shared telemetry labels, local-node favorites (#5554, #5550, #5549)
body:
Closes #5554
Closes #5550
Closes #5549

## #5554: Define Path with 3-byte hashes always failed

`meshcore.js` reads a contact's `out_path_len` with `readInt8()`. The byte is packed: top 2 bits = hash width (00 = 1 byte, 01 = 2, 10 = 3), low 6 bits = hop count. Every 3-byte path sets bit 7, so it came back negative.

- `set_out_path` read-back compared the signed value to the unsigned `expectedLen`, never matched, and threw. The route turned that into the 409 "device rejected" even though the device had stored the path.
- `get_contacts` only decoded `rawLen > 0`, and `formatOutPath` treats a negative as `OUT_PATH_UNKNOWN`, so every stored 3-byte path showed as flood.

Fix: new `decodeOutPathLen()` in `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts` masks the byte back to unsigned before decoding. `get_contacts` uses it; the read-back compares `outPathLen & 0xff`.

**Decisions**
- Only `0xFF` means unknown.
- Top bits `11` (reserved 4-byte width, which firmware rejects) read as unknown.

## #5550: Repeater and Companion telemetry labels differ

A Repeater source writes the local-poller names (`mc_pkt_*`, `mc_tx_air_secs`); a Companion polling the same repeater writes `mc_status_*`. Same firmware counters, two label sets.

**Decision: labels only.** No stored metric is renamed and there is no data migration. Each pair now shares one label in `TelemetryChart.tsx`:

| Label | remote status | local poller |
|---|---|---|
| Packets Received (total) | `mc_status_packets_recv` | `mc_pkt_recv` |
| Packets Sent (total) | `mc_status_packets_sent` | `mc_pkt_sent` |
| Sent (Flood) / Sent (Direct) | `mc_status_sent_*` | `mc_pkt_*_tx` |
| Received (Flood) / Received (Direct) | `mc_status_recv_*` | `mc_pkt_*_rx` |
| TX Air Time | `mc_status_air_time_secs` | `mc_tx_air_secs` |
| Errors | `mc_status_errors` | `mc_errors` (was unlabelled) |

`mc_battery_mv` and `mc_firmware_ver` also get labels and categories; they showed as raw keys. `MeshCoreInfoView` now takes its labels from `getTelemetryLabel`, so the Node Info page, the Node Details dropdown and the Dashboard agree.

Left alone on purpose: `mc_status_battery_volts` keeps "Battery (status)", because a remote node can also report an LPP `mc_battery_volts` and the two would collide.

**Out of scope (needs firmware):**
- Category B: `direct_dups` / `flood_dups` are not in the repeater's `stats-packets` CLI reply. Once `formatPacketStats` emits them, the poller can parse them.
- Category C: LPP sensor channels (`Battery (ch2)`, `Current (ch2)`, `Power (ch2)`) come over the mesh telemetry request, not the repeater serial CLI, so a Repeater source cannot report them for itself.

## #5549: Favorite the local node's telemetry

The hand-rolled graph grid in `MeshCoreInfoView` now has the same per-metric star as `TelemetryGraphs` (`UiIcon` `favorite` / `favoriteOff`), via `useFavorites` / `useToggleFavorite`.

**Decisions**
- Keyed on `telemetryRef.nodeId`: the companion's pubkey, or `repeaterPublicKey` for a Repeater source (#5539).
- Hidden

title: fix(map): CARTO key on report maps, one-world clamp, coverage overlap chooser (#5555, #5556, #5543)
body:
Closes #5555
Closes #5556
Closes #5543

Three map fixes in one PR.

## #5555: Traceroute Explorer and Coverage Report maps ignore the CARTO key

**Cause:** `ExplorerMap` and `CoverageMap` passed `tilesetId={mapTileset}` to `BaseMap` but not `cartoApiKey` or `styleJson`. With a CARTO preset, those two maps drew "API key required" watermark tiles while the main map was clean. (`TracerouteWidget`, named in the issue, already passes the key. The bug was in the Explorer report's own map.)

**Fix:**
- New hook `useBaseMapSettings()` (`src/components/map/useBaseMapSettings.ts`). It returns `{ tilesetId, customTilesets, cartoApiKey, styleJson }`, built the same way MeshCoreMap, NodesTab and DashboardMap build them. Callers spread it onto `<BaseMap {...baseMapSettings}>`.
- ExplorerMap and CoverageMap use the hook. MeshCoreMap and ReticulumMap moved to it too, since that was a straight swap.
- `BaseMap` still never calls `useSettings()`, because `EmbedMap` renders without a `SettingsProvider`.
- Sweep test (`baseMapCartoKey.sweep.test.ts`): any `<BaseMap>` tag that passes `tilesetId=` or spreads `useBaseMapSettings()` must also pass `cartoApiKey=` or use the spread.

## #5556: zoomed-out maps repeat the world, but markers draw on only one copy

This happens with Leaflet's defaults on every platform, not only iOS. Per the maintainer decision this PR takes **option B, one world**, in `BaseMap`, so every 2D map gets it:
- `MapContainer`: `maxBounds` set to the Web Mercator extent (±85.0511°, ±180°) and `maxBoundsViscosity: 1`. The latitude is the exact tile edge rather than a round ±85, so the world-fill zoom below matches the tiles.
- Raster base and overlay `TileLayer`s: `noWrap`.
- `VectorTileLayer` (MapLibre): `renderWorldCopies: false`.
- **Min zoom is computed, not fixed at 2.** At zoom 2 the world is 1024 px wide, so a fixed `minZoom: 2` still leaves grey bars on any wider window. The new `WorldFillMinZoom` controller sets the floor to `map.getBoundsZoom(WORLD_BOUNDS, true)`, the smallest zoom at which one world covers the whole container. It recomputes on every container `resize`. Results:
  - 1920×1080 desktop: 3
  - 390×800 phone: 2
  - 300×200 widget or embed: 1
  - Hidden 0×0 container: floor left unchanged

  A map that opens below its floor jumps to it with no animation.
- These options always have a value, so they don't hit the "omitted props must not be keys" trap (`BaseMap.tsx` ~156). Omitted interaction props still stay out of the options. A test checks this.
- `ZoomCeilingBackstop` (#5521) is untouched. It owns `maxZoom`; `WorldFillMinZoom` owns `minZoom`. `WorldFillMinZoom` mounts after it and before `children`, so a child's `fitBounds` already sees the floor.
- The 3D view (`Base3DMap`) is native MapLibre. Its GL layers draw on every world copy, so it doesn't have this bug and is unchanged. `TracerouteWidget`'s standalone `MapContainer` doesn't use `BaseMap` and is unchanged.
