title: fix(coverage): select the blocking live survey on SURVEY_ALREADY_LIVE (#5544)
body:
Closes #5544

## Problem
Starting a Coverage survey for a sender with a live survey failed with "This sender already has a live survey running." The bar stayed on "No survey", so the Stop button (shown only for a selected live survey) never appeared, and nothing hinted that the running survey existed.

## Change
- **Server** (`coverageSurveyRoutes.ts`): the 409 now reads `fail(res, 409, 'SURVEY_ALREADY_LIVE', msg, { liveSurveyId })`. The caller has already passed the sender-visibility gate, and `GET /surveys` lists the same survey to them, so the id reveals nothing new.
- **Client** (`CoverageSurveyBar.tsx`): on that 409 the bar closes the Start dialog and selects the blocking survey. If the cached list predates it (another tab or user started it), it refetches the list once first.
  - Creator or admin: the existing **Stop survey** button appears; the toast says "It is now selected; use Stop survey to end it."
  - Anyone else: the survey is selected read-only, with "started by another user. Only its creator or an admin can stop it."
  - An old server that omits `liveSurveyId` falls back to the old toast.
- `liveSurveyIdFromError()` helper in `coverageSurveyBar.helpers.ts`; two new strings in `en.json`.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. Airtime: zero. No packets sent.
2. Spam: none. No messages, notifications, or `dataEventEmitter` events.
3. Timers: none touched.

## Tests
- Route harness (`coverageSurveyRoutes.test.ts`): the 409 carries the blocking survey's id; a limited user blocked by an admin's survey gets the id and sees that survey in their list with `canEdit: false`.
- Component (`CoverageSurveyBar.test.tsx`): the creator's blocking survey gets selected and the dialog closes; Stop appears once the parent applies the selection; a non-creator gets the "another user" message and no Stop button; a missing cached survey triggers one refetch.
- Helper tests for `liveSurveyIdFromError`.
- Full suite: 25,369 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL containers up); both `tsc` configs clean; `lint:ci` clean.

## Browser check
Start a live survey for a sender, pick "No survey", then click **Start survey** again for the same sender. The running survey should become selected with a **Stop survey** button. Repeat as a second non-admin user who can see the sender: you should get the "started by another user" toast and no Stop button.

title: fix(translation): refine endpoint URL resolution
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
Takes a stab at resolving [Issue-5519](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/issues/5519)

This PR is broken up into 2 commits.

### Commit 1
Tackles the reported issue by using the following rules:

1. If the URL provided has no protocol (http/https) the protocol from the provider's default URL is prepended.
2. If the URL has no path, the path from the provider's default URL is appended.
3. If the URL has a path, it's used as is.
4. If no URL is provided at all, the provider's default URL is used.

*note* This resolution is done at 'run time' before every translation api call.

### Commit 2

This commit attempts to change the resolution of the API url from 'run time' to 'settings persist time'. Basically when you hit save on the settings page it does the resolution and persists the value.  At 'run time' it uses the configured value as is, or errors if it is blank.

I saw this as a problem to be fixed because if we continued persisting the API URL as blank and resolving it at run time, if future versions updated the default URL (as I have done in this PR....), it may silently break people's configuration that worked previously by changing the URL being used out from under them.  If we don't want to go this route, we should be able to just drop off the 2nd commit from this PR.

**NOTE** It should be noted, this change is breaking, anyone who previously setup a translation provider and has a blank URL persisted, will now error.  I'm thinking this is probably fine because there hasn't be an official release w/ the translation feature included yet?

LibreTranslate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
• Default Path: /translate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
• Default Endpoint: http://libretranslate:5000/translate (Default protocol: http://)

title: feat(nodes): remote admin shortcut from node details (#5535)
body:
Closes #5535.

For admins, the **Remote Admin: Available** badge in a node's details (Messages tab) is now a link. It opens Admin Commands on the same source with that node already selected.

## How
- `src/utils/adminDeepLink.ts` builds `/source/<sourceId>/admin?node=!xxxxxxxx` and parses it. The node id is strictly validated as `!` plus 8 hex digits, and anything else is dropped.
- `RemoteAdminLink.tsx` wraps the badge in a `<Link>`. If any of these conditions fails, it renders the same inert badge as before:
  - the user is an admin (the same check as the `admin` route itself),
  - the node is "Available",
  - the node has an id,
  - there is a sourceId.
- `AdminCommandsTab` reads `?node=` once on mount and preselects the matching node. With no match, it falls back to the local node as before.
- Meshtastic only. MeshCore mounts its remote admin console inline in the contact panel, so it has no separate badge.

## Screenshots
Badge on a node verified as admin-capable (hover shows "Open remote admin for Yeraze BLE Sandbox"):

![badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/bd95c02024402192d5de11501051b265ae7d03d8/docs/public/images/features/5535-remote-admin-badge.png)

After clicking, Admin Commands opens with the node preselected and a session passkey already acquired:

![admin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/bd95c02024402192d5de11501051b265ae7d03d8/docs/public/images/features/5535-admin-preselected.png)

## Testing
- The first version linked to `/admin`, which falls through to the Dashboard because the route only exists under `source/:sourceId/*`.
  - `RemoteAdminLink.routeIntegration.test.tsx` mounts the real nested route shape in a BrowserRouter, clicks the badge, and asserts the node is preselected.
  - The test fails against the old path.
- Unit tests cover the deep-link build/parse, the link vs. inert rendering, NodeDetailsBlock wiring, and AdminCommandsTab preselection.
- tsc clean (both configs). `lint:ci` clean. Targeted suites (139 tests, incl. MessagesTab/App/AdminCommandsTab/i18n): success.
- Driven in the dev container with a real click: the URL became `/source/<id>/admin?node=%21384df6f7` and the node was preselected.

title: feat(automations): node discovered/updated triggers for both protocols + packet tokens (#5534)
body:
Closes #5534.

The packet-token request depended on two missing pieces: `trigger.nodeDiscovered` never fired, and MeshCore raised no node triggers at all. This PR adds both, plus the tokens.

## Tokens
- `{{trigger.packetId}}`: Meshtastic, the MeshPacket that caused the event (unsigned).
- `{{trigger.packetHash}}`: MeshCore, the hash of the ADVERT frame.
- `{{trigger.publicKey}}` and `{{trigger.name}}`: on MeshCore node triggers.

Each token comes only from the current event, so a stale value can't carry over. It is empty when the event wasn't caused by a received packet, e.g. device sync or favorite/ignore edits.

## nodeDiscovered (both protocols)
Fires once per node **heard live** that has no row on that source. It fires instead of nodeUpdated for that packet. A deleted or purged node that is heard again counts as discovered again.

Device sync never counts as discovery:
- **Meshtastic NodeDB dump** arrives through `processNodeInfoProtobuf`, which never checks for discovery.
- **fw 2.8 hourly/reconnect replays** keep their original rx_time, so the 120 s `isLiveReception` window rejects them.
- **MeshCore** node triggers stay off until `connect()` has seeded contacts and read `get_contacts`, and turn off again on disconnect. The contact sync, and any adverts during it, never fire.

## MeshCore nodeUpdated
Fires only when name, lat/lon, advType or out path changes. A re-advert with nothing new fires nothing. `subjectNodeKey` = publicKey, same as nodeStale.

## Mesh impact
- **Nothing is transmitted.** Worst case is one automation event per received advert, and only when a tracked field changed. Path changes are debounced. Discovery is one event per new node per source.
- Existing per-automation rate limits and cooldowns still apply.
- The self-origin guards (#3914) still apply to both protocols, with a test for MeshCore.

## Not covered
MQTT sources (Meshtastic or MeshCore) raise no node triggers, the same as before.

## Testing
- 36 new tests: 10 MeshCore, 9 Meshtastic, 10 utils, 7 routing/context.
- tsc clean (both configs). `lint:ci` clean.
- Full vitest: success, 23,993 passed / 0 failed (PG/MySQL skipped; no schema change).
- Docs updated: `SubstitutionsHelp`, trigger catalog descriptions, `docs/features/automation-engine.md`.

+### Node discovered and updated
+
+**A new node is discovered** fires once, the first time a source hears a node **live** and has no
+row for it. It fires *instead of* **A node is updated** for that packet, never both. There is no
+permanent memory: delete a node and hear it again, and it is discovered again.

+Device syncs never count, so a reconnect does not fire it for every node:

+  original receive time, so anything received more than 2 minutes ago does not count.
+- **MeshCore.** The contact list loaded on connect (from the database and the companion) is stored
+  silently, as are adverts that arrive while it loads. After that, a live advert from an unknown
+  key, or a reply to a **Discover** sweep, is a discovery. When the first advert carries no name,
+  the trigger waits until the name arrives, so `{{ trigger.name }}` is set.

+On MeshCore, **A node is updated** fires only when the name, position, node type, or path changes.
+A re-advert that changes nothing does not fire it. `{{ trigger.changed }}` lists the fields:
+`name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `advType`, `outPath`, `pathLen`.
+
+MeshCore nodes have no node number, so `{{ node.* }}` is empty for them. Use
+`{{ trigger.publicKey }}` and `{{ trigger.name }}` instead. Cooldowns keyed per node use the public
+key.
+
+### Node triggers — originating packet

+Both node triggers expose the packet that caused the event:

+| Token | Protocol | Value |
+|-------|----------|-------|
+| `{{ trigger.packetId }}` | Meshtastic | Id of the received packet that caused the event, as an unsigned 32-bit number. |
+| `{{ trigger.packetHash }}` | MeshCore | Hash of the advert that caused the event, in the same 16-hex format as on the message trigger. Use it to link to `https://map.meshcore.com.hr/#/packets/{{ trigger.packetHash }}`. |
+
+Each token is **empty** on the other protocol, and empty whenever no single packet caused the event:
+device syncs, manual edits, merges, and other bookkeeping updates. On MeshCore, path changes and
+**Discover** replies are not adverts, so `{{ trigger.packetHash }}` is empty for them too.
+MeshMonitor never fills these from an earlier packet.
+
+`{{ trigger.packetHash }}` comes from the raw frame the companion logs just before it reports the
+advert. If that frame is missing, the token is empty.

title: feat(meshcore): local telemetry for directly-attached repeaters (#5533)
body:
Closes #5533.

A USB/serial-attached MeshCore **Repeater** source now collects the same local health stats as a Companion and shows them on the Info page.

## How
The repeater serial CLI exposes the same counters, so the poller reads them with local CLI verbs (MeshCore a366955):
- `stats-core` / `stats-radio` / `stats-packets` (CommonCLI.cpp:437-442) return JSON with the same keys as the companion `get_stats`.
- `clock` (CommonCLI.cpp:213-216) returns `HH:MM - d/m/yyyy UTC`, so minute resolution only.
- `ver` / `board` return firmware version, build and model.

Shared mappers (`src/server/utils/meshcoreRepeaterStats.ts`) feed both paths, and Companion output is unchanged. A missing or garbled field stays undefined, never 0.

## What changes for repeaters
- `meshcoreTelemetryPoller` polls repeaters on the existing 5-minute timer; no new timer. Rows are filed under the real `get public.key` key and scoped by sourceId. With no key yet, the poll is skipped.
- `/stats/:type` and `/info` (`telemetryRef`) work for repeaters.
- `MeshCoreInfoView` shows the health card and History graphs. RTC Sync stays Companion-only, since it writes the clock over the companion protocol.
- Device-health reboot/power detection now covers repeaters.
- RTC drift compares server time truncated to the minute, so an in-sync clock reads 0.

## Mesh impact
None. All six verbs are local serial reads with zero RF. They queue on the existing `repeaterCliChain` lock, so they can't interleave with a user's CLI session. Each read ends after a 300 ms idle gap (5 s ceiling). A busy, closed or silent link returns null and logs at debug level only.

## Not covered (follow-up)
Low-battery notifications and the lastHeard stamp are **not** wired for repeaters. The live local node row is keyed `'repeater'`, so writing a `meshcore_nodes` row under the real key would create a duplicate node. That needs a placeholder-to-real-key reconciliation first.

## Testing
- Parser tests use real firmware reply strings, with source lines cited. Also added: manager branching, fail-soft and mutex tests; poller repeater tests; `/info` route cases; Info view cases.
- tsc clean (both configs). `lint:ci` clean.
- Full vitest: success, 23,983 passed / 0 failed (PG/MySQL skipped; no schema change).
- **Not validated on hardware.** The dev rig has no USB-attached repeater (ttyUSB0 is Meshtastic, ttyUSB1 silent). Needs a check against a real repeater before release.

title: fix(db): scope migration information_schema checks to the current database
body:
## Summary

Old migrations checked `information_schema` (and PG catalogs) by table name alone. When one MySQL server hosts a second database (two MeshMonitor instances, or CI's parallel suites with isolated databases), a column or table in the *other* database makes the "already applied?" check skip the `ALTER`/`CREATE` here. #5525 hit this in migration 007 (`Unknown column 'map_tileset'`) and fixed only that one. On PostgreSQL the same thing happens across schemas in one database.

This PR adds the scope to every remaining unscoped check. Nothing else about any migration changes; they stay idempotent, the checks just look at the right database.

### MySQL (`TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()`)
- `034_add_via_store_forward` — `messages.viaStoreForward` column check
- `035_add_is_store_forward_server` — `nodes.isStoreForwardServer` column check
- (007 fixed in #5525; `addColumnIfMissingMysql` / `createTableIfMissingMysql` / `createIndexIfMissingMysql` in `helpers.ts` were already scoped, now covered by a test)

### PostgreSQL `information_schema` (`table_schema = current_schema()`)
- `005`, `007`, `008` (3 checks), `009` (3), `016`, `023`, `033`, `037` (5, incl. `table_constraints`), `047` (2), `091`, `096`, `163`
- `src/server/services/systemRestoreService.ts` — table-exists check during PG restore

### PostgreSQL catalogs
- `015`, `024`, `025`, `028` — `pg_constraint` lookups by `conname` now also match `connamespace = current_schema()::regnamespace`; `028`'s `pg_indexes` lookups match `schemaname = current_schema()`
- `031` — unique-index sweep matched `t.relname = 'nodes'`; now `t.oid = 'nodes'::regclass` (same as the constraint query above it)

PG checks already scoped to `'public'` are left alone.

### Also
- `messages.export.multiBackend.test.ts`: the hand-written `meshcore_messages` DDL from #5523 lacks the `senderTimestamp` column #5525 added, so that suite fails on all three backends on current `main`. Added the column.

## Tests
- New `src/server/migrations/informationSchemaScope.pgmysql.test.ts`: plants decoy tables/columns/indexes/constraints in a second MySQL database (or a second PG schema), runs migrations 034/035 + the three MySQL helpers, and PG migrations 008/024/047 against the target, and asserts the target still gets the change. Without this PR's migration edits, 4 of its 5 tests fail.
- All `*.pgmysql.test.ts` + `*multiBackend*.test.ts` + `src/server/migrations` run together against live PG (5433) / MySQL (3307): 0 failures, 0 skipped.
- Full suite: 25,139 passed, 109 pending (PG/MySQL suites all ran: 700 pgmysql/multiBackend tests passed, 0 pending). 3 `meshtasticManager.*` suites hit 10s hook timeouts under host load (load avg ~46) and pass when rerun alone.
- `tsc` (tsconfig.json + tsconfig.server.json) clean; `lint:ci` no FAIL lines.

## Mesh impact
None: migration checks only, no packets, notifications, or timers.

title: perf(build): split the main bundle
body:
## Summary

`main-*.js` had grown to 4.2 MB (1.04 MB gzip), and #5524 raised the PWA precache cap to 6 MiB to keep the build passing. This PR splits it so the cap can go back to 4 MiB.

### What's lazy-loaded

Every route page in `src/main.tsx` is now a `React.lazy` chunk:
- `App`
- Dashboard, MapAnalysis, Reports, Automations
- UnifiedMessages, UnifiedTelemetry, UnifiedPacketMonitor
- GlobalSettings, Users, PacketMonitor, PrivacyDocument
- MeshCoreSource, MeshCoreIngestSource, ReticulumSource

A new `RouteLoading` component (CSS module, plain text, so it never waits on i18n) replaces the inline Suspense fallbacks. `SourceApp` gets its own Suspense boundary. Component internals are untouched, and no vendor chunking was needed.

### Sizes (`npx vite build`)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `main` JS | 4,205,588 B (1,044 kB gzip) | 171,347 B (56 kB gzip) |
| Largest JS asset | `main`, 4.2 MB | `App`, 1.39 MB (300 kB gzip) |
| JS loaded for `/` (Dashboard) | ~5.9 MB (main + shared chunk) | ~2.2 MB |
| JS loaded for `/source/:id` (App) | ~5.9 MB | ~4.7 MB |
| PWA precache cap | 6 MiB | **4 MiB** |

Other large chunks: `BaseMap` 1.21 MB, MapLibre worker 510 kB, `MeshCoreSourcePage` 420 kB, `SettingsContext` 402 kB.

### BASE_URL: relative chunk URLs (`renderBuiltUrl`)

With `base: '/'`, Vite's preload helper built dependency URLs as `"/" + dep`. That is a root-absolute `/assets/...` path. `htmlRewriter.ts` rewrites `/assets/` only inside HTML, and `staticServing.ts` serves `${BASE_URL}/assets` only. So under `BASE_URL=/meshmonitor`, a lazy route's CSS/JS preload would 404. The emoji-picker lazy load already had this latent bug.

`experimental.renderBuiltUrl` now returns `{ relative: true }` for JS-hosted URLs. Preload deps become `./App-x.js` and resolve with `new URL(dep, import.meta.url)`, and dynamic `import()`s are relative too. They all land under `/meshmonitor/assets/`. The production build has no root-absolute `"/assets/` strings left in any JS chunk; the only `/assets/` strings left are `/api/assets/...` API calls. HTML and CSS keep the default, and the server still rewrites the HTML.

### CSS: kept eager, in the original cascade order

Letting each lazy chunk bring its own CSS was not safe. The global sheets share class names, so the order they load in decides which rule wins:
- `.node-name` and `.export-menu` appear in `nodes.css` / `SecurityTab.css` / `RelayNodeModal.css`.
- `.detail-row` appears in `SecurityTab.css` and `PacketMonitorPanel.css`.

I measured the winning declaration for every selector against a baseline build from `origin/main`. Both per-chunk CSS and `cssCodeSplit: false` changed 24 winning values; for example, `.detail-row` flips from grid to flex. `cssCodeSplit: false` also pushes the app's `body` / `*` / `:root` rules into `embed.html`.

Instead, a small plugin in `vite.config.ts` (`meshmonitor-eager-css`) fills `src/eagerStyles.ts` with an import of every stylesheet the lazy pages reach. It uses the order the old a

title: fix(api): v1 message search reads MeshCore history from the database
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #5523 (#5517). The API-token search `GET /api/v1/sources/:sourceId/messages/search` still scanned the in-memory ring of *connected* MeshCore managers. Disconnected sources and older history were missed, and MeshCore access for non-admins was all-or-nothing.

- New `src/server/utils/messageSearch.ts` holds the search logic: `parseMessageSearchQuery` and `searchReadableMessages(user, sourceId, params)`. Both `GET /api/messages/search` (session) and the v1 route call it, so they can't drift.
  - Meshtastic rows: scoped in SQL per source and readable channel (`resolveReadableMeshtasticChannels`), including virtual channels the caller can read.
  - MeshCore rows: read from `meshcore_messages` through `MeshCoreRepository.searchMessages` and `resolveReadableMeshcoreScope`, whether or not the source is connected.
- v1 request/response shape is unchanged: `q`, `caseSensitive`, `scope`, `channels`, `fromNodeId`, `startDate`/`endDate` (epoch **ms**), `limit` (max 100), `offset`; response `{ success, count, total, data[] }` with `source: 'standard' | 'meshcore'` on each hit. `attachSource('messages','read')` still gates the source, and Bearer auth is unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/features/message-search.md` gave the v1 path as `/api/v1/messages/search`, which has returned 404 since 4.14 removed the root paths. It now reads `/api/v1/sources/{sourceId}/messages/search`.
- Unrelated CI fix: `messages.export.multiBackend.test.ts` hand-writes its DDL and lacks the `senderTimestamp` column #5525 added, so it fails on main. This PR adds the same 3 lines as #5527/#5528. The hunks are identical, so they merge cleanly whichever PR lands first.

## Tests

`src/server/routes/v1/messages.search.test.ts` is rewritten on `createRouteTestApp` with real API tokens (`tokenFor`), real permission SQL and real repositories. No manager is registered. Cases:
- MeshCore rows on a source with no connected manager are found (admin, and non-admin with `messages:read`).
- A token without `channel_2:read` doesn't see channel 2, even when it asks for it with `channels=2`.
- A source that wasn't granted gets a 403 (Meshtastic and MeshCore), and other sources' rows never leak into the results.
- Meshtastic behavior: ms dates, filters, case sensitivity, scope, paging, the 100 cap, virtual channels.

Against the old handler, 4 of these fail (MeshCore history ×2, channel hiding, virtual channel).

## Mesh impact

None. This change only reads the database. It sends no packets and adds no timers or notifications.

## Verification

- `tsc` clean for `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.server.json`
- `lint:ci`: no in-repo FAILs
- Full Vitest run with PG and MySQL containers up: 25,133 passed, 109 skipped. The 9 failures fail the same way on clean `origin/main` (cb4d1f90c):

title: fix(notifications): partial preference saves so the Notifications tab can't drop mutes
body:
## Problem

#5522 made mute saves per-source and had `SettingsContext` re-read the row before posting, so a mute save no longer clobbered Notifications-tab edits. The reverse was still open: the Notifications tab keeps its own copy of the whole preferences row, mutes included, and posts all of it on save. A channel/DM mute set from the Channels tab or the MeshCore channel view after the Notifications tab loaded was lost when the user saved there.

## Fix: partial updates

**`POST /api/push/preferences` now merges the posted fields onto the stored row.** Each writer sends only the fields it owns.

- Base row: the stored row for `(user, sourceId)`. A source with no row yet starts from what `GET` answers (the `''` row, then the legacy `push_prefs_<id>` blob, then the defaults).
- A MeshCore / MeshCore-MQTT / Reticulum source's first row does **not** inherit the `''` row's mute lists (keyed by Meshtastic channel number / node id), the same rule the client applied via `sourceFallback` in #5522. `GET` and its `sourceFallback` flag are unchanged.
- The own-row read now rethrows (`getUserPreferences(..., { rethrow: true })`), so a failed read fails the save with a 500. It never falls through to defaults and overwrites the user's settings.
- Validation checks only fields that are present. No field is required any more. A body with only half a waypoint centre is still rejected.
- Middleware is unchanged: `requireAuth()` + `requirePermission('messages', 'read', { sourceIdFrom: 'body' })`. The response stays `{ success: true }`, so no consumer changes.
- The defaults object now lives in one shared constant used by both GET and POST.

**Clients:**
- `NotificationsTab` save posts only the fields it edits (an explicit list), so no `mutedChannels`, `mutedDMs`, or `sourceFallback`. Its Apprise "Save config" posts only `appriseUrls`.
- `SettingsContext.saveMutePreferences` posts only the list it changes. It dropped the client-side read-modify-write: the server merge makes the read unneeded, so no path can post defaults after a failed read. On a failed save the optimistic toggle still reverts.

Every other caller of the endpoint was checked: these three are the only ones in `src/`.

## Unrelated fix included

`main` currently fails `messages.export.multiBackend.test.ts` ("MeshCore: keywords, channel/DM split and keyset paging") on all three backends. #5523's suite hand-writes `meshcore_messages` DDL, and #5525 added `senderTimestamp` to the schema. The separate first commit adds the column to the fixture DDL.

## Mesh impact checklist

No packets, notifications, or timers are added or changed. This only changes how a settings row is written.

## Tests

- `notificationRoutes.preferencesMerge.test.ts` (new, `createRouteTestApp` harness, real repository):
  - a settings save keeps stored mutes
  - a single-list mute save keeps the other list and all settings
  - a first row fills from the GET defaults
  - a new Meshtastic per-source row inherits the `''` row, mutes in

title: feat(translation): translation cache + stored translations for every viewer (#5520)
body:
Closes #5520. Follow-up to #5480.

A message translated once is reused, and every viewer who can read that message sees the stored translation, **including anonymous viewers, without any provider call**. Spec with implementation notes: `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSLATION_CACHE_SPEC.md`.

## Data (migration 186, all three backends)
- **`translation_cache`** (global, server-internal): keyed by a sha256 of a JSON-encoded `[normalize(text), targetLang, sourceLang]` tuple. The JSON encoding rather than a `\0` join closes off key collisions, since mesh text can contain NUL. **The source text is never stored**, only its hash.
- **`message_translations`** (per-source, `withSourceScope`): `(sourceId, messageId, targetLang) → cacheKey`. A phrase reused across many messages is translated and stored once.

## Expiry (maintainer decisions)
- An unpinned, unreferenced entry is pruned after **30 days without use**. Every hit refreshes `lastUsedAt`.
- Unpinned, unreferenced entries are also capped at **10,000 rows**, evicting the least recently used first.
- **Pinned:** an entry is pinned the first time **≥2 distinct messages** use it (`pinnedAt`, sticky). Pinned entries never expire and are exempt from the cap, even after those messages are purged ("Hi", "Welcome", "Good morning").
- **No entry is ever pruned while a message still references it.**
- Pruning runs at startup (+30 s) and then hourly. It only touches the DB.

## Write path
`POST /api/translate` takes optional `{ sourceId, messageId }`. When present:
- It loads the message and checks visibility with the **same** `resolveMessageReadAccess` / `canReadChannel` as `GET /api/messages`. A message that is hidden or missing returns 404 with **no provider call**.
- It translates **the stored message text and ignores any client `text`**, so nobody can attach a fake translation to someone else's message.
- It looks up the cache, then links the message.

Free-text and v1 translations **skip the cache entirely**. Otherwise a `cached` flag or the response timing would reveal whether a phrase was ever sent. Composer drafts never touch it either.

## Read path
`GET /api/translate/stored?sourceId&lang&messageIds` (≤200 ids):
- Returns stored translations only for messages the viewer can read, checked per message with the same visibility check.
- Hidden ids are omitted silently, so there's no way to probe whether a message exists.
- It **never calls a provider**. It returns 403 when translation is off or the viewer can't read the source.

## UI
`useViewTranslations` fetches stored translations for the visible messages in a single batched, cached request, in the viewer's language (saved preference, else browser, else server default). They show inline without a click for everyone. Anonymous viewers get no Translate, retry or language controls; they can only dismiss a translation.

## Lifecycle

title: feat(meshcore): resend channel messages no repeater echoed (#5512)
body:
Closes #5512

## What

A **Resend** button on our own MeshCore channel posts that no repeater was heard relaying. It sends the same packet again after a confirm dialog.

## Design

- **Same bytes, same wire timestamp.** MeshCore repeaters dedupe a flood by payload hash (`timestamp + "name: text"`, path excluded). The resend reuses the original `sender_timestamp` and text, so a repeater that relayed the first copy drops the resend, a repeater that missed it carries it, and recipients never see a duplicate.
- **Timestamp is stored.** New nullable column `meshcore_messages.senderTimestamp` (**migration 186**, SQLite `INTEGER`, PG/MySQL `BIGINT`). Outgoing channel sends write it, so resend survives a restart. Rows sent before the migration (and every received message) stay `NULL`; resend is refused (`RESEND_UNAVAILABLE`) and the button is hidden for them.
- **Manager:** `MeshCoreManager.resendChannelMessage(messageId)` runs inside `runSerialized`. It goes through `performScopedSend` with `isAutoRetry=true` (no new row, no `message` event, no data-bus emit, so no automation / notification / Virtual Node fan-out) and `autoRetryOnMiss=false` (never arms the #3979 auto-retry). It reuses the original row's `scopeName` as the region override. Refusals throw a typed `MeshCoreResendError`; receive-only throws the existing `TxDisabledError`.
- **Route:** `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/:messageId/resend`, same middleware as `/messages/send` (`messageLimiter`, `requireAuth`, `requirePermission('messages','write')`, `requireMeshcoreTx()`), `ok()` / `fail()` envelope:

  | Code | HTTP |
  |---|---|
  | `ALREADY_HEARD`, `RESEND_TOO_OLD`, `RESEND_UNAVAILABLE`, `AUTO_RETRY_PENDING`, `SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED`, `TX_DISABLED` | 409 |
  | `RESEND_LIMIT` | 429 |
  | `RESEND_COOLDOWN` (+ `retryAfterSeconds`) | 429 |
  | `NOT_CHANNEL_MESSAGE`, `NOT_OWN_MESSAGE`, `INVALID_INPUT` | 400 |
  | `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
  | `SEND_FAILED` | 502 |

- **Read paths** (`getChannelMessages`, the boot-time pool load, `getRecentMessages`) now carry `senderTimestamp`, `resendCount`, `lastResendAt` and a computed `autoRetryPending`, from one batched `message_events` query (`MessageEventsRepository.getEventsForMessages`). Live changes ride the existing `meshcore:message:updated` socket event.
- **UI:** `MeshCoreMessageStream` shows the button next to the heard-by badge, using a new `resend` `UiIcon` (lucide `Repeat2`), a CSS module, `en.json` strings and the shared in-page `Modal` for the confirm. The stream ticks every 5 s, and only while some message could still become (or stop being) resendable, so the 30 s gate and 1 h age limit update without a reload. Wired from `MeshCoreChannelsView` behind `canSend`, like delete; hidden while the composer is disabled (disconnected, no write permission, receive-only).

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Max manual resends per message | **3** |
| Cooldown after the send and after each resend | **30 s** |
| Max message age | **1 hour**

title: feat(messages): filtered CSV export + search fixes (#5517)
body:
Closes #5517

## Summary

Adds a filtered CSV export of stored messages (for event logs / after-action reports, e.g. the ARRL SET on Oct 3) and fixes four bugs in the existing message search.

### Export — `GET /api/messages/export`

- **Export** button on **Unified Messages** opens a dialog: sources, channels (by name, matched across sources like the channel picker), channel/DM type, keywords *contains any of* / *leave out*, date range (entered in browser local time, sent as UTC ms), sender, time zone for `local_time`, include reactions. Download goes through a new `ApiService.exportMessagesCsv()` (no raw `fetch` in components).
- Columns: `timestamp_utc, local_time, network, source, channel, sender_name, sender_id, destination, message, message_id, rssi, snr, hops`.
- CSV: UTF-8 BOM, CRLF, RFC 4180 quoting, formula-injection guard (leading `'` on text cells starting with `= + - @` tab CR; numbers never guarded).
- New repository methods `MessagesRepository.getMessagesForExport` and `MeshCoreRepository.getMessagesForExport` **require a `sourceId`**, filter in SQL (Drizzle, dialect-branched LIKE with `%`/`_` escaped via `ESCAPE '~'`), and page by keyset `(time, id)` in batches of 1000. The route merges the per-source streams oldest-first (k-way merge, one page per source in memory) and streams the response with backpressure.
- Meshtastic time = canonical message time (`rxTime` when plausible, else `timestamp`), the same rule as `canonicalMessageTime`, so a filter agrees with what the UI shows. Traceroute rows are always excluded (as in the unified feed). Hops = `hopStart - hopLimit`; MeshCore uses its stored `hopCount`.

### Search fixes (`GET /api/messages/search`)

1. **Date units.** `SearchModal` sent epoch **seconds**; the repository compares ms, so any date filter matched nothing. The modal now sends local-day bounds in ms. (The start date was also parsed as UTC midnight while the end was local; both are local now.)
2. **Source scoping.** `searchMessages` had no source filter; the route trimmed by source *after* paging (short pages, wrong totals). Worse, the trim compared `m.sourceId`, which `convertRepoMessage` drops, so `?sourceId=` returned nothing at all. Search now takes per-source channel scopes in SQL, and hits keep their `sourceId`. The per-source page (`App.tsx`) passes its `sourceId`. The v1 route pushes its source down the same way.
3. **Virtual channels.** The route only granted `channel_0..7` and `-1`; Channel Database channels (`>= CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET`) were never searchable for non-admins. Access now comes from `resolveMessageReadAccess` (the `GET /api/messages` rule), including per-entry `canRead`.
4. **MeshCore.** Search scanned the in-memory ring (last 1000) of *connected* managers only. It now queries `meshcore_messages`, scoped per source and channel, connected or not.

Also: keyword LIKE now escapes `%`/`_` (shared `BaseRepository.textContains`).

## Defaults chosen (maintainer can change)

| Decision | Default |
|---|---|

title: feat(notifications): per-source channel mute fix + MeshCore channel mute (#5487)
body:
Closes #5487

## Summary

Two commits:

1. **fix(notifications): save and read channel/DM mutes per source.** Fixes the bug where Channels-tab mutes stopped blocking push/Apprise.
2. **feat(meshcore): mute a MeshCore channel.** Adds the feature the issue asks for.

## The bug

`SettingsContext` loaded and saved mutes through `/api/push/preferences` with **no sourceId**, so every mute landed on the user's `''` (default) row of `user_notification_preferences`. Readers disagreed about which row to trust:

| Reader | Row it read |
|---|---|
| Push / Apprise / desktop (`shouldFilterNotificationAsync`) | per-source row, falling back to `''` only when the source has **no** row |
| `/unread-counts`, `/unread-by-source` | `''` row, always |
| Channels-tab UI | `''` row |

Once a user saved per-source notification settings (which creates the per-source row), every mute set afterwards still showed in the UI and hid the badge, but **no longer blocked push or Apprise**. Bare channel numbers on the `''` row also muted that channel number on every source without its own row.

### Fix
- `SettingsContext` loads and saves mutes with the active `sourceId` and reloads when the source changes. Before each save it re-reads the row, so a mute save cannot revert Notifications-tab changes, and saving the channel list cannot overwrite the DM list from stale client state (or the other way round).
- `GET /api/push/preferences?sourceId=` now returns `sourceFallback: true` when the `''` row answered because the source has no row of its own. Non-Meshtastic views (MeshCore, Reticulum) ignore those Meshtastic-keyed mutes, so Meshtastic channel 1's mute never shows up as MeshCore channel 1's.
- `/unread-counts` and `/unread-by-source` read mutes from the same row as push filtering (shared `loadActiveMutes(userId, sourceId)`), per source inside the `/unread-by-source` loop.

## Migration 186 — `merge_default_row_mutes_into_source_rows`

Data-only, all three backends, idempotent, `settingsKey: migration_186_merge_default_row_mutes_into_source_rows`. For each user whose `''` row holds active mutes:

- Each of that user's **existing** per-source rows gets the `''` row's **active** mutes merged in: union by key (`channelId` / `nodeUuid`), and when both rows mute the same key the later `muteUntil` wins (`null` = indefinite beats any timestamp). The channel and DM lists merge separately, so neither overwrites the other.
- Expired `''` mutes are not copied. Mutes already on a per-source row are never dropped or shortened.
- **MeshCore / MeshCore-MQTT / Reticulum rows are skipped.** The `''` mutes came from the Meshtastic Channels tab and are keyed by Meshtastic channel number.
- **No rows are created.** A source with no row of its own still reads the `''` row through the existing fallback, so its mutes already apply. Creating rows would also freeze a copy of the `''` row's other settings onto every source.
- The `''` row is left untouched; it stays the fallback for row-less sources and c

title: fix(map): vector basemaps crash with node clustering (#5516)
body:
Closes #5516

## Root cause

The crash comes from vector basemaps plus node clustering, not from custom tilesets missing `maxZoom` (the server already requires it on save).

- `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-leaflet` extends plain `L.Layer`, not `GridLayer`. Only `GridLayer` registers itself in Leaflet's zoom-limit table (`map._addZoomLimit` in `beforeAdd`). `VectorTileLayer` wrote `maxzoom` into the MapLibre style only, so with any vector basemap `map.getMaxZoom()` was `Infinity`.
- `NodeMarkerCluster` (leaflet.markercluster, Nodes map) reads `getMaxZoom()` on mount and throws the **string** `"Map has no maxZoom specified"`.
- `ErrorBoundary` rendered `error.message`, which a string lacks, so the user saw a blank error box.

**The bundled CARTO vector presets were affected too** (`cartoVoyager`, `cartoPositron`, `cartoDarkMatter`, `cartoVoyagerDark`): they render through the same `VectorTileLayer`, so any user who picked one with clustering on hit the same crash. A regression test covers `cartoVoyager`.

## Changes

- `src/components/VectorTileLayer.tsx`: pass `maxZoom` to `L.maplibreGL`, and register the layer with `map._addZoomLimit` after `addTo` (removed with `_removeZoomLimit` on cleanup), the way `GridLayer` does. No `minZoom` is passed: the adapter forwards options to `maplibregl.Map`, which runs one zoom level below Leaflet, so a floor of 0 there would clamp the GL canvas at Leaflet zoom 0 (MapLibre's own floor is -2).
- `src/components/map/ZoomCeilingBackstop.tsx` (new), mounted in `BaseMap` before `children`: if no layer gave the map a finite ceiling, set the tileset's `maxZoom`; hand control back on tileset change. I chose this over a `maxZoom` prop on `MapContainer`: that prop is read once at mount and, as a map option, beats every layer bound, so switching to a tileset with a lower cap (e.g. OpenTopo, 17) would keep the stale ceiling.
- `src/config/tilesets.ts`: `normalizeCustomMaxZoom()` clamps custom tileset `maxZoom` to a finite 1–22 (18 when missing/NaN/non-numeric) in `getTilesetById` and `getAllTilesets`. Presets untouched.
- `src/components/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx`: show `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)`.

## Mesh impact

None: client-side map rendering only, no packets, notifications, or timers.

## Tests

- `src/components/map/BaseMap.vectorMaxZoom.test.tsx` (new): real Leaflet, react-leaflet and leaflet.markercluster, with only the MapLibre adapter faked as a plain `L.Layer`. Covers a custom vector tileset (ceiling 16), a broken `maxZoom` (falls back to 18), a CARTO vector preset (19), vector→raster→vector switches (16→17→19), and the backstop on its own. With the fix reverted, 4 of these fail with the exact `Map has no maxZoom specified` error.
- `VectorTileLayer.test.tsx`: `maxZoom` reaches `L.maplibreGL`, no `minZoom`, zoom limit registered and removed.
- `tilesets.test.ts`: clamp/default/rounding for `getTilesetById` and `getAllTilesets`.
- `ErrorBoundary.test.tsx` (new): renders a thrown `Error` and a t

title: feat(reports): Traceroute Explorer report card (#5511)
body:
Closes #5511.

Adds a **Traceroute Explorer** card to Analysis & Reports. It lists every stored traceroute across the sources the user can read, on a linked map and table. Design: https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/issues/5511#issuecomment-5932614735

## Screenshots

Map + Table, one run selected (map zooms to it; forward and return legs drawn):

![split](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5511-traceroute-explorer/docs/public/images/features/5511-traceroute-explorer-split.png)

Full screen with the map collapsed to a rail:

![fullscreen table](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5511-traceroute-explorer/docs/public/images/features/5511-traceroute-explorer-fullscreen-table.png)

## What's in it

**Backend:** `GET /api/traceroutes/explorer?hours=&sources=`
- New repo method `getTraceroutesForSources` (explicit source list, newest first, `since` + `limit`). Empty list returns nothing, never all sources.
- Source set = caller's `traceroute:read` sources (`resolvePermittedSourceIds`), narrowed by `sources`. Node names/positions also need `nodes:read` on that source; without it, runs show hex ids.
- Runs are channel-masked per source (`maskTraceroutesByChannel`).
- One merged node entry per node the runs mention (`mergeExplorerNodes`). Names come only from permitted sources. Positions come only from rows the caller can see on the map (`filterNodesByChannelPermission` + `maskNodeLocationByChannel`), with sign-flip correction, and Null Island is dropped.
- Scan cap 20,000 stored rows (queried as cap + 1); the response flags `truncated`. A busy multi-source install stores ~5 rows per traceroute, so 5,000 rows didn't cover 24h. Also returns `retentionPerPair` (`TRACEROUTE_HISTORY_LIMIT`).

**Frontend:** `src/components/Analysis/tracerouteExplorer/`
- `explorerModel.ts` holds pure logic:
  - parse legs with per-hop SNR, reusing `buildLegHopLinks`
  - merge one packet stored by several sources into a single run
  - **Route changed** / **Asymmetric** flags
  - filters, group-by-pair, link usage, path variants, summary
- Layout: **Table | Map + Table | Map**, saved in localStorage.
  - Draggable divider (also keyboard), stacks on phones.
  - **Collapse map** leaves a "Show map" rail.
  - **Full screen** pins the workspace to the viewport; Esc exits.
- Map: `BaseMap` + link-usage polylines (width = hops carried; optional median-SNR colouring). Hovered or selected run drawn through `TraceroutePathsLayer`. Clicking a node filters the table; "Filter table by map selection" turns that off.
- Table: group by pair (answer rate, recent-result strip, "N paths seen", median hops) or every run; both page 200 rows at a time. Source column shows "Name +N" with the full list on hover. Selecting a run zooms the map to it.
- Detail drawer reuses `TracerouteStrip`, `TracerouteCopyLinks`, `TracerouteHistoryModal`, plus a path-variant breakdown.
- New `maximize` / `minimize` UiIcons; 79 `en.json` keys.

**Docs:** `docs/featur

@@ -0,0 +1,138 @@
+# Traceroute Explorer
+
+The Traceroute Explorer lists every traceroute MeshMonitor has stored, across
+every source you can read, on a linked map and table. Use it to audit how
+traffic actually moves through your mesh without opening each node's
+traceroute history one at a time.
+
+Open it from **Analysis & Reports** (`/reports`) → **Traceroute Explorer**.
+
+![Traceroute Explorer in Map + Table layout, with one run selected](/images/features/5511-traceroute-explorer-split.png)
+
+## MeshMonitor sends nothing
+
+**This report sends zero packets.** It only reads traceroutes already in the
+database: ones you or the auto-traceroute scheduler requested, and ones your
+sources overheard. It has no "run traceroute" button.
+
+## What you see
+
+### Filters
+
+| Filter | What it does |
+|--------|--------------|
+| Time range | 6h, 24h (default), 7d, or everything stored. Changing it reloads the data. |
+| Source | One source, or all sources you can read. |
+| Result | All runs, only **Answered** runs, or only runs with **No response**. |
+| Transport | RF, MQTT and UDP, by the transport that carried the traceroute response. |
+| Node | Name, short name or `!id`. Matches a node at either end of a run or anywhere on its path. |
+| Max hops | Hide answered runs with more relays than this on the forward path. |
+
+Every filter except the time range runs in your browser, so the map and table
+update at once.
+
+### Summary bar
+
+Traceroutes, node pairs, the share that got an answer, median relay count,
+and how many runs took a different forward path from the pair's previous
+answered run.
+
+### Layout
+
+Pick **Table**, **Map + Table** (default) or **Map**. The choice is saved in
+your browser.
+
+- In **Map + Table**, drag the divider (or focus it and use the arrow keys)
+  to resize the panes. On a phone the map stacks above the table.
+- **Collapse map** shrinks the map to a thin rail so the table gets the full
+  width. **Show map** on the rail brings it back.
+- **Full screen** fills the browser window with the map and table. Press
+  **Esc** or **Exit full screen** to go back.
+
+![Full screen with the map collapsed to a rail](/images/features/5511-traceroute-explorer-fullscreen-table.png)
+
+### Table
+
+- **Group by pair** (default) shows one row per origin → destination pair:
+  when it last ran, its latest forward path with the SNR at each hop, a strip
+  of recent results (green answered, red no response), median relays, and the
+  answer rate. A **paths seen** tag means the pair has used more than one
+  route. Click a pair to list its runs.
+- **Every run** lists runs one per row, 200 at a time.
+
+Runs carry tags for their transport, **Route changed** (the forward path
+differs from the pair's previous answered run) and **Asymmetric** (the return
+path is not the forward path reversed).
+
+SNR colours: green at 0 dB or better, amber from −7 to 0 dB, red below
+−7 dB, grey when the hop reported no SNR (often an MQTT or UDP hop).
+
+When two of your sources stored the same traceroute (same packet), it shows
+once, listing both sources.
+
+### Map
+
+- With nothing selected, the map draws every node-to-node link the filtered
+  runs used. Thicker lines carried more traceroute hops. **Link SNR** recolours
+  the lines by the median SNR measured on each link.
+- Hover a run in the table to preview it on the map; click to pin it. The
+  forward path and return path draw in different colours with arrows.
+- Click a node to show only runs through that node; a **Through …** chip
+  appears under the filters. Untick **Filter table by map selection** to keep
+  the table unfiltered while you click around the map.
+
+Nodes appear only where you are allowed to see their position. A node whose
+position is on a channel you cannot view keeps its name in the table but has
+no marker.
+
+### Detail drawer
+
+Selecting a run shows its hop-by-hop strip, copy links for the forward and
+return paths, a **Pair history** button that opens the full stored history for
+that pair, and a bar chart of every forward path the pair has used in the
+loaded window.
+
+## Limits
+
+- **Retention:** MeshMonitor keeps the newest `TRACEROUTE_HISTORY_LIMIT` runs
+  per node pair (default 50) and prunes old traceroutes by age, so busy pairs
+  thin out over time. The summary bar shows the current limit.
+- **Window size:** one load reads at most 20,000 stored rows, newest first.
+  A traceroute that several sources stored counts once per source, so on a
+  busy multi-source install that is a few days. If a window holds more, a
+  banner says so; pick a shorter time range.
+- **Meshtastic only:** MeshCore path discovery does not store traceroutes in
+  this table.
+
+## Permissions
+
+`GET /api/traceroutes/explorer` scopes everything to the sources where you
+hold `traceroute:read` (admins see every enabled source):
+
+- Runs on a channel you cannot view on the map are left out, the same rule the
+  per-source traceroute views apply.
+- Node names and positions also need `nodes:read` on that source. With
+  `traceroute:read` alone you see the runs, labelled by node id.
+- Node positions come only from node rows you can see on the map.
+- A caller with no grants gets an empty list, not an error.
+
+## API
+
+`GET /api/traceroutes/explorer?hours=24&sources=id1,id2`
+
+| Param | Meaning |
+|-------|---------|
+| `hours` | Optional window, 1 to 8760. Omit for everything stored. |
+| `sources` | Optional comma-separated source ids, intersected with the ones you can read. |
+
+Response (`{ success: true, data }`):
+
+- `sources`: `[{ id, name }]` searched.
+- `runs`: newest first; each has `id`, `sourceId`, `timestamp`, `fromNodeNum`,
+  `toNodeNum`, the stored `route`/`routeBack`/`snrTowards`/`snrBack` JSON
+  strings (SNR in raw dB × 4), `channel`, `packetId` and `transportMechanism`.
+- `nodes`: one entry per node the runs mention: `nodeNum`, `nodeId`,
+  `shortName`, `longName`, `role`, `hwModel`, `latitude`, `longitude`.
+- `truncated`, `scanLimit` (20000 stored rows), `retentionPerPair`.
+
+Errors: `INVALID_HOURS` (400), `TRACEROUTE_EXPLORER_FAILED` (500).

title: feat(meshcore): show auto-add state, push contacts to the radio, explain the mismatch (#5502)
body:
Closes #5502

MeshCore companions keep their own contact table, separate from MeshMonitor's node list, and can only log in to, poll or message nodes in it. With `manual_add_contacts` on, nodes heard via advert never reach that table, and users saw logins refused (the #5351 guard) with no explanation.

## What's new: a "Radio contact list" section in MeshCore Settings (companion sources)
**Auto-add contacts: On / Off, with a toggle.**
- Writes bit 0 of `NodePrefs.manual_add_contacts`.
- meshcore.js's `setOtherParams` would collapse the byte to 0/1 and wipe the per-type auto-add bits. So a new `set_auto_add_contacts` command reads a fresh SelfInfo and rebuilds the opcode-38 frame, flipping only bit 0 and keeping the telemetry modes and advLocPolicy.
- Route: `POST /config/auto-add-contacts` (`configuration:write`).

**Missing-favourites banner.**
- Shows "N favourite(s) are not in the radio's contact list" from `GET /contacts/device-sync` (`nodes:read`, memory/DB only).
- When auto-add is off, it adds the explanation from the issue.
- The server startup warning also mentions auto-add when it's off.

**Push to radio:** `POST /contacts/push-to-device` (`nodes:write`).
- **Order (maintainer's choice):** favourites first, then the most recently heard nodes.
- **Room:** fills **free slots only and never evicts**; it never uses the confirm-full path. Room is re-checked after each batch, and it stops on a table-full refusal or any eviction.
- **Skips:** the local node, unknown advType and ignored/blocked nodes (#5408), each with a reason.
- **Unknown capacity:** favourites only.
- **One at a time:** one push per source; a second request gets 409.
- **Speed:** batched `add_contacts` reads the table twice per batch rather than per contact.
- **Timeout:** the route has `extendRequestTimeout(300 s)` (#5494) and a pin-test entry.
- **Result:** the summary lists added, already on the radio, no free slot, skipped by reason, and free slots before/after. When the radio is full, it points to the existing per-node **Add to radio** (#5349), which replaces the oldest non-favourite after the user confirms.

**Node Details:** the per-node "not in the radio's contact list" notice now points to this section.

**Docs:** a "Radio contact table vs MeshMonitor" section and a troubleshooting entry in `docs/features/meshcore.md`.

## Found and fixed during browser validation
- **False "missing" favourites:** the radio's `get_contacts` can time out after a reconnect (the list is then seeded from the DB and `onDevice` is unknown), and every favourite read as missing. The status now reports `deviceContactsKnown`; until the table is read, Settings says the list hasn't been read yet instead of showing a false count.
- **Full radio:** the summary was accurate but gave no next step; it now does.

## Mesh impact
None on RF. Auto-add and the push are serial-link writes to the local companion; nothing is transmitted.

- **MC-Sandbox:** the aut

title: feat(meshcore): favorite a node from Node Details (#5507)
body:
Closes #5507

## Change
A favorite star in the MeshCore **Contact Details** panel header, next to the collapse toggle.

- **Same action as the Nodes list star:** it reuses `actions.setNodeFavorite` (`POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/nodes/:publicKey/favorite`), including the #4840 best-effort push of the device's ContactInfo favorite bit. The list, map and this panel always agree, and no new route was added.
- **Permissions:** shown only with `nodes:write` (the same `canWriteNodes` gate as the panel's other actions). It isn't limited to companion sources: favorites apply to every role (#3588), and the device push is already companion-only on the server.
- **Feedback:** the star shows the server-confirmed state immediately. The `isFavorite` prop only updates when the node list refetches, a few seconds later; without this, the star looked like the click hadn't registered (seen in the browser check). A failure keeps the old state and shows an inline error.
- **Accessibility:** `UiIcon` filled/outline star, `aria-pressed`, and "Add to favorites" / "Remove from favorites" labels. Styles are in a CSS module.

## Mesh impact
None. The favorite is a server-side flag plus a serial-link write to the local companion's contact table. Nothing goes on air.

## Tests
- `MeshCoreContactDetailPanel.favorite.test.tsx`: renders both states; toggles in both directions with the right key; shows the new state as soon as the server confirms; a failure shows the error and keeps the old state; hidden without write permission or a handler.
- Panel suites: 52 passed. `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean.

## Browser validation (dev container, MC-Sandbox)

title: feat(meshcore): Discover Path countdown and response / no-response feedback (#5508)
body:
Closes #5508

## Problem
Discover Path resolved as soon as the device acked the flood (`Sent`), with no sign of whether the target ever replied. Users couldn't tell a discovery that worked from one that failed.

## Fix (matches MeshCore One)
- **Firmware timeout hint:** the native backend now returns `suggested_timeout_ms` from the `Sent` ack (bytes 6–9; meshcore.js already decodes it as `estTimeout`).
- **Wait budget:** `meshcorePathDiscoveryTimeoutMs()` (`src/server/constants/meshcorePathDiscovery.ts`) uses MC1's formula: no hint → 30 s; otherwise `hint/1000 × 1.2 + 8 s`, clamped to [5 s, 60 s]; final `max(20 s, …)`. The route returns it as `discoveryTimeoutMs`.
- **Button states:**
  1. Idle: **Discover Path**
  2. Sending: **Discovering…**
  3. Waiting: **Discovering… 23s**, counting down
  4. Reply: **Path updated — Direct / N hops**
  5. Expiry: **No response from <name>**
  
  Contact switches and unmounts clear the timers, and the panel's stale-reply guard drops a reply for a contact the user has left.
- **Detecting a reply:** the server stamps `pathDiscoveredAt` on the contact when a 0x8D path-discovery response arrives, so a reply counts even when it returns the **same** path. An `outPath`/`pathLen` change also counts. A code comment notes the remaining gap: if an identical-path reply arrives only through a full contact re-read, the stamp can be lost.
- **Route envelope:** the route now uses `ok()`/`fail()` (`INVALID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `DISCOVER_PATH_FAILED`). Its only consumer, `useMeshCore.discoverContactPath`, was updated to match. Auto-pathfinding only checks that the result is truthy, so it's unaffected. No shell system tests call this endpoint.

## Mesh impact
UI only. The countdown changes only the display. **No retransmits:** MC1's retransmit-during-budget is out of scope because it would add RF traffic.

## Tests
- Timeout helper (30 s default, 20 s floor, 60 s cap, mid-range formula).
- Backend: a real `Sent` frame parsed through meshcore.js.
- Route tests via `createRouteTestApp`.
- Component tests with fake timers: countdown, success, expiry, contact-switch cleanup.
- Full suite: 23,517 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` (server and frontend) and `lint:ci` clean.

## Browser validation (dev container, MC-Sandbox)
- **TRPK TRON V4** (repeater, path unknown): the firmware hint was 2.7 s, so the 20 s floor applied. The countdown ran 20 → 0 and ended in **No response from TRPK TRON V4**.
- **YerazeMM** (local companion): the reply arrived about 1.5 s after the click and showed **Path updated — Direct**. The path didn't change, so the `pathDiscoveredAt` stamp is what detected it.

![no response](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5508-discover-path-feedback/docs/public/images/features/5508-no-response.png)
![path updated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5508-discover-path-feedback/docs/public/images/features/5508-path-updated.png)

Note: #5507 also edits `MeshCoreContactDetailPanel.tsx`. Whichever

title: feat(meshcore): populate a repeater source's Nodes and Packet Monitor from its serial CLI (#5500)
body:
Closes #5500.

## What a stock repeater can report (verified: MeshCore main a366955 = repeater-v1.17.1)
- **Nodes:** only its `neighbors` table, which holds zero-hop **repeater** adverts. The reply is 8-hex key prefixes with age and SNR×4, about 6–7 entries (it is truncated at ~134 chars), and no names or positions. A repeater stores no companions, rooms or sensors, so for those an empty list is the truthful result.
- **Packets:** stock release builds stream nothing over serial. Live packet lines (`RAW:` hex + `RX` summary) exist only on builds with `-D MESH_PACKET_LOGGING=1`, which is commented out in every release env.

## Maintainer decisions
- **Packet Monitor:** support custom `MESH_PACKET_LOGGING` builds, and show an explanatory notice on stock firmware. The tab stays.
- **Nodes:** resolve each prefix to a full key known from any source; skip unknown or ambiguous prefixes (no prefix stubs).
- **Poll interval:** 5 minutes.

## Changes
**Serial CLI plumbing** (`meshcoreManager.ts`, new `utils/meshcoreRepeaterSerial.ts`)
- **Command queue:** every `sendRepeaterCommand` caller now runs one at a time. Before, concurrent callers (the refresh, advert, the admin console, `setName`/`setRadio`/`setTxPower`) shared one line stream and could steal each other's reply lines. A failed command does not block the queue.
- **Line filter:** `RAW:`, `RX`/`TX` log lines and `DEBUG:` lines are classified before reply matching, so they can never corrupt a command reply.
- `get public.key` is read on refresh. The real key is kept in `repeaterPublicKey`; the `'repeater'` placeholder stays, because about 20 files read the local node key.

**Nodes**
- A poller runs only on Repeater sources and only while connected. It sends only `neighbors`, a local serial command with zero airtime.
  - First poll 30 s after connect. A reconnect waits the longer of 30 s or the rest of the interval, so a flapping link can't burst.
  - It skips a tick if any CLI command is already in flight.
- Each prefix is resolved against `meshcore_nodes` from any source via the new `findNodesByPublicKeyPrefix` (hex-only input, case-insensitive). A unique match is upserted into this source with name, type and position copied, `snr = raw/4`, and `lastHeard = now − secs_ago`.
- Neighbour-graph rows are stored with the repeater's real key as the reporter.
- A possibly-truncated reply is merged rather than replacing the set.
- Fixes an existing bug: `parseMeshcoreNeighbors` dropped the first neighbour, because the firmware prefixes only the first line with `->`.
- The `neighbors` read ends after a 300 ms gap in serial output, instead of always waiting 5 s.

**Packet Monitor**
- On a logging build, a `RAW:` line waits up to 250 ms for its `RX` line. It takes SNR/RSSI only when the `len` matches, then goes through `parseObserverFrame` → `handleOtaPacket`, under the existing packet-log enable.
- Not re-emitted to the Virtual Node, Coverage or Observer feeds.

**UI**
- On a Repeater source, the empty Nodes

Firmware 2.8.1 reports whether the ack for a DM carries a valid proof from the recipient's key; MeshMonitor shows "Proven receipt" (valid), a warning when a proof fails ("this ack may be forged"), or a muted "Receipt not proven". On multi-hop paths a genuine receipt often reads "not proven", so that is never shown as a failure. Packet Monitor shows the raw value. Display only; migration 184. (#5279, #5489)

MeshMonitor now stores each channel's `use_aead` flag and sends it back on every channel write (edits, reorder, URLs, import/export, backup/restore, Virtual Node), so a MeshMonitor edit can no longer turn AEAD off. A read-only **AEAD** badge shows on the channel. Decrypting AEAD traffic and an editable setting come in Phase 2, after a 2.8.1 build ships. Migration 185. (#5248, #5492)
+- **Broadcast a waypoint from the Automation Engine** (`action.broadcastWaypoint`), with source, key, position, name, icon, expiry, channel, hop limit and "only send when changed". Every waypoint also gets an optional hop limit, set in the waypoint editor with an airtime warning. Migration 183. (#5482, #5484)
+- **MeshCore Trace Path: Auto return path**, on by default. The trace now reaches the target and comes back: repeaters and room servers are traced out and back through themselves, and companions turn at the last repeater. It falls back to one-way past the firmware's 63-hop limit. (#5485, #5490)
+- **Pin sidebar on MeshCore sources**, sharing one pin setting with Meshtastic. The MeshCore nav now follows the same rules: it starts expanded when pinned and collapses after a nav click when unpinned. (#5481, #5483)
+- **MeshCore Repeaters get their own map glyph**, a mesh relay, so they no longer look identical to a Meshtastic ROUTER on the Unified map. Meshtastic ROUTER / ROUTER_LATE / REPEATER keep the tower. Applies to 2D, 3D, legends and the traceroute strip. (#5491, #5501)
+
+### Changed
+- **Waypoints and data requests use the node's configured hop limit.** Waypoint sends used a fixed 3 hops; position, NodeInfo and telemetry requests used 3; NeighborInfo requests used 7. All now use the node's own LoRa hop limit, and a per-waypoint hop limit can only shorten it. On a node set above 3, these packets now reach further; NeighborInfo requests stop flooding to 7 hops. (#5484, #5488)
+- **Slow API requests get a `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` reply** instead of a silently dropped socket. Browsers resend a request whose connection closes with no reply, POSTs included, so a slow request re-ran on every resend (one Trace Path click put a trace on air every 30 s; a slow reboot request could reboot the node again). The handler still finishes in the background, and known-slow routes get a longer timeout. (#5494)

+
+### Fixed
+- **Web Push per source.** Subscribing on one source made every source show "Subscribed", and Unsubscribe on any source removed the browser from every source. Status and Unsubscribe are now per source, the browser subscription is only dropped when no source still uses it, and a new "Unsubscribe from all sources" button covers the silence-everything case. (#5493, #5495)
+- **MeshCore repeater Configuration** showed TX power 0, position 0,0 and preset "Custom". MeshMonitor now reads `get tx`, `get lat` and `get lon`, and matches presets within 0.001 MHz, since repeaters report frequencies like 869.6179809. (#5496, #5497)
+- **Telemetry range selector** vanished when the chosen window had no data, leaving no way to widen it again. (#5498, #5499)

body:
Closes #5491 (Option B, chosen by the maintainer: distinct glyphs everywhere).

## Problem
On the Unified map, a Meshtastic ROUTER and a MeshCore Repeater were **identical**, not just similar. `DashboardMap` draws every node, MeshCore included, as a `variant: 'meshtastic'` pin, and `categoryGlyphFamily()` mapped Meshtastic `mtRouter` / `mtRouterLate` / `mtRepeater` onto MeshCore's `'repeater'` family. So both got the same tower badge.

## Change
- New glyph family **`'router'`** (`GlyphFamily = MeshCoreCategory | 'router'`). Meshtastic ROUTER, ROUTER_LATE and REPEATER use it, drawn with the **existing tower, unchanged**. ROUTER_LATE keeps its clock badge.
- A **MeshCore Repeater** draws a new **mesh-relay** glyph: one hub linked to three peers, wide and round where the tower is tall and thin.
- Room Server, Sensor and Companion are unchanged.
- It applies everywhere the role glyph renders: 2D pins and corner badges, the MeshCore map, both legends, the traceroute strip, and the 3D map.
- The **3D map** keys its rasterized icons by glyph *family*. Rendering it through `roleGlyphMarkerSvg(family as NodeTypeCategory)` would have given Meshtastic routers the new MeshCore glyph in 3D. It now uses a new `glyphFamilyMarkerSvg()`, and a test asserts that 2D and 3D produce identical markup for every category.

## Screenshots

title: fix(meshcore): show a repeater's TX power, position and preset (#5496)
body:
Closes #5496

## Problem
For a MeshCore **repeater** source, the Configuration page showed TX power 0, lat/lon 0 and preset "Custom", while frequency/BW/SF/CR were right.

## Causes and fixes
**1. Fields never read.** `refreshLocalNode()`'s repeater branch sent only `get name` and `get radio`. It now also sends `get tx`, `get lat` and `get lon`. These are the command names in the firmware's `CommonCLI.cpp`, each replying `> <value>`; the issue's suggested `get tx_power` doesn't exist. A new `parseRepeaterNumber()` reads the value. A missing or error reply (older firmware, "unknown config") leaves the field **unknown** rather than 0.

**2. Preset never matched.** The firmware has no preset command; the page derives the preset from the radio values via `findPresetId`, which compared with `===`. The repeater reports `869.6179809` for the 869.618 MHz preset, so it always fell through to "Custom". Frequency and bandwidth now match within 0.001; the closest two preset frequencies are 0.093 MHz apart, so no false matches. This also helps companions that report float frequencies.

## Adverts
The issue's "advert buttons do nothing" turned out to be a red herring: adverts were sending fine (confirmed by the maintainer). The only bug was the parsing above.

## Mesh impact
None. The three extra CLI reads go over the serial link to the local repeater only, once per refresh.

## Tests
- `meshcoreManager.repeaterLocalNode.test.ts`: the reporter's device replies populate TX power, lat/lon and radio; missing replies stay unknown; `parseRepeaterNumber` handles ints, negative floats, errors and empty replies.
- `radioPresets.test.ts`: `869.6179809` resolves to `eu-uk-narrow`, and a neighbouring frequency still reads "Custom".
- Full suite: 23,393 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` (server and frontend) and `lint:ci` clean.

No UI change, so no screenshot. Hardware validation needs a serial-attached repeater, which the rig doesn't have.

title: fix(push): scope Web Push subscribe state and unsubscribe to the source (#5493)
body:
Closes #5493.

## Summary
A browser has **one** Web Push endpoint per origin, shared by every source it subscribes on. Two paths ignored that:
1. **Status:** each source's panel read only `pushManager.getSubscription()`, so subscribing on one source made every source show "Subscribed".
2. **Unsubscribe:** the client first called `subscription.unsubscribe()`, killing the browser endpoint for every source. Then `/api/push/unsubscribe` validated `sourceId`, ignored it, and deleted every source's row for the endpoint.

Broadcast was already source-scoped; the schema has had a `(userId, endpoint, sourceId)` unique index since migration 028.

## Fix
**Server**
- `removeSubscription(endpoint, sourceId?)`: with a `sourceId` it deletes only that source's rows. Without one it deletes all rows, which the expired-endpoint cleanup (404/410/other 4xx) still uses on purpose, because the endpoint itself is dead. New `getSubscriptionSourceIds(endpoint)`.
- `POST /api/push/unsubscribe` removes only `(endpoint, sourceId)` and returns `{ success, remainingSources }`.
- **New** `POST /api/push/subscription-status` `{ endpoint, sourceId }` returns `{ success, subscribed, otherSources }`. It uses the same auth and permission as subscribe, and is a POST so the endpoint URL stays out of logs.
- **New** `POST /api/push/unsubscribe-all` `{ endpoint }` returns `{ success, removed }`. Holding the endpoint is the ownership proof, and the only effect is stopping pushes to the caller's own browser.
- Counts only, never source ids, so nothing leaks about sources the user can't read. Responses stay flat because `ApiService` doesn't unwrap `data`; errors use `fail()`.

**Client (`NotificationsTab`, shared by Meshtastic and MeshCore sources)**
- Status comes from the server for the current source, and re-checks on source switch with a guard against a late reply for the old source. Falls back to the browser check if the request fails.
- Unsubscribe calls the server first, and only calls `subscription.unsubscribe()` when `remainingSources === 0`.
- Subscribe reuses the existing browser subscription.
- **New:** an "Unsubscribe from all sources" button (with a confirm dialog) and an "Also subscribed on N other source(s)" line. This is the reporter's "silence all" ask.
- With no source selected (legacy/unified view), Unsubscribe acts as unsubscribe-all, since there is no per-source row to target.

## Testing
- Repository: 3 new tests on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL (9 passes).
- Routes (`createRouteTestApp` harness): 7 tests, including a 403 on a source the user can't read.
- Service: expired-endpoint cleanup still removes all rows for 404/410/400/403, and keeps them for 413/429/500.
- Component: 9 tests. Status comes from the server per source; unsubscribe does not kill the browser subscription while other sources remain, and does when none remain; unsubscribe-all does both.
- Full Vitest suite with PG/MySQL up: `success: true`, 24,603 passed, 0 failed. Both `tsc` configs clean; `npm r

title: fix(http): stop browsers resending slow requests (RF re-transmits every 30 s)
body:
## Problem
`server.setTimeout(30000)` destroyed the socket of any request still running at 30 s **without sending a response**. Browsers treat a connection closed with no reply as a network error and **silently resend the request, POSTs included**. Every resend re-runs the handler. Found live while validating #5490: one click on MeshCore Trace Path put a trace on air every 30 s (9 in ~4 min) until the page was closed.

An audit found ~25 routes that can run past 30 s. Many transmit on RF. The worst:
- `POST /api/admin/reboot`: a resend **reboots the node again**.
- Remote `export-config`: up to ~193 s of admin round trips, all repeated on each resend.
- MeshCore remote/room login retries (up to ~5 min), neighbours, discover, and region sweeps.

## Fix
**1. Safety net for every route** (`src/server/middleware/requestTimeout.ts`, mounted app-wide)
- `respondOnSocketTimeout()` listens for the response's `timeout` event. Node only destroys a timed-out socket when nobody listens.
- It answers `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` ("may still complete in the background; check before retrying"). A reply is not retried by the browser.
- The handler still finishes in the background, and its late reply is dropped quietly instead of throwing `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`.
- Streaming responses that already sent headers keep the old destroy behaviour.

**2. Real results for known-slow routes**
`extendRequestTimeout(ms)` raises the socket timeout per route, ~15 s above each route's worst case:

| Area | Routes → timeout |
|---|---|
| MeshCore contacts | ping 45 s · neighbours / neighbours poll / time-sync / neighbors request 120 s · telemetry poll 90 s · discover / regions discover 180 s |
| MeshCore admin | admin login (+saved) 120 s · remote CLI / local CLI 75 s |
| MeshCore rooms / device / automation | room login (+saved) 120 s · connect 90 s · announce send / timer run 120 s |
| Meshtastic admin | session passkey 60 s · load-config / get-channel 90 s · load-owner / device metadata / reboot / set-time 75 s · export-config 240 s · auto-favorite run 180 s |
| Other | firmware restore 200 s · backup restore 90 s · script test 45 s · script dependency install 615 s (pip and npm run one after the other, 5 min each) |

**Left out, on purpose:**
- `POST /api/automations/:id/run-now` stays on the 504 net, since an automation's delays and scripts are unbounded. A comment says so.
- MeshCore trace-path is fixed inline in #5490.

## Mesh impact
Removes repeated RF traffic: a slow radio request now runs exactly once. Nothing new is sent, and no timer is added.

## Tests
- `requestTimeout.test.ts` uses a real HTTP server with a short socket timeout:
  - a slow handler gets a 504, not a dropped socket, and runs **once**; its late reply doesn't throw;
  - fast routes are untouched;
  - without the middleware the socket hangs up (reproduces the bug);
  - `extendRequestTimeout` lets a slow route return its real result.
- `requestTimeout.routes.test.ts` pins `extendRequestTimeout` on each liste

title: feat(channels): store and preserve ChannelSettings.use_aead (#5248 Phase 1)
body:
Refs #5248 (Phase 1 of 2). Implements the Phase 1 section of `docs/internal/dev-notes/AEAD_CHANNELS_PLAN.md`.

## Why
Firmware 2.8.1 (#9749 on `develop`) adds AES-CCM authenticated encryption for PSK channels, gated by `ChannelSettings.use_aead`. Two facts from firmware make this urgent before any firmware ships it:
- `set_channel` **replaces the whole channel**.
- MeshMonitor rebuilt `ChannelSettings` from the fields it knew and never stored `use_aead`.

So once a node runs AEAD, **any channel edit from MeshMonitor would silently turn AEAD off** and cut that node off from the rest of the channel. This PR stores the flag and sends it back on every write path. It is shown read-only; decrypt and an editable checkbox are Phase 2, after a 2.8.1 build ships.

## What changed
- **Migration 185:** `useAead` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false on the per-source `channels` table, all three backends, idempotent.
- **Repository:** an omitted flag keeps the stored value; a new row gets false. Source-scoped.
- **Device ingest:** stores `channel.settings.useAead ?? false`.
- **`createSetChannelMessage`** encodes `useAead`. How every builder now keeps it:
  - `deviceAdminService.setChannelConfig`, the local path all local callers use: fills an omitted flag from the stored row for its own source (read-modify-write).
  - `adminRoutes` setChannel: fills from the stored row locally, and `get-channel` / `get-config` return it. Remote-node edits carry the value `get-channel` read from the node back in the request.
  - Channels-tab edit (PUT): always keeps the stored flag, since it is read-only in Phase 1.
  - Reorder: sends the moved channel's flag, and false for emptied slots.
  - Channel URLs (encode/decode, URL import) and single-channel import/export: the file or URL's value wins, since those replace the channel.
  - Device config backup/restore: carries it.
  - `beaconOfferRoutes`: false, because an offer has no such field and replaces the slot.
  - Virtual Node `createChannel`: sends it, so a connected app that edits a channel sends it back.
- **UI:** a read-only **AEAD** badge (`AeadBadge`, CSS module, `securityCheck` icon) with the tooltip "This channel uses AES-CCM authenticated encryption. Only nodes with the same setting can read it." It appears in Configuration → Channels, the channel info modal and Export/Import. 3 locale keys.

## Screenshot
Channel info modal on the dev container, with `dummyB` seeded to `useAead = 1` and reverted afterwards:

![AEAD badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/aead-phase1-5248/docs/public/images/features/5248-aead-channel-badge.png)

## Testing
- New tests:
  - save → edit round trip keeps `useAead=true` in the encoded `set_channel` bytes
  - repository preserve-on-omit and per-source isolation
  - URL encode/decode, and export/import
  - migration 185 on SQLite, plus a pgmysql test against live PG 16 / MySQL 8.4
  - `AeadBadge`
- Rebased onto `main` after #5489, keeping migration 184 then 185.
- Full V
