title: fix(ui): contain settings maps, bound Automation number inputs
body:
Three behaviour bugs on the Meshtastic Automation page, plus the server-side interval clamp and draft re-seed fix the maintainer asked for. There is no issue for these.

## 1. Drafts "reset" when the viewport crosses the phone/desktop breakpoint

**Root cause: not an app bug. Chrome DevTools reloaded the page.** I traced it in the live app (read-only, in its own isolated browser context):

- Emulating `390x844,mobile,touch` and then `1280x900` (no `mobile`/`touch`) reloads the page. A `window` marker set before the switch is gone after it, and every ancestor of `.settings-content` up to `<html>` is a new node. DevTools reloads whenever the emulated `mobile`/`touch` flags change, and a reload drops every unsaved draft.
- A width change that leaves the flags alone (`390x844` to `1280x900`, or `390x844,mobile,touch` to `1280x900,mobile,touch`) keeps every node mounted. The Geofence event stays on "Exit" and the Auto Responder toggle stays on.
- In code, nothing in the Automation tree branches or keys on the viewport. `AutomationTab` renders one tree, `App` renders one `<main>`, and none of the `useIsMobile*` hooks sit above the sections. The Configuration page's `key` depends only on `sourceId`.

**Fix:** no viewport fix needed. A guard test stops a later `isMobile ? <A/> : <B/>` split or a viewport-based `key` from throwing drafts away without anyone noticing.

**Related fix, draft re-seed:** `AutoResponderSection` and `GeofenceTriggersSection` used to re-seed their drafts whenever the `triggers` prop changed *identity*, even with identical content. `AutomationContext` passes a stable array, so this did not fire in practice, but any parent that rebuilt the array on each render would have wiped unsaved edits. Both now build a `JSON.stringify` key of the saved values (`useMemo`), keep the last-seeded key in a ref, and re-seed only when the key changes. Mount is a no-op because the ref starts at the initial key. The dependency arrays list every value the effect reads, so nothing was added blindly or suppressed, and the `exhaustive-deps` baseline is unchanged. Auto Responder keys `enabled`, `triggers` and `skipIncompleteNodes` together, so a real change to any of them re-seeds as before.

## 2. The Geofence map paints over the sticky section nav at 1280px

**Root cause:** Leaflet gives its panes `z-index: 400` and its controls `1000`. `.leaflet-container` is `position: relative` with no z-index, so it forms no stacking context, and those values compete in the root context against the sticky `SectionNav` (`z-index: 10`). Once scrolled, the map tiles covered the nav and its search box. I confirmed this by screenshot, and confirmed that `isolation: isolate` on the wrapper fixes it.

**Fix:** a new `src/components/map/EmbeddedMapFrame.module.css` with `.frame { position: relative; isolation: isolate; }`. The frame becomes its own stacking context: the panes keep their order inside the map, and the map as a whole paints below the nav. I applied it to every

body:
## Summary

Five cosmetic and i18n follow-ups to #5465 on the Meshtastic Automation page. No behaviour changes. No tracking issue.

### 4. German Auto Responder add row wrapped at 1280px
"Hinzufügen" (122px) is about twice the width of "Add" (63px), so "Leeren" dropped to its own line.
**Fix:** Add and Clear now sit in one `nowrap` group (`.buttonGroup`), so they never split. The Cooldown group (`.cooldownGroup`, `flex: 1 1 12rem; min-width: 0`) shrinks first and its hint wraps inside it. Cooldown basis plus the German buttons comes to ~410px, under the ~599px row. On a phone the button group wraps as a whole. The #5465 pattern/response bases (`17rem` / `10rem`) are unchanged.

### 5. "Select a script..." clipped in the 181px Response field
**Fix:** `auto_responder.select_script` now reads "Choose script…", which fits. The select keeps its tooltip, now translatable (`auto_responder.script_select_title`). The trigger edit form uses the same key instead of its own hardcoded copy.

### 6. Untranslated Auto Responder strings
**Fix:** I swept `AutoResponderSection`, `TriggerItem` (the trigger view and edit form), `ScriptManagement` and `PatternExamples`, and moved ~140 hardcoded strings to `t()`: labels, placeholders, tooltips, validation errors, the test panel, badges, buttons and modals. The new keys follow the file's `auto_responder.*` naming and go into **`en.json` only**. Other locales fall back to English, with no machine translations. Notes:
- "Cooldown:" and "seconds per node (0 = disabled)" already had keys. They showed in English because `de.json` holds empty values for them. I also removed the inline English fallbacks, so `en.json` stays the only source.
- `t('common.permission_denied')` had no key and would have shown the raw key. It now has one.
- Mailbox help text with `<code>` examples is split, so translators never see the command syntax. The traceroute hint and the delete-script confirm use `<Trans>`.
- `PatternExamples.tsx` (the Pattern Examples & Templates card) is now data-driven. Patterns, regexes, the `TZ` env var, `TZ=America/New_York` and `docker-compose.yaml` stay in code. Descriptions are looked up by key, and the tips place those literals through `<Trans>` self-closing components (`Use <example/> for default matching…`), so translators never see pattern syntax. Side fix: two tips used to render doubled backslashes (`[^\\s]+`, `[\\w\\s]+`); they now show the real regex.

### 7. `<html lang>` stayed "en" in German
**Fix:** A new `src/config/documentLanguage.ts` sets `document.documentElement.lang` (as BCP 47, e.g. `zh_Hans` → `zh-Hans`) and `dir` (via `i18n.dir()`) on every `languageChanged`. `i18n.ts` binds it before `init()`, so the language restored from localStorage on load applies too. No RTL locale ships today, but `dir` is ready for one.

### 8. Geofence number inputs misaligned at 390px
Interval's input started at x=185 and Cooldown's at x=198 because the labels differ in width.
**Fix:** Both labels share `.numberLabel

title: fix(ui): full trigger placeholder on desktop, wrap geofence hints on phones
body:
Follow-up to #5463.

## Problem

1. **Auto Responder, desktop.** At a 1280px window the add-trigger row's pattern input was 154px wide (118px of text room). The pattern and Response fields split the row 1:2 from a zero flex basis, so the placeholder "e.g. weather {location}" (~222px) showed only "e.g. weather".
2. **Geofence Cooldown hint, phone.** At 390px the hint "Minimum time between triggers for each node. 0 = no cooldown." sat in the ~100px left beside the 120px label and 100px number input, so it wrapped to about one word per line. The "while inside" Interval row had the same markup.
3. **Locales.** #5463 shortened the English `auto_responder.trigger_placeholder`, but fr, id, pl, ru, zh_Hans and zh_Hant still held the old long translation.

## Fix

- `AutomationFormLayout.module.css`:
  - `.patternField` is now `flex: 1 1 17rem`, and a new `.responseField` (`flex: 2 1 10rem`) replaces the Response field's inline `flex: '2'`. The two bases plus the 120px type select and gaps come to ~568px, under the ~599px row at 1280px, so the row stays on one line; the pattern input gets ~282px (~246px of text), and the Response field (~181px) still takes the larger share of any extra width. The #5463 container query (`@container (max-width: 36rem)` → pattern at `flex-basis: 100%`) is unchanged, so narrow rows still give the pattern its own line.
  - New `.inlineHint` (`flex: 1 1 14rem`). Its basis is wider than the phone gap beside the input, so on a narrow row the hint wraps under the input and takes the full line; on desktop it fits beside the input as before. No media query.
- `AutoResponderSection.tsx`: the script-picker select's `minWidth: '200px'` is now `min(100%, 200px)`, so it cannot overflow the narrower Response field.
- `GeofenceTriggersSection.tsx`: the Cooldown and Interval rows get `.wrapRow`, and their hints get `.inlineHint`.

## Locale note

The key is removed from every non-English locale file (de, es, fr, id, nb_NO, pl, pt_BR, ru, sv, zh_Hans, zh_Hant; five of them already held `""`). `src/config/i18n.ts` sets `fallbackLng: 'en'` and preloads `en`, so these languages show the English placeholder until Weblate supplies a new translation. The coverage guard (`i18nLanguageCoverage.test.ts`) counts non-empty values against the English key set, so one missing key does not move any locale across its 50% threshold; it passes unchanged.

## Tests

- New `src/components/AutomationFormLayout.placeholderHint.test.ts` (stylesheet and markup assertions, as in `AutomationFormLayout.mobileFollowups.test.ts`): pattern basis leaves room for the placeholder, bases fit the 1280px row, the container query survives, the hint basis exceeds the phone gap, both Geofence rows wrap, and no non-English locale holds the key.
- Affected suites (AutomationFormLayout.*, GeofenceTriggersSection, i18nLanguageCoverage): 51/51 passed, `success: true`.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint:ci` exits 0 (Lint ratchet OK).

title: fix(ui): keep trigger fields inside their cards on phones
body:
## Problem

A 390x844 screenshot review after #5462 (mobile overflow) and #5457 (Configuration spacing) found four layout bugs. None make the page scroll sideways, but fields stick out of their cards.

| Where | Measured | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Timer Triggers: Name input, "Select a script..." select | right edge x=385 | card edge x=349 |
| Geofence Triggers: Name / Message / Event | 385 / 380 / 339 | card edge x=333 |
| Auto Responder: pattern placeholder | cut to "Try: weather, w" | readable |
| Configuration: gap below Device Backup (last section) | 49px | 33px |

Causes:
- The global `.setting-input` sets `width: 200px`. A `flex: 1` input or select in a flex row has an automatic minimum of that 200px, so beside a 120px label it can't shrink and runs past the card.
- The Auto Responder pattern input keeps the first line beside the 120px type select, which leaves about 140px of text on a phone.
- The "Enable Automatic Backups" block had an inline `marginBottom: '1rem'`. As the last block on the page, its margin collapses through the section and adds 16px below the list.

## Fix

All CSS goes in `AutomationFormLayout.module.css`, with no viewport media queries and no changes to the frozen global sheets.

- **Timer / Geofence trigger forms:** a new `.labeledField` class (`min-width: min(100%, 12rem); max-width: 100%`) goes on each `flex: 1` field or wrapper beside a label, and those rows get the existing `.wrapRow`. On a phone the field drops under its label at full width. On a desktop card the row has room, so nothing moves. The Timer edit form gets the same treatment. The Geofence Interval and Cooldown number rows stay as they were, since they didn't overflow.
- **Auto Responder:** the add row is now a size container (`.patternRow`). When it is narrower than 36rem, a container query gives the pattern field `flex-basis: 100%`, so it takes its own line. A container query tracks the row's real width, so a phone in landscape or a narrow window behaves the same way, and wide rows keep the desktop layout. I moved the inline `flex: '1'` into the class, because inline `flex` pinned the basis to 0. The English placeholder is now `e.g. weather {location}`, which fits a full-width phone input; the section description still explains comma-separated patterns. Other locales are untouched.
- **Configuration:** I removed the inline bottom margin. `.sectionStack > * + *` still spaces the sections (32px apart).

I checked the Timer / Geofence change against the live dev app at 390px by applying the same styles to the running (older) build. Every Timer field and the Geofence Name, Event and Message fields now end at x=333, inside the card. The one field still past the edge is the Geofence circle Radius input, which #5462 already fixed on main.

## Tests

- New `src/components/AutomationFormLayout.mobileFollowups.test.ts`, a CSS and markup test following `AutomationFormLayout.mobileOverflow.test.ts`. jsdom has no layout engine, so it checks the stylesheets and

title: fix(ui): stop Automation and Configuration pages scrolling sideways on phones
body:
## Summary

On a 390px-wide phone, the Meshtastic source's **Automation** page had a document `scrollWidth` of **618px**, and the **Configuration** page had one of **441px**, so both pages scrolled sideways. The bottom tab bar and sticky section nav scroll inside their own boxes, which is expected. They were not the cause.

## Culprits (measured at 390x844, dev container on `main`)

I walked every element whose `getBoundingClientRect().right > innerWidth` and that has no `overflow-x` clipping ancestor, then took the outermost row that still fit the screen.

**Automation page (scrollWidth 618):**

| Element | Box width | Content width | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto Responder "add trigger" row (`AutoResponderSection.tsx`) | 308px | 577px | One flex line: trigger, 120px type select, response, 214px cooldown group, Add, Clear. The Clear button ended at x=618 |
| Timer Triggers "Channel:" row (`TimerTriggersSection.tsx`) | 276px | 378px | 120px label + 200px select + help text on one line |
| Geofence circle Lat / Lng / Radius grid (`GeofenceMapEditor.tsx`) | 276px | 469px | `1fr 1fr 1fr`. A `1fr` track can't shrink below its content, and number inputs are ~190px wide |
| Geofence Triggers "Channel:" row (`GeofenceTriggersSection.tsx`) | 276px | 471px | Label + select + help + Verify Response checkbox on one line |

The Key Repair log table also runs past the screen, but it sits inside an `overflow: auto` box, so it did not widen the page.

**Configuration page (scrollWidth 441):**

| Element | Right edge |
|---|---|
| NTP Server / Rsyslog Server inputs (`width: 400px`) | 441 |
| "Set private key" button (`nowrap`) in the private-key row | 438 |
| Reboot / Purge / Reload Config button row | 421 |

**MeshCore Automations page:** already fits (scrollWidth 390). No change.

## Fix

- New `AutomationFormLayout.module.css`: `.wrapRow { flex-wrap: wrap }` for the add-trigger row and both Channel rows. `.growField { min-width: min(100%, 9rem) }` stops the `flex: 1` / `flex: 2` text fields from shrinking to slivers once the row can wrap.
- New `GeofenceMapEditor.module.css`: the circle grid is now `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))`, and its inputs get `width: 100%; min-width: 0`. That gives 3 columns on desktop and 2 on a phone.
- `ConfigurationTab.module.css`: `.dangerActions { flex-wrap: wrap }` for the warning-box buttons.
- The private-key row gets `flexWrap: 'wrap'`. The NTP and Rsyslog inputs, and the Admin Commands FEM LNA select, get `maxWidth: '100%'` next to their fixed `400px`.
- **No viewport media queries.** Wrapping only happens when a row is too narrow, so desktop is unchanged. At 1280px the add-trigger fields are 154px and 309px, above the 144px floor. Landscape phones are also covered, since `max-width`-only queries miss them (#5051–#5054).

## Verification

- I applied the same declarations live to the dev container's DOM at 390px. Automation dropped from 618 to 390 and Configuration from 441 to 390, with no overflowing elements left. T

## Problem
`deleteTelemetryByIds runs in batches and returns the real count` inserts and deletes 1,007 rows (2 × 500-row batches + 7). On CI's MySQL service container it sometimes exceeds Vitest's default 10 s. The timed-out test keeps running and writes into the next test's fixture, which then fails with `expected 9 to be null`.

Hit twice on 2026-09-28: #5450 (Node 25 leg) and #5438 (Node 24 leg). Both are unrelated changes.

## Fix
A 60 s timeout on that one test. The database is already isolated per suite (`isolationKey`), so this is not a fixture race.

## Tests
Ran against a local `mysql:8.4` container: 8 passed (SQLite + MySQL legs).

## Mesh impact
None. Test-only.

title: fix(meshcore): drop corrupt contact frames and scrub binary node names
body:
## Summary

MeshCore node list showed contacts whose names were raw binary bytes. The names are not what the remote nodes advertise. They come from corrupt serial frames.

## Root cause

The companion serial protocol frames every message as `>` + u16 length + payload, with **no checksum**. When the USB-serial stream drops bytes (easy during a large `get_contacts` dump), meshcore.js's `onDataReceived` re-syncs on the next `>` byte and parses a spliced frame as a Contact / NewAdvert record. `meshcoreManager` persisted those records as-is.

meshcore.js's `readCString(32)` does stop at the first NUL, so the decode itself is fine. The bytes it decodes are already wrong.

Evidence from the dev DB (read-only), all on `MC-Sandbox` (`/dev/ttyUSB2`, serial companion). 37 of 903 `meshcore_nodes` rows had control chars or U+FFFD in `name`:

| publicKey | name (UTF-8 hex) | what it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `8f6ef823eb2d80886ee0009900000000435331383720534320536f6c61720000` | `7c02` | the key holds the ASCII `CS187 SC Solar` of a neighbouring record, a spliced frame |
| `03586b005d00…436f636f6e7574205765` | `0544efbfbd3d…01` | key ends in `Coconut We` |
| `00000000…004b5134` | `521c2d23efbfbdefbfbd78…02` | key is zeros + `KQ4`; adv_type 79 |
| `99f9b7d6…573143` | `7237efbfbdefbfbd6553…02` | out_path decodes to `Black Rak…`; adv_type 76 |
| `00000000…746f6d706177…` | `efbfbd` | key holds `tompaw` |

Other rows carry adv_type values 115, 111, 101, 67, 48 and 45 (valid values are 0 to 4).

Six more rows had no control chars and ended in a single U+FFFD: `>�` (`3eefbfbd`), `j>�`, `·j>�`, `|j>�`, `%�j>�`. That tail is the **next Contact frame's serial header** swallowed into the name field. A Contact frame is 148 bytes, so its header is `3e 94 00`: `>`, then the length byte `0x94` (a lone UTF-8 continuation byte, so U+FFFD), then `0x00`, which ends the C string. The same `3e94` shows up inside the corrupt `out_path` values.

Some "corrupt" keys are real nodes whose name a spliced frame overwrote, for example `1cbae49c…` = "KF4LZA EDC T1000", `123a100f…` = "K471 Portable" (stored as `K47� $�D��Nm�\x02`), `badd9bf1…` = "DSoul-Bot" (stored as `>�`). So the ingest guard matters for real contacts too, not only phantom keys.

One more row is **genuine**: `Dvynsoul GAT562 Base` + U+FFFD (`…20efbfbd`), the same on both sources with a real key. The sender's name ends in a multi-byte character (likely an emoji) that was cut short before it reached us, so it decodes to a trailing U+FFFD. That one only needs a display fix.

## Fix

- **New `src/utils/meshcoreName.ts`**
  - `isCorruptMeshCoreContactRecord()` rejects a record whose `adv_type` is outside 0 to 4, or whose name has control chars, an undecodable byte anywhere but the tail, or ends in `>` + U+FFFD (the swallowed frame header).
  - `sanitizeMeshCoreName()` cuts at NUL, returns `null` on the `>` + U+FFFD tail, turns tab/CR/LF into spaces, drops a trailing U+FFFD run, and trims. It returns `null` if the name still holds c

title: fix(automation): stop phantom "Save changes" bar on the Automation page
body:
## Summary

Opening a Meshtastic source's Automation page (e.g. Sandbox → Automation) showed a "Save changes to Auto Acknowledge" bar with no edits made.

## Root cause

`AutoAcknowledgeSection` seeds its local form state with display fallbacks:

```ts
useState(regex || '^(test|ping)')
useState(message || DEFAULT_MESSAGE)
useState(messageDirect || DEFAULT_MESSAGE_DIRECT)
```

The re-seed effect and `resetChanges` use the same fallbacks, but the `hasChanges` effect compared the local value against the **raw** prop (`localMessageDirect !== messageDirect`). `AutomationContext` stores whatever `/api/settings` returns, and a blank string is a valid stored value (the server treats blank `autoAckMessageDirect` as "reuse the standard message", blank regex/message as "use the default"). So any source with a blank stored string was dirty the moment settings loaded. The existing `convertButton` test even worked around this in a comment.

The sibling sections on the same page had the same asymmetry:
- **Auto Announce:** `intervalHours || 6`, `message || DEFAULT`, `channelIndexes` empty → `[0]`, `schedule || '0 */6 * * *'`
- **Auto Welcome:** `message || DEFAULT`, `target || '0'`, `maxHops || 5`
- **Auto Key Management:** `intervalMinutes || 5`, `maxExchanges || 3`

## Fix

Each dirty check now compares against the same normalized baseline the local state is seeded with. The expressions stay inline in the effect, so no dependency arrays changed (no `exhaustive-deps` churn).

Auto Acknowledge also called `.sort()` in place on both `localEnabledChannels` and the parent's `enabledChannels` state inside the dirty check; it now sorts copies (numerically).

## Tests

New `src/components/automationSections.phantomDirty.test.tsx` renders each section with realistic loaded values that hit the fallback and asserts the SaveBar gets `hasChanges: false`:
- Auto Acknowledge, blank strings on mount, and after a rerender from context defaults to loaded values (the real load sequence)
- Auto Acknowledge does not reorder the parent's channel array
- Auto Announce / Auto Welcome / Auto Key Management with blank/zero stored values

All 6 fail on `main` (AutoAck `expected true to be false`; the 3 sibling cases fail when only their fixes are reverted) and pass with the fix. Related suites (`AutoAcknowledgeSection*.test.tsx`, `AutoAnnounceSection.test.tsx`) pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint:ci` reports "Lint ratchet OK" with no FAIL lines.

No mesh impact: frontend dirty-state only, no packets, timers or notifications touched.

## Follow-up: AutoAnnounceSection `nodeInfoChannels = []` render loop

`AutoAnnounceSection` defaulted `nodeInfoChannels = []`, which is a new array every render. The re-seed effect depends on it and sets state, so rendering the section without the prop re-rendered until the test worker ran out of heap. `AutomationTab` always passes the prop, so the live app was not affected, but any other caller would hang. The default is now a module-level frozen `

title: fix(config): show one Range Test notice on 2.8 builds
body:
## Problem
In Configuration → Modules → Range Test on a 2.8 node, two notices stacked under the header:
1. The `ModuleAvailabilityGate` notice: "Range Test is not included in this device's firmware build, so these settings cannot be changed." (moved under the header in #5449)
2. The older #5031 notice: "Range Test was removed in Meshtastic 2.8…". The gate's CSS faded it, since it sat inside the greyed controls.

Both say the same thing. The controls also got faded twice (gate 0.4 × section 0.4).

## Fix
- `ModuleAvailabilityNotice` takes an optional `detail` sentence, appended to the gate message.
- New `useModuleExcluded()` hook in `moduleAvailabilityContext.ts` tells a section whether an excluding gate wraps it.
- `RangeTestConfigSection`: when the firmware is 2.8+ (`isDisabled`), it passes "It was removed from Meshtastic firmware in 2.8." as the gate notice's `detail`. While the gate is active it hides its own notice and skips its own opacity class. With no active gate (`available` true or unknown) it keeps its old notice, as before.
- New locale key `rangetest_config.removed_in_28_detail`.

Result on a 2.8 build: one notice, "Range Test is not included in this device's firmware build, so these settings cannot be changed. It was removed from Meshtastic firmware in 2.8."

**Other sections checked:** only Range Test has its own version notice inside a `ModuleAvailabilityGate`. Traffic Management and MeshBeacon have "requires 2.8" notices but aren't wrapped in a gate, so they can't double up. No other gated section has its own notice.

## Tests
- `RangeTestConfigSection.firmware28.test.tsx`: three new cases. Gate excluded + 2.8 gives one `status` notice with both the exclusion text and the 2.8 reason, and no double fade. Gate excluded + pre-2.8 gives one plain exclusion notice. Gate available + 2.8 keeps the old notice.
- `ModuleAvailabilityGate.test.tsx`: the placement guard regex now accepts `<ModuleAvailabilityNotice … />` with props.
- `src/components/configuration/`: 19 files, 142 tests pass. ConfigurationTab tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` is clean. `npm run lint:ci` reports "Lint ratchet OK" with 0 FAIL lines.

## Screenshot

Configuration → Range Test on the Sandbox source (2.8 firmware, Range Test in `excluded_modules`): one notice, ending "It was removed from Meshtastic firmware in 2.8.", and the Enable Range Test control is faded once (effective opacity 0.4, not 0.16).

title: fix(config): full-width Status Message input with attached counter
body:
## Problem
In Configuration → Modules → Status Message, the **Node Status** input used the global `.setting-input` width (200px), so its placeholder was cut off ("Enter status messag"). Its `0/80` counter was absolutely positioned (`bottom: -1.2rem`) against a full-width wrapper, so it escaped the section and rendered on the same line as the next section's **Traffic Management** header.

## Fix
- New `StatusMessageConfigSection.module.css` (no global sheet changes): the input fills the column (`width: 100%`, `box-sizing: border-box`, two-class selector so it beats `.setting-input` regardless of load order), and the counter sits in normal flow, right-aligned directly under the input. The near-limit colour (>= 70 chars) moved from an inline style to a class; colours use `var(--color-*)` with no fallback.
- Admin Commands → Module Configuration had an identical copy of this field with the same bug; it now shares the module.
- Mobile: the input is 100% of the settings column with border-box sizing, so it cannot overflow at narrow widths.
- **Gap between all Configuration sections:** each section is the only child of its `#config-*` wrapper, so the global `.settings-section:last-child` rule zeroed its 2rem bottom margin and every section joined the next flush. `ConfigurationTab.module.css` now gives the `settings-content` container a `.sectionStack` class with `> * + * { margin-top: 2rem }`, so wrappers are spaced and the first/last sections gain no extra space. Gated wrappers (`.gated`) sit inside the wrapper, so they are unaffected. Frozen global sheets untouched.

## Tests
- New `StatusMessageConfigSection.test.tsx`: counter shares the input's wrapper, stays inside `.settings-section`, carries no absolute positioning; input keeps `setting-input`.
- Targeted vitest: 42/42 pass, `success: true`. `tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run lint:ci`: "Lint ratchet OK", 0 FAIL lines.
- Screenshots below, taken from this branch deployed to the dev container.

## One Year of MeshMonitor

Adds a year-in-review blog post marking MeshMonitor's first year, built from the request in Discord #general.

**First commit:** 2025-09-25 · **As of:** 2026-09-28 · **Span:** 368 days.

### What's in the post

+
+MeshMonitor turned one. The first commit landed on **25 September 2025**. As of **28 September 2026**, that is **368 days** of near-daily work. This post looks back at the year in numbers.
+
+All figures come straight from the git history, measured against the v4.16.2-rc5 tag. Read them as a snapshot, not a scoreboard.
+
+## The headline number
+
+**4,104 commits in 368 days.** That works out to about **11 commits a day**, every day, weekends included.
+
+The project recorded work on **362 of those 368 days**. Six days off in a year. The longest unbroken run was a **164-day streak**, from 9 April to 19 September 2026 — more than five months without a gap.
+
+## What the commits did
+
+The year splits cleanly by commit type:
+
+- **968 features** — new capability
+- **1,353 fixes** — more fixes than features, which is the healthy ratio for software people actually run
+- **780 chores** — dependency bumps, releases, housekeeping
+- **151 docs**, **141 refactors**, and a scatter of tests and CI work
+
+## Releases
+
+- **420 release tags** across the year
+- **71 minor version lines**, from the earliest v3 builds to today's v4.16.2-rc5
+- Roughly a tagged build every **1.3 days** on average
+
+## When the work happened
+
+The busiest single day was **3 February 2026 with 43 commits**. The busiest month was **February 2026 with 478**.
+
+Most commits landed in the **early afternoon** — noon, 1 PM and 3 PM were the three peak hours. Only about **13%** of commits came between 10 PM and 6 AM, so this was mostly daylight work, not a series of all-nighters. **Monday** was the most productive weekday by a clear margin.
+
+## The busiest corners of the code
+
+The files that changed most across the year (dependency locks and generated files excluded):
+
+- `src/server/meshtasticManager.ts` — the radio manager, touched **551 times**
+- `src/server/server.ts` — **470**
+- `src/services/database.ts` — **390**
+- `src/App.tsx` — **365**
+
+No surprise that the radio connection layer and the database saw the most churn. That is where the meshes stress the code.
+
+## Who built it
+
+- **Randall Hand** authored **3,305 commits** — about **81%** of the total
+- **Dependabot** contributed **426** keeping dependencies current
+- **Weblate** translators added roughly **170** across two bot accounts
+- Community contributors, including Midnight Cowboy and Nearl Crews, filed the rest
+
+Every translation, bug report, packet capture and pull request from the community shaped the year. Several of this year's best fixes started as a capture from someone running a mesh far larger than any test bench.
+
+## What a year of this built
+
+A quick tour of what shipped over twelve months, without listing every release:
+
+- **MeshCore support** — a whole second protocol, from first ingest to channel management, coverage reporting and virtual nodes
+- **The automation engine** — triggers, templates and packet-hash matching
+- **Firmware management** — OTA updates driven from the browser
+- **Coverage Report** — measured RF coverage maps built from real receptions
+- **Likely-aircraft and asset tracking** — ADS-B flight matching, trails and timeline playback
+- **Per-source permissions, OIDC, MFA** and a long run of security hardening
+- **The desktop app**, **embedded MQTT broker**, **estimated positions**, **impersonation detection** — and hundreds of fixes that never made a headline but kept large meshes connected
+
+## Thank you
+
+One year, 4,104 commits, and a community that keeps reporting the hard bugs. Here is to the next one.
+
+The full history is in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). The current build is **v4.16.2-rc5**.

title: feat: simple per-source message Forwarding next to Auto-Responder (#5446)
body:
Closes #5446

## Summary

Adds a simple **Forwarding** section next to the Auto-Responder, on both the Meshtastic Automation tab and the MeshCore Automations view. Each rule copies a matching incoming message to one node (DM) or another channel on the **same source**, and has its own enable/disable checkbox (for example "forward my DMs to my phone while I'm away").

**Rule fields:** `enabled`, `name`, `match { isDM | channel, fromNodeId?, textRegex? }`, `forwardTo { destinationNodeId | channel }`, optional `prefix` with `{from}` / `{channel}` tokens.

### Backend
- `src/types/forwarding.ts`: shared rule type, fixed limits, and structural validation (used by the route and the UI).
- `src/server/utils/forwardingEngine.ts`: protocol-neutral engine. Every mesh-safety rule lives here, so both protocols behave the same.
- `src/server/routes/forwardingRoutes.ts`: `GET/POST /api/sources/:id/forwarding`, gated on per-source `automation` read/write, `ok()`/`fail()` envelope, code `INVALID_FORWARDING_RULES`. Regex checked with the RE2-backed auto-ack validator.
- Storage: per-source setting `forwardingRules` (JSON array), like `meshcoreAutoResponderTriggers`. Listed in `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS` and `PER_SOURCE_KEYS_NOT_POSTABLE` (not `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`), so only the dedicated route writes it. No new table. The managers still validate again when they read the rules.
- Meshtastic (`meshtasticManager.checkForwarding`): runs after auto-ack and before auto-ping. It only handles newly inserted messages that pass `isLiveReception` (fw 2.8 NodeDB replays are never forwarded). Sends go through `enqueueAutomation` with **maxAttempts 1**, tagged `origin: 'automation'` (#5414). It respects `canTransmit()` and the automation airtime cutoff.
- MeshCore (`meshcoreManager.checkForwarding`): runs on `contact_message` and `channel_message`. Sends use `sendMessage` **without** channel auto-retry. Skipped when receive-only or when the device is a repeater.

### UI
- `src/components/forwarding/ForwardingSection.tsx` + CSS module (theme tokens only, `UiIcon`, `csrfFetch`, save bar). The MeshCore wrapper loads channels and contacts. On Meshtastic, AutomationTab passes device channels and nodes, and App passes `txDisabled={txGated}`.
- A shared-airtime warning shows next to every channel target.
- Receive-only / TX-disabled / MQTT sources: rules stay visible but **read-only**, with a `role="status"` paused note. Users without `automation:write` on the source also get a read-only view.
- Added a "Forwarding" entry to the automation section nav/search, plus en.json strings.

### Docs
- `docs/features/automation.md#forwarding` (full section) and a short entry in `docs/features/meshcore.md` that links to it.

## Mesh impact

**Airtime:** each forward is 1 packet × hop count (a 3-hop flood is about 4 transmissions). Each rule is **hard-capped at 5 forwards per rolling 60 s**, so at most about 5 × hops transmissions per minute per rule, with at most 20 rules per source. The cap is f

title: feat(automations): add action.setAutomationEnabled (#5445)
body:
Closes #5445

## Summary

Adds a native Automation Engine action, `action.setAutomationEnabled`, that enables, disables, or toggles an automation by id. Users no longer need the `action.runScript` + `curl` + API token workaround.

**Params**
- `automationId` (required): a literal id or a `{{ }}` template.
- `enabled`: a boolean, `"true"`/`"false"` (also `1`/`0`), or a template that resolves to one of those. Required for `set`.
- `mode`: `'set'` (default) or `'toggle'`. Toggle ignores `enabled`.

**Behaviour**
- The engine owns the write. It calls `automationsRepo.setEnabled`, then `load()`, the same reload the `/enable` and `/disable` routes use through `reloadAutomations()`. It is wired through an optional `ActionDeps.setAutomationEnabled`, which the engine layers over the mesh deps, so `meshActionDeps` does not import the singleton and no import cycle appears. If the state would not change, nothing is written and nothing reloads.
- **Unknown id**: the step fails with `no automation with id "…"` in the run log. As with any failed action, the rest of the run still goes ahead.
- **Run-log audit**: a new optional evaluator hook, `stepDetail`, stores `{ automationId, name, mode, enabled, previous }` on the step's `detail`. Only this action opts in, so run-log rows for other actions do not change. The run-log / trace `StepList` renders `detail`.
- **Self-disable short-circuit**: `EngineEvalContext` now carries `automationId` and a `halt` flag. When an automation disables itself, the executor sets the flag. A new `haltReason` evaluator hook stops the run after that action and appends a `run:halted` step ("run stopped") that gives the reason. The run keeps status `completed`.
- **Mid-run reload is safe**: `load()` swaps in a new index map and never mutates the old one, and the in-flight run holds its own `LoadedAutomation` (graph included). The one thing that could go stale is the rest of the current dispatch loop: rule A disables rule B, but B is still ahead in the list for the same event. `fireAutomation` now checks a `liveIds` set and skips such a rule. Run Now is exempt, because it fires disabled automations on purpose.
- **Dry run (Test panel)** never writes. It uses a read-only lookup to report what would change and to fail an unknown id. For a saved automation (`/:id/test`), it also halts on a self-disable, as a real run does.

**Frontend**
- New `automationSelect` field kind → `AutomationIdFieldInput` (CSS module). It is a dropdown of existing automations, shown by name and saved by id, with disabled ones marked. An "Enter an id or template…" choice swaps in the token-aware text field. A saved template or an id that matches no automation opens in that text field.
- The editor loads the automation list through `ApiService` (`/api/automations`), the same way it loads sources, scripts and regions. The prop is threaded as optional, so `TemplateGallery` and existing tests need no change.
- Fields: Automation, Change (Set to / Toggle), New state (hid

title: feat(map): CARTO vector basemaps + bundled CARTO Voyager Dark (#5448)
body:
Closes #5448

## Summary

Phase 2 of `docs/internal/dev-notes/CARTO_API_KEY_PLAN.md` (CARTO vector basemaps in 2D), plus a bundled **CARTO Voyager Dark** style: a dark map that keeps land-use color, which is what the issue asks for.

### Screenshots

The bundled Voyager Dark style, rendered by MapLibre 5 in headless Chromium (standalone harness, **no API key**). CARTO's vector tiles, sprites and glyphs all returned 200 without a key. Only its *raster* tiles carry the "API key required" watermark, so the vector render below is clean.

Central Park, z14: green parks, teal water, amber roads, light labels on dark halos:

![Voyager Dark, Central Park z14](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5448-carto-vector-voyager-dark/docs/public/images/features/5448-voyager-dark-park.png)

Seattle, z12:

![Voyager Dark, Seattle z12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5448-carto-vector-voyager-dark/docs/public/images/features/5448-voyager-dark-city.png)

The screenshots show the style itself, not the MeshMonitor UI, because I did not deploy the dev container.

### What changed

- **`styleUrl` on tilesets** (`src/config/tilesets.ts`). New presets `cartoVoyager`, `cartoPositron` and `cartoDarkMatter` point at CARTO's published GL styles. `cartoVoyagerDark` points at the bundled `map-styles/carto-voyager-dark.json`. All four set `isVector: true` explicitly, so `isVectorTileUrl` never has to sniff them.
- **`url` stays a raster template.** On style presets it holds the closest raster twin: `rastertiles/voyager`, `light_all`, `dark_all`, and `dark_all` for Voyager Dark, which has no twin. So the picker thumbnail, the "needs a CARTO key" warning (`isCartoUrl(url)`) and `validateTileUrl` all keep working. The new `getRasterTileset()` sends raster-only surfaces to that twin instead of feeding a style URL to a raster source.
- **`VectorTileLayer`.** When given `styleUrl`, it passes the style straight to `L.maplibreGL`, skipping the `.pbf` patch and default-style branches; `styleUrl` wins over `styleJson`. It resolves relative (bundled) styles against the server-injected `<base href>`, so a `/meshmonitor` sub-path works. It always installs `transformRequest: createCartoTransformRequest(cartoApiKey)`, which appends `?key=` to CARTO hosts only (style, TileJSON, `tiles-{a..d}` vector tiles, sprites, glyphs) and returns `undefined` for every other host and when there is no key. `BaseMap` passes `styleUrl` and `cartoApiKey` down.
- **3D (Phase 3 still deferred).** `resolve3DBasemap` uses the preset's raster twin with the key, not the osm substitution, so choosing a CARTO vector preset in 3D shows the matching CARTO raster. The traceroute mini-map does the same. Custom `.pbf` tilesets still fall back to osm, as before.
- **CSP.** CARTO serves GL styles from the **bare** `basemaps.cartocdn.com` host, which `https://*.basemaps.cartocdn.com` does not match. I added `https://basemaps.cartocdn.com` to the app `connect-src` and to the embed

title: docs(mqtt): meshtastic/firmware#11994 was declined upstream
body:
## Summary

Meshtastic declined [meshtastic/firmware#11994](https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/issues/11994#issuecomment-5871712581), our request for a per-packet `ok_to_mqtt` override. Their reason: `ok_to_mqtt` is a node-level privacy intent, and letting the phone API override it would defeat the flag.

Our text still said the direct-MQTT-module path "needs a firmware fix". This PR changes that wording to "declined upstream, by design" in:

- the `automationPacketTracker` and `mqttBridgeManager` comments
- the **Don't uplink MeshMonitor automation traffic** help text (`MqttBridgeConfigurationView.tsx` + `en.json`)
- `docs/features/mqtt-broker.md`, which now names the workarounds: turn off **OK to MQTT** on the node, or uplink through the MeshMonitor bridge instead of the node's own MQTT module.

There are no behaviour changes. The bridge-side drop from #5414 / #5418 stays the supported answer.

## Mesh impact

None: comments, docs and UI copy only.

title: fix(meshcore): take Last Heard from the companion clock, not the sender's (#5339)
body:
Closes #5339

## Problem
#5342 rejected sender times only before 2020 or more than a day ahead. MeshCore firmware boots a node with no RTC at a fixed 2024 default (`VolatileRTCClock`, 2024-05-15), which passes that check, so those nodes still pinned Last Heard at 2024 and their messages sorted wrong.

## Fix
**Last Heard (contact sync):** `refreshContacts()` now reads `last_mod` instead of `last_advert`. Firmware stamps `lastmod` with the **companion's own clock** whenever it hears an advert, message or path from the contact (`ContactInfo.h`: "by OUR clock"), and `startDeviceTimeSync()` keeps that clock on server time. `last_advert` (sender clock) is still stored for display but no longer drives Last Heard. The value is clamped to now, and a missing or implausible one keeps the last known value (#5341). The native backend now passes `last_mod` through from meshcore.js.

Live adverts, DMs and path updates already stamp `Date.now()`, so this closes the last path that trusted the sender's clock.

**Messages:** DM and channel ingest uses the sender's time only when it falls within a day before receipt (`plausibleMeshCoreMessageTimeMs`); otherwise receipt time. Channel ordering applies the same window so rows stored earlier sort right too. Room posts keep the loose check, because a room server replays a backlog of old but real posts on login.

Trade-off: DMs/channel messages drained from the companion's offline queue after a MeshMonitor outage longer than a day show drain time instead of send time.

## Mesh impact
None. Sends nothing, arms no timer, fires no notifications.

## Tests
- `meshcoreManager.lastHeard.test.ts` rewritten around `last_mod`: ignores a plausible 2024 `last_advert`, no fallback to `last_advert`, implausible `last_mod` dropped, fast companion clamped to now, stable across refreshes.
- Message window tests (incl. room posts keeping week-old times), 2024-stuck channel ordering, native backend `last_mod` mapping.
- Full Vitest suite: 22,526 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped locally; no schema change). `lint:ci` clean.

title: fix(packet-monitor): drop fw2.8 NodeDB replay bursts from the packet log (#5426)
body:
Closes #5426

## Problem
On every client connect, firmware 2.8 replays its NodeDB as ~50 POSITION/NODEINFO/TELEMETRY packets inside half a second, forced to `TRANSPORT_LORA`. The existing packet-log dedup (#5034) is in-memory and only collapses replays of receptions this manager already logged, so after a MeshMonitor restart (or for packets heard while disconnected) the whole burst landed in the Packet Monitor as fresh LoRa receptions. MQTT was not the cause (reporter confirmed MQTT is off).

## Fix
New `isNodeDbReplayForPacketLog()` in `packetLogDedup.ts`, checked before the dedup in `meshtasticManager`. An RF packet is skipped when **both** hold:
- `rx_time` is outside the 120 s live window (`isLiveReception`), since replays keep the original first-heard time, and
- RSSI is absent/0, since NodeDB stores SNR but not RSSI.

Requiring both keeps real packets logged when the node's clock lags the server (stale-looking `rx_time`, real RSSI). MQTT/UDP/INTERNAL never match.

## Mesh impact
None. Sends nothing, arms no timer, fires no notifications.

## Tests
- Unit tests for the predicate: replay burst, live packet without RSSI, lagging clock with RSSI, missing `rx_time`, non-RF transports.
- Full Vitest suite: 22,524 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL suites skipped locally; no schema change). `lint:ci` clean.

title: fix(config): show module-excluded notice under its own section header (#5447)
body:
Fixes #5447 ## Root cause `ModuleAvailabilityGate` rendered its "X is not included in this device's firmware build" notice *before* its children. Every gated `*ConfigSection` renders its own `

` inside the gate, so the DOM order for an excluded section was: ``` [Audio h3][Audio controls] <- section above, compiled in [notice: "Remote Hardware not included..."] [Remote Hardware h3][greyed controls] ``` Nothing separates the `config-*` wrappers, so the notice read as a warning about the section above. ## Fix The gate no longer draws the notice. When a module is excluded it provides a small context (`moduleAvailabilityContext.ts`) and wraps the section in a `.gated` container. A new `ModuleAvailabilityNotice` component reads that context and renders the notice, or nothing outside an excluding gate. All 14 gated sections (Telemetry, MQTT, Neighbor Info, Network, External Notification, Store & Forward, Range Test, Canned Messages, Audio, Remote Hardware, Detection Sensor, Paxcounter, Serial, Ambient Lighting) render `` right after their `

`. The order is now `[h3][notice][greyed controls]`. The CSS module greys out every child of the section except the `h3` and the notice, so the header and the notice stay at full strength and read as one unit. No global stylesheet changes; colours still use `var(--color-warning)`, and the icon still uses `UiIcon`. I chose this over lifting each `

` into `ConfigurationTab.tsx` because that would move header markup (and its docs link) out of 14 components. The context keeps each section's header where it is and adds one line per section. ## Tests - `ModuleAvailabilityGate.test.tsx`: renders the real `AudioConfigSection` (available) above the real `RemoteHardwareConfigSection` (excluded). It asserts the notice sits inside `#config-remotehardware`, not `#config-audio`, and is the Remote Hardware `

`'s next sibling. A guard test reads `ConfigurationTab.tsx`, finds every child of a `ModuleAvailabilityGate`, and checks each renders `` after its `

`. A gated section that forgets the notice would otherwise grey out with no explanation. - `ConfigurationTab.excludedModules.test.tsx`: the Paxcounter mock now has the real header/notice/controls shape, and the test asserts the notice follows the header inside `#config-paxcounter`. title: chore(deps): bump aedes from 1.1.2 to 1.2.0
body:
Bumps [aedes](https://github.com/moscajs/aedes) from 1.1.2 to 1.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from aedes's releases.

Release 1.2.0

  • chore: update release-it schema version and remove metrics disable flag (6747894)
  • fix: bound the inbound QoS 2 receive window (GHSA-5jvp-3p2v-5qgf) (#1154) (e1a6067)
  • fix: discard the QoS 2 dedup store on clean session (GHSA-p8r9-qf8w-p73r) (#1153) (c7acaa1)

Release 1.1.3

Security

GHSA-52qw-whmv-87c5 — remote unauthenticated denial of service (high).

A single MQTT packet using an Object.prototype property name as a topic filter or Client ID crashed the broker process. Unauthenticated under the default hooks; every connected client is dropped and no new connections are accepted until a supervisor restarts the process.

Reachable via SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE or CONNECT, and in a cluster it propagated to every peer broker. See the advisory for the triggers and full analysis.

client.subscriptions, client.duplicates, Aedes.clients and Aedes.brokers are now Object.create(null), and the SUBSCRIBE dedupe map is a real Map.

Upgrade to 1.1.3. The 2.0.0-beta line is still affected — there is no patched 2.x release yet.

Behaviour change for consumers

broker.clients and client.subscriptions no longer inherit from Object.prototype:

  • clients.hasOwnProperty(id) throws — use Object.hasOwn(clients, id) or id in clients
  • String(clients) throws; clients instanceof Object is false
  • util.inspect prints [Object: null prototype]

Object.keys, for...in, delete, JSON.stringify and spread are unaffected.

Reported by @​NotAFlightRisk and @​Un-Locksmith.

Commits

  • fix: reject prototype-named topics and client IDs (GHSA-52qw-whmv-87c5) (9a1686b)
  • fix: type LastHearthbeatTimestamp as number (#1151) (66506bc)

v4.38.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

body:
Bumps [maplibre-gl](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js) from 6.10.0 to 6.11.2.
Release notes

Sourced from maplibre-gl's releases.

v6.11.2

✨ Features and improvements

  • Improve rendering performance by uploading each tile's projection data once per frame instead of before every draw call (#8545) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Support multiple glyph variants in requests, caches, and atlases (#8488) (by @​NEKOYASAN)

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fix Map#once(type, layerId, listener) unsubscribing on the first event that misses the layer instead of the first event that hits it (#8499) (by @​cherenkov)
  • Remove hillshade gradient toward the poles (#8551) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Fix camera settings being undone during camera movement with terrain or transformCameraUpdate (#8550) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Fix zooming and panning with the pointer above the horizon moving the map in the opposite direction (#8544) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Fix the camera jumping when a drag over terrain ends at a pitch above 84° (#8541) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Ease the center elevation over terrain during easeTo and flyTo instead of holding it and jumping when the animation ends (#8543) (by @​johncarmack1984)
  • Fix fitBounds and cameraForBounds throwing on the globe projection when the padding exceeds the viewport, instead of warning and returning undefined as on mercator (#8538) (by @​drakeo338)
  • Keep raster tiles sharp at a fractional devicePixelRatio, where the canvas covered a different number of device pixel

@@ -6,6 +6,29 @@ The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+## [4.16.2-rc5] - 2026-09-28
+
+### Added
+- **Asset tracking.** Flag a node as an asset in Node Details → Asset tracking to keep its telemetry for 1–365 days (default 90) on every source, always draw its trail, and exempt it from automated cleanups. The Nodes map draws the asset's whole retained history, thinned to keep its shape, and a playback bar replays the trip with a moving marker at 60×/600×/3600×. Migration 181. (#5354, #5411, #5419, #5422)
+- **ADS-B flight matching for likely aircraft**, off by default. When a node becomes a likely aircraft, MeshMonitor asks a community ADS-B feed (adsb.lol or adsb.fi) which flight is there, at most twice per flagging, and shows the match in the popup and details. Migration 180. (#5374, #5410)
+- **Sign-flipped position correction**, off by default, per source. A node whose latitude or longitude sign was entered wrong is shown at its mirror point when exactly one mirror lands within range (default 500 km) of the source's own node or a set point, with a notice showing the reported coordinates. Stored data never changes. Distance auto-delete, MQTT geo-ignore, automation geofences, traceroute snapshots and MeshCore contacts all use the corrected point. (#5363, #5409, #5412)
+- **Drop automation traffic at the MQTT bridge uplink**, a per-bridge option, off by default. MeshMonitor's own automated sends (auto-ack, responders, announce, timers, geofences, Automation Engine actions, auto-ping and similar) never reach the upstream broker; manual sends still do. A drop counter shows beside the ok_to_mqtt counter. (#5414, #5418)
+- **Map clustering toggle** in Settings → Map, separate from the Map Click Zoom Gate. On by default. (#5404, #5407)
+- **Helm: expose Virtual Node ports** with `service.extraPorts`, pin a LoadBalancer IP with `service.annotations` (MetalLB, kube-vip, Cilium) or `loadBalancerIP`, and optionally put the Virtual Node on its own `virtualNodeService` so the web UI can stay behind an Ingress. (#5416, #5417)
+
+### Changed
+- **MeshCore remote logins wait longer and retry.** Each attempt waits the longer of twice the firmware's estimate or 10 s, and the admin buttons try up to 3 times on silence (never on a refused password). Every login screen shows live progress and a Cancel button. Behind a reverse proxy, a worst-case login can now take about 34 s. (#5400, #5405)
+- **MeshCore neighbour lists show the whole table.** The repeater sends at most 10 neighbours per reply, so the Contact Details button and "Poll Neighbours" now fetch up to 5 pages, each spaced by the 60 s radio gap, with live progress and Cancel. The scheduled autopoll stays at 1 page (strongest first) and merges into the stored list instead of shrinking it. (#5413, #5425)
+- **OTA firmware updates run on the selected source.** Disconnect, reconnect, verify, retry and cancel act on the source the update was started from, not the primary radio, and use its custom TCP port. (#5424, #5428, #5432)
+- **OTA board map** matches the Meshtastic release file names for 2.7.x and 2.8.0: 26 ESP32 boards fixed (including Station G3 and Mini ePaper S3), 13 nRF52 boards no longer offered OTA. Six models shared by several builds are refused with a clear message, and boards with sibling builds (e.g. Heltec V4 / V4 TFT) show a warning before flashing. (#5423, #5429, #5433)
+
+### Fixed
+- **Firmware update** failed at Extract on 2.8.0, which keeps each board's binary in a platform folder. (#5402, #5403)
+- **Positions** were dated by when a packet arrived, so firmware 2.8 NodeDB replays made stale fixes look newest (and kept stale likely-aircraft badges). They now carry the observation time. (#5401, #5406)
+- **Auto-Favorite** stacked one more hourly sweep on every reconnect; packet distribution counts ignored per-channel permissions. (#5427)
+- **Nodes list header** controls overflowed a narrow sidebar instead of wrapping. (#5420, #5421)
+- **MeshCore channel reorder** could open and immediately close when clicked just as the channel list loaded. (#5431)
+

title: fix(firmware): match OTA board map to Meshtastic release names (#5423 follow-up)
body:
Refs #5423

Follow-up to #5429. This audits the OTA board map in `src/server/services/firmwareHardwareMap.ts` against the real Meshtastic release names, then fixes every hw model whose board name or platform was wrong.

## How the list was built

- **Release names:** the `firmware-<ver>.json` manifest (`targets[].board/platform`) for **v2.8.0.47db0e3** and **v2.7.26.54e0d8d** (latest stable). For each `firmware-<platform>-<ver>.zip` I also listed the zip's central directory with HTTP range requests, and every ESP32-family manifest board ships exactly one `firmware-<board>-<ver>.bin`. The zip and the manifest agree 1:1.
- **hw model → board:** `custom_meshtastic_hw_model` in `variants/**/platformio.ini` at both tags. Where an env has no tag, I read `HW_VENDOR` from `src/platform/esp32/architecture.h` through the env's `-D` macro.
- **Renames across versions:** none. I diffed the 2.7.18 manifest (our minimum OTA version) against 2.7.26 and 2.8.0: later releases only **add** boards. One board name per hw model serves every OTA-capable version, so the map needs no per-version logic.
- **Underscore names:** `findFirmwareBinary`'s strict regex takes the board name as-is (`[_A-Za-z-]` need no escaping) and `checkBoardInManifest` compares strings exactly, so `thinknode_m2`, `CDEBYTE_EoRa-S3` and `seeed_wio_tracker_L2-tft` match. The new test runs every mapped board through both.

title: fix(firmware): run the OTA lifecycle on the selected source
body:
Refs #5424 (follow-up to #5428)

## Problem
The OTA firmware service disconnected and reconnected the **primary** Meshtastic manager at every step, not the source whose Configuration page started the update. A Meshtastic node accepts one TCP client, so an OTA from a non-primary TCP source freed the wrong node's slot, and the meshtastic CLI then hung on the real target.

## Fix
**Service (`firmwareUpdateService.ts`)**
- `startPreflight` takes `sourceId` and stores it on the update status (`status.sourceId`). It lives for the whole run and clears on cancel/done.
- A new `resolveUpdateManager()` re-resolves that source by id for every manager call: disconnect before backup, reconnect after backup/download/extract/flash failures, post-flash reconnect, verify (`waitForFirmwareVersion`), cancel, retry (via `executeFlash`) and done. Multi-call operations still capture it once (#3962 atomicity).
- If the source is gone mid-update, the service skips its reconnect. It never falls back to another radio, and `disconnectFromNode` fails the step.
- No `sourceId` (legacy single-source install) keeps the old primary/`fallbackManager` resolution.

**Routes (`firmwareUpdateRoutes.ts`)**, still admin-only as before:
- `POST /update`:
  - `400 SOURCE_ID_REQUIRED` when `sourceId` is missing and more than one Meshtastic source is registered.
  - `400 SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` / `409 SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED` via the #5371 `refuseNonMeshtasticSource`.
  - `404 SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id.
  - `400 OTA_GATEWAY_MISMATCH` when the gateway is not the source's own configured host.
  - `409 OTA_IN_PROGRESS` names the source that holds the running update. Before, this was a bare 500 from the service.
- `confirm` / `cancel` / `done` / `retry` return `409 OTA_SOURCE_MISMATCH` when the request's `sourceId` differs from the running update's.

**Frontend (`FirmwareUpdateSection.tsx`)**
- Every OTA call sends the selected `sourceId` from `SourceContext`, or omits it outside a provider.
- Only one OTA can run at a time. When the running update belongs to another source, the page shows a notice instead of that source's wizard modal.

Not changed: `POST /restore` never touched a manager (it only runs the CLI against `gatewayIp`), so it is out of scope here.

## Mesh impact
None. This sends no mesh packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers. It only changes which local TCP connection the OTA flow drops and restores.

## Tests
- `firmwareUpdateService.perSource.test.ts` (new): with A as primary and the update on B, B's manager gets the disconnect and every reconnect path (backup failure, cancel, retry→flash failure, done). Verify reads B's version. A vanished B touches no other radio. The legacy no-sourceId path still uses the primary. 8 of 9 fail on `main`.
- `firmwareUpdateRoutes.perSource.test.ts` (new, `createRouteTestApp` harness): sourceId threaded to preflight with B's bridged check; missing, unknown, MQTT, offline and gateway-mismatch sourceIds refused; busy source name

title: test(meshcore): stabilise MeshCoreChannelsView reorder tests
body:
## Summary

Two tests in the `display order` block of `MeshCoreChannelsView.test.tsx` failed now and then in CI (Node 22, under load) but always passed locally:
- `cancel discards the draft order` (v4.16.2-rc4 Release Pipeline: `Unable to find a label with the text of: Move # Public down` right after clicking Reorder)
- `reorder mode saves a custom order` (PR #5428)

## Root cause (a real component race, not just the tests)

The reorder panel closed through `useEffect(() => setReordering(false), [channelIdsKey])`.

1. The Reorder button first appears (`channels.length > 1`) in the commit that loads the channel list.
2. That same commit changes `channelIdsKey` from the `'0'` fallback to `'0,1,2'`, so the effect is queued. React runs passive effects later, in a scheduler macrotask.
3. `waitFor` sees the rows through a MutationObserver (a microtask) and can resolve before that macrotask runs. Whether it does depends on timing, so it only goes wrong under load.
4. The test clicks Reorder. Before rendering the click's update, React flushes the pending passive effect. The toggle sets `reordering` to true, then the stale effect sets it back to false. The panel never opens, and the next query fails.

A real user can hit the same thing (a click in the first moment after the list loads does nothing), so I fixed the component and did not just add waits to the tests.

## Fix

- `MeshCoreChannelsView.tsx`: store `reorderingFor`, the channel-set key the panel was opened against, and derive `reordering = reorderingFor === channelIdsKey` during render. The effect is gone. A changed channel set still closes the panel, now during render (the standard "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern), so no post-commit effect can undo a click.
- Tests:
  - New regression test: clicks Reorder from a MutationObserver callback so it lands in the gap every time. It **fails on every run against the old component** and passes with the fix.
  - New test: a reconnect refetch with the **same** channel set leaves the panel open, and a refetch that **adds** a slot closes it. This keeps the original safety behavior. It passes on both the old and new component.
  - `findAllByTestId` / `findByLabelText` after clicking Reorder in the existing tests.

## Before / after

| Run | Old component | New component |
|-----|---------------|---------------|
| Regression test (click in the effect gap) | 0/5 pass (fails every run) | 5/5 pass |
| Whole file, 60 runs, 8 in parallel, 16 CPU hogs | 60/60 pass (could not reproduce by load alone on this box) | 60/60 pass |
| `src/components/MeshCore/` | n/a | 593/593 pass |

Load alone did not trigger the flake locally. The deterministic MutationObserver test is the reproduction, and it pins the exact interleaving CI hit.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` (tsconfig.json and tsconfig.server.json): clean
- `npm run lint:ci`: no in-repo FAILs

title: fix(firmware): allow OTA for Station G3 (#5423)
body:
## Summary

MeshMonitor blocked OTA updates for Station G3 devices. Closes #5423.

## Root cause (verified)

`getBoardName(134)` already produced `station-g3` through the default enum-to-board conversion (`STATION_G3` is 134 in our protobufs submodule and in `src/utils/hardwareModel.ts`). The gap was `BOARD_PLATFORM_MAP`: it had no `station-g3` entry, so `getPlatformForBoard` returned `null` and `isOtaCapable` refused the device.

Sources checked:
- `meshtastic/firmware` master, `variants/esp32s3/station-g3/platformio.ini`: `custom_meshtastic_hw_model = 134`, `custom_meshtastic_hw_model_slug = STATION_G3`, `custom_meshtastic_architecture = esp32-s3`, `board_build.mcu = esp32s3`.
- Release `v2.7.26.54e0d8d` (latest stable): the `firmware-2.7.26.54e0d8d.json` manifest lists board `station-g3`. The `firmware-esp32s3-2.7.26.54e0d8d.zip` contains `firmware-station-g3-2.7.26.54e0d8d.bin`, which matches `findFirmwareBinary`'s strict pattern. It also contains `.factory.bin`, `.mt.json`, and `littlefs-…`, which are correctly skipped. The 2.8.0 prerelease manifest lists it too.

## Changes

- `firmwareHardwareMap.ts`: `STATION_G3: 'station-g3'` override (follows the G1/G2 pattern) and `'station-g3': 'esp32s3'`.
- Tests: `getBoardName(134)` gives `station-g3`, its platform is `esp32s3`, and it is OTA capable. `findFirmwareBinary` picks the G3 app binary out of the real v2.7.26 zip entry names.

Targeted vitest run: `success: true` (115 passing). `tsc` passes on the frontend and server configs, and `lint:ci` passes.

## Follow-ups found (not changed here, unverified)

I compared every `HARDWARE_MODELS` entry against the v2.7.26 release manifest.

**Models whose derived board name exists in the manifest but has no platform mapping, so OTA is blocked the same way:**
- `MINI_EPAPER_S3` (125) → `mini-epaper-s3` (esp32s3). This is the same bug as G3 and a likely candidate.
- `HELTEC_MESH_NODE_T096` (127), `HELTEC_MESH_NODE_T1` (133), `T_IMPULSE_PLUS` (135): nrf52840. OTA is not possible on these, so only the platform label is missing.

**Mapped models whose board name does NOT appear in the manifest**, so the manifest check fails even though the platform is known. Some are retired boards. Several look like naming mismatches between our map and the release, for example our `thinknode-m2` against the manifest's `thinknode_m2` (esp32s3), `heltec-sensor-hub` against `heltec_sensor_hub`, `heltec-capsule-sensor-v3` against `heltec_capsule_sensor_v3`, `t-lora-pager` against `tlora-pager`, `tbeam-1-watt` against `t-beam-1w`, `radiomaster-900-bandit-nano` against `radiomaster_900_bandit_nano`, and `m5stack-c6l` against `m5stack-unitc6l`. Each one needs checking against its variant's `platformio.ini` before any change.

title: fix(firmware): OTA uses the source's custom TCP port (#5424)
body:
## Summary

OTA firmware updates ignored a source's custom TCP port and always hit 4403. Closes #5424.

## Root cause (verified)

- **Frontend:** `FirmwareUpdateSection.tsx` built `gatewayIp` from `config.meshtasticNodeIp` only. `config` comes from `/api/poll?sourceId=…` (`usePoll` reads `useSource()`), and `resolveSourceConnectionConfig` returns the **selected source's** `host` and `port`. So the host was already per-source; only the port was dropped.
- **CLI:** the meshtastic CLI accepts `--host host:port`. `meshtastic/__main__.py` (2.7.8) splits `args.host` on `:` and passes the second part to `TCPInterface(portNumber=...)`. `socket.create_connection` accepts the string port.
- **Backend (a second bug the issue comment missed):** passing `host:port` alone would still have failed.
  - `executeBackup` and the verify CLI fallback called `waitForNodeTcpReady(gatewayIp)`, so the raw `10.0.0.5:5000` string became a socket host on port 4403. Backup would hang there.
  - The post-flash reboot wait and the post-failure wait hard-coded port 4403.
  - The #2981 guard compared the raw `gatewayIp` to the env IP. An appended port would slip past it.

## Changes

- New `src/utils/otaGateway.ts`, shared by the frontend and backend:
  - `buildOtaGateway(host, port)` appends `:port` only when the port is valid and not 4403.
  - `parseOtaGateway()` replaces the service's private `parseGateway`. It now keeps a bare IPv6 literal whole (the old parser read `fe80::1` as host `fe80:`, port 1) and accepts `[v6]:port`.
- Frontend: `gatewayIp = buildOtaGateway(meshtasticNodeIp, meshtasticTcpPort)`. The gateway summary now shows `IP: host:port`.
- Service: the backup and verify TCP probes use the parsed host and port. The post-flash and post-failure reboot waits use the source's API port. The OTA loader transfer port (**3232**) is unchanged, since the API port never applies to it.
- Route: the #2981 env-default guard compares the parsed host. IPv6 literals get a clear 400 (`OTA_IPV6_UNSUPPORTED`) before any disconnect, because the CLI's `split(':')` cannot handle IPv6 at all.

## Tests

- `src/utils/otaGateway.test.ts`: build and parse cases, including default port, missing port, out-of-range port, bare and bracketed IPv6, and round-trip.
- `FirmwareUpdateSection.gatewayPort.test.tsx`: the confirm call sends `host:port` for a custom port and the bare host for 4403 or no port. The summary shows the port.
- `firmwareUpdateService.test.ts`: backup probes `(host, 5000)` and passes `--host host:5000`. Flash readiness and the post-failure wait use 5000, the loader wait stays on 3232, and nothing waits on 4403.
- `firmwareUpdateRoutes.test.ts`: `host:port` passes through to preflight, the env-default guard still fires with a port, and IPv6 is rejected.

Targeted vitest run: `success: true` (179 passing). `tsc` passes on the frontend and server configs, and `lint:ci` passes.

## Mesh impact

None. No new packets, timers, or notifications. This only changes which TCP port the exi

title: fix: auto-favorite sweep stacking, distribution channel permissions, SQLite telemetry-types scope
body:
Three small follow-up fixes found during recent work. Each is its own commit.

## 1. A reconnect stacked another hourly Auto-Favorite sweep
Config capture completes again on every reconnect, and it armed the hourly staleness sweep with a bare `setInterval` that nothing ever cleared, so each reconnect added one more sweep.
- The interval now lives on the manager (`armAutoFavoriteSweep()`), is replaced when re-armed, and is cleared in `disconnect()` and `userDisconnect()`.
- Test: arming three times gives one sweep per hour, and disconnect stops it.

## 2. `/api/packets/stats/distribution` ignored per-channel permissions
The distribution counts covered every packet on the source, so a user limited to one channel saw totals and top talkers for channels they can't read. The packet list already filtered these rows in memory; the counts are SQL aggregates, so they now take a `visibility` filter that is the SQL twin of `filterPacketsByPermissions`. A packet is counted if:
- it is encrypted; or
- it is a text DM and the user can read messages; or
- it is not a DM and its channel is null or one the user may read.

The route passes the filter for non-admins; admins are unchanged.
- **Repository tests on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL:** 5 cases each, all 15 passing.
- **Route tests with the real-middleware harness:** a channel-0-only user, `messages:read` adding the DM, and an admin seeing everything.

## 3. `getAllNodesTelemetryTypesAsync` ignored `sourceId` on SQLite
The PostgreSQL/MySQL path scoped the query by source, but the SQLite path ran an unscoped sync query and cached every source's types under the per-source key. The sync query now takes a source scope, and the startup warmup passes `ALL_SOURCES` for the global cache slot. A per-source test covers it.

## Mesh impact
None. No packets are sent. Fix 1 only reduces timer work.

## Tests
- Full Vitest suite: 23,564 passed, 0 failed. The new PG/MySQL suite ran on all three backends.
- `tsc` (app and server) and `lint:ci` are clean.

title: fix(meshcore): page the neighbour table so lists past 10 show (#5413)
body:
Closes #5413
Supersedes #5415

## Problem

The MeshCore Neighbours list stopped at 10. Raising `count` (#5415) cannot fix it: the repeater's `REQ_TYPE_GET_NEIGHBOURS` handler (`examples/simple_repeater/MyMesh.cpp`) packs entries into a 130-byte buffer, 13 bytes each with our 8-byte prefix, and stops when it is full. One reply holds at most 10 entries whatever `count` says. The reply does carry the full table size, so a bigger table has to be walked with `offset`.

## What changed

**Paging** (`src/server/services/meshcoreNeighboursPaging.ts`)
- Reads the table 10 at a time with `offset`, merging pages by prefix (the repeater re-sorts per request, so an entry can move between pages).
- Stops when collected ≥ total (or the offset passes it), a page is empty, the page cap is hit, the user cancels, or a page gets no reply.
- **Every page waits the shared 60 s `lastMeshTxAt` floor** (#4618) and stamps it just before it sends. The check and the stamp run in the same tick, so two senders on one source cannot both go.
- **One login per fetch.** The repeater keeps a logged-in client in its ACL until the table fills and evicts the least-recently-active non-admin (`helpers/ClientACL.cpp`); there is no idle timeout. Pages 2+ pass `skipLogin`.
- 8-byte prefix unchanged.

**Who reads how much**

| Caller | Pages | order_by |
|---|---|---|
| Contact Details "Neighbours" button | up to 5 (the 50-entry table) | 0 newest |
| Neighbours Retrieval "Poll Neighbours" button | up to 5 | 0 newest |
| Autopoll scheduler | 1 (unchanged) | **2 strongest** |
| Auto-pathfinding | 1 (automated, unchanged) | 0 |
| `GET /contacts/:pk/neighbours` and `POST /nodes/:pk/neighbours/poll` (API) | 1, as before | as requested / 2 |

**Storage: never shrink a fuller set**
- All pages are collected, then stored **once**.
- A complete read replaces the stored set (it may rightly shrink or empty).
- Anything less (the scheduler's one page, the page cap, a cancel, a failure part-way) **merges**: fresh rows win, other stored rows stay with their heard age moved forward, trimmed to the table size the repeater reported. So the autopoll's one strongest-first page no longer undoes a manual 5-page read, and a cancelled or failed fetch keeps the stored set. A fetch that got nothing leaves the stored set untouched. I chose merge over "store only if larger" because it keeps the fresh rows from a partial read without ever dropping stored rows the partial read did not see.

**Progress and Cancel** (mirrors the #5400 login work)
- `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/nodes/:pk/neighbours/fetch` `{ requestId }` answers at once and runs the fetch in the background (a 5-minute open request would hit proxy timeouts).
- `GET .../neighbours/fetch/:requestId` returns the page, planned pages, table size, neighbours gathered so far, and time to the next page. `POST .../neighbours/fetch/:requestId/cancel` stops further pages.
- Registry (`meshcoreNeighboursFetchProgress.ts`) is in memory, private to the user and sour

title: feat: asset tracking Phase 3 — timeline playback (#5354)
body:
Phase 3, the last phase of the Asset Tracking epic: timeline playback. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ASSET_TRACKING_P3_SPEC.md`. Phases 1 and 2 were #5411 and #5419.

Closes #5354.

![playback bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5354-asset-p3/docs/public/images/features/asset-playback-bar.png)
![marker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5354-asset-p3/docs/public/images/features/asset-playback-marker.png)
![phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5354-asset-p3/docs/public/images/features/asset-playback-bar-mobile.png)

## What it does
A playback bar appears along the bottom of the **Nodes map** when an asset is selected and Show Position History is on.
- **Timeline:** one notch per fix, drawn as a single SVG, with gaps shaded. Drag or click to seek.
- **Controls:** play/pause, step one fix back or forward, and **60× / 600× / 3600×** speeds; the last speed is remembered.
- **Readout:** the fix time and date at the cursor, in the user's date and time format.
- **On the map:**
  - A **moving marker** slides between fixes with a time label. Inside a gap it holds at the last fix instead of cutting across.
  - **Trail up to cursor** is on by default. **Follow** is off by default; when on, it pans only when the marker leaves the middle 70 % of the view, at most once every 500 ms.
- **Performance:** the marker moves directly on the map each animation frame. The trail and readout update at about 5 Hz, and the trail rebuilds only when the cursor passes a fix.
- **Keyboard:** Space plays or pauses, ←/→ step, Home/End jump. The timeline is an ARIA slider.
- **Phone width:** the bar fits on one row. The step buttons hide; the arrow keys and dragging still step.
- It resets when the node changes, the history reloads, or Show Position History turns off. The traceroute banner moves up so it isn't hidden behind the bar.

## Mesh impact
None. Frontend only; no new requests.

## Tests
- Full Vitest suite: 23,542 tests, 0 failed. The PG/MySQL suites skip locally because this phase has no database changes; CI runs them. `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.
- **Unit tests** for `trackPlayback`: interpolation, gap hold, binary-search edges, gaps.
- **19 component tests** with a mocked animation clock: play, pause, stop at end, restart, stepping, speed persistence, keyboard, trail-up-to-cursor callback, follow only when off-centre, reset on node change.
- A **wiring test** for when the bar shows.
- **Dev container check** with a seeded 20-hour, 2,641-fix asset track:
  - At 3600× the cursor advanced about 1 hour per second, and the trail grew with the marker at its head.
  - Follow panned the map.
  - At 390 px wide the bar fitted in one row with no page scroll.
  - The seed data has since been removed.
