+# Asset Tracking Phase 3: timeline playback (#5354)
+
+See `ASSET_TRACKING_EPIC.md`. Phases 1 (#5411) and 2 (#5419) added the asset flag, retention, and the full-history thinned trail with gap segments (`segmentStart` markers, see `flattenAssetTrack` / `segmentBreaks` in `src/utils/positionHistoryDownsample.ts`).
+
+## Decisions (user, 2026-09-27)
+
+- **D1 Placement:** a playback bar along the bottom of the **Nodes map** (`NodesTab.tsx`). It shows only when the selected node is an asset (`selectedNode.asset`), Show Position History is on, and more than one fix is loaded.
+- **D2 Speeds:** **60×, 600× and 3600×** (1 min, 10 min, or 1 h of track per second). The last speed used is remembered in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch.
+- **D3 Map during playback:**
+  - A **moving marker** slides along the track, interpolated between fixes, with a time label.
+  - **Trail up to cursor:** a toggle, **on** by default. While the cursor isn't at the end, only fixes at or before the cursor are drawn.
+  - **Follow:** a toggle, **off** by default. It pans the map to keep the marker in view.
+
+## Mesh impact
+
+None. This is frontend only; it adds no requests.
+
+## Behaviour
+
+- **Timeline:** runs from the first to the last fix of the history currently shown, after the existing hours-slider filter.
+  - **Notches:** one per fix, drawn as a single SVG path or canvas. Up to 2,000 fixes, so not 2,000 DOM nodes.
+  - **Gaps:** shaded regions on the timeline.
+- **Cursor:**
+  - It starts at the end, which is today's full trail, so nothing changes until the user interacts.
+  - Dragging or clicking the timeline seeks.
+  - Pressing Play at the end restarts from the beginning.
+  - Playback stops at the end.
+- **Readout:** the fix time and calendar date at the cursor, using the user's time and date format settings (`useDisplaySettings` / `formatDateTime` helpers). Also the nearest fix's speed, when known.
+- **Interpolation:**
+  - Between two fixes in the **same segment**, interpolate lat/lon linearly by time.
+  - Inside a **gap**, don't interpolate across it: hold the marker at the last fix of the previous segment and dim it.
+  - Put this in a pure `src/utils/trackPlayback.ts`:
+    - `positionAt(fixes, t)` returns `{lat, lon, index, inGap}`;
+    - `indexAtOrBefore(fixes, t)`;
+    - `timelineGaps(fixes)`.
+  - Binary search on timestamps.
+- **Animation:**
+  - `requestAnimationFrame` advances the cursor by `elapsed × speed`.
+  - Move the marker **imperatively** through a Leaflet marker ref (`setLatLng`), not by re-rendering React each frame.
+  - Throttle the React state that drives "trail up to cursor" and the readout to about 5 Hz, so the up to 2,000 polylines aren't rebuilt every frame.
+- **Follow:** when on, pan (`map.panTo`, animate) only when the marker leaves the middle 70 % of the view, throttled to at most one pan every 500 ms.
+- **Controls, in a new `src/components/map/AssetPlaybackBar.tsx` with a CSS module:**
+  - Play/Pause and step back/forward one fix (use `UiIcon`, no emoji).
+  - The speed select.
+  - The "Trail up to cursor" and "Follow" checkboxes.
+  - The readout and the timeline.
+  - The bar collapses to one row at phone width, with no horizontal scroll.
+- **Keyboard,** while the timeline has focus: Space plays or pauses, ←/→ step one fix, Home/End jump. The timeline is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` set to the readout.
+- **Lifecycle:** stop and reset when the selected node changes, the history reloads, Show Position History turns off, or the component unmounts. Cancel the RAF.
+- **Wiring:**
+  - NodesTab passes the flattened asset history (the `positionHistory` already in MapContext, after the hours filter) and the Leaflet map instance.
+  - The trail-rendering code (NodesTab ~868–994) takes an optional `cursorTime`. When it is set and trail-up-to-cursor is on, drop fixes after it before downsampling and segmenting.
+  - The existing arrows and popups keep working.
+- **i18n:** `en.json` keys under `map.playback.*`.
+- **Docs:** a "Playback" paragraph in the Asset Tracking section of `docs/features/maps.md`.
+
+## Tests
+
+- **Unit tests for `trackPlayback`:**
+  - interpolation mid-segment;
+  - exactly at a fix;
+  - before the first and after the last fix;
+  - inside a gap (held and flagged);
+  - `indexAtOrBefore` edge cases;
+  - `timelineGaps`.

+  - Play at the end restarts.
+  - Step buttons.
+  - Speed is persisted.
+  - The keyboard keys work.
+  - Trail-up-to-cursor calls back with the cursor time.
+  - Follow pans only when the marker is off-centre.
+  - It resets when the node changes.

+

+
+- The tests above pass. The full suite passes; this change has no DB work, so PG/MySQL skips are acceptable here. `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

+  - playing moves the marker and grows the trail;
+  - the gap holds the marker;
+  - follow pans;
+  - the bar works at phone width.

title: feat: asset tracking Phase 2 — full-history trail with shape-preserving thinning (#5354)
body:
Phase 2 of the Asset Tracking epic (#5354): the Nodes map draws an asset's **whole retained history**, instead of stopping at 5,000 fixes. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ASSET_TRACKING_P2_SPEC.md`. Phase 1 was #5411.

Part of #5354. Phase 3 (timeline playback) follows.

![full-history trail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5354-asset-p2/docs/public/images/features/asset-full-history-trail.png)

*A seeded 5-day, 7,681-fix track drawn as 1,923 points. The break in the middle is a 2-hour gap.*

## What it does
- **`GET /api/assets/:nodeNum/track`** reads the asset's position history across every source the caller can see.
  - It pages 10,000 rows at a time and thins as it goes, so it never holds the whole window in memory.
  - A fix heard by several sources counts once.
  - Access follows the same rules as `/position-history`: `nodes:read` per source, private overrides checked per source, and channel `viewOnMap`.
  - An asset the caller can't see returns 404 `NOT_AN_ASSET`, so the flag doesn't leak.
  - Results are cached for 60 s and cleared when the asset changes.

+# Asset Tracking Phase 2: full-history trail (#5354)
+
+See `ASSET_TRACKING_EPIC.md`. Phase 1 (#5411) added the asset flag, per-asset retention, and the forced trail.
+
+## Problem
+
+For the selected node, the Nodes map pages `GET /api/nodes/:nodeId/position-history` (`src/App.tsx` ~1330–1370). Each page holds 1,500 telemetry rows, and paging stops at `MAX_ACCUMULATED_POSITION_FIXES` = 5,000 fixes. The client then downsamples to `MAX_RENDERED_POSITION_POINTS` = 500.
+
+An asset keeps up to 365 days of fixes. A node reporting every 30 s makes about 260k fixes over 90 days, so the map shows only the newest few days of an asset's history.
+
+## Decisions (user, 2026-09-27)
+
+- **D1 Point budget:** an asset's trail draws at most **2,000** points. Non-assets are unchanged (500).
+- **D2 Shape-preserving thinning on the server.** Split the window into equal time buckets, and keep the first, the last, and the fix farthest from the first-to-last chord in each bucket. Turns and stops survive.
+- **D3 Gaps:** break the trail when two consecutive fixes are more than **30 min** apart. Each drive then draws as its own segment, with no straight line across town.
+
+## Server: `GET /api/assets/:nodeNum/track?hours=&sources=a,b`
+
+- **Access:** mount it on `assetRoutes`, which already has `router.use(optionalAuth())`.
+  - Sources come from `resolvePermittedSourceIds(req)`, which requires `nodes:read` per source, intersected with `sources` when given.
+  - If the node has a private position override (`positionOverrideIsPrivate` on any permitted row) and the caller lacks `nodes_private:read` on that source, drop that source's rows. This mirrors `nodesRoutes` `/position-history` (~680) and `buildPositionFilter`.
+  - Also honour the channel `viewOnMap` rule the way `buildPositionFilter` does for non-admins.
+- **Guards:**
+  - 404 `NOT_AN_ASSET` if the node isn't in `asset_nodes`.
+  - `hours` is clamped to 1 … `retentionDays × 24`, defaulting to the full retention.
+- **Streaming read, so memory stays bounded:**
+  - Page through the node's `latitude`/`longitude`/`altitude`/`ground_speed`/`ground_track` telemetry rows for the permitted sources, oldest first, 10,000 rows per page, with a timestamp cursor.
+  - Pivot rows into fixes with the existing `positionHistoryPivot.ts` logic.
+  - Feed each fix into a bucket accumulator, which keeps only first/last/farthest per bucket.
+  - Never hold the whole window in memory.
+  - Add a repository method for the paged read (`telemetry.getPositionRowsForNodeNumPage({nodeNum, sourceIds, sinceMs, afterTs, limit})`), which must be dialect-agnostic.
+- **Cross-source dedupe:** an asset heard by several sources arrives once per source. Treat fixes within 5 s of each other with the same lat/lon (to 5 decimals) as one fix.
+- **Thinning, in pure `src/utils/trackThinning.ts`:**
+  - `buckets = ceil(2000 / 3)`. The bucket width is `window / buckets`.
+  - For each bucket, keep the first, last and farthest-from-chord fix, deduped.
+  - Always keep the first and last fix of each gap segment.
+  - Output is at most 2,000 points. If gap-segment endpoints push it over, drop from the densest buckets.
+  - Gap detection runs on the full stream before thinning: consecutive kept fixes more than 30 min apart start a new segment.
+- **Response:**
+
+  ```
+  ok(res, {
+    nodeNum, retentionDays, windowStartMs,
+    totalFixes,        // before thinning
+    segments: [ [ { latitude, longitude, altitude, timestamp, groundSpeed?, groundTrack? } … ] … ]
+  })
+  ```
+
+  Keep the fix fields compatible with the client's `PositionHistoryItem`, so the existing arrows and popups keep working.
+- **Cache:** 60 s in memory, keyed by (nodeNum, hours, sorted permitted sourceIds), with a small LRU cap.
+- **Tests:**
+  - **Unit tests for thinning:** budget respected; a turn survives; gap split at 30 min; segment endpoints kept; cross-source dedupe.
+  - **Route harness tests:** permission isolation, private override, `NOT_AN_ASSET`, hours clamping.
+  - **Multi-backend repository test** for the paged read, with isolated PG/MySQL databases.
+
+## Client
+
+- **App.tsx fetch (~1300–1370):** when `selectedNode.asset` is set, call `GET /api/assets/:nodeNum/track` once, through `ApiService`, instead of the paged loop. There is no `MAX_ACCUMULATED_POSITION_FIXES` cap on this path.
+  - Store the result so the map can tell segments apart. Add a `segmentStart?: true` marker on the first fix of each segment after the first, or store segments directly, whichever fits `positionHistory` in MapContext best.
+  - Non-assets keep today's path unchanged.
+- **NodesTab rendering (~868–994):**
+  - For an asset, use a render cap of 2,000, since the server already thinned the track; never downsample below the server output.
+  - **Do not join points across a segment boundary.** No polyline segment and no spline from the last fix of one segment to the first of the next.
+  - Arrows and popups stay as they are.
+  - "Points only" mode is unaffected.
+- **Slider:** it already ranges from the oldest loaded fix to now, so it covers the full retention automatically. Keep the "All" label.
+- **Legend / hint:** for an asset, show "Showing N of M fixes (thinned)" when `totalFixes > N`. Add the `en.json` key.
+
+## Mesh impact
+
+None. This only reads stored data.
+
+## Exit criteria
+
+- All the tests above pass.
+- The full suite passes with PG/MySQL up (create them with `docker run`; `docker start` won't bring back stopped `--rm` containers). `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

+  - the whole window draws;
+  - a gap longer than 30 min shows as a break;
+  - the point count is ≤ 2,000.

title: feat(mqtt): drop automation-originated packets at the bridge uplink (#5414)
body:
Closes #5414

## Summary

The firmware ORs `config.lora.config_ok_to_mqtt` into every phone-API packet (meshtastic/firmware#11994), so MeshMonitor cannot clear the `ok_to_mqtt` bit on one automated send. This PR adds a per-bridge option, **Don't uplink MeshMonitor automation traffic** (`dropAutomationUplinks`, default **off**), that keeps MeshMonitor's own automation sends off the upstream broker. They still go out over LoRa and to the local broker.

## How it works

- **Tagging at the send call.** The Meshtastic send methods take an optional `origin: 'automation' | 'manual'`. Absent means manual, so an untagged new automation keeps today's behaviour instead of silently eating a user's message. Inside `MeshtasticManager`, every queue send goes through `enqueueAutomation()` and auto-ping replies through `sendAutomationText()`.
- **Tracker** (`src/server/utils/automationPacketTracker.ts`): one map per sending source of `packetId → { fromNodeNum, expiresAt }`. It records the id the protobuf builder stamps on the MeshPacket, before `transport.send`. TTL 30 s, hard cap 512 per source, lazy eviction (no interval timer).
- **Multi-source:** a match needs both the packet id and the `from` node number of the source that sent it. An automation on source A only matches packets A's own node originated. A packet from B's node with the same 32-bit id is uplinked. The bridge's broker has no fixed link to a TCP source (devices can reach it directly or via `mqttLink`), so matching on the originating node is how the bridge tells "A's packet".
- **Drop rule:** `MqttBridgeManager.handleUplink` checks the tracker after the echo/pre-filter checks and before the `ok_to_mqtt` gate (a cheap sync lookup that also saves a decrypt). Matches increment the new `uplinkAutomationDrops`, next to `uplinkOkToMqttDrops` in the bridge status.
- **UI:** the bridge Configuration page adds a checkbox with help text naming the limits, and shows both drop counters.

### What is tagged as automation

Auto-ack (tapbacks + text), auto-responder (incl. script/mailbox/traceroute replies), timer and geofence triggers, auto-welcome, auto-ping, scheduled auto-announce and its NodeInfo broadcasts, Automation Engine actions (send message/DM, tapback, requestData: telemetry/position/traceroute/nodeinfo/neighbors/advert), auto-traceroute, key-repair NodeInfo exchanges (scheduled + immediate purge), remote LocalStats polling, telemetry hijack auto-retry, auto-favorite NeighborInfo requests, auto-enrichment NodeInfo pushes, and waypoint rebroadcasts.

Automated traceroutes used to leave the packet id to the firmware. They now carry an explicit random id (`crypto.randomInt`) so they can be matched. Manual traceroutes are unchanged.

### Not tagged (manual)

Route handlers (UI send, v1 API, including the v1 queued send), the **Send Announcement** button (`triggeredByAutomation=false`), manual NodeInfo copy/push, the key-mismatch warning route, virtual-node client traffic. Remote-admin packets (favorite/

title: fix(helm): add service.extraPorts to expose Virtual Node ports in K8s
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5416: the Helm chart never opens a Virtual Node Server port, and (follow-up on the issue) gives no way to pin the LoadBalancer IP.

- Since 4.0, Virtual Node is enabled per source from the Dashboard UI (not env vars), and the user picks an arbitrary TCP port there.
- The chart's `Deployment`/`Service` templates only wired up the web UI port, so a Virtual Node port existed only inside the pod's network namespace.
- The reporter then asked how to select the LoadBalancer IP. Bare-metal load balancers read it from a Service annotation, which the chart had no way to set.
- Bonus find: `docs/configuration/virtual-node.md` showed a `service.ports` list the templates never supported.

## Changes

**Commit 1 (`service.extraPorts`)**
- `service.extraPorts` (empty by default): each entry becomes a `containerPort` and a Service port.

**Commit 2 (LB IP selection + separate Virtual Node Service)**
- `service.annotations`: rendered into Service metadata. Pins the IP with MetalLB (`metallb.io/loadBalancerIPs`, older `metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs`), kube-vip (`kube-vip.io/loadbalancerIPs`), Cilium LB-IPAM (`lbipam.cilium.io/ips`) or a cloud provider's own key.
- `service.loadBalancerIP` (deprecated upstream, kept for LBs that still honour it), `loadBalancerClass`, `loadBalancerSourceRanges`: render only for `type: LoadBalancer`. `externalTrafficPolicy`: `LoadBalancer`/`NodePort` only. `nodePort` on the main port and each `extraPorts` entry: `NodePort`/`LoadBalancer` only. A leftover value on a `ClusterIP` Service never renders into an invalid spec.
- `virtualNodeService` (disabled by default): a second Service (`<fullname>-virtual-node`) selecting the same pod, with its own `type`, `annotations`, `loadBalancerIP`, `loadBalancerClass`, `loadBalancerSourceRanges`, `externalTrafficPolicy` and `ports`. Lets the web UI stay ClusterIP behind an Ingress while only the raw-TCP Virtual Node port(s) go out on a LoadBalancer with a pinned IP. Its ports get `containerPort`s, deduped against `service.extraPorts` by name and by port+protocol (k8s rejects duplicates). Enabling it with an empty `ports` list fails the render with a clear message.
- Shared helpers in `_helpers.tpl` (`meshmonitor.serviceTypeFields`, `meshmonitor.virtualNodeContainerPorts`).
- Docs (`docs/configuration/virtual-node.md`, `helm/README.md`): annotation table, MetalLB example, separate-Service example, note that an Ingress/HTTPRoute can't carry Virtual Node traffic, and that k3s's built-in ServiceLB (klipper-lb) can't pin an IP (it answers on node IPs).
- No chart version bump: prior helm-only PRs (#3434, #2448) left `Chart.yaml` alone; release bumps handle it.

Example (the reporter's question):

```yaml
service:
  type: LoadBalancer
  annotations:
    metallb.io/loadBalancerIPs: 192.168.1.240
  extraPorts:
    - name: virtual-node
      port: 4404
      targetPort: 4404
```

## Test plan

Run with `helm` v4.3.0 via `docker run alpine/helm`, schema-checked with `kubeconform -

title: feat: sign-flip follow-ups — geofences, traceroute snapshots, MeshCore (#5363)
body:
Refs #5363 (follow-up to #5409)

Everything here applies only when sign-flip correction is on for the source; with it off, behaviour is unchanged. The stored data (node rows, traceroute snapshots, MeshCore contacts) is never modified.

## (a) Automation geofences use the corrected position

- **Automation Engine `trigger.geofence`** (`automationEngineService.checkGeofences`): the node's point is passed through a new optional `NodeDataProvider.correctPosition`. The real provider (`meshNodeData.ts`) applies the shared detector with the node's source context; a provider without it, or a failure, falls back to the reported point. The engine stays DB-free.
- **Per-source geofence triggers** (`MeshtasticManager`): initial state, the per-position check (`checkGeofencesForNode`, now also given the sender's precision bits) and the while-inside re-check all use the corrected point.
- Consequence to know: turning correction on can make a flipped node "enter" a fence on its next position update — a single real transition, subject to the trigger's own cooldown. No new timers.

## (b) Traceroute `routePositions` snapshots corrected at display time

`correctRoutePositionsJson` / `applySignFlipToTraceroute(s)` correct each snapshot point with the same detector as the markers, per row's own source. Applied to `/api/poll` traceroutes, `/api/traceroutes/recent` and `/history`, the dashboard/unified bundle (`buildSourceTraceroutes`), and the live `traceroute:complete` WebSocket event (a copy; the event bus keeps the reported row). The embed already draws from live (corrected) positions. Not covered: the public `/api/v1` traceroute API (data API, not a display surface).

## (c) MeshCore support

- Reference: a MeshCore companion's own advertised position (`getLocalNode()`); a MeshCore MQTT ingest source has none, so it needs the manual point.
- Server: contacts/nodes corrected in `/snapshot`, `/contacts`, `/contacts/refresh`, `/nodes`, the live `meshcore:contact:updated` WebSocket event, the dashboard/unified bundle's MeshCore branch, and the MeshCore rows of `/api/nodes`. Positions masked by `viewOnMap` stay masked.
- UI: the settings live in the MeshCore **Node Display** section (same four per-source keys, read-only without `settings:write`); the MeshCore map popup (`MeshCoreDetails`) and the contact details panel show the "Position auto-corrected (sign flip)" notice with the reported coordinates.

## (d) Settings checkbox layout

The toggle sat centred above "Correct sign-flipped positions" because the global `.setting-item label { flex-direction: column }` outranks a module class on the label. It now uses an inner row span, like the other Node Display checkboxes.

**Screenshot:** not attached — per instructions I did not deploy the dev container. Needed for the settings row (both the Meshtastic Settings tab and the MeshCore Node Display section) and the MeshCore popup/contact notice.

## Mesh impact

No packets, notifications or timers are added. Geofence trigger

title: feat: asset tracking Phase 1 — asset flag, per-asset retention, forced trail (#5354)
body:
Phase 1 of the Asset Tracking epic (#5354). Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ASSET_TRACKING_EPIC.md`, spec: `ASSET_TRACKING_P1_SPEC.md`.

Part of #5354. Phase 2 (full-history trail) and Phase 3 (timeline playback) follow.

![asset section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5354-asset-p1/docs/public/images/features/asset-tracking-section.png)

## What it does
- **Asset flag, per physical node:** it applies across all sources, like the solar override. It's set in Node Details → **Asset tracking** by users with `settings:write`, and is read-only for everyone else. Migration 181 adds the global `asset_nodes` table, which is included in backups.
- **Retention:** 1–365 days per asset (default 90) for **all** of the asset's telemetry on every source. The section shows an estimated row count.
  - The hourly purge keeps asset rows until their own window has passed, on both SQLite and PG/MySQL.
  - A favourite that is also an asset keeps the longer window, row by row.
- **Always a trail:** the payload's `isMobile` becomes `mobile || asset`. So a parked asset still loads and draws its trail. This was the original bug: a node back from a trip showed no history.
  - It's a computed overlay only. The `mobile` column, the `becameMobile` trigger and the `node.mobile` automation token stay heuristic-only, so flagging an asset never fires `becameMobile`.
  - Mesh Issues and the automations node picker treat an asset as mobile.
- **Automated cleanups skip assets:** auto-delete-by-distance, the aircraft age-out, and the automation "delete node" action. The MQTT geo filter still ignores an asset but no longer purges it.
  - A manual Delete/Purge still works, and warns that it removes the retained history.
- **API:** `GET /api/assets` (filtered to the caller's permitted sources), `PUT`/`DELETE /api/assets/:nodeNum` (`settings:write`, audited), and `GET /api/assets/:nodeNum/estimate`.

## Mesh impact
None. Storage and UI only; nothing is sent over the mesh, no events fire, and no timers are added. Retention lives in the database, and the purge is idempotent across restarts.

## Tests
- Full Vitest suite with PostgreSQL and MySQL up: 23,335 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` (app and server) and `lint:ci` are clean.
- Multi-backend retention tests cover:
  - an asset's row older than 7 days surviving;
  - a row past the asset's window being deleted;
  - asset combined with favourite, in both directions;
  - assets with no favourites configured.
- Route tests use the real-middleware harness, including `optionalAuth` on the router. That caught a production bug where GET filtering treated every caller as anonymous.
- **Dev container checks:**
  - NMIA G2 is stationary by the heuristic (`mobile: 0`). Once flagged, it came back with `isMobile: true` and its position history loaded on the Nodes map.
  - The section saved and showed the estimate.
  - After seeding 10-day-old rows and restarting, the purge kept the asset's rows and deleted the non-asset's ("0 from

+# Asset Tracking Epic (#5354)
+
+## Goal
+
+Let an operator mark a node as a tracked **asset**, for example a GPS node on a vehicle. For an asset, MeshMonitor:
+- keeps its history for a chosen period;
+- always draws its trail, whatever the mobility heuristic says;
+- can draw its full history on the map;
+- can play that history back.
+
+The issue began as "pin the mobile flag" (a node parked after a trip showed no trail, because the 100 m / 500-fix heuristic had flipped it to stationary). It grew into this.
+
+## Decisions (user, 2026-09-27)
+
+- **Delivery:** an epic in 3 phases, each usable on its own.
+- **Scope:** one flag per **physical node** (nodeNum), global across sources, like the solar override (#3195). Visibility still follows each viewer's source permissions.
+- **Retention:** per asset, default **90 days**, range 1–365. The setting shows an estimated row count.
+- **What is kept:** **all telemetry** for the asset (position, battery, environment and so on), on every source that heard it.
+- **Permission:** `settings:write`, matching the solar override, because the flag extends storage on every source.
+- **Protection:** **automated** cleanups skip assets, as they already skip favourites. That covers auto-delete-by-distance, the aircraft age-out, the MQTT geo-filter purge, and the automation "delete node" action. A manual Delete Node still works, with a warning that it removes the retained history.
+
+## Phases
+
+### Phase 1: the asset flag, forced trail, and retention
+- [x] A global `asset_nodes` table: nodeNum PK, `retentionDays`, audit columns (migration 181).
+- [x] A PUT/DELETE route gated by `settings:write`. Reads are filtered to nodes on the caller's permitted sources.
+- [x] An "Asset tracking" section in Node Details: an enable switch, retention days, and the estimated rows.
+- [x] The node payload gains an `asset` field. The effective `isMobile` is `mobile || asset`. This is a computed overlay: the `mobile` column and the `becameMobile` trigger stay heuristic-only.
+- [x] The telemetry purge exempts assets up to their own retention.
+- [x] Automated node deleters skip assets.
+
+**Exit:**
+- A parked asset still draws its trail.
+- Its telemetry survives the 7-day purge and is removed after its own window.
+- An automated cleanup doesn't delete it.
+- A restart doesn't change any of this.
+
+### Phase 2: full-history trail
+- [ ] Replace the client's 5,000-fix cap with server-side time-bucket downsampling across the whole retained window, for assets.
+
+### Phase 3: timeline playback
+- [ ] A scrubber at the bottom of the map for a selected asset: a notch per fix, play/pause, speed, a time readout, and a "trail up to cursor" mode.
+
+## Mesh impact
+
+None in any phase. Everything is storage and UI; nothing is sent over the mesh.
+
+## Status log
+
+- 2026-09-27: epic planned; Phase 1 started on `feature/5354-asset-p1`.
+- 2026-09-27: Phase 1 implemented on `feature/5354-asset-p1`. Deviations from the spec:
+  - Purge: a favourite that is also an asset keeps the longer window **per row**. The favourite phase skips rows an asset window still covers, and the asset phase skips rows a favourite window still covers. The spec's "exclude assets from phase 2, let phase 3 decide" would have deleted favourite rows between the asset and favourite cutoffs whenever the favourite window was longer.
+  - Estimate endpoint scopes by the per-source `nodes:read` grant. `info` (the telemetry grant) is a global resource, so it can't narrow the count to permitted sources.

+  - Mesh Issues: `PooledNode` gains an optional `asset` flag; B5 treats an asset as mobile. The raw `mobile` value in finding evidence is unchanged.

title: feat: ADS-B flight matching for likely aircraft (#5374)
body:
Closes #5374. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ADSB_MATCH_SPEC.md`.

When a node becomes a **likely aircraft** (#5364/#5365), MeshMonitor can ask a free community ADS-B feed which aircraft is at that spot. The node popup and details then show the flight, linked to the feed's map with a credit.

![popup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5374-adsb-match/docs/public/images/features/adsb-flight-match-popup.png)

## What it does
- **Feeds:** adsb.lol (default) or adsb.fi. They share one client and one parser, since both return readsb JSON.
  - Off by default: a stock install makes no third-party calls.
  - airplanes.live was dropped from v1 because it returned 403 to anonymous requests in a live check.
- **Two lookups per flagging, at most:**
  - One runs when the node becomes flagged, giving "Possible match".
  - One runs on the node's next live position, 1–30 min later, giving "Matched" if it finds the same aircraft (ICAO hex).
  - The count lives in the database, so a restart can't allow extra lookups.
  - A failed lookup doesn't count, and a failed first lookup is retried on a later live position.
  - A node flagged on several sources at once makes one HTTP request.
- **Matching:**
  - The search radius grows with the age of the node's fix, from 5 to 90 km.
  - The aircraft must be within ±300 m of the node's altitude; aircraft on the ground are skipped.
  - If a second aircraft is nearly as close as the nearest, it reports no match.
  - **A match only confirms.** No match never clears the likely-aircraft flag.
- **Settings:** global, next to Elevation. An enable switch, a feed select showing each feed's terms, and an optional API key for adsb.lol's announced future key.
- **Also fixed:** a non-admin save of the Settings page could wipe a secret key, because non-admins never receive secret keys and the page posted them blank. `POST /api/settings` now drops secret keys from non-admin writers. This also covers `elevationSourceUrl`, which had the same gap.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** none. Outbound HTTPS only.
- **Rate:**
  - At most 2 requests per node per flagging, with a global queue spacing requests ≥ 1.1 s apart.
  - A 10-minute global backoff follows 429/403/5xx, timeouts or network errors.
  - A 60 s retry floor applies per node, and the queue is capped at 100.
- **Spam:** no notifications, events or automation triggers.
- **Timers:** the lookup allowance is persisted per flagging. A restart or settings save neither triggers a lookup nor resets the allowance.

## Tests
- Full Vitest suite with PostgreSQL and MySQL up: 23,209 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` (app and server) and `lint:ci` are clean.
- **Unit tests:** the matcher, feed parsing (fixtures in the live-response shape), and the lookup cap. Also covered: episodes, a restart not resetting the cap, backoff, cross-source reuse, and the failed-first-lookup retry. No test makes a network call.
- **Route and settings tests:** the flight-match route's per-source isolation

title: feat: detect and correct sign-flipped node positions (#5363)
body:
Closes #5363

## What

Operators in the western or southern hemisphere sometimes type their coordinates without the minus sign, so the node lands on the far side of the globe. With this change, when a position is **outside** the configured range of a reference point but **exactly one** mirror variant — `(-lat, lon)`, `(lat, -lon)` or `(-lat, -lon)` — is inside it, the maps show the mirror point and the node says so.

Skipped (position left as reported): 0 or 2+ matching variants (a node near the equator or prime meridian is ambiguous), unknown reference, missing / out-of-range / Null Island fixes (via `isBogusPosition`, including the precision-obscured `(offset, offset)` re-centred (0,0)), user overrides, and trilaterated estimates.

## Settings (Settings → Node Display, per source)

| Key | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `signFlipCorrectionEnabled` | off | |
| `signFlipCorrectionRangeKm` | 500 km (~311 mi) | stored in km like `autoDeleteByDistanceThresholdKm`, shown in the user's km/mi unit; clamped 10–2000 km |
| `signFlipReferenceLatitude` / `Longitude` | blank | blank = the source's own node (`getLocalNodeNumForSource` → its row, override honoured); a manual point wins |

Per source, matching the aircraft-detection keys (`SIGN_FLIP_NODE_DISPLAY_KEYS` joins `NODE_DISPLAY_SETTING_KEYS`, so it rides the existing scoped `?sourceId=` POST and GET back-fill skip). The reference is naturally per source. An MQTT source has no own node, so it needs a manual point; the help text says so.

The 2000 km cap is deliberate: the wider the circle, the likelier a genuine far-away node (e.g. heard over MQTT) has a mirror inside it. A Sydney node heard on a US MQTT source has its `(33, -151)` mirror ~1,800 km off California. The UI warns next to the input.

## Where the correction happens (and why server-side)

Pure detector: `src/utils/signFlipPosition.ts` (shared, unit tested). Server applier: `src/server/services/signFlipCorrection.ts`, applied where node payloads leave the API:

- `/api/poll` nodes (Nodes tab map, node list, node details)
- `/api/nodes?sourceId=` and `/api/nodes/active` (per row's own source; an unscoped `/api/nodes` returns rows merged across sources, so it has no single reference and is left alone)
- `buildSourceNodes` + `buildSourceNeighborInfo` → `/api/sources/:id/nodes`, `/api/sources/:id/dashboard`, `/api/unified/dashboard` (Dashboard map, Map Analysis)
- `/api/neighbor-info` (both routes)
- embed `/nodes`, `/neighborinfo`, `/traceroutes`

Server-side because the reference is per source and the unified views merge N sources' rows **before** the map sees them: correcting each source's rows first keeps the corrected point and its `reportedLatitude/Longitude` pair on the same record. The client merge (`mergeNodeRecords`) now carries `positionSignFlipCorrected` / `reportedLatitude` / `reportedLongitude` only from the record whose position was chosen, like the aircraft fields.

New API fields on a corrected node: `positionSignFlipCorrect

title: feat(map): separate clustering toggle from the Map Click Zoom Gate
body:
Closes #5404

## Summary
`mapZoomGateThreshold` drove both marker clustering and the click zoom gate / spiderfy, so turning off clustering (`0`) also turned off the gate. This adds an independent toggle.

- New global setting `mapClusteringEnabled` (boolean, **default on**, so nothing changes for existing users). Stored exactly like `mapZoomGateThreshold`: `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, SettingsContext state + localStorage + server load, SettingsTab draft/baseline/re-seed/reset/`handleSave` literal.
- `resolveClusterZoomThreshold(threshold, clusteringEnabled = true)` returns `undefined` when clustering is off, so NodesTab renders no cluster layer at any zoom. With clustering on it still uses the threshold (`0` still means no clustering).

title: fix: date positions by observation, not replay arrival; sweep re-checks aircraft verdicts (#5401)
body:
Fixes #5401.

## What was wrong
The trigger was on the mesh side. SKYC's new 250 m fix never reached one of the reporter's radio sources: smart broadcast didn't re-send it, and its channel was split. That source kept the old 800 m fix, so its own row is correctly flagged.

But the unified map should still have followed the newer fix. It picks each node's position, and with it the likely-aircraft flag, by `positionTimestamp`. Radio sources stamped that field with the time a packet **arrived**:
- A position packet stamped `now` even when it was a firmware 2.8 NodeDB replay. Those replays run hourly and on every reconnect. `lastHeard` already had a replay guard; this field didn't.
- A NodeInfo position from the radio's own NodeDB also stamped `now`.

So every replay re-dated the stale 800 m fix as the newest one. It outranked the genuinely newer fix, and the badge stayed.

## Changes
1. **Stamp the observation time** (`replayGuard.ts`: `resolvePositionObservedAtMs`, `resolveNodeDbPositionObservedAtMs`).
   - A live packet is still stamped `now`.
   - A replayed packet, or a retained MQTT frame, keeps its original `rx_time`.
   - A NodeInfo position uses the fix's own GPS time, then the radio's `lastHeard` for the node, and otherwise leaves the stored stamp alone. It is now stamped whenever lat/lon are accepted, not only when precision bits are present.
2. **The hourly aircraft sweep re-checks stored verdicts** before its other passes, using the existing silent recompute. A flag no longer outlives the altitude that caused it when a fixed node never sends another position.

## Not changed, and why
- **Refreshing the node query after an aircraft-settings save:** not needed. Node data already refetches every 5–30 s (Nodes page) and every 15 s (Dashboard). The 60 s `staleTime` cited in the issue belongs to the node-display *settings* query, not node data. The server recompute also runs in the background, so an immediate invalidation could refetch before it finishes.
- **A global (unscoped) save of the aircraft thresholds doesn't trigger a recompute.** Left as is. The hourly re-check now covers it within an hour.

## Mesh impact
None. No packets, events or timers; the change only affects how stored positions are dated.

## Tests
- Unit tests for both helpers.
- Tests against the real `processPositionMessageProtobuf`: a replayed position keeps its `rx_time`, a live one gets now.
- A unified-merge regression test: a replayed stale high fix no longer keeps the badge over a newer low fix.
- Sweep tests: the re-check runs first and even with age-out off; a failure doesn't stop the sweep; it is skipped with detection off.
- Full suite: 23,034 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

title: feat(meshcore): retry remote logins, wait longer, show progress, allow cancel (#5400)
body:
Closes #5400

## Problem

"Log in with saved password" and "Use a different password" on a MeshCore repeater tried once. Every login path also waited only the firmware's Sent `estTimeout` + 1 s (meshcore.js `login()`). A reply from a node several hops out lands after that, so each attempt timed out and the existing room/saved-login retries repeated the same miss (as @HougeDK saw).

## What changed

**Longer per-attempt wait: max(estTimeout × 2, 10 s)**, capped at 90 s against a garbage estimate. All numbers live in `src/server/constants/meshcoreLogin.ts`.
- `MeshCoreNativeBackend` now runs the login exchange itself (`runLoginExchange`: send `CMD_SEND_LOGIN`, wait for Sent, then LoginSuccess 0x85 or LoginFail 0x86) instead of calling meshcore.js `login()`. meshcore.js's listeners can't be detached from outside, so a longer wait or a cancel layered on top would leak them. No fork of meshcore.js.
- Every exit path (success, refusal, silence, Err, cancel, send failure, no Sent ack) runs one cleanup. Tests assert listener counts and `vi.getTimerCount() === 0` afterwards.

**One shared retry helper: `MeshCoreManager.loginToNodeWithRetry`.** Up to 3 attempts, retry only on `no_reply`, 2 s pause. Stops at once on `rejected`, `not_on_device`, or TX disabled (receive-only now throws instead of reading as silence).
- Used by admin `/admin/login` ("Log in" / "Use a different password"), `/admin/login-with-saved`, room `/rooms/login` + `/rooms/login-with-saved`, `ensureSavedLogin` (neighbours/stats/clock sync), and the room-sync scheduler.
- Virtual Node relay (`handleSendLogin`) keeps **one** attempt through `loginToNode`: the phone app retries itself, as it would against real firmware, and a hidden retry would double packets per app attempt. It gets the longer wait, so a slow reply is still relayed as LoginSuccess. The handler is fire-and-forget from the command switch, so the wait blocks no other VN traffic. The app-facing Sent `estTimeout` (12 s) is unchanged.
- `loginToNodeDetailed` is gone (no callers left).

**Live progress + cancel (UI requirement).**
- The login POSTs take an optional client-chosen `requestId`. `GET /admin/login-progress/:requestId` returns `{ phase, attempt, maxAttempts, waitMs, waitRemainingMs, cancelRequested, outcome }`; `POST /admin/login-cancel` aborts. Both are private to the user **and** source that started the login (404 otherwise), carry no password or key, and are in-memory (`src/server/services/meshcoreLoginProgress.ts`, bounded to 500 entries, finished ones kept 60 s). Without a `requestId` a login runs untracked as before, so API clients need no change.
- I chose polling over Socket.IO because the socket has no per-user room and components can't reach it. The poll runs only while a login is open, once a second; the countdown ticks locally.
- Cancel is an `AbortSignal` passed down to the backend: no further attempts, and the backend stops listening, so a late reply is ignored. An `ok` that raced the cancel still reads `c

title: fix(firmware): search extracted firmware zip recursively for platform-nested binaries
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #5402 — firmware OTA fails at **Extract** with `No matching firmware binary found for board "heltec-v4" in extracted files` when the Meshtastic release zip nests the per-board binary under a platform subdirectory (e.g. `esp32s3/firmware-heltec-v4-2.8.0.47db0e3.bin`).
- Root cause: `executeExtract()` listed the extraction directory with a non-recursive `fs.readdirSync(extractDir)`, so binaries under a subdirectory were never handed to `findFirmwareBinary()`.
- Fix: list the extraction directory recursively (`fs.readdirSync(extractDir, { recursive: true })`, supported on Node 20.1+/our Node 22+ baseline), and have `findFirmwareBinary()` match against each candidate's `path.basename()` while still returning the full relative path (e.g. `esp32s3/firmware-heltec-v4-2.8.0.47db0e3.bin`) so the existing `path.join(extractDir, matched)` call in `executeExtract()` continues to resolve correctly. Board/version matching, factory-binary rejection, and the strict naming regex are all unchanged — only the file discovery step is affected.

## Test plan

- [x] Added a unit test reproducing the exact zip layout from the issue (Heltec V4 binaries nested under `esp32s3/`, including a sibling `.factory.bin`), asserting the platform-nested binary is matched and the factory variant is still rejected.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/server/services/firmwareUpdateService.test.ts src/server/services/firmwareUpdateService.customUrl.test.ts src/server/services/firmwareUpdateService.localUpload.test.ts src/server/routes/firmwareUpdateRoutes.test.ts` — 154 passed, 0 failed.

- [x] `npm run lint:ci` — no new violations (ratchet gate passes).

title: feat(meshcore): reorder channel slots on the companion (#5379)
body:
Closes #5379

Adds **Reorder slots on device** to the MeshCore Channels settings page. It rewrites the companion's channel slots into a new order. Message history, unread markers, permissions, scopes and the MeshCore automation settings move with their channel.

This is the on-device half of #5379. #5392 covers the display-only sort in the Channels message view. This branch is based on `main`, not stacked on #5392.

## Firmware facts this relies on

Checked in `companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp`, `BaseChatMesh.cpp`, `DataStore.cpp` and meshcore.js:

- `CMD_SET_CHANNEL` (0x20) overwrites **one** slot in place and saves the whole table to flash. The firmware has no insert, no delete-and-shift, and no "set order" command. meshcore.js `deleteChannel` just writes an empty name and a zero secret.
- The table is a fixed array of `MAX_GROUP_CHANNELS` slots (40 on current companion builds). Empty slots persist as gaps, which is the #5324 "empty slot". DeviceInfo byte 3 reports the max (v3+), and `device_query` now exposes it as `max_channels`.
- An incoming channel message goes to the **first** slot whose secret matches (`findChannelIdx`).
- The write ack is the untagged global Ok/Err. A concurrent command can steal it (the #4631 failure), so the ack cannot be trusted either way.

A reorder is therefore a sequence of single-slot overwrites. Nothing is deleted and re-added. We read every original channel (name + full secret) before the first write.

## Design

### 1. Device write safety (`src/server/meshcoreChannelReorder.ts`, `MeshCoreManager.reorderChannels`)

1. **Read the full slot table twice** (new `get_channel_table`, under the shared radio-op lock). If the reads disagree, or the length differs from the firmware's `MAX_GROUP_CHANNELS`, we stop before any write. The request must name exactly the configured slots the device reports. Otherwise we return `ORDER_MISMATCH` and resync the DB mirror, so "reload and try again" works.
2. **Plan writes that never remove the last copy of a channel.** A write only lands on a slot that is empty, holds a duplicate, or holds something the target does not want. For a cycle (a plain swap is one), the planner first copies one channel into the highest free slot, then clears that slot at the end. The plan is simulated (`verifyPlan`) before any device IO, and a plan that breaks the rule is refused. A 300-case randomized test checks this property. If every slot is full and a cycle needs scratch space, we refuse with `NO_FREE_SLOT` and ask the user to delete a channel first.
3. **Write each slot and read it back** (new `set_channel_verified`: `CMD_SET_CHANNEL` + `CMD_GET_CHANNEL` on the same slot, under the radio-op lock, 15 s budget). The read-back decides; the ack does not. A failed slot write is retried once.
4. **Re-read the whole table** and compare it with the target.
5. **Remap the DB** (below). This step runs only after the device is confirmed in the new layout.

**Rollback:** any failure in steps 3-5 writes the original

body:
Phase 3, the last phase of the likely-aircraft epic: flight trails. Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/AIRCRAFT_DETECTION_EPIC.md`, spec: `AIRCRAFT_P3_SPEC.md`. Phases 1 and 2 were #5386 and #5391.

Closes #5364. Closes #5365.

## What it does
- **Flight trails.** A "Flight trails" checkbox under Likely aircraft in both Map Features panels (Nodes map and Dashboard). Off by default.
  - It draws the recent path of every likely aircraft the map shows. Each aircraft gets its own colour, with a dark outline and direction arrows, and hovering shows the name and the time of the nearest fix.
  - Trails follow Show / Mark / Hide, the age window, the transport toggles, and Show aged-out.
  - On the Unified dashboard, an aircraft heard by several sources draws as one trail.
- **Lookback** slider, shown while the box is ticked: 1 h to 7 days, default 6 h.
  - The checkbox and lookback are saved per user on the server (migration 178, `user_map_preferences`).
- **`GET /api/aircraft/trails`** returns trails only for flagged and aged-out nodes.
  - Same permission and privacy filtering as the Map Analysis trails: per-source `nodes:read`, private overrides, channel `viewOnMap`, hidden and orphaned nodes.
  - Each trail is downsampled to 500 points, with at most 200 trails.
- **MQTT position history** (your call during validation). MQTT sources stored no position history, so aircraft heard only over MQTT (49 of the 51 flagged nodes on the dev data) could never have a trail.
  - MQTT sources now store every trustworthy fix as position telemetry, the same rows TCP sources write.
  - A packet relayed by several gateways is stored once, deduped on its packet id.

- **3D** doesn't show trails, the same as Position History today.

title: feat: per-source First Heard for Meshtastic and MeshCore nodes (#5390)
body:
Closes #5390

## Summary

Adds a per-source **First Heard** timestamp for Meshtastic and MeshCore nodes and shows it next to Last Heard.

### Why a new column, not `createdAt`

`nodes.createdAt` is not an honest "first heard". Any INSERT sets it: a message that only references a node, a contact-URL import, a MeshCore contact the radio holds but never heard on air. It is also in ms while `lastHeard` is in seconds. So this PR adds `firstHeard`, driven by `lastHeard`, the column every reception path already writes.

### Storage (migration 179, renumbered from 178 after #5396 merged)

| Table | Column | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `nodes` | `firstHeard` | Unix **seconds** (same as `nodes.lastHeard`) |
| `meshcore_nodes` | `firstHeard` | epoch **ms** (same as `meshcore_nodes.lastHeard`) |

- Both tables are keyed by `sourceId`, so the value is per source.
- The repositories stamp it once, from the first plausible `lastHeard` a write carries, and never overwrite it (`src/utils/firstHeard.ts`). "Plausible" means after 2020-01-01 and no more than a day in the future, so unsynced clocks and drifted MeshCore RTCs (#5339) don't set it.
- If a row already has a `lastHeard` from before this column existed (or from a restored older backup), the older of the stored and incoming values wins.
- A caller-supplied `firstHeard` is ignored on update.
- Stamped in all three `nodes` write paths (async update, insert, SQLite sync upsert) and in `MeshCoreRepository.upsertNode`. The first-seen `ON CONFLICT` set deliberately leaves it out.
- **Backfill:** for rows with a `lastHeard`, `firstHeard` = the earlier of `createdAt` and `lastHeard` (skipping implausible values). Rows never heard stay `NULL` = unknown. Guarded by `firstHeard IS NULL`, so re-runs are no-ops. I skipped the per-node MIN over telemetry/messages: it scans large tables on every backend, and retention usually trims those below `createdAt` anyway.
- Idempotent on SQLite / PostgreSQL / MySQL (shared helpers, full DDL; MySQL uses `DIV` for integer seconds).

### API / UI

- `DeviceInfo.firstHeard` (seconds) from `dbNodeMapper`; `MeshCoreNode.firstHeard` (ms) from `getAllNodes`.
- The unified cross-source merge takes the earliest `firstHeard` across sources.
- Node Details (Meshtastic) and the MeshCore contact details panel: a **First Heard** card next to Last Heard.
- Map popups (Nodes tab, NodePopup, Dashboard, MeshCore map): a "First Heard: …" line under the last-heard footer.
- The node CSV/HTML export gains a First Heard column.
- Backup: `nodes` is dumped with `SELECT *`, so the column rides along. (`meshcore_nodes` was not in the backup set before this PR and still isn't.)

### Mesh impact checklist

No packets, notifications, or timers. Read/write of a local column only.

## Tests

- `src/utils/firstHeard.test.ts`: plausibility + set-once logic, including the seconds-vs-ms trap.
- `nodes.firstHeard.multiBackend.test.ts`: set on insert, never overwritten, null until first reception, rejects implausible valu

## What

A view-only window picker beside the Nodes list count: **Setting (last 24h)** / last 24h / last 3d / last 7d / last 30d / all. It replaces the read-only `· last 24h` suffix from #5344 (same spot, same tooltip text when on "Setting").

## Semantics (decided)

The issue says both "ephemeral override" and "default / hard cap", and also offers "all", so a hard cap would make most choices no-ops on the default 24h install. I went with **override for display only**:

- The pick replaces the Settings window for the **Nodes list and its map**, wider or narrower. The poll already delivers every node, so widening needs no server change.
- **Setting** restores `maxNodeAgeHours` exactly.
- It **never** writes the setting and never reaches the server. The choice lives in this browser's `localStorage` (`nodesQuickAgeHours`, try/catch guarded), shared across sources.
- Favorites, imported-never-heard nodes, and the MeshCore local node stay exempt, as before.
- Not affected: the Messages tab (it shares `processedNodes`, so the override only applies while `activeTab === 'nodes'`), the Dashboard map, background jobs, and the server.

- **Meshtastic** (`useSourceView`): the list filter, the traceroute/route-segment cap and the marker cap all use the same list window. The Map age slider now clamps to that window, and says `All (7d from Nodes filter)` / `Narrows the Nodes list window` when the quick filter sets the cap.

title: feat(unified-messages): show per-source hop count inline (#5366)
body:
Closes #5366

## Summary

The Unified Messages collapsed row now shows each source's hop count inline, inside that source's tag. Before, you had to open the reception modal to see hops.

```
[Base Station 0] [Roof 2] [MeshCore Box MESHCORE 3] [Old Node ?]
```

## Changes

- **`HopBadge`** (`src/components/unified/HopBadge.tsx` + `.module.css`): a small numeric pill. It takes the source tag's color through `currentColor`, so it needs no theme tokens. The `title` and `aria-label` name the source, for example "Heard by Roof: 2 hops".
- **`receptionHopCount()` / `hopDisplay()`** (`src/pages/unifiedHops.ts`): one place to work out hops, used by both the badge and the modal.
  - Meshtastic (including MQTT): `hopStart - hopLimit`.
  - A missing `hopStart` (old firmware) or missing `hopLimit` counts as **unknown (`?`)**, never 0.
  - `hopLimit > hopStart` is a corrupt pair and also counts as unknown. The old modal showed "direct" for this case.
  - MeshCore: uses the decoded `hopCount`.
- **Server** (`/api/unified/messages`): MeshCore receptions now return `hopCount` from `meshcore_messages.hopCount`. That column already holds the decoded `path_len` (bottom 6 bits; `0xFF` direct → 0). Before this, MeshCore receptions sent `hopStart`/`hopLimit` as null, so their modal hop column always showed "—". Meshtastic receptions return `hopCount: null`.

## Emoji intentionally not used

The issue asks for number emoji (keycap digits). The CLAUDE.md hard rule says app-owned interface icons use `UiIcon` and must not hardcode emoji in JSX or locale copy. So the badges are styled numeric text in a CSS module. This also covers the issue's note about counts of 10 and above, where no keycap emoji exists: the badge shows the raw number.

## Permissions

The server already builds `receptions[]` only from sources the user can read (`messages:read` or `channel_N:read` per source). The badge renders one per reception, so it shows nothing the user could not already see in the modal.

## Mesh impact

None. This is display-only. It sends no packets, fires no notifications, and arms no timers.

## Tests

- `src/pages/unifiedHops.test.ts`: derivation edge cases (direct, missing `hopStart`/`hopLimit`, corrupt pair, MeshCore `hopCount`, invalid `hopCount` fallback, 10+).
- `src/components/unified/HopBadge.test.tsx`: renders the count, 0 for direct, 10+, `?` with an unknown label, the English aria-label, and no emoji.
- `src/server/routes/unifiedRoutes.test.ts`: MeshCore receptions carry `hopCount`, and a MeshCore row without a hop count returns null. Meshtastic receptions return `hopCount: null` and keep `hopStart`.

Local checks: targeted Vitest JSON `success: true` (80 passed), `tsc --noEmit` clean for `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.server.json`, and the new test files, and `lint:ci` ratchet OK.

title: feat(meshcore): channel list sort dropdown and custom display order (#5385, #5379)
body:
Closes #5385. Refs #5379 (display-order half only; see "Device reorder" below).

## What

The MeshCore Channels list gets an order bar under its header:

- **Sort dropdown:** Device order (default, same as before), Channel name, Last message, Custom.
- **Reorder button:** opens a reorder mode with a drag handle per row (dnd-kit, same touch-safe `DRAG_HANDLE_TOUCH_STYLE` as the #5233 fix) plus move up / move down buttons for keyboard and anyone who can't drag. **Save order** stores the order and switches the dropdown to Custom; **Cancel** drops the draft.

One model covers both issues: "Custom" is the drag-and-drop order.

- Last message: newest first; channels with no messages sink to the bottom in slot order.
- Name: ignores a leading `#` and case, numeric-aware.
- Custom: channels added after the order was saved go to the end in slot order; deleted slots drop out.
- The existing "unread first" toggle (#3703) still works and layers on top of whichever sort is picked.

## Display order only

This never writes to the device. Slot indices stay where the firmware has them, so message history (`channel-<idx>`), sends, VN clients, bridge rules and automations that name a slot are untouched.

**Storage:** per source, in localStorage (`meshmonitor-meshcore-channel-sort-mode-<sourceId>` and `...-custom-order-<sourceId>`), next to the per-source unread markers this view already keeps there. I did not use server settings because saving them needs `settings:write`, and read-only viewers should still be able to sort their own list. The trade-off: the choice is per browser, not per user.

## Device reorder (#5379), not done

#5379 asks for the order to be written to the companion (delete and re-add slots via CMD_SET_CHANNEL). This PR does not do that, on purpose. Moving slots would shift the `channel-<idx>` key that message history, bridge rules, automations and VN clients rely on, and a partial failure could leave empty slots (#5324). That needs its own decision. #5379 stays open for it.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** zero. No packets, no device ops, only local storage writes.
2. **Spam:** none. No messages, events or notifications.
3. **Timers:** none.

## Tests

- `meshcoreChannelOrder.test.ts`: sort modes, custom-order merge, move, per-source persistence, junk input.
- `MeshCoreChannelsView.test.tsx`: dropdown sorts and persists per source; last-message order; reorder via arrows saves a custom order and sends only GETs; cancel drops the draft.

title: feat: likely-aircraft age-out and reclassify as fixed, Phase 2 (#5364, #5365)
body:
Phase 2 of the likely-aircraft epic (#5364, #5365): age out stale aircraft and reclassify stationary ones as fixed. Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/AIRCRAFT_DETECTION_EPIC.md`, spec: `AIRCRAFT_P2_SPEC.md`. Phase 1 was #5386.

Part of #5364 and #5365. Phase 3 (flight trails) follows.

## What it does
- **Age-out (per source, off by default).** A likely aircraft not heard for N hours (default 24, range 6–168) is ignored or deleted.
  - **Ignore** is database-only, with reason `aircraft`. Nothing goes to any radio.
  - **Delete** is an opt-in, and the setting warns that it removes the node and its history.
  - Favourites, the local node, and nodes already ignored for another reason are never touched.
- **Auto-lift.** An aged-out aircraft that sends a new **live** position is un-ignored and classified again. Firmware 2.8 NodeDB replays don't count (`isLiveReception`), and manual or geo ignores are never lifted.
- **Once per silence.** A hand un-ignore sticks until the node is heard again. It isn't re-ignored at the next sweep.
- **Reclassify as fixed.** A flagged node heard in the last 24 h, with at least 3 fixes all within 200 m, loses the flag and gets a sticky "fixed" mark, so a bad GPS altitude doesn't flag it again. The mark clears if the node moves more than 1 km. This runs whenever detection is on.
- **UI:**
  - Settings → Node Display: the age-out switch, hours, action with the Delete warning, and a last-run summary.
  - "Show aged-out" in Map Features on both maps: aged-out nodes are drawn dimmed, with the badge.
  - Popup lines "Aged out (likely aircraft)" and "Reclassified as fixed".
  - A reason column in Ignored Nodes.
- **Migration 177** adds `aircraftAgedOutAt`, `aircraftFixedAt`, `aircraftFixedLatitude` and `aircraftFixedLongitude` to `nodes`.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** none. Nothing is sent. The ignore is database-only.
  - This PR also fixes a gap: the #2601 re-apply would have pushed an `aircraft` ignore to the local radio. The firmware would then drop the node's packets and the auto-lift could never fire. That push is now skipped for reason `aircraft`.
- **Spam:** ignore, delete and lift fire no notifications or automation events.
- **Timers:** the hourly sweep's last run is stored per source in `aircraftAgeOutLastRunAt`. A restart or settings save neither triggers nor re-arms it; this was checked on the dev container by restarting it.

title: fix(mesh-issues): exempt each source's local node from C2 over-broadcasting (#5388)
body:
Fixes #5388

## Problem

Mesh Issues rule C2 "Broadcasting too often" flagged MeshMonitor's own directly-connected nodes. The firmware streams `deviceMetrics` to its client over the phone API about every 60s, far faster than it broadcasts to the mesh. Those rows land in `telemetry` just like mesh-heard rows, so C2 read the phone-API cadence (median ~60s) as over-broadcasting.

## Fix (issue Option 1, scoped per source)

The analysis pools physical nodes across sources, and each cadence sample carries its `sourceId`. So the exemption drops the **(sourceId, nodeNum)** pair, not the whole node:

- `meshIssuesAnalysisService.resolveLocalNodeSources()` reads each source's local node number through `resolveLocalNodeNums()` → `SettingsRepository.getLocalNodeNumForSource()` (#5382). It reads the DB, so a disconnected source is still covered. MQTT sources have no local node and drop out. A lookup failure logs a warning and falls back to "no local nodes" instead of aborting the run.
- **Telemetry cadence:** C2's cadence series is built from the telemetry rows minus the rows a node reported on the source where it is local. Tier A still gets the full series, unchanged.
- **Position cadence:** stage 1 still pools every source (local rows can only make a node *more* likely to be a candidate). A local candidate's stage-2 read runs on its own, without the sources where it is local. If it is local on every source we read, there is nothing to measure and we skip the query. Local nodes number at most one per source, so the query count stays bounded.
- `TierCRuleContext.localNodeSources` (nodeNum → local source ids) passes into `evaluateC2`. As a second guard, C2 refuses a stream fed only by local sources and never quotes such a stream as `otherStreamMedianSeconds`.

Result: a node that is local on source A but heard over the mesh on source B gets its cadence from B alone. The finding's `sources` show `src-b`.

### Other rules checked
- **C1 excessive packets:** already skips each source's local node in `duplicateKeySchedulerService`. No change.
- **C1 key security / time offset:** these do not use cadence.
- **A5 telemetry-cadence clause (Tier A, not Tier C), possibly the same shape:** it reads broadcast `TELEMETRY_APP` rows from `packet_log` for ROUTER/ROUTER_LATE nodes, across all sources. If phone-only local telemetry gets logged there as an rx broadcast, a local router could trip A5's cadence clause the same way. It only applies when `packet_log` is enabled, and I left it alone here. It is a candidate follow-up.

### Follow-up (not in this PR)
Option 2 from the issue: tag telemetry rows `viaMesh`/local at insert time and filter cadence on it. That would protect every future cadence rule, but it needs a migration, so it is out of scope here. Option 3 (stop storing local deviceMetrics) stays rejected. Device Health, LocalStats and the airtime automation all depend on those rows.

## Mesh impact
None. This is analysis-only. It sends no packets, arms no timers and

title: feat: likely-aircraft detection, Phase 1 (#5364, #5365)
body:
Phase 1 of the likely-aircraft epic (#5364, #5365). Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/AIRCRAFT_DETECTION_EPIC.md`, spec: `AIRCRAFT_P1_SPEC.md`.

Part of #5364 and #5365. Phases 2 (age-out, reclassify as fixed) and 3 (flight trails) follow; ADS-B cross-checking is split to #5374.

## What it does
- **Classifier.** A node is a likely aircraft when its altitude is more than the threshold above the terrain under it (DEM via `ElevationProvider`, default 500 m). With no terrain data it falls back to altitude above sea level (default 5000 m). Fixed hysteresis of max(50 m, 10%). A mountaintop repeater stays a fixed node.
- **Pipeline.** New `aircraftClassificationService` classifies on position and NodeInfo updates (Meshtastic TCP and MQTT), in batches, with a startup backfill and a silent re-run when thresholds change. Results persist per source on `nodes` (migration 175).
- **Settings.** Per source, in Settings → Node Display: enable switch, height-above-ground threshold, sea-level fallback.
- **Auto-Favorite.** New "Exclude likely aircraft" switch, on by default. Likely aircraft are never auto-added. An auto-added node is removed only after it is flagged at two hourly sweeps at least 45 min apart. Strikes persist in the DB, so a restart or settings save can't reset them. User and locked favourites are never touched.
- **Automation.** New trigger "Became likely aircraft", fired once per transition.
- **Map.** Plane badge on the marker, a popup line ("Likely aircraft · 6.3 km above ground"), a list icon, and a Show / Mark / Hide control in both Map Features panels. The choice is saved per user (migration 176). Hide never hides a favourite.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** none. The feature sends no packets.
- **Spam:** the only indirect path is the automation trigger. It fires once per transition, and automations keep their own rate limits and cooldowns.
- **Timers:** Auto-Favorite strikes are stored in the DB. A settings save or restart does not re-arm or clear them. Elevation lookups are HTTP tile fetches (cached), not mesh traffic, and respect `elevationEnabled`.

Map control, badge, and popup:

title: fix: maxNodeAgeHours 0 in TX jobs, node metrics and VN replay (#5376)
body:
Fixes #5376

## Problem
`maxNodeAgeHours = 0` means "show all nodes" in the UI (#4947), but four server paths still computed `cutoff = now`, so they treated 0 as "no nodes":

- auto-traceroute target selection
- remote-admin scanner candidate set
- system node-count metrics (`systemNodeCount` / `systemDirectNodeCount`)
- Virtual Node NodeInfo replay (VN clients got no nodes)

## Fix
**Display-only paths: 0 = all nodes.** `saveSystemNodeMetrics` and `sendNodeInfosFromDb` now call a new `NodesRepository.getHeardNodes(sourceId)` when the window is 0. It drops the age cutoff but keeps the `lastHeard IS NOT NULL` filter, so never-heard placeholder rows (#2602) still stay out of the VN replay.

**TX-selecting jobs: 0 falls back to a new bound.** New per-source setting **`txTargetMaxAgeHoursWhenUnlimited`**, default **24 h**, range **1-720 h** (0 rejected, since it is the bound). `getTxTargetMaxAgeHours()` returns `maxNodeAgeHours` when it is above 0, else this setting. It is used by:
- `getNodeNeedingTracerouteAsync` (auto-traceroute). `selectNodeNeedingTraceroute` also guards a 0 input with the 24 h default.
- `getNodeNeedingRemoteAdminCheckAsync` (remote-admin scanner)
- `getNodesNeedingRemoteLocalStatsAsync` (remote LocalStats). This one was not listed in the issue, but it also picks TX targets. Its old 0 behavior was already "1 day", which the 24 h default keeps.

**Setting plumbing.** Per-source, to match `maxNodeAgeHours`, and read with `getSettingForSource(sourceId, …)`. It sits outside the frozen ten-key Node Display seed, like `maxInfraNodeAgeHours`.
- Added to `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` and `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS`. The POST validates it and returns 400 `INVALID_TX_TARGET_MAX_AGE_HOURS` for a bad value.
- New `SETTINGS_TAB_PER_SOURCE_KEYS` = the frozen ten plus this key. SettingsTab's split save routes it to the scoped POST, and the GET keeps it out of the global back-fill.
- SettingsTab uses a Category C draft field (`initial*` snapshot, fetch, baseline, applyDraft, `handleSave` literal). The input sits directly under the node window in Settings → Node Display, with a warning (CSS module, `var(--color-warning)`, `UiIcon alert`) that it limits which nodes MeshMonitor transmits to. en.json has 3 new keys, and `docs/features/automation.md` has a troubleshooting note.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** the rate does not change. The existing timers still decide how often traceroute, remote-admin and LocalStats fire. Only the set of nodes each tick can pick from changes. With the node window at 0, that set was empty before (no TX at all). It is now nodes heard in the last 24 h by default, which is the same set as the default 24 h node window.
- **Spam:** no new send paths or events. The bound keeps these jobs from targeting long-gone nodes when the display shows all nodes. The UI warns next to the input.
- **Timers:** no scheduler state or timestamps changed. A save does not re-arm anything.

## Tests
- `database.maxNodeAge.perSource.test.ts`: 0 → 24 h d

title: fix(sources): MQTT sources no longer send or write config through the primary radio (#5375)
body:
Fixes #5375

## Problem

`resolveSourceManager()` hands back the **primary Meshtastic TCP manager** for an `mqtt_broker`, `mqtt_bridge` or MeshCore sourceId. #5371 closed that hole for identity, device config, keys and remote admin. This PR closes it for everything that transmits, writes channel/device config, or reads "our" node for DM counts.

## Behaviour change

Default: **refuse** with `400 SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` when a non-Meshtastic source would transmit or write config through another source's radio. Where the request also saves a DB row the user asked for, the row still saves and only the push to a radio is skipped.

| Route / path | Old behaviour (MQTT source id) | New behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/messages/send`, v1 `POST messages` | Sent over the primary TCP radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `POST /api/traceroute`, `/position/request`, `/nodeinfo/request`, `/neighborinfo/request`, `/telemetry/request` + v1 `actions/*` | Sent over the primary radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `POST /api/nodes/:id/send-key-warning`, `/nodes/:num/scan-remote-admin` | Sent over the primary radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `POST /api/announce/send` | Announced over the primary radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `PUT /api/channels/:id`, `POST /api/channels/:slot/import` | Saved row, then pushed channel to primary radio | Saves row, skips push |
| `POST /api/channels/reorder` | Rewrote the **primary's** channels (radio + DB rows) | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `POST /api/channels/encode-url`, `/import-config`, `/refresh`, `POST /api/nodes/refresh` | Read/wrote/refreshed the primary radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `POST /api/backup/restore/:file` | Restored device config onto the primary radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| Beacon-offer accept | Wrote channel to primary radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| Favorite / ignored `syncToDevice`, auto-delete-by-distance ignore sync | Admin packet to primary radio | Row saved, sync `skipped` |
| Traceroute / LocalStats / time-sync / remote-admin-scanner interval apply | Re-armed the **primary's** scheduler | Settings saved, no scheduler touched |
| `POST /api/purge/nodes` | Purged source rows, then refreshed primary radio | Purges rows, no refresh |
| `GET /api/device/tx-status` | Primary radio's TX state | `{ canTransmit: false, hasLocalRadio: false, ... }`; same for a disabled non-Meshtastic source; a disconnected TCP source ⇒ `connected: false` with the permissive TX default |
| `/api/poll` unread DMs, `/messages/unread-counts`, `/first-unread` | Counted DMs to the primary node | Source's own node; none ⇒ DM counting skipped |
| `POST /api/messages/mark-read` (DM) | Marked the primary node's DMs | Own node; none ⇒ `{ marked: 0 }` |
| `POST /api/connection/disconnect`, `/reconnect`, `/configure` | Disconnected / reconnected / re-addressed the **primary** radio | 400 `SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` |
| `GET /api/connection` | Primary radio's link status | MQTT source's own

title: fix: read each source's local node number from the key the manager writes (#5377)
body:
Fixes #5377

## Problem
The Meshtastic manager writes its local node number as `localNodeNum_<sourceId>` (bare `localNodeNum` only for the legacy `default` id). Per-source readers called `settings.getSettingForSource(id, 'localNodeNum')`, which reads `source:<id>:localNodeNum`. Only migration 050 ever wrote that shape, as a one-time snapshot of the pre-4.x global. Source ids are UUIDs, so on a real install every source missed:

- `GET /api/config?sourceId=` returned no `localNodeInfo` / `deviceMetadata`
- telemetry "available nodes" never marked the local node secure
- spam detection and packet-count exclusion did not exclude the local node
- auto-delete-by-distance did not protect the local node (inline and batch)

The existing config route test seeded `setSourceSetting(..., 'localNodeNum')`, a key shape no production code writes, so it passed.

## Fix
- `SettingsRepository.getLocalNodeNumForSource(sourceId)` is the one accessor. It reads `localNodeNum_<id>`, falls back to the migration-050 `source:<id>:localNodeNum` row for a source not reconnected since, and reads the bare key only when no source is given. It never falls back from a source to the global key, so MQTT/MeshCore sources do not inherit another source's node.
- `localNodeNumSettingKey` moved to the settings repository (so `database.ts` can use it without an import cycle); `utils/localNodeNums.ts` re-exports it and uses the accessor.
- Readers switched: `configRoutes`, `telemetryRoutes`, `database.ts` (packet counts and top broadcasters), `duplicateKeySchedulerService`, `autoDeleteByDistanceService` (both paths), plus bare-key readers that already had a source: dead-nodes (`securityRoutes`), v1 `status` and `messages`, and the Apprise/push local-name fallback.
- No migration: the dual-read covers existing rows, and the manager rewrites the canonical key on every connect. Backup/restore copy the settings table wholesale, so no change there.

## Tests
- `settings.test.ts` (SQLite + PG + MySQL): accessor reads the manager's key, `getSettingForSource` does not (documents the bug), no global fallback, legacy fallback, current key wins.
- `configRoutes.test.ts` (route harness): seeds via `new MeshtasticManager(sourceA).localNodeSettingKey('localNodeNum')` so the key comes from the real writer; asserts source B stays empty; covers the migration-050 fallback.
- Mock updates in the suites that stub the settings repo.

Local: full Vitest suite `success: true` (22,325 tests, 0 failed, PG/MySQL containers up), `tsc` clean on both configs, `lint:ci` OK.

## Mesh impact
None: read-path only, no packets, timers or notifications added.

title: fix(meshcore-vn): show PKI export/import status on the MeshCore Info view
body:
Fixes #5380

## Summary

The **PKI Export** / **PKI Import** rows lived in the Virtual Node block of `InfoTab.tsx`. The server only reports those flags for MeshCore virtual nodes, but a MeshCore source opens the MeshCore page, which has no Info tab. The rows could never render.

- New `MeshCoreVirtualNodeCard` on the MeshCore **Node Info** view (next to Identity / Radio / Health / Counters). Read-only: status, server running, admin commands, PKI export, PKI import, connected clients. Reads `GET /api/virtual-node/status` (60s refetch, same cadence as the Info tab) and picks this source's entry.
- The card renders nothing when the status call fails (it needs a login) or the source has no entry. PKI rows only show when the server reports a boolean.
- Removed the dead PKI rows from `InfoTab.tsx`.
- Reuses existing `info.virtual_node*` / `common.*` locale keys and the existing `meshcore-info-card` layout, so no new copy and no new CSS.

## Mesh impact

None. Read-only UI; no packets, notifications, or timers beyond one authenticated HTTP poll per minute while the view is open.

## Tests

- `MeshCoreVirtualNodeCard.test.tsx`: allowed/blocked rows for the right source, rows omitted when flags are absent, disabled state, nothing rendered on missing source or failed call.
- `InfoTab.transportBreakdown.test.tsx`: PKI rows no longer render even when the status reports them.
- `tsc` (both configs) clean; `lint:ci` passes.

title: fix(neighbor-info): treat maxNodeAgeHours 0 as show-all on the server
body:
Follow-up to #5352; refs #5338

## Summary

#5352 fixes the per-source Nodes tab when **Max node age = 0** ("never / show all", #4947). The server's neighbor-info endpoints had the same bug: they set cutoff = now at 0, so every neighbor link dropped off the map.

- `src/server/routes/neighborInfoRoutes.ts` (GET `/api/neighbor-info`)
- `src/server/services/sourceDashboardData.ts` `buildSourceNeighborInfo` (GET `/api/sources/:id/neighbor-info` and the per-source / unified dashboard bundles)

Both now use no cutoff (`-Infinity`) when `maxNodeAgeHours <= 0`, matching the frontend guard.

## Tests

- `neighborInfoRoutes.test.ts` (route harness): a 30-day-old link survives with `maxNodeAgeHours = 0`.
- `sourceRoutes.neighbor-info.test.ts`: same for the per-source endpoint.
- Both suites: 27/27 pass (`success=true`); `tsc` server + frontend clean; `lint:ci` ratchet OK.

## Mesh impact

Read-only display path. It sends no packets, fires no notifications, and arms no timers.

## Left alone (separate issue to follow)

These server paths also read `maxNodeAgeHours = 0` as "no nodes". I left them unchanged because the first two pick TX targets, so treating 0 as "all nodes" is a policy call:

- Auto-traceroute selection: `src/server/services/autoTracerouteSelectionService.ts` (`activeNodeCutoff`)
- Remote-admin scanner: `src/services/database.ts` `getNodeNeedingRemoteAdminCheckAsync` (`activeNodeCutoffSeconds`)
- System node-count metrics: `src/server/meshtasticManager.ts` (`getActiveNodes(maxNodeAgeHours / 24)`)
- Virtual-node NodeInfo replay: `src/server/virtualNodeServer.ts` `sendNodeInfosFromDb` (VN clients get no nodes)
