title: feat(ui): name the three node-age controls by role and show the active window (#5344)
body:
Closes #5344.

Three controls filter nodes by age, and the UI didn't say which was which. So the sidebar, the Nodes list and the map each showed a different count with no explanation. Following the decisions on the issue, they stay separate controls, but each one now says what it does.

## Changes
- **Sidebar activity pill:** it reads `65/798 active · 2h`, with the count in bold and "active · 2h" muted. The tooltip says: "65 of 798 nodes heard in the last 2 hours. Informational only: it does not filter the Nodes list or map." The status row can wrap, so the pill drops to its own line instead of clipping. It fits 5-digit counts at the 200 px minimum sidebar width and in the mobile drawer.
- **Settings → Node Display:**
  - The field is now labelled "Node list & map window (hours)", on both Meshtastic and MeshCore.
  - The new description says it's the default window for the Nodes list and map, that 0 shows all nodes, and that the map's age filter can narrow it but never widen it.
- **Cutoff next to counts:** the Nodes header shows `Nodes (151) · last 24h` (or `· all` when unlimited), in the per-source Nodes tab and the MeshCore Nodes list.
- **Map age filter:** both Map Features panels, the Nodes tab and the Dashboard map, now use one shared `MapAgeFilterControl`.
  - The control shows "Showing: last 6h" as its status line.
  - The top stop reads "All (24h from Settings)", or "All (no limit in Settings)" when the setting is 0.
  - A hint underneath says it narrows the Settings window and can't widen it.
- **Shared formatter:** `src/utils/ageWindow.ts` formats durations like "30m / 6h / 3d / all". Every cutoff label treats a window of 0 or below, unset, or non-numeric as "all".
- **Slider stop labels:** the map slider's stops also use the new formatter. Stops under two days now read in hours, so the 24h stop shows `24h` instead of `1d`.
- **i18n and docs:** new English strings only; strings other languages already translate are left untouched. `settings.md`, `maps.md` and `meshcore.md` use the new names.

It doesn't touch `useSourceView.ts`. The bug where 0 hid everything except favourites (#5338) is fixed separately in #5352.

## Screenshots (dev container)
Dashboard sidebar pills and the Dashboard map's age filter:
![Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5344-node-age-clarity/docs/public/images/features/5344-dashboard-sidebar-map.png)

Per-source Nodes header and the Nodes tab map filter. This screenshot was taken before the spacing fix, which the Dashboard shot shows.
![Nodes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5344-node-age-clarity/docs/public/images/features/5344-nodes-header.png)

## Mesh impact
None: this changes text and UI only.

## Testing
- Full Vitest suite: 20,973 passed, 0 failed. Both `tsc` configs are clean, and `lint:ci` passes.
- **New tests:** the formatter; locale tests that pin the wording; component tests for `MapAgeFilterControl` and `NodeAgeWindowSuffix` against the real

title: fix(meshcore-vn): handle the 10 unhandled companion commands (#5350)
body:
Fixes #5350

## Summary

The MeshCore Virtual Node fell through to `Err(UnsupportedCmd)` for ten companion commands, so the mobile app showed a bare "Error" banner on delete, rename, reset path, reboot and the rest. Each command now gets an explicit, firmware-shaped reply. Behaviour follows the existing VN design: commands that change the node or the contact list MeshMonitor shares sit behind **Allow admin commands**, read-only ones are ungated, and the two the VN should never serve are refused with a specific code.

Note on the original report: per the follow-up comment on the issue, the iOS app's *map* delete may not send `RemoveContact` at all. This PR closes the command gap either way; if a trace-log capture shows a different opcode for map delete, that needs its own issue.

## Command → behaviour

| Opcode | Command | Gate | Behaviour |
|-------:|---------|------|-----------|
| 9 | AddUpdateContact | admin | Diffed against the contact as the VN advertised it. Rename → new `set_contact_name` bridge command (read-modify-write, read-back verified, keeps flags/path/coords). Favourite bit → `setNodeFavorite` (MeshMonitor owns favourites). Route set to unknown (-1) → `resetContactPath`. Manual route or telemetry-permission-only edits → `Err(UnsupportedCmd)`. Unknown contact → `Err(NotFound)` (adding goes through ImportContact). |
| 13 | ResetPath | admin | `manager.resetContactPath` → Ok / `Err(NotFound)` / `Err(BadState)` |
| 15 | RemoveContact | admin | `manager.removeContact` (also deletes the `meshcore_nodes` row) → Ok / `Err(NotFound)` / `Err(BadState)` |
| 16 | ShareContact | none (like SendSelfAdvert); receive-only refuses | `manager.shareContact` → Ok / `Err(NotFound)` / `Err(BadState)` |
| 17 | ExportContact | none (read-only) | `manager.exportContact` → `ExportContact(11)` + advert bytes; no key = self |
| 18 | ImportContact | admin | `manager.importContact` → Ok; short advert → `Err(IllegalArg)` |
| 19 | Reboot | admin | Requires the `"reboot"` magic string (firmware parity). `manager.rebootDevice`; no reply on success (firmware sends none, meshcore.js resolves after 1s); audit row written |
| 24 | ImportPrivateKey | always refused | `Disabled(15)`, same as firmware built without `ENABLE_PRIVATE_KEY_IMPORT`; meshcore.js rejects with `"disabled"` |
| 25 | SendRawData | always refused | `Err(UnsupportedCmd)`, explicit case instead of the default |
| 56 | GetStats | none (serial read) | `Stats(24)` for core / radio / packets in the firmware layout (core carries `err_flags` u16 before `queue_len`); unknown sub-type → `Err(IllegalArg)` |

Also: `GetContacts` now sends the device's real `flags` byte instead of a hardcoded `0`, so an app that echoes it back in AddUpdateContact sees the true favourite state.

Why AddUpdateContact is not written verbatim: the VN advertises `pathLen` as a hop count, but the device stores a packed `out_path_len` for 2/3-byte hashes, and `reconcileDeviceFavorites` treats MeshMonitor as the source of truth for the f

title: fix(mqtt): MQTT broker sources no longer show another source's Device Info (#5367)
body:
Fixes #5367

## Root cause

`resolveSourceManager()` only narrows to `meshtastic_tcp` managers. For an `mqtt_broker` / `mqtt_bridge` / `meshcore` sourceId it returns the **primary** TCP manager (by design, invariant I2). `/api/poll` built the Info tab's node ID, node name, firmware, LoRa config, device metadata and `deviceNodeNums` from that manager. So "Home Mqtt" (mqtt_broker) showed the Liligo T3S3's `!bf85a9d1` / `SKYM - AUX - LT` / `2.8.1.d3b4b34`. Only Node Address differed, because the frontend reads it from the source row.

The device-config, security-key and remote-admin routes resolve the same way. Saving the Node Identity form, rebooting, or running an admin command from the broker's view would have hit the TCP node's radio.

This is not an rc2/rc3 regression. The fallback dates from #2993. #5283 (v4.16.1) made it visible by restoring the **Open** button for `mqtt_broker` sources, which exposed the Meshtastic App shell (Info, Device Config, Admin tabs) for a source with no radio. The bridge already hid Device Config and Admin; the broker never did.

## Fix

**Server**
- New `resolveOwnMeshtasticManager(sourceId)` in `src/server/utils/resolveSourceManager.ts`. It returns this source's own Meshtastic manager, or `null`, and never another source's. No sourceId keeps legacy primary/fallback behaviour.
- `/api/poll`: `config.localNodeInfo`, `config.deviceMetadata`, `deviceConfig` and `deviceNodeNums` now come from that manager. A source with no local node gets none of them (`deviceNodeNums: []`). That includes a sourceId with no live manager (a disconnected TCP source), which used to borrow the primary's identity too. Connection status, nodes and messages are unchanged.
- New `requireMeshtasticDeviceSource()` guard (`src/server/utils/requireMeshtasticDeviceSource.ts`) returns `400 SOURCE_NOT_MESHTASTIC` (existing code) when the sourceId names a registered non-Meshtastic manager. It runs after auth and is mounted on:
  - `GET /config/current` and all 13 `POST /config/*`
  - `GET /device-config`, `GET /device/backup`, `POST /device/reboot`, `POST /device/purge-nodedb`
  - `GET /device/security-keys` (this was returning the TCP node's private key for the broker id)
  - `POST /admin/{load-config, ensure-session-passkey, session-passkey-status, get-channel, load-owner, get-device-metadata, reboot, set-time, export-config, import-config, commands}`
  
  Omitted sourceIds, Meshtastic sources, and unregistered ids pass through unchanged, so existing callers and tests see no change.

**Frontend**
- `App.tsx` / `Sidebar.tsx`: Device Configuration and Remote Admin are hidden for `mqtt_broker` too (new `hideDeviceConfig` Sidebar prop; the bridge's `mqttReadOnly` behaviour is unchanged, and the broker keeps its send capability).
- `InfoTab.tsx`: on an MQTT-only source it shows a "no local node" note, never renders a device config it was handed, and skips the security-key fetch.

## UI change: screenshot needed

The Info tab on an `mqtt_broker` source no

title: fix(meshcore): notify for new nodes first heard without a name (#5340)
body:
Fixes #5340

## Root cause

MeshCore companions default to auto-add-contacts mode. In that mode the firmware reports a newly heard node with a **pubkey-only** `0x80` push (`PushCodes.Advert`); the native backend turns it into a `contact_advertised` event with no `adv_name`.

`notifyNewNodeDiscovered()` returned early for want of a display name, and nothing ever retried:

- the name arrives through the debounced `get_contacts` re-read (`refreshContacts()`), which never notifies, or
- through a later advert, which sees the contact as already known (`wasKnown`), so it skips the notify.

So "Newly Found Nodes" never fired for a MeshCore companion in its default mode. The reporter's logs confirm it: no `New MeshCore Device Detected` line at all. Only manual-add mode (`0x8A`, which carries the name) could notify.

## Fix (`src/server/meshcoreManager.ts`)

- A first sighting without a name goes into `pendingNewNodeNotifications`. `refreshContacts()` and later adverts resolve it once the name shows up. It still notifies at most once per key (`notifiedNewNodes`).
- `connect()` now holds `newNodeNotifySuppressed` while it seeds contacts from the DB and runs `get_contacts`. Adverts that race ahead of that sync can't be told apart from known contacts, so they don't notify. (Before this PR, a named `0x8A` in that window could notify for a known node on reconnect; the new test covers it.)
- `disconnect` clears pending keys.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. No packets sent. The `get_contacts` re-read already ran on every nameless advert (#3646); this PR only reads its result.
2. **Spam:** one notification per genuinely new public key per process, deduped as before. A bulk contact sync (first connect with hundreds of contacts, or reconnect) never notifies: `refreshContacts()` only resolves keys already parked as new, and the connect-time sync suppresses new-node notifications. No feedback loop: notifications don't feed back into the contact path. No new limit added.
3. **Timers:** no new timer. After a restart, known contacts come back from the DB seed before notifications are armed again, so a restart doesn't re-notify for them.

## Tests

`src/server/meshcoreManager.contactPersistence.test.ts` gains 6 cases: pubkey-only advert then name from `get_contacts`, then name from a later advert, a 201-contact sync that notifies only for the one new key, a 200-contact sync with nothing pending, adverts racing the connect-time sync, and a pending key whose contact is gone. 5 of the 6 fail without the fix.

- `npx vitest run src/server/meshcoreManager*`: 596 passed, 0 failed
- `tsc --noEmit` (app + server): clean
- ESLint counts for the touched files match the baseline

title: fix(scripts): match release runs to the tag's commit in watch-release.sh
body:
`scripts/watch-release.sh` reported a false "all green" on v4.16.2-rc2 and rc3.

## Cause
The script listed the last N `--event release` runs across **every** release and treated TAG as a label only. Straight after `gh release create`, the new tag's runs hadn't registered yet, so the previous release's finished runs counted as a pass. `gh run list --event release` also returned stale pages that left out the most recent releases entirely.

## Fix
- **Match runs by commit.** The script resolves TAG (or the latest release when no tag is given) to its commit SHA, lists runs with `--commit <sha>`, keeps only `release`-event runs, and takes the newest run per workflow name. A re-created release leaves an older run of the same workflow on that commit.
- **Wait for every release workflow.** Before declaring a pass, the script requires a run from every workflow that has an `on: release` trigger in `.github/workflows`: Desktop Release, Docker Build and Publish, Release Pipeline and Reticulum Bridge. `WATCH_RELEASE_EXPECTED` overrides that list.
- **Same interface.** Exit codes and `-q` behave as before. An unknown tag now exits 2.

## Tested against real releases
- `v4.16.2-rc3` resolves to `a62b0f43`: the 4 runs are green, so it passes.
- `v4.16.2-rc2` resolves to `b20df5a7`: the duplicate Release Pipeline run is collapsed and it passes.
- With no argument, the script picks the latest release (rc3) and passes.
- An unknown tag exits 2 with a clear message.
- With an expected workflow that hasn't registered, the script keeps waiting and doesn't pass.

+
+### Added
+- **Coverage Report** replaces the Range Test module that firmware 2.8 removed, and it's passive: MeshMonitor sends nothing. Every position fix a radio source hears is stored with that radio's SNR, RSSI and hop data, and Reports → Coverage plots the fixes on a map coloured by signal. Drive a GPS node around and read the map.
+  - MQTT gateways (opt-in recording) and MeshCore receptions also count as receivers.

+- **`{{ trigger.packetHash }}`** on MeshCore "A message is received" automations: the 16-character on-wire packet hash, for linking a message to CoreScope maps such as `map.meshcore.com.hr/#/packets/<hash>`. Best-effort for DMs. (#5357, #5359)
+- **MeshCore "Add to radio"** adds a node the radio hasn't stored to its contact list, so you can log in to it. If the list is full, favourites are never evicted. (#5349, #5351)
+- **User Scripts Gallery:** Discord Webhook DM / PUBLIC. (#5345, #5346)
+
+### Changed
+- **MeshCore adverts default to zero-hop, and automated flood adverts are limited to one per hour per source.** That covers the auto-announce burst, timer triggers and the automation advert action, and the limit survives restarts. A manual flood advert asks for confirmation and states its airtime cost. Saved configs with no mode set keep flooding, but fall under the hourly limit. (#5347)
+- **Longest Active and Record Holder cards need `traceroute:read`** on the source, and Clear Record needs `traceroute:write`. They used `info` before, which applies across all sources and so could not limit them to one. (#5330)

+- **Position History:** the heading triangle no longer blocks hover and click on the dot beneath it. (#5356, #5358)
+- **Dashboard Packet Rate card** is limited to the selected source, and starring a derived chart now keeps its underlying data from being pruned. (#5332)

title: feat(automation): {{ trigger.packetHash }} for MeshCore messages; verify channel frames by decryption (#5357)
body:
Closes #5357.

Adds `{{ trigger.packetHash }}` to the Automation Engine's "A message is received" trigger for MeshCore messages. It is the 16-character on-wire packet hash (`calculateMeshCorePacketHash`, the same value `packet_capture.py` and CoreScope sites such as `map.meshcore.com.hr/#/packets/<hash>` key on). An automation can now link a received message to its packet.

## Linking each message to its raw frame
The companion radio delivers decoded messages separately from the raw frames it hears (LogRxData), so each message has to be matched to the frame that produced it.
- **Channel messages (changed): matched by decryption, not arrival order.** Of the waiting GRP_TXT frames, the one used is the frame whose channel hash matches, whose MAC checks out, and whose decrypted timestamp and text equal the received message. That frame supplies the hash plus path, SNR, RSSI and scope. If no frame checks out, nothing is attached; no guess is made.
  - This also fixes route and SNR being attached to the wrong message. Previously matching went by arrival order, so a duplicate flood copy or a frame from a channel we don't hold could land on the next message.
  - Other copies of a matched frame are dropped from the buffer, and a 30-second set of used hashes keeps late copies out.
- **Channel 0:** the firmware always loads the default "Public" key into slot 0 but reports it as empty, so we fall back to that key when the database has none. A wrong key can only fail to match; it can never produce a false match.
- **Text cut short:** the firmware truncates text to fit its frame, so a received text of 160 bytes or more only has to be a prefix of the decrypted text.
- **DMs: best-effort.** A DM can't be decrypted without the radio's private key, so matching still goes by the one-byte sender hash. Duplicate copies are dropped the same way, and ties are broken by the message's `path_len` and then SNR. SNR only arrives with v3 message frames, which aren't in use yet, so path length does the tie-breaking today. The docs describe the DM value as best-effort.
- **MQTT-ingested channel messages:** the hash is computed straight from `raw_hex`, so it is exact. It's added to the event after the database insert, so the stored row is unchanged.
- **Always empty for:** room posts, messages the radio queued while MeshMonitor was disconnected, outbound messages, and Meshtastic or Reticulum messages.
- **Layering:** the manager fills an in-memory cache of channel keys from the `channels` table on connect and after each channel sync, and hands the backend a synchronous lookup function. The backend still has no database access, and the message handler stays synchronous, so message and auto-ack order are unchanged.

**Case:** the token is uppercase. CoreScope's `/api/packets/<hash>` lookup ignores case. The site's live-update filter doesn't, so on an uppercase link new sightings of that packet won't stream in live; the docs mention this.

## Behaviour change
A channel message whos

title: fix(restore): reset PostgreSQL sequences after restore; migration 174 repairs restored installs
body:
## Summary
A PostgreSQL restore puts every row back with its original `id` but never advanced the tables' serial/identity sequences. After a restore, the next insert without an explicit id got an id that already existed: plain inserts failed with a duplicate-key error, and `insertIgnore` (`onConflictDoNothing()` with no target) **silently dropped the row**, until the sequence passed the highest restored id. MySQL and SQLite advance their counters on explicit-id inserts, so only PostgreSQL was affected. Found while designing saved surveys for #5277.

## Changes
- **Shared helper** `resetPostgresSequences(client)` in `src/server/migrations/postgresSequences.ts` (raw SQL allowed there). Finds every owned sequence in the current schema (tables and partitioned tables) via `pg_get_serial_sequence`; names come from `quote_ident()` / the catalog, never string-built. **Forward-only:** it advances a sequence to MAX(id) only when MAX has caught up with the sequence's real next value, so it never hands out ids of deleted rows and is always idempotent. It also fixes the old helper's off-by-one (an empty table's first id was 2).
- **Restore** (`systemRestoreService.restorePostgres`): calls the helper on the restore client after the last insert, before COMMIT; a failure rolls the restore back. `setval` isn't transactional, but forward-only moves make that harmless.
- **`migrate-db` CLI** uses the shared helper instead of its own copy (same output, "Checked N sequences, advanced M").
- **Migration 174** runs the reset once on PostgreSQL, so installs already restored with the bug are repaired on upgrade. One bad sequence is logged and skipped rather than blocking boot. No-op on SQLite and MySQL.

## Mesh impact checklist
None: database maintenance only. No sends, events or timers.

## Issues Resolved
None filed; follow-up from #5277.

## Documentation Updates
None needed (internal behaviour; restore now just works).

## Testing
- [x] Reproduced on real PostgreSQL: with the reset disabled the new restore regression test fails with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint`; with it enabled a plain insert gets id 41 and a Drizzle `onConflictDoNothing()` insert gets 42 instead of being dropped
- [x] Helper on real PG: SERIAL, IDENTITY and a mixed-case quoted table all get 6 after explicit ids 1..5; empty table gets 1; never moves backward; idempotent; runs inside a transaction
- [x] Migration 174: repairs a stale PG sequence (collides before, 8 after); SQLite and MySQL no-ops; real MySQL shows AUTO_INCREMENT already advances on its own
- [x] Full Vitest suite with PG/MySQL up: success, 22,145 total, 0 failed; PG/MySQL suites ran (0 pending)
- [x] `tsc` clean for both configs; `lint:ci` clean

title: feat(coverage): saved surveys, Phase 4b (#5277)
body:
## Summary
The last phase of the Coverage Report epic. A **saved survey** is one sender over one time window, with a name, notes and an optional broadcast interval. Its receptions are kept past the normal retention period until the survey is deleted, so a drive can be revisited weeks later. Surveys can be started live (they end when stopped, or on their own after 24 h) or saved from the range being viewed. Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/COVERAGE_P4_SPEC.md` §2b.

## Changes
- **Table** `coverage_surveys` (migration 173, SQLite/PG/MySQL), **global** by design: one survey spans every source that heard the sender. UUID text primary key, not serial. Added to CLAUDE.md's global-by-design exceptions and registered with the migrate-db CLI.
- **Repository** `CoverageSurveysRepository` (CRUD, live lookup, caps, exemption windows). Live surveys end at read time via `effectiveSurveyEndAt` (24 h cap): no timer, so a restart or save can't extend or reset one.
- **Retention exemption** through the single `purgeOlderThan(cutoff, exemptions)` seam P1 reserved: receptions of a survey's sender inside its window are skipped by the hourly sweep. Source deletion and purge-all-nodes still delete receptions (U6).
- **Routes** `/api/analysis/coverage/surveys` (list, create, update, stop, delete), `ok()`/`fail()`:
  - List: admins see all; others see their own plus surveys whose sender they can see; anonymous users see none.
  - Create: any logged-in user who can see the sender (`SENDER_NOT_VISIBLE` otherwise), Meshtastic via `buildPositionFilter`, MeshCore via `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`.
  - Edit, stop, delete: creator or admin (`FORBIDDEN`).
  - Caps (U4): 24 h live, 7-day saved range, 50 per user, 500 total (`SURVEY_LIMIT_REACHED`); one live survey per sender (`SURVEY_ALREADY_LIVE`).
  - `/receivers` gains `since`/`until` so an old survey still lists its receivers.
  - `parseSenderParam` moved to `src/server/utils/coverageSenderParam.ts` to break a circular import between the two route files.
- **Backup** (U3): `coverage_surveys` plus the receptions inside survey windows (ids dropped, so restore assigns fresh ones). Other receptions are still not backed up.
- **UI** `CoverageSurveyBar`: survey picker (searchable), Start survey, Save as survey, Stop, Edit (name, notes, interval), Delete with the shared `Modal` confirm; live badge with elapsed time and auto-end. Selecting a survey sets the sender, window and saved receiver view, and feeds its interval to gap detection. `/reports?report=coverage&survey=<id>` opens one.
- **Docs:** "Saved surveys" section in `docs/features/coverage-report.md`; epic phase log (all four phases now checked off).

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime: zero.** No sends.
2. **Spam: none.** No messages, notifications or events.
3. **Timers: none new.** Live-survey end is computed at read time from the stored start time; the hourly retention sweep only gains a WHERE clause.

title: fix(meshcore): stable node list, clear not-on-radio errors, unambiguous prefix lookups (#5349)
body:
Fixes #5349.

## What investigation found
The issue blamed a prefix collision in `resolveContactByPrefix`. Checking the code showed that none of the three symptoms goes through it: every contact-message, login and path-discovery frame carries a prefix of 6 bytes or more, so contacts that only share the first byte (`57…`) cannot collide there. Each symptom has its own cause. The full write-up, with file and line references and firmware citations, is in `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_5349_INVESTIGATION.md`.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Node lists show 6, then 7, then 13 | `useMeshCore.recomputeNodes` rebuilt the node list from the radio's contact table on every contact push, dropping nodes known only from the database. A reload brought them back. | Merge contacts into the existing list. Keep `advType` from the contact, then the previous/DB value, then 0; it was `?? 0`, which wiped the stored type. |
| "Log in" fails instantly | The radio answers `ERR_CODE_NOT_FOUND` for a contact it doesn't hold, without transmitting (`MyMesh.cpp`). MeshMonitor showed Log in for contacts seen only through 0x8A NewAdvert (manual-add mode, hop limit, or full table), ignored 0x8F and 0x90, and returned a generic 401. | Before login, status and CLI, check the radio holds the contact; this is a local read. If not, return 409 `CONTACT_NOT_ON_DEVICE` with a readable message. Contacts carry `onDevice`, and 0x8F / 0x90 are handled. The UI shows a notice and disables login and CLI for those contacts. |
| Repeater stuck as non-repeater | Most likely the firmware ignoring adverts that are not newer than the stored one (`BaseChatMesh.cpp:124`), while MeshMonitor kept re-applying the radio's stale type. The UI's `?? 0` made it worse. | The list-merge fix above removes the UI part. A stale-type warning is left for later, until the reporter's case is confirmed. |
| Prefix lookups | Only 1–3-byte path-hop hashes realistically collide, which gave wrong repeater names. | `resolveContactByPrefix` and `resolvePublicKey`, plus the frontend key helpers (`uniquePrefixMatch`), now return nothing when several contacts match. Hops are named only when exactly one repeater or room server matches. |

## New: "Add to radio"
This adds a node the radio hasn't stored to its contact table (`CMD_ADD_UPDATE_CONTACT`), so you can log in to it. `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/contacts/:publicKey/add-to-device` uses `nodes:write` scoped to the source, the device rate limiter and an audit entry.

Checked against the firmware source: when the table is full, the radio either evicts the oldest non-favourite contact and pushes 0x8F (when "overwrite oldest" is on), or refuses with `ERR_TABLE_FULL`. It never evicts a favourite, except when adding with type NONE, which we never do.

How the add is protected:
- When the table is full, or its capacity can't be read, the first call returns 409 `CONTACT_TABLE_FULL_CONFIRM` with the count and capacity, and the UI asks the user to confirm.

 upgraded to a MeshMonitor version with this feature appear — there is no

+### Likely gaps
+
+Pick one sender and the map draws **dashed lines** between consecutive
+fixes where the next fix arrived much later than expected: a likely dead
+zone. Hover a line to see how long the gap was and roughly how many fixes

+

+"Other"). Above about 3,000 points it shows an even sample and says so.

title: feat(meshcore): zero-hop adverts by default, hourly floor on automated floods
body:
## Summary
Every advert MeshMonitor sent for a MeshCore source was a **flood** advert: rebroadcast by every repeater within 8 hops. With 20 repeaters in reach that is about 9 s (US) / 25 s (EU) of channel time per advert, against 0.4–1.3 s for a zero-hop advert. There was no zero-hop option, and a timer trigger could flood every minute. Found while writing the Coverage Report's MeshCore survey guidance (#5277, P3).

## Changes
- **`sendAdvert(mode)`** with a required `'zero_hop' | 'flood'` (shared type in `src/types/meshcoreAdvert.ts`). Companion sends the ZeroHop/Flood type byte; repeater runs `advert.zerohop` / `advert`.
- **Hourly floor on automated floods** (auto-announce advert burst, timer triggers, automation `advert` action): at most one flood per 60 min per source. The last flood time is stored per source in the DB (`meshcoreLastFloodAdvertAt`, not client-postable), so a restart or settings save can't reset it. A flood inside the window is skipped and reported (timer `lastError`, automation step failure), never retried or downgraded. Reads are serialised so two automated floods firing together can't both pass. Manual floods aren't blocked but do count.
- **Defaults:** new configs and the manual button use zero-hop. Existing saved configs with no mode keep **flood** (no silent behaviour change) but fall under the floor.
- **Manual UI:** "Advert (nearby, zero-hop)" is the primary button; "Flood advert" asks for confirmation and states the cost. Status bar and Settings → Device actions.
- **Config UIs:** Zero-hop / Flood choice with the cost and hourly-limit warning next to Flood, in the auto-announce burst, timer triggers and the automation `advert` action.
- **`POST /meshcore/advert`** takes `{ mode }` (missing = zero-hop, bad = 400 `INVALID_ADVERT_MODE`), now `ok()`/`fail()`; the one consumer reads only `success`/`error`.
- **Also fixed:**
  - Virtual node `SendSelfAdvert` ignored the app's type byte and always flooded; it now follows it like real firmware.
  - Old repeater firmware without `advert.zerohop` quietly floods on that command. Detected from the reply, recorded as a flood, returned as 409 `ZERO_HOP_ADVERT_UNSUPPORTED`, and further zero-hop requests to that repeater are refused until restart so a timer can't keep flooding.
  - `advert.zerohop` added to the receive-only RF CLI verbs (it could bypass receive-only). The local console quick action now sends `advert.zerohop`.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/meshcore.md` (Adverts / Automated flood limit), automation engine, REST API, receive-only.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** before, every advert flooded and a timer could flood every minute (up to 60 floods/hour ≈ 9–25 min of airtime per hour per source). Now automated floods are capped at 1/hour/source, and new configs plus the button default to zero-hop (one transmission).
2. **Spam:** the floor covers every automated path; manual floods need a confirmation that states the cost; receive-only guards unchanged (and extended t

If you turn the filter on without configuring a selected-contacts list or a name regex, every contact surviving the narrowing filters is targeted. A live **matching targets** preview shows how many contacts the current settings would target, updating as you edit. All settings are per-source and saved from the shared MeshCore Automations save bar.
 
+## Adverts
+
+An advert announces this node so others can add it as a contact. MeshMonitor sends two kinds:
+
+- **Zero-hop** reaches only nodes in direct radio range. No repeater forwards it, so it costs one transmission (roughly 0.4–1.3 s of channel time).
+- **Flood** is forwarded by every repeater within 8 hops. With 20 repeaters in reach that is about 9 s (US presets) or 25 s (EU presets) of shared channel time for a single advert.
+
+The status bar and **Configuration → Device actions** offer **Advert (nearby, zero-hop)** as the main button. **Flood advert** sits beside it and asks you to confirm, stating the cost, before it sends. In the device console, `advert.zerohop` sends a zero-hop advert and `advert` sends a flood; the console's quick-action button sends the zero-hop one.
+
+Repeater firmware that predates the `advert.zerohop` CLI verb floods when asked for a zero-hop advert. MeshMonitor spots this from the repeater's reply, reports that a flood went out, and refuses further zero-hop requests to that repeater until it reconnects. Update the repeater firmware to fix it.
+
+### Automated flood limit

+Automated adverts (the auto-announce advert burst, timer triggers, and the automation **Announce self (advert)** action) can pick zero-hop or flood. New settings default to zero-hop. Settings saved before this choice existed keep flooding, as they always did.
+
+Automated floods are limited to **one per hour per source**. The time of the last flood lives in the database, so restarting MeshMonitor or saving settings does not reset it. Any flood counts toward the hour, including a manual one. When an automated flood falls inside the hour, MeshMonitor skips it (it does not send a zero-hop advert instead) and logs why; a timer trigger records the reason as its last error, and an automation step fails with it. title: Add Discord Webhook DM/PUBLIC to User Scripts Gallery
body:
## Summary
- Adds two User Scripts Gallery entries — **Discord Webhook DM** and **Discord Webhook PUBLIC** — JavaScript Auto Responder scripts submitted by @coinraiser that forward mesh messages (direct and channel respectively) to a Discord channel via webhook, with a rich embed showing SNR, RSSI, hop count, sender, and message text.
- The scripts are hosted externally at [`coinraiser/MeshMonitor-Discord`](https://github.com/coinraiser/MeshMonitor-Discord), so this follows the established external-repo pattern (like the `Codename-11/meshmonitor_user-scripts`, `maxhayim/*`, and `KF7R/meshmonitor-nogales-bwt` entries already in the gallery): only `docs/.vitepress/data/user-scripts.json` is touched (plus the regenerated server-side copy), no in-repo copy of the scripts.
- Ran `npm run scripts:gallery` to regenerate `src/server/data/userScriptsGallery.json` so the two copies stay in sync per the drift-guard test.

## Review notes
- Each script builds a fixed `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/{id}/{token}` URL entirely from `WEBHOOK_ID`/`WEBHOOK_TOKEN` environment variables (loaded via `dotenv` from a local `.env`), never from message text — no SSRF/URL-injection surface.
- No shell-out, `eval`, or arbitrary code execution. The forwarded message text only ever lands inside a JSON string value via `JSON.stringify`, so there's no injection into the Discord embed structure.
- Straightforward `fetch()` POST with a `.catch` on the promise, so a webhook failure won't crash the script.
- The two scripts are near-identical (title/emoji differ) and are meant to be wired to separate Automation Engine "Run Script" rules — one for DMs, one for channel messages — per the source repo's README, which matches MeshMonitor's actual `{{ trigger.* }}` substitution token syntax.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('docs/.vitepress/data/user-scripts.json'))"` — valid JSON
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/unit/UserScriptsGallery.security.test.ts src/server/data/userScriptsGallery.test.ts docs/.vitepress/utils/scriptVersion.test.ts` — 64/64 passing
- [x] `npx vitepress build docs` — docs site builds cleanly with the new gallery entries

Closes #5345

title: fix(meshcore): don't stamp lastHeard to "now" on a contact sync with no advert time
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5341: a favorited, powered-off MeshCore companion's "Last Heard" kept advancing every couple of hours, which the reporter suspected was a node-identity collision from a truncated public key.

That theory doesn't hold: MeshCore nodes are keyed by the full 32-byte public key (`meshcore_nodes` PK is `(sourceId, publicKey)`), so there's no realistic prefix collision. The real cause is that several code paths stamp a contact's `lastSeen` to `Date.now()` without having heard from the node, and `upsertNode()`'s forward-only `lastHeard` guard (#5131) only rejects values *older* than the stored one. "Now" always looks newer, so it sails through.

Three such paths:

1. **`refreshContacts()`**: on every contact sync (reconnect, or debounced after *any* contact's path-update push) it fell back to `Date.now()` for a contact whose device record has no `last_advert` (e.g. added via discovery/QR).
2. **`resetContactPath()`**: a local serial write, yet it set `lastSeen: Date.now()`. The DM-ack-timeout retry (`handleDmAckTimeout`) calls it exactly when the node has gone silent, so every failed DM to an offline node (manual, automation, scheduled) bumped its Last Heard.
3. **`setContactOutPath()`**: same problem; called by the manual "define path" action, Discover Regions, and the owner-name fetch.

## Fix

- `refreshContacts()` snapshots the known `lastSeen` per contact before rebuilding the map, and falls back to that, not `Date.now()`, when the device reports no advert time.
- `resetContactPath()` and `setContactOutPath()` no longer touch `lastSeen`.

Paths that stamp "now" on a genuine reply from the node (live advert, DM received, path-discovery response, discovery response, owner-name reply, telemetry/neighbours `markHeard`) are unchanged.

## Interaction with #5342

#5342 (issue #5339) edits the same `lastSeen` line in `refreshContacts()`: it discards an implausible `last_advert` (drifted RTC) and falls back to `nowMs`, a variable this PR removes. The two conflict textually, and as written #5342 would re-open #5341 for drifted-clock contacts (every sync would stamp "now"). Whichever merges second should resolve to:

```ts
const advertMs = rawAdvertMs !== undefined && isPlausibleMeshCoreTimeMs(rawAdvertMs, Date.now()) ? rawAdvertMs : undefined;
lastSeen: advertMs ?? previousLastSeen.get(c.public_key),
```

and #5342's two "falls back to now" tests should expect the previous value (or `undefined`) instead.

## Test plan
- [x] `src/server/meshcoreManager.lastHeard.test.ts`: replaced the test that asserted the old "falls back to now" behavior; added a "known value survives a later no-advert-time sync" test; added tests that `resetContactPath` and `setContactOutPath` keep the known `lastSeen`.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/server/meshcoreManager src/db/repositories/meshcore src/server/services/meshcoreRemoteTelemetryScheduler src/server/routes/meshcoreRoutes`: 1132 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped, `success: true`
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.ser

title: fix(meshcore): fall back to receipt time when a node's clock is drifted
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5339. A MeshCore node with an unsynced or drifted RTC stamps its adverts and messages with whatever bogus time its own clock currently holds — the reporter observed a single mesh spread from year 2000 to year 2087. MeshMonitor was trusting that device-reported time verbatim in two places, both of which use it as a **sort key**, not just a display value:

- **Node `lastSeen`** (`refreshContacts()`'s bulk `get_contacts` sync, added in #3645): the companion-reported `last_advert` was stored as-is. A drifted clock pins the node's Last Heard at an implausible date, which then breaks Last Heard sort order *and* the node-visibility "maximum age" filter for as long as that value sticks around (a past-drifted node looks stale forever; a future-drifted one never expires).
- **Message `timestamp`** (contact/channel/room message ingestion): the device's `sender_timestamp` was stored as-is, and `messageOrder.ts` sorts channel/DM streams on that field — so a message from a drifted-clock node gets stuck at a bogus position (e.g. the very bottom, behind a "2038" timestamp) indefinitely.

## Fix

Added a small shared helper, `src/server/utils/meshcoreTimestamp.ts` (`isPlausibleMeshCoreTimeMs` / `plausibleMeshCoreTimeMs`), that accepts a device-reported time only when it falls between 2020-01-01 and "now + 1 day" (generous slack for ordinary clock skew, not multi-year drift). Both ingestion sites now fall back to MeshMonitor's own receipt clock (`Date.now()`) when the reported time is missing *or* implausible.

This is the same class of fix already applied to the Meshtastic ingestion paths for boot-uptime clocks (`utils/messageTime.ts`'s `plausibleRxTime`, #4206) — MeshCore's drift just runs in both directions, so this adds a ceiling as well as a floor.

Importantly, this is **strictly additive** to #3645, not a reversion of it: a plausible reported time (however old) is still preserved exactly as before, so a reconnect still doesn't reset every node's Last Heard to "now" (the regression #3645 fixed, and which #2119 separately declined to "fix" by always preferring server time for Meshtastic — this only intervenes when the device's own time is nonsensical, not merely old).

## Changes

- `src/server/utils/meshcoreTimestamp.ts` (new) — the plausibility helper, with unit tests.
- `src/server/meshcoreManager.ts`:
  - `contact_message` / `channel_message` / `room_message` handlers now resolve `timestamp` via `plausibleMeshCoreTimeMs(data.sender_timestamp)` instead of a bare `? … : Date.now()` ternary.
  - `refreshContacts()` now clamps the derived `advertMs` through `isPlausibleMeshCoreTimeMs` before using it for `lastSeen`, falling back to `nowMs` (the same fallback already used when no advert time is reported at all).
- New regression tests: `src/server/meshcoreManager.timestampDrift.test.ts` (message ingestion, past + future drift, all three message types), extended `src/server/meshcoreManager.lastHeard.test.ts` (contact refresh, past + future dr

title: feat(coverage): MeshCore receptions on the Coverage Report, Phase 3 (#5277)
body:
## Summary
Adds MeshCore to the Coverage Report. MeshCore nodes report their position only in adverts, so a companion source now records every advert with a position it hears, along with the SNR, RSSI and hops of that reception. MeshCore Observer sources can opt in per source, as MQTT gateways did in Phase 2. MeshMonitor still sends nothing. Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/COVERAGE_P3_SPEC.md`.

## Changes
- **Recording** (`src/server/utils/coverageMeshCore.ts`): companion `ota_packet` path (always on) and Observer `handleMessage` path (opt-in via `coverage_mqtt_enabled`). Payload-type check first, so other packets cost one compare. Reuses `decodeMeshCorePacket`; `packetKey` = firmware packet hash; `pathKey` = hops + last-hop hash (width kept).
- **Ed25519 signature check** before recording, via `@michaelhart/meshcore-decoder` (already a dependency), run before the replay guard so forged adverts can't poison it.
- **Clockless replay guard**: advert timestamps are unreliable (1994–2103 in the dev DB), so it mirrors firmware's `timestamp <= last` rule with a 60 s window for relayed copies. Also skips our own advert echoing back and observers that are our own companions.
- **Privacy fix:** P1/P2 routes kept any row with a null `senderNodeNum`, which every MeshCore row has. New `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`: the node must be in `meshcore_nodes` for that source (admins included), plus per-source `nodes:viewOnMap` for non-admins. Branches on the row's `protocol`, never `source.type`.
- **API:** hops 0–63; `sender=` accepts a 64-hex public key; `mqttSources` includes observers with a `protocol` field; receiver filter falls back to client-side filtering past 6,000 characters (64-hex ids are wide). MeshCore companion receivers are named from the manager's self info, falling back to the source name.
- **UI:** short public keys (`c34891e5…`), MeshCore badge, **Observer** label, hash-width-aware path in the popup ("3 hops via 66"), hops up to 8, MeshCore survey guidance. Observer sources get the Coverage recording toggle, whose warning says volume is unmeasured.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/coverage-report.md` (MeshCore survey guidance, recording, privacy); epic phase log.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime: zero from MeshMonitor.** The survey's cost is the operator's adverts. Guidance: **zero-hop adverts only, every 60 s** (~0.7% of the channel on US SF7, ~1.9% on EU SF8). Never flood for a survey: with 20 repeaters in reach a flood advert costs ~9 s (US) / ~25 s (EU) of channel time.
2. **Spam: none.** No messages, notifications or automation events; nothing emitted on the event bus.
3. **Timers:** none new. The replay guard is in-memory and forgets after 1 h; a restart only means an old re-sent advert could be recorded once.
4. **Flagged, not changed here:** MeshMonitor's own MeshCore "Send advert" button, the auto-announce advert burst and the automation `advert` action all send a **flood** advert. The survey guidance tells users not to use the button.

body:
## Summary
Phase 1 mapped what your own radios hear. Phase 2 lets an MQTT source (broker or bridge) record what every **uplinking gateway** hears, so one drive shows the coverage of every gateway in the area, each with its own SNR/RSSI. It is **off by default per source** because of row volume; turning it on asks for confirmation and quotes measured numbers. MeshMonitor still sends nothing. Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/COVERAGE_P2_SPEC.md`.

## Changes
- **Recording** (`mqttIngestion.ts` POSITION case, after the geo/ignore/distance gates): pure `evaluateMqttCoverageReception` (`src/server/utils/coverageMqtt.ts`) applies the skip rules: no gateway id, the gateway's own packets, our own gateway echoed back, via-MQTT, non-LoRa transport, SNR 0 with no RSSI (local/UDP copy), packet id 0, rx_time > 600 s old, ok_to_mqtt=0, ignored gateway. One row per gateway (`receiverKind: 'mqtt_gateway'`). No schema change.
- **Setting** `coverage_mqtt_enabled`, per source only (`PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS`), read with `getSettingForSource` never the bare key (#5080); 30 s cache, fail-closed, invalidated on save so it takes effect without a restart.

title: feat(telemetry): purge telemetry outliers with preview (#5333)
body:
Closes #5333.

Remove bad telemetry readings (a spurious 1000 °C, a 0 V battery) without throwing away good history.

## What it does
- **Chart menu:** a new "Clean outliers…" item in each telemetry chart's ⋯ menu on the Info and node graphs. It works on that node, that metric and that source.
- **Settings sweep:** a new Danger Zone entry in Settings. Pick a source and a metric, and every node's series for that metric is judged on its own.
- **Detection** (`src/utils/telemetryOutliers.ts`): a point is removed when it sits more than k × MAD from the median of its own series, and/or falls outside optional min / max bounds. k defaults to 6 (about 4σ on normal data) and can be set from 2 to 20.
  - Series with fewer than 10 points are skipped.
  - A flat series (MAD 0) flags nothing, and the dialog suggests a bound instead. The mean-absolute-deviation fallback would have removed real values.
- **Preview first:** it shows the affected count, the range of values being removed, the series median and a table of the flagged points. Delete is a separate, confirmed step.
- **Delete safety:** the preview returns the highest row id in scope and a fingerprint of the flagged ids. Delete re-runs the analysis only over rows up to that id. If the flagged set has changed, it returns 409 `PREVIEW_STALE` and deletes nothing. The net effect: newer rows are never touched, and it removes exactly what you previewed or nothing.
- **Audit and access:** each purge writes a `telemetry_outliers_purged` audit entry. The feature is admin-only through the existing `/api/purge` router, and every call is scoped by `sourceId`.

Endpoints: `POST /api/purge/telemetry/outliers/preview`, `POST /api/purge/telemetry/outliers` and `GET /api/purge/telemetry/outliers/types`, all using the `ok()` / `fail()` helpers.

## Mesh impact
None. It only touches the database: no packets, timers or notifications.

## Screenshot (dev container, preview only — nothing was deleted)
![Clean outliers dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/5333-telemetry-outlier-purge/docs/public/images/features/5333-clean-outliers.png)

## Testing
- Full Vitest suite with PostgreSQL and MySQL running: 0 failed (109 skipped, the normal count).
- New tests:
  - the detection math;
  - the repository queries on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL, each suite on its own database;
  - per-source isolation: a purge on source A never touches source B;
  - route tests on `createRouteTestApp`: admin and non-admin, 400 validation, 404 unknown source, preview deletes nothing, rows above the cutoff survive, a stale preview gets 409, the audit entry is written;
  - dialog component tests, including the menu item being hidden for non-admins.
- Both `tsc` configs are clean, and `lint:ci` passes.
- Checked in the browser: on a real Voltage series, k=6 flags 0 of 7,421 readings, k=3 flags 45 and k=2 flags 887. I found and fixed a layout bug where the k field stretched to 180 px tall.

## Not included
- The Dashboard fav

title: feat(coverage): Coverage Report — measured RF coverage map, Phase 1 (#5277)
body:
## Summary
Firmware 2.8 removed the Range Test module. This adds a passive replacement: every position fix a Meshtastic radio source hears is stored with that radio's SNR, RSSI and hop data, and **Reports → Coverage** plots the fixes on a map coloured by signal. MeshMonitor sends nothing; the operator drives a GPS node around and reads the map. Phase 1 of 4 in the Coverage Report epic (plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/COVERAGE_REPORT_EPIC.md`, spec: `COVERAGE_P1_SPEC.md`).

## Changes
- **Data:** migration 172 creates `coverage_receptions` on SQLite/PG/MySQL. One row per packet per path (unique on source, receiver, sender, packet, path). The schema already carries `protocol` and `receiverKind` so P2 (MQTT gateways) and P3 (MeshCore) reuse it. New `CoverageReceptionsRepository`.
- **Recording** (`meshtasticManager.maybeRecordCoverageReception`): always on for radio sources, non-blocking, never throws into RX, no `dataEventEmitter` emit. Skips MQTT/UDP/API transports, our own position, Store & Forward, Virtual Node requests, packets without an id, and stale rx_time (> 10 min, fw 2.8 NodeDB replays).
- **Zero-hop detection:** a hop_limit-0 packet arrives 0/0 with relay_node zeroed by the receiver, so true zero-hop is identified by `decoded.bitfield` presence (verified against firmware source), not the relay byte.
- **Retention:** hourly cutoff purge; global setting `coverage_retention_days` (1–90, default 7) in Global Settings → Coverage Report, GLOBAL_ONLY. Source deletion and purge-all-nodes delete that source's receptions. Not in backups (regenerable), but carried by the migrate-db CLI.
- **API:** `GET /api/analysis/coverage/{receivers,senders,receptions}`, `ok()`/`fail()` envelope, per-source `nodes:read` permission. `buildPositionFilter` extracted unchanged into `src/server/utils/positionVisibility.ts` so these routes apply the same hidden-from-map / private-position / channel viewOnMap gates as `/api/analysis/positions`. Receivers come from recorded rows, not source-type strings.
- **UI:** Coverage card on the Reports page: BaseMap with one dot per fix coloured by best SNR or RSSI (new `rssiToColor`), receiver markers, filters (time presets + custom, sender, receivers, hops exact/up-to, colour metric), popup naming the sender and listing each receiver with SNR, RSSI, direct/relayed and distance. Setup guidance panel with the airtime table.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/coverage-report.md`, entries in analysis-reports.md, global-settings.md and the sidebar.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime: zero.** No sends, requests, traceroutes or config pushes. The only cost is the operator's survey-node setup; the guidance recommends hop_limit 0 (1 tx per fix, ~2% of the channel for a 1 h drive at 30 s) and gives hop_limit 1 as the fallback for receivers older than fw 2.7.20, which drop zero-hop packets.
2. **Spam: none.** No messages, notifications or automation events; receptions are not emitted on the event bus.
3. **Timers:** only the hourly retention

--- docs/features/coverage-report.md (+152/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+# Coverage Report
+
+The Coverage Report is a passive, measured coverage map: dots on a map,
+coloured by signal, built from real position packets your radios already
+heard. It replaces the Range Test module Meshtastic firmware 2.8 removed —
+but works differently. Range Test made two nodes trade dedicated test
+packets. Coverage Report needs no dedicated test traffic at all: drive a node
+that broadcasts its position, and every receiver that hears it becomes a
+data point.
+
+## MeshMonitor sends nothing
+
+**This feature sends zero packets.** It only records position packets a
+Meshtastic source already received over RF. MeshMonitor never pushes
+configuration to your survey node and never requests anything from the mesh
+to build this report. The only airtime cost is the survey node's own
+position broadcasts — see [How to survey](#how-to-survey) below for the
+numbers.
+
+## How to survey
+
+Take one node with GPS for a drive (or walk) around the area you want to
+map, with position broadcast turned on. Recommended settings on that node:
+
+- **hop_limit 0** — the position travels no further than direct radio range,
+  which is what a coverage map wants to measure.
+- **Smart position** enabled — it honours `hop_limit 0` rather than
+  overriding it with the firmware default of 3.
+- **Position interval 30 seconds or more** — more frequent broadcasts add
+  airtime without adding much new coverage data.
+
+**Receiver firmware caveat:** a receiving node only keeps a zero-hop
+(`hop_limit 0`) packet on firmware **2.7.20 or later** — older firmware
+drops packets with `hop_start == 0` before it even decrypts them. If any
+node in your mesh that might hear the survey drive runs older firmware, use
+**hop_limit 1** instead. A direct copy still shows as 0 hops in the report;
+the cost is that each neighbour now rebroadcasts the packet once too.
+
+Airtime cost at a 30-second position interval:
+
+| `hop_limit` | Tx per fix | % of channel per hour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 0 | 1 | ~2% |
+| 1 | 2–4 | ~4–8% |
+| 3 | 4–8 | ~8–16% |
+
+These are rough estimates (a position packet takes about 0.5–0.6 s on
+LongFast) and scale with how many neighbours rebroadcast. `hop_limit 3` is
+shown for reference only — it is not recommended for surveying.
+
+The report's own **Setup guidance** panel (collapsed by default, below the
+map) repeats this same recommendation and table.
+
+## Reading the report
+
+Open **Analysis & Reports** from the dashboard sidebar, then click the
+**Coverage Report** card.
+
+### Filters
+
+- **Time range** — presets (1 h, 6 h, 24 h default, 3 days, 7 days) or a
+  custom from/to range with an **Apply** button. Nothing refetches until you
+  click a preset, click Apply, or click Refresh.
+- **Sender** — narrow to one survey node, or leave on **All**. The dropdown
+  shows each sender's name, `!id`, and how many fixes it produced in the
+  current window.
+- **Receivers** — a checkbox list of every receiver that has heard anything
+  in the retention window, defaulting to all selected.
+- **Hops** — Any, or an exact hop count 0–7. Check **Up to this many hops**
+  to turn it into a ceiling instead of an exact match.
+- **Colour by** — SNR (default) or RSSI.
+- **Refresh** — re-runs the current filters against the latest data. The
+  report does not poll in the background.
+
+### The map
+
+Each dot is one physical position fix. Its colour is the **best** (highest)
+reading among the receptions currently in scope — with one receiver
+selected, that receiver's own reading. Receiver locations are drawn as
+larger, distinctly outlined markers with a permanent name label.
+
+Click a dot to see every reception of that fix within your current filter:
+receiver name, SNR, RSSI, whether it arrived **direct** or **relayed** (with
+the hop count and the relaying node's short ID), and the distance between
+the fix and that receiver. RSSI can be blank ("—") when the receiving
+firmware didn't report it; SNR is blank the same way. A path shows as
+**Unknown** rather than a hop count when the packet's zero-hop bitfield
+isn't present — that happens on firmware older than 2.5.0.
+
+The legend shows the same four signal bands (Excellent / Good / Fair /
+Poor) used elsewhere in MeshMonitor, plus **No data**. For a fix heard with
+one or more hops, the colour reflects the **last relay's link**, not a
+straight line back to the original sender — the dot's position is the
+sender's, but its colour describes the hop that actually reached the
+receiver you're looking at.
+
+A **truncation banner** appears if a window returns more than the report
+will load (about 10,000 rows); narrow the time range or filters to see the
+rest. An **empty state** explains that only receptions recorded since you
+upgraded to a MeshMonitor version with this feature appear — there is no
+backfill from data collected before that.
+
+## What gets recorded
+
+In this release, only **Meshtastic radio (RF) sources** record receptions,
+and they do so **always** — there's no per-source toggle to turn it off, the
+way there is for the packet log. A position packet that arrived over MQTT on
+a Meshtastic source is skipped, since an MQTT-relayed copy's SNR isn't your
+radio's own reading.
+
+MeshMonitor stores **one row per distinct path**: the same fix heard
+directly and heard again relayed through a different neighbour are two
+separate rows, because they describe two different links. An exact repeat
+of the same path (a retransmission of the identical packet through the
+identical relay) collapses into the one row already stored — first copy
+wins, later copies aren't merged in.
+
+## Retention
+
+Open **Global Settings → Coverage Report** to set how many days of receptions are
+kept, from **1 to 90**, default **7**. This is a single, deployment-wide
+setting, not a per-source one. An hourly background sweep deletes rows older
+than the configured window. **Lowering the value deletes older data on the
+next sweep, and that cannot be undone** — the settings field warns about
+this before you save.
+
+## Privacy
+
+A position only appears on the Coverage Report if it would also appear on
+the [Map Analysis](./map-analysis) positions layer: hidden-from-map nodes,
+private overrides you don't hold the permission to view, and channels
+without "view on map" enabled are all excluded, using the same checks as
+`/api/analysis/positions`. You also need **read** permission on a source to
+see its receivers, senders, or receptions at all — a source you can't read
+contributes nothing to the report.
+
+## What's next
+
+Phase 1 covers Meshtastic RF receptions only. Planned follow-ups (not yet
+built, and not scheduled): MQTT gateway receivers as their own opt-in
+receiver type, MeshCore receptions, and likely-gap detection, saved surveys
+exempt from retention, a summary panel, and CSV/GeoJSON export.
+
+## Related
+
+- [Analysis & Reports](./analysis-reports) — the workspace this report's
+  card lives in
+- [Map Analysis](./map-analysis) — the positions layer this report reuses
+  the same visibility rules from
+- [Packet Monitor](./packet-monitor) — the opt-in per-source packet logs,
+  a different feature with its own retention model
+- [Global Settings](./global-settings) — where the retention window is configured

title: feat(telemetry): per-transport traffic series + device-counter labels, Phase 3 (#5101)
body:
Closes #5101 (Phase 3 of 3; the epic is complete once this merges). Epic plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSPORT_BREAKDOWN_EPIC.md`. Spec: `TRANSPORT_BREAKDOWN_P3_SPEC.md`.

## Device counters (these cannot be split)
The node's firmware LocalStats counters have no transport field, so they keep their "(Device)" titles and gain a visible one-line caption saying they cover all transports combined. The caption appears on:
- the Info tab: Radio Statistics and Packets TX / RX;
- Packet Rate Trends and the Dashboard Packet Rate card;
- the Device telemetry charts.

The Unified Telemetry page's short labels gain "(Device)" too. Existing translated strings are unchanged; only new keys were added.

## New MeshMonitor-computed series
Both charts appear on the Info tab ("Traffic by Transport") and as Dashboard favorite cards:
- **Nodes Heard by Transport:** three lines. Each counts the nodes whose `transportLast*` stamp for that transport falls inside the 5-minute bin. A node heard over two transports counts on both lines.
- **Packets Received by Transport:** a stacked area. Each received packet counts once, under its transport.

How it's stored:
- As ordinary `telemetry` rows under the local node: 6 types per Meshtastic TCP source, 1,728 rows a day per source, no migration. Each row's `packetId` is the bin index, so the unique index from migration 032 keeps only the first write for a bin.
- **Packet counting:** an in-memory counter at the packet-receive seam, with the current bin checkpointed to a per-source settings row every 30 s (only when counts changed), when each bin opens, and on graceful shutdown.
  - A restart mid-bin restores the counts.
  - A bin that closed while the process was down is written on startup.
  - A crash loses at most the last 30 s of packet counts.
- **Timers:** both are `unref`'d, and neither reads a setting, so no settings save can re-arm them. Clients can't POST the checkpoint key.

## Fixes found by live validation
- **Firmware 2.8 NodeDB replays were counted as live packets** (#5034): about 70 extra RF packets per reconnect. The counter now requires `isLiveReception` (`rx_time` within 120 s). Node stamps keep the existing 6 h replay rule (#4192), so Nodes Heard still spikes in a bin that contains a reconnect. Spec R12 documents this.
- **Idle sources left holes after a crash:** an idle source's checkpoint never moved forward, so a crash across a bin boundary left a gap. A zero-count checkpoint is now written when each bin opens (R13).
- **New nodes lost their first stamp:** `upsertNode`'s INSERT branch dropped `transportLast*`, so a brand-new node's first transport stamp was lost. Fixed, with tests on all three backends.

## Fixes you approved
- The Dashboard Packet Rate card ignored the selected source, so it showed rates across all sources.
- Starring a derived chart (Packet Rate, and the new transport charts) now protects its underlying rows from telemetry retention, through an expansion map in `telemetryRetention.ts`.

title: feat(transport): per-transport route records and message split, Phase 2 (#5101)
body:
Refs #5101 (Phase 2 of 3). Epic plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSPORT_BREAKDOWN_EPIC.md`. Spec: `TRANSPORT_BREAKDOWN_P2_SPEC.md`.

## Migrations (idempotent on all three backends; full column DDL; nothing is dropped or rebuilt)
- **169:** adds `route_segments.transportMechanism INTEGER` and an index on `(sourceId, transportMechanism, distanceKm)`, so the per-transport record lookups stay fast on ~865k-row tables.
- **170:** adds `messages.transportMechanism INTEGER`.
- **171:** a best-effort reclassify of existing record holders, as you chose.
  - How it works: it matches each old record to the traceroute that produced it, using a pure, unit-tested helper (`segmentTransportBackfill.ts`). That sets its transport per hop.
  - Scope: it touches only flagged record-holder rows (at most 50 candidate traceroutes per segment), and every write is guarded with `IS NULL`. If one record has the same transport as another on the same source, the longer one is kept.
  - Failure: it never blocks boot, and a second run changes nothing.
  - On the dev DB: 2 records examined, both unmatched because their traceroutes were pruned, so both stay RF and show a note saying why.

## Behaviour
- **Route segments** store their transport per hop: the traceroute's transport, or MQTT when that hop's SNR is the unknown-SNR marker. MQTT ingestion stamps MQTT on everything it writes.
- **Record holders** are kept per (source, transport). The Longest Active and Record Holder cards show one labelled record per transport, and hide transports with no record. Clear Record works per transport and then refetches the records. MQTT-only sources show a single unlabelled record.
- **Messages:**
  - Every received message stores its transport, and outbound messages store INTERNAL (0), as you chose.
  - Total Messages gains a UDP count.
  - A message flagged `viaMqtt` counts as MQTT, as you chose (`classifyMessageTransport`). This keeps Phase 1's counts the same.
- **Bug fixes found along the way** (you approved all three):
  - Longest Active no longer returns the frozen record-holder copy.
  - MQTT sources now set record holders.
  - Route-segment permissions are now per source. The routes are gated on `traceroute` (read for the cards, write for Clear Record) instead of `info`, which is cross-source by design. DELETE requires a `sourceId` and takes an optional `transport`. Previously, SQLite cleared every source's record and PostgreSQL/MySQL returned 500. The Info tab hides the two cards when the user lacks `traceroute:read`.
- **API** changes are additive: the existing top-level fields are kept (now the longest record across transports), plus `transport` and `byTransport: {rf, udp, mqtt}`. `tests/api-exercise-test.sh` is unaffected: it calls these routes as admin without a `sourceId`.

**Permission change to note:** a non-admin with `info` but no `traceroute` grant on a source no longer sees these two cards for that source.

## Mesh impact
None. These are database and UI changes only; n

title: feat(info): per-transport breakdown, Phase 1 (#5101)
body: Refs #5101 (Phase 1 of 3). Epic plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSPORT_BREAKDOWN_EPIC.md`; spec: `TRANSPORT_BREAKDOWN_P1_SPEC.md`. Splits the Info-tab widgets whose data already records transport into RF / UDP / MQTT, and fixes two bugs that recorded the wrong transport. No migrations. ## Bug fixes - **MQTT-ingested traceroutes were classed as RF.** `mqttIngestion.ts` never set `transportMechanism`, so it stayed NULL and read as RF. It is now stamped MQTT. - **Some bridged packets were logged as LoRa.** The `packet_log` RX write used `transportMechanism ?? LORA`, so a packet marked only with `viaMqtt` was logged as LoRa. It now uses `resolveRadioPacketTransport`. Rows already stored stay as they are until packet-log retention removes them (24 h by default). ## Widgets - **Network Survey → Reach by hop count:** each hop bucket is now a stacked RF / UDP / MQTT bar. A route counts as MQTT if any hop on its forward leg has the unknown-SNR marker (the same rule the map uses, #5097); otherwise it takes the traceroute's own transport, with NULL as RF. The survey response adds `byTransport` per bucket only when asked (`includeTransport`), so the Map Analysis `/hop-counts` payload doesn't change. - **Packet Distribution / Nodes by Packet Type:** one All / RF / UDP / MQTT selector drives both cards, backed by `?transport=` on `/api/packets/stats/distribution`. A single `transportConditions` helper in `packetLog.ts` now builds both the Packet Monitor's exact-mechanism filter and this class filter. - **Network Statistics:** - **Total Nodes** gains "Heard via RF · UDP · MQTT". A node heard over more than one transport counts in each, and a note explains this whenever the parts add up to more than the total. - **Total Messages** is now a real per-source count from the new `GET /api/messages/counts`, split RF / MQTT. Before, it was the poll window, which never showed more than 100. The route shares a new `resolveMessageReadAccess` helper, pulled out of `GET /api/messages` unchanged, so the count respects per-channel read permissions. - The breakdowns and the selector are hidden on MQTT-only sources, where they could only ever read "MQTT = total". ## Behaviour change (approved) The per-source poll now passes `transportMechanism` and `transportLastRf/Mqtt/Udp` through `mapDbNodeToDeviceInfo`. As a result, the per-source map's RF / UDP / MQTT toggles now read the same per-transport timestamps (#4240) as the Dashboard map: - UDP nodes start obeying Show UDP. - A node whose only recent transport is MQTT hides while Show MQTT is off. ## Mesh impact None. These changes only read data already stored: no packets, notifications or timers. ## Screenshots (dev container, live data) Info tab, desktop and phone width: ![Info tab desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/5101-p1-transport-widgets/docs/public/images/features/5101-p1-info-desktop.png)

title: fix(dashboard): pin the topbar so iOS 27 stops fogging it (#5286)
body:
Follow-up to #5309 / #5319 (#5286).

## Problem
On an iOS 27 home-screen app the main Dashboard topbar still renders fogged, while per-source pages render crisp — with header text at the same height. So the blur gap isn't the difference; layout is. `.app-header` (per-source) is `position: fixed`; `.dashboard-topbar` sat in the flex column. iOS appears to tint the status-bar band with a fixed top-edge bar's colour instead of blurring.

## Change
- `.dashboard-topbar`: `position: fixed; top/left/right: 0; z-index: 1100` (above the mobile drawer at 1099 and Leaflet controls).
- `.dashboard-page`: `padding-top: var(--dashboard-topbar-height)` so the body starts below it.
- Corrected the App.css comment that said fixed bars blur the same.

Also covers `MeshCoreSourcePage`, which reuses these classes.

## Verification
Dev container, Chrome: desktop 1400×900 and mobile 390×844 — topbar 0→bar height, `.dashboard-body` starts flush below (0px gap/overlap), no page scroll, drawer + backdrop start at the topbar bottom, close control clickable. Style tests pass (204). The iOS blur itself needs on-device confirmation.

Mesh impact: none (CSS only).

title: fix(channels): delete the channel row, and shift cards while dragging (#5324)
body:
Refs #5324. The issue stays open: this fixes two bugs found while investigating it, but not yet the reported "Channel 4 still Empty after moving Channel 5".

## 1. Deleting a channel never removed its row or messages

`handleDeleteChannel` disables the slot on the device, then calls `DELETE /api/channels/:id` to remove MeshMonitor's row and that channel's messages. That call sent no `sourceId`, which the route requires, so it answered 400. The client treated the error as "best-effort" and ignored it. The slot was disabled on the node, but the database row and the channel's messages stayed.

**Fix:** send the resolved `sourceId` as a query parameter, which the route already reads.

## 2. Dragging a channel gave no visual feedback

`SortableContext items={slotOrder}` holds numeric slot indices, but each card called `useSortable({ id: String(slotId) })`. dnd-kit finds items with `indexOf`, so every card sat at index -1 and no card moved aside during a drag. The dragged card stayed in place while a see-through copy floated over the target. Dropping still reordered the list, but the drag looked broken, which may be why the reporter said it only "appears to move".

**Fix:** register the cards under the numeric id.

Mid-drag on the fixed build, dragging `gauntlet` from slot 6 up past slot 5: slot 5 now moves down to make room.

![Channel cards shift during drag](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/fix/5324-channel-delete-dnd/docs/public/images/features/5324-channel-drag-shift.png)

## What this doesn't cover

The reorder itself (`POST /api/channels/reorder`) looks correct. A Meshtastic firmware source read also found nothing that would reject or blank a channel written into an empty slot, and Commit saves to flash and reboots the node. Two explanations remain open for the report, and the reporter's answers on the issue should settle which:
- Apply was never clicked.
- The node silently dropped a settings write, so the config read after its reboot restored slot 4 as empty.

## Testing

- New `ChannelsConfigSection.test.tsx`: the delete call carries `sourceId`, and every card's sortable id is found in the `SortableContext` items. Both tests fail on the old code.

title: feat(enrichment): run NodeInfo Enrichment Fix All on a schedule (#5287)
body:
Closes #5287.

Runs the NodeInfo Enrichment "Fix All" on a schedule — the same analyze + fill-blanks path as the manual button, no new enrichment logic. Global, one scheduler for the install, like Position Estimation.

## Mesh impact

This arms a timer and can transmit, so the checklist applies. **The limits below were agreed with the maintainer before implementation.**

**1. Airtime.** Filling the database costs nothing — it copies blank fields between rows. The cost is the optional **push to device NodeDB**, which sends one over-the-air NodeInfo request with `want_response` per enriched node: roughly 8 transmissions on a 3-hop mesh (request plus reply). Nothing throttled it. To make that concrete, a Run now on my dev instance filled **1,353 nodes** in one pass; pushing all of those at once would have been ~10,800 transmissions.

So a scheduled run fills the DB in one pass and pushes separately:
- **at most 25 NodeInfo requests per run, 30 s apart** (worst case ~200 transmissions over ~12.5 min),
- the remainder in a **persisted queue**, bounded at 1,000, drained first on the next run,
- a **failed push is dropped, never retried**,
- turning push off clears the queue, so re-enabling it later does not release a stale backlog at once.

Default: disabled, push off.

**2. Spam / loops.** No text, no automations fired; enrichment is fill-blanks-only and never re-triggers itself.

**3. Timer safety.** A once-a-minute check compares against a **persisted** last-run time: neither a restart nor a settings save counts as a run, and nothing is re-armed by saving. Enabling does not fire immediately — the enable moment is stored as the reference and the first run lands one full period later. "Run now" is the explicit way to run at once. The run time is recorded when the DB pass finishes, so a crash mid-push does not cause an immediate re-run.

**Schedule floor: one hour.** Interval clamped to 1 hour – 7 days. A cron that fires more often than hourly (`* * * * *`, `*/30 …`, `0,30 …`) is **refused on save with a 400**, and ignored again at run time as a backstop.

## UI

Settings → **Auto-Enrichment**: enable, interval or cron, the push option **with its airtime cost stated right beside it**, Run now, last run + summary, and pending pushes. Also in the config search.

![Auto-Enrichment settings section — attached below]

## Testing

- Full suite: **20,499 passing, 0 failures**. `tsc --noEmit` clean, `lint:ci` clean.
- 20 scheduler tests: the hourly cron floor over several shapes, interval clamping, no run on the enabling tick, a restart honouring the persisted last run, no overlapping runs, push off → no pushes and cleared queue, **exactly 25 pushes with 24 × 30 s gaps and the rest queued**, the next run draining the queue first, failed pushes not requeued, the queue bound, no duplicate queue entries.
- 16 route tests (real harness): valid saves, out-of-range intervals, too-frequent and invalid crons refused, switching to interval without fixing a bad cron, ba

title: fix(lora): follow use_preset for bandwidth, and name presets 9-16
body:
Fixes #5320.

## What was wrong

The modem-preset enum is duplicated across four independent hand-maintained literals, and three of them stopped at `SHORT_TURBO` (8). The configuration *editor* (`MODEM_PRESET_OPTIONS`) stayed current, so a preset could be selected but not displayed back — a `LONG_TURBO` node rendered as `Modem Preset: Unknown (9)`.

The more serious half is the frequency. `config.proto` on `use_preset`:

> When enabled, the `modem_preset` fields will be adhered to, else the `bandwidth`/`spread_factor`/`coding_rate` will be taken from their respective manually defined fields

Firmware ignores those three fields whenever a preset is in use, **and does not write the preset's parameters back into them** — they keep whatever was last stored. A bench RAK4631 on `LONG_TURBO`, read over the TCP API:

```
use_preset    = True
modem_preset  = 9      # LONG_TURBO -> 500 kHz
bandwidth     = 250    # stale; MEDIUM_FAST's parameters,
spread_factor = 9      # ignored by firmware because use_preset is set
coding_rate   = 5
region        = 1      # US
channel_num   = 14
```

Both frequency call sites took that stale bandwidth at face value:

```ts
// deviceAdminService.ts
typeof loraConfigWithDefaults.bandwidth === 'number' && loraConfigWithDefaults.bandwidth > 0
  ? loraConfigWithDefaults.bandwidth : 250,
// sourceRoutes.ts
Number(lora.bandwidth ?? 250),
```

The channel grid is bandwidth-spaced, so the displayed frequency was only right when the stored value happened to match the preset. `LONG_FAST` is 250 kHz — which is why this went unnoticed — while `SHORT_TURBO` / `LONG_TURBO` / `MEDIUM_TURBO` (500 kHz) and `LONG_SLOW` / `LONG_MODERATE` (125 kHz) were all wrong. The node above read **905.375 MHz** while actually on **908.750 MHz**: two slots and 3.375 MHz out.

## What changed

- `calculateLoRaFrequency` takes `usePreset` and resolves the bandwidth the way firmware does — on a preset, from the preset; otherwise from the explicit field. **A genuine manual bandwidth (`use_preset = false`) is still honoured**, so a custom config is untouched. Keying on `bandwidth > 0` instead would not have fixed the reported node, since its stale field is non-zero.
- `deviceAdminService` also returned `bandwidth` straight from that stale field, so the panel reported `250` for a radio running `500`. It now reports the effective bandwidth.
- `MODEM_PRESET_NAMES` (0-16) and the preset → bandwidth table are now canonical in `src/utils/loraFrequency.ts`; the display panel, the backup enum map and `configuration/constants.ts` all read from there instead of their own copies.
- The bandwidth table moved out of the frontend tree because `src/components/**` is not in `tsconfig.server.json`'s include set — a server import from it would compile and then fail at runtime (#4655). `constants.ts` re-exports `getPresetBandwidthKHz`, so its public API is unchanged and its existing tests cover the re-export.
- The panel keeps its Title Case strings (`Long Turbo`), derived from
