title: fix(mobile): node list fills the phone (#5316); blur gap without Version/NN (#5286)
body:
Fixes #5316. Refs #5286. That issue stays open until the reporter confirms the fix on their device.

## #5316: node list leaves a map sliver on the right in per-source view

**Cause:** `NodesTab` renders the expanded list at its stored drag width as an inline `style={{ width }}`. The default is 380px. An inline width beats the mobile rule in `nodes.css`, so on a 390–430px phone the list stopped 10–50px short of the edge. Taps in that strip landed on the map and the controls behind it. Unified doesn't show this because its drawer passes the width through a CSS variable, which the mobile rule overrides, and puts a backdrop over the rest of the screen.

**Fix:** new `resolveNodeSidebarRenderWidth()` in `src/utils/sidebarWidth.ts`. On mobile, a width that would leave less than 64px of map renders as `100%`.
- A width the user dragged narrower is kept, so the list stays resizable on a phone (the intent of the earlier mobile-resize work).
- A landscape phone (~844px) keeps the 380px list next to the map.
- Desktop is unchanged.

## #5286: header still fogged in the rc1 home-screen app

In rc1 a Safari tab showed a sharp header, but the reporter's home-screen app didn't. The rc1 detection (#5309) needs Safari's `Version/NN` UA token, and iOS home-screen web apps have historically sent a UA without `Version/NN … Safari/NNN`. If the reporter's app does the same, the check returns false and no gap applies.

**Fix:** when `navigator.standalone` is true and `Version/NN` is missing, the gap now applies unless the `iPhone OS NN_` token shows a pre-freeze iOS (below 18). Worst case, an iOS 18 home-screen app gets 20px of extra header padding.

**This root cause is a strong guess, not a measurement.** I don't have the reporter's UA string. If rc2 still fogs, the next thing to get is `navigator.userAgent` and `navigator.standalone` from their home-screen app.

## Testing

- Full Vitest suite: 20,435 passed, 0 failed (109 skipped: PG/MySQL containers not running; no schema changes).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `lint:ci` clean.
- New unit tests: 5 for the render width (390/393/430px phones, drag-to-edge, narrow drag kept, landscape, desktop) and 3 for the missing-`Version/NN` UA cases.

title: feat(nodes): add a node from a Meshtastic contact URL (#5317)
body:
Closes #5317.

MeshMonitor already exports a node as a `https://meshtastic.org/v/#...` link. This is the decode side, and it is the only way to message a node this source has never heard: no packet means no row, and no row means no conversation to open.

Follows @Yeraze's triage plan, with one addition (the badge) picked from its optional list.

## What it does

**`decodeSharedContactUrl()`** mirrors the existing encode. It takes the full link or a bare payload — a pasted link often loses the prefix — and refuses anything that is not a decodable contact carrying a usable nodeNum, so a junk paste cannot write a junk row.

**`POST /api/nodes/import-contact-url`** decodes and writes one source-scoped row through the usual `upsertNode` merge, behind `nodes:write` on that source. **It sends nothing over the mesh** — no airtime, so the mesh-impact checklist does not apply.

Re-importing a node that already exists refreshes its identity from the newer link rather than erroring, which is useful for repairing a stale name or key.

**`nodes.importedAt`** (migration 168, all three backends) marks a row as added-from-a-link and never heard. Set only when the row is new, so importing a node that has already been heard does not re-badge it, and the badge clears itself once traffic arrives and sets `lastHeard`.

**UI:** "+ Add from URL" in the node list header opens a paste-and-confirm modal; imported rows carry an "IMPORTED" badge until heard.

## Two bugs the tests did not catch

Both found by driving the real app, and both now have regression tests:

1. **The field never reached the client.** `mapDbNodeToDeviceInfo` is an explicit allowlist and exists in two copies (`nodeDbMaintenanceService.ts`, `dbNodeMapper.ts`). The column was in the DB and the route response, and still arrived `undefined` in `/api/poll`, so the badge could not render.
2. **The row was hidden.** Both copies of the age filter drop any node without `lastHeard` — which is every imported contact. The row existed and never appeared in the list, making the feature useless. Imported-but-unheard nodes now survive the cutoff; normal age rules resume once heard.

## Testing

- Full suite: **20,439 passing, 0 failures**, run with the PostgreSQL and MySQL containers up (skips fell from 1,036 to 109, so the multi-backend suites genuinely ran — this adds a column, so that matters). `tsc --noEmit` clean, `lint:ci` clean.
- New: 9 route tests (real link from the issue, bare payload, source isolation, no re-badge, four junk-link shapes, permission and anonymous), 2 mapper pass-through tests, 2 age-filter tests.
- Verified in a real browser against the dev container by importing the first link from the issue: the node appears with the badge and "Never" as last heard, as in the screenshots.

## Screenshots

Modal and the badged row are attached below.

title: fix(nodes): pick the unified position by observation, not by lastHeard
body:
Fixes #5292.

## Cause

A node heard on several sources has one `nodes` row per source. Both merges picked the newest row by `lastHeard` that carried a fix — but `lastHeard` moves on **any** traffic, not just position packets. Telemetry, neighbour info or routing on a source holding an older, coarser fix made that row "newest", and the unified marker jumped to the coarser grid cell with no new position behind it. The reported node drifted kilometres between a 14-bit (±1.5 km) and a 13-bit (±2.9 km) rendering of one physical spot.

**Two things the issue does not mention:**

1. **The server has the same flaw.** `src/server/utils/mergeNodesAcrossSources.ts` (unified `/api/nodes` and `/api/poll`) picks the newest-`lastHeard` row wholesale and only back-fills *empty* fields from older rows, so its position came from the same wrong row. Fixing only the client hook would have left the API serving the drifting position.
2. **MQTT ingest never stored the inputs the fix needs.** `mqttIngestion.ts` wrote latitude and longitude but not `positionPrecisionBits` or `positionTimestamp`. The column has existed since the 001 baseline; only the TCP path wrote it. So MQTT-fed rows could not be ranked on either axis.

## Fix

New shared `src/utils/positionSelection.ts` — `pickPositionRecord`:

1. Candidates are rows with a usable fix (the caller keeps its own Null-Island policy).
2. Order by `positionTimestamp`, i.e. when the **position** was observed, not when the source last heard anything.
3. Treat observations within 10 minutes as the same event and prefer the finer `positionPrecisionBits` among them. This is the case that actually flaps: several sources receive the same transmission seconds apart, one over RF and the rest relayed through MQTT, each storing it at whatever precision its path preserved.
4. Fall back to `lastHeard` (seconds, converted) for rows written before the ingest path stored a position timestamp.

A genuinely newer fix still wins whatever its precision, so a node that moves is never pinned to a stale finer position.

The window is the one judgement call: it is sized for **relay lag**, not for transmit interval. A slow MQTT hop puts the same packet in a second row seconds to minutes later; ten minutes covers that while keeping a real move prompt. Easy to change if it reads wrong.

Both merges call it, and each carries coordinates, altitude, precision and timestamp from the **same** row, so a merged row never describes a fix that is half one source's and half another's.

MQTT ingest now persists `positionPrecisionBits` and `positionTimestamp`, both dropped with the coordinates on a bogus fix — a precision describing a position we refused to store would otherwise outrank a real one.

## Testing

- `positionSelection.test.ts`: 9 cases, including the exact PARC geometry (coarse row newest by `lastHeard`, fine row newest by observation), a real move winning once outside the window, missing precision ranking last, and the seconds/milliseconds fallb

title: fix(mobile): hide the node-list arrow under the map sheet, contain long timezones (#5291)
body:
Fixes #5291. Two mobile-portrait layout bugs from NullVoid's report, fixed separately below.

## 1. Node-list arrow over the Map controls sheet

The collapsed node-list expand arrow stayed above the open sheet and overlapped its heading.

The issue's diagnosis is right, and it rules out the obvious fix: the arrow renders outside `.map-container`, which is a stacking context at `z-index: 1`, so the sheet's own `1001` is confined below it and raising that number changes nothing.

So `MapSidebar` marks the root element while it is open (`mm-map-sheet-open`) and `nodes.css` hides the arrow from that shared ancestor. `display: none`, not `visibility`/`opacity`, so it leaves hit-testing and the focus order as the issue asks.

CSS decides *when*, which keeps the breakpoints in one place:
- **Full-sheet (`max-width: 768px`)** — hidden, since the sheet covers the whole pane including that corner.
- **Short landscape** — still visible. There the sheet is a right-edge half-panel capped at 60% of the pane, so it never reaches the top-left arrow. The rule is declared after the width block so it wins on a viewport matching both (e.g. 667x375).
- **Desktop** — untouched.

The marker is reference-counted, because the Dashboard renders its own `MapSidebar` and the first one to close must not clear it for the other.

## 2. Custom POSIX timezone overflowing its field

`EST5EDT,M3.2.0/02:00:00,M11.1.0/02:00:00` pushed the chevron outside the field. Two causes:

- The label's flex wrapper had `flex: 1` and no `min-width: 0`, so it refused to shrink below the string's min-content width. It now shrinks, and the raw POSIX text wraps with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` everywhere it is displayed: the closed trigger, the "use custom value" row and each preset's value line.
- The trigger carried an inline `width: 400px`. Inline styles beat stylesheets, so the mobile rule could only reach it with `!important`. That width moves to `.config-custom-dropdown` in `settings.css`, so the responsive rule owns sizing; the `!important`s in App.css are now redundant but left alone as a separate change.

The chevron keeps `flex-shrink: 0`, and **the stored POSIX value is untouched** — this is presentation only.

## Testing

- Full suite: 19,477 passing, 0 failures. `tsc --noEmit` clean, `lint:ci` clean.
- 18 new assertions across two files. The CSS half uses the repo's `cssCascadeResolver` rather than substring greps, so it asserts which rule *wins* at a concrete viewport (portrait phone, 667x375 landscape, desktop) — the failure mode #5053/#5054/#5060 all had. The React half asserts the marker is set, cleared on collapse, cleared on unmount, and held while a second panel is open.

## Not verified on a device

title: fix(meshcore): match the shell's bottom-bar query so landscape lays out
body:
Fixes #5311. Split out of #5310, which bundled two unrelated bottom-bar problems; the portrait gap stays there.

## Cause

Three stylesheets decide when the shell is in bottom-bar mode, and one disagreed:

| File | Query | Matches landscape (956x440 CSS)? |
|---|---|---|
| `src/components/Sidebar.css` | `(max-width: 768px), (max-height: 500px) and (orientation: landscape)` | yes |
| `src/components/nav/SourceNav.module.css` | same | yes |
| `src/components/MeshCore/MeshCorePage.css` | `(max-width: 768px)` | **no** |

In landscape a phone is 956 CSS px wide, so the MeshCore page kept its desktop layout while the nav switched to its full-width bottom bar. `.meshcore-page-body` stayed `flex-direction: row`, so the bar took the whole flex row as an item and the content pane beside it got nothing — a nav row stranded mid-page above an empty body.

Same trap as #5051-#5054: in landscape the width is the long axis, so a width-only mobile query never fires.

## Fix

Widen the query to the one the other two already share.

## Testing

`MeshCorePage.mobileQuery.test.ts` reads all three stylesheets and asserts they declare the same query, that the `column-reverse` rule sits inside it, and that no width-only mobile block remains. jsdom implements no cascade or media matching, so only a source-level assertion can catch two stylesheets drifting apart. Confirmed it fails without the fix (3 of 5 assertions) and passes with it.

Driven in the dev container at 956x440 (iPhone landscape): `.meshcore-page-body` computes `column-reverse`, and the bar measures 44px docked at 396→440 instead of stretching the full 354px height.

![MeshCore source page in landscape with the nav docked at the bottom and the node list filling the page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/fix/5311-meshcore-landscape/docs/public/images/features/5311-meshcore-landscape-after.png)

## Mesh impact

CSS only. No packets, notifications, or timers.

title: fix(header): keep top-bar text below iOS 27's home-screen status-bar blur (#5286)
body:
Fixes #5286.

## What the blur actually is

iOS 27 home-screen web apps draw a system blur over the top of the screen — the status-bar area plus roughly 20px below it — over whatever the page paints there. A Safari tab does not. That is why the header title rendered fogged at rest and turned sharp when the page was pulled down, moving it out of the band.

I built a throwaway test page and drove it on the reporter's iPhone before writing this fix. Measured there:

- **No page CSS changes it.** A fixed bar, an in-flow bar and no bar at all blurred identically — with no bar, the page's own first line of text blurred instead.
- **The band is ~80px tall** from the top edge, on a device with a 62px top inset, so the blur covers the inset plus a ~20px fade.
- **The suggestions in the issue do not work.** Safari 26+ ignores `theme-color`; `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: black-translucent` made no difference; and neither did moving the bar's background onto an absolutely-positioned child (the known Safari 26 tinting workaround).

The only thing that helps is keeping text out of the band, and `+20px` is enough.

## The change

- `--status-bar-blur-gap`, `0px` by default, added to the top-bar padding and height of the per-source header (`AppHeader.css`) and the Dashboard bar (`dashboard.css`), and to `--app-header-height`.
- Set to `20px` only when `navigator.standalone` is true and Safari reports version 27 or later. The detection runs in JS because `(display-mode: standalone)` reports **false** in an iOS 27 home-screen app while `navigator.standalone` reports true — measured on-device.
- The value clamps to `0` when there is no top inset, so landscape is unaffected.
- Safari tabs, iOS 26 and earlier, Android and desktop are all unchanged.

## Testing

- Full suite: 19,453 passing, 0 failures. `tsc --noEmit` clean, `lint:ci` clean.
- 5 new unit tests for the detection (iOS 27 home-screen app, Safari tab, iOS 26, and a browser with no `navigator.standalone`).
- Confirmed on the reporter's iPhone on iOS 27: header sharp in the home-screen app, unchanged in a Safari tab.

@Nullvoid3771 this is deployed at the dev instance if you would like to confirm it on your device before it merges.

## Not included

While testing, a separate problem turned up: on a per-source page in the same home-screen app, a ~62px band of background appears below the bottom nav bar. It is not caused by this change (it reproduces without it) and my attempts to fix it were based on a theory the test page later disproved — a plain fixed `bottom: 0` bar docks flush on that device. Filing it separately rather than holding this fix.

title: feat(meshcore): decode MULTIPART and CONTROL payloads
body:
Follows #5285, which added MULTIPART (0x0A) and CONTROL (0x0B) to the payload-type list (thanks @bryan-arcus). Naming them is right, but both still fell through the decoder's `else` and rendered as raw hex. This decodes their bodies.

The public docs give the CONTROL first byte only ("upper 4 bits is sub_type") and say nothing about MULTIPART's fields, so the layouts come from the firmware.

## MULTIPART (0x0A)

From `Mesh::createMultiAck` and the `PAYLOAD_TYPE_MULTIPART` case in `Mesh::onRecvPacket`:

```
byte 0     remaining << 4 | inner_payload_type
bytes 1..  the inner payload
```

`remaining` counts the packets of the sequence still to come, so 0 marks the last one. The firmware writes and reads only an inner ACK today, so its 4-byte CRC is decoded; any other inner type is named and left as hex.

## CONTROL (0x0B)

The first byte is `sub_type << 4 | sub_flags`. The two live sub-types are the node-discovery pair MeshMonitor already speaks over the companion link (#1027, #4516):

```
REQ  (0x80): [0] sub_type|prefix_only, [1] type filter, [2..5] tag (LE), [6..9] optional since
RESP (0x90): [0] sub_type|node_type, [1] SNR of the request as the responder heard it,
             [2..5] echoed tag, [6..] public key (32 B, or 8 when prefix_only was asked)
```

Both are decoded. An unknown sub-type keeps its raw hex rather than being guessed at.

## A second gap

`meshcore.js` names only the payload types it shipped with and returns null for anything newer, so a MULTIPART or CONTROL packet heard over a **direct radio link** was stored in the packet log with no name at all. `meshcoreNativeBackend` now falls back to our own table, and keeps null for a genuinely unknown type rather than storing a hex string that reads like a name. The MQTT observer path already names both types, so it needed no change.

## Testing

- 13 new decoder cases: the remaining count and wrapped ACK, an unhandled wrapped type, a truncated wrapped CRC, a discovery request (including `prefix_only`), a discovery response with a negative SNR, an unknown sub-type, and a truncated response.
- Full Vitest suite: `success: true`, 19,456 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` clean, `lint:ci` has no in-repo failures.
- Driven in the dev container against seeded CONTROL and MULTIPART rows: both render in the monitor list and decode in the detail modal (screenshots below). The seeded rows were deleted afterwards.

### Screenshots

CONTROL — a node-discovery response:

![CONTROL node-discovery response decoded in the packet-detail modal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/main/docs/public/images/features/5285-meshcore-control-decode.png)

MULTIPART — a wrapped ACK:

![MULTIPART packet wrapping an ACK decoded in the packet-detail modal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/main/docs/public/images/features/5285-meshcore-multipart-decode.png)

## Mesh impact

Decode and display only. No packets sent, no notifications, no timers.

title: chore(deps): bump mqtt from 5.15.2 to 5.16.0
body:
Bumps [mqtt](https://github.com/mqttjs/MQTT.js) from 5.15.2 to 5.16.0.
Release notes

Sourced from mqtt's releases.

Release 5.16.0

Security

This release fixes six advisories. All are reachable from a malicious or misbehaving broker — or anyone who can inject packets into a cleartext mqtt:// hop — with no special client configuration beyond speaking MQTT 5. Upgrade to 5.16.0; everything <= 5.15.2 is affected, including the v4 line, and there is no backport.

Advisory Severity Impact
GHSA-c8jq-r765-cq7g High An unsolicited MQTT 5 Topic Alias throws an uncaught TypeError in the stream write path — kills the Node process, repeatable on every reconnect.
GHSA-rj8f-4655-cgg2 High A SUBACK with the wrong number of reason codes crashes the process, or silently misreports which topics are subscribed.
GHSA-gfxc-3w7m-8ch4 High CONNACK properties were merged into the caller's own options object. A maximumPacketSize of 1 permanently kills the client, survives reconnects, and escapes to other clients built from the same options.
GHSA-fwrw-4mhv-wxvm High A single unsolicited AUTH packet crashes the process on a default MQTT 5 client. Enhanced authentication did not have to be configured.
GHSA-8phv-jwjm-93rr Medium A duplicate CONNACK re-runs connection setup mid-session: in-flight QoS 1 resent under the same ids, all topics resubscribed, message-id state reset.
GHSA-h8jm-hm87-fqw3 Low The advertised receiveMaximum was ignored for inbound QoS 2, letting a broker grow the incoming store without bound. Reconnecting does not clear it.

body:
Bumps [maplibre-gl](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js) from 6.9.0 to 6.10.0.
Release notes

Sourced from maplibre-gl's releases.

v6.10.0

✨ Features and improvements

  • Show the sky in globe view, fading out with altitude instead of with the globe to mercator transition (#8464) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Speed up fill and fill-extrusion triangulation by looking up each vertex's deduplicated index once instead of hashing every triangle corner, and every outline point of a ring that is not subdivided, again (#8425) (by @​cherenkov)
  • Test whether a Marker is behind terrain with a CPU ray walk over the DEM instead of a depth-buffer readback, removing a GPU stall per marker while a map with terrain moves (#8387) (by @​johncarmack1984)

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fix partially blank maps in older Safari versions (#8427) (by @​birkskyum)
  • Fix setStyle calling Map.setTerrain with the wrong this, which made a terrain change in a style diff throw (#8451) (by @​HarelM)
  • Fix hillshade rendering artifacts on mobile GPUs at high zoom levels (#8431) (by @​Turbo87)
  • Free the pooled terrain drape textures once the map is at rest and when terrain is removed, instead of keeping every drape allocated during a pan resident for the life of the map (#8400) (by @​johncarmack1984)

v6.9.1

✨ Features and improvements

  • Stop the scale control forcing a synchronous layout and rewriting its DOM on every frame of a pan or zoom (#8403) (by @​cherenkov)
  • Speed up merging adjacent symbol-placement: line features that share a label, which took time quadratic in the number of features that chain together (

Sourced from @​tanstack/react-virtual's releases.

@​tanstack/react-virtual@​3.14.13

Patch Changes

  • #1282 b48e3b0 - Skip flushSync for the synchronous notify raised from measureElement. React calls measureElement from a ref callback, i.e. while it is committing, and flushSync cannot flush there — it warns in development instead. The commit phase already runs at discrete (sync) priority, so the update lands in the same lane and the same frame without flushSync. Notifies from every other path (ResizeObserver re-measures, scroll adjustments) still flush synchronously.

title: fix(analysis): count hops only from traceroutes the local node took part in (#5289)
body:
Fixes #5289.

## Cause

The issue proposed skipping empty `route` arrays. That would be wrong: `'[]'` is how a real direct neighbour is stored (and #4570 has a test pinning that it stays 0 hops).

The actual bug is that `getHopCounts` counted traceroutes the local node never took part in. It grouped every answered row by `toNodeNum`, but the table holds two kinds of row the code didn't account for:

- **Third-party traces.** An MQTT source ingests every traceroute on the broker, between any two nodes.
- **Responses with no pending row.** These are stored responder→requester, so `toNodeNum` is the *requester*.

So when node X traced its neighbour Y, the row `from=Y, to=X, route=[]` shaded **X** as 0 hops from us, however far away X was.

Measured on the dev database (grouped the way the old query did):

| Source | Nodes shaded | Shaded 0-hop | Disagree with `hopsAway` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yeraze MQTT Broker | 3,756 | 1,532 | 80 of 94 |
| Florida MQTT | 3,611 | 1,366 | 77 of 92 |
| Official MQTT | 1,141 | 1,140 | n/a |

None of the ~550k traceroute rows on these sources involve a local node, so none of that shading meant anything. This also matches the reporter's "4 radios in MQTT" setup.

## Fix

- `getHopCounts` now takes `localNodeNums` and counts only rows where the source's local node is on either end, keyed on the other end:
  - `fromNodeNum = local`: a pending request filled by its response. The peer is `toNodeNum`.
  - `toNodeNum = local`: a response inserted with no pending row. The peer is `fromNodeNum`.
  - If a peer appears in both shapes, the newest row wins.
- A new helper, `resolveLocalNodeNums` (`src/server/utils/localNodeNums.ts`), reads each source's persisted `localNodeNum` setting (the same key `MeshtasticManager.localNodeSettingKey` writes), so it also works for disconnected sources. Both callers use it: `GET /api/analysis/hop-counts` and the Network Survey hop distribution.
- Sources with no local node (MQTT, MeshCore) now return no entries, so their nodes render **grey**. This was a maintainer decision: show only hops we measured ourselves, and don't fall back to `hopsAway`.
- An empty route still means a direct neighbour (0 hops).

## Testing

- New SQLite cases cover: a third-party trace is ignored, a responder→local row is keyed on the responder, the newest row wins across both shapes, and a source with no local node returns nothing.
- New multi-backend cases cover the changed SQL.
- Existing tests now pass `localNodeNums`.
- Route and survey tests check that local node numbers are passed through.
- Full Vitest suite with the PostgreSQL and MySQL containers up: `success: true`, 20,375 passed, 0 failed. The multi-backend hop-count file ran all 27 cases with 0 skipped.
- `tsc` clean, and `lint:ci` has no in-repo failures.

## Mesh impact

Read-only query change. No packets sent, no notifications, and no timers.

title: perf: make large node sets usable
body:
## Context

Companion to #5283, which makes MQTT-only deployments show their data. This one addresses what happens when they do.

The UI is comfortable with a node set the size of an RF mesh, tens to low hundreds. Fed from MQTT it sees thousands, and three things become apparent: the node list mounts a DOM subtree per row, the map mounts a DOM element per marker, and a flat list of several thousand nodes is hard to read even once it scrolls smoothly.

Measured against a live instance fed from the public broker, growing from roughly 4,400 to 9,000 nodes over the session.

## Measurement caveat

All figures below were captured with headless Chromium, which runs without GPU compositing and uses software rasterization, so absolute frame times are inflated. The before-and-after comparisons within the same environment are meaningful; the absolute numbers are not. Confirmed by hand in a real browser that the improvement is clear, but worth re-measuring on your own machine.

## Changes

**Fetch `/api/poll` once at mount rather than three times.** Traced by instrumenting `window.fetch` and capturing stack traces: a normal query mount, plus `checkConnectionStatus()` doing a bare `authFetch` that bypassed the cache, plus that same function calling `refetchPoll()`. Now routed through `queryClient.fetchQuery` so it dedupes. Three calls become one, 11.58MB becomes 3.91MB, total bytes over 30 seconds 18.20MB to 10.53MB.

**Avoid invalidating the whole poll cache on three WebSocket events.** `traceroute:complete` now merges into the cache, deriving `hopCount` client-side the same way the server does. `routing:update` and `telemetry:batch` cannot be merged from their payloads: `routing:update`'s `status: 'ack'` does not distinguish delivered from confirmed, and the confirmed case carries SNR and RSSI the payload lacks, while `telemetry:batch` carries raw per-metric rows rather than poll's aggregated shape. Rather than reconstruct those and risk wrong data, both get a 2-second trailing debounce.

**Virtualize the node list** using `@tanstack/react-virtual`, already a dependency and already used in the packet monitor. Dynamic measurement, since row heights vary between 63 and 77px.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DOM elements at rest | 232,172 | 1,196 |
| Idle 30s long tasks | 13 / 17,075ms | 1 / 69ms |
| Scroll average frame time | 422ms | 16.8ms |
| Scroll dropped frames | 76.9% | 0.5% |

A side effect: the first-load empty state window fell from about 5.6s to 0.8s, since React no longer mounts 232,000 elements before replacing it.

**Cluster map markers.** With around 2,700 markers, panning ran at 93% dropped frames. Profiling put the cost in the compositor rather than application JS: `Layerize` at 3,052ms against 250ms, `UpdateLayer` at 68,278 calls against 4,420. Icon construction is already cached well and is not the cost; this is the structural cost of one DOM element per marker.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Pan average frame time | 81.78ms |

title: fix(mqtt): let MQTT-only deployments see their own data
body:
## Problem

On an install with an MQTT source and no enabled `meshtastic_tcp` source, the Nodes, Messages and Channels tabs render their "Connect to Meshtastic node" empty states even though ingest is working and the database is filling up. The node count in the tab header is correct; only the list body is empty.

Two smaller issues compound it: the map renders no markers for such a source, and embedded-broker sources cannot reach the per-source view at all.

## Root cause

`resolveSourceManager()` narrows to `meshtastic_tcp` managers. An `mqtt_bridge` source is registered in `sourceManagerRegistry`, but `isMeshtasticManager()` rejects it, so the helper returns `getPrimaryMeshtasticManager() ?? fallbackManager`. With no enabled Meshtastic source that is `fallbackManager`, which has never connected.

`pollRoutes.ts` then calls `getConnectionStatus()` on it. That method is purely `this`-based, so `/api/poll?sourceId=<mqtt source>` reports `connected: false` regardless of the real bridge's state. `checkConnectionStatus()` in `App.tsx` sets `connectionStatus` from that response, and `shouldShowData()` gates the three tabs on it. `MqttBridgeManager.getConnectionStatus()` already returns a correct, Meshtastic-shaped status.

## Reproduction

Clean checkout of `main` at v4.16.1-rc6, fresh SQLite database, one `mqtt_bridge` source against `mqtt.meshtastic.org` on `msh/US/#`, no Meshtastic source enabled.

| | |
|---|---|
| `/api/sources/:id/status` | `connected: true`, `nodeCount: 628` |
| database, scoped to source | 628 nodes, 18 messages |
| `/api/poll?sourceId=<id>` | `connected: false` |
| UI | "Nodes (439)" header, empty body, Disconnected |

## Changes

**Report the MQTT source's own connection status.** When the polled `sourceId` names a registered MQTT-typed manager, look it up directly from `sourceManagerRegistry`; otherwise behaviour is unchanged. This mirrors the existing pattern in `channelRoutes.ts` and deliberately leaves `resolveSourceManager()` alone so its other call sites are unaffected. Adds `isMqttConnectionStatusManager()` following the existing predicate convention and reusing `isMqttSourceType`.

**Restore the Open button for `mqtt_broker` sources.** One condition in `DashboardSidebar.tsx`. The guard originally excluded both broker and bridge because neither had a detail page; `1ea2fbb2` narrowed it to broker only, and #3169 then gave both a page. #3171 identified this same guard and fixed it, but was included in the #3172 revert and not reissued afterwards. #3333 has since added the poll-path manager methods broker sources needed, so the backend side is in place. Verified by creating a broker source, publishing synthetic packets to its own embedded listener, and confirming nodes appear scoped to that source.

**Skip the transport filters on MQTT-only sources.** `mqtt_bridge` and `mqtt_broker` cannot produce an RF-classified node, so the RF / UDP / MQTT filters have no meaning there and can only blank the map. They are skipped and

## Summary

Version bump for the **4.16.1** stable release, plus its changelog section.

- Bumped across all five files: `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `helm/meshmonitor/Chart.yaml`, `desktop/package.json`, `desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`. No stray `-rc6` references remain.
- Added the `[4.16.1]` changelog section so this release does not repeat the gap #5281 just backfilled, and emptied `[Unreleased]` — both of its bullets (#5202, #5184) ship here.

## How the notes were assembled

From `git log v4.16.0..main`, **not** a merge-date search. The date search is what put two 4.15.0 fixes into the 4.15.2 release notes, and I carried that error into #5281 before catching it. 50 substantive commits plus 11 Dependabot updates.

## Security entry

`#5225` and `#5227` are called out under `### Security` rather than left in `Fixed`. Reading both PRs in full, they are a genuine cross-source leak: `GET /api/messages`, `GET /api/messages/channel/:channel` and `GET /api/messages/unread-counts` checked permissions with **no source id at all**, then answered for the caller-supplied `?sourceId=`, so a `messages:read` grant on any one source returned another source's messages — bodies included on the first two. My first draft described this as "message metadata" and blamed a default-source fallback; both were wrong, and the committed text is corrected.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors
- [x] `npm run docs:build` — clean
- [x] `system-test` label applied, per the convention that release version-bump chores always run the hardware suite

+- **Configuration search** — find a setting without knowing which page holds it, both within a page and across all of them. (#5182, #5226)

+- **MQTT hop-limit override split into a raise and a clamp**, so the two intentions no longer share one control. (#5188, #5190, #5256)
+- **Beacons list** — a table-backed list behind a button that carries the current count. (#5232, #5235)

+- **"Mark all read"** beside the Sources unread toggle. (#5197, #5224)
+- **Module settings are gated on the device's `excluded_modules` bitmask**, so a firmware build that cannot run a module no longer offers to configure it. (#5065, #5273)
+- **Mobile channels layout** — Beacons and the send actions move to their own row, letting the composer collapse to one line. (#5265, #5267)
+
 ### Fixed
-- **MeshCore DM/channel retries no longer read as duplicate messages** — `MeshCoreManager`'s ack-timeout DM retry (#3977) and echo-miss channel retry (#3979) resent through meshcore.js's `sendTextMessage()`/`sendChannelTextMessage()` wrappers, which always mint a fresh `senderTimestamp` (and, for DMs, hardcode `attempt = 0`) on every call. A retransmit of an already-sent message therefore looked like a brand-new send to the recipient (and to any mesh dedup keyed on sender+timestamp), so a companion connected through the Virtual Node could see the same message arrive more than once even though it was only sent once. Retries now drive the library's lower-level `sendCommandSendTxtMsg`/`sendCommandSendChannelTxtMsg` directly, reusing the ORIGINAL send's `senderTimestamp` with an incrementing `attempt` — matching what other MeshCore clients and the firmware's own retry cadence expect. (#5202)
-- **Bundled Apprise API server no longer logs `BrokenPipeError` tracebacks** — when a notification request took longer to process than the Node client's fetch timeout (or the client otherwise disconnected early), `apprise-api.py` tried to write a response to an already-closed socket and let the resulting `BrokenPipeError` propagate, printing a noisy "Exception occurred during processing of request" traceback to the container log even though the underlying notification had already been dispatched. Response writes now swallow a broken/reset connection instead of raising. (#5184)
+- **Traceroutes are sent at the node's configured hop limit**, not a fixed 7. (#5262)
+- **MeshCore** — DM and channel retries reuse the original `senderTimestamp` with an incrementing attempt, so a retransmit no longer reads as a duplicate message (#5202, #5203); `lastHeard` only moves forward and every receive path stamps it (#5242); `runExclusiveRadioOp` is bounded so a stuck radio op cannot park the chain forever (#5244); in-flight Auto-Pathfinding runs are cancelled on stop or reconnect (#5171); `/dev/serial/by-id` and `by-path` serial paths are accepted (#5172, #5174); the Repeater serial path is checked too, warn-only (#5178, #5179); the admin console reports a clear error when it receives HTML instead of JSON (#5268, #5270); snr columns widened to REAL/DOUBLE (#5175, #5176).
+- **The embedded MQTT broker stops without hanging on connected clients.** (#5264, #5266)
+- **Shared-key channels no longer swallow history**, and local edits show without a restart. (#5183, #5269)
+- **NodeInfo enrichment** — blank values no longer undo enrichment, map labels are no longer stubbed (#5231, #5234), and the count stops oscillating on repeated Fix All (#5193, #5198).
+- **MeshMonitor no longer connects to a `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` nobody configured.** (#5237, #5239)
+- **Enum settings are validated on both load paths, from one list**, so a bad stored value cannot reach the UI through the path that skipped the check. (#5261)
+- **`clearPacketLogs` quotes the `sourceId` identifier in its delete.** (#5238)
+- **Maps** — centre on the rendered marker and add a Spread Nodes toggle (#5177, #5181); outline the popup badge and pin its actions below the scroll (#5247, #5253).
+- **Line breaks are preserved** in the unified messages card and modal. (#5250, #5251)
+- **The channel reorder handle can be dragged on touch.** (#5233, #5240)
+- **The Add Widget picker on the dashboard scrolls.** (#5191, #5192)
+- **DM list falls back to sorting nodes by `lastHeard` descending.** (#5143)
+- **Mobile** — Security tables, the Packet Distribution toolbar and telemetry marker density on a phone (#5194, #5195, #5196, #5199), plus two global class collisions that overlapped the issue-card text (#5200).
+- **The bundled Apprise API server swallows `BrokenPipeError`** when a client disconnects early, instead of printing a traceback for a notification it already dispatched. (#5184, #5185)
+
+### Security
+- **Cross-source message leak on three endpoints** — `GET /api/messages`, `GET /api/messages/channel/:channel` (#5227) and `GET /api/messages/unread-counts` (#5225) checked permissions with **no source id at all**, then answered for the caller-supplied `?sourceId=`. A `messages:read` grant on any one source returned another source's messages, bodies included. All three now scope the check to the requested source.
+
+### Changed
+- **armv7 JS artifacts build natively rather than under QEMU**, and the armv7 Docker build has enough time to finish. (#5205, #5207)
+- **A Retag workflow** moves an alias tag without a rebuild. (#5206)

## Summary

Ahead of the 4.16.1 release, two public "what shipped" surfaces were behind.

**CHANGELOG.md skipped two releases.** Its last real section was `[4.15.2-rc2] - 2026-08-22`; there was no `[4.16.0]` section at all, even though 4.16.0 shipped 2026-09-10 with 50 commits. 4.15.1 and 4.15.2 final were also missing. Everything since sat under `[Unreleased]`, which held two bullets.

Root cause: `/create-release` writes the GitHub release body but never touches `CHANGELOG.md`, so the file falls behind every release unless someone edits it by hand.

**The blog had no 4.16.0 post.** The blog index bills itself as "News, releases, security advisories, and feature announcements", and its newest release post was `2026-08-21-v4.15.0-release` — so the site carried no record of a feature release from three weeks earlier.

## Changes

- **`[4.16.0] - 2026-09-10`**, **`[4.15.2] - 2026-09-01`** and **`[4.15.1] - 2026-08-21`** added, written from the published release notes in the Keep a Changelog shape the recent entries use (Added / Changed / Fixed / Security). CI and dependency churn are omitted, matching `[4.15.0]`.
- **`[4.15.2-rc2]` folded into `[4.15.2]`** instead of leaving both. Every rc2 bullet shipped inside 4.15.2, so keeping both duplicated them. Nothing is lost — the rc2 entries are preserved verbatim under the final version heading, except the Site Planner `/api/rf/coverage` fix, which moved into the new `[4.15.1]` section where it actually shipped.

title: feat(messages): @ mention autocomplete and chips in conversations (#5276)
body:
Closes #5276 (mention notifications and unread badges excepted — see below).

## The format question, settled first
Meshtastic has **no protocol field** for a mention. The `@` tagging in the official apps is a plain-text convention, and there is a written cross-platform contract for it: [meshtastic/design#21](https://github.com/meshtastic/design/issues/21). The token is `@!` + the node's 8 hex digits, e.g. `@!ffccee11` — a display name never goes on the wire, so a rename cannot orphan an old mention. iOS ([`MentionParser.swift`](https://github.com/meshtastic/Meshtastic-Apple/blob/main/Meshtastic/Helpers/MentionParser.swift)) and Android ([`Mention.kt`](https://github.com/meshtastic/Meshtastic-Android/blob/main/core/model/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/meshtastic/core/model/Mention.kt)) ship it; the web client has it open as [web#1242](https://github.com/meshtastic/web/issues/1242).

MeshMonitor implements that token exactly, so mentions sent from here highlight in the official apps and theirs highlight here. Two app-level divergences, and what this does about them:
- iOS matches **lowercase** hex only, Android matches either → we **emit lowercase**.
- Android appends a trailing space, iOS does not → we **append one** (harmless to both, and what a typist expects).
- We **parse case-insensitively**, since Android-composed text can carry uppercase.

## What this adds
- **Autocomplete** in three composers — Meshtastic channels, Meshtastic DMs, MeshCore conversations. Filters on long name, short name or node id, ordered most-recently-heard first, capped at 5 like Android. Arrow keys, Enter, Tab, Escape, mouse. The local node is left out of its own list.
- **The list claims Enter before the send handler**, so picking a node cannot fire a half-written message. `me@host` never triggers it, and a resolved `@!…` token does not re-trigger.
- **Chips in received messages**, resolved to the node's *current* name at render time, so a rename shows through in old messages. Clicking one opens that node; a mention of the local node is styled apart; an unknown node stays readable as its raw token.
- **MeshCore keeps its own `@[Name]` form** (#3851, borrowed from Kiekr.App), which `actionExecutor` and the automation catalog already depend on. The two formats share the popup via `buildInsertion`, never the parser — one parser would be wrong for both.

## Screenshots
Autocomplete, and a sent mention rendered as a chip:

![mention autocomplete](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/mentions-5276/docs/public/images/features/5276-mention-autocomplete.png)

![mention chip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/mentions-5276/docs/public/images/features/5276-mention-chip.png)

## Mesh impact
No new packets, no timers, no notifications. A mention is text inside a message the operator was already sending. Worth knowing: `@!ffccee11 ` is 11 bytes against a ~200-byte payload, so several mentions cost more airtime than the visible text sugg

Refs #5255. Builds the manual half; auto-apply is deliberately not here.

## What this does
**Settings → Scripts** gains a **Check for updates** button. It asks each script's source repository which version it publishes, shows the result per script, and offers a one-click **Update** with a **Roll back**.

Scope follows the decisions on the issue:
- **Scripts only.** Community Add-ons (Docker sidecars) are untouched.
- **Any GitHub repo**, not just the gallery.
- **Check only; an admin installs.** Nothing runs on a timer, so third-party code never changes under an operator without a click.
- **One backup, with rollback.**

### Where a source comes from
1. `source:` (or `repository:`) in the script's own `mm_meta`, so an author controls it,
2. a GitHub path an admin types into the card, stored in the `scriptUpdateSources` setting,
3. the bundled gallery listing, matched on filename.

A script with none of these says so and offers the input; it is never guessed at.

### Safety
- Every fetch goes through the existing SSRF guard, to a URL **rebuilt** from a parsed `owner/repo/path`. A source string cannot redirect the request off GitHub or at an internal address; anything that is not a plain GitHub file path is refused at parse time.
- Downloads are capped at 512KB and rejected if they are a web page or contain a NUL byte.
- The new file is written to a temp name and renamed into place, so an interrupted write cannot leave a half-written script for the auto-responder to execute. The file mode is preserved.
- Reading update status needs `settings:read`; updating, rolling back and setting a source need `settings:write`.

### Also in here
- Example scripts now declare `version` and `source`, so the gallery and the update check have real data.
- `npm run scripts:gallery` regenerates the server's copy of the gallery listing, and a test fails if the two drift.

## Screenshot
An installed script at v0.1.0 whose source publishes v1.0.0:

![script update available](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/script-updates-5255/docs/public/images/features/5255-script-updates.png)

## Mesh impact
None: no packets, notifications or timers. Outbound HTTP happens only when an admin presses a button.

## Verification
Driven against real GitHub in the dev container:
- **Check:** an installed `hello.js` at v0.1.0 pointed at a commit in this branch reported `latestVersion: 1.0.0, updateAvailable: true`; a gallery-listed script resolved its source by filename with no `source:` line of its own.
- **Update:** the card showed v1.0.0 and offered **Roll back**; the file on disk was replaced.
- **Roll back:** the card returned to v0.1.0 and the update offer came back.
- Full suite: 19,351 passed, 0 failed. Lint ratchet OK.

New tests: source parsing and version comparison (12), the update service including SSRF-blocked, oversized, HTML and binary responses, backup/rollback and mode preservation (17), and the routes' permission split and filename handling (7).

title: feat(config): gate module sections on the device's excluded_modules bitmask (#5065)
body:
Closes #5065.

## Summary
A firmware build can leave modules out (`MESHTASTIC_EXCLUDE_MODULES`, reduced and vendor images), and the device says which ones in `DeviceMetadata.excluded_modules`. MeshMonitor read that field nowhere, so on a reduced build it offered config for modules the device does not have, and it gated Range Test on a firmware version string instead.

- **Backend:** `src/utils/excludedModules.ts` maps the 15 `ExcludedModules` bits to module keys. `processDeviceMetadata` stores the mask on the local node; `getCurrentConfig()` reports per-module availability through the existing `supportedModules` payload.
- **Frontend:** `ModuleAvailabilityGate` wraps a section, shows a notice, and switches its controls off. The section stays visible, since a vanished section reads as a MeshMonitor bug (the #5041 pattern). Applied to 14 sections: MQTT, Serial, External Notification, Store & Forward, Range Test, Telemetry, Canned Messages, Audio, Remote Hardware, Neighbor Info, Ambient Lighting, Detection Sensor, Paxcounter, Network.
- **Range Test** keeps its own wording for the 2.8 removal (#5031). The build gate (`rangetest`) and the firmware gate (`rangeTest`) are separate keys, so a 2.7 build that excluded the module says so rather than blaming 2.8.

**Fails open everywhere.** An absent or unparseable field leaves every section enabled, so older firmware behaves exactly as it does today. Bluetooth has a bit but no config section of its own, so nothing consumes that key yet.

## Screenshot
A device reporting Paxcounter excluded (forced locally for the shot; the stub is not committed):

![excluded module notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/excluded-modules-5065/docs/public/images/features/5065-excluded-module.png)

## Mesh impact
None: no packets, notifications or timers. The bitmask arrives in DeviceMetadata we already receive.

## Verification
- Deployed the branch to the dev container with the mask forced to Paxcounter, and confirmed `/api/config/current` reported `paxcounter: false` and the section rendered the notice and greyed out.
- Full suite: 19,311 passed, 0 failed. Lint ratchet OK.
- New tests: bitmask helper (fail-open, per-bit, all 15 keys), manager payload including the split Range Test gates and the DeviceMetadata round trip, and the gate component.

title: fix(meshcore): surface a clear error when admin console gets HTML instead of JSON
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #5268 — MeshCore remote admin console occasionally surfaces the raw browser error `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON` instead of a useful message.
- `useMeshCore.ts` (the hook backing the MeshCore admin/local CLI console) called `response.json()` unconditionally at 57 call sites, with no check of `response.ok` or `content-type` first. If anything upstream returns an HTML body instead of JSON — a proxy/edge error page, a session redirect, a rate-limit response, or (on `BASE_URL` deployments) a request that misses the `/api` prefix and falls through to the SPA shell — the raw `JSON.parse` `SyntaxError` bubbled straight into the UI. This is the same class of bug already fixed once for the main app in `ApiService.request()` (#5078); the MeshCore hook uses its own fetch wrapper and never got that guard.
- Adds a shared `parseJsonResponse()` helper (`src/utils/parseJsonResponse.ts`) mirroring the #5078 guard: it checks for a `text/html` content-type and throws a message naming the HTTP status and content-type, instead of letting the opaque parse error through. All 57 `response.json()` call sites in `useMeshCore.ts` now go through it.
- This does not change *what* produces the HTML in the reporter's environment — that still needs more diagnostic info from them (status code, `cf-ray` header, `BASE_URL` config) — but it turns any future occurrence into an actionable error instead of a dead end.

## Mesh impact
Purely HTTP response-parsing on the client. No new packets, no change to send/retry logic, no new timers.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — passes
- [x] `npm run lint:ci` — passes (one new `no-explicit-any` site added with a targeted `eslint-disable-next-line`, matching `response.json()`'s own untyped `Promise<any>` return type)
- [x] Added `src/utils/parseJsonResponse.test.ts` covering: normal JSON, missing content-type, JSON served as `text/plain`, and an HTML body (with and without a context label)
- [x] Full `npx vitest run`: 19,035 passed, 0 real failures. (18 failures on the first run were the documented uninitialized-submodule environmental issue — `protobufs/` was empty in this fresh checkout; re-ran after `git submodule update --init --recursive` and both previously-failing suites pass cleanly.)

title: fix(channels): stop shared-key channels swallowing history; show local edits without a restart (#5183)
body:
Fixes the two problems reported in discussion #5183.

## 1. A channel's history moved permanently into Channel 0

`channelRoutes.ts` kept its own channel-move detector that matched on **PSK alone**. The shared detector in `utils/channelMoveDetection.ts` was fixed in #3452 to require PSK **and** name, unique on both sides, but the route copy never picked that up.

With Channel 0 and a secondary both on the default `AQ==` key (common), each matched the other. The reverse match was then dropped as a "duplicate", so it applied as a **one-way move**: any channel edit or add through the Channels routes rewrote the secondary's whole history into Channel 0. It is permanent, because a moved row keeps no record of its original channel.

**Fix:** the routes use the shared detector, and snapshots now carry names.

Two scoping defects on the same migration path:
- **Config-sync migration was unscoped.** `MeshtasticManager.detectAndMigrateChannelChanges` migrated messages and permissions without a `sourceId`, so a move detected on one source rewrote every other source's rows in the same slots. The reporter runs two nodes.
- **Permission migration made scoped grants global.** `migratePermissionsForChannelMoves` read `channel_N` grants across all sources and re-inserted them **without their `sourceId`**, turning a grant on one source into a grant on every source. It now takes an optional `sourceId`, scopes to it, and keeps each row's own `sourceId`. The reorder route and the config-sync path both pass their source.

## 2. Channel edits didn't show until a restart

The device doesn't push channel changes to a connected client. For the local node, Admin Commands reads a channel back from the **database** (`/get-channel`), and nothing wrote the edit there, so it only appeared after the next full config sync.

- A successful **local** `setChannel` now mirrors the channel into that source's database row. This is the same write the Channels tab's `PUT` already makes, and the next sync still overwrites it with the device's values. A failed mirror is logged but doesn't fail the command, since the device already has the change.
- `/load-config` for a local channel serves the stored row. It used to send `get_config_request(0)`, which is `DEVICE_CONFIG`, not a channel, and returned a blank placeholder.
- PSK shorthand (`none` / `default` / `simpleN`) is translated once, in `utils/channelPsk.ts`, shared by the `setChannel` builder and the mirror. The stored key therefore matches what the device reports, and move detection still recognises the channel.

**Scope note:** the Device Configuration page's channel editor already writes the database through the Channels `PUT`, so this change doesn't explain the report of that page not updating. If it still lags, we need more detail from the reporter.

## Recovery

Messages already moved into Channel 0 can't be separated back out automatically: a stored message row has no PSK or channel name to tell them apart. This fix prevents it

title: feat(channels): give mobile its own action row, collapse the composer to one line (#5265)
body:
Closes #5265 — reported by NullVoid on Discord.

## What was actually crowding the header

The mobile header is a **deliberate** single nowrap row (#3385): heading + selector + a `⋯` kebab, with the inline per-channel actions folded into that kebab so it never spills past one line.

The Beacons button (#5232) landed in that row afterwards and was never folded in with the others — `BeaconsPanel` renders its own button inside `.channels-controls`, so the hiding rule (`.channel-actions`, `.mqtt-toggle`) never covered it. It took width from the channel selector until the channel name truncated. That's a regression against an existing design, not a general layout shortfall.

## The change

On mobile, Beacons and the two send-actions (alert bell, position) move to their own short row under the header. The composer loses the buttons it was wrapping onto a second row and collapses from two rows to one — **which is what pays for the row this adds. Net vertical change: zero.** Desktop renders nothing new; the row isn't rendered above the breakpoint.

**One correction to the issue's reasoning.** It says the composer "splits its width between the input and three trailing icon buttons, leaving the field narrower than it needs to be." It didn't — `.input-with-counter` already took `flex: 1 1 100%` on mobile, so the input was full-width on its own row with the buttons wrapped beneath. The win is the row saved, not width reclaimed.

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**Rendered in exactly one place per width, not duplicated and CSS-hidden.** Two copies would look identical while handing the accessibility tree two elements sharing an `aria-label`. There's a test that fails if they're ever both rendered.

title: fix(mqtt): stop the broker without hanging on connected clients (#5264)
body:
Fixes #5264.

## Root cause

It isn't the `server.on('error')` handler the issue points at. That one is attached to a fresh `net.Server` on every `start()`, so it can't accumulate.

`MqttBroker.stop()` awaited `server.close(cb)` **before** closing Aedes:

```ts
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => { this.server!.close(() => resolve()); });  // hangs
...
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => { this.aedes!.close(() => resolve()); });   // never reached
```

`net.Server.close` stops accepting new connections immediately, but only invokes its callback once **every existing connection has ended**. An MQTT client (the radio, the bridge, the TCP-linked device) keeps its socket open indefinitely, so `stop()` never resolved. That one fact explains every symptom in the report:

| Symptom | Why |
|---|---|
| Save hangs ~6 min, then "Network error" | `PUT /api/sources/:id` awaits `removeManager` → `manager.stop()` → `broker.stop()`, which never returns. |
| `:1883` refuses connections while logs say "listening" | `server.close` already unbound the listener; the "listening" log is from the original start. |
| `MaxListenersExceededWarning: 11 close listeners added to [Server]` | The stuck manager is never replaced, so each retry calls `server.close(cb)` again **on the same Server**, adding one `close` listener per save. |
| Only after the broker has clients | With nobody connected, `server.close` calls back immediately. |
| Container restart clears it | A new process means a new Server with no connections. |

## Fix

`stop()` now:
1. unbinds the listener and closes Aedes, which disconnects every client it knows;
2. destroys any socket Aedes never adopted (tracked per connection; e.g. one still mid-CONNECT);
3. waits for the server to close.

It is also **single-flight**: concurrent or repeated calls share one teardown and one `close` listener. It clears its handles up front so a restart right after a stop is never refused with "already started". Each step is bounded at 5 s, so a misbehaving client degrades to a logged warning rather than a request that never returns.

## Mesh impact

None. This is the local broker's socket lifecycle only: no packets, timers, or notifications. The connected radio and bridge are disconnected on save, which is what a restart was always meant to do. MQTT clients reconnect on their own (the TCP-linked device re-attaches via the registry's `manager-stopped` / `manager-started` events, which now actually fire).

## Tests

- `transports/mqttBroker.test.ts`: real broker plus a real `mqtt` client on an ephemeral port. `stop()` resolves while a client is connected, disconnects that client, frees the port for a restart, survives 15 concurrent calls with no `MaxListenersExceededWarning`, and can be started again afterwards. **4 of 5 fail on `main`.** The port test passes there too, which matches the report: the port is unbound even though stop hangs.
- `mqttBrokerManager.restart.test.ts`: the reported scenario end to end. It runs twelve sav

title: fix(traceroute): send at the node's configured hop limit, not a fixed 7
body:
Follow-up raised in review on #5259.

## What

`createTracerouteMessage` built every traceroute with a hardcoded `hopLimit: 7`. The firmware sends a client-built packet at the hop_limit it carries: it neither substitutes nor caps it at `lora.hop_limit`. So every traceroute, including each Auto Traceroute run, flooded further than any other traffic the node originates.

`sendTraceroute` now passes `getConfiguredHopLimit()`. That is the same source admin packets already use, and how the Meshtastic CLI sizes traceroutes (from `localConfig.lora.hop_limit`). Before the LoRa config arrives it falls back to the firmware default of 3, and the value is clamped to the 3-bit protocol max.

## Mesh impact

- **Airtime:** negative only. A node at the default hop limit of 3 now traces 3 hops instead of 7. That matters most for Auto Traceroute, which runs on a timer across the node list.
- **Reach trade-off:** a target further out than the node's own hop limit can no longer be traced. That is the same reach the node's text messages already have. Operators who need deeper traces raise the device hop limit, which is now noted in the Auto Traceroute docs.
- No new sends, timers, or notification paths.

## Tests

- `meshtasticProtobufService.tracerouteHopLimit.test.ts` **decodes the real ToRadio bytes**: the given hop limit goes on the wire, the no-argument default is 3 rather than 7, and it is clamped to 7 max.
- `meshtasticManager.tracerouteHopLimit.test.ts`: `sendTraceroute` passes the configured hop limit, and the default before config arrives.

Full suite: **19,241 passed, 0 failed** (1,032 pending are the PostgreSQL/MySQL container suites; no schema change). Lint ratchet OK.

## Not changed here

Other hardcoded hop limits remain in `meshtasticProtobufService.ts`: position and nodeinfo exchange (3), and one remote-node request (7). They weren't part of this ask.

title: fix(settings): validate enum settings on both load paths, from one list
body:
Follow-up to the review of #5018, which flagged that the new setting's server-load handler cast an arbitrary string straight to its union type. **Nine others did the same**, and the cause is duplication rather than carelessness.

## Why it happened

Every enum-shaped setting has **two** entry points — a `localStorage` seed at mount, and the server settings response shortly after — and each carried its own hand-written copy of the valid values. So they drifted. Most seeds allowlisted; most server handlers did:

```ts
setTemperatureUnitState(settings.temperatureUnit as TemperatureUnit);
```

which is a promise to the compiler, not a check. A stored `"foo"` reached component state as a value matching neither branch of whatever consumed it — the UI silently rendered its else-case with nothing to explain why.

## What was unchecked

| Setting | localStorage seed | Server load |
|---|---|---|
| `temperatureUnit` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `distanceUnit` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `positionHistoryLineStyle` | ✅ | ❌ |
| **`preferredSortField`** | ❌ | ❌ |
| `preferredSortDirection` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `timeFormat` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `dateFormat` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `mapPinStyle` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `nodeListStyle` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `iconStyle` | ✅ | ❌ |

`preferredSortField` is the worst case — unchecked on **both** paths, nine possible values, nothing anywhere confirming the stored string was one of them.

## The fix

Adding ten bespoke comparisons would have left the duplication that caused this. Instead the valid values live once in `settingsEnums.ts`, and both paths resolve through one helper:

```ts
const v = pickSetting(settings.temperatureUnit, TEMPERATURE_UNITS);
if (v) { setTemperatureUnitState(v); localStorage.setItem('temperatureUnit', v); }
```

Divergence becomes impossible rather than fixed once. `nodeHopsCalculation` and `preferredDashboardSortOption` were already validated and move onto the shared lists too, so **no inline copy of a valid-value list is left anywhere** in the context.

`pickSetting` takes `unknown` on purpose: both callers hand it something typed `string` that's really "whatever was in the database", and a `string` signature would invite back the cast this removes.

## Compile-time exhaustiveness

`satisfies readonly T[]` rejects a value that isn't in the union — but says nothing about a union member **missing from a list**. That's the dangerous direction: add a value to a union, forget the list, and `pickSetting` silently rejects a perfectly valid setting, reverting the user's choice with no error anywhere.

The `_exhaustive` block fails the build and names the culprit. Verified by deleting `'YYYY-MM-DD'` from `DATE_FORMATS`:

```
error TS2322: Type 'boolean' is not assignable to type '["missing from list:", "YYYY-MM-DD"]'.
```

## Tests

`pickSetting` accepts every listed value, rejects unlisted ones, rejects the non-strings a JSON payload can actually contain (`null`, number, boolean, object, array — each of which sailed through the old cast), rejects near-misses (`'c'`, `' C'`, `'C '`)

title: feat(solar): let operators mark a node as solar, or not (#3195)
body:
Closes #3195.

## What

Solar detection needs a visible daily charge/discharge cycle. A node whose panel and battery far outsize its load (the reporter's 8×18650 bank) sits near full all day, never shows one, and is never detected. Operators can now say what they already know.

- **Mark as solar**: a node appears in the Solar Monitoring report with a *Marked solar* tag even when detection found nothing (score 0, chart still drawn).
- **Not a solar node**: a detected node drops out of the report and the forecast.
- **Use auto-detection**: clears either, handing the node back to the detector.

## Design

**Global per physical node, no `sourceId`** (chosen with @Yeraze). A solar panel is a property of the hardware, and the report already pools telemetry across sources, so a per-source flag would let one node be "solar" on one source and "not solar" on another. This follows the `estimated_positions` global-by-design carve-out.

- **Migration 167**: `solar_node_overrides (nodeNum PK, isSolar, updatedBy, updatedAt)`. `nodeNum` is BIGINT on PostgreSQL and MySQL, because a signed INTEGER overflows for roughly half of real node numbers. No backfill: no row means auto-detect, today's behaviour. Idempotent on all three backends.
- Registered in `BACKUP_TABLES` and the CLI migration table list, so it survives backup/restore and SQLite→PG/MySQL migration.
- `identifySolarNodes(rows, nodes, days, overrides?)`:
  - a node marked not solar is skipped before any analysis;
  - a node marked solar with no pattern gets a manual entry charting whichever metric it reports;
  - one below the ratio threshold keeps its real stats;
  - one with no telemetry in the window is still listed with an empty chart, so the flag visibly took effect.
- The forecast applies the same overrides. Manual entries have null rates, so they are skipped from simulation, matching existing behaviour for nodes without rate data.

## API

`PUT /api/analysis/solar-overrides/:nodeNum` with body `{ isSolar: true | false | null }`. `null` clears. It uses the `ok`/`fail` envelope and requires `settings:write`, the same global grant as other deployment-wide config.

`GET /api/analysis/solar-nodes` gains:
- `manual_overrides`, **filtered to nodes on the requester's permitted sources**. The table is global and keyed by nodeNum, so without this filter a user scoped to one source could learn node numbers from a source they can't read (a marked node is listed even with no telemetry). Covered by a route test.
- `analyzed_nodes` for the picker: only nodes with battery or voltage telemetry in the window, the only ones a flag can chart.

## Mesh impact

None: read-side analysis only. It sends no packets, adds no timers, and fires no notifications.

## Verified in the running app

Deployed to the dev container and driven through the real report on a live 386-node dataset: marking a node raised *Solar nodes detected* from 36 to 37 and tagged its card; clearing it returned the count to 36. The override was removed

title: feat(automation): per-automation hop-limit override for automated sends (#5121)
body:
Closes #5121.

## What

Automated text can now pin its hop count, most often **0** so a status message or reply stays in the local RF neighbourhood. Default is **Inherit** everywhere, so no existing send changes.

| Send path | Where the setting lives |
|---|---|
| Automation Engine **Send a message** | per action, advanced field `hopLimit` |
| Automation Engine **Send a tapback** | per action, advanced field `hopLimit` |
| **Auto-Announce** | per-source setting `autoAnnounceHopLimit` |
| **Auto-Acknowledge** (reply + tapback) | per-source setting `autoAckHopLimit` |

## Two firmware facts shape the design

**1. Lower only.** The firmware does not cap a client-supplied `hop_limit` at the node's own `lora.hop_limit`, so an unchecked override would extend reach. `sendTextMessage` clamps it to `getConfiguredHopLimit()`: choosing 5 on a node set to 3 sends at 3. Chosen with @Yeraze.

**2. Zero needs `want_ack` off.** `Router.cpp:463`:
```cpp
if (src == RX_SRC_USER && p->want_ack && p->hop_limit == 0) {
    p->hop_limit = Default::getConfiguredOrDefaultHopLimit(config.lora.hop_limit);
}
```
`createTextMessage` always set `want_ack`, so a naive `hop_limit: 0` would silently go out at full reach, which defeats the whole issue. A zero-hop send now drops `want_ack`, which means it is **sent exactly once**:
- the stored `messages` row is `wantAck: false`, `deliveryState: 'delivered'`, instead of sitting at `pending` forever;
- `MessageQueueService` forces a single attempt and reports success on handoff, rather than parking it for an ACK that never comes and failing it in the orphan sweep;
- an automation DM at 0 skips the queue even with **DM resend attempts** set, so `maxAttempts` cannot turn into blind resends.

For channel sends (announcements, channel replies) that costs nothing: broadcasts are never ACKed. For DMs it means no delivery confirmation, which @Yeraze chose over "no zero-hop DMs". The UI says so next to the field.

## Mesh impact

- **Airtime:** negative only. The override is capped at the node's own hop limit, so it can shorten reach but never extend it. It adds no packets.
- **Spam / feedback loops:** no new sends, no new notification paths, no change to what triggers an automation.
- **Timers:** none added or touched; nothing here can be reset by a settings save.

## Other details

- The legacy Auto-Ack → automation converter carries `autoAckHopLimit` onto the generated tapback and reply (listed as *converted*, not approximated: the engine honours it identically).
- Both keys are in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS` **and** `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS`; the parity and report pin tests move from 33 to 34 `autoAck*` keys.
- `meshActionDeps` only widens the `sendTextMessage` call when an override is set, so every existing automation reaches the manager with the identical argument list.
- MeshCore has no hop-limit field; the setting is ignored there (MeshCore scope already limits flood reach).

## Tests

- `hopLimitOverride.test.ts`: parse/clamp/setting r

title: feat(map): choose what the official pin's colour means (#5018)
body:
Closes #5018 — reported by Hunter in Discord after #4880 landed.

## The coupling

Pin **shape** and pin **colour** were the same choice:

- `pinStyle: 'official'` → circle, always filled with `meshtasticNodeColor(nodeNum)` (#4880)
- `pinStyle: 'meshmonitor'` → teardrop, always filled with `getHopColor(hops)`

So preferring the official look cost you hop distance at a glance. New `mapPinColorMode: 'node' | 'hops'` separates the two, defaulting to `'node'` so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't go looking.

**`'hops'` reuses `getHopColor()` itself**, not a lookalike palette. The two styles then agree on what a given hop distance looks like and differ only in shape — inventing a parallel scale would teach two colour languages for one fact.

`fixedColor` still wins over both: that's how the Dashboard's yellow overlay and the MeshCore/Reticulum maps pin a whole layer to one colour, which is a different question from what a node's own colour means.

The control only appears when the official style is selected. The teardrop is hop-coloured by construction, so offering the choice there would imply one that doesn't exist.

## The part most likely to go wrong

**Three** components draw node markers — `DashboardMap`, `NodeMarkersLayer`, `NodesTab` — and each caches icons by an `iconSig` string. Both halves fail quietly:

- A map that never reads the setting ignores the toggle. A previous map toggle (#5177) shipped to **one of three** with a fully green suite.
- A map that reads it but omits it from the cache key recolours only nodes that re-render for some other reason — which reads as *flaky*, not *broken*.

All three are wired, and `mapPinColorMode.wiring.test.ts` asserts each one reads the setting, passes `colorMode`, **and** interpolates it into its cache key (plus that `mapPinStyle` is still in there, so this didn't displace it).

## Verified on the dev rig

Same 223 markers, flipped through the real settings UI and save:

| mode | distinct fills | within the hop ramp |
|---|---|---|
| `hops` | 8 | **223 / 223** |
| `node` | 198 | 30 (coincidental collisions + no-data grey) |

**Hop Count** — official circles, hop colours:

_See screenshot below._

## Tests

Six on `createNodeIcon`: the default still produces #4880's identity colour; `'hops'` uses the ramp; both styles agree for each hop count; the short name still renders (it's the official pin, not a teardrop); `fixedColor` beats both; and the teardrop is untouched regardless of mode. Plus the four-part wiring guard above.

Two existing `SettingsTab` suites needed the new required prop — without the callback, save threw and left the SaveBar dirty, which is how the omission surfaced rather than passing silently.

Full suite **19,088 passed, 0 failed**. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint:ci` clean.

title: fix(firmware): make the custom URL an actual install target (#5011)
body:
Fixes #5011.

## The issue understates the problem

It's framed as missing validation and blob→raw resolution. Those are symptoms. **The Custom URL feature was never wired up.**

`firmwareCustomUrl` was written by `setCustomUrl()` and read back in exactly one place — `GET /status`, to refill the text box after a reload. **Nothing in the install path ever consumed it.**

Meanwhile `filterByChannel` treated `'custom'` identically to `'alpha'` — *"'alpha', 'custom' and 'nightly' return all"* — so selecting **Custom URL** listed every GitHub release, and installing one fetched that release's zip from GitHub.

The URL was never requested by anything, which is exactly why @tapedeck's follow-up found a **raw** URL failed the same way. All three reported symptoms follow from that one fact: there was no code path to fail, nothing to validate, and nothing to resolve.

## Wiring it up

A custom URL is the same artifact shape as the local upload #5249 just added — one binary, no release metadata, no version to verify against — only fetched rather than read off disk. So this reuses that scaffolding rather than inventing a parallel one.

- `filterByChannel('custom')` now returns **nothing**. It is not a release feed.
- `startPreflight({ customUrl })` sets `customMode`. The board, OTA-capability and ≥ 2.7.18 gates all still apply.
- `executeDownload` fetches the URL and writes a loose `.bin` into `extracted/` under a **fixed** name — extract has nothing to unzip, and nothing derived from the URL reaches a path. The existing `assertSafeUrl` SSRF guard covers it, and matters more here than anywhere else in the file: **this is the only download target a user types.**
- Extract bypasses `findFirmwareBinary`, and `verifyUpdate` reports the running version rather than comparing it to a URL. Both now key off a shared `isUnversionedLooseBin` predicate instead of `localMode` alone.

**Nightly is deliberately excluded** from that predicate. It's also a loose `.bin`, but it has a real version and a conforming `firmware-<board>-<x.y.z>.<sha>.bin` name, so it keeps both the matcher and the version check.

## Then what the issue asked for

| Ask | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| blob→raw resolution | `github.com/<o>/<r>/blob/<ref>/<path>` → `raw.githubusercontent.com/...`, at save time **and** again before preflight, so a URL stored by an older build can't reach `fetch` in page form. The UI says it converted rather than silently storing something different from what you typed. |
| Content-type validation | A response that is clearly a document (`text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`) is refused with an error naming the **Raw** link. |
| Error feedback | The save route validates URL shape and scheme, returning 400 with a reason instead of storing anything. |

Only *obvious documents* are rejected — servers are too inconsistent about binary types to allowlist (raw.githubusercontent sends `application/octet-stream`, some object stores send `binary/octet-stream`, plenty send nothing). A m

title: feat(mqtt): split the hop-limit override into a raise and a clamp (#5188, #5190)
body:
Closes #5188. Closes #5190.

## What

Splits the `mqtt_broker` source's `downlinkHopLimitOverride` (#4081) — a blunt "set `hop_limit` to N" that both raised and lowered every packet on every portnum — into two independent, opt-in knobs.

| | Rule | Range | Scope | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Clamp** (#5190) | `min(arrived, max)` | 0–7 | all portnums, per-portnum exemptions | off |
| **Raise** (#5188) | `max(arrived, target)` | 1–3 | Position / Telemetry / NodeInfo / NeighborInfo, chosen individually | off |

Raise runs first, clamp second, so the clamp is always the final airtime authority: `min(max(arrived, raise), clamp)`. The editor warns when a raise target sits above the clamp maximum.

Both are **off by default** — no existing install changes behavior on upgrade.

## Mesh impact

Per the CLAUDE.md checklist. The limits below were brought to @Yeraze and chosen by them, not picked during implementation.

- **Clamp only reduces airtime.** It can never increase a hop budget. Its worst case is a quieter mesh.
- **Raise costs airtime, permanently.** Going from `hop_limit` 1 to 3 on a broadcast turns roughly one retransmission into a flood across the receiving cluster — on a dense cluster, several times the airtime per forwarded packet, for every packet of those four types from that source, for as long as it stays on. That is why the target caps at 3, the portnums are opt-in one at a time, the section carries a "bypasses firmware hop scaling" banner, and enabling it requires a second confirming click.
- **No new timers, no new scheduled sends, no new notification paths.** This only rewrites one field on packets already being forwarded, so there is no timer for a settings save to reset.
- **Neither knob sends anything.** Packet count is unchanged; only each packet's reach.

## Two egress paths now agree

The transform previously ran only in Aedes `authorizeForward`. A radio reached through `mqttLink` — broker `local-packet` → `ToRadio.mqttClientProxyMessage` — got the raw payload, so `downlinkHopLimitOverride` **silently did nothing** on that topology. `handleLinkedBrokerLocalPacket` now applies the linked broker's policy.

The `local-packet` payload stays untransformed on purpose: ingestion, the packet log, and the uplink bridge must see the wire bytes as they arrived, so the consumer applies the transform rather than the emitter.

A standalone `mqtt_bridge` used as a link target has no policy of its own and still forwards unchanged — the call is duck-typed and documented.

## Back-compat

No data migration, matching #4081's seam.

- `resolveHopLimitPolicy()` maps a stored `downlinkHopLimitOverride: N` onto `min(max(arrived, N), N) === N` — byte-identical to the old behavior — and `zeroHopInjection` onto a clamp at 0. Existing suites pass untouched.
- Opening a legacy source in the editor loads it as a **clamp** at N with the raise **off**, and says so in a notice. Switching on a firmware-hop-scaling bypass for an operator who never asked
