title: feat(firmware): flash a .bin uploaded from disk, not just a URL (#5249)
body:
Closes #5249 — adds a **Local File (Upload)** release channel so a firmware `.bin` can be sent straight from the browser, instead of having to be published at an HTTP(S) URL first.

## Approach

Reuses the existing OTA wizard rather than forking it. A staged upload behaves exactly like the **nightly** channel already does — a loose `.bin` with no zip — so the download step copies the file into place and the extract step hands it straight back. Backup, flash, reboot and verify are untouched.

**Server**
- `POST /api/firmware/upload` stages the bytes; `DELETE` discards them. Raw body plus an `X-Firmware-Filename` header, matching the geojson / map-style / script upload routes — **no multipart dependency added**. Admin-gated like every other firmware route.
- 32 MB cap. (An ESP32 app image is a few MB; the existing 256 MB *download* cap is sized for release zips that bundle a whole platform's TFT/audio assets, which an upload never does.)
- Filename reduced to a basename with unsafe characters stripped, so a crafted name can't escape the staging directory or inject a path into the message shown in the UI.
- Single staging slot, replaced on re-upload. Cleared after a successful flash; **deliberately kept after a cancel**, since cancelling usually precedes a retry and re-picking a 4 MB file to do that would be gratuitous.
- Board name, OTA capability and the ≥ 2.7.18 running-firmware gate all still apply. An upload is not a way around them.

**Frontend** — file picker, staged-file name and size, Discard, and an acknowledgement checkbox gating Install. The warning names the actual board (via the existing `getHardwareModelName` map) rather than a bare model number. 11 locale keys added.

## A bug this would otherwise have introduced

`verifyUpdate` compares the node's post-flash version against `targetVersion` — which for an upload carries the **filename**, because an upload has no version. That comparison would have failed on *every successful flash* and reported it as an error.

Local mode now reports the version the node came back with and says plainly that nothing was checked against it.

## Validation: warn, don't block (deliberate)

MeshMonitor does **not** check that the binary belongs to this board.

Every OTA-capable board is ESP32, so the ESP-IDF app header could be parsed — but the local PlatformIO build this feature exists for is named `firmware.bin` with no board in the name, so filename matching is useless, and header matching was judged more than this needs for now. The UI names the expected board and requires an explicit acknowledgement instead.

Parsing `esp_app_desc_t` at offset `0x20` (magic `0xABCD5432`, `project_name[32]`, `version[32]`) stays an easy follow-up if we later want the warning to state what the file actually *is*.

Relatedly, `findFirmwareBinary` is **bypassed** for an upload. It exists to pick one board's binary out of a multi-board release zip; a single uploaded file has no such ambiguity, and running it would reject

title: fix(unified): preserve line breaks in the messages card and modal (#5250)
body:
Closes #5250.

## The bug

A message containing newlines renders them in the per-source Channel and DM views but collapses them to spaces in Unified Messages — card and details modal alike. The same message looked different depending on which view you opened it from.

The per-source views set `white-space: pre-line` inline (`ChannelsTab.tsx`, `MessagesTab.tsx`). The unified card and modal style their text through `unified.css`, which declared only `line-height` and `word-break` — so `white-space` fell back to `normal`.

The report's diagnosis was exact; this is the fix it proposed.

## The fix

`white-space: pre-line` on `.unified-msg-card__text` and `.unified-modal__text`. `pre-line` rather than `pre-wrap` to match the per-source views: collapse runs of spaces, keep the line breaks.

`.unified-reply-preview__text` keeps its `nowrap` — a single-line ellipsised quote, where a blanket "preserve newlines everywhere" change would be wrong. That's now pinned by a test so the next reader doesn't have to guess which of the three is deliberate.

## One thing I checked rather than assumed

The card renders through `renderMessageWithLinks`, which could plausibly have stripped `\n` before CSS ever mattered — making the fix work for the modal and silently not for the card. It doesn't: it slices with `substring` and never touches whitespace, and `MessagesTab` already pairs it with `pre-line`. So CSS alone is sufficient for both sites.

## Testing

jsdom applies neither external stylesheets nor layout, so a render test cannot catch this — the element has no computed `white-space` either way. `src/styles/unifiedMessageLineBreaks.test.ts` reads the stylesheet source instead and resolves each property the way the cascade does (last declaration at equal specificity wins), so a later block cannot quietly override the fix.

**Verified to fail without the change** — exactly the two rules, with the `nowrap` guard still passing:

```
WITHOUT the fix: success False passed 1 failed 2
  correctly failed: .unified-msg-card__text keeps newlines (the card body)
  correctly failed: .unified-modal__text keeps newlines (the details modal body)
```

All 13 `src/styles/` suites pass (213 tests). Typecheck and `npm run lint:ci` clean.

**No screenshot attached.** The dev container and its image are both gone from this machine and free memory is ~8 GB, so a from-scratch rebuild is disproportionate for two CSS declarations that a test proves are load-bearing. Say the word and I'll build it and capture before/after.

title: fix(meshcore): bound runExclusiveRadioOp so a stuck radio op can't park the chain forever
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5243.

`runExclusiveRadioOp` chained unbounded on `fn`: the chain only advances when `fn`'s promise settles, and `sendCommand`'s outer `withTimeout` does **not** settle it — that timeout only rejects the *caller's* promise, it never cancels `fn` or advances `radioOpChain`. An op with no timer of its own (nothing resolves/rejects until a device push arrives that never comes) therefore parked the chain for the life of the connection: every later radio op queued behind it sat in `.then()` and its executor — including the `sendToRadioFrame` call that does the actual serial write — never ran again.

The reporter captured this with `strace` on the serial fd and traced the actual culprit to `set_out_path` (invoked by the owner-name fetch that follows a successful `discover_nodes`), which wraps `getContacts()`/`setContactPath()`/`addOrUpdateContact()` with no timer anywhere in the block.

- `runExclusiveRadioOp` now wraps every queued op in a 60s backstop timeout (kept above `trace_path`'s existing 45s inner timeout) so a stuck op always eventually settles the chain, even with no timer of its own.
- Tracks which op currently holds the chain (`radioOpHead`) so a timeout on a *different* command logs the real culprit instead of silently blaming whichever command happened to be queued behind it.
- `set_out_path` gets its own 15s inner timeout (mirroring `request_owner`) so it self-releases well before the 60s backstop, rather than parking discovery/owner-name resolution behind a full backstop wait every time.

Not applied: the reporter's caveat about the timed-out op's stale `once(Ok)`/`once(Err)` listeners remaining registered on the shared, tag-less response events (a late push could be consumed by an abandoned listener and mis-attributed) is a real, separate hazard already flagged in the existing `runExclusiveRadioOp` doc comment for foreign `Err`s. Left out of this PR to keep the fix focused on the chain-parking bug itself.

## Test plan

- Added `src/server/meshcoreNativeBackend.radioOpChain.test.ts`:
  - A radio op that never settles (no ack, ever) is released by the 60s backstop instead of parking the chain forever — a queued op behind it still reaches `sendToRadioFrame`.
  - `set_out_path` settles on its own 15s inner timer, well before the 60s backstop.
  - Both tests were verified to fail (hang/timeout) against the pre-fix code, confirming they reproduce the actual reported bug.
- Full `meshcoreNativeBackend*` suite: 148/148 passing.
- `npm run lint:ci` (the CI ratchet gate): passing, no new violations introduced.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the server project: clean.

title: fix(meshcore): lastHeard only moves forward, and every receive path stamps it
body:
Follow-up to #5132, which HougeDK reported as still broken on that PR: telemetry under an hour old, yet an inactive-node alert citing 13–21 hours, with Node Details agreeing with the alert.

## Why #5132 didn't hold

It was necessary but not sufficient. It made a telemetry round-trip stamp `lastHeard`, and **the stamp lands** — but nothing stopped the next writer from undoing it.

`persistContact()` writes the firmware's own `contact.lastSeen`, which the device refreshes **only on an ADVERT**. `upsertNode` had no ordering rule, so last writer won. For a node that adverts twice a day, the last writer was almost always the stale one, and `lastHeard` snapped back to the advert time within a contact-sync cycle of every telemetry poll:

```
contact sync   → lastHeard = advert time      (13h ago)
telemetry poll → lastHeard = now              ✅ #5132
contact sync   → lastHeard = advert time      ❌ clobbered, still 13h ago
inactive-node notifier reads 13h → alert
```

That reproduces the report exactly, including why Node Details "fits with the alert" while telemetry is fresh.

## The fix

**1. `lastHeard` is monotonic.** `upsertNode` drops an incoming `lastHeard` older than or equal to the stored one. A lower value is never news — it's a staler observer's opinion, not evidence the node went away.

The guard is surgical: a stale write still updates its *other* fields, so a contact sync carrying a rename alongside an old `lastSeen` keeps the rename. This is the choke point every writer already passes through, so it fixes the clobber on **all paths at once** rather than one caller at a time — which is what "any path updates lastHeard" actually requires.

**2. Every path that receives something stamps it**, through a new `MeshCoreRepository.markHeard(sourceId, publicKey, heardAtMs)` that documents what "heard" means and shares the guard:

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Remote telemetry round-trip | stamped (#5132), then clobbered | stamped, sticks |
| Local companion telemetry poll | **never stamped** | stamped on a productive poll |
| Neighbours reply | **never stamped** | stamped |
| Advert / contact sync | stamped | unchanged |
| Direct message | stamped | unchanged |

The companion case mattered on its own: the local node's `lastHeard` moved only on its own adverts, so a node we poll every 5 minutes over USB could be reported inactive.

## Deliberately not stamped

- **Observer `/status` heartbeat** — proves the observer is talking to its MQTT broker, not that it's reachable on the mesh. That exemption and its rationale are unchanged.
- **Local edits** (renaming a contact, resetting a route) — say nothing about whether a node is on the air.
- **Raw OTA packets** — MeshCore carries only hash prefixes, so they can't be attributed to a public key.

## Meshtastic is unaffected

It already stamps `nodes.lastHeard` on essentially every packet via `lastHeardFor()` / `resolveLastHeardSec()` (which has its own replay guard). Note its unit is **seconds

title: feat(auto-traceroute): per-filter AND/OR modes and named channels (#5230)
body:
Closes #5230.

## What the issue asked for, and what was already there

The issue asks for a multi-select channel filter so Auto Traceroute can be scoped to chosen channels. Most of that already existed — `filterChannels` + `filterChannelsEnabled`, persisted per source, with a multi-select UI, filtering on `nodes.channel` (which is the `lastHeardChannel` the issue postulates, under a different name).

What did **not** work is the part that makes it useful. The five node-matching filters were a hard-coded **union**, so ticking a channel could only ever *widen* the candidate pool. Selecting `{LongTurbo}` alongside a role filter still traced every router on every other channel — the exact airtime waste the issue is about.

## What changed

**Per-filter AND/OR mode** on all five filters (nodes, channels, roles, hardware models, name regex), rather than hard-coding channel as a scope:

- `'or'` keeps the filter in the union — **the default**, and an install that never touches it behaves identically to before. The stored value is absent, and anything that is not literally `'and'` reads as `'or'`.
- `'and'` makes the filter a scope the node must also satisfy.
- A pure-AND config is a plain intersection, not an empty set: the union clause is vacuous when no `'or'` filter is configured.
- An enabled-but-**empty** filter participates in neither group. Switching channels to AND *before* picking one is not a request to trace nothing, and treating it as a scope would silently halt the scheduler.

**The picker now names channels.** `nodes.channel` mixes two id spaces — 0-7 are device slots, `>= CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET` is `offset + channel_database.id` from server-side decryption. On a live install the virtual ids dominate (measured on a real DB: 5,678 nodes at `102`, 1,983 at `101`, only 1,489 at a genuine slot `0`), so the old "Ch 102" labels were unreadable for precisely the operators this serves. Both spaces now resolve, so it reads **LongFast**.

**The AND exclusion is visible.** A node with no decoded channel cannot be "heard on LongTurbo", so an AND scope drops it — 4,012 of 13,518 nodes on that same live DB. The picker reports the count instead of letting the match preview collapse for no stated reason.

The client-side preview mirrors the new backend logic. If the two drift the preview becomes a confident lie, which is worse than no preview because the user tunes against it.

## Judgment calls worth a reviewer's eye

- **Invalid modes are rejected, not coerced.** A typo silently falling back to `'or'` would *widen* the traced set — the opposite of what someone reaching for `'and'` wants. `400`, with the offending field named.
- **Empty ≠ scope**, as above. Pinned by a test, because getting it wrong stops every auto-traceroute silently.
- `PER_SOURCE_KEYS_NOT_POSTABLE` grew 17 → 22. The five mode keys are written by the dedicated `POST /api/settings/traceroute-nodes` route, same as their `*Enabled` siblings, so they belong in that exemption set. The size pin

title: fix(channels): let the reorder handle be dragged on touch (#5233)
body:
Fixes #5233 — on mobile the Channels drag handle didn't respond to touch: a long-press selected the 6-dot glyph as text instead of starting a drag, so channel slots couldn't be reordered on a phone.

## Root cause — not what the issue guessed

The issue hypothesized a native HTML5 `draggable` implementation, which is mouse-only. It isn't: the channel list already uses `@dnd-kit` with a `PointerSensor`, the same as every other reorder surface in the app.

The real cause is one missing CSS property. Without `touch-action: none` the browser claims the touch gesture for scrolling or text selection **before** the sensor sees a single `pointermove` — so the drag never starts, and the long-press falls through to the selection UI. A mouse never contends for the gesture, which is why desktop was fine and this shipped.

The sibling handles in `ChannelDatabaseSection` and `DashboardSidebar` both already set it. The Channels handle was **the only reorder activator in the app that did not**.

## The fix

Rather than restate the properties a fourth time, they move into a shared `DRAG_HANDLE_TOUCH_STYLE` that both hand-styled handles now spread, so the next handle can't quietly ship without them:

```ts
export const DRAG_HANDLE_TOUCH_STYLE: CSSProperties = {
  touchAction: 'none',
  userSelect: 'none',
  WebkitUserSelect: 'none',
  WebkitTouchCallout: 'none',
};
```

The prefixed pair isn't redundant with `user-select`: Safari honored the unprefixed property only from 17.4, and the iOS long-press callout has no unprefixed property at all.

The `⠿` braille character the handle drew is replaced with a `UiIcon` (`dragHandle` → lucide `GripVertical`). It was selectable content — the thing the long-press actually selected — and a hardcoded Unicode icon stand-in, which CLAUDE.md bans. `DashboardSidebar` drew the same glyph and gets the same treatment; its drag already worked, but a long-press could still raise the selection callout over it.

## Verified in a real browser, not just jsdom

This is a touch bug, so unit tests alone aren't proof. Deployed to the dev container and drove Chrome at 390×844 with `mobile,touch` emulation:

| | result |
|---|---|
| computed `touch-action` on the handle | `none` |
| dispatching `pointerType: 'touch'` on the handle | drag activates — `aria-pressed` → `true`, card takes the 0.8 dragging opacity |
| completing the gesture | slot carried from position 2 → position 0 |
| after Cancel | original order restored; `/api/channels` confirms nothing was written to the device |

Before the fix the same gesture did nothing at all.

_Screenshot below._

## Tests

New `dragHandleStyle.test.tsx` renders `ChannelsConfigSection` and asserts the handle carries the touch properties, plus that it draws an `<svg>` rather than the `⠿` glyph. A matching pin was added to the existing Edit-mode suite in `DashboardSidebar.test.tsx`, which already has the harness that reveals those handles.

Confirmed the pin actually bites: reverting just the `...DRAG_HAND

title: fix(sources): stop connecting to MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP nobody configured (#5237)
body:
Fixes the first half of #5237: a MeshCore-only install logging `EHOSTUNREACH 192.168.1.100:4403` every 60-90 seconds forever, where neither disabling nor deleting the Meshtastic source stopped it. (The PostgreSQL `clearPacketLogs` failure in the same report is #5238, separate.)

This takes **option B** from the issue triage — drop the S4 env-IP fallback outright — and additionally stops the fresh-install auto-create from using the placeholder IP.

## What was dialling an address nobody configured

**The "S4" fallback in `bootstrapSources`.** Whenever no `meshtastic_tcp` source auto-connected, it called `fallbackManager.connect()` against `env.meshtasticNodeIp`. That value is never empty — it falls back to the placeholder `192.168.1.100` — so any install that never set the variable dialled it. `TcpTransport` then retried on a 60s-capped backoff with no attempt limit, and nothing ever called `disconnect()` on the singleton, so no UI action could stop it.

S4 fired in exactly three cases, and all three are the operator saying "do not connect":

- the install has no Meshtastic node at all (MeshCore-only, MQTT-only);
- every `meshtastic_tcp` source is disabled;
- every `meshtastic_tcp` source has `autoConnect: false` — where connecting anyway overrode the precise intent of that flag.

**The fresh-install auto-create**, which built an always-`enabled: true` Default row from the same placeholder.

## The fix

- `bootstrapSources` no longer calls `fallbackManager.connect()`, and no longer takes a `fallbackManager` dep. It logs one line saying nothing connected and where to add a source.
- The auto-create now requires `env.meshtasticNodeIpProvided` — the "was MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP actually set" flag `environment.ts` already exposes. The gate is *was it provided*, not *does it differ from the default*, so explicitly setting `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP=192.168.1.100` still works (scenario 2b).

This resolves the "open Q1" that `bootstrapSources.ts` has carried since #3962 Phase 2 — in favour of dropping — and matches what `_legacyDefaultSource.ts` has done on the migration path since discussion #2604.

`fallbackManager` is **not** retired. It remains the concrete instance behind `getPrimaryMeshtasticManager(registry) ?? fallbackManager`, so that resolution never yields `undefined`. It is simply never connected at boot.

## Measured, not assumed

Booting a fresh SQLite database with `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` unset, on a network where `192.168.1.100` happens to host a real node:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| node rows ingested | **201** | 0 (1 synthetic `!ffffffff` broadcast row) |
| startup log lines | 900 | 297 |
| Meshtastic connections attempted | 1, succeeded | 0 |

So the bug was worse than the reported log spam. The reporter's placeholder address was unreachable, so they got `EHOSTUNREACH`. On a network where that address is occupied, a fresh install silently connected to and ingested 201 nodes from a device the operator never configured.

title: fix(packet-log): quote sourceId identifier in clearPacketLogs delete
body:
## Summary

- Fixes `PacketLogRepository.clearPacketLogs(sourceId)` failing on PostgreSQL with `column "sourceid" does not exist` — reported in #5237 when clearing packet logs after deleting a source (surfaces via `DatabaseService.purgeAllNodesAsync`).
- Root cause: the per-source branch built its `DELETE` with a raw, unquoted `sourceId` identifier (`` sql`DELETE FROM packet_log WHERE sourceId = ${sourceId}` ``). PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase, so this resolved to `sourceid`, which doesn't exist — the real column is the quoted camelCase `"sourceId"`. SQLite and MySQL fold case-insensitively, so the bug never surfaced on those backends.
- Fix: switched to the same Drizzle query-builder pattern the sibling `deletePacketLogsForNode` method already uses (`this.db.delete(packetLog).where(eq(packetLog.sourceId, sourceId))`), rather than raw SQL.
- Added `packetLog.clearPacketLogs.multiBackend.test.ts`, exercising the sourceId-scoped and unscoped delete paths on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, so a case-folding regression like this can't hide behind the SQLite-only suite again.

## Scope note

This PR addresses only the packet-log deletion bug from #5237. The issue also reports the Meshtastic fallback manager retrying a placeholder IP forever on MeshCore-only installs — that's a separate, already-tracked design question (explicitly deferred to the maintainer as "open Q1" in `bootstrapSources.ts`, and pinned by `bootstrapSources.test.ts` Scenario 6). See my comment on the issue for root-cause analysis and proposed remediation options; I've left that part unimplemented pending direction.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/db/repositories/packetLog.clearPacketLogs.multiBackend.test.ts src/db/repositories/packetLog.test.ts src/server/services/packetLogService.test.ts src/server/routes/packetRoutes.test.ts` — all pass (SQLite; PostgreSQL/MySQL suites skip locally without the test containers, per CLAUDE.md, and will run in CI).
- [x] `npm run lint:ci` — clean, no baseline growth.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.server.json` — clean.

title: feat(beacons): table-backed beacons list behind a button with a count (#5232)
body:
Closes #5232.

## The problem

MeshBeacon invitations rendered as a stack of cards inline above the channel list. That worked for one invitation and failed for three: on a phone the cards pushed the message list down to a sliver, and because a beacon re-advertises on its own interval there was no end state where they stayed gone.

## What was already there

The deduped table already existed — `mesh_beacon_offers` (migration 147), one row per `(sourceId, nodeNum)`, with `firstSeenAt` / `lastSeenAt`, and a `dismissedAt` that a rebroadcast preserves. So "dismiss and it comes straight back on the next broadcast" is not what the current code does, and there is a repository test pinning that.

What *does* resurface a dismissal is the sender changing its advertised channel, key, region or preset. That is deliberate — a re-keyed channel is a new invitation, not one already declined — but it leaves no way to say "never again" to a neighbouring mesh that keeps re-targeting. That is the gap this closes.

## What changed

**A Beacons button in the channels controls row**, badged with the pending count for the source. The count is its own `COUNT(*)` endpoint so the badge is right without fetching anything else; the list loads only when the modal opens.

![Beacons button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/beacons-table-ui-5232/docs/public/images/features/5232-beacons-button.png)

**A modal with a sortable table** — node, offer, first heard, last heard — with free-text search over node name/id, message and channel name, and a pending / hidden / all filter. Un-actionable offers stay listed with their reason, as before.

![Beacons list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/beacons-table-ui-5232/docs/public/images/features/5232-beacons-modal.png)

**Mute** (migration 166, `mesh_beacon_offers.mutedAt`) — the permanent form of dismiss. It survives both the rebroadcast and the content change; only an explicit un-mute clears it, and un-muting clears the dismissal too so one action brings a row back whichever way it was hidden.

![Hidden filter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/beacons-table-ui-5232/docs/public/images/features/5232-beacons-hidden.png)

The button outlives the badge on purpose: `total > 0` renders it, `pending > 0` badges it, so muting everything does not strand the un-mute.

### Also fixed

`regionName` read `.name` off `REGION_OPTIONS`, whose entries carry `label`. Every lookup missed, so a beacon advertising the US mesh rendered as "Advertises a mesh on LONG_FAST / region 1" — in the plain note and in the regulator-compliance warning alike. Caught by driving the deployed app, not by a test.

## API

| | |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/sources/:id/beacon-offers/count` | `{ pending, total }` |
| `POST /api/sources/:id/beacon-offers/:nodeNum/mute` | permanent hide |
| `POST /api/sources/:id/beacon-offers/:nodeNum/unmute` | clears both flags |

The offered channel PSK still never leaves

title: fix(nodeinfo): stop blank values from undoing enrichment, and un-stub map labels (#5231)
body:
Fixes #5231.

## What was wrong

Three separate holes, all the same shape: **a value that is present but carries no information was treated as data.**

### 1. `publicKey: ''` wiped the enriched key on the next packet

protobuf.js decodes an unset `bytes` field to an **empty buffer**, which is truthy. So the MQTT NodeInfo ingest did:

```ts
publicKey: user.publicKey ? Buffer.from(user.publicKey).toString('base64') : …
//         ^ empty buffer is truthy      ^ Buffer.from(empty).toString('base64') === ''
```

and `upsertNode` merged it with `??`, which does not catch `''`:

```ts
publicKey: nodeData.publicKey ?? existingNode.publicKey,   // '' wins
```

Every keyless NodeInfo packet therefore wiped the key the user had just copied in, and the enrichment report offered the identical copy again on the next refresh. This is the **"fields resurrect after a successful Fix All"** follow-up in the issue — donors at 8/8, copy applied, "No nodes need enrichment", then the same two rows come back.

### 2. The deprecated all-zero MAC

`User.macaddr` is *"Deprecated in Meshtastic 2.1.x"* (mesh.proto), so plenty of nodes broadcast six zero bytes. Hex-encoded that is `'000000000000'` — a non-empty string that

- sailed past `upsertNode`'s `''` guard and overwrote a real MAC, and
- counted as a **filled field** in `isNodeInfoFieldBlank`, so a donor was credited with a MAC it does not have and the offered copy changed nothing.

Same never-converging loop as #5193, a different sentinel. It is also exactly the reporter's SKYB screenshot: target `Address 000000000000`, donor `c4d266f1c31d`.

### 3. The map's `e848` label

MeshMonitor inserts a stub row named `Node !9e80e848` / `e848` the first time a node turns up as a traceroute hop or a neighbour entry (`mqttIngestion.ts` and the TCP equivalent). Those are non-empty strings, so `mergeNodeRecords` — which takes each field from the **newest record that has "a value"** — let a busy MQTT source's stub eclipse the real `SKYC` another source had learned. Hence "heard by 5 sources" and a hex marker label.

Note this is **display-side only**: the per-source rows are correct, and enrichment never reported the names as fillable because the stub is not blank.

## Fixes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/utils/nodeFieldBlanks.ts` *(new)* | Shared predicates: `isBlankMacAddr`, `isPlaceholderLongName`, `isPlaceholderShortName`. Used by both halves of the app so server and frontend agree. |
| `src/server/mqttIngestion.ts` | NodeInfo ingest omits an empty public key and an empty/all-zero MAC instead of encoding them to strings. |
| `src/db/repositories/nodes.ts` | `publicKey` merges with the same blank-string guard the names already use, on the update / insert / conflict paths. An all-zero MAC is "not provided" everywhere `''` already was. |
| `src/server/services/nodeInfoCopyService.ts` | `isNodeInfoFieldBlank` reads an all-zero macaddr as blank — the #5193 rule restated: *the analyzer's notion of blank must match what the repo

title: chore(release): bump to 4.16.1-rc3
body:
Version bump for the 4.16.1-rc3 release candidate.

All five version files updated per CLAUDE.md: `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (regenerated via `npm install --package-lock-only`), `helm/meshmonitor/Chart.yaml` (both `version` and `appVersion`), `desktop/package.json`, `desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.

## What rc3 picks up over rc2

20 commits. The headline is four **cross-source permission leaks**, all the same shape — `hasPermission` called with no `sourceId` while the handler answered for a caller-supplied `?sourceId=`, so a grant on any one source read another source's data:

| PR | endpoint | leaked |
|---|---|---|
| #5227 | `GET /api/messages` | DM **bodies** |
| #5227 | `GET /api/messages/channel/:channel` | channel message bodies |
| #5225 | `GET /api/messages/unread-counts` | DM counts |
| #5225 | `GET /api/messages/first-unread` | oldest-unread timestamps |

Also in this RC:

- **#5226** — per-page and cross-page configuration search
- **#5228** — waypoint arrival alerts with a radius and dedupe (#4750)
- **#5224** — "Mark all read" beside the Sources unread toggle (#5197)
- **#5203** — MeshCore DM/channel retries reuse the original `senderTimestamp` (#5202); also fixes a `NO_CHANNEL` flood
- **#5219** — the `react-leaflet` `GeoJSON` mock gap that had been flaking CI for days
- **#5205 / #9d9b8f04 / #5206** — armv7 Docker timeout, native JS build (−42%), and a Retag workflow
- 11 dependency bumps, including react/react-dom 19.3.0 (grouped so the family can no longer be split)

## Versioning note

Two of these are features on a line that had carried only fixes. Numbering as `4.16.1-rc3` rather than `4.17.0-rc1` is a deliberate call — raised and decided before cutting.

Carries the `system-test` label — release version bumps always run the hardware suite.

title: feat(notifications): waypoint arrival alerts with a radius and dedupe (#4750)
body:
Closes #4750.

Alerts you when a waypoint arrives from the mesh near you. Configured per source on that source's **Notifications** tab, beside the other alert toggles — Meshtastic only, since MeshCore has no waypoint concept, so the block is gated exactly like traceroutes.

![Waypoint arrival settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/waypoint-notifications-4750/docs/public/images/features/4750-waypoint-notifications.png)

## Mesh impact checklist

**Airtime: zero.** Nothing here transmits — it reacts to a packet that already arrived.

**Spam: real, and it is the whole design problem.** One waypoint fans out to web push, Apprise and desktop for every user with the flag on, and waypoints rebroadcast on a schedule. Three rules bound it:

### 1. Only mesh-received waypoints alert

The notifier is called from `upsertFromMesh` and nowhere else. `createLocal`, `update`, and the rebroadcast tick are the user's own actions and our own transmissions — alerting on those would be telling the user about themselves, and would let our own sends re-enter as notifications the way the automation engine did in #3914. There is no filtering inside the notifier to catch a mistake here, so the wiring is asserted directly in `waypointService.test.ts`.

### 2. A radius, measured per user

Default **10 km** — a LongFast neighbourhood, not a region. Each user has their own centre and radius, so the filter runs per user and the fan-out targets individual users rather than re-broadening to everyone with the flag.

The centre is the user's explicit lat/lon when set, else **the source's own node position**, which follows a mobile node. With neither, the user is **skipped**. Failing open there would alert on every waypoint anywhere on the mesh, which is the one outcome the radius exists to prevent.

### 3. Does a save reset a safety timer? — no, and this is the load-bearing bit

Dedupe state is a **table**, not an in-memory Map like `lowBatteryNotificationService`'s cooldown. In-memory state answers "no, I haven't told them" to every question after a container restart, and the next rebroadcast sweep would re-alert every waypoint in range at once.

The key is the **waypoint id alone** — deliberately no name or position comparison. Per @Yeraze on the issue: waypoints do not move, they get recreated with the same name and a fresh id, and that recreation *should* read as new. Keying on the id gives that for free while a rebroadcast of a known id stays silent.

Rows are written only on a successful send, so a waypoint that arrived out of range leaves no row and will alert if it later comes back while your reference point has moved closer. They are dropped on delete and on the expiry sweep, which bounds the table and lets a reused id alert again.

**Default OFF**, matching `notify_on_inactive_node` and `notify_on_low_battery` rather than the flags that default TRUE. An upgrade must not start alerting people who never asked.

## Changes

- **Migration 165** —
author: Yeraze
diff:
--- docs/features/notifications.md (+34/-1)
@@ -585,6 +585,7 @@ Notification filtering applies to **both Web Push and Apprise** notifications:
 - **Emoji Reactions**: Enable/disable notifications for emoji-only messages (third priority)
 - **Newly Found Nodes**: Enable/disable notifications when new nodes are discovered
 - **Successful Traceroutes**: Enable/disable notifications for completed traceroute responses
+- **Waypoint Arrivals**: Enable/disable notifications when a waypoint arrives from the mesh nearby
 - **Enabled Channels**: Specific channels to receive notifications from
 - **Direct Messages**: Enable/disable direct message notifications
 
@@ -597,6 +598,7 @@ The filtering follows this priority order for **message notifications**:
 **Special Event Notifications** (bypass message filtering):
 - **Newly Found Nodes** → Sent when a new node appears on the mesh (includes node name and hop count)
 - **Successful Traceroutes** → Sent when a traceroute completes (includes full forward and return route)
+- **Waypoint Arrivals** → Sent the first time a waypoint arrives from the mesh inside your radius (see below)
 
 ::: tip Emoji Reaction Filtering
 When "Emoji Reactions" is disabled, notifications will be suppressed for messages containing only emojis (e.g., "👍", "😀", "❤️"). Messages with emojis mixed with text will still trigger notifications normally. This is useful for reducing notification noise from emoji reactions and tapbacks.
@@ -606,6 +608,37 @@ When "Emoji Reactions" is disabled, notifications will be suppressed for message
 New Node and Traceroute notifications bypass normal message filtering (whitelist/blacklist/channel settings) and are only sent if you have that specific preference enabled. These notifications help you stay informed about mesh network topology changes and connectivity testing without cluttering your message notifications.
 :::
 
+### Waypoint Arrivals
+
+Alerts you when someone places a waypoint near you. Configured per source, on that source's **Notifications** tab, beside the other alert toggles. Meshtastic only — MeshCore has no waypoint concept, so the block is hidden there.
+
+Off by default. Turning it on reveals two settings:
+
+- **Alert within** — the radius, in kilometres. Default 10 km, roughly a LongFast neighbourhood. This is what keeps a busy mesh from alerting you about waypoints two counties away.
+- **Measured from** — a latitude and longitude. Leave both empty (the normal case) and the radius is measured from that source's own node, which follows it when the node is mobile. Fill them in when your server's node sits somewhere other than the area you care about.
+
+![Waypoint arrival settings on a source's Notifications tab](/images/features/4750-waypoint-notifications.png)
+
+::: warning No reference point, no alerts
+If you leave the coordinates empty and the source's node has never reported a position, nothing is sent. This is deliberate: the alternative would be treating "no centre" as "no radius", which alerts on every waypoint anywhere on the mesh.
+:::
+
+#### You are alerted once per waypoint
+
+Waypoints rebroadcast on a schedule, so the first alert is the only one. MeshMonitor records which waypoints it has told you about and stays silent on every rebroadcast of the same one.
+
+That record is keyed on the waypoint's **id**, not its name or position — and that is what you want, because waypoints do not move. Someone who "moves" a waypoint actually creates a new one with a new id, and you are alerted about it, correctly, as a new waypoint. The record is cleared when a waypoint is deleted or expires, so an id that gets reused later alerts again.
+
+The record lives in the database rather than in memory, so restarting the container does not re-alert you about everything in range.
+
+#### What does not alert you
+
+Only waypoints that arrive **over the air** trigger a notification. Waypoints you create or edit in MeshMonitor, and the periodic rebroadcasts MeshMonitor sends of your own waypoints, are silent — you already know about those.
+
+#### Airtime
+
+None. This feature transmits nothing; it reacts to packets that already arrived.
+
 ### MeshCore Sources
 
 MeshCore sources have their own **Notifications** tab, and the settings are tailored to what MeshCore actually supports. Because MeshCore and Meshtastic expose different capabilities, the notification options shown for a MeshCore source are a subset:
@@ -617,7 +650,7 @@ MeshCore sources have their own **Notifications** tab, and the settings are tail
 | **Newly Found Nodes** | ✅ | Sent the first time a contact advertises (display name + device type: Companion / Repeater / Room Server). |
 | **Server Events** | ✅ | Source connect/disconnect/reconnect. |
 | **Web Push / Apprise / Monitored-node picker** | ✅ | Delivery and node selection work the same as Meshtastic. |
-| Direct Messages, Emoji Reactions, MQTT, Traceroutes, Channel selection, Keyword filtering, percentage battery threshold | ❌ | Hidden for MeshCore — these depend on Meshtastic-only protocol features or data. |
+| Direct Messages, Emoji Reactions, MQTT, Traceroutes, Waypoint arrivals, Channel selection, Keyword filtering, percentage battery threshold | ❌ | Hidden for MeshCore — these depend on Meshtastic-only protocol features or data. |
 
 All preferences are scoped per-source, so a MeshCore source and a Meshtastic source can have independent thresholds and monitored-node lists.
 
--- docs/features/waypoints.md (+6/-0)
@@ -94,6 +94,12 @@ Migration **130** adds the `channel` column that records which slot a waypoint i
 
 The daily database maintenance tick sweeps expired waypoints (with a grace window) and emits `waypoint:expired` events for each removed row.
 
+## Arrival notifications
+
+You can be alerted when a waypoint arrives from the mesh inside a radius you choose. It is off by default and configured per source, on that source's **Notifications** tab — see [Waypoint Arrivals](/features/notifications#waypoint-arrivals).
+
+Migration **165** adds the four preference columns (`notify_on_waypoint`, `waypoint_radius_km`, `waypoint_center_lat`, `waypoint_center_lon`) and the `waypoint_notifications` ledger, one row per (user, source, waypoint) already alerted on. The ledger is what makes a rebroadcast silent; rows are removed when a waypoint is deleted or swept as expired.
+
 ## Limitations and follow-ups
 
 - **Rebroadcast scheduler is not yet wired**. The `rebroadcast_interval_s` column is persisted and accepted by the API, but no timer fires it. Waypoints you create are broadcast once on save; resends rely on the stock Meshtastic firmware behaviour at this time.

--- public/locales/en.json (+7/-1)

   "config_search.filter_automation": "Search automations...",
   "config_search.filter_notifications": "Search notification settings...",
-  "config_search.filter_admin": "Search admin sections..."

title: fix(security): scope the message-list permission gates to the requested source
body:
Completes the sweep started in #5225. Same class of cross-source leak, but these two endpoints return message **bodies** rather than counts.

## The leak

`GET /api/messages` and `GET /api/messages/channel/:channel` checked permissions with **no source id**, then answered for the caller-supplied `?sourceId=`. A grant on any one source returned another source's messages.

**I checked `GET /` during #5225 and wrongly cleared it.** That check used the default `limit`, and a 50-message sample from a busy source is all channel traffic — the DMs never appeared. At `limit=500` it is plain. On the live install, an account with `messages:read` on three MQTT sources and none on a Meshtastic TCP source:

```
GET /api/messages?sourceId=<tcp-source>&limit=500

{ fromNodeId: '!d8ee7714', toNodeId: '!384df6f7',
  text: 'MeshMonitor #5124 badge test', channel: -1 }
```

That is the DM text, read by an account with no `messages` grant on that source.

## What changed

Three gates in `GET /`:

| gate | why it matters |
|---|---|
| `messages:read` | DMs pass the downstream filter on this flag alone |
| `channel_0:read` | the legacy blanket channel gate |
| `channel_${id}:read` loop building `authorizedChannelIds` | un-scoped, a channel grant on **one** source unhides that channel on **every** source |

The third is easy to miss — it sits well below the other two and feeds the filter rather than a 403.

`GET /channel/:channel` gets the same treatment. Its `sourceIdParam` was already resolved above the gate, so only the call changed.

With `?sourceId=` omitted both endpoints still span every source, and an un-scoped `hasPermission` keeps its union-across-sources meaning.

## No lockout risk

Worth stating explicitly, since scoping a gate is exactly how you lock people out: `messages` is a **sourcey** resource, so a global (`sourceId = NULL`) grant authorizes nothing in `checkPermissionAsync`'s sourcey branch either way. Those misleading NULL rows were removed in #4448. Same reasoning applies retroactively to #5225.

## About the `/channel/:channel` half

I could **not** reproduce that one on the live install: every source this account lacks `channel_0` on is MQTT, and MQTT sources store virtual channels (`CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET + id`, ≥ 100), so channel 0 has no rows there to leak. That is a property of this install's data, not evidence the endpoint is safe.

The harness has no such gap. Without the fix, its test returns source B's `'channel B'` text to a caller holding only source A.

## Testing

| | without fix | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` — no other-source DM bodies | **fails** | passes |
| `GET /channel/:channel` — no other-source messages | **fails** | passes |
| both "still returns the caller's own source" guards | pass | pass |
| admin sees both sources | pass | pass |

The two positive cases are deliberate: they catch the reverse failure, where scoping the gate blanks out the source the caller legitimately holds.

Real harness throughout — real session, re

title: feat(settings): add per-page and cross-page configuration search (#5182)
body:
Closes #5182.

## What

Two search surfaces over MeshMonitor's configuration, sharing one matching rule.

### 1. Per-page filter

`SectionNav` grows an opt-in filter box, so Settings, Device, Automation, Notifications and Admin each get one for free (and so does any future page that uses the picker).

It narrows **both** the chip row and the sections those chips point at, matching each section's **rendered text** — not just its heading. Typing `battery` on the Settings tab keeps Telemetry, Solar Monitoring and Sorting, none of which is *called* "Battery". That is what makes it work without anyone maintaining a per-setting index, and what makes new settings searchable the day they land.

A short keyword list per section covers the words that appear nowhere on screen (`gps` → Position, `radio` → LoRa). Escape clears the box rather than closing whatever modal is listening further up.

Non-matching sections are hidden with a generated `<style>` rather than by setting a class or `hidden` on the section nodes: those nodes belong to the tab that rendered them, and the tab's next render would clobber the change.

### 2. Cross-page palette

**Ctrl/Cmd+,** (or **Search Settings**, new at the top of the sidebar's Configuration group) opens a palette that searches every configuration page at once — including the ones not currently mounted, which is exactly the case the page filter cannot serve. Results are labelled with the page they live on; arrow keys move, Enter opens, Escape dismisses.

Picking one navigates to `route#section-id`. `SectionNav` now honours such a hash on mount and on `hashchange`, scrolling the section clear of the fixed header with the offset it already computes for clicks — so the deep link is useful on its own, not just from the palette.

Ctrl+K stays message search. The obvious palette chords are taken by the browser (Ctrl+Shift+P opens a private window in Firefox, Ctrl+Shift+K its console), so this uses the conventional "preferences" chord.

## Why a section-level index, not a per-setting one

A per-input catalogue would have to be hand-maintained and would rot the first time somebody added a checkbox without touching it. The section list is already maintained — every tab renders its picker from it. So the palette searches sections; once you land, the page's own filter takes over and *does* see individual settings, because by then they are rendered.

## Structural change

The five tabs' inline `SectionNav items={[...]}` arrays are lifted into `src/components/search/configSections.ts`, so the tab, its filter and the palette read one list. `GLOBAL_SECTIONS`/`SOURCE_SECTIONS` move there with them.

Visibility gates moved too, so the palette never hands out a deep link to a section the user cannot see: admin-only panels, the `settings:write`-gated batch jobs, SQLite-only Database Maintenance, OTA-gated Firmware Updates. Opened outside a source (the standalone Global Settings page) it offers only global sections — with several sources con

title: fix(security): scope the unread-counts permission gate to the requested source
body:
Found while investigating why `/unread-by-source` returned `{}` on the dev install. That endpoint turned out to be **correct** — the session was the anonymous user, which holds `messages:read` on the MQTT sources but not the Meshtastic TCP ones, so withholding the TCP source's DM was the right answer.

Chasing it surfaced a real leak in the sibling endpoint instead.

## The leak

`GET /api/messages/unread-counts` checked permissions with **no source id**:

```ts
const hasChannelsRead = isAdmin || await hasPermission(req.user, 'channel_0', 'read');
const hasMessagesRead = isAdmin || await hasPermission(req.user, 'messages', 'read');
```

…then answered for the caller-supplied `?sourceId=`. Holding either grant on **any one** source was enough to read **every** source's unread counts, one request at a time.

Reproduced live — an account with `messages:read` on three MQTT sources and none on a TCP source:

```
GET /api/messages/unread-counts?sourceId=<tcp-source>
-> { "directMessages": { "!d8ee7714": 1 } }
```

This is the #3745 cross-source shape, reached by *naming* sources rather than enumerating them. `/unread-by-source` re-checks per source id and documents the hazard — but describes this sibling as *"bounded … the caller names the source and sees only that source"*. That is true of the **response**; it says nothing about whether the caller was entitled to name it.

## The fix

Both gates are scoped to `unreadSourceId`, which moves to the top of the handler since the gates now depend on it.

With `?sourceId=` omitted the queries deliberately span every source (`ALL_SOURCES`), and an un-scoped `hasPermission` keeps its original meaning there — the cross-source view is unchanged.

## Scope: what I did *not* change

`GET /api/messages` has the same un-scoped gate shape. I checked it against the live install rather than assuming: requesting a source the caller has no `messages` grant on returns **0 DMs** — its downstream MM-SEC-3 per-channel filtering already bounds it. Left alone deliberately.

## About the test — worth reading

The regression test reproduces the **exact live permission shape**: `messages:read` on A only, but `channel_0:viewOnMap` on **both**.

That second grant is load-bearing. Sender visibility is filtered separately by `filterNodesByChannelPermission`, so without a viewOnMap grant on B the DM is dropped by *that* filter regardless — and the test passes against the unfixed code, proving nothing.

I wrote it that way first, and checked. It passed both with and without the fix. As written now:

| | result |
|---|---|
| without the fix | **fails** — `{ '!0b000002': 1 }` vs `{}` |
| with the fix | passes |

The other two cases guard the reverse failure: that scoping the gate does not lock a user out of their own source, and that admins still see every source.

## Testing

- 3 new tests in `messageRoutes.unreadCountsScope.test.ts`, through the real harness (real session, real `optionalAuth`, real permission rows).

title: feat(messages): add "Mark all read" beside the Sources unread toggle (#5197)
body:
Closes #5197

## The request, and the part of it I did not do

The issue asked to **replace** the sidebar's "Unread DM indicator" toggle with a "Mark all as read" action, on the grounds that the toggle *"also lives in Settings"*.

**It does not.** `unreadIndicatorEnabled` appears in exactly two files — `DashboardSidebar.tsx` and `DashboardPage.tsx` — and nowhere in Settings. The sidebar chip is its only control, and it gates the 15s `useUnreadBySource` poll as well as the badge, so removing it would leave no way to stop either. The placement was deliberate in #5124, for the same 5+ source profile as this requester.

So this implements the **"or adding beside"** half, which is the useful part.

## Backend

New `POST /api/messages/mark-all-dms-read`.

The existing `/mark-read` `allDMs` flag could not serve this:

- it resolves **one** manager and marks DMs to or from that single source's local node, so on a multi-source install it clears one badge and leaves the rest lit;
- it returns 500 `Local node not connected` when that manager has no local node — for a bulk action, one disconnected source would fail the whole sweep.

The per-source traversal behind the badge is extracted into `collectVisibleUnreadDms`, now shared by `/unread-by-source` (which counts) and the new route (which clears). **That shared seam is the point.** If the two drifted:

- a DM the badge counted but the sweep skipped → the badge survives "mark all read";
- a DM the sweep cleared but the badge never counted → it silently marks conversations the caller cannot see.

Per-source `messages:read`, per-sender channel visibility and mutes therefore apply identically to both.

Marking goes through the same repository call that opening a conversation already uses, so this adds no new read-state semantics — it is the manual "open each thread" loop the reporter does today, executed server-side.

## Frontend

`useMarkAllDmsRead` mirrors the existing `useMarkAsRead`, invalidating both `unreadBySource` and `unreadCounts` (the per-conversation badges read the same state).

The control renders **only when something is unread** — no permanent header space for an action with nothing to do, and it keeps both controls fitting on a narrow screen. It confirms above 50 unread: read state has no undo, so clearing a large backlog by stray tap is unrecoverable, while below that a prompt is just friction on a frequent action.

## Testing

- **7 route tests** through the real harness (real session, real `optionalAuth`, real permission rows): the badge-actually-reaches-zero contract, per-source isolation, sender visibility, anonymous and unprivileged rejection, idempotency.
- **8 sidebar tests**, including an explicit anti-regression that both controls render together.
- Full Vitest suite: **18,701 passed, 0 failed, 0 suites failed**. `tsc` (both projects) and `lint:ci` clean.

One detail worth recording: anonymous callers get **403, not 401**, because `optionalAuth` attaches the seeded `anonymous` *user*

title: chore(deps): bump react, react-dom and their types to 19.3.0 together
body:
Replaces #5210 and #5214, which could not merge individually.

## Why they were stuck

Dependabot split the React 19.2.8 → 19.3.0 release across two PRs:

| PR | Packages |
|---|---|
| #5210 | `react-dom`, `@types/react-dom` |
| #5214 | `react`, `@types/react` |

`react-dom` refuses to run against a different `react` version:

```
Error: Incompatible React versions: The "react" and "react-dom" packages
must have the exact same version.
```

That throws at **import time**, so each PR on its own failed **all 1272 test files at collection** with `Tests  no tests` — a total CI wipeout that reads nothing like a version skew. And merging either one first would have left `main` itself mismatched.

## This PR

1. **Bumps all four together** — `react`, `react-dom`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` to 19.3.0.
2. **Adds a `react` group to `.github/dependabot.yml`** so the family always moves as one PR in future.

The grouping is the same remedy already applied to two other sibling families that pin each other exactly:

- `vitest` — added after `@vitest/coverage-v8` 5.0.0 landed with no matching vitest PR (#5114, #5107)
- `codeql-action` — added after init/autobuild/analyze/upload-sarif kept arriving as four broken-in-isolation PRs (#4519/#4521/#4531, #4635/#4637/#4644)

It is listed **before** `development-dependencies` deliberately. That group matches `@types/*`, which is precisely how `@types/react` got separated from `react` in the first place; group order is first-match-wins, so the react group has to precede it. The comment in the file records this so it does not get reordered away.

## Testing

- Full Vitest suite: **18,686 passed, 0 failed, 0 suites failed.**
- `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:ci` clean.
- Verified at runtime that both resolve to the same version:
  ```
  react 19.3.0 | react-dom 19.3.0
  ```

Closes #5210
Closes #5214

title: fix(test): add the missing GeoJSON export to DashboardMap's react-leaflet mock
body:
Fixes the flake that is currently blocking three overnight Dependabot PRs (#5210, #5214, #5217).

## What was wrong

`DashboardMap.test.tsx` mocks `react-leaflet` but never exported `GeoJSON`. The #4794 test pushes a **visible** `geoJsonLayer`, so `DashboardMap` renders `<GeoJsonOverlay>` (`DashboardMap.tsx:847`, guarded on `geoJsonLayers.length > 0`), and that component reads `GeoJSON` off the mock:

```
Error: [vitest] No "GeoJSON" export is defined on the "react-leaflet" mock
  ❯ src/components/GeoJsonOverlay.tsx:76:12
```

The throw happens **asynchronously**, inside the overlay's render, *after* `await findByLabelText('Coverage overlay')` has already resolved. It tears down the React tree, so the very next query runs against an empty body and fails with something that looks unrelated:

```
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find a label with the text of: 3D Terrain
Ignored nodes: comments, script, style
<body>
  <div />
</body>
```

## Why it took a while to pin down

It depends on when React commits the overlay subtree relative to the assertions, so it only shows up on slower runners — and it presents differently each time:

| Where | Presentation |
|---|---|
| #5200 CI | `Unhandled Errors: 1`, **0 failed tests**, job still exit 1 |
| #5203 CI | `Test Suite (25.x)` failure, diagnosed as an unrelated `EmbedMap` flake |
| #5217 CI | Hard failure on `Test Suite (22.x)` — on a PR that changes **only** a GitHub Action version |

It passes **3/3 locally in isolation**, which is why it kept getting waved through as environmental.

`#5217` is what made it undeniable: that PR bumps `github/codeql-action` and touches no application code or dependency at all, so a test failure there cannot be attributable to anything but `main`.

## The fix

One line, mirroring the mock `EmbedMap.test.tsx` already carries:

```tsx
GeoJSON: () => <div data-testid="geojson" />,
```

The comment above it records why it is required rather than optional, so it does not get tidied away as unused.

## Testing

- `DashboardMap.test.tsx`, `EmbedMap.test.tsx` and all of `src/components/map`: **744 passed, 0 failed, 0 suites failed.**
- `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:ci` clean.

Once this lands, the three blocked Dependabot PRs need a rebase to pick it up.

v6.9.0

✨ Features and improvements

  • Improved support for drawing the letters of Devanagari, Khmer, Burmese and the other complex scripts and also draws Arabic and Hebrew labels correctly without loading a right-to-left text plugin, which deprecates setRTLTextPlugin and getRTLTextPluginStatus (#8343) (by @​HarelM)
  • Read sprite and image pixels back through an OffscreenCanvas where available, removing a main-thread stall of tens of milliseconds on GPU-accelerated browsers when a sprite loads (#8339) (by @​cherenkov)

  • Re-render at most one stale terrain drape per frame and keep drapes that differ only by zoom while the map moves, so a finger lift over terrain no longer re-renders every tile at once (#8368) (by @​johncarmack1984)

  • Fix setStyle() throwing while terrain is still loading because an intermediate render tried to compile a terrain shader before the replacement style initialized its projection (#6824) (by @​miakh)

  • Treat camera options passed as undefined as not given in jumpTo, easeTo and flyTo; they were coerced to NaN (#8373) (by @​vlumi)

title: perf(ci): build the armv7 JS artifacts natively instead of under QEMU
body:
Follow-up to #5205, which raised the armv7 timeout to stop the build failing. This attacks the cause instead of the symptom.

## What was wrong

The armv7 image built its whole `builder` stage under QEMU. Three of its four expensive steps didn't need emulation at all — Vite and tsc emit platform-independent JavaScript, so running them on an emulated ARM CPU bought nothing. Only the native modules (better-sqlite3) genuinely have to be built for the target.

## The split

- **`jsbuilder`** — pinned to `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM`, produces `dist/` on the build host's own architecture.
- **`deps`** — stays emulated; its only job is an armv7 `node_modules`.
- **runtime** — takes `node_modules` from `deps`, `dist`/`protobufs` from `jsbuilder`.

Getting those two crossed is the one way to break this subtly, so it's called out in a comment at the COPY site: `dist` from the emulated stage would merely be slow, but `node_modules` from the native stage would ship amd64 better-sqlite3 binaries into an armv7 image.

## Measured

QEMU on a 16-core amd64 host, cold cache, `--progress=plain`:

| step | baseline | split |
|---|---|---|
| Vite build | 5:06 | **0:32** (native) |
| tsc server build | 2:22 | **0:13** (native) |
| npm install | 9:51 | 9:38 (still emulated — the part that must be) |
| apt + apprise venv | 3:14 | 3:43 |
| **wall clock** | **18:25** | **10:44** — −42% |

CI runs ~2.4× slower than this host, which puts the ~39.5-minute build around **23 minutes** — the difference between comfortable headroom under #5205's raised timeout and creeping back toward it.

## Verified equivalent, not just faster

- **All 823 files under `dist/` hash identically** to the CI-built emulated image for the same source (v4.16.1-rc2). This is the claim the whole change rests on, so it was checked rather than assumed.
- **better-sqlite3 loads and executes** under armv7 emulation in the built image — the native module is still compiled by the emulated stage, exactly as before.
- **The container boots**: migrations run, the admin account seeds, and both the Express server (3001) and the Apprise API (8000) listen.

## Left for later, deliberately

The emulated `npm install` stays a *full* install rather than `--omit=dev`, so the shipped `node_modules` is unchanged by this PR. It is now 62% of the remaining build and the obvious next step — but it changes what ships, so it wants its own change and its own verification.

## Reproducing the measurement

The header comment in `Dockerfile.armv7` carries the commands. The one non-obvious part: `--progress=plain` is required, because the default TUI collapses the per-step `#N DONE <secs>s` lines and the timings become unrecoverable.

## Testing

No unit tests — this is a Dockerfile. The real verification is the byte-identical `dist/` diff, the native-module check and the boot test above, plus CI's own `Docker Build` leg on this PR.

title: feat(ci): add a Retag workflow for moving an alias without a rebuild
body:
Follow-up to #5205. Lets `:dev` (or any alias) be re-pointed at an already-built version in about a minute, with no rebuild.

## Why

The release pipeline builds each platform to an intermediate tag (`<version>-main`, `<version>-armv7`) and only then combines them. Those intermediate tags are never deleted — the cleanup step is a no-op that just echoes their names — so once a version has built successfully its alias can be recreated from them directly.

v4.16.1-rc2 is the case that motivated this:

1. `build-armv7` timed out, `create-manifest` was skipped, and **no `:VERSION` tag published at all** — not for any platform.
2. #5205 raised the timeout, but a workflow *re-run* uses the workflow file at the tag's commit, which still had the old cap. So the rebuild had to go through `workflow_dispatch`.
3. The `:dev` manifest step is gated on `github.event_name == 'release'`. Under dispatch it doesn't run — so `ghcr.io/yeraze/meshmonitor:4.16.1-rc2` exists and works, but `:dev` still resolves to rc1:

```
dev          -> ac6312fd  (= 4.16.1-rc1)
4.16.1-rc1   -> ac6312fd
4.16.1-rc2   -> 286758b9   <- only reachable by exact tag
```

Testers who track `:dev` would see none of the rc2 fixes, which defeats cutting the RC. Without this workflow the choices were a 40-minute full rebuild, or deleting a release that already holds ~1 GB of signed and notarized desktop assets.

## Behaviour

`workflow_dispatch` with `version` (e.g. `4.16.1-rc2`) and `alias` (default `dev`):

- **Verifies both `-main` and `-armv7` exist first** and fails with a clear message if not. It refuses to touch the alias unless both platforms are present — a half-populated `:dev` that silently dropped armv7 is worse than leaving the alias where it was, and `imagetools create` alone would surface that as an opaque manifest error rather than "this version was never fully built".
- Prints what the alias resolved to **before and after**, so the move is auditable from the run log.
- Uses the same `GITHUB_TOKEN` + `packages: write` auth as `create-manifest`; no new secrets.

## Note on the gap this works around

This is a sharp tool, not a fix for the underlying gating. Leaving the `:dev` step release-only is deliberate — the dispatch input's own documented example is `2.21.2-test`, and a test dispatch that silently moved `:dev` would be worse than the gap. An explicit, separately-invoked retag is the safer shape.

## Testing

No unit tests — it's a dispatch-only workflow with no repo code. YAML validated with `yaml.safe_load`. It will be exercised immediately after merge to move `:dev` to 4.16.1-rc2, and that run is the real verification.

author: Yeraze
diff:
--- .github/workflows/retag.yml (+93/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# Re-point a moving alias tag (:dev, :latest, …) at a version that is already
+# built and published, without rebuilding anything.
+#
+# Why this exists: the release pipeline builds each platform to an intermediate
+# tag (`<version>-main`, `<version>-armv7`) and only then combines them into the
+# real tags. Those intermediate tags are never deleted, so once a version has
+# built successfully its alias can be recreated from them in about a minute.
+#
+# v4.16.1-rc2 is the case that motivated it. Its armv7 build timed out, so
+# `create-manifest` was skipped and no `:VERSION` tag published at all; the
+# rebuild had to go through `workflow_dispatch`, and the `:dev` step is gated on
+# `github.event_name == 'release'`. The result was a published release whose
+# image existed but which every `:dev` follower was invisible to. The choice then
+# is a 40-minute rebuild, deleting a release that already holds ~1 GB of signed
+# desktop assets, or this.
+name: Retag
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      version:
+        description: 'Already-published version to point at (e.g. 4.16.1-rc2). Must have -main and -armv7 tags.'
+        required: true
+      alias:
+        description: 'Alias tag to move (e.g. dev, latest)'
+        required: true
+        default: 'dev'
+
+env:
+  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
+
+jobs:
+  retag:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      packages: write
+
+    steps:
+      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
+        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f  # v4
+        with:
+          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
+          username: ${{ github.actor }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Resolve image name
+        id: meta
+        run: echo "image=$(echo ${{ github.repository }} | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+
+      - name: Verify the source tags exist
+        # Fail here with a clear message rather than let `imagetools create`
+        # produce a confusing manifest error, and refuse to touch the alias at
+        # all unless BOTH platforms are present — a half-populated `:dev` that
+        # silently drops armv7 would be worse than leaving it where it was.
+        run: |
+          MAIN="${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.version }}-main"
+          ARMV7="${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.version }}-armv7"
+          missing=0
+          for ref in "$MAIN" "$ARMV7"; do
+            if docker buildx imagetools inspect "$ref" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+              echo "found: $ref"
+            else
+              echo "MISSING: $ref"
+              missing=1
+            fi
+          done
+          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
+            echo "::error::Cannot retag ${{ inputs.alias }} — version ${{ inputs.version }} has not been fully built."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+      - name: Show what the alias points at now
+        continue-on-error: true
+        run: |
+          echo "Before:"
+          docker buildx imagetools inspect \
+            "${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.alias }}" || echo "  (alias does not exist yet)"
+
+      - name: Move the alias
+        run: |
+          docker buildx imagetools create \
+            -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.alias }} \
+            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.version }}-main \
+            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.version }}-armv7
+
+      - name: Confirm the result
+        run: |
+          echo "After:"
+          docker buildx imagetools inspect \
+            "${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}:${{ inputs.alias }}"
+          echo "::notice::${{ inputs.alias }} now points at ${{ inputs.version }}"

title: fix(ci): give the armv7 Docker build enough time to finish
body:
The v4.16.1-rc2 release published on GitHub but **no Docker image did** — `ghcr.io/yeraze/meshmonitor:4.16.1-rc2` does not exist, only the intermediate `4.16.1-rc2-main` tag.

## What happened

`build-armv7` timed out at its 40-minute step cap, twice, both times at exactly the same place:

```
#34 [stage-1 15/15] RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh
#34 DONE 0.1s
#35 [linux/arm/v7] generating sbom ...
#35 DONE 8.6s
#36 exporting to image
#36 exporting layers
##[error]The action 'Build and push (armv7)' has timed out after 40 minutes.
```

Every build stage finished. It ran out of wall clock writing the result.

`create-manifest` has `needs: [build-main, build-armv7, smoke-test]`, so a failure there skips the manifest entirely and the `:VERSION` tag never gets created — for *any* platform, not just armv7.

## Why now

This is a margin that has been shrinking for weeks, not a new regression:

| release | build-armv7 |
|---|---|
| v4.16.0-rc2 | 35m 31s |
| v4.16.0-rc3 | 35m 46s |
| v4.16.0-rc4 | 35m 45s |
| v4.16.0-rc5 | 35m 12s |
| v4.16.0-rc6 | 40m 34s |
| v4.16.1-rc1 | 40m 18s — scraped through |
| **v4.16.1-rc2** | **timed out (×2)** |

## The change

`build-armv7` job 45 → 80 min, its build step 40 → 75 min. `build-main` is untouched (still 45/40).

The headroom is deliberately generous rather than "just enough". At 40 minutes every release was a coin flip, and the two timeouts burned ~80 minutes of runner time between them while publishing nothing. A higher cap costs extra minutes only on runs that actually need them.

## The real fix, noted but not done here

The emulated cost is concentrated in two steps:

```
#15 [builder  5/12]  npm install     1436s (23.9m)
#22 [builder 11/12]  npm run build    585s (9.8m)
#13 [stage-1  3/15]  apt + apprise    322s (5.4m)
```

Cross-compiling the builder stage natively on amd64 and running only the runtime stage under armv7 would cut most of that and let this timeout come back down. That is a real piece of work and rc2 is unpublishable until something lands, so it is recorded in the job comment rather than attempted here.

## After merge

v4.16.1-rc2 needs re-cutting: a workflow re-run uses the workflow file **at the tag's commit**, which still has the 40-minute cap. `workflow_dispatch` is not equivalent either — the `:dev` manifest step is gated on `github.event_name == 'release'`, so a dispatch would publish `:4.16.1-rc2` but strand `:dev`. The release will be deleted and recreated against a `main` that contains this fix.

title: fix(meshcore): DM/channel retries reuse the original senderTimestamp
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5202 — MeshCore DM/channel retries were generating a new wire `senderTimestamp` (and, for DMs, hardcoding `attempt = 0`) on every retransmit, so a retry read as a brand-new message to the recipient and could show up as a visible duplicate.

- `MeshCoreManager.performScopedSend` now computes (or accepts) an explicit `{ attempt, senderTimestamp }` and passes both through the `send_message` bridge command, instead of letting `meshcore.js`'s `sendTextMessage()`/`sendChannelTextMessage()` wrappers mint a fresh timestamp internally on every call.
- The DM ack-timeout retry cascade (`pendingDmRetries`, #3977) now carries the *original* `senderTimestamp` across the whole same-path + flood retry sequence, incrementing `attempt` by 1 on each resend — matching the official MeshCore app's retry semantics.
- The channel echo-miss retry (`pendingChannelRetries`, #3979) reuses the *original* `senderTimestamp` on its one-shot resend (channel frames carry no `attempt` field, so an identical `(sender, timestamp, text)` payload is what lets normal mesh dedup recognize the resend as the same message).
- `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts` adds two small helpers (`sendTextMessageWithAttempt`, `sendChannelTextMessageWithTimestamp`) that drive the vendored library's lower-level `sendCommandSendTxtMsg`/`sendCommandSendChannelTxtMsg` directly — replicating the wrappers' own `Sent`/`Ok`/`Err` correlation — whenever an explicit `senderTimestamp` is supplied. A caller that doesn't need retry control (`sendRoomPost`) is unaffected and keeps using the library wrappers unchanged.

No change to the pinned `@liamcottle/meshcore.js` fork is required — the lower-level primitives it already exposes accept these fields; they just weren't being used.

No new sends, timers, or airtime cost: this changes what data an *already-existing* retransmission carries, and if anything reduces effective mesh traffic (fewer duplicate messages visible to recipients).

## Test plan
- [x] Added `meshcoreManager.dmRetry.test.ts` case: every send across the full same-path + flood retry cascade carries the same `sender_timestamp`, with `attempt` advancing `[0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- [x] Added `meshcoreManager.channelRetry.test.ts` case: the one-shot channel resend carries the same `sender_timestamp` as the original send.
- [x] Added `meshcoreNativeBackend.test.ts` cases: a `send_message` bridge call with explicit `attempt`/`sender_timestamp` bypasses the library wrappers and drives `sendCommandSendTxtMsg`/`sendCommandSendChannelTxtMsg` directly with the caller's values, while still surfacing the firmware's `Sent` response (`expectedAckCrc`/`estTimeout`).
- [x] Verified the fix against the actual installed `@liamcottle/meshcore.js` fork (not just documentation) to confirm the wrapper behavior and the lower-level primitives' signatures.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.server.json` — clean.
- [x] Full MeshCore-related Vitest suite (88 files / 1390 tests) — all passing.
- [x] `npm run lint:ci` — no new

title: fix(security): stop two global class collisions overlapping the issue-card text on mobile
body:
Spotted while verifying #5194 in the deployed container — reported here rather than filed separately, at the maintainer's request.

## Problem

Every Security issue card — Time Offset, Low-Entropy, Duplicate Key, Excessive Packets — printed its node name directly on top of its node ID at phone widths. Both lines are legible on desktop, so this only showed up in portrait.

## Root cause

`.node-info` and `.node-name` are generic names that two **other** global sheets also claim, and both turn the element into a flex row:

| Sheet | Rule |
|---|---|
| `AppHeader.css` | `.node-info { display: flex; align-items: center }` |
| `nodes.css` | `.node-name { display: flex; flex: 1; min-width: 0 }` |

`SecurityTab.css` never declared `display` on either, so those rules won by default. The card's three stacked lines (name / node id / last seen) were laid out **side by side** instead, and the name — `flex: 1` with `min-width: 0` in a row too narrow to hold it — collapsed to **zero measured width** and overflowed straight over the node id. A wide desktop card fits the row, which is why this went unnoticed.

Measured before the fix, at 390px:

```
.node-name   x=49  y=8208  w=0    <- collapsed, text overflows
.node-id     x=65  y=8235  w=156  <- name renders on top of this
.node-last-seen x=229 y=8237 w=112
```

## Fix

State the intended block layout explicitly, scoped under `.security-tab` (0,2,0) so it outranks the bare global selectors (0,1,0). The mobile `flex-basis: 100%` override is scoped to match, or it would now lose to its own base rule.

The global sheets are left alone: they are frozen per CLAUDE.md, and other pages depend on those rules. A comment at the fix records why the scoping is load-bearing, since unscoping it looks like harmless tidying and silently restores the bug.

## Verification

In the dev container at 390x844: **87 issue cards on the Security page, zero overlapping line pairs.**

![Time Offset cards stacking correctly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/claude/fix-security-time-offset-card-overlap/docs/public/images/features/security-issue-card-stacking-after.png)

## Testing

- `src/components/SecurityTab.issueCardCollision.test.ts` — asserts the collision still exists in the two global sheets (so the guard cannot quietly become dead weight), that the scoped rules declare `display: block`, that no unscoped `.node-info`/`.node-name` rule is left behind, and that the mobile override keeps its scope. jsdom applies no cross-sheet cascade, so a render test cannot catch this — same approach `TelemetryGraphs.layout.test.ts` uses for #5093.
- Full Vitest suite: **18,652 passed, 0 failed**.

Independent of #5199 — no file overlap beyond `SecurityTab.css`, which touches different rules.
