title: feat(mqtt): several topic rewrite rules per direction on one bridge (#6516)
body:
Closes #6516. (Grew out of support question #6515, now closed.)

## What

An `mqtt_bridge` can now hold **up to 8** topic-rewrite rules per direction, so several upstream branches can share one connection.

- **Downlink:** the rule with the **longest** matching `from` wins; only one rule applies, so rules never chain. Several `from` values can share a `to`, merging branches into one local prefix. A packet cross-posted to two branches is republished locally **once** (echo cache keyed on the post-rewrite topic).
- **Uplink:** a local packet goes upstream **once**, to the **first** matching rule in list order (labelled *Primary* in the UI). New `uplinkRewriteFanOut` (default **off**) sends it to **every** matching rule instead; each copy keeps its own echo entry, so loop suppression holds per branch.
- **Backward compatible:** `downlinkTopicRewrite` / `uplinkTopicRewrite` accept the old single object or a list. Both editors save **one** rule as the old object (downgrade-safe) and write a list only for 2+.
- **Validation** (`validateMqttBridgeRewrites`): cap of 8, per-rule checks with the rule index in the error, no repeated downlink `from`, no exact-duplicate uplink rule, boolean `uplinkRewriteFanOut`. The cap lives in `src/server/constants/mqttBridge.ts`, shared by server and UI.
- **UI:** new shared `TopicRewriteList` component (CSS module, `UiIcon`) used by the bridge **Topic rewrites** section and the broker modal's **Bridge topic rewrites**. The broker modal used to have its own single-pair hydrate/compare/serialize code, which would have wiped a list on the next save; it now goes through the shared helpers in `mqttBridgeConfig.ts`. The fan-out toggle (bridge settings page) shows a warning when on.
- **Redaction:** `uplinkRewriteFanOut` added to the catalogue as `withheld`; the rewrite keys already were.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/mqtt-broker.md` gets a "Several rules per direction" section; the "needs separate bridges" caveat is gone. It also notes that, for **uplink**, the local prefix must sit under the parent broker's root topic (the broker only emits `local-packet` under its root).

title: fix(meshcore): pick up a contact's new name after a rename advert (#6512)
body:
Fixes #6512.

## Problem
The companion firmware's `PUSH_CODE_ADVERT` (0x80) for a stored contact carries only the public key. The handler kept `existing.advName`, and the debounced `get_contacts` re-read ran only when the contact had no name. A renamed Room Server kept its old name until the source reconnected.

## Fix
- The raw advert frame (LogRxData, which arrives just before the push) now stashes its sanitized name next to the hash/position/hops already kept.
- A key-only `contact_advertised` push for a known contact schedules the existing debounced re-read when the stashed name differs from ours, or when no raw frame was seen.
- The raw name is only **compared**, never written to the contact: the firmware checks the signature, MeshMonitor doesn't, and the serial link has no checksum. A bad frame costs one local read.
- The re-read loop now also refreshes the Ignore/Block name snapshot (`noteAdvertName`). Persistence to `meshcore_nodes`, the WS update and `nodeUpdated` already ran there.

## Mesh impact
- **Airtime:** none. `get_contacts` is a local serial read, coalesced by the existing 1.5 s debounce. It runs on a rename, or when a key-only push arrives with no raw frame.
- **Spam:** no sends, no new notifications beyond the existing `nodeUpdated` on a real name change.
- **Timers:** no new timer or cooldown.

## Tests
- `meshcoreManager.newNodeRefresh.test.ts`: the old "does NOT re-fetch for an already-known node" test encoded the bug. Now: same name → no read; new name → read, new name persisted and emitted; key-only push with no frame → read. The two new cases fail without the fix.
- All `src/server/meshcoreManager*` suites pass (116 files, 1289 tests); `tsc` clean; `lint:ci` clean.

title: fix(mqtt): refuse an mqtt_broker config the broker cannot start with
body:
## Summary
Found while testing #6510 through the API: `POST /api/sources` accepted an `mqtt_broker` with no `auth` or `gateway`. The row saved, then `MqttBrokerManager` threw on start (`getLocalNodeInfo` reads `gateway.nodeNum` of undefined). Every bridge that used it as a parent failed to start too, and status showed "Failed to fetch source status".

The dashboard form always sends these fields, so only API callers hit this.

POST and PUT now return `400 INVALID_BROKER_CONFIG` unless the config has all of the following:
- `listener.port` is an integer from 1 to 65535
- `auth.username` is non-blank and `auth.password` is non-empty
- `gateway.nodeNum` is an unsigned 32-bit integer and `gateway.nodeId` looks like `!xxxxxxxx`

PUT validates the merged config, the same one the other broker checks use. A non-admin save with the masked password is restored before the check, so it still passes.

**Not covered:** a broken row already in the database still fails on start. No such row can come from the UI.

## Mesh impact checklist
This adds save-time validation only. It sends no packets and arms no timers.

## Tests
- New `sourceRoutes.mqttBrokerCore.test.ts` (route harness): 9 refusal cases, a complete config accepted, and a PUT that drops `gateway` refused with the stored row unchanged.
- The 42 existing suites that mention `mqtt_broker` still pass (1,672 tests).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` and `lint:ci` are clean.

| Source | Rule | Badge |

| Bridge, no parent broker and no linked node | any mode except publish-only | **Monitor only** |
| Bridge, no local side | publish-only | none (nothing local to publish) |
| Bridge with parent broker or linked node | bidirectional / subscribe-only / publish-only | **Uplink + Downlink** / **Downlink** / **Uplink** |
| Broker | union of its enabled bridges' directions | **Uplink** / **Downlink** / **Uplink + Downlink**; no bridges = **Local only** |

title: fix(unread): SQLite read rows are per user (#6505)
body:
## Problem
On SQLite, `read_messages.message_id` was the table's only primary key, and every mark-read path inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Once any user read a message, every other user's mark-read for it was silently dropped, so their badge and unread divider stayed lit forever. Single-user installs never saw it. PostgreSQL and MySQL were already correct; they check `(messageId, userId)` with `NOT EXISTS`.

## Fix
- **Migration 242 (SQLite):** rebuilds `read_messages` with `PRIMARY KEY (message_id, user_id)`, using the same pattern as migration 115 (foreign keys off around a transaction, copy, drop, rename). It skips if the key is already composite and drops a leftover rebuild table from a crashed run. PG/MySQL: no-op.
- `user_id` stays nullable so old rows copy unchanged. No write path stores NULL (anonymous writes use 0).
- The Drizzle schema now declares the composite key.
- The SQLite mark-read paths return real inserts (`result.changes`), not every attempted row, which matches PG/MySQL `rowCount`.

## Testing
- New migration test: rows survive, the key is composite, the FK cascade still works, and it is idempotent, including after a leftover rebuild table.
- New repository tests on all three backends: user 2 can mark a message user 1 already read, through the channel, DM and by-id paths. With the migration disabled, the three SQLite cases fail.
- Every test file that touches `read_messages` passes with the PG and MySQL containers up (278 tests, 0 skipped).
- Ran the migration on a copy of the dev DB: all 42,408 rows kept, 43 ms, no FK violations.
- `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

## Mesh impact
None. This changes only the database; it sends no packets and starts no timers.

Closes #6505

title: feat(unread): optionally count channel replies & tapbacks on the source badge (#5254)
body:
Closes #5254.

## Departure from the issue's suggested approach

The issue proposed adding an indexed `messages.packetId` column, backfilled from the id tail. This PR skips that: **same behaviour, no backfill of the largest table.**

The parent of every counted reply was sent by the source's **own** node, so its primary key is known in full: `${sourceId}_${localNodeNum}_${replyId}`. That shape is used by outbound sends (`meshtasticManager.ts`, `v1/actions.ts`) and inbound inserts alike. In the dev DB, all own-sent channel rows match it, and no row lacks a source prefix. The query then does a primary-key lookup instead of a suffix match:

- EXPLAIN on MySQL: `eq_ref PRIMARY`. On PG: `Index Only Scan using messages_pkey`. On SQLite: `COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_messages_1`.
- Migration 241 adds `idx_messages_source_reply (sourceId, replyId)`, so the scan reads only reply rows. On a synthetic SQLite table with 500k rows (100k per source), one source takes 34 ms without the index and 13 ms with it. The existing `/unread-counts` channel query on the same data takes 67 ms.
- MySQL uses `CONCAT(?, replyId)` **without** `CAST`. A cast gives the result the connection collation at IMPLICIT strength, which fails against `messages.id` with "Illegal mix of collations". Caught by the MySQL container suite.

A `packetId` column is still a fair follow-up for the frontend code that re-parses the id tail. It is not needed here.

## What changes

- **Preference:** `user_map_preferences.unread_include_replies`, `DEFAULT FALSE` (migration 241). It is per-user and saves through `/api/user/map-preferences`, beside `unread_indicator_enabled`.
- **UI:** an **Include replies** chip sits beside **Unread DM indicator** and shows only while the indicator is on. The badge shows DMs plus replies, and its tooltip names both.
- **`GET /unread-by-source?includeReplies=true`** adds `channelReplies` per source. The gates match `/unread-counts`:
  - `messages:read` on that source, kept per the issue.
  - `channel_N:read` on **that** source, or a virtual-channel grant. `messages:read` alone counts nothing.
  - Muted channels are skipped.
  - Plain replies and tapbacks (`emoji = 1`) both count. A source's own replies don't.
- **`POST /mark-all-dms-read?includeReplies=true` now clears the same reply rows.** Both endpoints share one traversal, so the sweep and the badge can't disagree (#5197). With the option off, behaviour is unchanged.
- Fixed in review: replies are no longer dropped when a source has unread DMs but its manager can't list nodes.

## Known limits

- **Pre-existing, not new: SQLite `read_messages.message_id` is the table's only primary key.** If user A has already read a message, user B's "mark read" insert is silently ignored (`onConflictDoNothing`). This already affects DMs and channels. It can also make a reply badge survive "Mark all read" for a second user. Filed as #6505.
- Replies to messages whose ids predate the source prefix won't count. None exist in the

title: fix(lxc): meshmonitor-update never leaves the app down; memory-aware build
body:
## Summary

Makes `lxc/meshmonitor-update` safe to fail: it no longer leaves MeshMonitor stopped when an update goes wrong, it checks memory **before** stopping anything, and it builds in less memory on small containers. Docs updated to match. Shell script and docs only — no app code changes.

## Why

On a 4 GB Debian 12 LXC, going 4.17.1 → 4.18.1 left the app down twice in one evening:

1. An earlier run's `git stash pop` had conflicted on `package-lock.json` (which `npm install` rewrites), leaving it unmerged.
2. The next run stopped the services, couldn't stash ("needs merge"), and exited at `git pull` — with MeshMonitor stopped.
3. `--rollback` then ran out of Node heap: it builds with `${NODE_HEAP_CAP:-1536}`, because the RAM-based cap is only computed in pre-flight, *after* the rollback dispatch — and 1536 MB is too small for the type check.

## What changes

**Source tree — checked before anything is stopped**
- A modified or conflicted `package-lock.json` (a generated file) is reset to `HEAD`.
- Any other modified tracked file, a merge/rebase in progress, or local commits that can't fast-forward → the run refuses with the services still up and lists the files.
- No more stash/pop; the update is `git merge --ff-only origin/main`.
- `npm ci` instead of `npm install` (update and rollback): lockfile-exact, never rewrites `package-lock.json`. `.npmrc` already pins `legacy-peer-deps`, so the committed lockfile is valid for `npm ci`.

**Memory — measured, and checked before anything is stopped**

Each build step alone, peak cgroup memory, 4.18.1, 4 GB LXC with no swap:

| Step | Heap needed | Peak |
|---|---|---|
| type check `tsc` (tsconfig `noEmit`) | > 2048 MB (fails at 2048, ok at 3072) | ~3.0 GB |
| `vite build` | heap cap makes no difference (native) | ~1.2 GB |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` | 1536 MB (fails at 1024) | ~1.7 GB |

A Node heap cap can't make a step need less memory — below the need it aborts, above the machine's RAM it swaps or gets OOM-killed. So instead:
- **Budget** = `MemAvailable` + `SwapFree` + what the services free when stopped.
- ≥ ~3.3 GB → **full** build. ≥ ~1.9 GB → **lean** build: the type check is skipped (it writes no files and CI runs it on every commit, so the app is the same). Less → **refuse**, app still running, with a "add RAM or swap" message.
- Per-step heap caps (type check 3072 MB, npm and server build 1536 MB). If the type check still runs out of memory during a full build, it carries on lean instead of failing; real type errors still fail.
- `--rollback` uses the same plan (fixes the 1536 MB fallback).
- If the `build` script ever stops being `tsc && vite build`, it's run as-is (no lean mode).
- Overrides: `BUILD_MODE=full|lean`, `HEAP_TYPECHECK=<MB>`, `HEAP_SERVER=<MB>`.

**Automatic recovery**
- Between stopping and restarting the services, any failure — a `die`, a `set -e` failure, an OOM build, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, a closed SSH session (SIGHUP), a dead output pipe — runs an EXIT trap that resets

+Before it stops anything, the updater adds up the memory the build can use —
+free RAM, free swap, and what MeshMonitor gives back when it is stopped — and
+picks a build:
+
+- **About 3.3 GB or more → full build** (type check, client, server).
+- **About 1.9 GB or more → lean build**: the type check is skipped. It writes
+  no files and upstream CI runs it on every commit, so the app is the same.
+  The recommended 2 GB RAM + 1 GB swap usually gets a lean build.
+- **Less → the update refuses**, with MeshMonitor still running, and asks for
+  more RAM or swap (`pct set <ctid> --memory … --swap …`).
+
+If the type check still runs out of memory during a full build, the updater
+carries on with a lean build instead of failing. Overrides, if you know
+better:
+
+```bash
+BUILD_MODE=lean meshmonitor-update        # always skip the type check
+BUILD_MODE=full meshmonitor-update        # always run it
+HEAP_TYPECHECK=2560 meshmonitor-update    # Node heap for the type check (MB, default 3072)
+HEAP_SERVER=2048 meshmonitor-update       # Node heap for npm and the server build (MB, default 1536)
+```
 
 ## Updating
 
@@ -539,7 +574,25 @@ meshmonitor-update -n    # dry run — preview what would change
 meshmonitor-update -h    # see all options
 ```
 
-This performs a `git pull`, rebuilds the app, and restarts services in place.
+This fast-forwards the checkout to the latest `main`, rebuilds the app, and
+restarts services in place. What to expect:
+
+- **It checks before stopping anything.** If tracked files in `/opt/meshmonitor`
+  have local edits, it lists them and refuses, with MeshMonitor still running —
+  move your changes out of the checkout (e.g. `git stash`) and run it again. A
+  modified or conflicted `package-lock.json` is a generated file and is simply
+  reset. It also refuses when there isn't enough memory to build (see
+  [Update memory](#update-memory)).
+- **Dependencies are installed with `npm ci`**, exactly as `package-lock.json`
+  pins them, so the checkout stays clean for the next update.
+- **A failed update doesn't leave MeshMonitor down.** If anything fails while
+  the services are stopped — the pull, the install, the build, or a Ctrl-C or
+  dropped SSH session — the updater puts the previous version back, rebuilds
+  it, and restarts it. `/data` is not touched (the new version never started).
+  The details go to `meshmonitor-update-recovery-<time>.log` in the backup
+  folder.
+- If the new version starts but doesn't respond, use `meshmonitor-update -r`
+  (rollback from the backup taken at the start of the run).

title: feat(auth): anonymous sending only by explicit opt-in; audit v1 sends (#6499)
body:
Closes #6499.

## Why
`POST /api/messages/send` ran under `optionalAuth()`, so granting the built-in **anonymous** account a channel or messages **write** grant let visitors who aren't signed in transmit to the mesh. That's easy to do by accident while setting up a public read-only view. The MeshCore and MQTT-native send routes already require sign-in.

## Decision (maintainer)
Keep anonymous sending possible, but only by explicit opt-in.

## What changes
- **New global admin setting `allowAnonymousSend`, default OFF**, in Settings → Public instance (works with or without public-instance mode on). The toggle carries a warning: anonymous sending transmits over the radio and also needs the anonymous account's write grants.
- **Gate** (`requireAnonymousSendAllowed`, `src/server/utils/anonymousSendGate.ts`): a request with no user or the `anonymous` user gets **401 `AUTH_REQUIRED`** while the setting is off, before any parsing, node lookup, permission check or send. Signed-in users are unchanged.
- **Routes gated** — every send route that could transmit without sign-in:
  - `POST /api/messages/send` (Meshtastic channel/DM sends; also what Unified Messages posts to)
  - `POST /api/nodes/:nodeId/send-key-warning` (sends a DM)
  - Reticulum `POST /messages` and `POST /propagation/sync`
  MeshCore, MQTT-native and room routes already use `requireAuth()`; v1 routes need an API token.
- **Users tab:** the `anonymous` account shows a warning when it holds a channel/messages write grant, saying it has no effect unless anonymous sending is enabled.
- **v1 audit:** `POST /api/v1/messages` now writes the same no-text `message_sent` audit row (`via: 'v1'`) on both the single-packet (201) and split/queued (202) paths. Fire-and-forget; an audit failure never fails the response.

## ⚠️ Upgrade note
Anyone who **deliberately** gave the anonymous account write grants loses anonymous sending until an admin turns on **Allow anonymous sending**. Worth a line in the release notes.

## Not in scope (possible follow-up)
Other transmitting actions guarded only by a permission grant that the anonymous account could hold (e.g. traceroute or position/NodeInfo requests) were not swept here; this PR covers message sending, as the issue asked.

## Mesh impact
No new transmissions; this narrows who can send. `messageLimiter` stays on the send routes.

## Tests
- New `messageRoutes.anonymousSend.test.ts` (route harness): anonymous + write grant + setting off/absent → 401 and no send; setting on → send proceeds (still 403 without a grant); signed-in unchanged; gate wired on the key-warning and Reticulum routes.
- New `v1/messages.sendAudit.test.ts`: one row without text, DM destination recorded, audit failure still 201, failed send writes nothing.
- Settings persistence accepts the key; `SettingsTab.publicInstance` and `UsersTab` component tests.
- Targeted runs: 13 + 24 + 41, and a regression run over messageRoutes / nodesRoutes / reticulumRoutes / v1 messages (29 files, 382 tests)

title: fix(meshcore): auto-pathfinding claims the TX slot; Unified replies keep the parent's scope (#6500)
body:
Closes #6500. Also documents the #6498 decision.

## 1. Auto-pathfinding respects the 60 s TX floor
Auto-pathfinding (`MeshCoreManager`) sent `discover_path` / `get_neighbours` over RF without checking the per-source mesh-TX floor, so it could transmit inside another job's cooldown and jump ahead of a queued manual click (#6497).

- Each target now calls `tryClaimMeshTxSlot()` **before** sending — the same claim every other scheduler uses since #6497 (refused while a manual reservation is held or the floor is closed; stamps the floor when granted).
- A refused claim sends nothing and counts nothing; the run waits one interval and retries that target. After **3** refusals in a row it leaves the target for the next run (`AUTO_PATHFINDING_MAX_CLAIM_MISSES`). This can only delay or skip sends.
- Reconnect/generation and receive-only checks still run before every attempt. Manual discover-path / trace routes are unchanged.

## 2. Unified MeshCore replies keep the parent's scope
A MeshCore reply sent from Unified Messages (#6496) went out on the node's default scope; the per-source view copies the parent's scope.
- `/api/unified/messages` MeshCore items gain optional `scopeName` (first merged reception with one). Not position/name/key/text/timestamp; public-instance sentinel audit passes.
- The composer passes it as `scope` on a MeshCore **reply** only; plain sends and tapbacks unchanged.
- Docs: the "known limitation" note is removed.
- Not covered: the per-source view also treats a parent with `scopeCode === 0` as "reply unscoped"; Unified replies to such a parent use the node default.

## #6498 (closed as intended)
Docs now state that a channel-database read grant shows that channel under every source that heard it, with the source names — that's what makes virtual-channel-only viewers (#4116) work.

## Mesh impact
- Part 1 can only reduce or delay transmissions. No new timers.
- Part 2 changes which scope one user-initiated reply uses; no extra packets.

## Tests
- `meshcoreManager.autoPathfindingRunCancellation.test.ts`: no send while a reservation is held; no send inside the floor and the same target retried one interval later; a successful claim stamps once; gives up after 3 refusals and moves on. One existing reconnect-race test stubs the claim to true (its two runs fall inside one floor window).
- `unifiedRoutes.meshcoreMerge.test.ts` (scope present/absent), `unifiedSendRequest.test.ts` (reply includes `scope`, plain send/Meshtastic don't), `UnifiedSendComposer.test.tsx` (composer sends it).
- Targeted runs: 10 + 206 tests passed; client and server tsc clean; `lint:ci` clean.

title: feat(meshcore): manual actions queue for the next RF slot with a countdown (#6493)
body:
Closes #6493.

## Problem
On a MeshCore source every RF job shares one 60 s mesh-TX floor (`lastMeshTxAt`). Schedulers re-check every 30 s, so with automations on they usually take the slot the moment it opens, and a person clicking **Poll Status** keeps getting "Too soon since last mesh transmission; retry in Ns".

## What changes
A click during the cooldown is **queued on the server** and sent when the slot opens. The button shows **"Queued — sending in N s"** with a live countdown.

**Limits (approved by the maintainer):**
| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Max wait per request | 180 s |
| Waiting requests per source | 5 |
| Per user per source | 1 — a newer click **replaces** the older one, which ends "Replaced by your newer request" and sends nothing |
| Leaked reservation (tab gone without a clean close) | dropped 90 s after its last heartbeat |
| Order between users | first come, first served; each gets its own later slot |

Past a limit, the request answers today's 429 with a numeric `retryAfterSeconds`; the button counts down and re-enables. **It never resends on its own.**

### Covered actions
Poll Status / Poll Environment (LPP), neighbours poll, **Sync Now**, page 1 of the paged neighbours fetch. Pages 2–5 keep giving way (so one fetch doesn't block schedulers for ~5 min). The v1 `request-telemetry` waits only with `wait: true`; without it scripts keep the quick 429 they handle today.

### Server
- `ManualMeshTxQueue` per source in `MeshCoreManager` (in memory). Only the head of the queue can claim, and the floor check and stamp happen in one synchronous step, so two grants are always ≥ 60 s apart. The floor value and its persistence are unchanged.
- Schedulers (remote telemetry, neighbours, time sync, room sync) and auto-ping **skip their tick while a reservation is held**, and now claim the slot atomically **before** marking a node, so a skipped tick changes nothing.
- Routes wait through `awaitManualMeshTxSlot`: it aborts on client disconnect or socket timeout, and re-checks (client still there, nothing sent yet, source connected, not receive-only) right before claiming. A request that disconnects, is replaced or times out **sends nothing and marks nothing**.
- Socket timeouts raised on these routes (280–310 s) so a waiting request is never dropped and resent by the browser (#5494).
- New `GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/tx-queue/:requestId` (owner-only) for position and ETA. New codes: 409 `MESH_TX_SUPERSEDED`, 429 `MESH_TX_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` / `MESH_TX_QUEUE_FULL`. Success bodies unchanged except additive `waitedSecs`. Permissions unchanged.

### UI
A shared store/hook/status component on the telemetry, time-sync and neighbours-fetch panels: queued countdown, "Sending…", "Replaced by your newer request (Poll Environment (LPP))", "Replaces your queued Poll Status for YerazeMM", and a numeric-429 cooldown. The queued button is disabled; other buttons on the source stay enabled so you can replace your queued action.

## Screenshot (live, real

title: feat(unified): reply, tapback and delivery status on Unified Messages (#3045 P3)
body:
Phase 3 of 3 for #3045 (Unified Messages send; dup #4824). Closes #3045. Builds on #6492 (sender list) and #6494 (composer). Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/UNIFIED_SEND_EPIC.md`.

## What
With one channel selected, each message gets **Reply** and **React** buttons (in a bar under the card, not inside it, so they don't open the reception modal). Hidden on All Channels, signed out, in public view, and on messages that can't be answered.

### Reply
- A "Replying to …" banner above the composer; **Send from** narrows to nodes of the **same protocol** as the parent.
- **Meshtastic / MQTT:** `replyId` = the parent's wire **`packetId`** (never `requestId`), so any Meshtastic-family node can reply, even one that didn't hear the parent.
- **MeshCore:** a plain-text reply prefixed `@[Name]: ` (same as the MeshCore view); hidden when the name can't form a mention.

### Tapback
- **React** opens the existing `EmojiPickerModal` (new optional `subtitle`: "Sends from {{source}}"). Picking an emoji is the send: **one click, one packet**.
- **Meshtastic / MQTT:** `{text: emoji, replyId: packetId, emoji: 1}` through the existing send routes.
- **MeshCore:** `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/:rowId/reaction`. That route looks the parent up **in the sending source**, so only a MeshCore node that holds a row ref for the message *and* has reactions outbound on is selectable; others show greyed out ("did not hear this message" / "reactions are turned off"). MeshCore emoji filtering reuses `reactionEmojiOptions` / `isReactionEmoji`.

### Delivery status
Meshtastic/MQTT messages you sent show `MessageStatusIndicator` next to the time (pending / transmitted / received / failed / timed out). MeshCore shows none here.

### Server (small)
- `/api/unified/senders` refs gain `reactionsOutbound` (MeshCore only; a settings read).
- `/api/unified/messages` Meshtastic items gain `deliveryState`, `ackFailed`, `routingErrorReceived` from our own sent row (with the merge-upgrade when another source's copy arrives first). Not position/name/key/text/timestamp; public-instance sentinel audit passes.

## Screenshots (live, dev container, gauntlet)
![Reply banner and row actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/unified-send-p3/docs/public/images/features/unified-send-reply.png)

![Tapback picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feature/unified-send-p3/docs/public/images/features/unified-send-react.png)

## Live validation (with the user's OK, gauntlet only)
Auto-ack on Sandbox and MeshCore telemetry polling were paused first (every automation was already off) and restored afterwards; a 60 s watch after connecting showed no mesh traffic we didn't cause. Then, one click each:

| Protocol | Action | Result |

| Meshtastic (Sandbox) | reply on gauntlet | delivered; ↳ quote and ✓ status shown |
| Meshtastic (Sandbox) | 👍 tapback | delivered; pill shown |
| MeshCore (MC-Sandbox) | 👍 reaction | 200; pill shown |

title: chore(i18n): machine-translated top-up for fr, ru and zh_Hans
body:
French, Russian and Simplified Chinese had slipped to or under the 50% readiness threshold that `src/config/i18nLanguageCoverage.test.ts` tracks (new English strings, most recently the Unified send composer in #6494). This fills enough of the gaps to bring each back to **53%**.

> **Machine-translated.** All strings in this PR were translated by Claude, not by a human translator. Weblate translators: please review them. They will show in Weblate as translated, because i18next JSON has no "needs review" flag.

## What changed

| Language | Strings filled | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| fr | 266 | 50.0% → 53.0% |
| ru | 518 | 47.1% → 53.0% |
| zh_Hans | 300 | 49.6% → 53.0% |

body:
Phase 2 of 3 for #3045 (Unified Messages send; dup #4824). Builds on #6492 (`GET /api/unified/senders`). Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/UNIFIED_SEND_EPIC.md`.

## What
A send box under the Unified Messages feed, for one explicit channel.

- **Where it shows:** a single channel only. Hidden on **All Channels** (no "send everywhere"), for anonymous viewers, and in public-instance view.
- **Send from** picker, always visible:
  - nodes that can send now are selectable;
  - nodes you may use but that can't send right now (not connected, transmit off, MQTT send off, …) are greyed out with the reason;
  - nodes you have no permission for are not listed;
  - each source is listed once.
  - If every node is greyed out, the box is shown disabled and the picker reads "No sender available". If no node is even a candidate, nothing renders.
- **Default node per channel, per browser** (localStorage, like #5792). Only a manual pick is stored. If the stored node can no longer send, it falls back to the first eligible node and shows a notice naming the new one.
- **Sends through the existing per-source routes** with the ref's own channel number (never a number from anywhere else):
  - Meshtastic → `POST /api/messages/send` `{ sourceId, text, channel }`
  - MQTT native → `POST /api/sources/:id/mqtt/native/send` `{ text, channel }`
  - MeshCore → `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/send` `{ text, channelIdx }` (no scope / senderName, same as a plain send in the MeshCore view)
- **Reuses `MessageComposeInput`** (byte counter, emoji). Byte cap per kind: 200 for Meshtastic/MQTT, `meshcoreChannelMaxBytes(nodeName)` for MeshCore (worst case if the node name can't be read). Newlines off for MeshCore.
- **Drafts:** one draft store per channel, so text never crosses channels; a channel switch remounts the composer.
- **Errors keep the draft** and show inline: rate limited ("try again in Ns" from `retryAfterSeconds`), transmit off, not connected, forbidden, or the server's message. Every error except 429 refetches the sender list (a read).
- `@` mentions aren't offered yet (the page has no node list). Replies and tapbacks are Phase 3.

LongFast on the dev container with every radio disconnected (no-transmit state), so the picker reads "No sender available" and the box is disabled:

- **One click = at most one POST, to the one node shown**, on that node's channel. No fan-out to other sources sharing the channel name.

title: feat(unified): send groundwork — rate limit, send audit, sender list (#3045 P1)
body:
Phase 1 of 3 for #3045 (Unified Messages send; dup #4824). Server only, no UI. Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/UNIFIED_SEND_EPIC.md`.

## What

### 1. Rate limit on Meshtastic send
- `POST /api/messages/send` now runs behind `messageLimiter` (`RATE_LIMIT_MESSAGES`, 30/min in production, per IP, one bucket shared with the MeshCore, MQTT-native and v1 send routes).
- **This also caps the existing Meshtastic Channels and DM tabs.** Before, that route had only the global `/api` limiter.
- The 429 body gains `code: 'RATE_LIMITED'` and `retryAfterSeconds` (plus a `Retry-After` header). Existing fields are unchanged. The Meshtastic tabs call this route with `authFetch`, so for now they show their generic send error on a 429; Phase 2 handles it in the new composer.

### 2. Send audit rows
Fire-and-forget rows on **successful** sends only. **No message text and no length.** An audit failure never fails or delays the response (the radio already transmitted).

| Route | Action |
|-------|--------|
| `POST /api/messages/send` | `message_sent` |
| `POST /api/sources/:id/mqtt/native/send` | `mqtt_native_message_sent` |
| `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/send` (plain) | `meshcore_message_sent` |
| `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/rooms/post` | `meshcore_room_post_sent` |

Details JSON: source, channel or DM target, reply id, tapback flag. MeshCore sent-as / resend / reaction keep their existing rows (no doubles). Rows show in the existing Audit Log tab.

### 3. `GET /api/unified/senders`
For each unified channel, which sources the viewer may send from right now, and why not:
`{ success, data: { channels: [{ name, sources: [{ sourceId, sourceName, channelNumber, canSend, sendKind, sendBlockedReason }] }] } }`

Checks, first failure wins: visibility gate → source kind → slot rule → **per-source** permission → live state.
- **Slot rule (the hazard this phase exists for):** `/api/unified/channels` lists every virtual channel (`100 + id`) under every source. Meshtastic `/send` would put that on slot 0 (Primary) and MeshCore would put it on another slot. The list never offers a virtual channel through a Meshtastic TCP or MeshCore source, and never a physical slot through MQTT native.
- **Permissions** are always looked up for the ref's own source (`getUserPermissionSetAsync(userId, sourceId)`), never across sources. Meshtastic needs `channel_N:write`, MeshCore `messages:write`, MQTT native `messages:write` + channel-database read.
- **Live state:** not connected, TX disabled / receive-only, MeshCore repeater, MQTT-native preconditions (the same `prepareMqttNativeSend` the send path runs, extracted so the two can't drift).
- Anonymous viewers get an empty list before any manager or permission work.
- `/api/unified/channels` output is unchanged (same grouping, now shared via `buildUnifiedChannelGroups`).
- `unifiedSendEligibility.ts` is added to the MQTT-native send guard's allowlist. It runs the precondition and channel check only and never transmits.

+# Unified Messages Send — Epic (#3045, dup #4824)
+
+**Goal:** send channel messages, replies and tapbacks from the Unified Messages page
+(`src/pages/UnifiedMessagesPage.tsx`) through one chosen source per send, with the
+existing per-source permissions, a rate limit and an audit trail.
+
+## Decisions (user, 2026-11-18 — final)
+
+| Topic | Decision |
+|-------|----------|
+| Fan-out | **One source per send.** The composer always names exactly one sending node. No multi-source send, no confirm dialog. |
+| Rate limit | Add `messageLimiter` (`RATE_LIMIT_MESSAGES`, 30/min prod) to Meshtastic `POST /api/messages/send`. This also caps the existing Meshtastic Channels/DM tabs; say so in the PR. |
+| Audit | Every send writes an audit row: user, time, source, channel (or DM target), reply/tapback flag. **No message text** (matches `auditMeshcoreEvent`). Read through the existing audit log. |
+| Default node per channel | Per browser (localStorage), like `unifiedChannelPreference.ts` (#5792). |
+| Roles table in #3045 | Maps onto existing per-source permissions: Meshtastic channel send = `channel_N:write` on that source; MeshCore = `messages:write`; MQTT native = `messages:write` + channel-database `canRead`. Never `anySource` for a send. |
+| Out of scope | Sending on the **All Channels** view (needs one explicit channel); **DMs** from Unified; **Reticulum** (no channels). |
+
+## Architecture
+
+No new server send path. The Unified composer calls the existing per-source routes and always passes the source id:
+
+| Source type | Route | Channel argument |
+|-------------|-------|------------------|
+| Meshtastic TCP | `POST /api/messages/send` `{sourceId, text, channel, replyId?, emoji?}` | physical slot 0–7 only |
+| MQTT native | `POST /api/sources/:id/mqtt/native/send` | virtual channel (`>= CHANNEL_DB_OFFSET`) only; native send must be enabled |
+| MeshCore | `POST /api/sources/:id/meshcore/messages/send` `{text, channelIdx}` | physical MeshCore channel idx |
+
+Hazards found in orientation:
+1. `/api/unified/channels` lists every virtual channel (`100 + id`) under **every** source. Meshtastic `/send` clamps a channel above 7 to 0 (sends on Primary); MeshCore accepts 0–255 (sends on another slot). A source ref is a valid sender only for a real slot of its type, or (MQTT native) a virtual channel with native send on.
+2. Sender eligibility must be computed server-side per source ref (permission + connected + TX enabled / not receive-only / MQTT native on). `/api/unified/sources-status` has no permission filter and no TX state.
+3. Meshtastic `replyId` / tapback is the wire packet id, so it works from any Meshtastic source. MeshCore reactions look the parent row up in the sending source, so only a source whose `mc:<sourceId>:<rowId>` is in the item's `meshcoreRowRefs` can react. A MeshCore reply is a plain `@[Name]: ` text prefix and works from any MeshCore source.
+
+## Mesh impact
+
+- Airtime: one send = one transmission from one node (× hops). No timers, no fan-out.
+- Spam: covered by `messageLimiter` (now on every channel-send route used here); no automation trigger added.
+- Timers: none.
+
+## Phases
+
+- [x] **P1 — Server.** `messageLimiter` on `/api/messages/send`; send audit rows (Meshtastic, MQTT native, MeshCore; no text); a permission-filtered per-source-ref sender list (`canSend` + reason) for Unified, with route-harness tests.
+  *Exit:* routes tested with `createRouteTestApp`; virtual/physical slot rules enforced in the sender list; CI green; merged.
+- [ ] **P2 — Composer.** `MessageComposeInput` on Unified for one explicit channel; node picker limited to eligible senders; per-browser default node per channel; byte limit per source type; hidden/disabled on All Channels. Docs + screenshot.
+  *Exit:* live-validated on the dev container (no transmit unless the user OKs reconnecting radios; `gauntlet` only); merged.
+- [ ] **P3 — Replies, tapbacks, status.** Reply and tapback from Unified rows (rules in hazard 3); delivery status where the sent row already tracks it. Docs + screenshot.
+  *Exit:* live-validated; merged.
+
+## Phase 1 result (server)
+
+- `messageLimiter` on `POST /api/messages/send`; its 429 now carries `code: 'RATE_LIMITED'` and `retryAfterSeconds`. The bucket is per IP and shared with the MeshCore, MQTT-native and v1 send routes. The existing Meshtastic tabs show their generic send error on a 429 until P2 handles it.
+- Audit rows (no text, no length), successful sends only: `message_sent` (Meshtastic), `mqtt_native_message_sent`, `meshcore_message_sent`, `meshcore_room_post_sent`. MeshCore sent-as / resend / reaction keep their existing rows.
+- `GET /api/unified/senders` → `{ success, data: { channels: [{ name, sources: [{ sourceId, sourceName, channelNumber, canSend, sendKind, sendBlockedReason }] }] } }`. Anonymous viewers get `[]`. Built from `buildUnifiedChannelGroups` (`src/server/services/unifiedChannelGroups.ts`, shared with `/channels`) and `resolveUnifiedSenders` (`src/server/services/unifiedSendEligibility.ts`). Check order: visibility gate → source kind → slot rule → per-source permission → live state. `sendKind` is non-null only once permission passed.
+- `prepareMqttNativeSend` is the one MQTT-native precondition for both the send path and the list; `unifiedSendEligibility.ts` is on the `mqttNativeSendService` guard allowlist (it never transmits).
+- Deviation: `loadEnabledVirtualChannels()` returns Meshtastic-protocol channel-database rows only, so MeshCore-protocol rows never appear in the sender list.
+- Found, not fixed (follow-ups): `/api/unified/channels` lists each virtual channel under every source with no read check on that source (source names visible to a channel-database-only reader); `POST /api/v1/messages` writes no audit row; `/api/messages/send` still clamps channel > 7 to 0; it uses `optionalAuth`, so an anonymous account granted write can send; `parseDestinationNum` runs before the permission check.
+

+

title: feat(notifications): mute except @mentions for MeshCore channels and rooms (#6490)
body:
Closes #6490.

## What
A muted MeshCore channel or room can now still alert on `@[YourNode]` mentions. The mute menu gains a **Still alert on @mentions** checkbox. Tick it, then pick a duration. Ticking it on an existing mute updates that mute and keeps its expiry.

This reverses the P11 Q3 default ("a mute wins over a mention") as an opt-in only. Plain mutes behave as before.

## How
- **Data:** optional `allowMentions: boolean` on each `mutedChannels` / `mutedDMs` rule. The rules are JSON in the existing preference columns, so **no migration**. Old rules read as `false`.
- **Server:** `NotificationMuteVenue` gets `isMention`. `isVenueMuted()` lets a mention venue past a rule with `allowMentions`. Only `meshcoreMentionNotificationService` sets `isMention`, so plain message alerts stay muted. Push, Apprise and desktop services need no change: `muteVenue` already rides the payload into `payloadBlockedForUserAsync`.
- **Dedup:** the mention runs before the message notifier and claims the shared dedup key only after the mute filter passes, so a user with mute + `allowMentions` gets exactly one alert (tested).
- **Route:** `POST /api/push/preferences` rejects a non-boolean `allowMentions` (`fail(…, 'INVALID_MUTE_RULE')`).
- **UI:** `MuteMenu` gets `mentionOption` / `allowMentions` / `onAllowMentionsChange`. Shown on **MeshCore Channels and Rooms only**, the venues the mention service covers. Not shown on Meshtastic channels or any DM view, where it would do nothing. Muted venues keep hiding unread dots and sounds, which the reporter asked for. The bell title reads "Muted except @mentions" when set.

## Scope notes
- Needs **Mentions** turned on for the source. Docs say so.
- MeshCore DMs are not mention venues, so no option there.

## Screenshot
MeshCore channel muted with **Still alert on @mentions** ticked, after reload (bell title reads "Muted except @mentions — click to change"). Verified live on the dev container: tick + 1 hour saves `allowMentions: true`; untick while muted keeps the same `muteUntil`. Rooms not driven live (no room server on the dev sources); covered by unit tests.

![Mute except mentions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/6490-mute-except-mentions/docs/public/images/features/6490-mute-except-mentions.png)

## Mesh impact
- Airtime: none, nothing is transmitted.
- Spam: mentions keep the existing persisted 5-minute per-sender cooldown (`meshcoreMentionNotifyState`). No new timer, so a save or restart resets nothing.

## Tests
- `isVenueMuted` unit tests: plain mute, `allowMentions` mute, expired rule.
- Notifier tests: muted-except-mentions channel alerts once for a mention and not for a plain message; same for a room.
- Route harness test: `allowMentions` survives save, a later partial save, and GET; non-boolean rejected.
- `MuteMenu` tests: checkbox hidden by default, choice passed with duration, applied immediately while muted.
- Targeted run: 8 files, 163 tests passed. tsc client + server clean. `lin

title: feat(meshcore): Auto Resend until the required repeaters hear it (#6240)
body:
Closes #6240.

## What

A new per-source toggle under **Settings → Required repeaters**: **Auto Resend until the required repeaters hear it**. It is off by default and disabled while the Required Repeater(s) list is empty. When on, MeshMonitor resends this source's own messages on the server until the ANY/ALL rule is met, so the reporter no longer has to keep clicking **Resend** when one of the three repeaters on a shared tower misses a message.

![Auto Resend toggle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/meshcore-auto-resend-6240/docs/public/images/features/6240-auto-resend-on.png)

*(Component rendered in jsdom with the app's MeshCore and settings CSS, not the full app shell.)*

## How

- **Scope:** every own send on the source, including channel messages, DMs, automated sends and sender-name raw sends (decided with the maintainer). Reactions and room posts are excluded.
- **One gate:** each attempt calls `resendChannelMessage(id, { auto: true })`, so Auto Resend shares every manual Resend limit and refusal:
  - 30 s cooldown after the send and after each resend;
  - **3 resends per message**, manual and auto counted together;
  - 1 h max age;
  - refused once the rule is met, a DM is acknowledged, or a #3979 retry is pending.

  The count is persisted: auto resends write `retry` events with `auto: true`, and `summarizeResends` counts them.
- **When it re-arms:** only on a wait — `RESEND_COOLDOWN`, `AUTO_RETRY_PENDING`, or a DM still in its ack-retry cascade. Any other refusal or error (send failed, receive-only, disconnected) ends Auto Resend for that message, so a failing radio cannot loop.
- **Settings read at fire time:** the toggle and the list are read when each timer fires, so turning the toggle off or emptying the list stops pending resends.
- **#3979 overlap:** while Auto Resend is active, the one-shot channel retry is not armed, so the total stays at 1 + 3.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:**
   - At most 3 extra floods per message, 30 s apart. Opt-in, per source.
   - Each copy reuses the original wire timestamp and text. A repeater that already relayed the message drops the copy by payload hash, so in practice only a repeater that missed it rebroadcasts.
   - The UI warns next to the toggle that each resend is another flood.
2. **Spam:**
   - A resend creates no new message row and emits no `message` event. It never reaches the data bus, so it fires no automation, notification or Virtual Node relay.
   - **Safety stop:** if a message uses all 3 resends and the rule is still unmet one echo window later, Auto Resend pauses for that channel or DM contact for 1 hour and logs a warning. title: fix(time-sync): an interval-only save no longer turns Time Sync off
body:
## Problem

`POST /api/settings/time-sync-nodes` called `setTimeSyncInterval(enabled ? interval : 0)`. A request that sent `intervalMinutes` without `enabled` read the missing flag as false and passed 0. That stopped the scheduler, though the stored setting still said Time Sync was on. The UI showed it enabled; nothing ran until the next reconnect.

## Fix

The route reads the saved settings back (per-source, global fallback) after writing them, and applies the stored `enabled` and interval whenever either field was sent. A save of only the node filter or expiration still leaves the scheduler alone.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** no change to the configured rate; Time Sync now keeps running when the user meant it to.
2. **Spam:** none.
3. **Save resets timer:** the setter's unchanged-interval guard (#6483) applies; this PR only fixes which values reach it.

## Tests

Two route tests in `sourceScopedAccess.scope.test.ts`, with the settings writes reaching the real test DB:
- an interval-only save keeps Time Sync on (fails on `main`, passes here);
- an enabled-only save uses the stored interval, disabling passes 0, and a filter-only save does not touch the scheduler (regression guard; passes on both).

`sourceScopedAccess.scope.test.ts` 359 passed, `settingsRoutes.test.ts` 140 passed.

title: fix(localstats): stop leaking the local LocalStats first-request timer
body:
## Problem

`startLocalStatsScheduler` arms a 30-second "first request" `setTimeout` and never kept the handle. Each settings save or reconnect that restarted the scheduler added one more LocalStats request, and a disconnect did not cancel the pending one.

## Fix

- Track the timer in `localStatsFirstRequestTimeout` and clear it in `stopLocalStatsScheduler()`, which `startLocalStatsScheduler()` now calls first.
- `setLocalStatsInterval` returns early when the interval is unchanged and the scheduler is armed, so an unrelated save does not restart collection.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** none. LocalStats goes to the local radio over TCP, not over the air. The fix removes the extra requests.
2. **Spam:** none.
3. **Save resets timer:** a save with the same interval no longer restarts the collection cycle.

## Tests

`src/server/meshtasticManager.localStatsTimerLeak.test.ts` (3 tests). All 3 fail on `main` and pass here. Related suites (applyManagerSettings, settingsRoutes, remoteLocalStats*): 172 passed.

title: fix(schedulers): saves no longer re-time remote admin scan, time sync and key repair
body:
## Problem

The remote admin scanner, Auto Time Sync and Auto Key Repair each run on a plain `setInterval` that does not send at start. Every restart begins a fresh full interval, and a settings save restarted all three, even when the timing had not changed. Each save pushed the next run back by a full interval. A user who saved settings often enough would stop the run altogether.

The scanner and time sync starts also `await` the database before they arm the timer. Two starts close together could each arm a timer, and nothing cleared the first one.

## Fix

- `setRemoteAdminScannerInterval` and `setTimeSyncInterval` return early when the interval is unchanged and the timer is armed (same guard as #6479 / #6482).
- `setKeyRepairSettings` restarts only when `enabled` or the interval changed, or when it should run but has no timer. A max-exchanges or purge change no longer re-times it.
- A generation counter drops a start whose DB read was overtaken by a newer start or stop. New `stopRemoteAdminScanner()` / `stopTimeSyncScheduler()` replace the inline clears in `disconnect()` and `userDisconnect()`.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** no new sends. A save can no longer delay a run; runs still never come sooner than one interval after a (re)start.
2. **Spam:** none; the fix removes duplicate timers.
3. **Save resets timer:** this PR is the fix. I did not add a persisted last-run time like #6479: these schedulers never send at start, so a restart can only delay them, not send early. A persisted time would help only a source that reconnects more often than its interval.

## Tests

`src/server/meshtasticManager.schedulerSaveRetime.test.ts` (8 tests). The 5 bug tests fail on `main` and pass here; the 3 sanity tests (new interval restarts, disable stops) pass on both. Related suites (applyManagerSettings, settingsRoutes, sourceScopedAccess.scope, node-identity-guards, meshcoreTimeSyncScheduler): 562 passed.

title: fix(localstats): saves and restarts keep the Auto Remote LocalStats interval
body:
## Summary
Auto Remote LocalStats had the save-rearm bug that #6479 fixed for Auto Traceroute. Every save of the section, every reconnect and every restart re-armed the scheduler, which sent the next over-the-air telemetry request within 0–5 minutes. The last send time lived only in memory.

This PR applies the #6479 fix:

- **Persisted last send.** Each source's last request time is stored as `remoteLocalStatsLastSentAt`. The key is server-managed and can't be posted by clients.
- **A restart is not a trigger.** A scheduler (re)start waits for whichever is later: the startup jitter, or last send + interval. A generation counter drops a start that a newer start or a stop overtook, so there are no double timers and nothing is armed after a disconnect.
- **Filter-only saves change nothing.** `setRemoteLocalStatsInterval()` skips the restart when the interval is unchanged and the scheduler is armed.
- **The interval route saves its value.** `POST /settings/remote-localstats-interval` now writes the per-source `remoteLocalStatsIntervalMinutes`, so the value survives a restart. It also requires a whole number from 0 to 1440; the UI input is already integer-only.

## Mesh impact
1. **Airtime:** this only removes sends. Before, each save, reconnect or restart could add one telemetry request (a unicast with hop limit = hops away + 2). Now requests stay at one per interval per source.
2. **Spam:** none added.
3. **Save resets a timer:** this is the bug being fixed. Last-fire is persisted, and the tests cover a restart with a recent send, saves with the same and a new interval, a reconnect, and per-source isolation.

## Tests
- New `meshtasticManager.remoteLocalStatsLastSent.test.ts`: 8 cases. All 8 fail on `main` and pass here.
- `sourceScopedAccess.scope.test.ts`: the route saves for the named source only; fractional and out-of-range values return 400 and save nothing.
- `settings.allowlist.test.ts`: the new key is server-managed.
- Existing `remoteLocalStatsScheduler.txDisabled`, `tracerouteLastSent` and `applyManagerSettings` suites pass. `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.

## Docs
`automation-upkeep.md#auto-remote-localstats` explains that saves and restarts keep the interval.

title: test(public-instance): stop the sentinel audit flagging random tokens
body:
## Summary
`publicInstance.sentinelAudit` failed at random on #6478. The failing check was:

```
/csrf-token | geometry | geom:altMT | $.csrfToken
```

The audit plants the altitude `2741` and flags any response that contains those digits. `/csrf-token` returns 64 random hex characters, which can hold `2741` (or `2743`, the MeshCore altitude) by chance. It is rare, but the audit fetches the route in several variants on every PR, so it happens. Session cookies and ETags carry the same risk.

The scanners now skip the **values** of:
- the `csrfToken` JSON key
- the `set-cookie` and `etag` headers

These values are random per request and can't carry seeded data. Their names are still scanned, and so is every other field.

## Tests
- New `publicInstanceAudit.test.ts`: a token holding the sentinel passes, the same digits in any other field or header still fail.
- `publicInstance.sentinelAudit.test.ts` passes.
- `tsc` and `lint:ci` clean.

title: fix(traceroute): saves and restarts keep the Auto Traceroute interval
body:
## Summary

Saving the Auto Traceroute section, reconnecting to the node, or restarting MeshMonitor could send auto traceroutes more often than the configured interval. This PR stores each source's last auto-traceroute time, so a save, reconnect or restart never sends one sooner than **last send + interval**.

### The bug, as found in the code

- `AutoTracerouteSection` saves via a per-source `POST /api/settings` (that branch does **not** re-arm), then calls `onIntervalChange(interval)` on **every** save, filter-only saves included. That goes to `POST /api/settings/traceroute-interval`, which called `setTracerouteInterval()` and re-armed the scheduler.
- Every (re)start cleared the timer and scheduled the first run after a random 0–5 min delay (or the interval, if shorter).
- The last send time lived only in memory, behind a 30 s guard. Saves more than 30 s apart, every reconnect (`configComplete` restarts the scheduler) and every process restart each sent a fresh traceroute within 0–5 min.
- `POST /settings/traceroute-interval` re-armed the timer but never saved the value. A `POST /api/settings` with no `sourceId` wrote the global row, which `applyManagerSettings` does not read for a source.

### Changes

1. **Persisted last send:** a per-source `autoTracerouteLastSentAt` (epoch ms), written each time an auto traceroute actually goes out. Skips for TX off, the schedule window, the airtime gate or no target do not count. It is server-managed: listed in `PER_SOURCE_SETTINGS_KEYS` and `PER_SOURCE_KEYS_NOT_POSTABLE`, and not in `VALID_SETTINGS_KEYS`, so the client cannot clear it. This copies `remoteLocalStatsRetryState` / `reticulumLastAnnounceAt`.
2. **Restart rule:** first run = `max(startup jitter, lastSent + interval)`, where `lastSent = max(in-memory, persisted)`, capped at one interval so a future timestamp (clock moved back) cannot stall the scheduler. With nothing persisted, the old 0–5 min jitter still applies. A generation counter drops a start that a newer start, or a stop (disconnect), overtook while it read the DB.
3. **No-op saves:** `setTracerouteInterval()` returns early when the interval is unchanged and the scheduler is armed. A new interval reschedules from the last send.
4. **`POST /settings/traceroute-interval` now saves** the value as the resolved source's `tracerouteIntervalMinutes` (global row only if no source resolves), so it survives a restart.
5. **Recent-traceroutes list sizing** (`/api/traceroutes/recent`, `/api/poll`) reads the per-source interval. With no source named it still reads the global row, as before. There is no single interval across sources, so the cross-source list keeps its old sizing.
6. **Interval bounds:** one normalizer, `normalizeTracerouteIntervalMinutes`, used by the setter, the route and `applyManagerSettings`. A stored 1 or 2 used to be applied at startup (`applyManagerSettings` accepted 0–60). The setter and startup now raise 1–2 to 3. The route rejects 1–2 (and fractions) with `400 INVALID_INT

title: feat(scripts): Script Secrets store for user-script API keys
body:
## Summary

Adds **Script Secrets**: admins store API keys and similar values in **Settings › Scripts › Script Secrets**, and every user script receives each one as an environment variable of the same name. The INJ-01 filter strips container variables named like secrets (`*API_KEY*`, `*TOKEN*`, …), so until now a script had no supported way to get an API key.

> [!WARNING]
> **Every script receives every secret (a deliberate global scope).** Any script uploaded to MeshMonitor can read every stored value, print it, send it over the mesh, or send it to any web server. Users with `automation:write` can point a trigger at an existing script and so make it use the secrets, even though they cannot see or change them. The panel shows this warning permanently, and the docs repeat it.

## Design

- **Storage:** new global table `script_secrets` (migration **240**; `name` PK, `encryptedValue`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`) on all three backends. Values are AES-256-GCM envelopes `{v,kid,iv,ct,tag}` keyed by HKDF(SESSION_SECRET), with new info strings `script-secrets-aead-v1` / `script-secrets-fingerprint-v1`. This follows `meshcoreCredentialStore.ts`.
- **SESSION_SECRET required:** without an explicit `SESSION_SECRET`, writes return `409 SESSION_SECRET_REQUIRED` and the panel is disabled with the reason. Deletes still work.
- **Write only, admin only:** `GET /api/script-secrets` returns `{canStore, reason?, secrets:[{name, updatedAt, status}]}`, `PUT /api/script-secrets/:name {value}` returns `{name, updatedAt, created}`, and `DELETE` returns `{success}`. No route returns a value. All three use `requireAdmin()` and the `ok`/`fail` envelope. The router mounts at `/script-secrets`, not under `/scripts`, because Express matches paths case-insensitively and that would collide with `/scripts/:filename/source`.
- **Audit:** `script_secret_created` / `_updated` / `_deleted` rows hold `{name}` only.
- **Validation:** names match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$`. Values are 1–4096 chars with no NUL. At most 50 secrets.
  - Codes: `INVALID_SECRET_NAME`, `RESERVED_SECRET_NAME`, `INVALID_SECRET_VALUE`, `TOO_MANY_SECRETS`.
- **Injection:** `buildScriptChildEnv` builds `sanitize(env) → + secrets → + dep paths → PYTHONSAFEPATH=1`.
  - A secret is added only if its name is valid and not reserved, the caller or process did not already set that name, and the value has no NUL.
  - Names that merely *look* secret (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) are allowed, since that is the point of the feature.
  - `sanitizeScriptEnv`, which the dependency installer uses, never gets secrets.
- **Reserved names:**
  - Process basics and interpreter/loader controls: `PATH`, `HOME`, `IFS`, `BASH_ENV` and similar, plus the prefixes `LD_`, `DYLD_`, `PYTHON`, `NODE_`, `NPM_CONFIG_`, `LC_`.
  - The deny filter's exact names and prefixes (`SESSION_SECRET`, `DATABASE_*`, `OIDC_*`, …).
  - Every variable the script callers set: `MESSAGE`, `CHANNEL`, `ROUTE`, `SCOPE`, …, plus the prefixes `PARAM_`, `MSG_`, `FROM_`, `MESHCORE_

(5) the `translation_cache` table (issue #5520) — one row per hashed (text, language) pair, shared so a phrase is translated once; it stores no text and no message reference, and no route reads it. The links from a message to an entry (`message_translations`) ARE per-source, and every read goes through the message-list visibility check. See `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSLATION_CACHE_SPEC.md`. (6) the `cross_source_links` table (issue #5561, map "heard here" edges) — an hourly aggregate of "source A's radio was heard by source B", so each row names **two** sources (`txSourceId`, `rxSourceId`) and has no single `sourceId`. **Two-source read rule:** a row, and anything derived from it, is shown only when the viewer can read BOTH sources (admins see all); never reveal "another source" to someone who can read only one. `CrossSourceLinksRepository.getLinks` takes the permitted source list and requires both ends in it, and the route drops any edge whose endpoint position fails `buildPositionFilter` / `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`. All classification goes through `src/server/services/crossSourceCorrelation.ts` (#5559/#5560 use the same rule read-side). Source deletion and purge remove rows on either end. (7) the `automation_fire_state` table (migration 219) — each automation's persisted cooldown / rate-limit state, so a restart or a save never re-arms a rule; global like the `automations` table it belongs to, keyed by `automationId` plus the engine's cooldown `scopeKey`. Deleting an automation deletes its rows. (8) the `script_secrets` table (migration 240) — admin-stored values (API keys) that **every** user script on **every** source receives as environment variables; a user decision, stated in the UI and docs. Values are AES-256-GCM envelopes keyed from SESSION_SECRET (`scriptSecretStore.ts`), decrypted into an in-memory snapshot that `buildScriptChildEnv` adds after the INJ-01 deny filter; no API returns a value. Adding a new per-source data type should still get a `sourceId` column unless you have a concrete cross-source-by-design reason like decryption.
 - **`meshcore_trace_runs` (migration 225, #6276) is per-source.** An attempt log of the MeshCore traces a source sent (target, path, origin, answered/timeout/failed), written by `MeshCoreManager.traceContactPathDetailed` (the manager picks the tag and passes it to the backend) and read by the Traceroute Explorer, which joins it to `meshcore_hop_snr` by `(sourceId, traceTag, authCode)`. Source deletion purges it; retention follows `HOP_SNR_RETENTION_MS` (90 d); `pending` rows from before startup are swept to `timeout`.
 - **Permissions are per-source.** `permissions.sourceId` was added in migration 022, refined in 033. `requirePermission(resource, action, { sourceIdFrom })` checks the named source; **without `sourceIdFrom` a per-source resource passes on a grant for ANY source**, so never omit it on a route that acts on a `sourceId` from the request. Meshtastic device routes that fall back to the primary source use `requireDeviceSourcePermission()` + `getDeviceSourceTarget(req)` (`src/server/utils/deviceSourcePermission.ts`), which resolve the source once for both the check and the action.
 - **Frontend uses `SourceContext`** (`src/contexts/SourceContext.tsx`). `useSource()` returns `{ sourceId, sourceName }`; `sourceId` is `null` outside a `SourceProvider` (legacy/single-source views).

title: feat(automation): Automation Engine honors the per-source airtime cutoff
body:
## Summary

Automation Engine rules now honor the per-source **Cutoff Airtime Utilization Threshold**. Before this change, only the built-in automations paused. Engine rules kept sending on a busy channel, though `AUTOMATION_ENGINE_PLAN.md` said they would pause.

- `MeshtasticManager.getAirtimeGateVerdict()` returns one verdict with its figures: `{ gated, channelUtilization, threshold, measuredFrom }`. `isAutomationAirtimeGated()` now calls it, so the legacy timers, the status banner and the Engine all use the same check.
- `NodeDataProvider.getAirtimeGate(sourceId)` is a new optional hook. `meshNodeData.ts` implements it through the registry and `isMeshtasticManager`. Any other source, a missing manager or a throw returns `null`, and the action sends (fails open). The simulator passes the hook through read-only.
- In `actionExecutor.ts`, `pushOrSkipMesh` checks the gate per target, right before the dep call. Checks run in this order: empty-send rule → protocol skips → target resolution → airtime gate → dep → TX_DISABLED.
  - **Gated:** sendMessage (every target and channel), tapback, requestData (every op), broadcastWaypoint, tracePathSchedule, and deviceReboot with a remote `targetNodeNum`. broadcastWaypoint and tracePathSchedule check before the dep, so a skip does not stamp the 30-minute floor or consume the trace's due slot.
  - **Not gated:** local reboot, nodeManage, notify, runScript, setAutomationEnabled, setSourceForwardingEnabled, delay, nothing, setVar.
- A skip records `{ skipped, airtimeCutoff, sourceId, channelUtilization, threshold, reason }`. `actionStepDetail` copies only those fields into the run log, so the dry-run `text` never lands there. A multi-source action logs either an all-skipped row (`sourceIds`) or a `partial` row (`airtimeSkipped`).
- In `automationEngineService.ts`, every non-manual dispatch site goes through `stampAndFire`. When every counting action was airtime-skipped, it refunds the cooldown and rate-limit stamp in memory and in `automation_fire_state`. `nothing` and `delay` don't count. The refund touches the cooldown key only if it still holds this fire's timestamp, restoring the previous stamp or deleting the key, and it removes exactly one rate event.
- Run-log throttle: while a rule's runs are all-skipped, it writes at most one `automation_runs` row per rule per 10 minutes. The live trace still shows every run.
- **Run now** bypasses the cutoff. Its run log gains an `airtime:bypassed` step with the figures.
- UI: StepList labels a full skip "paused: airtime over cutoff" and a partial one "partly sent". The Test panel headline says "would be skipped now on <src>: airtime X% > Y%" and still shows the rendered text.
- Docs: `automation.md#airtime-cutoff` (which used to say the Engine is not covered), `automation-engine.md`, a new "Airtime cutoff" section in `automation-engine-reference.md`, `automation-upkeep.md`, `AUTOMATION_ENGINE_PLAN.md`, and the `automation.airtime_cutoff.description` string in `en.jso

+### Airtime cutoff {#airtime-cutoff}
+
+Engine rules honor the source's [Cutoff Airtime Utilization Threshold](/features/automation#airtime-cutoff),
+the same verdict that pauses the built-in automations. While a Meshtastic source's Channel
+Utilization is over its threshold (default `30%`), these actions send nothing on that source:
+
+| Held back | Never held back (they send nothing on the mesh) |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Send a message**, **Send a tapback**, **Request data** (every op), **Broadcast a waypoint**, **Reboot the node** with a remote target. **Trace MeshCore paths on a schedule** checks too, but runs only on MeshCore, which has no reading, so it is never held back today | **Reboot the node** (local), **Manage the node**, **Send a notification**, **Run a script**, **Enable or disable an automation**, **Turn forwarding on or off**, **Pause**, **Do nothing**, **Set a variable** |
+
+How it behaves:
+
+- **Per target.** Each selected source is checked on its own, so a busy source holds back its send
+  while a quiet one still sends. The run log then says *partly sent* and names the held-back sources.
+- **The run goes on.** A held-back step is logged as *paused: airtime over cutoff* with the reading
+  and the threshold, the later steps still run, and the run counts as completed.
+- **Cooldown and rate limit are given back** when every step that counts was held back (*Do nothing*
+  and *Pause* don't count either way). The rule can then fire again as soon as the channel clears,
+  instead of waiting out a window in which it sent nothing. A run that did anything else (a
+  notification, a script, a send on another source) keeps its stamp.
+- **A held-back send is dropped, not queued.** Nothing replays it when the channel clears; the next
+  event that fires the rule sends. Triggers that fire once per change (a geofence crossing, *left
+  home*, a stale or declining-battery alert) have already moved on, so that alert is not sent again.
+  A bridge rule that relays onto a busy Meshtastic source drops those relays the same way.
+- **Set a variable** steps still run on every held-back run.
+- **Run log stays short.** While every send of a rule is held back, the run log stores at most one
+  row per rule every 10 minutes. The live trace still shows every run.
+- **Run now ignores the cutoff.** You asked for the send, so it goes, and the run log adds an
+  *airtime cutoff ignored (Run now)* line with the reading.
+- **Test panel** shows *would be skipped now: airtime X% > Y%* and still shows the text that would
+  be sent.
+- **Only Meshtastic sources have a reading.** MeshCore, Reticulum and MQTT sources are never held
+  back. A Meshtastic source with no reading yet is not held back either.
+- **No per-rule opt-out.** Set the source's threshold to `0` to turn the cutoff off for that source.
+
+A held-back **Broadcast a waypoint** does not use up its 30-minute floor, and a held-back scheduled
+trace path stays due, so each goes out on the next run after the channel clears.

+The empty-send rule and the protocol skips (for example a tapback on Reticulum) are checked first; the
+cutoff is only asked about a send that would otherwise go out.

body:
## Summary

Four built-in automations can be built in the Automation Engine instead: Auto Acknowledge, Auto Announce, Timer Triggers and Geofence Triggers. Each one now shows a small muted line, "You can also build this in the Automation Engine." The line links to the Automation Engine page (`/automations`) through react-router, so the link keeps the app's base URL.

### Where the note appears

The note sits directly under each section's header, in the `ConfigSection` `notice` slot, below any "paused" (receive-only) note. Geofence Triggers does not use `ConfigSection`, so its note goes straight after the section description.

| View | Sections |
|------|----------|
| Per-source Automation tab (Meshtastic) | Auto Acknowledge, Auto Announce, Timer Triggers, Geofence Triggers |
| MeshCore Automations view | Auto-Acknowledge, Auto-Announce, Timer Triggers (MeshCore has no Geofence section) |

### Design notes
- `AutomationEngineNote` is new (`src/components/shared/config/`). It renders a `UiIcon` "bot" icon and a react-router `Link`, styled by a CSS module that uses `var(--color-*)` tokens only.
- **Gating:** the note shows only when the viewer can read the global `automations` resource, the same check the sidebar's Automation Engine link uses. `AutomationTab` and `MeshCoreAutomationsView` compute that check and pass it down through `AutomationEngineNoteContext`, which defaults to `false`. Many section tests mock `AuthContext` or run without an `AuthProvider`, so the note does not read auth itself. Without the context, or outside a Router, the note renders nothing.
- **Auto Acknowledge:** the existing "Convert to an Automation…" button is unchanged. The note sits beside it and is not wired to the dialog.
- **i18n:** one new key, `automation.engine_note`, added to `public/locales/en.json` only. Weblate supplies the other locales.
- No packets, timers or notifications, so the mesh impact checklist does not apply.

title: fix(traceroute): Auto Traceroute is off by default; docs and fallbacks agree
body:
## Summary

Auto Traceroute has always started **off**: the manager field starts at 0 and the DB seeds `tracerouteIntervalMinutes = '0'`. The docs and UI copy said it ran every 3 minutes, and two routes read a missing interval as 5 minutes. This PR makes everything agree: **no value saved = off**. A saved interval keeps working unchanged.

### Code
- New `src/server/utils/tracerouteInterval.ts`: `parseTracerouteIntervalMinutes()` turns a missing or unreadable value into 0; a saved number passes through. `recentTracerouteLimit()` holds the recent-traceroutes row-limit math.
- `tracerouteRoutes.ts` (`GET /api/traceroutes/recent`) and `pollRoutes.ts` (poll, recent traceroutes) used `|| '5'`. Both now call the shared helper. The output stays the same: 5 minutes and "off" both sized the list at 12 rows/hour.
- Already correct, left alone: `applyManagerSettings.ts` (skips null, manager stays 0), both `{FEATURES}` checks in `meshtasticManager.ts` (absent = no icon), `SettingsContext` (localStorage fallback 0), the `database.ts` seed (`'0'`).
- MeshCore has no auto-traceroute interval reader.

### Docs / UI copy
- `docs/features/automation-upkeep.md`: off by default; 3-60 minutes (UI `min={3} max={60}`); the box starts at 15 when you turn it on; 15-30 minutes suggested.
- `docs/api/REST_API.md`: drop "scheduled every 3 minutes by the system".
- `docs/api/API_REFERENCE.md`: interval is 0 or 3-60, per source. Fix the `/settings/traceroute-interval` body and response (`intervalMinutes`, not ms), and note that this call does not save the value.
- `public/locales/en.json`: drop "Default: 3 minutes" and "Requires container restart" (a save re-arms the timer live). Other locales still carry the old text and need updating through translation.

## Mesh impact checklist

1. **Airtime:** no change at runtime. Auto Traceroute was already off by default, and no send path changes. The fix stops the docs and UI from telling users to expect (or set) a 3-minute interval, which would send about 20 traceroutes/hour per source.
2. **Spam:** no new packets, events or notifications.
3. **Save resets the timer: yes, found and not fixed here.** Every Auto Traceroute save (filter-only saves too, since the section always sends `tracerouteIntervalMinutes`) calls `setTracerouteInterval()`. That clears the timer and re-arms it with a random first fire 0 to min(interval, 5 min) out. No last-fire time is persisted. On a 60-minute interval, a save sends within 5 minutes. The only guard is the in-memory 30 s `MIN_TRACEROUTE_INTERVAL_MS`. To fix this, persist the last-fire time, as `autoAnnounceService` does. That belongs in its own issue.

- New `src/server/utils/tracerouteInterval.test.ts`: absent == saved 0, saved values pass through, and the limit math.

title: fix(docs): default the compose configurator to plain HTTP production mode
body:
## Summary

The Docker Compose configurator on the docs site defaulted to **Development** mode, which writes `NODE_ENV=development`. This PR makes the plain-HTTP production mode the default and relabels the options.

- **Default:** `deploymentMode` is now `production-http` (was `development`).
- **Labels and order:**
  1. **Plain HTTP (LAN)**: "Direct HTTP on your local network. Use a reverse proxy for internet access." (was "Production without Reverse Proxy — Direct HTTP access (not recommended)")
  2. **Reverse Proxy (HTTPS)**: "HTTPS via nginx, Caddy, or Traefik. Use this for internet access."
  3. **Development (contributors)**: "For working on MeshMonitor itself. Sets NODE_ENV=development, which loosens login and API rate limits."
- **Beyond the brief:** the proxy option is renamed from "Production with Reverse Proxy" to "Reverse Proxy (HTTPS)" so the three labels read alike. No other doc uses the old label. Easy to revert.
- **New optional "Server Address" field** (non-proxy modes only, inside the existing Port section, so step numbers don't change). When set, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` becomes `http://localhost:PORT,http://<addr>:PORT` and the "Access MeshMonitor at" URL uses the address. A pasted URL like `http://192.168.1.50:8080/` is cut down to the bare host. See "ALLOWED_ORIGINS" below. Drop this commit hunk if you'd rather keep the change minimal.
- `docs/configurator.md`: the Deployment Modes list matches the new order and labels, and notes the default.

## What development mode changes (why it shouldn't be the default)

Defaults from `src/server/config/environment.ts` L747-750 (keyed on `NODE_ENV === 'development'`), with windows from `src/server/middleware/rateLimiters.ts`:

| Limiter | production | development | Window | Private-IP exempt? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auth (failed logins) `authLimiter` | **5** | **100** | 15 min | **No**, applies to LAN clients too |
| API `apiLimiter` | 1000 | 10000 | 15 min | Yes (RFC 1918 + loopback skipped) |
| Messages `messageLimiter` | 30 | 100 | 1 min | No |
| Translate `translateLimiter` | 30 | 120 | 1 min | No |
| Meshtastic / MeshCore device limiters | 10 | 60 | 1 min | No |

Among others, the elevation, RF coverage, GNSS, message export and elevation tile limiters also switch on `env.isProduction` (e.g. elevation 20 vs 120 per minute), but those skip private IPs.

Other `isDevelopment` effects (`isDevelopment` is `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`):
- `server.ts:957`: unhandled 500s return the raw `err.message` instead of "Something went wrong".
- `server.ts:168`: CORS also allows `http://localhost:3000/5173/8080`.
- `scriptRoutes.ts:50` and `meshtasticManager.ts:13188`: the auto-responder scripts directory moves from `/data/scripts` (the volume) to `<project root>/data/scripts`, so scripts would land outside the data volume in a container.
- Extra debug logging (`server.ts:1156`, `scriptRoutes.ts:272`).

## Checks on production-http output

- **SESSION_SECRET:** comes from `.env` (`env_file: .env`); Po
