title: docs(configuration): add "Choosing a database" page
body:
## Summary

The homepage promotes SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL, but no published page explained how to set up the latter two. The old guide lived in `docs/database/` (excluded from the site) and `docs/development/database.md` (written for developers).

This PR adds `docs/configuration/database.md`, "Choosing a Database", with:

- When to stay on SQLite and when to switch
- Compose examples for PostgreSQL 16 and MySQL 8.4 (image `ghcr.io/yeraze/meshmonitor:latest`, `8080:3001`, `/data` volume)
- `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_PATH`, `DATABASE_POOL_SIZE`, and TLS
- Moving SQLite data with `migrate-db`, run in a one-off container on the compose network
- Backups per backend, and real log messages for troubleshooting

It also adds one sidebar line (Production & Operations) and one link each in `configuration/index.md` and `configuration/production.md`.

## Checked against code

- Scheme detection: `postgres://`, `postgresql://`, `mysql://`, `mariadb://`. Anything else logs a warning and falls back to SQLite (`src/db/index.ts`, `src/server/config/environment.ts`).
- When `DATABASE_URL` is set, SQLite init is skipped and `DATABASE_PATH` goes unused (`src/services/database.ts`).
- `DATABASE_POOL_SIZE` defaults to 20.
- `postgresSsl` is hard-coded to `false`, but `sslmode` in the URL overrides it. I checked this against the installed `pg`: `no-verify` gives `{rejectUnauthorized:false}` and `verify-full` gives `{}`.
- MySQL: `parseMySQLUrl` drops the query string, so there is no TLS option.
- Passwords are percent-decoded on both drivers.
- `migrate-db` only copies SQLite to PostgreSQL or MySQL. The page lists the tables in its skip set. `--dry-run` writes nothing.
- System Backup has round-trip tests only within the same backend, and restore drops columns the live table lacks. The page therefore says not to use it to switch backends.
- System Backups go to `/data/system-backups`.
- CI runs `postgres:16` and `mysql:8`. No MariaDB in CI, and the page says so.

## Differences from `docs/development/database.md`

- The dev page runs the migrator with `--network host` against `localhost:5432`. This page uses `docker compose run --rm meshmonitor npm run migrate-db ...` with the service hostname instead, so the database needs no published port.
- The dev page lists "multiple MeshMonitor instances sharing one database" as a reason to use PostgreSQL. I left that out because nothing in the code supports it.
- This page keeps the dev page's warning to migrate with the image version that wrote the SQLite file.

## Not verified end to end

- I did not run the `docker compose run … migrate-db`, `pg_dump` and `mysqldump --no-tablespaces` commands.
- The MySQL health check pings `127.0.0.1` because the official image's first-boot setup server has networking off. That comes from how the image behaves, not from this repo.
- Driver error strings (`ECONNREFUSED`, `password authentication failed`, `Access denied`, `self-signed certificate`) come from pg, mysql2 and Node.

## Poss

@@ -0,0 +1,225 @@
+# Choosing a Database: SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL
+
+MeshMonitor can store its data in SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL. SQLite is the default and needs no setup. One setting, `DATABASE_URL`, picks the backend.
+
+## Which one should I use?
+
+**Stay on SQLite** unless you have a reason to move. It is a single file in the `/data` volume, needs no extra container, and handles a typical home or club install well, including on a Raspberry Pi.
+
+**Pick PostgreSQL or MySQL** when:
+
+- You already run one of them and want MeshMonitor's data there, with your existing backups and monitoring.
+- You want to run the database on a separate host or managed service.
+- Your install is large (many sources, long retention) and you want a server database you can tune.
+
+| Backend | How to select it | Tested in CI |
+|---------|------------------|--------------|
+| SQLite | Leave `DATABASE_URL` unset | Yes |
+| PostgreSQL | `DATABASE_URL=postgres://...` or `postgresql://...` | PostgreSQL 16 |
+| MySQL | `DATABASE_URL=mysql://...` | MySQL 8 |
+| MariaDB | `DATABASE_URL=mariadb://...` | No (uses the MySQL driver) |
+
+::: warning Switching starts with an empty database
+Setting `DATABASE_URL` on an existing install does not move your data. MeshMonitor connects to the new database, builds its tables, and creates a fresh `admin` account (password `changeme`, or `ADMIN_PASSWORD` if set). Your SQLite file stays untouched in `/data`. To bring your data along, see [Move existing data](#move-existing-data).
+:::
+
+## Settings
+
+| Variable | What it does | Default |
+|----------|--------------|---------|
+| `DATABASE_URL` | Connection string for PostgreSQL or MySQL. Unset means SQLite. | unset |
+| `DATABASE_PATH` | SQLite file location. Ignored when `DATABASE_URL` is set. | `/data/meshmonitor.db` |
+| `DATABASE_POOL_SIZE` | Most connections MeshMonitor opens to PostgreSQL or MySQL. | `20` |
+
+Keep the `/data` volume even on PostgreSQL or MySQL. MeshMonitor still writes backups and logs there.
+
+If a password holds characters such as `@`, `:`, `/` or `#`, percent-encode them in the URL (`@` becomes `%40`).
+
+## SQLite
+
+Nothing to set up. The default compose file already mounts `/data`:
+
+```yaml
+services:
+  meshmonitor:
+    image: ghcr.io/yeraze/meshmonitor:latest
+    ports:
+      - "8080:3001"
+    volumes:
+      - meshmonitor-data:/data
+
+volumes:
+  meshmonitor-data:
+```
+
+To keep the file somewhere else in the container, set `DATABASE_PATH`.
+
+## PostgreSQL
+
+```yaml
+services:
+  postgres:
+    image: postgres:16
+    restart: unless-stopped
+    environment:
+      - POSTGRES_DB=meshmonitor
+      - POSTGRES_USER=meshmonitor
+      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
+    volumes:
+      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
+    healthcheck:
+      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U meshmonitor -d meshmonitor"]
+      interval: 10s
+      timeout: 5s
+      retries: 5
+
+  meshmonitor:
+    image: ghcr.io/yeraze/meshmonitor:latest
+    restart: unless-stopped
+    ports:
+      - "8080:3001"
+    volumes:
+      - meshmonitor-data:/data
+    environment:
+      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://meshmonitor:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/meshmonitor
+      - SESSION_SECRET=${SESSION_SECRET}
+    depends_on:
+      postgres:
+        condition: service_healthy
+
+volumes:
+  meshmonitor-data:
+  postgres-data:
+```
+
+Put the secrets in a `.env` file next to the compose file:
+
+```bash
+POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pick-a-long-random-password
+SESSION_SECRET=output-of-openssl-rand-hex-32
+```
+
+Use the service name (`postgres`) as the host, not `localhost`: inside the MeshMonitor container, `localhost` is MeshMonitor itself.
+
+**TLS to a remote server:** add `sslmode` to the URL.
+
+- `?sslmode=verify-full` encrypts and checks the server certificate.
+- `?sslmode=no-verify` encrypts but skips the check (for self-signed certificates).
+
+## MySQL
+
+```yaml
+services:
+  mysql:
+    image: mysql:8.4
+    restart: unless-stopped
+    environment:
+      - MYSQL_DATABASE=meshmonitor
+      - MYSQL_USER=meshmonitor
+      - MYSQL_PASSWORD=${MYSQL_PASSWORD}
+      - MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD}
+    volumes:
+      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
+    healthcheck:
+      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "127.0.0.1"]
+      interval: 10s
+      timeout: 5s
+      retries: 10
+
+  meshmonitor:
+    image: ghcr.io/yeraze/meshmonitor:latest
+    restart: unless-stopped
+    ports:
+      - "8080:3001"
+    volumes:
+      - meshmonitor-data:/data
+    environment:
+      - DATABASE_URL=mysql://meshmonitor:${MYSQL_PASSWORD}@mysql:3306/meshmonitor
+      - SESSION_SECRET=${SESSION_SECRET}
+    depends_on:
+      mysql:
+        condition: service_healthy
+
+volumes:
+  meshmonitor-data:
+  mysql-data:
+```
+
+The health check pings `127.0.0.1` on purpose. On first start MySQL runs a setup server with networking off, so a TCP ping only passes once the real server is up.
+
+MeshMonitor reads only host, port, user, password and database name from a MySQL URL. Anything after `?` is ignored, so it cannot connect over TLS. If your MySQL server requires TLS, use PostgreSQL or a local MySQL instead.
+
+## Move existing data
+
+MeshMonitor ships a one-way tool that copies a SQLite database into PostgreSQL or MySQL. It does not go the other way, and it does not copy between PostgreSQL and MySQL.
+
+These steps assume the PostgreSQL compose file above; for MySQL, swap the service name and URL.
+
+::: tip Migrate before you upgrade
+Run the copy with the same MeshMonitor version that wrote your SQLite database. A newer tool may expect tables or columns your database does not have yet. The steps below use your current `meshmonitor` image, so do not pull a new one until the switch is done; startup migrations bring the new database up to date when you upgrade later.
+:::
+
+1. **Back up first.** Make a [System Backup](/features/system-backup) or copy `meshmonitor.db` out of the volume.
+2. **Add the database service** to your compose file, but do **not** set `DATABASE_URL` yet. MeshMonitor must not start against the new database before the copy, or it creates its own rows first.
+3. **Stop MeshMonitor and start the database:**
+   ```bash
+   docker compose stop meshmonitor
+   docker compose up -d postgres
+   ```
+4. **Preview the copy** (writes nothing):
+   ```bash
+   docker compose run --rm meshmonitor npm run migrate-db -- \
+     --from sqlite:/data/meshmonitor.db \
+     --to postgres://meshmonitor:YOUR_PASSWORD@postgres:5432/meshmonitor \
+     --dry-run
+   ```
+5. **Run it for real:** repeat the command without `--dry-run`. The tool builds the tables, copies each one, and prints a row count per table.
+6. **Switch over:** add `DATABASE_URL` to the `meshmonitor` service and run `docker compose up -d`. Keep the same `SESSION_SECRET`.
+7. **Check:** `docker compose logs meshmonitor | grep -i database` should show `Database: PostgreSQL`, and you should log in with your old account.
+
+The tool skips a few tables of logs and per-user state: the packet log, backup history, auto-traceroute and auto key-repair logs and state, the Auto-Pathfinding target list, and saved map preferences. Everything else, including users, sources, nodes, messages and telemetry, comes across.
+
+Your SQLite file stays in `/data`. To go back, remove `DATABASE_URL` and restart; anything recorded while on PostgreSQL or MySQL stays there.
+
+::: warning System Backup is not a migration tool
+A System Backup restores into whichever database MeshMonitor is running on. Restore is tested only into the same kind of database the backup came from. Some column names differ between SQLite and PostgreSQL/MySQL, so a SQLite backup restored into PostgreSQL or MySQL can lose data. Use `migrate-db` to switch.
+:::
+
+## Backups
+
+[System Backup](/features/system-backup) works on all three backends. It exports every table to JSON under `/data/system-backups` and can run on a schedule. That is the simplest choice for any backend.
+
+You can also use the database's own tools:
+
+- **SQLite:** stop MeshMonitor, then copy `meshmonitor.db` out of the `/data` volume.
+- **PostgreSQL:**
+  ```bash
+  docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U meshmonitor meshmonitor > meshmonitor.sql
+  ```
+- **MySQL:**
+  ```bash
+  docker compose exec -T mysql sh -c 'mysqldump --no-tablespaces -u meshmonitor -p"$MYSQL_PASSWORD" meshmonitor' > meshmonitor.sql
+  ```
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+**`DATABASE_URL provided but not recognized as PostgreSQL or MySQL. Using SQLite.`**
+The URL must start with `postgres://`, `postgresql://`, `mysql://` or `mariadb://`. Until you fix it, MeshMonitor runs on SQLite.
+
+**`PostgreSQL connection failed: ...` or `MySQL connection failed: ...`**
+MeshMonitor could not reach the database at startup. The text after the colon says why:
+
+- `ECONNREFUSED` or `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`: wrong host or port, or the database is not up yet. Use the compose service name as the host and keep the `depends_on` health check.
+- `password authentication failed` (PostgreSQL) or `Access denied` (MySQL): the user or password in the URL does not match. Check for characters that need percent-encoding.
+- `self-signed certificate` (PostgreSQL): add `?sslmode=no-verify`, or give the server a trusted certificate and use `?sslmode=verify-full`.
+
+**`Invalid MySQL connection string`**
+MeshMonitor could not parse the MySQL URL. Check its shape (`mysql://user:password@host:3306/database`) and percent-encode special characters in the password.
+
+**`Pool saturated: ... Consider raising DATABASE_POOL_SIZE.`**
+Requests waited for a free PostgreSQL connection. Raise `DATABASE_POOL_SIZE` (default 20), and make sure the server's `max_connections` allows it.
+
+**After switching, the app is empty and only the `admin` account exists.**
+MeshMonitor is on a fresh database. Your data is still in the SQLite file; follow [Move existing data](#move-existing-data).
+
+For schema details and tuning tips, see the developer [Database](/development/database) page.

title: fix(helm,compose): stop seeding a fake node IP; drop retired upgrade/TLS knobs
body:
## Summary

### Helm chart
- `env.meshtasticNodeIp` defaults to `""`; `deployment.yaml` emits `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` only when it is set (`{{- with }}`). The old `192.168.1.100` default made every default install create a source that dials a fake address forever, the same bug #5237 fixed for Docker (`bootstrapSources.ts` auto-creates only when the var is set).
- Removed `env.meshtasticUseTls` and the `MESHTASTIC_USE_TLS` env. `grep -rn MESHTASTIC_USE_TLS src/` finds only `VITE_MESHTASTIC_USE_TLS` in `src/vite-env.d.ts`, so the server never read it.
- Removed the retired `autoupgrade` block and its `AUTO_UPGRADE_ENABLED` env (no reader in `src/`).
- Chart `version` 4.18.0 → 4.18.1 (`appVersion` unchanged).

### docker-compose.yml
- Dropped the pointer to the removed `docker-compose.upgrade.yml` overlay.
- `env_file` now uses the long form with `required: false`, so a missing `.env` no longer fails `docker compose up`.
- `NODE_ENV=production` instead of `development`. Removed the two now-redundant commented `# - NODE_ENV=production` lines. `COOKIE_SECURE` already defaults to false, so plain-HTTP logins still work.

### Docs
- `README.md` and `helm/README.md`: removed `meshtasticUseTls`, and `meshtasticNodeIp` is now listed as optional. Removed the helm README's "Setup with TLS/HTTPS" example, which only toggled the dead TLS flag.
- I left `docs/deployment/HELM_GUIDE.md` and `DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` alone because #6466 already edits those lines. Its HELM_GUIDE text says "The chart default is 192.168.1.100", which goes stale once this merges. Whichever PR lands second should fix it.

## Evidence
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config -q` passes with no `.env` in the tree (Compose v5.1.3).
- Parsed `values.yaml`: `env` = `{meshtasticNodeIp: '', nodeEnv: production, port: '3001', baseUrl: ''}`, and it has no `autoupgrade` key.
- `grep -rn "autoupgrade|meshtasticUseTls|AUTO_UPGRADE" helm/` finds nothing.
- No system test depends on the root compose file's `NODE_ENV=development`. The `tests/*.sh` scripts write their own compose files, and the ones that set `NODE_ENV` use `production`.
- I could not run `helm lint` or `helm template` locally because helm is not installed. The chart is linted by `scripts/build-helm-repo.sh` in Deploy Documentation, which runs only on main, so please run `helm template helm/meshmonitor` with and without `--set env.meshtasticNodeIp=10.0.0.5` before merging.

## Mesh impact
None. This sends no packets and adds no timers or notifications. Fewer default installs will dial a fake IP.

## Note
`build-helm-repo.sh` publishes the chart whenever `helm/**` changes on main. Chart 4.18.1 will be published before the app's 4.18.1 release, and the release bump will repackage that version with different contents.

title: docs: fix install and onboarding facts against the code
body:
Fixes factual errors in the install and onboarding docs, each checked against the code. Merges cleanly with #6464 (`git merge-tree` against `docs/site-hygiene`); none of the lines #6464 changes are touched.

## Changes

**getting-started.md**
- Removed the `export MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP=...` steps ("Change the Bootstrap Source Address" and meshtasticd). The Quick Start compose hard-codes the value, so a shell export does nothing, and `localhost` inside the container is the container. Replaced with "edit the compose file before first start" and "add a source in the Sources sidebar".
- Marked `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` optional and pointed at the Sources sidebar **+** button. Evidence: `environment.ts:565-569` (`wasProvided` only for a non-empty value), `defaultSourceConfig.ts:235-260`, `features/multi-source.md:38-40`.
- Moved the LAN-IP `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` warning up to the Quick Start (it sat ~100 lines later).
- `:dev` tag note: `:dev` moves on every release, stable included (`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:331-341`). The old text said it could lag `:latest`.
- "Database errors" fix: the volume is `<project>_meshmonitor-data`, not `meshmonitor-meshmonitor-data`. Added a data-loss warning and a link to System Backup.
- Restarts sign everyone out when `SESSION_SECRET` is unset (`environment.ts:461-476`).
- Dropped the "Rate limiting: stricter in production" bullet: the Quick Start already runs in production mode.
- Fixed the source-type list (Serial/BLE go through bridge sidecars), and pointed the Kubernetes links at `HELM_GUIDE`.

**configuration/meshtasticd.md**: replaced "set the node IP to localhost" with a table of which host to use for each way MeshMonitor runs.

**configuration/desktop.md**: now matches the current app.
- The setup window has no node IP field. It shows Web UI Port, Allowed Origins and Autostart, and says to add sources in the web UI (`desktop/src/index.html:254-305`). `meshtastic_ip` is legacy and empty by default (`config.rs:7-15`, `:33-41`).
- Autostart is saved but not wired up (`config.rs:18-20`, `index.html` hint).
- Remote access now uses the Allowed Origins field. Removed the launcher scripts: `lib.rs:281-300` sets `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `DATABASE_PATH`, `DATA_DIR`, `SESSION_SECRET` and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` on the child process, which overrides shell values. The env table now lists what the app sets.
- Windows data path is `%APPDATA%\MeshMonitor` (`dirs::data_dir()` = Roaming, `config.rs:126-128`), not `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
- Tray menu: added "View Logs" and the real "Settings..." label (`tray.rs:13-17`).
- Session reset: deleting `session_secret` makes `config.json` fail to parse, and `Config::load` then falls back to defaults for every field (`config.rs` has no `serde(default)` on it). The doc now says to replace the value instead.
- Removed the "Auto-upgrade: Automatic" row (retired in 4.13), and linked Watchtower instead.

**configuration/production.md** (Helm section only) and **deployment/HELM_GUIDE.md** / **DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.

body:
Corrects factual errors in `docs/faq.md` found in an audit. This is a correction pass, not the full FAQ restructure.

## Changes and evidence

Removed "MeshMonitor itself handles HTTPS": `src/server` imports no `https`/`http2` module. Diagnosis now points at the `Cookie secure:` startup log line (`sessionConfig.ts`).

- **Admin password reset.** No "Admin Panel" or super admin exists. Steps now use the **Users** page and **Set Password** (`en.json` `users.set_password`). `setUserPassword` (`src/server/auth/localAuth.ts`) blocks only SSO and locked accounts, not admins.

title: docs(site): fix leaked internal pages, broken logo, dead anchors and wrong claims
body:
First pass from a full review of meshmonitor.org. Covers mechanical fixes, factual errors found by checking docs against code, and homepage/README claims.

## Site hygiene
- `docs/superpowers/` (21 design specs + 4 reviews) and `docs/releases/` (pre-4.x notes) were publishing and in site search. Added to `srcExclude`.
- Navbar logo pointed at a non-existent `/images/logo.svg` (404 on every page). Now uses `logo.png`.
- `/getting-started`, `/configurator`, `/deployment/*`, `/developers/*` now have a sidebar. New `/features/` landing page; the Features nav link used to open Settings.
- Removed two "Coming Soon" development stub pages; links now point at the real dev notes on GitHub.
- Configuration sidebar: dropped the retired auto-upgrade page and the duplicate Push Notifications link. Renamed the second "Receive-Only Mode" to "MeshCore Receive-Only". Stripped emoji from labels.
- 10 dead anchors fixed with explicit `{#id}`s (headings with `—`, `→`, leading digits).
- The 4.18 blog post threw a render error (`{{ }}` in inline code); wrapped in `v-pre`.

## Factual errors (checked against code)
- **Data loss:** `production.md` and `configuration/index.md` mounted the volume at `/app/data`. The app writes to `/data` (`dataDir.ts`), so the database was lost on the next pull. Fixed everywhere.
- Non-existent image names (`meshmonitor:latest`, `yeraze/meshmonitor`) and `8080:8080` port maps (the app listens on 3001), plus the Traefik label port.
- Env-var reference defaults were wrong for TZ, connect/reconnect timeouts, module config delay, TRUST_PROXY, COOKIE_SECURE and COOKIE_SAMESITE (`environment.ts`).
- The High Availability section ran several replicas against one SQLite file and one radio. Replaced with a single-instance note.
- In-app help links: documented Auto Delete by Distance (the link had no target) and fixed the Auto LocalStats anchor in `AutoLocalStatsSection.tsx`.
- Store & Forward: MeshMonitor is a passive client and never requests history (`CLIENT_HISTORY` is unused). Fixed the homepage card and the page, which contradicted itself.

## Claims (judgment calls, open to veto)
- README: removed "One-click Self-Upgrade" (retired in 4.13). Vite 7 → 8. Analysis & Reports line updated.
- Homepage:
  - Replaced the Store & Forward card with **Mesh Diagnostics** and **Public-Instance Mode** cards.
  - Named Reticulum and the Automation Engine.
  - MQTT can send, not just receive. Map colors are by hop count, not signal strength.
  - OTA is admin/ESP32-only. Removed the PWA "system tray" claim. Push needs HTTPS.
- Quick Start no longer seeds `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` (optional since #5237). It points users to the Sources **+** button and the CORS/blank-screen FAQ.
- Meta description cut to 129 chars and now names Reticulum.

Not in this PR: FAQ rewrite, onboarding consolidation, splitting the large how-to pages, and the Helm chart default node IP. Follow-ups.

## Test plan
- [x] `vitepress build docs` passes with no errors
- [x] All fixed anchors pr

title: fix(api-docs): derive Swagger UI server URL from the request
body:
Fixes #6462

## Problem
`src/server/routes/v1/openapi.yaml` hardcoded `http://localhost:8080/api/v1` as its first `servers` entry. Swagger UI's "Try it out" always sent requests there, whatever host, IP or reverse proxy the docs were opened from, and ignored `BASE_URL`.

## Fix
- `docs.ts` now builds the spec's `servers` entry for each request from `req.baseUrl`, with `/docs` removed. That gives a host-relative URL such as `/api/v1` or `/meshmonitor/api/v1`, which the browser resolves against the host the page was loaded from.
- The Swagger UI page uses `swaggerUi.serveFiles(undefined, options)` plus `req.swaggerDoc`, so `swagger-ui-init.js` gets the per-request spec. This follows the dynamic-spec pattern in the swagger-ui-express docs. Previously the `swaggerInit` script came from a shared module-level global.
- `/api/v1/docs/openapi.json` returns the same per-request spec.
- The static `openapi.yaml` now uses a relative `/api/v1`, so `/openapi.yaml` no longer points at localhost either.
- `docs/public/openapi.yaml`, the copy on the website, is unchanged.

## Mesh impact checklist
Not applicable: this sends no packets, fires no notifications and arms no timers.

## Tests
- New `src/server/routes/v1/docs.test.ts` covers the server URL with and without `BASE_URL`, `openapi.json`, `swagger-ui-init.js` and the UI page.
- `src/server/routes/v1/` passes: 19 files, 337 tests. Server `tsc` and `lint:ci` are clean.
- Full suite: 37,428 passed. 6 failed, all in `linkPreviewRoutes.test.ts`, and they fail the same way with this change reverted. That suite's SSRF DNS guard can't resolve hosts in the sandbox, so the failure is environmental; CI is the authority. 1,924 were skipped because no PG/MySQL containers were running, which doesn't matter here since there are no schema changes.

-- Authored by Roger 🤓

title: feat(lora): support FEM_LNA_Mode AUTO (3) and keep unknown values (#6452)
body:
Closes #6452.

Meshtastic added `Config.LoRaConfig.FEM_LNA_Mode` **AUTO = 3** (meshtastic/protobufs#1175). Firmware `develop` makes it the default on fresh installs and factory resets for boards with a switchable LNA (meshtastic/firmware#12380); the firmware then switches the LNA by the measured noise floor. It is not yet in a tagged firmware release.

## Problem
Both LoRa dropdowns offered only DISABLED / ENABLED / NOT_PRESENT. These are Device Configuration (`LoRaConfigSection`) and Admin Commands. A controlled `<select>` whose value has no option shows the first option, so a node in AUTO looked DISABLED, and re-picking what appeared selected silently turned AUTO off.

## Changes
- **AUTO (3)** added to `FEM_LNA_MODE_OPTIONS` and the server `FemLnaMode` constants, with help text in both dropdowns. The help text names no firmware version, since #12380 isn't released yet.
- **Unknown values are kept.** `femLnaModeOptionsFor(current)` adds an `Unknown (N)` option when the node reports a value newer than the list, so a future enum entry shows as itself and a save sends it back unchanged. Both dropdowns use it.
- **No protobufs submodule bump.** protobufjs encodes and decodes the number 3 without the enum entry. Round-trip tests prove both directions through the real code: `createSetLoRaConfigMessage` outbound, and `parseIncomingData` inbound, which feeds the UI. They also cover a value (7) outside the schema. Bumping to upstream `master` would pull in 33 unrelated commits; that belongs to the regular protobufs sync.

## Mesh impact
None. It is a config field, sent only when the user saves.

## Testing
- `protobufService.femLnaMode.test.ts`: adds AUTO and value 7 round trips through the real builder, plus inbound decoding of `femLnaMode` 3 through `parseIncomingData`.
- New `LoRaConfigSection.femLnaMode.test.tsx`: AUTO shows as selected; value 7 shows and selects `Unknown (7)`; a known value gets no Unknown option; picking AUTO reports 3.
- `LoRaConfigSection.test.tsx`: the three-value assertion becomes four, and `femLnaModeOptionsFor` gets unit tests.
- LoRa, Admin Commands and constants suites: 26 files, 264/264 pass. Both `tsc` configs are clean and the lint ratchet passes.

title: fix(admin): send add_contact before set_favorite_node from Admin Commands
body:
Follow-up to the gap @joroses found on #6451.

## Problem
The Admin Commands tab's **Set favorite** (`AdminCommandsTab.tsx` → `executeCommand('setFavoriteNode')`) built a lone `set_favorite_node` in `adminRoutes.ts` and never went through `FavoritesService`, so the #6153 `add_contact` step never ran on that path. `set_favorite_node` only flags an existing NodeDB entry, so favoriting a node the target radio didn't hold did nothing, for both local and remote targets.

The other favorite paths already send `add_contact` first, because they go through `FavoritesService`: the node-list toggle (`nodesRoutes.ts`), Auto-Favorite, and the Automation Engine `favorite` action.

## Fix
- `setFavoriteNode` sends `add_contact` in the executor's existing `preSend` hook, before `set_favorite_node`.
- The packet comes from the same builder every other favorite path uses: `FavoritesService.buildFavoritedContactMessage`, now public and exposed on the manager. Any guards added there apply to this path too, including the key-mismatch, name and role checks discussed on #6451.
- Both packets use the executor's one session passkey, with no second passkey request.
- If the builder declines (for example, no public key), only `set_favorite_node` goes out. If `add_contact` fails, the error is logged and `set_favorite_node` still goes out, as in `FavoritesService`.
- The response shape, async operation flow and #4487 retries are unchanged.

## Overlap with #6451
#6451 changes the body of `buildFavoritedContactMessage`. This PR only changes its visibility (`private` → public), so whichever merges second has a one-line rebase.

## Mesh impact
One extra admin packet per manual **Set favorite** click from this tab, the same as the node-list toggle already sends. It is user-initiated, with no timer and no fan-out.

## Testing
- New `adminRoutes.favoriteNode.test.ts` (route harness, real `set_favorite_node` encoder), covering:
  - local and remote targets: `add_contact` goes out first, then `set_favorite_node`, both to the target and with one passkey;
  - builder declines → `set_favorite_node` alone;
  - `add_contact` fails → `set_favorite_node` still sent;
  - missing `favoriteNodeNum` → 400, nothing sent.
- Without the route change, 3 of the 5 tests fail.
- Admin route and `FavoritesService` suites: 17 files, 315/315 pass. `tsc` is clean and the lint ratchet passes.

--- CHANGELOG.md (+55/-0)
@@ -6,6 +6,61 @@ The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+## [4.18.0] - 2026-11-17
+
+This release adds support for the Meshtastic `is_automation` bit. MeshMonitor's automation sends now set bit 2 of `Data.bitfield`; messages that carry it show a bot icon, Packet Monitor shows the flag, and Auto-Ack, Auto-Responder and new Automation Engine rules ignore bots unless you tell them not to. It also adds public-instance mode, which trims what signed-out viewers see; an embedded MeshCore MQTT broker; Meshtastic sends over MQTT with no radio; mesh-wide notification defaults; Direct RF Contacts history; verified remote config saves; a security digest preview; and owner and email claims in the Analyzer Observer token. Fixes cover MeshCore telemetry, maps and repeater names, the Virtual Node, the MT↔MC bridge, MQTT config saves and server-side PKI DM decryption. It covers everything since 4.17.3. Upgrading runs migrations 233 to 239 automatically. Read **Upgrade notes** at the end of this section first.
+
+### Added
+- **Meshtastic `is_automation` bit.** Every automation send sets bit 2 (`0x04`) of `Data.bitfield`; manual sends are unchanged. Messages with the bit show a bot icon in channels, DMs and Unified Messages, and Packet Monitor has an `is_automation` column. The Automation Engine message trigger gains a **Sent by** filter (any, people only, automations only) and a `trigger.isAutomation` token; new rules start at people only. Auto-Ack and Auto-Responder skip automated messages unless you tick their new **Respond to automated messages** box. Live messages carry the flag, so the icon shows at once. (#6449, #6450, #6455)
+- **Public-instance mode**, off by default. When an admin turns it on, signed-out viewers and embeds see positions snapped to a ~1.5 km grid, rounded distance, bearing and altitude, and no raw payloads. Four toggles, each on by default, also hide long names, hide public keys, round times down to the hour and hide message text. CSV and NDJSON exports are blocked for signed-out viewers. A test calls every route signed out and fails on any leak. Embed maps spread nodes that share a cell. Signed-in users and the v1 API see full data. (#5156, #6433, #6434, #6435, #6445)
+- **Hide nodes that declined MQTT** from signed-out viewers, a per-source setting, off by default. A node whose last MQTT packet set `ok_to_mqtt` to false, and that this source never heard directly over RF, is hidden with all its data. (#5156, #6393)
+- **Embedded MeshCore MQTT broker**, a new source type that MeshCore observers publish to directly. Logins need a signed token or a static password, and every login is bound to an allowlist of observer keys. Caps limit observers, message rate and payload size; the Overview tab shows each connection and the last refused logins. Opt-in upstream forwarding sends allowlisted observers on as-is or under MeshMonitor's own observer key. The default port is 1884. (#6197, #6400)
+- **Send Meshtastic messages over MQTT with no radio**, off by default per source. Each source gets its own generated node and can send channel text on Channel Database channels, PKI DMs to nodes with a trusted key, and a NodeInfo every 3 hours. Sends cap at 6 a minute and 60 an hour per source, use hop limit 3, and never come from automations. The toggle warns about downlink airtime. It needs `SESSION_SECRET`. (#4305, #6395)
+- **Mesh-wide notification defaults** with per-source overrides. Apprise and desktop alerts hold an event for 5 seconds and send once, naming every source that saw it. Inactive and low-battery alerts dedup by node across sources, and a browser keeps one Web Push subscription, filtered per source. (#5729, #6394)
+- **Direct RF Contacts** for Meshtastic and MeshCore: a daily history of the nodes each source hears directly over RF. It adds a report on the Analysis tab with CSV export, a Direct RF section on node detail, and a Network survey "Heard directly" table that no longer empties when the packet log rolls over. History keeps 30 days by default (1 to 365) and starts at upgrade. (#6210, #6388)
+- **Verified remote config saves.** A **Verify config saves** box on the Admin Commands tab runs each remote save as a job: send, wait 90 seconds, read the section back, and resend only when a changed field still holds its old value. A missed reply never triggers a resend. A **Verified saves** panel lists jobs and can cancel them. (#4487, #6417)
+- **Security digest Preview.** A Preview button beside Send now shows the digest's title and body with a character count, and warns over Discord's 2,000-character limit. It sends nothing. (#6453, #6456)
+- **Owner and email claims in the Analyzer Observer token**, so LetsMesh and MeshMapper can link an observer to an account. Set them per source or per broker; only token-mode brokers carry them. (#6454, #6458)
+- **Room Sync re-joins rooms without a saved password.** A room this radio logged in to before gets a blank-password login, which a room server's ACL accepts, after each connect and on its normal interval. A refusal turns auto-sync off for that room. (#6408, #6415)
+- **Per-trigger enable and disable** for the Meshtastic Auto-Responder, as on MeshCore. (#6405, #6413)
+- **MeshCore Auto-Responder scripts get `HOPS`, `ROUTE`, `ROUTE_NAMES`, `HASH_SIZE` and `SCOPE`.** (#6402, #6412)
+- **Gateway names** in the "Colour nodes by gateway" legend and in popup gateway chips, in place of hex ids. (#6386, #6387)
+- **LoRa transparent mode warning.** A banner and a read-only box on the LoRa config page show when a node runs in transparent mode. The Info tab shows the nRF52 bootloader version. (#6181, #6321, #6392)
+- **Room login hint** for the stock MeshCore guest password `hello`, with a button that fills it in. (#6407, #6414)
+
+### Changed
+- **MeshCore Companion heartbeat is on by default, every 60 seconds.** The probe is a local request that sends nothing over the radio. Three failed probes start a reconnect, so a hung companion is caught in about 3 minutes. (#6437, #6446)
+- **Position requests carry an empty Position.** Exchange Position no longer sends your node's own position, so relays that drop duplicate positions no longer drop the request. The far node still learns your position from your normal broadcasts. (#6047, #6391)
+- **Virtual Node apps can send waypoints.** Only admin packets stay blocked when admin commands are off. (#6442)
+- **Settings checkboxes sit inline** with their labels. (#6444)
+- **Port numbers use the shared `PortNum` constants**, and lint rejects bare ones. (#6440)
+- **Docs:** CardMesh links follow its GitHub rename, contributed by @maxhayim. (#6419)
+- **Dependency updates**, including rotating-file-stream 4, web-push 4, maplibre-gl 6.18 and satellite.js 7.2. (#6420 to #6430)
+- **Translations** refreshed from Hosted Weblate. (#6340, #6432)
+
+### Fixed
+- **Server-side PKI DM decryption** built its nonce in the wrong byte order, so it could never open a real firmware DM. It now matches firmware. (#6395)
+- **MQTT config saves report a refusal.** When the node refuses the save, for example on firmware built without MQTT, the save returns an error and the cached config stays as it was. MQTT checkboxes no longer stay ticked after a reload when the node reports them off. (#6439, #6448)
+- **MeshCore remote telemetry keeps every sensor.** A local Cayenne-LPP decoder reads the records after an altitude reading, such as INA3221 voltage, current and power. (#6389, #6390)
+- **MeshCore repeater sources over serial show their name** instead of `Unknown Repeater`. Contributed by @vitska, in their first MeshMonitor PR. (#6431)
+- **MeshCore maps draw one neighbour line per pair**, and the tooltip shows both directions with their age. Before, the shown SNR flipped between stale and current values. (#6403, #6404)
+- **Automation:** `source-connected` and `source-disconnected` fire for MeshCore sources, once per change (#6437, #6446); MeshCore telemetry triggers carry the node name, key and role (#6397, #6398); the MT↔MC bridge relays the operator's own MeshCore channel posts (#6409, #6410); the Remote Telemetry and Time Sync automation sections save again (#6399, #6411).
+- **Virtual Node:** a text message from one app reaches the other connected apps (#6436, #6438); NodeInfo carries the radio's lock and LoRa-heard flags, so Android 2.8 shows the right lock and no "unheard" badge (#5921, #6416); MeshMonitor's own MeshCore channel sends show 0 hops, not "63 hops, 4-byte" (#6441, #6443).
+- **Neighbour info scopes by source** before it picks the latest row per pair, so a source no longer loses links another source holds. (#6396)
+
+### Upgrade notes
+- **Migrations 233 to 239** run on start on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.
+- **Auto-Ack and Auto-Responder skip automated messages by default.** A message flagged `is_automation` gets no reply unless you tick **Respond to automated messages**. A MeshMonitor bot that answered another bot will stop.
+- **Automation sends set the `is_automation` bit.** There is no setting to turn it off.
+- **New Automation Engine message rules** default to **People only**. Existing rules are unchanged.
+- **MeshCore Companion heartbeat:** existing Companion sources with no stored heartbeat get 60 seconds. That includes sources where you turned it off under the old form, which stored nothing for off. Set it to 0 to turn it off again.
+- **Notifications:** push subscriptions collapse to one per browser. Per-source settings keep working until you edit them. Push rows with no user, and the anonymous account, get every source the anonymous account can read. Apprise and desktop alerts arrive up to 5 seconds later.
+- **Public-instance mode, hide-declined-MQTT nodes, MQTT sends with no radio and broker forwarding are all off by default.** With public-instance mode on, the CoT/TAK feed is not trimmed; Settings warns about it.
+- **The MeshCore MQTT broker** listens on 1884 by default. Docker and Helm do not expose it; map the port yourself.
+- **MQTT config saves** wait up to 5 seconds for a refusal. A refused MQTT restore now fails instead of passing.
+- **Exchange Position** no longer sends your position to the far node.
+- **Room Sync:** rooms with auto-sync on that this radio logged in to before get one blank-password login after each connect, at most one per source per minute, skipped when a login ran in the last hour.
+
 ## [4.17.3] - 2026-11-13
 
 This release brings MeshCore close to Meshtastic across most of the app, using one shared implementation for both protocols where they overlap. It also closes a MeshCore channel-secret leak in the v1 API, fixes a cross-source backup read, and adds an opt-in node-name anti-spam filter. It covers everything since 4.17.2. Upgrading runs migrations 223 to 232 automatically. Read **Upgrade notes** at the end of this section first.

title: feat(meshcore): owner/email claims in the Analyzer Observer token (#6454)
body:
Closes #6454.

Adds optional `owner` / `email` claims to the MeshCore Analyzer Observer's signed MQTT auth token, so LetsMesh and MeshMapper can link an observer to an account. The claim format matches `meshcore-packet-capture`.

## Changes
- **Config** (`meshcoreConfig.ts`): adds optional `ownerPublicKey` / `ownerEmail` at the source level, with a per-broker override.
  - `normalizeObserverBrokers` resolves each broker's value (its own value, else the source default) and validates it: the owner key must be 64 hex characters and is uppercased; the email gets a simple shape check and is lowercased. An invalid value is dropped with a warning that never logs the value.
  - The claims apply only to brokers that use a signed token. Password-mode brokers carry none.
  - An invalid per-broker override does **not** fall back to the source default, so a broker given a different identity never receives the default email.
- **Shared rules:** the validation lives in `src/utils/observerOwnerClaims.ts`, used by both the server and the UI.
- **Token** (`meshcoreObserverToken.ts`): `opts.claims` is spread into the payload only when present, so with no claims the token is exactly `{ publicKey, aud, iat, exp }` as before. The claims are re-checked when the token is minted.
- **Publisher:** tokens are grouped by audience **plus claims**. Before, two brokers on the same audience with different owners would have shared one token. With no claims the grouping is unchanged.
- **Redaction:** `ownerPublicKey` / `ownerEmail` are hidden from viewers and anonymous callers at both levels, the same treatment as `tokenAudience`. Editors see them, and an editor's save keeps them (new route-harness test).
- **UI:** adds owner key and email fields at the source level, with a **Use this companion's key** button, plus per-broker overrides shown only for token-mode brokers. Fields are checked as you type using the same rules, and a privacy note beside the email field says it goes to the broker operator.
- **Docs:** `meshcore-analyzer-observer.md` gains "Claiming your observer (LetsMesh / MeshMapper)" and adds both fields to what leaves your network.

## Mesh impact
None. The claims travel only inside the MQTT auth token, over IP. Saving the config already rebuilds the publisher, which drops the cached tokens, so the token refresh cadence is unchanged.

## Note
`MAX_OBSERVER_CONFIG_BYTES` (1,536) is unchanged. Source-level fields add about 110 bytes. Overrides on all 8 brokers could exceed the cap, and the save then fails with the existing `OBSERVER_CONFIG_TOO_LARGE` error.

## Testing
- Token: 35 pass. Tests decode the payload: with no claims it has exactly the 4 original keys; claims are normalized, invalid values are left out, and `verifyAuthToken` still verifies the signature.
- Config normalization: 39 pass. Publisher: 62 pass.
- Redaction, editor-merge and observer validation routes, plus the public-instance sentinel audit: 317 pass.
- Observer UI and config: 130 pass. Other obs

title: feat(security): preview the security digest before sending (#6453)
body:
Refs #6453.

The reporter's Detailed security digest fails on Discord, while Summary works. The likely cause is Discord's 2,000-character message limit. They asked how to see what MeshMonitor sends. The issue reply gives the `?overflow=split` workaround. This PR adds a way to see the message.

## Changes
- **`POST /api/security/digest/preview`** `{ sourceId }`. It requires the same permissions as `/digest/send` (`security:write` + `nodes:read` on the source) and returns `{ title, body, format, reportType, length, combined, configured }`. It never sends anything and never returns the Apprise URL, which holds the webhook secret.
- **One builder:** `securityDigestService` now builds the message in shared helpers (`buildSourceMessage`, `buildCombinedMessage`, `postToApprise`). Preview and send use the same code, so the preview can't drift from what goes out. Send behaviour is unchanged.
- **Preview button** beside Send now:
  - It shows the title and body as plain monospace text, plus the character count.
  - It warns over 2,000 characters and suggests Summary or `?overflow=split`.
  - It notes a suppressed digest, a missing Apprise URL, a source the daily run combines with others, and unsaved edits ("Preview shows saved settings").
- **Docs:** `docs/features/security.md` covers Preview and the Discord `?overflow=split` tip.

## Notes
"Send now" always sends a single-source digest. The daily run combines sources that have no Apprise URL of their own into one message. Preview shows what Send now sends, and notes when the daily digest will be longer.

## Mesh impact
None. No radio traffic.

## Testing
- Digest service and route suites: 64/64 pass. New tests check that the preview's title, body and length match the captured send request, cover summary, detailed, suppressed, combined and not-configured cases, confirm Preview never calls fetch, and cover the route's permission matrix.
- Security tab UI and semantic tokens: 45/45 pass. Public-instance sentinel audit: 15/15 pass.
- Both `tsc` configs are clean and the lint ratchet passes.

title: fix(websocket): send isAutomation, xeddsaSigned and viaMqtt on live messages (#6449)
body:
Follow-up to #6450 (#6449).

## Problem
On the dev build, an Auto-Ack reply showed the bot icon about 5 seconds after the message appeared. `transformMessageForClient` (`socketEventGates.ts`) builds the `message:new` socket payload from an explicit field list, and that list never included the hop-display badge flags. The live row arrived without them, and the icon showed only when the next poll replaced the row.

The same gap delayed the XEdDSA shield and the MQTT badge.

## Fix
Add `isAutomation`, `xeddsaSigned` and `viaMqtt` to the socket payload, shaped the way the poll shapes them (`transformDbMessage.ts`). These are booleans, gated by the same per-channel read rule as the rest of the message.

## Mesh impact
None. Server-to-browser payload only.

## Testing
- New test in `webSocketService.gates.test.ts`: it fails before the fix and passes after.
- The gates suite and the public-instance sentinel audit pass (61/61).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` is clean and the lint ratchet passes.

title: refactor(channel-db): drop dead sourceId column and move UI to Global Settings
body:
## Summary

The `channel_database.sourceId` column added by migration 021 was never wired up:

- `ChannelDatabaseRepository` reads (`getAllAsync`, `getEnabledAsync`, `getByIdAsync`) never filtered by `sourceId`.
- HTTP routes (`channelDatabaseRoutes.ts`, `v1/channelDatabase.ts`) never passed `sourceId` to `createAsync`, so every API-created row landed with `sourceId = NULL`.
- `channelDecryptionService` is a singleton with one flat cache populated from `getEnabledAsync()` — the union of every enabled row.
- After #3089 merged, MQTT ingestion decrypts against that same global cache, making the per-source illusion even more misleading.

Permissions (`channel_database_permissions`) are already keyed only on `(userId × channelDatabaseId)` with no source dimension, so dropping the column is consistent with the existing permission model.

## What's in here

**Migration 063 (`063_drop_source_id_from_channel_database.ts`)**
Drops the column across SQLite (`ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN`), PostgreSQL (`DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS`), and MySQL (information_schema guard + drop). Idempotent.

**Schema / repository / types**
- `src/db/schema/channelDatabase.ts`: drop `sourceId` from all three dialect tables.
- `src/db/repositories/channelDatabase.ts`: drop `sourceId` arg on `createAsync` and the field on `mapToDbChannelDatabase`.
- `src/db/types.ts`: drop `sourceId` from `DbChannelDatabase`.
- `src/db/repositories/channelDatabase.test.ts`: drop `sourceId` from the SQLite/PG/MySQL test schemas.

**Unified routes**
- `src/server/routes/unifiedRoutes.ts`: drop the `vc.sourceId === source.id` filters in both `/channels` and `/messages`. Virtual channels are global — every readable channel-db entry is surfaced under every source the user can read. Comments updated. The matching test was rewritten to assert the new global semantics.

**MQTT bootstrap (post-rebase reconcile with #3089)**
- `src/server/mqttIngestion.ts`: `bootstrapMqttChannelDatabase` no longer passes `sourceId` to `createAsync`. The auto-seeded LongFast row is unowned, matching the global model.

**Frontend — UI relocation**
- `src/components/ConfigurationTab.tsx`: drop the `ChannelDatabaseSection` import, the `config-channel-database` menu entry, and its render block. The now-unused `useAuth` import was removed too.
- `src/components/SettingsTab.tsx`: import `ChannelDatabaseSection`, add `'settings-channel-database'` to `GLOBAL_SECTIONS`, register an admin-gated menu entry between System Backup and Database Maintenance, and mount the section. The device-specific `rebroadcastMode` prop is dropped; the component already handles `undefined` by hiding the rebroadcast warning block — appropriate for a global context.

**Registry / tests**
- `src/db/migrations.ts`: register migration 063 with the standard idempotent pattern.
- `src/db/migrations.test.ts`: bump count 62 → 63 and update the "last migration" assertion.

## Migration numbering

Latest migration on `main` post-#3089 is **62**. PR #3089 did not add any mi

title: feat(mqtt): full source-scoped ingest with channel decryption and unified-view fixes
body:
## Summary

MQTT bridges were connecting to upstream brokers but contributing almost nothing to the unified views. This PR fixes the entire ingest path so MQTT-relayed traffic lands properly attributed, decrypts via the channel database, and dedups across TCP + MQTT receptions of the same mesh packet.

**Before:** ~99% packet drop rate on Florida MQTT, zero messages in DB from MQTT sources, no MQTT entries in the unified channels picker or source filter.

**After:** ~25–35% ingest rate, full nodes/messages/telemetry/traceroutes/neighbors populated per MQTT source, picker entries from TCP and MQTT collapse to one logical channel, and a single mesh packet heard by TCP + Florida MQTT + Yeraze Broker appears as one unified entry with three receptions.

## What's in here

### Ingest pipeline (`src/server/mqttIngestion.ts`)
- `ingestServiceEnvelope` is async now and dispatches four additional portnums with the same storage semantics as the TCP path: `TRACEROUTE_APP` (incl. route segments + hop telemetry), `NEIGHBORINFO_APP`, `PAXCOUNTER_APP`, and `STORE_FORWARD_APP` (`ROUTER_HEARTBEAT` + `ROUTER_TEXT_*`).
- Server-side channel decryption via `channelDecryptionService`, mirroring `meshtasticManager.processMeshPacket` — encrypted packets get a synthetic `decoded` field populated from any matching `channel_database` PSK.
- `bootstrapMqttChannelDatabase` auto-seeds the well-known LongFast key (`AQ==`, expanded by `expandShorthandPsk`) so MQTT decryption works out of the box for new MQTT sources. Idempotent across multiple sources.
- Auto-records each `(envelope.channelId, packet.channel)` pair seen into the per-source `channels` table so the unified channels picker surfaces MQTT-side labels.
- Message row IDs now use the TCP convention `${sourceId}_${fromNum}_${packetId}`. This is load-bearing — `extractPacketIdFromRowId` in `unifiedRoutes.ts` splits on `_` and reads the trailing segment for the cross-source dedup key. Previously diverged with hyphens, which made the same packet appear N times in the unified view.
- Messages now flow through `databaseService.messages.insertMessage(msg, sourceId)` (repo) instead of `databaseService.insertMessage(msg)` (facade). The facade drops the `sourceId`, leaving rows orphaned with `sourceId=NULL` and invisible to source-scoped queries.

### Geo-membership seed (`src/server/mqttPacketFilter.ts`, `mqttBridgeManager.ts`)
- `seedMembership(positions)` marks nodes whose stored position is inside the bbox as `'in'` on bridge start, so non-POSITION traffic from already-known nodes flows without waiting for a fresh `POSITION_APP` broadcast (which can be hours and is reset on every restart).
- `seedTrustedNodes(nodeNums)` bypasses the bbox check for any node already heard directly by a non-MQTT source — fixes the case where the operator's own station (GPS off, no stored position) was geo-dropped on MQTT-relayed copies of its own packets.

### Unified routes (`src/server/routes/unifiedRoutes.ts`)
- `/telemetry`: `getLatestTelem

title: feat(desktop): remove Meshtastic IP requirement from first-run setup
body:
## Summary

The desktop setup window predates multi-source support and forced every fresh install to enter a Meshtastic node IP before the backend could start. That assumption breaks for MeshCore-only users (the most common desktop case today) and for users who want to configure sources from the web UI.

After this change, the first-run flow boots the backend with **zero sources configured**; users add Meshtastic or MeshCore sources from the web UI's Sources page.

## Changes

**Setup window (`desktop/src/index.html`)**
- Drop the Meshtastic Node IP and Meshtastic Port form fields
- Replace with an info block pointing users at the web UI Sources page
- Remove the IP-required validation (only the Web UI Port range is still validated)
- Rename **"Start with Windows"** → **"Autostart on Login"** so the label works cross-platform; hint updated to "Automatically start MeshMonitor when you log in"
- Retitle window subtitle from "Desktop Setup" to "Desktop preferences" (the same view serves both first-run and ongoing settings via tray)

**Rust config (`desktop/src-tauri/src/config.rs`)**
- Mark legacy `meshtastic_ip` / `meshtastic_port` with `#[serde(default)]` so older configs without them deserialize cleanly. Doc comment clarifies they're retained for backwards compat with existing installs.
- Honest doc comment on `auto_start` noting it's persisted-but-not-yet-wired to a platform autostart implementation.

**Non-breaking for existing users:** `lib.rs:200-204` already only passes `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` env to the backend when the value is non-empty, so legacy desktop users with a populated `config.json` continue to auto-derive their Meshtastic source on startup. The only change for them is that the simplified UI no longer lets them edit that IP in-place.

**Migration path for existing users:** the env-derived Meshtastic source appears as a regular row in the web UI `/sources` page in 4.x, so users who want to retire it can edit its host or delete it there — same as any user-created source. No need to hand-edit `config.json` unless they specifically want to clear the legacy env shim itself.

## Verification

End-to-end on a fresh macOS DMG build (4.6.1, arm64):

- ✅ Wiped `~/Library/Application Support/MeshMonitor/{config.json,meshmonitor.db}` for true first-run
- ✅ Setup window appears with no required fields, no Meshtastic IP block
- ✅ Hitting "Start MeshMonitor" with all defaults: `desktop.log` shows `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP: <unset> (no Meshtastic node configured)`
- ✅ Backend starts cleanly, web UI loads on port 8080
- ✅ User adds a MeshCore source pointing at `/dev/cu.usbserial-4` from the Sources page; native backend connects to the device
- ✅ Full Vitest suite: **5075 passed, 0 failed** (537 skipped, 21 todo) — 286.80s
- ✅ Rust unit tests for `src-tauri`: 2 passed, 0 failed

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh macOS DMG install: setup window shows no Meshtastic IP, no required fields
- [ ] Save with defaults → backend boots with `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` unset and z

title: fix: clear recovery message on SQLITE_CORRUPT migration failure
body:
$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

- Detects `SQLITE_CORRUPT` errors during SQLite migration runs and replaces the raw Node.js stack-trace crash with a clear, actionable error message
- Prints the exact database file path and copy/delete commands the user needs to recover
- Exits cleanly with code 1 instead of crashing with an unhandled exception

Fixes #3085 — reported on Raspberry Pi / Raspbian baremetal where SD card corruption caused `SqliteError: database disk image is malformed` during migration 059.

## What changed

`src/services/database.ts` — in the SQLite migration loop's catch block, added a check for `error.code === 'SQLITE_CORRUPT'`. When detected, logs a formatted message like:

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
DATABASE CORRUPTION DETECTED
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Your SQLite database file is corrupted (SQLITE_CORRUPT).
On Raspberry Pi this is usually caused by SD card failure
or an unexpected power loss during a write operation.

Database location: /path/to/meshmonitor.db

To recover:
  1. Back up:  cp "/path/to/meshmonitor.db" "/path/to/meshmonitor.db.bak"
  2. Delete:   rm "/path/to/meshmonitor.db"
  3. Restart MeshMonitor — a fresh database will be created.
...
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

Then calls `process.exit(1)` rather than rethrowing (which produced an unhelpful `UncaughtException` crash).

title: test(system): stabilize hardware test suite and make it manually-triggered
body:
## Summary

System Tests (Hardware) has been intermittently failing on PRs for weeks at `Test 14: Send message to Yeraze Station G2 and wait for response → HTTP 500`. Local-runner investigation (firmware logs in `/var/log/meshtastic-*` + container logs) confirmed the root cause is a hardware TCP flap between containers, not a code regression. This PR fixes the test sequencing so the suite runs cleanly, then switches the workflow to manual-only because the suite is still a slow serialized hardware run that mostly tests environmental stability.

## Test plan

- [x] Full `tests/system-tests.sh` run locally — **ALL 11 suites pass** after these changes (was previously failing at Test 14 in Reverse Proxy and OIDC)
- [x] New Test 12b/13b/11b stability gates fired and confirmed `Connection stable for 20s` in each script
- [x] `wait_for_reconnect` grace period catches the fast-reboot path that fails the modem-preset verify
- [x] Workflow file syntax sanity (`workflow_dispatch` only)

## What changed

### 1. URL_1 in `test-config-import.sh` — primary channel unnamed (was `primary`)

The factory-default Meshtastic state leaves the primary channel name empty. The previous URL_1 forced the device into a non-default state on the first import. Rebuilt the URL with channel 0 `name=""` while preserving the rest (dummyA/dummyB secondaries, LONG_FAST preset, US region, 3 hop limit, all PSKs). Verified round-trip via MeshMonitor's own decoder. Added `scripts/rebuild-config-url.ts` as the one-shot helper.

### 2. Settle delays between hardware-sharing test containers

The Meshtastic firmware allows **one** TCP API client at a time and force-closes the previous session when a new connection arrives. Firmware logs show `ApiServer: Force close previous TCP connection` followed by `Incoming API connection` whenever a test container teardown is immediately followed by the next container's startup. The device's session table takes ~60s to fully recover. Added 60s `sleep` between Quick Start cleanup → Reverse Proxy startup, and Reverse Proxy → OIDC startup.

### 3. Live-connection stability gates

The existing `Test 12/13/11: Wait for Meshtastic node connection and data sync` only verified channels/nodes were populated in the DB — that could pass on a brief 4s connect window before the device force-closed the session. Added `Test 12b/13b/11b` that polls `/api/connection` and requires `connected:true && nodeResponsive:true` sustained for **20 seconds** (max wait 180s), resetting the stability counter on any flap. `nodeResponsive` is bound to `MyNodeInfo` arrival on the current socket, so it cleanly tracks whether the live connection has settled.

### 4. `wait_for_reconnect` resilient to fast reboots

When the device reboots faster than the 1s disconnect-poll can catch, the script never sees `connected:false` and returns immediately — `verify_config` then runs against pre-reboot state and fails (e.g. modem preset mismatch). Added a 45s grace period when the disconnect window

--- scripts/rebuild-config-url.ts (+76/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+/**
+ * One-off helper: take a Meshtastic channel-config URL, clear channel 0's
+ * `name` field, and emit a new URL with the primary channel unnamed.
+ *
+ * Used by tests/test-config-import.sh authors to keep URL_1 (the first
+ * import cycle in the system test suite) representative of a real
+ * default device — Meshtastic's factory state leaves the primary channel
+ * with an empty `name`.
+ *
+ * Run with: npx tsx scripts/rebuild-config-url.ts <URL>
+ */
+import { loadProtobufDefinitions, getProtobufRoot } from '../src/server/protobufLoader.js';
+
+function urlsafeB64Decode(b64: string): Buffer {
+  const padLen = (4 - (b64.length % 4)) % 4;
+  const padded = b64 + '='.repeat(padLen);
+  const normal = padded.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
+  return Buffer.from(normal, 'base64');
+}
+
+async function main() {
+  const url = process.argv[2];
+  if (!url) {
+    console.error('Usage: npx tsx scripts/rebuild-config-url.ts <meshtastic-channel-url>');
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+
+  await loadProtobufDefinitions();
+  const root = getProtobufRoot();
+  if (!root) throw new Error('protobuf root not loaded');
+
+  const ChannelSet = root.lookupType('meshtastic.ChannelSet');
+
+  const fragment = url.split('#')[1];
+  const bytes = urlsafeB64Decode(fragment);
+  const decoded = ChannelSet.decode(bytes);
+  const obj: any = ChannelSet.toObject(decoded, { defaults: true, longs: Number, enums: Number, bytes: String });
+
+  console.log('Before:');
+  for (const [i, s] of (obj.settings ?? []).entries()) {
+    console.log(`  [${i}] role=${s.role} name=${JSON.stringify(s.name)}`);
+  }
+
+  if (obj.settings && obj.settings.length > 0) {
+    obj.settings[0].name = '';
+  }
+
+  // toObject with bytes:String gave us base64; encode wants Uint8Array back.
+  if (obj.settings) {
+    for (const s of obj.settings) {
+      if (typeof s.psk === 'string') {
+        s.psk = Buffer.from(s.psk, 'base64');
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  const reencoded = ChannelSet.create(obj);
+  const encoded = ChannelSet.encode(reencoded).finish();
+  const b64 = Buffer.from(encoded).toString('base64').replace(/=+$/, '');
+  const newUrl = `https://meshtastic.org/e/#${b64}`;
+
+  console.log('\nAfter:');
+  const verify = ChannelSet.decode(urlsafeB64Decode(b64));
+  const verifyObj: any = ChannelSet.toObject(verify, { defaults: true, longs: Number, enums: Number });
+  for (const [i, s] of (verifyObj.settings ?? []).entries()) {
+    console.log(`  [${i}] role=${s.role} name=${JSON.stringify(s.name)}`);
+  }
+
+  console.log('\nNew URL:');
+  console.log(newUrl);
+}
+
+main().catch((err) => {
+  console.error(err);
+  process.exit(1);
+});

title: fix(meshcore): split NUL-separated DeviceInfo remainder for Info panel
body:
## Summary
- The Meshcore Node Info panel was showing the HW Model and firmware version string concatenated together with unprintable boxes (the raw NUL bytes between them), and the Firmware row was displaying the build date instead of the firmware version.
- Root cause was in the `device_query` handler in `meshcoreNativeBackend.ts`:
  1. The upstream `@liamcottle/meshcore.js` library reads the entire remainder of the `DeviceInfo` frame as a single `manufacturerModel` string. Newer firmware packs NUL-separated segments (`"<model>\0<verString>\0"`) into that remainder, so both fields landed in the Model row.
  2. The handler explicitly set `ver: info?.firmware_build_date`, and the UI prefers `ver` over `firmwareVer` — so "Firmware" rendered as `<build_date> (<build_date>)`.
- Fix: split the remainder on `\0`, use the first segment as the model and the second (when present) as the firmware version string. UI now shows `Heltec V3` in the Model row and `v1.7.0 (01 Jan 2026)` in the Firmware row. Older firmware that doesn't pack a version string falls back to `v<firmwareVer> (<build_date>)`.

## Test plan
- [x] Added `device_query: splits NUL-separated remainder into model + version` regression test (`Heltec V3\0v1.7.0\0` → `model: "Heltec V3"`, `ver: "v1.7.0"`)
- [x] Added `device_query: handles plain model with no trailing version string` test (older-firmware fallback path)
- [x] `npx vitest run src/server/meshcoreNativeBackend.test.ts` — 23/23 pass
- [x] `npx vitest run` — full suite 5073/5073 pass
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [ ] Verify on real hardware: a Meshcore companion that previously showed boxes in the Model row now renders the model cleanly, and the Firmware row shows the version string + build date

title: fix(meshcore): make MeshCorePage fill the dashboard shell height
body:
## Summary

When viewing a MeshCore source, the page didn't fill the viewport — the left sub-toolbar stopped roughly 4rem short of the bottom and there was a visible dead band below the map / content area. The Meshtastic source pages didn't have this issue.

Root cause: `.meshcore-page` set `height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-height) - 4rem)` on the assumption it was nested inside the legacy `.app-main`, which has `padding: 2rem` all around (4rem combined vertical). After the source-detail page moved to the `.dashboard-page` shell (no padding around its children), the `-4rem` subtracted nonexistent gutter and the page came up short.

Switched to `flex: 1; min-height: 0` so the page fills whatever vertical space its flex parent gives it. The dashboard shell is itself a 100dvh flex column with the topbar above, so the math works out automatically and the layout is now context-independent.

Also dropped the now-redundant border / border-radius — those were "card in 2rem padding" decoration that looked awkward flush against the topbar in the dashboard shell.

## Test plan

- [x] All MeshCore tests pass (69/69)
- [x] Deployed locally and manually verified: sub-toolbar reaches the bottom, no dead band below the content, page is flush with the topbar
- [ ] Sanity-check both views (nodes / channels / dms / configuration) render edge-to-edge

title: feat(sources): add Prune Outside ROI action for mqtt_bridge sources
body:
## Summary

After #3078 landed, real-world testing surfaced a UX gap: the MQTT bridge geo filter is forward-only — it gates ingestion at packet arrival time but leaves rows that were ingested *before* the current bbox was configured (or with a wider previous bbox) in the database. After tightening an ROI, those legacy rows still appear on the map even though new outside-bbox traffic is correctly dropped.

Concrete numbers from local dev container at investigation time: Florida bridge had 113 nodes outside its bbox, all 15–27h old. Geo filter dropped 653/666 (98%) of new packets correctly — but the stale rows persisted.

This PR adds a surgical kebab-menu cleanup action.

## What's new

- `NodesRepository.pruneNodesOutsideBbox(sourceId, bbox)` — Drizzle DELETE that targets nodes with non-null position outside the bbox. Nodes without a recorded position are kept (no evidence they're outside).
- `DatabaseService.pruneNodesOutsideBboxAsync` thin passthrough.
- `POST /api/sources/:id/prune-outside-roi` — validates the source is an `mqtt_bridge` with at least one geo bound configured, unpacks the bbox from `downlinkFilters.geo`, returns `{ count }`.
- **"Prune Outside ROI" kebab item** on mqtt_bridge cards (sidebar), conditional on a configured bbox. Confirmation dialog + result toast in `DashboardPage`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — full suite: 10036 passed, 0 failed, 6 new repo tests + 6 new route tests

title: feat(mqtt): detect broker ACL restrictions and surface to user
body:
## Summary

When an upstream MQTT broker has ACLs that make it effectively publish-only or subscribe-only, MeshMonitor used to silently lose traffic and bury the rejection in generic logs. This change detects per-topic SUBACK denials (qos 0x80) and CONNACK auth failures, surfaces them as a `permissionMessage` on the bridge status, and shows a yellow "⚠ restricted" badge on the sidebar source card.

- `MqttBrokerClient` now reads mqtt.js's SUBACK packet (incl. partial-failure path via `ErrorWithSubackPacket.packet.granted`), tracks denied topics, classifies CONNACK return codes 4/5 as auth failures, exposes `getCapabilities()`, and emits `permission-denied`.
- `MqttBridgeStatus` gains `capabilities` + `permissionMessage`. New `buildPermissionMessage()` produces a one-line summary: full-denial → "publish-only — downlink disabled", partial → "Broker denied N subscription(s): …", auth → "Broker rejected authentication".
- `DashboardSidebar` shows the badge inline with the status row, visible even when the link is connected, with the message as tooltip.

### Out of scope

Publish-side denial cannot be reliably detected at QoS 0 / MQTT 3.1.1 — brokers silently drop denied publishes (no PUBACK at QoS 0). The capability surface reports `canPublish: 'unknown'` to make that explicit. Future work: optional MQTT 5 protocol upgrade for richer reason codes, or QoS 1 + PUBACK inspection on uplink.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — full suite: 5048 passed, 0 failed (3 new test files in `mqttBridgeManager.permission.test.ts`)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] ESLint on touched files — 0 errors (5 pre-existing `any` warnings unrelated to this change)
- [ ] Manual smoke: point bridge at a Mosquitto with `topic deny` ACL for a subscription and confirm the "⚠ restricted" badge appears with the denial message in the tooltip
- [ ] Manual smoke: bad creds → "Broker rejected authentication" tooltip

title: feat(meshcore): render telemetry graphs in DM contact-detail pane
body:
## Summary
- Mounts the existing `<TelemetryGraphs>` component under the per-node telemetry-retrieval config in the MeshCore DM view, so an operator who has just enabled remote telemetry polling for a contact can see the resulting plotted history in the same panel.
- MeshCore's remote-telemetry scheduler already persists rows to the `telemetry` table keyed on the contact's 64-char `publicKey`, and the existing `/api/telemetry/:nodeId?sourceId=...` endpoint already serves them — so this is a frontend wiring change plus one targeted permission fix.
- Fixes `checkNodeChannelAccess` so non-admin MeshCore users are not 403'd: the Meshtastic per-channel `viewOnMap` model does not apply to 64-char hex pubkeys, and the calling route already enforces `info:read`/`dashboard:read` plus source-level access. Anonymous callers remain blocked.

## Implementation notes
- DM view (`src/components/MeshCore/MeshCoreDirectMessagesView.tsx`): gated on the same `sourceId + baseUrl + isRealNodeKey(selected)` predicate that already gates `MeshCoreNodeTelemetryConfig`, so prefix-only contacts and singleton-mode renders don't mount the heavy graphs component.
- Permission helper (`src/server/utils/nodeEnhancer.ts`): early-return when the nodeId matches `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/` (MeshCore pubkey), returning `!!user` so unauthenticated callers still get `false`.
- Existing DM view test was upgraded to mount a sentinel `<TelemetryGraphs>` stub so we can assert it is rendered (or not) based on props — three new test cases cover the positive path, prefix-only peer, and singleton mode.
- Two new `checkNodeChannelAccess` test cases cover the MeshCore allow path and the anonymous-deny path.

## Test plan

title: fix(mqtt-source): preserve saved password on edit when field is blank
body:
## Summary
- Editing an MQTT source via the admin UI and changing an unrelated field (e.g. the geofence bounding box on an `mqtt_bridge`, or the listener port on an `mqtt_broker`) was silently wiping the saved upstream/auth password.
- The frontend deliberately clears the password input on load (admin GET round-trips it; non-admin GETs strip it) and drops the field from the PUT payload when the user has not typed a new one, expecting the server to re-merge the stored value. The PUT handler was instead doing a full `JSON.stringify` replace of `config`.
- Fix: new `preserveSourceCredentials()` helper in `src/server/routes/sourceRoutes.ts` re-injects `upstream.password` (bridge) or `auth.password` (broker) from the existing row when the incoming config omits it. Admins can still rotate the password by supplying a new value.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run src/server/routes/sourceRoutes.credentialPreserve.test.ts` — 5 new regression tests covering missing password, explicit `undefined`, and successful rotation for both source types.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/server/routes/sourceRoutes` — all 99 source-route tests pass (no regressions).
- [ ] Manual UI smoke test: edit an `mqtt_bridge`, change only the geofence bounds, save, reopen — password remains set.
- [ ] Manual UI smoke test: edit an `mqtt_bridge`, type a new password, save, reopen — new password takes effect.

title: feat(mqtt-bridge): seed bbox from detected node positions on first enable
body:
## Summary

When a user creates an `mqtt_bridge` source and first enables the "Restrict to geographic bounding box" filter, the map editor used to drop them at (0,0) in the middle of the ocean. Now it seeds the bbox from the bounds of currently-detected node positions (with 10% padding, min 0.05° ≈ 5km), so the user starts looking at their actual network and can refine from there.

- Skips (0,0) nodes — the firmware's "no GPS fix yet" sentinel.
- Only seeds when the form is empty; if you clear the bbox or hand-edit the numbers, your values stick.
- Helpers extracted to `DashboardPage.bboxSeed.ts` so they're unit-testable without JSDOM.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run src/pages/DashboardPage.bboxSeed.test.ts` — 6 new tests (empty/null nodes, (0,0) sentinel skip, multi-node bounding, single-node minimum padding, partial position rows, `bboxToFormStrings` rounding)
- [x] `vitest run src/pages/DashboardPage.test.tsx` — existing 22 DashboardPage tests still pass
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [ ] Manual: open the dev container, add an mqtt_bridge source, check the geofence box, confirm the editor opens with a sensible rectangle around the live nodes instead of empty ocean

title: fix(desktop): stop creating a phantom Meshtastic source on MeshCore-only installs
body:
## Summary

Surfaced by discussion [#2604](https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/discussions/2604) (bfsampson — macOS desktop, MeshCore-only, two companions): `server-stderr.log` was buried under ~140 lines of

```
[ERROR] ❌ TCP socket error: connect ENETUNREACH 192.168.1.100:4403
[ERROR] Reconnection failed: connect ENETUNREACH 192.168.1.100:4403
```

despite the user having no Meshtastic node at that address — or any Meshtastic node at all. The actual MeshCore failure (`[ERROR] [MeshCore] Connection failed: undefined`) appeared exactly once, drowned out by the noise.

### Root cause

The Tauri desktop bundle's `Config::default()` hard-coded `meshtastic_ip: String::from("192.168.1.100")` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/config.rs:34`) and unconditionally passed it to the spawned Node server as `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:160`). The server read the env var, treated it as a real user-configured value, and migration `_legacyDefaultSource.ts` seeded an `enabled=1` Meshtastic TCP source from it. For every fresh install — including MeshCore-only users who never wanted a Meshtastic source — the manager registry then flapped against that placeholder forever.

### Fix

Layered so existing Docker users who set `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` themselves are not affected:

| Layer | Change |
|-------|--------|
| `desktop/src-tauri/src/config.rs` | Default `meshtastic_ip` to the empty string. The placeholder example still lives in the setup-screen UI hint (`desktop/src/index.html`), it's just no longer baked into runtime config. |
| `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` | Skip `.env("MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP", …)` / `MESHTASTIC_TCP_PORT` when no IP is configured. The desktop.log records the unset state explicitly so future reports are unambiguous. |
| `src/server/migrations/_legacyDefaultSource.ts` | When the helper synthesizes a default Meshtastic source for an empty `sources` table and `MESHTASTIC_NODE_IP` is unset/empty/whitespace, insert with `enabled=0` instead of `enabled=1`. Docker users with the env var explicitly set keep `enabled=1`. SQLite, Postgres, and MySQL paths all updated symmetrically. |
| `src/server/meshcoreManager.ts` | Separately: connect() catch now surfaces `error.stack ?? error.message` for genuine `Error` rejections, a sentinel string for the empty-rejection case (`"rejected without an Error — likely port open / AppStart timeout / library-internal"`), and `String(err)` for any other shape. No more `Connection failed: undefined`. |

### Why two unrelated things in one PR

Both bugs surfaced from the same diagnostic — bfsampson's three log files — and neither makes sense to ship without the other. The phantom Meshtastic source explains 99% of his stderr noise; the lossy-error fix is what lets us actually diagnose his remaining real MeshCore failure on the next attempt.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/server/migrations/_legacyDefaultSource.test.ts src/server/meshcoreManager.connect-error.test.ts src/server/meshcoreManager.channels.test

title: feat(mqtt-bridge): interactive map editor for filter geographic bounding box
body:
## Summary

Replace the four free-text bbox inputs on the **MQTT Bridge** source-config modal with a Leaflet-backed interactive editor. Click two corners to draw, drag any corner handle to resize, "Clear" to start over. The numeric inputs stay beneath the map for precise tuning and are two-way bound — drag the map, the numbers update; type a number, the rectangle re-renders.

## Why

Pulling a useful Florida-sized bbox out of `minLat / maxLat / minLng / maxLng` text boxes required jumping over to Google Maps to read coordinates, then typing them back into the modal. The bbox is a fundamentally spatial filter, so editing it should be spatial too.

## Design notes

- New focused component `src/components/BBoxMapEditor.tsx` (not a variant of the existing `GeofenceMapEditor`). The auto-responder's `GeofenceShape` discriminated union (`circle | polygon`) already powers a separate geofence-triggers feature; growing it to include `bbox` would force changes across `src/utils/geometry.ts`, `GeofenceTriggersSection.tsx`, and the geofence test suite for no MQTT-side benefit. Keeping the MQTT filter's rectangular data model (`{ minLat, maxLat, minLng, maxLng }`) self-contained is cleaner.
- Same Leaflet + OSM tile pattern as the existing `GeofenceMapEditor` for visual consistency.
- Drag-corner UX: dragging any corner updates the bbox such that the OPPOSITE corner stays fixed (i.e. dragging SW updates `minLat + minLng`; NE stays put).
- The `bboxFromForm()` helper tolerates partial / NaN values in the text inputs so a user mid-typing doesn't break the map.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Full vitest: **9967/9967 pass** (no behavior change to filter pipeline; new component is presentational)
- [ ] Manual smoke in dev container — open Add Source → MQTT Bridge → enable geo bbox → click two corners → drag corners → verify the four numeric inputs update in sync

- **`docs/features/mqtt-broker.md`** — full feature page: the two source types, the two device paths (direct TCP and `mqttClientProxyMessage` client-proxy), filter semantics, quick-setup walk-through, comparison table against the MQTT Proxy Sidecar and node's built-in MQTT, troubleshooting, limitations.
