title: fix: Apply Proto3 defaults to LoRa config fields to ensure proper display
body:
## Summary
- Fixed LoRa configuration fields not displaying correctly due to Protocol Buffers 3 default value omission
- Applied explicit defaults for `usePreset` (false) and `frequencyOffset` (0) in three key locations
- Configuration changes made via Meshtastic app while container is offline now properly reflected when container starts

## Problem
Protocol Buffers 3 omits fields with default values (false for booleans, 0 for numeric types) during JSON serialization. This caused:
- "Use Preset" checkbox appeared checked when it should be unchecked
- "Frequency Offset" not displayed when set to 0
- Changes made via Meshtastic app while container was offline were not reflected in UI

## Solution
Applied explicit Proto3 default values in three locations:
1. **processFromRadio** (lines 562-595): When receiving config from device
2. **getCurrentConfig** (lines 797-824): When returning config to frontend
3. **buildDeviceConfigFromActual** (lines 3671-3756): When building config for export

## Testing
- Verified "Use Preset" checkbox correctly shows unchecked state when device has `usePreset=false`
- Verified "Frequency Offset" displays 0 when device has `frequencyOffset=0`
- Verified configuration changes made via Meshtastic app are properly loaded after container restart
- Tested with config changes made while container was offline

Fixes #623

title: fix: Use explicit null check for welcomedAt to prevent re-welcomes
body:
## Summary

Fixed a potential edge case in auto-welcome logic where a node with `welcomedAt=0` could be re-welcomed repeatedly due to JavaScript's truthy evaluation treating `0` as falsy.

## Changes

**Before:**
```typescript
if (node.welcomedAt) {
  logger.debug(`⏭️  Skipping auto-welcome for ${nodeId} - already welcomed previously`);
  return;
}
```

**After:**
```typescript
if (node.welcomedAt !== null && node.welcomedAt !== undefined) {
  logger.debug(`⏭️  Skipping auto-welcome for ${nodeId} - already welcomed previously`);
  return;
}
```

## Impact

This defensive programming approach ensures that any non-null, non-undefined value (including `0`) will prevent re-welcomes.

While no production code path currently sets `welcomedAt` to `0`, this fix makes the code more robust against edge cases such as:
- Legacy data from old databases
- Database corruption or failed updates  
- Restored backups with unusual timestamp values

## Testing

- All 16 existing auto-welcome tests pass
- No behavioral changes for normal cases (where `welcomedAt` is either `null` or a proper timestamp)

## Related Issues

Fixes #607

body:
Part 2 of 2 for #6523 (part 1: #6554, merged). Closes #6523 apart from the per-node timezone work, which is tracked separately.

## What
- **Global Settings → Solar Monitoring** (admin-only, like ADS-B/elevation; its keys were already admin-only writes):
  - Optional **Open-Meteo API key**, with how to get one. Blank uses the free tier (non-commercial, < 10k calls/day); a key uses the paid host.
  - **Grid cell size** (0.05°–1°) and **refresh interval** (1–24 h).
  - **Call estimate table** from `/api/solar/usage`: active nodes, then cells and "up to" calls/day per grid at the selected interval.
  - Free-tier **warning** when the choice exceeds 9,000/day.
  - Privacy note and the **"Weather data by Open-Meteo.com"** credit (CC BY 4.0).
  - "Refresh now" calls `POST /api/solar/refresh`.
- **Telemetry charts:** each node shows its own sunlight curve (W/m²) via `useSolarIrradiance`. The Dashboard's single global fetch is gone. No request is made while the feature is off or the overlay is hidden; refetch is every 15 min on hour-snapped keys.
- **Analysis → Solar Monitoring report, re-sourced per node:**
  - **Production overlay:** each node's own cell, in W/m².
  - **Low-sun forecast:** daily Wh/m² vs that node's own stored past days (needs ≥ 3 days; UTC days with ≥ 22 hours). The 75% threshold, 0–1.5 factor and battery simulation are unchanged.
  - **Horizon:** 3 days (Open-Meteo `forecast_days=2`).
  - **Position gate:** same as part 1; the caller's grants are loaded once per request.
- **forecast.solar removed:** service, `/api/solar/estimates*` and `/trigger`, repository, schema, and the latitude/longitude/azimuth/declination settings (`App.tsx`, `SettingsContext`, `GlobalSettingsPage`, `SettingsTab`). **Migration 246** drops `solar_estimates` (all three backends). **Migration 244** now skips when the table is missing, so restoring an older backup doesn't throw on boot. Backup/restore and the migrate-db CLI are updated.
- Docs: solar-monitoring, settings, analysis-reports, REST_API, public OpenAPI.

## API changes (breaking)
- `/api/solar/estimates`, `/api/solar/estimates/range`, `/api/solar/trigger`: removed.
- `/api/analysis/solar-nodes`:
  - `solar_production` moved onto each node as `{ timestamp, wattsPerM2 }`.
- `/api/analysis/solar-forecast`:
  - forecast fields are now per simulation, named `*_wh_m2`;
  - adds `nodes_without_forecast`.

## Mesh impact
None: no RF, no packets. Outbound Open-Meteo budget is enforced server-side (part 1).

## Review notes
- An independent review found no leak, migration or save-path defects. Its fixes are in the last commit: admin-gated section, grants loaded once, 3-day horizon.
- A node with **Hide from Map** still shows its sunlight curve on its telemetry graphs, which still show. Deliberate; easy to flip if unwanted.
- No route-level test for the analysis wiring yet; `computeSolarForecast` / `summarizeSolarProduction` are unit-tested (new `solarAnalysis.forecast.test.ts`).

title: feat(solar): per-node Open-Meteo sunlight + cloud cover backend (#6523)
body:
Part 1 of 2 for #6523: server side of per-node solar curves. The follow-up PR changes the Settings UI and chart overlay, and removes forecast.solar.

## What
- **`solar_irradiance` (migration 245):** global cache of hourly Open-Meteo `shortwave_radiation` (W/m²) and `cloud_cover` (%) per grid cell. Global by design, since weather doesn't depend on which source heard the node; added to CLAUDE.md's global-table list, system backup and the CLI migrator.
- **`openMeteoSolarService`:** an hourly tick (:07 UTC) collects every node heard in the last 7 days on every source (Meshtastic + MeshCore). It snaps each effective position (override, else the GPS fix with the source's sign-flip correction) to the configured grid and fetches cells older than the refresh interval. `timeformat=unixtime` means no local-time strings, so the #6553 parse bug can't recur.
- **`GET /api/solar/irradiance?sourceId&nodeId&start&end`:** telemetry read gate, then channel access, then the map position gate (`buildPositionFilter` / `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`). Position is resolved server-side and the cell is never returned.
- **Admin-only:** `GET /api/solar/usage` returns active node count plus cells per grid size (for the Settings estimate). `POST /api/solar/refresh` starts a pass.
- **v1 solar is now per node at `/api/v1/sources/:sourceId/solar?nodeId&start&end`** (behind `attachSource('nodes','read')`, like other per-source v1 routes) and returns W/m² + cloud cover. **`/api/v1/solar` and `/api/v1/solar/range` are removed** (breaking, per decision on #6523). OpenAPI and the public-surfaces guard updated.
- **New settings, all admin-only writes:** `solarMonitoringGridSize` (0.05/0.1/0.25/0.5/1°, default 0.1), `solarMonitoringRefreshHours` (1/2/3/6/12/24, default 3), `solar_open_meteo_api_token` (secret via `_token`; blank means free tier, set means the paid `customer-api` host).

## Budget safety (no RF; external API only)
- **Restart- and save-safe:** "due" comes from each cell's stored `fetchedAt`. A restart, a save or a refresh click never refetches a fresh cell.
- **Free tier (no key):** cells are capped to what 9,000 calls/day allows at the refresh interval, most recently heard first. Every call is also counted against a persisted per-UTC-day counter (`solarOpenMeteoCallLog`, server-owned, not saveable), and a pass stops at 4,000 calls (the hourly limit is 5,000). A test runs a 2,000-cell mesh whose recency order shuffles across 72 hourly ticks and stays at or under 9,000/day; without the counter it reaches about 11,500.
- **Pacing and errors:** chunks of 50, paced at 500/min (limit 600). 429/5xx end the pass; other 4xx skip the chunk. Nothing retries before the next tick.
- **Private position overrides are never sent.**

## Privacy
- Open-Meteo receives rounded cell centres only, and only when Solar Monitoring is on.
- Public-instance anonymous viewers already get ~1.4 km positions. The smallest grid cell is ~5.5 km, so the curve reveals less than the map does.

Rows carry a `protocol` (`'meshtastic'` default, `'meshcore'` since #5552); every list read defaults to Meshtastic rows, so pass `'meshcore'`/`'all'` deliberately — a MeshCore secret must never reach a Meshtastic consumer. (2) the `estimated_positions` table (issue #3271) — one row per physical `nodeNum`, pooled from traceroute + neighbor observations across ALL Meshtastic sources (incl. MQTT) by the scheduled `positionEstimationService`; estimation is **Meshtastic-only** (MeshCore excluded) and runs as a global batch job (`positionEstimationScheduler`), not in realtime. MeshCore estimates (#6260) are the exception to the exception: they are computed on read, per source, by `meshcorePositionEstimator.ts` (`GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/estimated-positions`) with the same `solveNodePosition` and max-uncertainty setting, and are **never stored in this table**. (3) the `automations` / `automation_runs` / `automation_variables` / `automation_variable_values` tables (issue #3653, Automation Engine) — automations and their user-defined variables are **global** (no `sourceId`); a workflow evaluates against events from every source, and a `condition.sourceFilter` block inside its `config` graph scopes it to a subset. Variable values are keyed by an explicit `scopeKey` (global/source/node/sourceNode) rather than a row-level `sourceId`. See `docs/internal/dev-notes/AUTOMATION_ENGINE_PLAN.md`. (4) the `coverage_surveys` table (issue #5277, Coverage Report) — a saved survey is one sender over one time window, heard by receivers on many sources, so it is **global**; it holds no reception data, its receptions are still read through the per-source `/receptions` route, and the survey list is gated on sender visibility. See `docs/internal/dev-notes/COVERAGE_P4_SPEC.md` §2b. (5) the `translation_cache` table (issue #5520) — one row per hashed (text, language) pair, shared so a phrase is translated once; it stores no text and no message reference, and no route reads it. The links from a message to an entry (`message_translations`) ARE per-source, and every read goes through the message-list visibility check. See `docs/internal/dev-notes/TRANSLATION_CACHE_SPEC.md`. (6) the `cross_source_links` table (issue #5561, map "heard here" edges) — an hourly aggregate of "source A's radio was heard by source B", so each row names **two** sources (`txSourceId`, `rxSourceId`) and has no single `sourceId`. **Two-source read rule:** a row, and anything derived from it, is shown only when the viewer can read BOTH sources (admins see all); never reveal "another source" to someone who can read only one. `CrossSourceLinksRepository.getLinks` takes the permitted source list and requires both ends in it, and the route drops any edge whose endpoint position fails `buildPositionFilter` / `buildMeshCorePositionFilter`. All classification goes through `src/server/services/crossSourceCorrelation.ts` (#5559/#5560 use the same rule read-side). Source deletion and purge remove rows on either end. (7) the `automation_fire_state` table (migration 219) — each automation's persisted cooldown / rate-limit state, so a restart or a save never re-arms a rule; global like the `automations` table it belongs to, keyed by `automationId` plus the engine's cooldown `scopeKey`. Deleting an automation deletes its rows. (8) the `script_secrets` table (migration 240) — admin-stored values (API keys) that **every** user script on **every** source receives as environment variables; a user decision, stated in the UI and docs. Values are AES-256-GCM envelopes keyed from SESSION_SECRET (`scriptSecretStore.ts`), decrypted into an in-memory snapshot that `buildScriptChildEnv` adds after the INJ-01 deny filter; no API returns a value. (9) the `solar_irradiance` table (migration 245, #6523) — Open-Meteo hourly sunlight + cloud cover per grid cell (`"<grid>:<lat>:<lon>"`), fetched by `openMeteoSolarService` for every active node's effective position on every source; weather at a place does not depend on which source heard the node, and sharing cells is what keeps the call count down. Rows hold no node reference; a node's curve is read only through `getNodeIrradiance` (`src/server/utils/solarNodeCell.ts`), which applies the telemetry read gate plus `buildPositionFilter` / `buildMeshCorePositionFilter` and never returns the cell. Private position overrides are never sent. Adding a new per-source data type should still get a `sourceId` column unless you have a concrete cross-source-by-design reason like decryption.
 - **`meshcore_trace_runs` (migration 225, #6276) is per-source.** An attempt log of the MeshCore traces a source sent (target, path, origin, answered/timeout/failed), written by `MeshCoreManager.traceContactPathDetailed` (the manager picks the tag and passes it to the backend) and read by the Traceroute Explorer, which joins it to `meshcore_hop_snr` by `(sourceId, traceTag, authCode)`. Source deletion purges it; retention follows `HOP_SNR_RETENTION_MS` (90 d); `pending` rows from before startup are swept to `timeout`.
 - **Permissions are per-source.** `permissions.sourceId` was added in migration 022, refined in 033. `requirePermission(resource, action, { sourceIdFrom })` checks the named source; **without `sourceIdFrom` a per-source resource passes on a grant for ANY source**, so never omit it on a route that acts on a `sourceId` from the request. Meshtastic device routes that fall back to the primary source use `requireDeviceSourcePermission()` + `getDeviceSourceTarget(req)` (`src/server/utils/deviceSourcePermission.ts`), which resolve the source once for both the check and the action.
 - **Frontend uses `SourceContext`** (`src/contexts/SourceContext.tsx`). `useSource()` returns `{ sourceId, sourceName }`; `sourceId` is `null` outside a `SourceProvider` (legacy/single-source views).

title: fix(solar): request forecast.solar timestamps in UTC (#6523)
body:
Phase 1 of #6523 (timezone parse bug). Per-node timezone and per-node solar curves follow in later PRs.

## Problem
forecast.solar returns offset-less local timestamps (`2024-11-05 14:00:00`) at the panel's location. `new Date()` read them in the container's TZ, so the overlay shifted by the zone gap (default Docker `TZ=UTC`).

## Fix
- Request `?time=utc`; forecast.solar then returns `2026-11-23T13:00:00+00:00` (verified with a live call).
- Parse with `Date.parse`, skip unparseable keys.
- Migration 244 deletes stored `solar_estimates` once (rows were shifted and can't be corrected in place). The next hourly fetch refills them. Consumers (solar analysis, automations, v1 API) read the same table and get correct rows after one fetch.

## Mesh impact
None: no packets, no timers changed. Same one forecast.solar call per hour.

## Tests
- `solarMonitoringService.test.ts`: URL asserts `?time=utc`; stored epochs asserted exactly; unparseable-key case. Passed under `TZ=America/Chicago`.
- `migrations.test.ts` passes. `tsc` + `lint:ci` clean.

Refs #6523

title: feat(meshcore): show last-hop SNR/RSSI in the Message Route modal (#6551)
body:
Closes #6551

## Summary
The MeshCore **Message Route** modal now shows a **Last hop signal** row: SNR, plus RSSI when the message has it, labelled with where it was measured:
- relayed message → `from hop #N` (N = last row of the hop list below it)
- direct message (`hopCount === 0`) → `from sender`
- hop count known, path not stored → `from last repeater`
- no SNR → row hidden

The message stream is unchanged: it still shows signal only on direct messages, so a relayed value never sits next to the sender's name.

Same component serves every MeshCore source type, so companion and repeater/ingest sources both get it (RSSI renders only where stored).

![Message Route modal with Last hop signal row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/6551-route-modal-signal/docs/public/images/features/6551-route-modal-signal.png)

## Mesh impact
Display only. No packets, timers, or notifications.

## Tests
- 4 new cases in `MeshCoreMessageRouteModal.test.tsx` (relayed, direct w/o RSSI, unknown path, no SNR); file passes 19/19.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `lint:ci` clean.

title: build(deps): bump i18next from 27.0.0 to 27.2.2
body:
Bumps [i18next](https://github.com/i18next/i18next) from 27.0.0 to 27.2.2.
Release notes

Sourced from i18next's releases.

v27.2.2

  • fix: setDefaultNamespace() works on a clone. A clone's translator keeps its own options object, so the call changed i18n.options.defaultNS while t() kept using the old default namespace. i18next-http-middleware hands every request a clone, so req.i18n.setDefaultNamespace() did nothing there. (#2106)
  • fix: supportedLngs works in any casing. Every other language code is formatted (pt-br to pt-BR, EN to en, all lowercase with lowerCaseLng), but supportedLngs was compared as written, so supportedLngs: ['pt-br'], ['EN'], or ['pt-BR'] with lowerCaseLng: true refused that language and fell back. They are now compared in that formatted form (also by loadLanguages()), while options.supportedLngs stays as written. (#1791)
  • fix(types): resources typed with named interfaces get their nested keys. The key types only walked into objects with an index signature, which a type alias has and an interface does not, so t('nested.key') failed with TS2345 while t('nested') compiled. Interfaces now give the same keys as type aliases, so t('nested') without returnObjects is rejected for them too. (#2326)
  • fix(types): typed keys work with strictNullChecks: false. Without strict null checks undefined passes extends string, so the key prefix, namespace and context checks took a missing keyPrefix, ns or context for a value: t('title') was rejected (only t('ns:title') compiled), t() returned string, and react-i18next's Trans accepted no i18nKey. A new type test project compiles with strictNullChecks: false; with strict null checks the types resolve as before. (#2085)

v27.2.1

  • fix: a variable passed as undefined renders as an empty string when its placeholder has a format too ({{amount, number}}), as {{amount}} already did. The placeholder stayed in the result with the default skipOnVariables: true, and debug mode logged "missed to pass in variable" with either setting. Thanks

title: build(deps): bump @simplewebauthn/server from 14.0.3 to 14.1.0
body:
Bumps [@simplewebauthn/server](https://github.com/MasterKale/SimpleWebAuthn/tree/HEAD/packages/server) from 14.0.3 to 14.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​simplewebauthn/server's releases.

v14.1.0

Changes:

  • [server] Support for the FIDO Convenience Metadata Service has been added with the new ConvenienceMetadataService. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/advanced/server/metadata-service#convenience-metadata-service for more info (#812)
  • [server] verifyRegistrationResponse() and verifyAuthenticationResponse() will now raise a SimpleWebAuthnError when expectedRPID or expectedOrigin are not valid values (#824)
  • [server] "android-key" attestation statement verification now checks that the x5c root certificate is a known one before verifying the certificate chain (#821)
  • [server] "android-key" attestation statement verification now knows about the new Google Android Key Attestation CA1 trust anchor (#820)
  • [server] "tpm" attestation statement verification now properly parses non-TPM_ALG_NULL schemes in pubArea (#822)
Changelog

Sourced from @​simplewebauthn/server's changelog.

v14.1.0

Changes:

  • [server] Support for the FIDO Convenience Metadata Service has been added with the new ConvenienceMetadataService. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/advanced/server/metadata-service#convenience-metadata-service for more info (#812)
  • [server] verifyRegistrationResponse() and verifyAuthenticationResponse() will now raise a SimpleWebAuthnError when expectedRPID or expectedOrigin

title: refactor(meshcore): one channel-text store for device and MQTT feeds (#6341 P6)
body:
Phase 6 of #6341, the last one. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6341_P6_SPEC.md`; plan: `ISSUE_6341_EPIC.md`. Closes #6341.

## Changes
- **One store path.** New `src/server/services/meshcoreChannelTextStore.ts` (`storeDecryptedChannelText`): message filter, reactions (pending and late), mc1Hash, insert, `selfOrigin`, emit, after-store hook. The device's `storeDecryptedGroupText` and the MQTT feed's `ingestChannelMessage` both call it. Per-path differences stay as options: id builder, radio metadata (hops, receivedAt), block-hit counting, in-memory pool, stats.
- **Row ids unchanged.** `buildId` keeps each path's formula (`frameChannelMessageId` with the key fingerprint for the device, `channelMessageId` with the channel hash for MQTT, which migration 228 depends on). Golden-id tests pin `rpt`, `cmp` and `mqtt` ids.
- `src/server/services/meshcoreLocalSenderNames.ts` now holds the sender-name override registry and `isLocalMeshCoreSenderName` (moved out of `meshcoreManager.ts`; test helper re-exported).
- MQTT's private `decryptGroupText` is gone; it uses the shared `decryptGroupTextFrame`.

## Behaviour changes (MQTT feeds only, maintainer-approved)
- Feed message events now carry `selfOrigin` when the sender name is one of this install's radio names or a recent "Send as" name. Automations then skip our own sends heard back on the feed unless "include self" is on. A stranger on a region feed who shares a local node's name also won't trigger automations (accepted).
- Late reaction updates are emitted after the message, matching the device path.

## Mesh impact
None: no packets, notifications or timers change.

## Tests
New: `meshcoreChannelTextStore.test.ts` (20 cases incl. golden ids), `meshcoreMqttManager.selfOrigin.test.ts`. Behaviour suites passed with no assertion changes: device repeater/companion/OTA ingest, sender-name override, channel heard, reactions, all `meshcoreMqttManager*`, broker integration, reaction ingest, message notifier, mention notifications, automation engine, migration 228. Targeted batch after rebasing on P4 + P5: 3,442 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

title: feat(clock): out-of-sync samples for Meshtastic and MeshCore MQTT feeds (#6341 P5)
body:
Phase 5 of #6341: #6273 follow-ups. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6341_P5_SPEC.md`; plan: `ISSUE_6341_EPIC.md`.

## Changes
- **Protocol-neutral sample store.** `recordClockSample(telemetry, subject, …)` takes `{ nodeId, nodeNum, publicKey }`; `detectClockOffset` keeps its signature and wraps it. `node:clockOffset`, `onClockOffset` and the `clockOutOfSync` trigger context carry `nodeNum`, so Meshtastic nodes resolve names in automations and Device Health.
- **Meshtastic samples** from live LoRa TELEMETRY_APP and POSITION_APP packets, one an hour per node. `clockSampleGate.ts` requires: `rxTime` within ±120 s of server time (both directions), no firmware replay, no store-and-forward/MQTT/proxy/Virtual Node, LoRa transport, not the local node, plausible sender time (a node with no clock sends uptime or 0 and is skipped). Offset is server time minus sender time, so a wrong local radio clock stops sampling instead of flagging every node. Meshtastic MQTT sources are never sampled.
- **MeshCore MQTT feeds** (`meshcore_mqtt`, broker): a sample is stored only when two different observers report the same advert with offsets of the same sign (`MqttClockAgreement`: 2,000 nodes, 8 observers, 10-minute TTL). The smaller offset is stored, so the existing two-sample, once-per-episode rule fires only when both observers see the node out of sync. The advert signature is verified at most once.
- Copy: the trigger is no longer MeshCore-only; Device Health drops "(MeshCore)"; substitutions list `nodeNum`; docs updated.

Maintainer decisions: skip Meshtastic nodes with no clock; accept that MQTT observer identity (topic/`origin_id`) is unauthenticated.

## Mesh impact
Passive: no packets. Alerts use the existing caps (Device Health 10/hour). History lives in telemetry, so a restart or save never re-fires an episode.

## Release note
"Clock out of sync" now covers Meshtastic nodes (from live LoRa telemetry and position timestamps) and MeshCore MQTT feeds (when two observers agree). Nodes without a set clock are ignored.

## Tests
New: `clockSampleGate.test.ts`, `meshtasticManager.clockSample.test.ts`, `meshcoreMqttClockSamples.test.ts`, `meshcoreMqttManager.clockSample(.perSource).test.ts`. Extended: `meshcoreDeviceHealth.clockOffset`, engine `clockOutOfSync`, `deviceHealth`. Targeted batch (Meshtastic manager, MeshCore MQTT, device health, automation engine, security scan): 4,017 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

title: feat(meshcore): 'Send as' on automated sends and the channel composer (#6341 P4)
body:
Phase 4 of #6341: #6282 sender-name follow-ups. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6341_P4_SPEC.md`; plan: `ISSUE_6341_EPIC.md`.

## Changes
- **Automated sends can use an allowed name.** `sendAutomatedText({ senderName })` routes MeshCore channel sends to `sendChannelMessageAs` for timer triggers, Auto Responder (channel replies), Auto Announce (`meshcoreAutoAnnounceSenderName`, per source) and the Automation Engine send action. DMs and Meshtastic ignore it.
- **Run-time rule:** a name that is no longer allowed or can't be sent (opt-in off, firmware < 13, client repeat on, not a companion) falls back to the node's own name with one warning per source/label/name/reason. No retry, no silent drop.
- **Split planning** uses the smaller of the raw cap and the node-name cap, so every part fits whichever path sends it.
- **`GET /api/sources/:id/meshcore/sender-names`** for pickers: passes on `messages:write`, `automation:write` or `configuration:read`; returns `[]` when off.
- **Editors:** "Send as" picker (shared `SenderNamePicker`) in the timer, responder, announce and Automation Engine editors. Save checks are syntax only (a stale name never blocks a save); a save that sets or changes a name writes a `meshcore_sender_name_automation_set` audit row.
- **Channel composer:** "Send as" picker when the source has names enabled; the counter switches to the raw cap.
- **Fix:** both send routes held a short override name to the node-name cap before the raw cap, so valid texts were refused.

Maintainer decisions: fall back + warn; senders may read the list; audit on save only. Virtual Node raw packets stay refused (#5350).

## Mesh impact
No new packets. A name shortens the text cap, so a long automated text may need one more part. Existing limits still bound it: max 3 parts, 10 s between parts, 5-minute split-timer floor, 4 channels per timer. Raw sends skip the #3979 channel auto-retry, so they send fewer packets.

## Release note
Timer triggers, Auto Responder channel replies, Auto Announce and the Automation Engine send action can send MeshCore channel messages under one of the source's allowed sender names, and the channel composer has a "Send as" picker. If a name is no longer allowed when the message goes out, it is sent under the node's own name with a warning. A name lowers the text limit slightly.

## Tests
New: `meshcoreManager.automatedSenderName.test.ts`, `meshcoreAutomationRoutes.senderName.test.ts` (route harness), `automation.senderName.test.ts`, `SenderNameField.test.tsx`. Extended: split plan, simulator, meshActionDeps, actionExecutor, both send-route sender-name suites, `meshcoreRoutes.scope` guard, MeshCoreChannelsView. Targeted batch: 8,817 passed; the one failure (route-scope guard) is fixed and re-run. Dev deploy loads cleanly; no MeshCore radio was connected, so the picker (needs firmware ≥ 13) was checked by component tests, not by screenshot.

title: feat(reticulum): Notifications tab, bridge link alerts, gated new-destination alerts (#6341 P3)
body:
Phase 3 of #6341. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6341_P3_SPEC.md`; plan: `ISSUE_6341_EPIC.md`.

## Changes
- **Notifications tab on Reticulum sources** (shared `NotificationsTab`, signed-in only). New capability row: DMs, new destinations, server events, keyword filters, templates. A new `nodeMonitoring` capability hides inactive-node, low-battery and the node picker (and skips the node load) where they can't work.
- **DM notifications** now use `dispatchMessageNotification`: per-DM mute (new mute menu in the DM view), click-through opens the conversation, sender shown by sanitised display name (falls back to a short hash).
- **Bridge re-delivery no longer double-notifies or re-fires automations:** `upsertMessage` / `upsertDestination` return `{ inserted }`.
- **New-destination alerts** for LXMF delivery destinations only, behind `newNodeAlertGate` (48 h learning, 10/hour/source, "(+N more)"). Own destinations skipped. The gate's earliest-row lookup also reads `reticulum_destinations`, so existing sources don't go quiet for 48 h.
- **Bridge connection lost/restored alerts** via `brokerLinkNotifier` (new options: `'bridge'` wording, custom event names, name getter; MQTT callers unchanged). 120 s grace (bridge backoff tops at 60 s); the user's Disconnect alerts at once; stop/edit/shutdown stay silent.

Maintainer decision: accept rare false alerts for peers evicted past the 2,000-destination cap after a restart (bounded by the hourly cap).

## Mesh impact
No packets sent. Notifications are capped per source by the existing gate; gate state is persisted, so a save, restart or edit never re-arms or clears it. Link alerts are debounced 120 s.

## Release note

title: feat(notifications): gated new-node alerts for MQTT feeds (#6341 P2)
body:
Phase 2 of #6341. Spec: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6341_P2_SPEC.md`; plan: `ISSUE_6341_EPIC.md`.

## Changes
- **Shared new-node alert code.** `newNodeAlertTracker.ts` (bounded dedup/pending sets plus an in-flight claim, so copies of one advert from many observers use one cap slot) and `meshcoreNewNodeAlert.ts` (alert + gated helper), extracted from `MeshCoreManager`. The Repeater path and the MeshCore MQTT feed both use them; only the Companion path runs Auto Welcome.
- **MeshCore MQTT feeds now alert on new nodes** (`meshcore_mqtt` and `meshcore_mqtt_broker`), behind `newNodeAlertGate` (48 h learning, 10/hour/source, "(+N more)"). An alert needs a verified advert signature whatever the global toggle says; the check runs once per new key.
- **Meshtastic MQTT (`mqtt_bridge`, `mqtt_broker`) alerts go through the same gate.** They were uncapped. TCP sources are unchanged.
- The gate's earliest-node lookup also reads `nodes`, so a long-running Meshtastic MQTT source does not go quiet for 48 h after upgrade.
- Node purge re-arms the window for gated sources.
- Notifications tab: feed rows show the toggle and a learning note; docs updated.

Maintainer decision: a feed sighting the gate drops counts as "known" for #5729 cross-source dedup.

## Mesh impact
No packets. Notifications only, capped per source by the existing gate. Gate state is persisted per source, so a save, restart or reconnect never re-arms or clears it; only a purge re-arms it (adds quiet time). Feed adverts raise no automation events (#5553).

## Release note
New-node alerts now cover MQTT feeds. Meshtastic MQTT bridge and broker sources are capped at 10 alerts per hour per source, and a source new to MeshMonitor learns for 48 hours first. MeshCore MQTT feeds now alert on new nodes whose advert signature verifies; the preference defaults on, so an existing feed starts alerting for new keys after the update, up to the cap. Over-cap alerts are dropped and the next one ends with "(+N more new nodes since the last alert)". Meshtastic TCP sources are unchanged.

## Tests
New: `meshcoreMqttManager.newNodeAlert(.perSource).test.ts`, `newNodeAlertTracker.test.ts`, `newNodeAlertGate.realDeps.test.ts`, `purgeRoutes.rearm.test.ts`. Extended: `database.service`, `notificationService`, `nodes.test.ts` (SQLite/PG/MySQL), capability + NotificationsTab tests. Targeted runs with PG/MySQL containers up: 0 failed, 0 skipped; all 118 `meshcoreManager*` suites pass. Verified on the dev container: the MeshCore broker feed's Notifications tab shows the toggle and note, no console errors.

title: fix(meshcore): channel reorder moves notification prefs; MySQL per-source prefs (#6341 P1)
body:
Phase 1 of #6341 (MeshCore parity deferred follow-ups). Plan: `docs/internal/dev-notes/ISSUE_6341_EPIC.md`.

## Changes
- **Channel reorder moves notification preferences (#5379 gap).** `MeshCoreChannelRemapRepository.remapChannelSlots` now rewrites each of the source's `user_notification_preferences` rows, `enabled_channels` and `muted_channels`, in the same transaction as messages, read markers, permissions and settings. Only slot ids (< 1000) move; keyed ids, unknown entries and malformed JSON stay as they are; a mute keeps its `muteUntil`.
- **MySQL: one notification-preference row per user across all sources (bug found while testing).** The MySQL baseline declared `userId INT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, which MySQL names `userId`. Migration 051 only dropped `idx_user_notification_preferences_userId`, so baseline-built MySQL databases still refused a second per-source row (`ER_DUP_ENTRY`). Migration 243 (MySQL only; SQLite/PG no-op, idempotent) swaps that unique index for a plain one, since the `users` FK needs an index.

## Mesh impact
None: no packets, notifications or timers change.

## Tests
`meshcoreChannelRemap.multiBackend.test.ts`: prefs follow a 3-cycle, other sources untouched, `muteUntil` kept, slot 0 / keyed ids unchanged, junk and malformed JSON kept. Ran locally on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL containers: 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; `migrations.test.ts` passes.

title: feat(meshcore-mqtt): mark one observer as "My node" on an ingest/broker source (#6532)
body:
Closes #6532. Follow-up to #6531 / #6533.

## What
A `meshcore_mqtt` or `meshcore_mqtt_broker` source can now name one observer as the owner's node. The new optional config field is `localObserverKey`, set as **My node** in the source form. The change is display only.

| Where | Effect |
|---|---|
| Ingest Overview and Nodes tabs | **My node** badge on that observer |
| Dashboard map | `isLocal` rows draw at the larger marker size. Device-backed MeshCore sources get this too (the dashboard had no MeshCore local marker before). |
| `/api/nodes` | `isLocal: true` and hop 0, the same as a device source's radio |
| Sign-flip correction | Uses the observer's stored position, or a **public** location override, as the source's reference point |

![My node badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/mqtt-my-node-6532/docs/public/images/features/6532-ingest-my-node.png)

## Design
- A single helper, `meshCoreDisplayLocalKey()` in `sourceManagerTypes.ts`, returns the radio's key for a device source and the configured observer for an ingest or broker source. It is upper-cased, and keys are compared case-insensitively.
- `getLocalNode()` and `getLocalNodeInfo()` **stay null** on ingest managers. The survey found that a non-null value would miscount the unified active count (`unifiedRoutes.ts`) and could leak into the Meshtastic local-node set. Every transmit and config path narrows to the device manager, so the key never reaches them.
- **Validation:** 64 hex characters on both source types. On a broker it must also be on the observer allowlist when one is set. This is enforced server-side and in the form.
- **Redaction:** the key is `withheld`, the same class as the broker allowlist: editors see it, viewers do not.

## Decisions (maintainer, on #6532)
The marker applies to the dashboard for all MeshCore sources. There is one local observer per source. It is display only: distance and "hops from me" origins are unchanged.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. Nothing is sent.
2. **Spam:** no messages, events or notifications.
3. **Timers:** none.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - Broker config validation and normalization.
  - The `meshCoreDisplayLocalKey` truth table.
  - `isLocal` on `/ingest/overview` and `/ingest/nodes`, including case-insensitive matching and the none-configured case.
  - The dashboard row flag.
  - The sign-flip reference: stored position, public override, private override ignored, none configured.
  - Broker form round-trip and errors.
  - The ingest view badge.
  - Config-redaction fixtures.
- **Live in the dev container:**
  1. Set **My node** on a test broker source through `PUT /api/sources/:id`.
  2. Published a `/status` heartbeat.
  3. The Overview showed the **My node** badge.
  4. `/ingest/nodes`, `/api/sources/:id/dashboard` and `/api/nodes` all flagged it: `isLocal: true` and hop 0.
  5. The dashboard marker rendered at 60 px.
- `lint:ci` clean.

title: feat(meshcore-mqtt): observer battery/uptime history and location override for ingest sources (#6531)
body:
Closes #6531. Part 3 ("my node") is split out as #6532.

## What
**1. Battery and uptime history for MQTT observers.** `/status` heartbeats on a `meshcore_mqtt` or `meshcore_mqtt_broker` source now write battery and uptime as telemetry, next to noise floor. The rows come from the same `statusToTelemetryRows` mapping the remote-telemetry scheduler uses for device-backed repeaters, so the series names and units match:

| Field | Series | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Battery | `mc_status_battery_volts` | V (mV / 1000) |
| Uptime | `mc_status_uptime_secs` | s |
| Noise floor | `mc_status_noise_floor` | dB (unchanged) |

Solar Monitoring already reads `mc_status_battery_volts`, and Solar Analysis already includes MQTT-fed source types, so a solar observer gets the forecast overlay and solar-node detection with no further change. All three rows go out in one `insertTelemetryBatch` under the existing 60 s per-observer throttle, renamed `MIN_STATUS_SAMPLE_MS`.

**2. Location override on MQTT ingest/broker sources.** The three `/nodes/:publicKey/position-override` routes move from `meshcoreContactsRoutes.ts` into a new `meshcorePositionOverrideRoutes.ts`. It is mounted on the data side of the barrel, behind `anyMeshCoreRouteGuard`. Permissions are unchanged: `nodes:write` plus `requireAuth()` to edit, and `nodes:read` / `viewOnMap` / `nodes_private:read` to read. In the POST, the live-contact fallback runs only for a device manager; an ingest node must already have a stored row, which an observer gets from its first heartbeat. The ingest page's **Nodes** tab gets an **Override location** button that reuses `PositionOverrideModal`. It shows only to signed-in users with `nodes:write` on the source.

![Ingest Nodes tab with location override](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/feat/mqtt-observer-telemetry-6531/docs/public/images/features/6531-ingest-location-override.png)

## Decisions (maintainer)
- Battery and uptime are recorded for **every** observer on the source, not favorites only. This matches noise floor, and favorites-only would have meant opening the device-only favorite route to ingest sources.
- Uptime is kept: a reset marks a brown-out.

## Mesh impact checklist
1. **Airtime:** none. This is passive ingest of data that already arrives over MQTT, and nothing is sent to the mesh.
2. **Spam:** no messages. Reboot and power-change detection (`meshcoreDeviceHealth`) runs only in the device pollers, not on this path, so no new notifications fire. Mesh Issues reads the series only when someone views it.
3. **Timers:** none added. The throttle works per heartbeat and is not a scheduler.
4. **DB growth:** up to 3 rows per observer per ~5 min heartbeat, about 860 per observer per day, against about 290 today. Telemetry retention prunes them.

## Testing
- `meshcoreMqttManager.status.test.ts`: all three rows land in one batch, mV → V conversion, uptime 0 is kept, an implausible battery value is skipped, and the shared throttle applies.

title: fix(meshcore): let the MQTT ingest source page scroll (#6527)
body:
Fixes #6527.

## Problem
On a MeshCore MQTT ingest source, the Nodes, Channels, Packets and Notifications tabs can't scroll; lists past the viewport are cut off.

`MeshCoreIngestSourcePage` wraps `MeshCoreIngestView` in `.dashboard-page`, which is `height: 100dvh; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden`. The view root `.wrap` had no `flex: 1`, `min-height: 0`, or `overflow-y`, so nothing scrolled.

## Fix
Add `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto;` to `.wrap` in `MeshCoreIngestView.module.css`. `MeshCoreIngestView` only renders on this page.

This also gives the Packets tab (`.meshcore-packet-monitor { height: 100% }`) and the Notifications pane (`flex: 1; min-height: 0`) a bounded parent, so their own inner scrollers size against the remaining space instead of an unbounded one.

## Mesh impact
CSS only: no packets, notifications, or timers.

## Testing

title: fix(meshcore): hide status-bar controls from viewers without connection:write (#6524)
body:
Fixes #6524

## Problem
The MeshCore page status bar always rendered **Advert (nearby, zero-hop)**, **Flood advert**, **Disconnect** (and **Connect** when disconnected). Every one of these hits a route guarded by `requireAuth()` + `requirePermission('connection', 'write', { sourceIdFrom: 'params.id' })` (`src/server/routes/meshcoreDeviceRoutes.ts`), so anonymous guests and read-only users saw buttons that could only return permission errors.

## Change
- `MeshCoreStatusBar` takes a new `canControl` prop (default `true`). When it is false, the whole control group is hidden. The connection status text and the receive-only chip stay visible.
- `MeshCorePage` passes `canControl = authStatus.authenticated && hasPermission('connection', 'write', { sourceId })`. This is the same check the routes make: an anonymous user with a `connection:write` grant would still fail `requireAuth()`, so being signed in is required as well.
- Server-side enforcement is unchanged. Hiding the buttons is not the access control.

## Tests
- New `MeshCoreStatusBar.canControl.test.tsx`: controls hidden when connected and when disconnected without permission, and shown with permission.
- `src/components/MeshCore` suite: 1675 tests pass. One suite (`meshcoreResponderMatch.test.ts`) fails to load locally because the `re2` native module isn't built in this environment. It fails the same way with this change stashed, so CI is the authority there.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:ci` are clean.

## Mesh impact
None. This change only removes UI. It sends no packets and adds no timers or notifications.
